sentence_336: Antisemitism was commonly used as an instrument for settling personal conflicts in the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]], starting with the conflict between [[Joseph_Stalin|Joseph Stalin]] and [[Leon_Trotsky|Leon Trotsky]] and continuing through numerous conspiracy-theories spread by official propaganda.
sentence_337: [[Antisemitism_in_the_Soviet_Union|Antisemitism in the USSR]] reached new heights after 1948 during the campaign against the "[[Rootless_cosmopolitan|rootless cosmopolitan]]" (euphemism for "Jew") in which numerous Yiddish-language poets, writers, painters and sculptors were killed or arrested.
sentence_338: This culminated in the so-called [[Doctors'_Plot|Doctors' Plot]] (1952–1953).
sentence_339: Similar antisemitic propaganda in Poland resulted in the flight of Polish Jewish survivors from the country.
sentence_340: After the war, the [[Kielce_pogrom|Kielce pogrom]] and the "[[March_1968_events|March 1968 events]]" in communist Poland represented further incidents of antisemitism in Europe.
sentence_341: The [[Anti-Jewish_violence_in_Poland,_1944–1946|anti-Jewish violence in postwar Poland]] has a common theme of [[Blood_libel|blood libel]] rumours.
sentence_342: Further information: [[Antisemitism_in_Europe#21st_century|Antisemitism in Europe § 21st century]]
sentence_343: Physical assaults against Jews in those countries included beatings, stabbings and other violence, which increased markedly, sometimes resulting in serious injury and death.
sentence_344: A 2015 report by the US State Department on religious freedom declared that "European anti-Israel sentiment crossed the line into anti-Semitism."
sentence_345: This rise in antisemitic attacks is associated with both the [[Muslim_anti-Semitism|Muslim anti-Semitism]] and the rise of far-right political parties as a result of the economic crisis of 2008.
sentence_346: This rise in the support for far right ideas in western and eastern Europe has resulted in the increase of antisemitic acts, mostly attacks on Jewish memorials, synagogues and cemeteries but also a number of physical attacks against Jews.
sentence_347: In Eastern Europe the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the instability of the new states has brought the rise of nationalist movements and the accusation against Jews for the economic crisis, taking over the local economy and bribing the government, along with traditional and religious motives for antisemitism such as [[Blood_libel|blood libels]].
sentence_348: Most of the antisemitic incidents are against Jewish cemeteries and building (community centers and synagogues).
sentence_349: Nevertheless, there were several violent attacks against Jews in Moscow in 2006 when a neo-Nazi stabbed 9 people at the Bolshaya Bronnaya Synagogue, the failed bomb attack on the same synagogue in 1999, the threats against Jewish pilgrims in Uman, Ukraine and the attack against a [[Menorah_(Temple)|menorah]] by extremist Christian organization in Moldova in 2009.
sentence_350: According to [[Paul_Johnson_(writer)|Paul Johnson]], antisemitic policies are a sign of a state which is poorly governed.
sentence_351: While no European state currently has such policies, the Economist Intelligence Unit notes the rise in political uncertainty, notably populism and nationalism, as something that is particularly alarming for Jews.
sentence_352: Main article: [[Antisemitism_in_the_Arab_world|Antisemitism in the Arab world]]
sentence_353: [[Robert_L._Bernstein|Robert Bernstein]], founder of [[Human_Rights_Watch|Human Rights Watch]], says that antisemitism is "deeply ingrained and institutionalized" in "Arab nations in modern times."
sentence_354: In a 2011 survey by the [[Pew_Research_Center|Pew Research Center]], all of the Muslim-majority Middle Eastern countries polled held few positive opinions of Jews.
sentence_355: In the questionnaire, only 2% of [[Egypt|Egyptians]], 3% of [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] Muslims, and 2% of [[Jordan|Jordanians]] reported having a positive view of Jews.
sentence_356: Muslim-majority countries outside the Middle East similarly had few who held positive views of Jews, with 4% of [[Turkey|Turks]] and 9% of [[Indonesia|Indonesians]] viewing Jews favorably.
sentence_357: According to a 2011 exhibition at the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington, United States, some of the dialogue from Middle East media and commentators about Jews bear a striking resemblance to [[Nazi_propaganda|Nazi propaganda]].
sentence_358: According to Josef Joffe of [[Newsweek|Newsweek]], "anti-Semitism—the real stuff, not just bad-mouthing particular Israeli policies—is as much part of Arab life today as the hijab or the hookah.
sentence_359: Whereas this darkest of creeds is no longer tolerated in polite society in the West, in the Arab world, Jew hatred remains culturally endemic."
sentence_360: Muslim clerics in the Middle East have frequently referred to Jews as descendants of apes and pigs, which are conventional epithets for Jews and Christians.
sentence_361: According to professor [[Robert_Wistrich|Robert Wistrich]], director of the [[Vidal_Sassoon_International_Center_for_the_Study_of_Antisemitism|Vidal Sassoon International Center for the Study of Antisemitism]] (SICSA), the calls for the destruction of Israel by [[Iran|Iran]] or by [[Hamas|Hamas]], [[Hezbollah|Hezbollah]], [[Islamic_Jihad_Movement_in_Palestine|Islamic Jihad]], or the [[Muslim_Brotherhood|Muslim Brotherhood]], represent a contemporary mode of genocidal antisemitism.
sentence_362: Antisemitism has been explained in terms of [[Racism|racism]], [[Xenophobia|xenophobia]], [[Psychological_projection|projected guilt]], displaced aggression, and the search for a [[Scapegoat|scapegoat]].
sentence_363: Some explanations assign partial blame to the perception of Jewish people as unsociable.
sentence_364: Such a perception may have arisen by many Jews having strictly kept to their own communities, with their own practices and laws.
sentence_365: It has also been suggested that parts of antisemitism arose from a perception of Jewish people as greedy (as often used in [[Stereotypes_of_Jews#Greed|stereotypes of Jews]]), and this perception has probably evolved in Europe during Medieval times where a large portion of [[Moneylender|money lending]] was operated by Jews.
sentence_366: Factors contributing to this situation included that Jews were restricted from other professions, while the [[Christian_Church|Christian Church]] declared for their followers that money lending constituted immoral "[[Usury|usury]]".
sentence_367: [[Education|Education]] plays an important role in addressing and overcoming [[Prejudice|prejudice]] and countering social [[Discrimination|discrimination]].
sentence_368: However, education is not only about challenging the conditions of intolerance and ignorance in which anti-Semitism manifests itself; it is also about building a sense of [[Global_citizenship_education|global citizenship]] and solidarity, respect for, and enjoyment of diversity and the ability to live peacefully together as active, democratic citizens.
sentence_369: Education equips learners with the [[Knowledge|knowledge]] to identify anti-Semitism and biased or prejudiced messages, and raises awareness about the forms, manifestations and impact of anti-Semitism faced by [[Jews|Jews]] and Jewish communities.
sentence_370: Main article: Geography of antisemitism
sentence_371: A March 2008 report by the [[United_States_Department_of_State|U.S.
sentence_372: State Department]] found that there was an increase in antisemitism across the world, and that both old and new expressions of antisemitism persist.
sentence_373: A 2012 report by the U.S. [[Bureau_of_Democracy,_Human_Rights_and_Labor|Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labor]] also noted a continued global increase in antisemitism, and found that Holocaust denial and opposition to Israeli policy at times was used to promote or justify blatant antisemitism.
sentence_374: In 2014, the ADL conducted a study titled "", which also reported high antisemitism figures around the world and, among other findings, that as many as "27% of people who have never met a Jew nevertheless harbor strong prejudices against him".
sentence_375: Their study also showed that 75% of Muslims in the Middle East and North Africa held antisemitic views.
sentence_376: See also: Antisemitism in Africa
sentence_377: In 2019, deputy justice minister Jean de Dieu Momo advanced an [[Antisemitic_canard|antisemitic canard]] during prime time on [[Cameroon_Radio_Television|Cameroon Radio Television]], and suggested that Jewish people had brought the [[Holocaust|holocaust]] upon themselves.
sentence_378: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Algeria|History of the Jews in Algeria]]
sentence_379: Almost all Jews in [[Algeria|Algeria]] left upon independence in 1962.
sentence_380: Algeria's 140,000 Jews had French citizenship since 1870 (briefly revoked by Vichy France in 1940), and they mainly went to [[France|France]], with some going to [[Israel|Israel]].
sentence_381: In [[Egypt|Egypt]], Dar al-Fadhilah published a translation of [[Henry_Ford|Henry Ford]]'s antisemitic treatise, [[The_International_Jew|The International Jew]], complete with distinctly antisemitic imagery on the cover.
sentence_382: On 5 May 2001, after [[Shimon_Peres|Shimon Peres]] visited [[Egypt|Egypt]], the Egyptian [[Al_Akhbar_(Egypt)|al-Akhbar]] internet paper said that "lies and deceit are not foreign to Jews[...].
sentence_383: For this reason, Allah changed their shape and made them into monkeys and pigs."
sentence_384: In July 2012, Egypt's Al Nahar channel fooled actors into thinking they were on an Israeli television show and filmed their reactions to being told it was an Israeli television show.
sentence_385: In response, some of the actors launched into antisemitic rants or dialogue, and many became violent.
sentence_386: Actress Mayer El Beblawi said that "Allah did not curse the worm and moth as much as he cursed the Jews" while actor Mahmoud Abdel Ghaffar launched into a violent rage and said, "You brought me someone who looks like a Jew...
sentence_387: I hate the Jews to death" after finding out it was a prank.
sentence_388: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Libya|History of the Jews in Libya]]
sentence_389: [[Libya|Libya]] once had one of the oldest Jewish communities in the world, dating back to 300 BCE.
sentence_390: Despite the repression of Jews in the late 1930s, as a result of the pro-Nazi Fascist Italian regime, Jews were a third of the population of [[Tripoli|Libya]] till 1941.
sentence_391: In 1942 the Nazi German troops occupied the Jewish quarter of Benghazi, plundering shops and deporting more than 2,000 Jews across the desert.
sentence_392: Sent to work in labor camps, more than one-fifth of this group of Jews perished.
sentence_393: A series of pogroms started in November 1945, while more than 140 Jews were killed in [[Tripoli|Tripoli]] and most synagogues in the city looted.
sentence_394: Upon Libya's independence in 1951, most of the Jewish community emigrated from Libya.
sentence_395: After the [[Suez_Crisis|Suez Crisis]] in 1956, another series of pogroms forced all but about 100 Jews to flee.
sentence_396: When [[Muammar_al-Gaddafi|Muammar al-Gaddafi]] came to power in 1969, all remaining Jewish property was confiscated and all debts to Jews canceled.
sentence_397: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Morocco|History of the Jews in Morocco]]
sentence_398: [[Jew|Jewish]] communities, in [[Islam|Islamic]] times often living in [[Ghetto|ghettos]] known as [[Mellah|mellah]], have existed in [[Morocco|Morocco]] for at least 2,000 years.
sentence_399: Intermittent large scale massacres (such as that of [[1033_Fez_massacre|6,000 Jews in Fez]] in 1033, over 100,000 Jews in Fez and [[Marrakesh|Marrakesh]] in 1146 and again in Marrakesh in 1232) were accompanied by systematic discrimination through the years.
sentence_400: In 1875, 20 Jews were killed by a mob in [[Demnat|Demnat]], Morocco; elsewhere in Morocco, Jews were attacked and killed in the streets in broad daylight.
sentence_401: While the pro-Nazi [[Vichy_France|Vichy]] regime during [[World_War_II|World War II]] passed discriminatory laws against Jews, [[Mohammed_V_of_Morocco|King Muhammad]] prevented deportation of Jews to death camps (although Jews with French, as opposed to Moroccan, citizenship, being directly subject to Vichy law, were still deported.)
sentence_402: In 1948, approximately 265,000 Jews lived in Morocco.
sentence_403: Between 5,000 and 8,000 live there now.
sentence_404: In June 1948, soon after [[Israel|Israel]] was established and in the midst of the first Arab-Israeli war, riots against Jews broke out in [[Oujda|Oujda]] and [[Djerada|Djerada]], killing 44 Jews.
sentence_405: In 1948–9, 18,000 Jews left the country for Israel.
sentence_406: After this, Jewish emigration continued (to Israel and elsewhere), but slowed to a few thousand per year.
sentence_407: Through the early fifties, [[Zionism|Zionist]] organizations encouraged emigration, particularly in the poorer south of the country, seeing Moroccan Jews as valuable contributors to the Jewish State.
sentence_408: In 1955, Morocco attained independence and emigration to Israel had increased further until 1956.
sentence_409: Then it was prohibited until 1963, when it resumed.
sentence_410: By 1967, only 60,000 Jews remained in Morocco.
sentence_411: The [[Six-Day_War|Six-Day War]] in 1967 led to increased Arab-Jewish tensions worldwide, including Morocco.
sentence_412: By 1971, the Jewish population was down to 35,000; however, most of this wave of emigration went to [[Europe|Europe]] and [[North_America|North America]] rather than [[Israel|Israel]].
sentence_413: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Tunisia|History of the Jews in Tunisia]]
sentence_414: Jews have lived in Tunisia for at least 2,300 years.
sentence_415: In the 13th century, Jews were expelled from their homes in [[Kairouan|Kairouan]] and were ultimately restricted to ghettos, known as hara.
sentence_416: Forced to wear distinctive clothing, several Jews earned high positions in the Tunisian government.
sentence_417: Several prominent international traders were Tunisian Jews.
sentence_418: From 1855 to 1864, [[Muhammad_Bey|Muhammad Bey]] relaxed dhimmi laws, but reinstated them in the face of anti-Jewish riots that continued at least until 1869.
sentence_419: Tunisia, as the only Middle Eastern country under direct [[Nazism|Nazi]] control during World War II, was also the site of racist antisemitic measures activities such as the yellow star, prison camps, deportations, and other persecution.
sentence_420: In 1948, approximately 105,000 Jews lived in [[Tunisia|Tunisia]].
sentence_421: Only about 1,500 remain there today.
sentence_422: Following Tunisia's independence from France in 1956, a number of anti-Jewish policies led to emigration, of which half went to Israel and the other half to France.
sentence_423: After attacks in 1967, Jewish emigration both to Israel and [[France|France]] accelerated.
sentence_424: There were also attacks in 1982, 1985, and most recently in 2002 when a suicide bombing in Djerba took 21 lives (most of them German tourists) near the local synagogue, in a terrorist attack claimed by [[Al-Qaeda|Al-Qaeda]].
sentence_425: In modern-day Tunisia, there have been many instances of antisemitic acts and statements.
sentence_426: Since the government is not quick to condemn them, antisemitism spreads throughout Tunisian society.
sentence_427: Following the Ben Ali regime, there have been an increasing number of public offenses against Jews in Tunisia.
sentence_428: For example, in February 2012, when Egyptian cleric Wagdi Ghanaim entered Tunisia, he was welcomed by Islamists who chanted "Death to the Jews" as a sign of their support.
sentence_429: The following month, during protests in Tunis, a Salafi sheik told young Tunisians to gather and learn to kill Jews.
sentence_430: In the past, The Tunisian government has made efforts to block Jews from entering high positions, and some moderate members have tried to cover up the more extremist antisemitic efforts by appointing Jews to governmental positions.
sentence_431: However, it is known that Muslim clerics believe that if the Muslim Brotherhood leads the regime, that will enhance their hatred towards Jews.
sentence_432: In response to the prevalent antisemitism, the Tunisian government has publicly protected the dwindling population and its marks of Jewish culture, for example synagogues, and advised them to settle in Djerba, a French tourist attraction.
sentence_433: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_South_Africa|History of the Jews in South Africa]]
sentence_434: Antisemitism has been present in the history of [[South_Africa|South Africa]] since Europeans first set foot ashore on the [[Cape_Peninsula|Cape Peninsula]].
sentence_435: In the years 1652–1795 Jews were not allowed to settle at the Cape.
sentence_436: An 1868 Act would sanction religious discrimination.
sentence_437: Antisemitism reached its apotheosis in the years leading up to [[World_War_II|World War II]].
sentence_438: Inspired by the rise of [[National_socialism|national socialism]] in [[Germany|Germany]] the [[Ossewabrandwag|Ossewabrandwag]] (OB) – whose membership accounted for almost 25% of the 1940 [[Afrikaner|Afrikaner]] population – and the National Party faction New Order would champion a more programmatic solution to the 'Jewish problem'.
sentence_439: Main article: [[Antisemitism_in_Japan|Antisemitism in Japan]]
sentence_440: The Japanese first learned about antisemitism in 1918, during the cooperation of the [[Imperial_Japanese_Army|Imperial Japanese Army]] with the [[White_movement|White movement]] in [[Siberia|Siberia]].
sentence_441: [[White_Army#Structure|White Army]] soldiers had been issued copies of The Protocols of the Elders of Zion, and "The Protocols continue to be used as evidence of Jewish conspiracies even though they are widely acknowledged to be a forgery.
sentence_442: During [[World_War_II|World War II]], [[Nazi_Germany|Nazi Germany]] encouraged Japan to adopt antisemitic policies.
sentence_443: In the post-war period, [[Extremism|extremist groups]] and [[Ideologues|ideologues]] have promoted [[Conspiracy_theories|conspiracy theories]].
sentence_444: See also: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Pakistan|History of the Jews in Pakistan]] and [[Antisemitism_in_Pakistan|Antisemitism in Pakistan]]
sentence_445: The U.S. State Department's first Report on Global Anti-Semitism mentioned a strong feeling of antisemitism in [[Pakistan|Pakistan]].
sentence_446: In Pakistan, a country without Jewish communities, antisemitic sentiment fanned by antisemitic articles in the press is widespread.
sentence_447: In Pakistan, Jews are often regarded as miserly.
sentence_448: After Israel's independence in 1948, violent incidents occurred against Pakistan's small Jewish community of about 2,000 [[Bene_Israel|Bene Israel]] Jews.
sentence_449: The [[Magain_Shalome_Synagogue|Magain Shalome Synagogue]] in Karachi was attacked, as were individual Jews.
sentence_450: The persecution of Jews resulted in their exodus via India to Israel (see [[Pakistanis_in_Israel|Pakistanis in Israel]]), the UK, Canada and other countries.
sentence_451: The [[Peshawar|Peshawar]] Jewish community ceased to exist although a small community reportedly still exists in [[Karachi|Karachi]].
sentence_452: A substantial number of people in Pakistan believe that the [[September_11_attacks|September 11 attacks]] on the World Trade Center in New York were a secret Jewish conspiracy organized by Israel's [[MOSSAD|MOSSAD]], as were the [[7_July_2005_London_bombings|7 July 2005 London bombings]], allegedly perpetrated by Jews in order to discredit Muslims.
sentence_453: Pakistani [[Political_commentator|political commentator]] [[Zaid_Hamid|Zaid Hamid]] claimed that Indian Jews perpetrated the [[2008_Mumbai_attacks|2008 Mumbai attacks]].
sentence_454: Such allegations echo traditional antisemitic theories.
sentence_455: The Jewish religious movement of [[Chabad_Lubavich|Chabad Lubavich]] had a [[Nariman_House|mission house]] in [[Mumbai|Mumbai]], [[India|India]] that was attacked in the [[2008_Mumbai_attacks|2008 Mumbai attacks]], perpetrated by militants connected to Pakistan led by [[Ajmal_Kasab|Ajmal Kasab]], a Pakistani national.
sentence_456: [[Antisemitic|Antisemitic]] intents were evident from the testimonies of Kasab following his arrest and trial.
sentence_457: See also: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Malaysia|History of the Jews in Malaysia]]
sentence_458: Although [[Malaysia|Malaysia]] presently has no substantial Jewish population, the country has reportedly become an example of a phenomenon called "antisemitism without Jews."
sentence_459: In his treatise on Malay identity, "The Malay Dilemma," which was published in 1970, Malaysian Prime Minister [[Mahathir_Mohamad|Mahathir Mohamad]] wrote: "The Jews are not only hooked-nosed... but understand money instinctively.... Jewish stinginess and financial wizardry gained them the economic control of Europe and provoked antisemitism which waxed and waned throughout Europe through the ages."
sentence_460: The Malay-language [[Utusan_Malaysia|Utusan Malaysia]] daily stated in an editorial that Malaysians "cannot allow anyone, especially the Jews, to interfere secretly in this country's business...
sentence_461: When the drums are pounded hard in the name of human rights, the pro-Jewish people will have their best opportunity to interfere in any Islamic country," the newspaper said.
sentence_462: "We might not realize that the enthusiasm to support actions such as demonstrations will cause us to help foreign groups succeed in their mission of controlling this country."
sentence_463: Prime Minister [[Najib_Razak|Najib Razak]]'s office subsequently issued a statement late Monday saying Utusan's claim did "not reflect the views of the government."
sentence_464: [[Indonesian_Jews|Indonesian Jews]] face anti-Jewish discrimination.
sentence_465: See also: [[Holocaust_denial#Iran|Holocaust denial § Iran]]
sentence_466: [[Mahmoud_Ahmadinejad|Mahmoud Ahmadinejad]], former president of Iran, has frequently been accused of denying the Holocaust.
sentence_467: [[Ali_Khamenei|Ali Khamenei]], the supreme leader of Iran, has repeatedly doubted the validity of the reported casualties of the Holocaust.
sentence_468: In one meeting he claimed that the Zionists have had "close relations" with the Nazi leaders and that "providing exaggerated statistics [of the Holocaust] has been a method to justify the Zionists' cruel treatment of the Palestinians".
sentence_469: In July 2012, the winner of Iran's first annual International [[Wall_Street|Wall Street]] Downfall Cartoon Festival, jointly sponsored by the semi-state-run Iranian media outlet [[Fars_News|Fars News]], was an antisemitic cartoon depicting Jews praying before the [[New_York_Stock_Exchange|New York Stock Exchange]], which is made to look like the [[Western_Wall|Western Wall]].
sentence_470: Other cartoons in the contest were antisemitic as well.
sentence_471: The national director of the [[Anti-Defamation_League|Anti-Defamation League]], [[Abraham_Foxman|Abraham Foxman]], condemned the cartoon, stating that "Here's the anti-Semitic notion of Jews and their love for money, the canard that Jews 'control' Wall Street, and a cynical perversion of the Western Wall, the holiest site in Judaism," and "Once again Iran takes the prize for promoting antisemitism."
sentence_472: [[Anti-Defamation_League|ADL]]/Global 100 reported in 2014 that 56% of Iranians hold antisemitic beliefs, and 18% of them agreed that Jews probably talk too much about [[The_Holocaust|the Holocaust]].
sentence_473: However, the reported results (56%) were reported to be the lowest in the Middle East.
sentence_474: [[Iranian_Jews|Iranian Jews]] along with Christians and Zoroastrians are protected under the Constitution and have seats reserved for them in the Iranian Parliament, However, de facto harassment still occurs.
sentence_475: In 2004, [[Al-Manar|Al-Manar]], a media network affiliated with [[Hezbollah|Hezbollah]], aired a drama series, The Diaspora, which observers allege is based on historical antisemitic allegations.
sentence_476: [[BBC|BBC]] correspondents who have watched the program says it quotes extensively from the Protocols of the Elders of Zion.
sentence_477: See also: [[Tomorrow's_Pioneers|Tomorrow's Pioneers]], [[Racism_in_the_Palestinian_territories|Racism in the Palestinian territories]], and [[Textbooks_in_the_Israeli–Palestinian_conflict|Textbooks in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
sentence_478: In March 2011, the Israeli government issued a paper claiming that "Anti-Israel and anti-Semitic messages are heard regularly in the government and private media and in the mosques and are taught in school books," to the extent that they are "an integral part of the fabric of life inside the PA." In August 2012, Israeli Strategic Affairs Ministry director-general Yossi Kuperwasser stated that Palestinian incitement to antisemitism is "going on all the time" and that it is "worrying and disturbing."
sentence_479: At an institutional level, he said the PA has been promoting three key messages to the Palestinian people that constitute incitement: "that the Palestinians would eventually be the sole sovereign on all the land from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea; that Jews, especially those who live in Israel, were not really human beings but rather 'the scum of mankind'; and that all tools were legitimate in the struggle against Israel and the Jews."
sentence_480: In August 2014, the [[Hamas|Hamas]]' spokesman in Doha said on live television that [[Blood_libel|Jews use blood to make matzos]].
sentence_481: Main articles: [[Antisemitism_in_Saudi_Arabia|Antisemitism in Saudi Arabia]] and [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Saudi_Arabia|History of the Jews in Saudi Arabia]]
sentence_482: [[Saudi-Arabian_textbook_controversy|Saudi textbooks]] vilify Jews, call Jews apes; demand that students avoid and not befriend Jews; claim that Jews worship the devil; and encourage Muslims to engage in [[Jihad|Jihad]] to vanquish Jews.
sentence_483: Saudi Arabian government officials and state religious leaders often promote the idea that Jews are conspiring to take over the entire world; as proof of their claims they publish and frequently cite The Protocols of the Elders of Zion as factual.
sentence_484: In 2004, the official Saudi Arabia tourism website said that Jews and holders of Israeli passports would not be issued visas to enter the country.
sentence_485: After an uproar, the restriction against Jews was removed from the website although the ban against Israeli passport-holders remained.
sentence_486: In late 2014, a Saudi newspaper reported that foreign workers of most religions, including Judaism, were welcome in the kingdom, but Israeli citizens were not.
sentence_487: Main articles: [[Antisemitism_in_Turkey|Antisemitism in Turkey]] and [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Turkey|History of the Jews in Turkey]]
sentence_488: In 2003, the [[Neve_Shalom_Synagogue|Neve Shalom Synagogue]] was targeted in a car bombing, killing 21 Turkish Muslims and 6 Jews.
sentence_489: In June 2011, the Economist suggested that "The best way for Turks to promote democracy would be to vote against the ruling party".
sentence_490: Not long after, the Turkish Prime Minister, [[Recep_Tayyip_Erdoğan|Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]], said that "The International media, as they are supported by Israel, would not be happy with the continuation of the AKP government".
sentence_491: The Hurriyet Daily News quoted Erdoğan at the time as claiming "The Economist is part of an Israeli conspiracy that aims to topple the Turkish government".
sentence_492: Moreover, during Erdogan's tenure, Hitler's [[Mein_Kampf|Mein Kampf]] has once again become a best selling book in Turkey.
sentence_493: Prime Minister Erdogan called antisemitism a "crime against humanity."
sentence_494: He also said that "as a minority, they're our citizens.
sentence_495: Both their security and the right to observe their faith are under our guarantee."
sentence_496: While Erdoğan declared being against antisemitism, he has been accused of invoking [[Antisemitic_canard|antisemitic stereotypes]] in public statements.
sentence_497: Main articles: [[Antisemitism_in_Europe|Antisemitism in Europe]] and [[New_antisemitism|New antisemitism]]
sentence_498: According to a 2004 report from the Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs, antisemitism had increased significantly in Europe since 2000, with significant increases in verbal attacks against Jews and vandalism such as graffiti, fire bombings of Jewish schools, desecration of synagogues and cemeteries.
sentence_499: Germany, France, Britain, and Russia are the countries with the highest rate of antisemitic incidents in Europe.
sentence_500: The Netherlands and Sweden have also consistently had high rates of antisemitic attacks since 2000.
sentence_501: Some claim that recent European antisemitic violence can actually be seen as a spillover from the long running [[Arab–Israeli_conflict|Arab-Israeli conflict]] since the majority of the perpetrators are from the [[Islam_in_Europe|large Muslim immigrant communities in European cities]].
sentence_502: However, compared to France, the United Kingdom and much of the rest of Europe, in Germany Arab and pro-Palestinian groups are involved in only a small percentage of antisemitic incidents.
sentence_503: According to The Stephen Roth Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism and Racism, most of the more extreme attacks on Jewish sites and physical attacks on Jews in Europe come from militant Islamic and Muslim groups, and most Jews tend to be assaulted in countries where groups of young Muslim immigrants reside.
sentence_504: On 1 January 2006, Britain's chief rabbi, Lord [[Jonathan_Sacks|Jonathan Sacks]], warned that what he called a "tsunami of antisemitism" was spreading globally.
sentence_505: In an interview with [[BBC_Radio_4|BBC Radio 4]], Sacks said: "A number of my rabbinical colleagues throughout Europe have been assaulted and attacked on the streets.
sentence_506: We've had synagogues desecrated.
sentence_507: We've had Jewish schools burnt to the ground—not here but in France.
sentence_508: People are attempting to silence and even ban Jewish societies on campuses on the grounds that Jews must support the state of Israel, therefore they should be banned, which is quite extraordinary because... British Jews see themselves as British citizens.
sentence_509: So it's that kind of feeling that you don't know what's going to happen next that's making... some European Jewish communities uncomfortable."
sentence_510: Following an escalation in antisemitism in 2012, which included the [[Toulouse_and_Montauban_shootings|deadly shooting of three children]] at a Jewish school in France, the European Jewish Congress demanded in July a more proactive response.
sentence_511: EJC President Moshe Kantor explained, "We call on authorities to take a more proactive approach so there would be no reason for statements of regret and denunciation.
sentence_512: All these smaller attacks remind me of smaller tremors before a massive earthquake.
sentence_513: The Jewish community cannot afford to be subject to an earthquake and the authorities cannot say that the writing was not on the wall."
sentence_514: He added that European countries should take legislative efforts to ban any form of , as well as to equip the authorities with the necessary tools to confront any attempt to expand [[Terrorist|terrorist]] and violent activities against Jewish communities in Europe.
sentence_516: Despite a dwindling number of Jews living in Belarus, antisemitism is still manifested, including defacing Holocaust monuments, and Nazi and racist graffiti, which are tolerated by many Belarusians and authorities.
sentence_517: There are a number of reports about antisemitic attitudes of Belarusian authorities, including President [[Alexander_Lukashenka|Alexander Lukashenka]], see "[[Antisemitism_in_Belarus|Antisemitism in Belarus]]" for details.
sentence_518: In 2005 Yakov Basin, vice president of the Union of Jewish Organizations and Communities of Belarus reported that the authorities " turning a blind eye to blatant expressions of anti-Semitism among officials, writers and the dominant [[Russian_Orthodox_Church|Russian Orthodox Church]]".
sentence_519: He also reported about openly anti-Semitic books published by the Church.
sentence_520: Still, Belarusian Jews do not generally feel threatened.
sentence_522: In the 21st century, antisemitism in Hungary has evolved and received an institutional framework, while verbal and physical aggression against Jews has escalated, creating a great difference between its earlier manifestations in the 1990s and recent developments.
sentence_523: One of the major representatives of this institutionalized antisemitic ideology is the popular Hungarian party [[Jobbik|Jobbik]], which received 17 percent of the vote in the April 2010 national election.
sentence_524: The far-right subculture, which ranges from nationalist shops to radical-nationalist and neo-Nazi festivals and events, plays a major role in the institutionalization of Hungarian antisemitism in the 21st century.
sentence_525: The contemporary antisemitic rhetoric has been updated and expanded, but is still based on the old antisemitic notions.
sentence_526: The traditional accusations and motifs include such phrases as Jewish occupation, international Jewish conspiracy, Jewish responsibility for the [[Treaty_of_Trianon|Treaty of Trianon]], Judeo-Bolshevism, as well as blood libels against Jews.
sentence_527: Nevertheless, the past few years have seen the reemergence of the blood libel and an increase in Holocaust relativization and denial, while the monetary crisis has revived references to the "Jewish banker class".
sentence_528: The [[University_of_Warsaw|University of Warsaw]]'s study in 2016 found that 37% of surveyed Poles expressed negative attitudes towards Jews (up from 32% in 2015); 56% said that they wouldn't accept a Jew in their family (up from 46%); and 32% wouldn't want Jewish neighbors (up from 27%).
sentence_529: In November 2015, following Antoni Macierewicz's (Law and Justice party) designation as Minister of National Defence, he faced allegations of antisemitism and protests by the [[Anti_Defamation_League|Anti Defamation League]].
sentence_530: In February 2018, the Polish Prime Minister [[Mateusz_Morawiecki|Mateusz Morawiecki]] stated that "there were Jewish perpetrators" of the [[Holocaust|Holocaust]], "not only German perpetrators."
sentence_531: [[Ronald_Lauder|Ronald Lauder]], the president of the [[World_Jewish_Congress|World Jewish Congress]], condemned Morawiecki's words: "This is nothing short of an attempt to falsify history, that is one of the very worst forms of anti-Semitism and Holocaust obfuscation."
sentence_532: Israeli politician [[Yair_Lapid|Yair Lapid]], head of the centrist [[Yesh_Atid|Yesh Atid]] party, said Morawiecki's remark is "anti-Semitism of the oldest kind."
sentence_534: Since the early 2000s, levels of antisemitism in Russia have been low, and steadily decreasing.
sentence_535: President of the Russian Jewish Congress attributes this in part to the vanished state sponsorship of antisemitism.
sentence_536: At the same time experts warn that worsening economic conditions may lead to the surge of [[Xenophobia|xenophobia]] and antisemitism in particular.
sentence_537: The 2019 [[Pew_Research_Center|Pew Research]] poll found that 18% of Russians held unfavorable views of Jews.
sentence_539: [[Oleh_Tyahnybok|Oleh Tyahnybok]], the leader of the far-right [[Svoboda_(political_party)|Svoboda]] party, whose members hold senior positions in [[Cabinet_of_Ukraine|Ukraine's government]], urged his party to fight "the Moscow-Jewish mafia ruling Ukraine."
sentence_540: The Algemeiner Journal reported: "Svoboda supporters include among their heroes leaders of pro-Nazi World War II organizations known for their [[The_Holocaust_in_Ukraine|atrocities against Jews]] and [[Massacres_of_Poles_in_Volhynia_and_Eastern_Galicia|Poles]], such as the [[Organization_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists|Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists]] (OUN), the [[Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army|Ukrainian Insurgent Army]] (UPA), and the [[14th_Waffen_Grenadier_Division_of_the_SS_(1st_Ukrainian)|14th Waffen-SS Galicia Division]]".
sentence_541: According to [[The_Simon_Wiesenthal_Center|The Simon Wiesenthal Center]] (in January 2011) "Ukraine has, to the best of our knowledge, never conducted a single investigation of a local Nazi war criminal, let alone prosecuted a Holocaust perpetrator."
sentence_542: According to Der Spiegel, [[Dmytro_Yarosh|Dmytro Yarosh]], leader of the far-right [[Right_Sector|Right Sector]], wrote: "I wonder how it came to pass that most of the billionaires in Ukraine are Jews?"
sentence_543: Late February 2014 Yarosh pledged during a meeting with [[Israel|Israel]]'s ambassador in [[Kyiv|Kyiv]] to fight all forms of racism.
sentence_544: Right Sector's leader for West Ukraine, [[Oleksandr_Muzychko|Oleksandr Muzychko]], has talked about fighting "communists, Jews and Russians for as long as blood flows in my veins."
sentence_545: Muzychko was shot dead on 24 March 2014.
sentence_546: An official inquiry concluded he had shot himself in the heart at the end of a chase with the [[Ukrainian_police|Ukrainian police]].
sentence_547: In April 2014, [[Donetsk|Donetsk]] Chief Rabbi Pinchas Vishedski said that "Anti-Semitic incidents in the Russian-speaking east were rare, unlike in [[Kyiv|Kyiv]] and western Ukraine."
sentence_548: In an April 2014 article about anti-Jewish violence in Ukraine in [[Haaretz|Haaretz]] no incidents outside this "Russian-speaking east" were mentioned.
sentence_549: According to the Israel's Ambassador to Ukraine, the antisemitism occurs here much less frequently than in other European countries, and has more a hooligan's nature rather than a system.
sentence_550: In March 2017, Ukrainian politician [[Nadiya_Savchenko|Nadiya Savchenko]] said during a television interview that Jews held disproportionate control over Ukraine.
sentence_551: In May 2017, the [[Security_Service_of_Ukraine|Security Service of Ukraine]] (SBU) senior officer Vasily Vovk wrote that Jews "aren't Ukrainians and I will destroy you along with [Ukrainian oligarch and Jewish lawmaker Vadim] [[Vadim_Rabinovich|Rabinovych]].
sentence_552: I'm telling you one more time - go to hell, zhidi [kikes], the Ukrainian people have had it to here with you.
sentence_553: Ukraine must be governed by Ukrainians."
sentence_554: The antisemitism report for 2017 that Israel's [[Ministry_of_Diaspora_Affairs|Ministry of Diaspora Affairs]] under [[Naftali_Bennett|Naftali Bennett]] published in January 2018 stated that "A striking exception in the trend of decrease in antisemitic incidents in Eastern Europe was Ukraine, where the number of recorded antisemitic attacks was doubled from last year and surpassed the tally for all the incidents reported throughout the entire region combined.
sentence_557: There have been some antisemitic crimes reported in the last decade among Finns; the most common types include [[Defamation|defamation]], [[Criminal_threatening|verbal threats]], and [[Property_damage|damage to property]].
sentence_559: In 2010, the [[Norwegian_Broadcasting_Corporation|Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation]] after one year of research, revealed that antisemitism was common among some 8th, 9th, and 10th graders in Oslo's schools.
sentence_560: Teachers at schools with large numbers of [[Muslim|Muslims]] revealed that Muslim students often "praise or admire Adolf Hitler for his killing of [[Jew|Jews]]", that "Jew-hate is legitimate within vast groups of Muslim students" and that "Muslims laugh or command [teachers] to stop when trying to educate about the [[Holocaust|Holocaust]]".
sentence_561: Additionally, "while some students might protest when some express support for [[Terrorism|terrorism]], none object when students express hate of Jews", saying that it says in "the [[Quran|Quran]] that you shall kill Jews, all true Muslims hate Jews".
sentence_562: Most of these students were said to be born and raised in Norway.
sentence_563: One [[Jew|Jewish]] father also stated that his child had been taken by a Muslim mob after school (though the child managed to escape), reportedly "to be taken out to the forest and [[Lynching|hung]] because he was a Jew".
sentence_564: Norwegian Education Minister Kristin Halvorsen referred to the antisemitism reported in this study as being "completely unacceptable."
sentence_565: The head of a local Islamic council joined Jewish leaders and Halvorsen in denouncing such antisemitism.
sentence_566: In October 2012, the [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-Operation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Co-Operation in Europe]] issued a report regarding antisemitism in Norway, criticizing Norway for an increase in antisemitism in the country and blaming Norwegian officials for failing to address antisemitism."
sentence_568: After Germany and Austria, Sweden has the highest rate of antisemitic incidents in Europe, though the Netherlands has reported a higher rate of antisemitism in some years.
sentence_569: A government study in 2006 estimated that 15% of Swedes agree with the statement: "The Jews have too much influence in the world today".
sentence_570: 5% of the total adult population and 39% of adult Muslims "harbour systematic antisemitic views".
sentence_571: The former prime minister [[Göran_Persson|Göran Persson]] described these results as "surprising and terrifying".
sentence_572: However, the rabbi of Stockholm's Orthodox Jewish community, Meir Horden, said that "It's not true to say that the Swedes are anti-Semitic.
sentence_573: Some of them are hostile to Israel because they support the weak side, which they perceive the [[Palestinian_people|Palestinians]] to be."
sentence_574: In 2009, a synagogue that served the Jewish community in Malmö was set ablaze.
sentence_575: Jewish cemeteries were repeatedly desecrated, worshippers were abused while returning home from prayer, and masked men mockingly chanted "Hitler" in the streets.
sentence_576: As a result of security concerns, Malmö's synagogue has guards and rocket-proof glass in the windows, and the Jewish kindergarten can only be reached through thick steel security doors.
sentence_577: In early 2010, the Swedish publication The Local published series of articles about the growing antisemitism in [[Malmö,_Sweden|Malmö, Sweden]].
sentence_578: In 2009, the Malmö police received reports of 79 antisemitic incidents, which was twice the number of the previous year (2008).
sentence_579: Fredrik Sieradzki, spokesman for the Malmö Jewish community, estimated that the already small Jewish population is shrinking by 5% a year.
sentence_580: "Malmö is a place to move away from," he said, citing antisemitism as the primary reason.
sentence_581: In March 2010, Fredrik Sieradzk told Die Presse, an Austrian Internet publication, that Jews are being "harassed and physically attacked" by "people from the Middle East," although he added that only a small number of Malmö's 40,000 Muslims "exhibit hatred of Jews."
sentence_582: In October 2010, The Forward reported on the current state of Jews and the level of antisemitism in Sweden.
sentence_583: Henrik Bachner, a writer and professor of history at the University of Lund, claimed that members of the Swedish Parliament have attended anti-Israel rallies where the Israeli flag was burned while the flags of Hamas and Hezbollah were waved, and the rhetoric was often antisemitic—not just anti-Israel.
sentence_584: Judith Popinski, an 86-year-old Holocaust survivor, stated that she is no longer invited to schools that have a large Muslim presence to tell her story of surviving the Holocaust.
sentence_585: In December 2010, the [[Jews|Jewish]] [[Human_rights|human rights]] organization [[Simon_Wiesenthal_Center|Simon Wiesenthal Center]] issued a travel advisory concerning Sweden, advising Jews to express "extreme caution" when visiting the southern parts of the country due to an alleged increase in verbal and physical harassment of Jewish citizens in the city of [[Malmö|Malmö]].
sentence_586: [[Ilmar_Reepalu|Ilmar Reepalu]], the mayor of Malmö for over 15 years, has been accused of failing to protect the Jewish community in Malmö, causing 30 Jewish families to leave the city in 2010, and more preparing to leave, which has left the possibility that Malmö's Jewish community will disappear soon.
sentence_587: Critics of Reepalu say that his statements, such as antisemitism in Malmö actually being an "understandable" consequence of Israeli policy in the Middle East, have encouraged young Muslims to abuse and harass the Jewish community.
sentence_588: In an interview with the Sunday Telegraph in February 2010, Reepalu said, "There haven't been any attacks on Jewish people, and if Jews from the city want to move to Israel that is not a matter for Malmö," which renewed concerns about Reepalu.
sentence_590: Antisemitism in Greece manifests itself in religious, political and media discourse.
sentence_591: The recent [[Greek_government-debt_crisis|Greek government-debt crisis]] has facilitated the rise of far right groups in Greece, most notably the formerly obscure [[Golden_Dawn_(Greece)|Golden Dawn]].
sentence_592: Jews have lived in Greece since antiquity, but the largest community of around 20,000 [[Sephardic_Jews|Sephardic Jews]] settled in [[Thessalonica|Thessalonica]] after an invitation from the [[Ottoman_Sultan|Ottoman Sultan]] in the 15th century.
sentence_593: After Thessalonica was annexed to Greece in 1913, the Greek government recognized Jews as Greek citizens with full rights and attributed Judaism the status of a recognized and protected religion.
sentence_594: Currently in Greece, Jewish communities representing the 5,000 Greek Jews are legal entities under public law.
sentence_595: According to the [[Anti-Defamation_League|ADL]] (Anti-Defamation League) report of 2015, the "ADL Global 100", a report of the status of antisemitism in 100 countries around the world, 69% of the adult population in Greece harbor antisemitic attitudes and 85% think that "Jews have too much power in the business world".
sentence_596: In March 2015, a survey about the Greeks' perceptions of the holocaust was published.
sentence_597: Its findings showed that less than 60 percent of the respondents think that holocaust teaching should be included in the curriculum.
sentence_599: The ongoing political conflict between Israel and Palestine has played an important role in the development and expression of [[Antisemitism_in_the_21st_century|antisemitism in the 21st century]], and in Italy as well.
sentence_600: The [[Second_Intifada|Second Intifada]], which began in late September 2000, has set in motion unexpected mechanisms, whereby traditional anti-Jewish prejudices were mixed with politically based stereotypes.
sentence_601: In this belief system, Israeli Jews were charged with full responsibility for the fate of the peace process and with the conflict presented as embodying the struggle between good (the Palestinians) and evil (the Israeli Jews).
sentence_605: In 2016 the Belgium government-funded, Catholic Sint-Jozefs Institute secondary school in [[Torhout|Torhout]] declared that it was "very proud" of a retired teacher who won a prize for his antisemitic cartoon at the [[International_Holocaust_Cartoon_Competition|International Holocaust Cartoon Competition]] in Iran.
sentence_606: Despite a backlash from the Jewish community, the cartoonist was celebrated as a champion of "free speech."
sentence_607: [[Dimitri_Verhulst|Dimitri Verhulst]] claimed in an op-ed in the newspaper [[De_Morgen|De Morgen]] that "being Jewish is not a religion, no God would give creatures such an ugly nose."
sentence_608: He accused the Jews of harbouring a [[Superiority_complex|superiority complex]] due to the notion of [[Jews_as_the_chosen_people|Jews as the chosen people]], and said "talking to the Chosen is difficult" because they unjustly accuse critics of antisemitism.
sentence_609: De Morgen's editor-in-chief defended Verhulst on the basis that the op-ed was "a harsh criticism on Israel's politics towards the Palestinian people."
sentence_610: Main articles: [[Antisemitism_in_21st-century_France|Antisemitism in 21st-century France]] and [[History_of_the_Jews_in_France|History of the Jews in France]]
sentence_611: France is home to the continent's largest Jewish community (about 600,000).
sentence_612: Jewish leaders decry an intensifying antisemitism in France, mainly among Muslims of [[Arab|Arab]] or African heritage, but also growing among [[Caribbean|Caribbean]] islanders from former French colonies.
sentence_613: Former Interior Minister [[Nicolas_Sarkozy|Nicolas Sarkozy]] denounced the killing of [[Ilan_Halimi|Ilan Halimi]] on 13 February 2006 as an antisemitic crime.
sentence_614: Jewish philanthropist Baron [[Eric_de_Rothschild|Eric de Rothschild]] suggests that the extent of antisemitism in France has been exaggerated.
sentence_615: In an interview with [[The_Jerusalem_Post|The Jerusalem Post]] he says that "the one thing you can't say is that France is an anti-Semitic country."
sentence_616: In March 2012, Mohammed Merah [[Toulouse_and_Montauban_shootings|opened fire at a Jewish school]] in Toulouse, killing a teacher and three children.
sentence_617: An 8-year-old girl was shot in the head at point blank range.
sentence_618: President [[Nicolas_Sarkozy|Nicolas Sarkozy]] said that it was "obvious" it was an antisemitic attack and that, "I want to say to all the leaders of the Jewish community, how close we feel to them.
sentence_619: All of France is by their side."
sentence_620: The Israeli Prime Minister condemned the "despicable anti-Semitic" murders.
sentence_621: After a 32-hour siege and standoff with the police outside his house, and a French raid, Merah jumped off a balcony and was shot in the head and killed.
sentence_622: Merah told police during the standoff that he intended to keep on attacking, and he loved death the way the police loved life.
sentence_623: He also claimed connections with al-Qaeda.
sentence_624: 4 months later, in July 2012, a French Jewish teenager wearing a "distinctive religious symbol" was the victim of a violent antisemitic attack on a train travelling between Toulouse and Lyon.
sentence_625: The teen was first verbally harassed and later beaten up by two assailants.
sentence_626: [[Richard_Prasquier|Richard Prasquier]] from the French Jewish umbrella group, [[Conseil_Représentatif_des_Institutions_juives_de_France|CRIF]], called the attack "another development in the worrying trend of anti-Semitism in our country."
sentence_627: Another incident in July 2012 dealt with the vandalism of the synagogue of [[Noisy-le-Grand|Noisy-le-Grand]] of the Seine-Saint-Denis district in [[Paris|Paris]].
sentence_628: The synagogue was vandalized three times in a ten-day period.
sentence_629: Prayer books and shawls were thrown on the floor, windows were shattered, drawers were ransacked, and walls, tables, clocks, and floors were vandalized.
sentence_630: The authorities were alerted of the incidents by the Bureau National de Vigilance Contre L'Antisémtisme (BNVCA), a French antisemitism watchdog group, which called for more measures to be taken to prevent future hate crimes.
sentence_631: BNVCA President Sammy Ghozlan stated that, "Despite the measures taken, things persist, and I think that we need additional legislation, because the Jewish community is annoyed."
sentence_632: In August 2012, [[Abraham_Cooper|Abraham Cooper]], the dean of the [[Simon_Wiesenthal_Center|Simon Wiesenthal Center]], met French Interior Minister [[Manuel_Valls|Manuel Valls]] and reported that antisemitic attacks against French Jews increased by 40% since [[Toulouse_and_Montauban_shootings|Merah's shooting spree]] in [[Toulouse|Toulouse]].
sentence_633: Cooper pressed Valls to take extra measures to secure the safety of French Jews, as well as to discuss strategies to foil an increasing trend of lone-wolf terrorists on the Internet.
sentence_634: Further information: [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Germany|History of the Jews in Germany]]
sentence_635: [[Wolfgang_Schäuble|Wolfgang Schäuble]], the Interior Minister of Germany in 2006, pointed out the official policy of Germany: "We will not tolerate any form of extremism, xenophobia or anti-Semitism."
sentence_636: Although the number of extreme right-wing groups and organisations grew from 141 (2001) to 182 (2006), especially in the formerly communist East Germany, Germany's measures against right-wing groups and antisemitism are effective, despite Germany having the highest rates of antisemitic acts in Europe.
sentence_637: According to the annual reports of the [[Bundesamt_für_Verfassungsschutz|Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution]] the overall number of far-right extremists in Germany dropped during the last years from 49,700 (2001), 45,000 (2002), 41,500 (2003), 40,700 (2004), 39,000 (2005), to 38,600 in 2006.
sentence_638: Germany provided several million euros to fund "nationwide programs aimed at fighting far-right extremism, including teams of traveling consultants, and victims' groups."
sentence_639: In July 2012, two women were assaulted in Germany, sprayed with tear gas, and were shown a "[[Nazi_salute|Hitler salute]]," apparently because of a [[Star_of_David|Star of David]] necklace that they wore.
sentence_640: In late August 2012, [[Berlin|Berlin]] police investigated an attack on a 53-year-old rabbi and his 6-year-old daughter, allegedly by four Arab teens, after which the rabbi needed treatment for head wounds at a hospital.
sentence_641: The police classified the attack as a hate crime.
sentence_642: Jüdische Allgemeine reported that the rabbi was wearing a [[Kippah|kippah]] and was approached by one of the teens, who asked the rabbi if he was Jewish.
sentence_643: The teen then attacked the rabbi while yelling antisemitic comments, and threatened to kill the rabbi's daughter.
sentence_644: Berlin's mayor condemned the attack, saying that "Berlin is an international city in which intolerance, xenophobia and anti-Semitism are not being tolerated.
sentence_645: Police will undertake all efforts to find and arrest the perpetrators."
sentence_646: In October 2012, various historians, including Dr. Julius H. Schoeps, a prominent German-Jewish historian and a member of the German Interior Ministry's commission to combat antisemitism, charged the majority of [[Bundestag|Bundestag]] deputies with failing to understand antisemitism and the imperativeness of periodic legislative reports on German antisemitism.
sentence_647: Schoeps cited various antisemitic statements by German parliament members as well.
sentence_648: The report in question determined that 15% of Germans are antisemitic while over 20% espouse "latent anti-Semitism," but the report has been criticized for downplaying the sharpness of antisemitism in Germany, as well as for failing to examine anti-Israel media coverage in Germany.
sentence_649: Further information: History of the Jews in the Netherlands
sentence_650: The [[Netherlands|Netherlands]] has the second highest incidence of antisemitic incidents in the European Union.
sentence_651: However, it is difficult to obtain exact figures because the specific groups against whom attacks are made are not specifically identified in police reports, and analyses of police data for antisemitism therefore relies on key-word searches, e.g. "Jew" or "Israel".
sentence_652: According to Centre for Information and Documentation on Israel (CIDI), a pro-Israel lobby group in the Netherlands, the number of antisemitic incidents reported in the whole of the Netherlands was 108 in 2008, 93 in 2009, and 124 in 2010.
sentence_653: Some two-thirds of this are acts of aggression.
sentence_655: According to the NRC Handelsblad newspaper, the number of antisemitic incidents in [[Amsterdam|Amsterdam]] was 14 in 2008 and 30 in 2009.
sentence_656: In 2010, Raphaël Evers, an [[Orthodox_judaism|orthodox]] rabbi in [[Amsterdam|Amsterdam]], told the [[Norway|Norwegian]] newspaper [[Aftenposten|Aftenposten]] that Jews can no longer be safe in the city anymore due to the risk of violent assaults.
sentence_657: "We Jews no longer feel at home here in the Netherlands.
sentence_658: Many people talk about moving to Israel," he said.
sentence_659: According to the [[Anne_Frank_Foundation|Anne Frank Foundation]], antisemitism in the Netherlands in 2011 was roughly at the same level as in 2010.
sentence_660: Actual antisemitic incidents increased from 19 in 2010 to 30 in 2011.
sentence_661: Verbal antisemitic incidents dropped slightly from 1173 in 2010 to 1098 in 2011.
sentence_662: This accounts for 75%–80% of all verbal racist incidents in the Netherlands.
sentence_663: Antisemitism is more prevalent in the age group 23–27 years, which is a younger group than that of racist incidents in general.
sentence_664: Main articles: [[Antisemitism_in_the_United_Kingdom|Antisemitism in the United Kingdom]] and [[British_Jews|British Jews]]
sentence_665: See also: [[Antisemitism_in_the_UK_Labour_Party|Antisemitism in the UK Labour Party]]
sentence_666: In 2017 an [[Institute_for_Jewish_Policy_Research|Institute for Jewish Policy Research]] survey found that the levels of antisemitism in Great Britain were among the lowest in the world, with 2.4% expressing multiple antisemitic attitudes, and about 70% having a favourable opinion of Jews.
sentence_667: However, only 17% had a favourable opinion of Israel, with 33% holding an unfavourable view.
sentence_668: In 2017, a report by the Campaign Against Antisemitism (CAA) found that the previous year, 2016, had been the worst on record for antisemitic hate crime in the UK.
sentence_669: Prior to that, 2015 had been the worst year on record, and 2014 was the worst year on record before that.
sentence_670: The report found that in 2016, antisemitic crime rose by 15% compared to 2015, or 45% compared to 2014.
sentence_671: It also found that 1 in 10 antisemitic crimes was violent.
sentence_672: Despite rising levels of antisemitic crime, the report said there had been a decrease in the [[Criminal_charge|charging]] of antisemitic crime.
sentence_673: In the report's foreword, the CAA's Chairman wrote: "Britain has the political will to fight antisemitism and strong laws with which to do it, but those responsible for tackling the rapidly growing racist targeting of British Jews are failing to enforce the law.
sentence_674: There is a very real danger of Jewish citizens emigrating, as has happened elsewhere in Europe unless there is radical change."
sentence_675: Every year since 2015, the CAA has commissioned polling by [[YouGov|YouGov]] concerning the attitude of the British public toward British Jews.
sentence_676: In 2017, their polling found that 36% of British adults believed at least one of the antisemitic statements pollsters had shown them to be true, a reduction from 39% in 2016 and 45% in 2015.
sentence_677: Additionally, the polling revealed widespread fear amongst British Jews, with almost 1 in 3 saying that they had considered emigrating in the last two years due to antisemitism, and 37% saying that they concealed their Judaism in public.
sentence_678: The report gave various indications as to the cause of the fears, with British Jews identifying Islamist antisemitism, [[Far-left_antisemitism|far-left antisemitism]] and far-right antisemitism as their main concerns, in that order.
sentence_679: 78% of British Jews saying that they had witnessed antisemitism disguised as a political comment about Israel, 76% thoughts that political developments were contributing antisemitism, and 52% felt that the [[Crown_Prosecution_Service|Crown Prosecution Service]] was not doing enough.
sentence_680: In 2005, a group of British [[Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom|Members of Parliament]] set up an inquiry into antisemitism, which published its findings in 2006.
sentence_681: Its report stated that "until recently, the prevailing opinion both within the Jewish community and beyond [had been] that antisemitism had receded to the point that it existed only on the margins of society."
sentence_682: It found a reversal of this progress since 2000.
sentence_683: The inquiry was reconstituted following a surge in antisemitic incidents in Britain during the summer of 2014, and the new inquiry published its report in 2015, making recommendations for reducing antisemitism.
sentence_684: In 2016, the [[Home_Affairs_Select_Committee|Home Affairs Select Committee]] held an inquiry into the rise of antisemitism in the UK.
sentence_685: The inquiry called [[David_Cameron|David Cameron]], [[Tim_Farron|Tim Farron]], [[Angus_Robertson|Angus Robertson]], [[Jeremy_Corbyn|Jeremy Corbyn]], [[Ken_Livingstone|Ken Livingstone]] and others to give evidence.
sentence_687: Although antisemitism in Canada is less prevalent than in many other countries, there have been recent incidents.
sentence_688: For example, a 2004 study identified 24 incidents of antisemitism between 14 March and 14 July 2004 in Newfoundland, Montreal, Quebec City, Ottawa, the Greater Toronto Area (GTA), and some smaller Ontario communities.
sentence_689: The incidents included vandalism and other attacks on four synagogues, six cemeteries, four schools, and a number of businesses and private residences.
sentence_690: Main article: [[Antisemitism_in_the_United_States|Antisemitism in the United States]]
sentence_691: See also: [[History_of_antisemitism_in_the_United_States|History of antisemitism in the United States]]
sentence_692: In April 2019, the [[Anti-Defamation_League|Anti-Defamation League]] said antisemitic incidents remained at "near-historic" levels in the U.S. in 2018, and assaults had more than doubled that year, though overall incidents were down 5% from 2017.
sentence_693: Separately, it cited FBI data showing Jews were the most likely to be targeted by religious-based hate crime for every year since 1991.
sentence_695: Commission on Civil Rights]] examined antisemitism on college campuses.
sentence_696: It reported that "incidents of threatened bodily injury, physical intimidation or property damage are now rare", but antisemitism still occurs on many campuses and is a "serious problem."
sentence_698: Department of Education]]'s [[Office_for_Civil_Rights|Office for Civil Rights]] protect college students from antisemitism through vigorous enforcement of Title VI of the [[Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964|Civil Rights Act of 1964]] and further recommended that [[United_States_Congress|Congress]] clarify that Title VI applies to discrimination against Jewish students.
sentence_699: On 19 September 2006, [[Yale_University|Yale University]] founded the [[Yale_Initiative_for_the_Interdisciplinary_Study_of_Anti-Semitism|Yale Initiative for the Interdisciplinary Study of Anti-Semitism]] (YIISA), the first North American university-based center for study of the subject, as part of its Institution for Social and Policy Studies.
sentence_700: Director Charles Small of the Center cited the increase in antisemitism worldwide in recent years as generating a "need to understand the current manifestation of this disease".
sentence_701: In June 2011, Yale voted to close this initiative.
sentence_702: After carrying out a routine review, the faculty review committee said that the initiative had not met its research and teaching standards.
sentence_703: [[Donald_Green|Donald Green]], then head of Yale's Institution for Social and Policy Studies, the body under whose aegis the antisemitism initiative was run, said that it had not had many papers published in the relevant leading journals or attracted many students.
sentence_704: As with other programs that had been in a similar situation, the initiative had therefore been cancelled.
sentence_705: This decision has been criticized by figures such as former U.S. Commission on Civil Rights Staff Director Kenneth L. Marcus, who is now the director of the Initiative to Combat Anti-Semitism and Anti-Israelism in America's Educational Systems at the Institute for Jewish and Community Research, and [[Deborah_Lipstadt|Deborah Lipstadt]], who described the decision as "weird" and "strange."
sentence_706: [[Antony_Lerman|Antony Lerman]] has supported Yale's decision, describing the YIISA as a politicized initiative that was devoted to the promotion of Israel rather than to serious research on antisemitism.
sentence_707: A 2007 survey by the [[Anti-Defamation_League|Anti-Defamation League]] (ADL) concluded that 15% of Americans hold antisemitic views, which was in-line with the average of the previous ten years, but a decline from the 29% of the early sixties.
sentence_708: The survey concluded that education was a strong predictor, "with most educated Americans being remarkably free of prejudicial views."
sentence_709: The belief that Jews have too much power was considered a common antisemitic view by the ADL.
sentence_710: Other views indicating antisemitism, according to the survey, include the view that Jews are more loyal to Israel than America, and that they are responsible for the death of [[Jesus|Jesus of Nazareth]].
sentence_711: The survey found that antisemitic Americans are likely to be intolerant generally, e.g. regarding immigration and free-speech.
sentence_712: The 2007 survey also found that 29% of foreign-born [[Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans|Hispanics]] and 32% of [[African_American|African-Americans]] hold strong antisemitic beliefs, three times more than the 10% for whites.
sentence_713: A 2009 study published in [[Boston_Review|Boston Review]] found that nearly 25% of non-Jewish Americans blamed Jews for the [[Financial_crisis_of_2007–2008|financial crisis of 2007–2008]], with a higher percentage among Democrats than Republicans.
sentence_714: 32% of Democrats blamed Jews for the financial crisis, versus 18% for Republicans.
sentence_715: In August 2012, the [[California_state_assembly|California state assembly]] approved a [[Non-binding_resolution|non-binding resolution]] that "encourages university leaders to combat a wide array of anti-Jewish and anti-Israel actions," although the resolution "is purely symbolic and does not carry policy implications."
sentence_716: In April 2017, [[Politico|Politico Magazine]] published an article purporting to show links between U.S. President [[Donald_Trump|Donald Trump]], Russian President [[Vladimir_Putin|Vladimir Putin]] and the Jewish outreach organization [[Chabad-Lubavitch|Chabad-Lubavitch]].
sentence_717: The article was condemned, with the head of the Anti-Defamation League [[Jonathan_Greenblatt|Jonathan Greenblatt]] saying that it "evokes age-old myths about Jews".
sentence_718: In November 2017, Jonathan Greenblatt, national director and CEO of the Anti-Defamation League, stated in an interview, "While anti-Semitic attitudes have remained consistent at 14%... anti-Semitic incidents have been on the rise.
sentence_719: In 2016 we saw a 34% increase over the prior year in acts of harassment, vandalism, or violence directed at Jewish individuals and institutions.
sentence_720: During the first three-quarters of 2017, there was a 67% increase over the same period in 2016.
sentence_721: We've seen double the number of incidents in K-12 schools, and almost a 60% increase on college campuses."
sentence_722: On 29 October 2018, an antisemitic terrorist [[Pittsburgh_synagogue_shooting|attacked the Tree of Life Synagogue]] in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
sentence_723: On 25 April 2019, [[The_New_York_Times|The New York Times]]'s international edition included a cartoon featuring U.S. President [[Donald_Trump|Donald Trump]] and Israeli PM [[Benjamin_Netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]].
sentence_724: Trump was shown wearing a [[Kippah|kippah]] and Netanyahu was displayed as Trump's dog wearing a collar with the [[Star_of_David|Star of David]].
sentence_725: After criticism from public and religious figures, The Times admitted to using "anti-Semitic tropes".
sentence_726: On 29 April, The New York Times came under scrutiny again for publishing another anti-Semitic cartoon featuring PM Netanyahu.
sentence_727: Further information: [[Antisemitism_in_Venezuela|Antisemitism in Venezuela]] and [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Venezuela|History of the Jews in Venezuela]]
sentence_728: In a 2009 news story, Michael Rowan and Douglas E. Schoen wrote, "In an infamous Christmas Eve speech several years ago, Chávez said the Jews killed Christ and have been gobbling up wealth and causing poverty and injustice worldwide ever since."
sentence_729: [[Hugo_Chávez|Hugo Chávez]] stated that "[t]he world is for all of us, then, but it so happens that a minority, the descendants of the same ones that crucified Christ, the descendants of the same ones that kicked [[Simón_Bolívar|Bolívar]] out of here and also crucified him in their own way over there in Santa Marta, in Colombia.
sentence_730: A minority has taken possession of all of the wealth of the world."
sentence_731: In February 2012, opposition candidate for the [[2012_Venezuelan_presidential_election|2012 Venezuelan presidential election]] [[Henrique_Capriles|Henrique Capriles]] was subject to what foreign journalists characterized as vicious attacks by state-run media sources.
sentence_732: [[The_Wall_Street_Journal|The Wall Street Journal]] said that Capriles "was vilified in a campaign in Venezuela's state-run media, which insinuated he was, among other things, a homosexual and a Zionist agent".
sentence_733: A 13 February 2012 opinion article in the state-owned [[Radio_Nacional_de_Venezuela|Radio Nacional de Venezuela]], titled "The Enemy is Zionism" attacked Capriles' Jewish ancestry and linked him with Jewish national groups because of a meeting he had held with local Jewish leaders, saying, "This is our enemy, the Zionism that Capriles today represents... Zionism, along with capitalism, are responsible for 90% of world poverty and imperialist wars."

title: Anno Domini
sentence_0: "AD" and "Christian era" redirect here.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Anno_Domini_(disambiguation)|Anno Domini (disambiguation)]], [[AD_(disambiguation)|AD (disambiguation)]], and [[Christian_era_(disambiguation)|Christian era (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: The terms anno Domini (AD) and before Christ (BC) are used to label or number years in the [[Julian_calendar|Julian]] and [[Gregorian_calendar|Gregorian calendars]].
sentence_3: The term anno Domini is Medieval Latin and means "in the year of the Lord" but is often presented using "our Lord" instead of "the Lord", taken from the full original phrase "anno Domini nostri Jesu Christi", which translates to "in the year of our Lord Jesus Christ".
sentence_4: This [[Calendar_era|calendar era]] is based on the traditionally reckoned year of the [[Annunciation|conception]] or [[Nativity_of_Jesus|birth]] of [[Jesus_of_Nazareth|Jesus of Nazareth]], with AD counting years from the start of this [[Epoch_(date_reference)|epoch]] and BC denoting years before the start of the era.
sentence_5: There is no [[Year_zero|year zero]] in this scheme, so the year AD 1 immediately follows the year 1 BC.
sentence_6: This dating system was devised in 525 by [[Dionysius_Exiguus|Dionysius Exiguus]] of [[Scythia_Minor|Scythia Minor]] but was not widely used until after 800.
sentence_7: The [[Gregorian_calendar|Gregorian calendar]] is the most widely used [[Calendar|calendar]] in the world today.
sentence_8: For decades, it has been the unofficial global standard, adopted in the pragmatic interests of international communication, transportation, and commercial integration, and recognized by international institutions such as the United Nations.
sentence_9: Traditionally, English follows [[Latin|Latin]] usage by placing the "AD" abbreviation before the year number.
sentence_10: However, BC is placed after the year number (for example: AD 2020, but 68 BC), which also preserves syntactic order.
sentence_11: The abbreviation is also widely used after the number of a century or [[Millennium|millennium]], as in "fourth century AD" or "second millennium AD" (although conservative usage formerly rejected such expressions).
sentence_12: Because BC is the English abbreviation for Before Christ, it is sometimes incorrectly concluded that AD means After Death, i.e., after the death of Jesus.
sentence_13: However, this would mean that the approximate 33 years commonly associated with the life of Jesus would be included in neither the BC nor the AD time scales.
sentence_14: Terminology that is viewed by some as being more neutral and inclusive of non-Christian people is to call this the Current or [[Common_Era|Common Era]] (abbreviated as CE), with the preceding years referred to as Before the Common or Current Era (BCE).
sentence_15: [[Astronomical_year_numbering|Astronomical year numbering]] and [[ISO_8601|ISO 8601]] avoid words or abbreviations related to Christianity but use the same numbers for AD years.
sentence_16: Further information: [[Ante_Christum_natum|Ante Christum natum]]
sentence_17: The Anno Domini dating system was devised in 525 by [[Dionysius_Exiguus|Dionysius Exiguus]] to enumerate the years in his [[Dionysius_Exiguus'_Easter_table|Easter table]].
sentence_18: His system was to replace the Diocletian era that had been used in an old [[Easter_table|Easter table]] because he did not wish to continue the memory of a tyrant who [[Diocletianic_Persecution|persecuted Christians]].
sentence_19: The last year of the old table, Diocletian Anno Martyrium 247, was immediately followed by the first year of his table, Anno Domini 532.
sentence_20: When he devised his table, [[Julian_calendar|Julian calendar]] years were identified by naming the consuls who held office that year—he himself stated that the "present year" was "the consulship of [[Flavius_Anicius_Probus_Iunior|Probus Junior]]", which was 525 years "since the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ".
sentence_21: Thus Dionysius implied that [[Incarnation_(Christianity)|Jesus' incarnation]] occurred 525 years earlier, without stating the specific year during which his birth or conception occurred.
sentence_22: "However, nowhere in his exposition of his table does Dionysius relate his epoch to any other dating system, whether consulate, [[Olympiad|Olympiad]], [[Anno_Mundi|year of the world]], or regnal year of Augustus; much less does he explain or justify the underlying date."
sentence_23: Bonnie J. Blackburn and Leofranc Holford-Strevens briefly present arguments for 2 BC, 1 BC, or AD 1 as the year Dionysius intended for the [[Nativity_of_Jesus|Nativity]] or [[Incarnation_(Christianity)|incarnation]].
sentence_24: Among the sources of confusion are:

list.value: In modern times, [[Incarnation|incarnation]] is synonymous with the conception, but some ancient writers, such as [[Bede|Bede]], considered incarnation to be synonymous with the Nativity.
The civil or consular year began on 1 January, but the Diocletian year began on 29 August (30 August in the year before a Julian leap year).
There were inaccuracies in the lists of consuls.
There were confused summations of emperors' regnal years.

sentence_25: It is not known how Dionysius established the year of Jesus's birth.
sentence_26: Two major theories are that Dionysius based his calculation on the Gospel of Luke, which states that Jesus was "about thirty years old" shortly after "the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar", and hence subtracted thirty years from that date, or that Dionysius counted back 532 years from the first year of his new table.
sentence_27: It has also been speculated by Georges Declercq that Dionysius' desire to replace Diocletian years with a calendar based on the incarnation of Christ was intended to prevent people from believing the imminent [[End_of_the_world_(religion)|end of the world]].
sentence_28: At the time, it was believed by some that the [[Resurrection_of_the_dead|resurrection of the dead]] and end of the world would occur 500 years after the birth of Jesus.
sentence_29: The old [[Anno_Mundi|Anno Mundi]] calendar theoretically commenced with the [[Dating_creation|creation of the world]] based on information in the [[Old_Testament|Old Testament]].
sentence_30: It was believed that, based on the Anno Mundi calendar, Jesus was born in the year 5500 (5500 years after the world was created) with the year 6000 of the Anno Mundi calendar marking the end of the world.
sentence_31: Anno Mundi 6000 (approximately AD 500) was thus equated with the end of the world but this date had already passed in the time of Dionysius.
sentence_32: The [[Anglo-Saxons|Anglo-Saxon]] historian [[Venerable_Bede|Saint (Venerable) Bede]], who was familiar with the work of [[Dionysius_Exiguus|Dionysius Exiguus]], used Anno Domini dating in his [[Ecclesiastical_History_of_the_English_People|Ecclesiastical History of the English People]], which he completed in AD 731.
sentence_33: In the History he also used the [[Latin|Latin]] phrase ante [...] incarnationis dominicae tempus anno sexagesimo ("in the sixtieth year before the time of the Lord's incarnation"), which is equivalent to the English "before Christ", to identify years before the first year of this era.
sentence_34: Both Dionysius and Bede regarded Anno Domini as beginning at the incarnation of [[Jesus_Christ|Jesus Christ]], but "the distinction between Incarnation and Nativity was not drawn until the late 9th century, when in some places the Incarnation epoch was identified with Christ's conception, i. e., the Annunciation on March 25" ("Annunciation style" dating).
sentence_35: On the continent of Europe, Anno Domini was introduced as the era of choice of the [[Carolingian_Renaissance|Carolingian Renaissance]] by the English cleric and scholar [[Alcuin|Alcuin]] in the late eighth century.
sentence_36: Its endorsement by Emperor [[Charlemagne|Charlemagne]] and [[List_of_Frankish_Kings#Carolingian_dynasty|his successors]] popularizing the use of the epoch and spreading it throughout the Carolingian Empire ultimately lies at the core of the system's prevalence.
sentence_37: According to the [[Catholic_Encyclopedia|Catholic Encyclopedia]], popes continued to date documents according to regnal years for some time, but usage of AD gradually became more common in Catholic countries from the 11th to the 14th centuries.
sentence_38: In 1422, [[Portugal|Portugal]] became the last Western European country to [[Spanish_era|switch to]] the system begun by Dionysius.
sentence_39: [[Eastern_Orthodox|Eastern Orthodox]] countries only began to adopt AD instead of the [[Byzantine_calendar|Byzantine calendar]] in 1700 when Russia did so, with others adopting it in the 19th and 20th centuries.
sentence_40: Although Anno Domini was in widespread use by the 9th century, the term "Before Christ" (or its equivalent) did not become common until much later.
sentence_41: Bede used the expression "anno [...] ante incarnationem Dominicam" (in the year before the incarnation of the Lord) twice.
sentence_42: "Anno ante Christi nativitatem" (in the year before the birth of Christ) is found in 1474 in a work by a German monk.
