sentence_419: Alexander's legacy extended beyond his military conquests.
sentence_420: His campaigns greatly increased contacts and trade between East and West, and vast areas to the east were significantly exposed to Greek civilization and influence.
sentence_421: Some of the cities he founded became major cultural centers, many surviving into the 21st century.
sentence_422: His chroniclers recorded valuable information about the areas through which he marched, while the Greeks themselves got a sense of belonging to a world beyond the Mediterranean.
sentence_423: Main article: [[Hellenistic_period|Hellenistic period]]
sentence_424: Alexander's most immediate legacy was the introduction of Macedonian rule to huge new swathes of Asia.
sentence_425: At the time of his death, Alexander's empire covered some 5,200,000 km (2,000,000 sq mi), and was the largest state of its time.
sentence_426: Many of these areas remained in Macedonian hands or under Greek influence for the next 200–300 years.
sentence_427: The [[Hellenistic_period#The_successors|successor states]] that emerged were, at least initially, dominant forces, and these 300 years are often referred to as the [[Hellenistic_period|Hellenistic period]].
sentence_428: The eastern borders of Alexander's empire began to collapse even during his lifetime.
sentence_429: However, the power vacuum he left in the northwest of the Indian subcontinent directly gave rise to one of the most powerful Indian dynasties in history, the [[Maurya_Empire|Maurya Empire]].
sentence_430: Taking advantage of this power vacuum, [[Chandragupta_Maurya|Chandragupta Maurya]] (referred to in Greek sources as "Sandrokottos"), of relatively humble origin, took control of the [[Punjab_region|Punjab]], and with that power base proceeded to conquer the [[Nanda_Empire|Nanda Empire]].
sentence_431: Further information: [[List_of_cities_founded_by_Alexander_the_Great|List of cities founded by Alexander the Great]]
sentence_432: Over the course of his conquests, Alexander founded some [[Alexandria_(disambiguation)#West_and_Central_Asia|twenty cities that bore his name]], most of them east of the [[Tigris|Tigris]].
sentence_433: The first, and greatest, was [[Alexandria|Alexandria]] in Egypt, which would become one of the leading Mediterranean cities.
sentence_434: The cities' locations reflected trade routes as well as defensive positions.
sentence_435: At first, the cities must have been inhospitable, little more than defensive garrisons.
sentence_436: Following Alexander's death, many Greeks who had settled there tried to return to Greece.
sentence_437: However, a century or so after Alexander's death, many of the Alexandrias were thriving, with elaborate public buildings and substantial populations that included both Greek and local peoples.
sentence_438: In 334 BC, Alexander the Great donated funds for the completion of the new temple of [[Athena_Polias|Athena Polias]] in [[Priene|Priene]], in modern-day western Turkey.
sentence_439: An [[Priene_Inscription|inscription from the temple]], now housed in the [[British_Museum|British Museum]], declares: "King Alexander dedicated [this temple] to Athena Polias."
sentence_440: This inscription is one of the few independent archaeological discoveries confirming an episode from Alexander's life.
sentence_441: The temple was designed by [[Pythius_of_Priene|Pytheos]], one of the architects of the [[Mausoleum_at_Halicarnassus|Mausoleum at Halicarnassus]].
sentence_442: Libanius wrote that Alexander founded the temple of Zeus Bottiaios (Ancient Greek: Βοττιαίου Δῖός), in the place where later the city of [[Antioch|Antioch]] was built.
sentence_443: Main article: [[Hellenistic_civilization|Hellenistic civilization]]
sentence_444: Hellenization was coined by the German historian [[Johann_Gustav_Droysen|Johann Gustav Droysen]] to denote the spread of Greek language, culture, and population into the former Persian empire after Alexander's conquest.
sentence_445: That this export took place is undoubted, and can be seen in the great Hellenistic cities of, for instance, [[Alexandria|Alexandria]], [[Antioch|Antioch]] and [[Seleucia|Seleucia]] (south of modern [[Baghdad|Baghdad]]).
sentence_446: Alexander sought to insert Greek elements into [[Culture_of_Iran|Persian culture]] and attempted to hybridize Greek and Persian culture.
sentence_447: This culminated in his aspiration to homogenize the populations of Asia and Europe.
sentence_448: However, his successors explicitly rejected such policies.
sentence_449: Nevertheless, Hellenization occurred throughout the region, accompanied by a distinct and opposite 'Orientalization' of the successor states.
sentence_450: The core of the Hellenistic culture promulgated by the conquests was essentially [[Athenian|Athenian]].
sentence_451: The close association of men from across Greece in Alexander's army directly led to the emergence of the largely [[Attic_Greek|Attic]]-based "[[Koine|koine]]", or "common" Greek dialect.
sentence_452: Koine spread throughout the Hellenistic world, becoming the [[Lingua_franca|lingua franca]] of Hellenistic lands and eventually the ancestor of modern Greek.
sentence_453: Furthermore, [[Urban_planning|town planning]], education, local government, and art current in the Hellenistic period were all based on Classical Greek ideals, evolving into distinct new forms commonly grouped as Hellenistic.
sentence_454: Aspects of Hellenistic culture were still evident in the traditions of the Byzantine Empire in the mid-15th century.

section_39.value: Hellenization in South and Central Asia

sentence_455: Main articles: [[Indo-Greek_Kingdom|Indo-Greek Kingdom]], [[Indo-Greek_art|Indo-Greek art]], and [[Greco-Buddhism|Greco-Buddhism]]
sentence_456: Some of the most pronounced effects of Hellenization can be seen in Afghanistan and India, in the region of the relatively late-rising [[Greco-Bactrian_Kingdom|Greco-Bactrian Kingdom]] (250–125 BC) (in modern [[Afghanistan|Afghanistan]], [[Pakistan|Pakistan]], and [[Tajikistan|Tajikistan]]) and the [[Indo-Greeks|Indo-Greek Kingdom]] (180 BC – 10 AD) in modern Afghanistan and India.
sentence_457: On the [[Silk_Road|Silk Road]] trade routes, Hellenistic culture hybridized with Iranian and [[Buddhist|Buddhist]] cultures.
sentence_458: The cosmopolitan art and mythology of [[Gandhara|Gandhara]] (a region spanning the upper confluence of the Indus, Swat and Kabul rivers in modern Pakistan) of the ~3rd century BC to the ~5th century AD are most evident of the direct contact between Hellenistic civilization and South Asia, as are the [[Edicts_of_Ashoka|Edicts of Ashoka]], which directly mention the Greeks within Ashoka's dominion as converting to Buddhism and the reception of Buddhist emissaries by Ashoka's contemporaries in the Hellenistic world.
sentence_459: The resulting syncretism known as [[Greco-Buddhism|Greco-Buddhism]] influenced the development of Buddhism and created a culture of [[Greco-Buddhist_art|Greco-Buddhist art]].
sentence_460: These Greco-Buddhist kingdoms sent some of the first Buddhist missionaries to [[China|China]], [[Sri_Lanka|Sri Lanka]] and Hellenistic Asia and Europe (Greco-Buddhist monasticism).
sentence_461: Some of the first and most influential figurative portrayals of the [[Gautama_Buddha|Buddha]] appeared at this time, perhaps modelled on Greek statues of [[Apollo|Apollo]] in the Greco-Buddhist style.
sentence_462: Several Buddhist traditions may have been influenced by the [[Ancient_Greek_religion|ancient Greek religion]]: the concept of [[Boddhisatvas|Boddhisatvas]] is reminiscent of Greek divine heroes, and some [[Mahayana|Mahayana]] [[Offering_(Buddhism)|ceremonial practices]] (burning [[Incense|incense]], gifts of flowers, and food placed on altars) are similar to those practised by the ancient Greeks; however, similar practices were also observed amongst the native Indic culture.
sentence_463: One Greek king, [[Menander_I|Menander I]], probably became Buddhist, and was immortalized in [[Buddhist_texts|Buddhist literature]] as 'Milinda'.
sentence_464: The process of Hellenization also spurred trade between the east and west.
sentence_465: For example, Greek astronomical instruments dating to the 3rd century BC were found in the [[Greco-Bactrian|Greco-Bactrian]] city of [[Ai_Khanoum|Ai Khanoum]] in modern-day [[Afghanistan|Afghanistan]], while the Greek concept of a [[Spherical_earth|spherical earth]] surrounded by the spheres of planets eventually supplanted the long-standing Indian cosmological belief of a disc consisting of four continents grouped around a central mountain (Mount Meru) like the petals of a flower.
sentence_466: The [[Yavanajataka|Yavanajataka]] (lit.
sentence_467: Greek astronomical treatise) and [[Paulisa_Siddhanta|Paulisa Siddhanta]] texts depict the influence of Greek astronomical ideas on Indian astronomy.
sentence_468: Following the conquests of Alexander the Great in the east, [[Hellenistic_influence_on_Indian_art|Hellenistic influence on Indian art]] was far-ranging.
sentence_469: In the area of [[Architecture|architecture]], a few examples of the [[Ionic_order|Ionic order]] can be found as far as [[Pakistan|Pakistan]] with the [[Jandial|Jandial temple]] near [[Taxila|Taxila]].
sentence_470: Several examples of [[Capital_(architecture)|capitals]] displaying Ionic influences can be seen as far as [[Patna|Patna]], especially with the [[Pataliputra_capital|Pataliputra capital]], dated to the 3rd century BC.
sentence_471: The [[Corinthian_order|Corinthian order]] is also heavily represented in the [[Greco-Buddhist_art|art of Gandhara]], especially through [[Indo-Corinthian_capital|Indo-Corinthian capitals]].
sentence_472: Alexander and his exploits were admired by many Romans, especially generals, who wanted to associate themselves with his achievements.
sentence_473: Polybius began his [[The_Histories_(Polybius)|Histories]] by reminding Romans of Alexander's achievements, and thereafter Roman leaders saw him as a role model.
sentence_474: [[Pompey_the_Great|Pompey the Great]] adopted the epithet "Magnus" and even Alexander's anastole-type haircut, and searched the conquered lands of the east for Alexander's 260-year-old cloak, which he then wore as a sign of greatness.
sentence_475: [[Julius_Caesar|Julius Caesar]] dedicated a [[Lysippus|Lysippean]] [[Equestrian_statue|equestrian]] [[Bronze|bronze]] statue but replaced Alexander's head with his own, while [[Octavian|Octavian]] visited Alexander's tomb in Alexandria and temporarily changed his seal from a sphinx to Alexander's profile.
sentence_476: The emperor [[Trajan|Trajan]] also admired Alexander, as did [[Nero|Nero]] and [[Caracalla|Caracalla]].
sentence_477: The Macriani, a Roman family that in the person of [[Macrinus|Macrinus]] briefly ascended to the imperial throne, kept images of Alexander on their persons, either on jewellery, or embroidered into their clothes.
sentence_478: On the other hand, some Roman writers, particularly Republican figures, used Alexander as a cautionary tale of how [[Autocratic|autocratic]] tendencies can be kept in check by [[Roman_republic|republican]] values.
sentence_479: Alexander was used by these writers as an example of ruler values such as amicita (friendship) and clementia (clemency), but also iracundia (anger) and cupiditas gloriae (over-desire for glory).
sentence_480: [[Julian_(emperor)|Emperor Julian]] in his satire called "The Caesars", describes a contest between the previous Roman emperors, with Alexander the Great called in as an extra contestant, in the presence of the assembled gods.
sentence_481: The [[Itinerarium_Alexandri|Itinerarium Alexandri]] is a [[4th-century|4th-century]] Latin [[Itinerarium|Itinerarium]] which describes Alexander the Great's campaigns.

section_41.value: Unsuccessful plan to cut a canal through the isthmus

sentence_482: [[Pausanias_(geographer)|Pausanias]] writes that Alexander wanted to dig the Mimas mountain (today at the [[Karaburun|Karaburun]] area), but he didn't succeed.
sentence_483: He also mentions that this was the only unsuccessful project of Alexander.
sentence_484: In addition, [[Pliny_the_Elder|Pliny the Elder]] writes about this unsuccessful plan adding that the distance was 12 kilometres (7 ⁄2 mi), and the purpose was to cut a canal through the isthmus, so as to connect the Caystrian and Hermaean bays.

section_42.value: Naming of the Icarus island in the Persian Gulf

sentence_485: [[Arrian|Arrian]] wrote that [[Aristobulus_of_Cassandreia|Aristobulus]] said that the [[Ikaros_(Failaka_Island)|Icarus island]] (modern [[Failaka_Island|Failaka Island]]) in the [[Persian_Gulf|Persian Gulf]] had this name because Alexander ordered the island to be named like this, after the [[Icaria|Icarus island]] in the [[Aegean_Sea|Aegean Sea]].
sentence_486: Main article: [[Alexander_the_Great_in_legend|Alexander the Great in legend]]
sentence_487: Legendary accounts surround the life of Alexander the Great, many deriving from his own lifetime, probably encouraged by Alexander himself.
sentence_488: His court historian Callisthenes portrayed the sea in [[Cilicia|Cilicia]] as drawing back from him in proskynesis.
sentence_489: Writing shortly after Alexander's death, another participant, [[Onesicritus|Onesicritus]], invented a [[Courtship|tryst]] between Alexander and Thalestris, queen of the mythical Amazons.
sentence_490: When Onesicritus read this passage to his patron, Alexander's general and later King [[Lysimachus|Lysimachus]] reportedly quipped, "I wonder where I was at the time."
sentence_491: In the first centuries after Alexander's death, probably in Alexandria, a quantity of the legendary material coalesced into a text known as the [[Alexander_Romance|Alexander Romance]], later falsely ascribed to Callisthenes and therefore known as Pseudo-Callisthenes.
sentence_492: This text underwent numerous expansions and revisions throughout Antiquity and the [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]], containing many dubious stories, and was translated into numerous languages.
sentence_493: Main articles: [[Cultural_depictions_of_Alexander_the_Great|Cultural depictions of Alexander the Great]] and Alexander the Great in the Quran
sentence_494: Alexander the Great's accomplishments and legacy have been depicted in many cultures.
sentence_495: Alexander has figured in both high and popular culture beginning in his own era to the present day.
sentence_496: The Alexander Romance, in particular, has had a significant impact on portrayals of Alexander in later cultures, from Persian to medieval European to modern Greek.
sentence_497: Alexander features prominently in modern Greek folklore, more so than any other ancient figure.
sentence_498: The colloquial form of his name in modern Greek ("O Megalexandros") is a household name, and he is the only ancient hero to appear in the [[Karagiozis|Karagiozis]] shadow play.
sentence_499: One well-known fable among Greek seamen involves a solitary [[Mermaid|mermaid]] who would grasp a ship's prow during a storm and ask the captain "Is King Alexander alive?"
sentence_500: The correct answer is "He is alive and well and rules the world!"
sentence_501: causing the mermaid to vanish and the sea to calm.
sentence_502: Any other answer would cause the mermaid to turn into a raging [[Gorgon|Gorgon]] who would drag the ship to the bottom of the sea, all hands aboard.
sentence_503: In pre-Islamic [[Middle_Persian_language|Middle Persian]] ([[Zoroastrian|Zoroastrian]]) literature, Alexander is referred to by the epithet gujastak, meaning "accursed", and is accused of destroying temples and burning the sacred texts of Zoroastrianism.
sentence_504: In Sunni Islamic Persia, under the influence of the [[Alexander_Romance|Alexander Romance]] (in [[Persian_language|Persian]]: اسکندرنامه‎ Iskandarnamah), a more positive portrayal of Alexander emerges.
sentence_505: Firdausi's [[Shahnameh|Shahnameh]] ("The Book of Kings") includes Alexander in a line of legitimate Persian [[Shah|shahs]], a mythical figure who explored the far reaches of the world in search of the [[Fountain_of_Youth|Fountain of Youth]].
sentence_506: Later Persian writers associate him with philosophy, portraying him at a symposium with figures such as [[Socrates|Socrates]], [[Plato|Plato]] and Aristotle, in search of immortality.
sentence_507: The figure of [[Dhul-Qarnayn|Dhul-Qarnayn]] (literally "the Two-Horned One") mentioned in the [[Quran|Quran]] is believed by scholars to be based on later legends of Alexander.
sentence_508: In this tradition, he was a heroic figure who built a wall to defend against the nations of [[Gog_and_Magog|Gog and Magog]].
sentence_509: He then travelled the known world in search of the Water of Life and Immortality, eventually becoming a prophet.
sentence_510: The [[Syriac_language|Syriac]] version of the Alexander Romance portrays him as an ideal Christian world conqueror who prayed to "the one true God".
sentence_511: In Egypt, Alexander was portrayed as the son of [[Nectanebo_II|Nectanebo II]], the last [[Pharaoh|pharaoh]] before the Persian conquest.
sentence_512: His defeat of Darius was depicted as Egypt's salvation, "proving" Egypt was still ruled by an Egyptian.
sentence_513: According to [[Josephus|Josephus]], Alexander was shown the [[Book_of_Daniel|Book of Daniel]] when he entered Jerusalem, which described a mighty Greek king who would conquer the Persian Empire.
sentence_514: This is cited as a reason for sparing Jerusalem.
sentence_515: In [[Hindi|Hindi]] and [[Urdu|Urdu]], the name "Sikandar", derived from the Persian name for Alexander, denotes a rising young talent, and the Delhi Sultanate ruler [[Alauddin_Khalji|Aladdin Khajli]] stylized himself as "Sikandar-i-Sani" (the Second Alexander the Great).
sentence_516: In [[Medieval_India|medieval India]], Turkic and Afghan sovereigns from the Iranian-cultured region of Central Asia brought positive cultural connotations of Alexander to the Indian subcontinent, resulting in the efflorescence of Sikandernameh ([[Alexander_romance|Alexander Romances]]) written by Indo-Persian poets such as [[Amir_Khusrow|Amir Khusrow]] and the prominence of Alexander the Great as a popular subject in Mughal-era Persian miniatures.
sentence_517: In [[Middle_Ages|medieval Europe]], Alexander the Great was revered as a member of the [[Nine_Worthies|Nine Worthies]], a group of heroes whose lives were believed to encapsulate all the ideal qualities of [[Chivalry|chivalry]].
sentence_518: In Greek Anthology there are poems referring to Alexander.
sentence_519: Irish playwright [[Aubrey_Thomas_de_Vere|Aubrey Thomas de Vere]] wrote [[Alexander_the_Great,_a_Dramatic_Poem|Alexander the Great, a Dramatic Poem]].
sentence_520: In popular culture, the British heavy metal band [[Iron_Maiden|Iron Maiden]] included a song titled "Alexander the Great" on their 1986 album [[Somewhere_in_Time_(Iron_Maiden_album)|Somewhere in Time]].
sentence_521: Written by bass player [[Steve_Harris_(musician)|Steve Harris]], the song retells Alexander's life.
sentence_522: Main article: [[Historiography_of_Alexander_the_Great|Historiography of Alexander the Great]]
sentence_523: Apart from a few inscriptions and fragments, texts written by people who actually knew Alexander or who gathered information from men who served with Alexander were all lost.
sentence_524: Contemporaries who wrote accounts of his life included Alexander's campaign historian Callisthenes; Alexander's generals Ptolemy and [[Nearchus|Nearchus]]; [[Aristobulus_of_Cassandreia|Aristobulus]], a junior officer on the campaigns; and Onesicritus, Alexander's chief helmsman.
sentence_525: Their works are lost, but later works based on these [[Primary_source|original sources]] have survived.
sentence_526: The earliest of these is [[Diodorus_Siculus|Diodorus Siculus]] (1st century BC), followed by Quintus Curtius Rufus (mid-to-late 1st century AD), Arrian (1st to 2nd century AD), the biographer Plutarch (1st to 2nd century AD), and finally [[Justin_(historian)|Justin]], whose work dated as late as the 4th century.
sentence_527: Of these, Arrian is generally considered the most reliable, given that he used Ptolemy and Aristobulus as his sources, closely followed by Diodorus.

sentence_4: The Black Sea is a [[Body_of_water|body of water]], located in western [[Eurasia|Eurasia]].
sentence_5: Depending on the view, it is classified as a [[Marginal_sea|marginal sea]], but also as the world's largest inland body of water (surpassing the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]]).
sentence_6: It is [[Inflow_(hydrology)|supplied by]] major rivers, principally the [[Danube|Danube]], [[Dnieper_River|Dnieper]] and [[Don_River_(Russia)|Don]].
sentence_7: The watersheds of many countries drain into the sea beyond the six that share its coast.
sentence_8: The Black Sea covers 436,400 km (168,500 sq mi) (not including the [[Sea_of_Azov|Sea of Azov]]), a maximum depth of 2,212 m (7,257 ft), and a volume of 547,000 km (131,000 cu mi), making it the world's largest inland body of water.
sentence_9: Most of its coasts rapidly ascend.
sentence_10: These rises are the [[Pontic_Mountains|Pontic Mountains]] to the south, bar the southwest facing peninsulas, the Caucasus Mountains to the east and the [[Crimean_Mountains|Crimean Mountains]] to the mid-north.
sentence_11: In the west the coast is generally small [[Floodplain|floodplains]] below foothills such as: the [[Strandzha|Strandzha]]; Cape Emine, a dwindling of the east end of the [[Balkan_Mountains|Balkan Mountains]]; and the [[Dobruja_Plateau|Dobruja Plateau]] considerably further north.
sentence_12: The longest east–west extent is about 1,175 km (730 mi).
sentence_13: Important cities along the coast include [[Istanbul|Istanbul]], [[Odessa|Odessa]], [[Varna|Varna]], [[Samsun|Samsun]], [[Sochi|Sochi]], [[Sevastopol|Sevastopol]], [[Constanța|Constanța]], [[Trabzon|Trabzon]], Novorossiysk, [[Burgas|Burgas]], [[Batumi|Batumi]], etc.
sentence_14: The Black Sea is bordered by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey, and Ukraine.
sentence_15: It has a positive [[Water_balance|water balance]] with an annual net outflow of 300 km (72 cu mi) per year through the [[Bosporus|Bosporus]] and the [[Dardanelles|Dardanelles]] into the [[Aegean_Sea|Aegean Sea]].
sentence_16: While the net flow of water through the Bosporus and Dardanelles (known collectively as the [[Turkish_Straits|Turkish Straits]]) is out of the Black Sea, generally water is flowing in both directions simultaneously.
sentence_17: Denser, more [[Saline_water|saline water]] from the Aegean flows into the Black Sea underneath the less dense, fresher outflowing water from the Black Sea.
sentence_18: This creates a significant and permanent layer of deep water which does not drain or mix and is therefore [[Anoxic_waters|anoxic]].
sentence_19: This anoxic layer is responsible for the preservation of ancient shipwrecks which have been found in the Black Sea.
sentence_20: The Black Sea ultimately drains into the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]], via the Turkish Straits and the Aegean Sea.
sentence_21: The Bosporus Strait connects it to the small [[Sea_of_Marmara|Sea of Marmara]] which in turn is connected to the Aegean Sea via the Strait of the Dardanelles.
sentence_22: To the north the Black Sea is connected to the [[Sea_of_Azov|Sea of Azov]] by the [[Kerch_Strait|Kerch Strait]].
sentence_23: The water level has varied significantly over geological time.
sentence_24: Due to these variations in the water level in the basin, the surrounding shelf and associated aprons have sometimes been dry land.
sentence_25: At certain critical water levels, connections with surrounding water bodies can become established.
sentence_26: It is through the most active of these connective routes, the [[Turkish_Straits|Turkish Straits]], that the Black Sea joins the [[World_ocean|world ocean]].
sentence_27: During geological periods when this hydrological link was not present, the Black Sea was an [[Endorheic_basin|endorheic basin]], operating independently of the global ocean system (similar to the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] today).
sentence_28: Currently, the Black Sea water level is relatively high; thus, water is being exchanged with the Mediterranean.
sentence_29: The Turkish Straits connect the Black Sea with the Aegean Sea and comprise the Bosporus, the Sea of Marmara, and the Dardanelles.
sentence_30: The [[Black_Sea_undersea_river|Black Sea undersea river]] is a current of particularly saline water flowing through the Bosporus Strait and along the seabed of the Black Sea, the first of its kind discovered.

sentence_38: The Black Sea is divided into two depositional basins—the Western Black Sea and Eastern Black Sea—separated by the Mid-Black Sea High, which includes the Andrusov Ridge, Tetyaev High, and Archangelsky High, extending south from the [[Crimea|Crimean Peninsula]].
sentence_39: The basin includes two distinct relict [[Back-arc_basin|back-arc basins]] which were initiated by the splitting of an [[Albian|Albian]] [[Volcanic_arc|volcanic arc]] and the [[Subduction|subduction]] of both the [[Paleo-Tethys_Ocean|Paleo]]- and Neo-[[Tethys_Ocean|Tethys]] Oceans, but the timings of these events remain uncertain.
sentence_40: Arc volcanism and extension occurred as the Neo-Tethys Ocean subducted under the southern margin of [[Laurasia|Laurasia]] during the [[Mesozoic|Mesozoic]].
sentence_41: Uplift and compressional deformation took place as the Neotethys continued to close.
sentence_42: Seismic surveys indicate that rifting began in the Western Black Sea in the [[Barremian|Barremian]] and [[Aptian|Aptian]] followed by the formation of oceanic crust 20 million years later in the [[Santonian|Santonian]].
sentence_43: Since its initiation, compressional tectonic environments led to [[Subsidence|subsidence]] in the basin, interspersed with extensional phases resulting in large-scale [[Volcanism|volcanism]] and numerous [[Orogeny|orogenies]], causing the uplift of the Greater Caucasus, [[Pontides|Pontides]], Southern [[Crimea|Crimean Peninsula]] and [[Balkan|Balkanides]] mountain ranges.
sentence_44: During the [[Messinian_salinity_crisis|Messinian salinity crisis]] in the neighboring Mediterranean Sea, water levels fell but without drying up the sea.
sentence_45: The ongoing collision between the Eurasian and [[African_Plate|African]] plates and westward escape of the [[Anatolian_Plate|Anatolian]] block along the North Anatolian Fault and [[East_Anatolian_Fault|East Anatolian Faults]] dictates the current tectonic regime, which features enhanced subsidence in the Black Sea basin and significant volcanic activity in the Anatolian region.
sentence_46: These geological mechanisms, in the long term, have caused the periodic isolations of the Black Sea from the rest of the global ocean system.
sentence_47: The large shelf to the north of the basin is up to 190 km (120 mi) wide and features a shallow apron with gradients between 1:40 and 1:1000.
sentence_48: The southern edge around Turkey and the eastern edge around [[Georgia_(country)|Georgia]], however, are typified by a narrow shelf that rarely exceeds 20 km (12 mi) in width and a steep apron that is typically 1:40 gradient with numerous submarine canyons and channel extensions.
sentence_49: The [[Euxine_abyssal_plain|Euxine abyssal plain]] in the centre of the Black Sea reaches a maximum depth of 2,212 metres (7,257.22 feet) just south of [[Yalta|Yalta]] on the [[Crimea|Crimean Peninsula]].
sentence_50: The [[Littoral_zone|littoral zone]] of the Black Sea is often referred to as the Pontic littoral or Pontic zone.
sentence_51: The area surrounding the Black Sea is commonly referred to as the Black Sea Region.
sentence_52: Its northern part lies within the [[Chernozem|Chernozem]] belt (black soil belt) which goes from eastern Croatia ([[Slavonia|Slavonia]]), along the [[Danube|Danube]] (northern Serbia, northern Bulgaria ([[Danubian_Plain_(Bulgaria)|Danubian Plain]]) and southern Romania (Wallachian Plain)) to northeast Ukraine and further across the Central Black Earth Region and southern Russia into [[Siberia|Siberia]].
sentence_53: The Paleo-[[Euxinia|Euxinian]] is described by the accumulation of eolian silt deposits (related to the [[Riss_glaciation|Riss glaciation]]) and the lowering of sea levels ([[Marine_isotope_stage|MIS]] 6, 8 and 10).
sentence_54: The Karangat [[Marine_transgression|marine transgression]] occurred during the [[Eemian_Interglacial|Eemian Interglacial]] (MIS 5e).
sentence_55: This may have been the highest sea levels reached in the late [[Pleistocene|Pleistocene]].
sentence_56: Based on this some scholars have suggested that the [[Crimean_Peninsula|Crimean Peninsula]] was isolated from the mainland by a shallow strait during the Eemian Interglacial.
sentence_57: The Neoeuxinian transgression began with an inflow of waters from the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]].
sentence_58: Neoeuxinian deposits are found in the Black Sea below -20 m water depth in three layers.
sentence_59: The upper layers correspond with the peak of the Khvalinian transgression, on the shelf shallow-water sands and [[Coquina|coquina]] mixed with silty sands and brackish-water fauna, and inside the Black Sea Depression hydrotroilite silts.
sentence_60: The middle layers on the shelf are sands with brackish-water mollusc shells.
sentence_61: Of continental origin, the lower level on the [[Continental_shelf|shelf]] is mostly [[Alluvial|alluvial]] sands with pebbles, mixed with less common lacustrine silts and freshwater [[Mollusc_shells|mollusc shells]].
sentence_62: Inside the Black Sea Depression they are [[Terrigenous_sediment|terrigenous]] non-carbonate [[Silts|silts]], and at the foot of the [[Continental_slope|continental slope]] [[Turbidite|turbidite]] sediments.
sentence_63: The Black Sea contains oil and natural gas resources but exploration in the sea is incomplete.
sentence_64: As of 2017, 20 wells are in place.
sentence_65: Throughout much of its existence, the Black Sea has had significant oil and gas-forming potential because of significant inflows of sediment and nutrient-rich waters.
sentence_66: However, this varies geographically.
sentence_67: For example, prospects are poorer off the coast of Bulgaria because of the large influx of sediment from the Danube which obscured sunlight and diluted organic-rich sediments.
sentence_68: Many of the discoveries to date have taken place offshore of Romania in the Western Black Sea and only a few discoveries have been made in the Eastern Black Sea.
sentence_69: During the [[Eocene|Eocene]], the Paratethys Ocean was partially isolated and sea levels fell.
sentence_70: During this time sand shed off the rising Balkanide, Pontide and Caucasus mountains trapped organic material in the Maykop Suite of rocks through the [[Oligocene|Oligocene]] and early [[Miocene|Miocene]].
sentence_71: Natural gas appears in rocks deposited in the Miocene and Pliocene by the paleo-Dnieper and pale-Dniester rivers, or in deep-water Oligocene-age rocks.
sentence_72: Serious exploration began in 1999 with two deep-water wells, Limanköy-1 and Limanköy-2, drilled in Turkish waters.
sentence_73: Next, the HPX (Hopa)-1 deepwater well targeted late Miocene sandstone units in Achara-Trialet fold belt (also known as the Gurian fold belt) along the Georgia-Turkey maritime border.
sentence_74: Although geologists inferred that these rocks might have hydrocarbons that migrated from the Maykop Suite, the well was unsuccessful.
sentence_75: No more drilling happened for five years after the HPX-1 well.
sentence_76: Then in 2010, Sinop-1 targeted carbonate reservoirs potentially charged from the nearby Maykop Suite on the Andrusov Ridge, but the well-struck only Cretaceous volcanic rocks.
sentence_77: Yassihöyük-1 encountered similar problems.
sentence_78: Other Turkish wells, Sürmene-1 and Sile-1 drilled in the Eastern Black Sea in 2011 and 2015 respectively tested four-way closures above Cretaceous volcanoes, with no results in either case.
sentence_79: A different Turkish well, Kastamonu-1 drilled in 2011 did successfully find thermogenic gas in Pliocene and Miocene shale-cored anticlines in the Western Black Sea.
sentence_80: A year later in 2012, Romania drilled Domino-1 which struck gas prompting the drilling of other wells in the Neptun Deep.
sentence_81: In 2016, the Bulgarian well Polshkov-1 targeted Maykop Suite sandstones in the Polshkov High and Russia is in the process of drilling Jurassic carbonates on the Shatsky Ridge as of 2018.
sentence_82: In August 2020, [[Turkey|Turkey]] has found 320 billion cubic meters of [[Natural_gas|natural gas]] in the biggest ever discovery in the Black Sea, and hopes to begin production by 2023.
sentence_83: The Turkish [[Fatih_(drillship)|drilling ship Fatih]], had been carrying out exploration operations in the Tuna-1 sector in the western Black Sea for the past month.
sentence_84: The sector is near where [[Romania|Romania]] has also found gas reserves.
sentence_85: Current names of the sea are usually equivalents of the English name "Black Sea", including these given in the countries bordering the sea:

Laz and [[Mingrelian_language|Mingrelian]]: უჩა ზუღა, IPA: [[Help:IPA|[utʃɑ zuɣɑ]], or simply ზუღა, IPA: [[Help:IPA|[zuɣɑ]], "Sea"

sentence_86: Such names have not yet been shown conclusively to predate the 13th century.
sentence_87: In [[Greece|Greece]], the historical name "Euxine Sea" holds a different meaning (see below), is still widely used:

sentence_88: The principal [[Greek_language|Greek]] name Póntos Áxeinos is generally accepted to be a rendering of [[Iranian_languages|Iranian]] word *axšaina- (dark colored), compare [[Avestan_language|Avestan]] axšaēna- (dark colored), [[Old_Persian_language|Old Persian]] axšaina- ([[Turquoise|turquoise]] colored), [[Middle_Persian_language|Middle Persian]] axšēn/xašēn (blue), and [[New_Persian_language|New Persian]] xašīn (blue), as well as [[Ossetic_language|Ossetic]] œxsīn (dark gray).
sentence_89: Ancient Greek voyagers adopted the name as Á-xe(i)nos, identified with the Greek word áxeinos (inhospitable).
sentence_90: The name Πόντος Ἄξεινος Póntos Áxeinos (Inhospitable Sea), first attested in [[Pindar|Pindar]] (c. 475 BC), was considered an ill omen and was [[Euphemism|euphemized]] to its opposite, Εὔξεινος Πόντος Eúxeinos Póntos (Hospitable Sea), also first attested in Pindar.
sentence_91: This became the commonly used designation in Greek, although in mythological contexts the "true" name Póntos Áxeinos remained favored.
sentence_92: [[Strabo|Strabo]]'s [[Geographica|Geographica]] (1.2.10) reports that in antiquity, the Black Sea was often simply called "the Sea" (ὁ πόντος ho Pontos).
sentence_93: He also thought the Black Sea was called "inhospitable" before Greek colonization for its difficult navigation and hostile [[Barbarian|barbarian]] natives (7.3.6), and that the name was changed to "hospitable" after the [[Milesians_(Greek)|Milesians]] colonized the [[Pontus_(region)|Pontus]] region of the southern shoreline, bringing it within Greek civilization.
sentence_94: Popular supposition derives "Black Sea" from the dark color of the water or climatic conditions.
sentence_95: Rather, it referred to a system of [[Color_in_Chinese_culture|color symbolism]] representing the cardinal directions, with black or dark for north, red for south, white for west, and green or light blue for east.
sentence_96: Hence "Black Sea" meant "Northern Sea", while "Red Sea" from the time of [[Herodotus|Herodotus]] (c. 450 BC) designated the waters south of the known world, the [[Indian_Ocean|Indian Ocean]] together with today's [[Persian_Gulf|Persian Gulf]] and [[Red_Sea|Red Sea]].
sentence_97: According to this scheme, the name could not have originated with the [[Scythians|Scythians]], who principally roamed north of the sea, but only with a people living between the northern (black) and southern (red) seas: this points to the [[Achaemenid_Empire|Achaemenids]] (550–330 BC).
sentence_98: In the [[Bundahishn|Greater Bundahishn]], a [[Middle_Persian|Middle Persian]] [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrian]] scripture, the Black Sea is called Siyābun.
sentence_99: In the tenth-century Persian geography book [[Hudud_al-'Alam|Hudud al-'Alam]], the Black Sea is called Sea of the Georgians (daryā-yi Gurz).
sentence_100: [[The_Georgian_Chronicles|The Georgian Chronicles]] use the name zğua sperisa ზღუა სპერისა (Sea of Speri) after the [[Kartvelian_peoples|Kartvelian]] tribe of Speris or [[Saspers|Saspers]].
sentence_101: Other modern names such as Chyornoye more and Karadeniz, originated in the 13th century.
sentence_102: A 1570 map Asiae Nova Descriptio from [[Abraham_Ortelius|Abraham Ortelius]]'s Theatrum Orbis Terrarum labels the sea Mar Maggior (Great Sea), compare Latin mare major.
sentence_103: English writers of the 18th century often used Euxine Sea ([[English|/ˈjuːksɪn/]] or [[English|/ˈjuːkˌsaɪn/]]), for example [[Edward_Gibbon|Edward Gibbon]] throughout his [[The_History_of_the_Decline_and_Fall_of_the_Roman_Empire|Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire]].
sentence_104: During the [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]], it was called either Bahr-e Siyah or Karadeniz, both meaning "Black Sea" in [[Ottoman_Turkish_language|Turkish]].
sentence_105: The Black Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, and is the world's largest body of water with a [[Meromictic|meromictic]] basin.
sentence_106: The deep waters do not mix with the upper layers of water that receive oxygen from the atmosphere.
sentence_107: As a result, over 90% of the deeper Black Sea volume is [[Anoxic_waters|anoxic]] water.
sentence_108: The Black Sea's circulation patterns are primarily controlled by basin topography and [[Fluvial|fluvial]] inputs, which result in a strongly stratified vertical structure.
sentence_109: Because of the extreme stratification, it is classified as a [[Estuary#Salt_wedge|salt wedge estuary]].
sentence_110: The Black Sea only experiences water transfer with the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]], so all inflow and outflow occurs in the [[Bosporus|Bosporus]] and [[Dardanelles|Dardanelles]].
sentence_111: Inflow from the Mediterranean has a higher salinity and density than the outflow, creating the classic estuarine circulation.
sentence_112: This means that the inflow of dense water from the Mediterranean occurs at the bottom of the basin while the outflow of fresher Black Sea surface-water into the [[Marmara_Sea|Marmara Sea]] occurs near the surface.
sentence_113: The outflow is 16 000 m/s (around 500 km/year) and the inflow is 11 000 m/s (around 350 km/year), acc to Gregg (2002).
sentence_114: The following water budget can be estimated:
sentence_115: The southern sill of the Bosporus is located at -36.5 m below present sea level (deepest spot of the shallowest cross-section in the Bosporus, located in front of [[Dolmabahçe_Palace|Dolmabahçe Palace]]) and has a wet section of around 38 000 m2.
sentence_116: Inflow and outflow current speeds are averaged around 0.3 to 0.4 m/s, but much higher speeds are found locally, inducing significant turbulence and vertical shear.
sentence_117: This allows for turbulent mixing of the two layers.
sentence_118: Surface water leaves the Black Sea with a salinity of 17 [[Practical_salinity_unit|Practical salinity unit]] (PSU) and reaches the Mediterranean with a salinity of 34 PSU.
sentence_119: Likewise, an inflow of the Mediterranean with salinity 38.5 PSU experiences a decrease to about 34 psu.
sentence_120: Mean surface circulation is [[Cyclonic_rotation|cyclonic]] and waters around the perimeter of the Black Sea circulate in a basin-wide shelfbreak [[Gyre|gyre]] known as the Rim Current.
sentence_121: The Rim Current has a maximum velocity of about 50–100 cm/s.
sentence_122: Within this feature, two smaller cyclonic gyres operate, occupying the eastern and western sectors of the basin.
sentence_123: The Eastern and Western Gyres are well-organized systems in the winter but dissipate into a series of interconnected [[Eddy_(fluid_dynamics)|eddies]] in the summer and autumn.
sentence_124: Mesoscale activity in the peripheral flow becomes more pronounced during these warmer seasons and is subject to interannual variability.
sentence_125: Outside of the Rim Current, numerous quasi-permanent coastal eddies are formed as a result of upwelling around the coastal apron and "wind curl" mechanisms.
sentence_126: The intra-annual strength of these features is controlled by seasonal atmospheric and fluvial variations.
sentence_127: During the spring, the Batumi eddy forms in the southeastern corner of the sea.
sentence_128: Beneath the surface waters—from about 50–100 meters—there exists a halocline that stops at the Cold Intermediate Layer (CIL).
sentence_129: This layer is composed of cool, salty surface waters, which are the result of localized atmospheric cooling and decreased fluvial input during the winter months.
sentence_130: It is the remnant of the winter surface mixed layer.
sentence_131: The base of the CIL is marked by a major [[Pycnocline|pycnocline]] at about 100–200 metres (330–660 ft) and this density disparity is the major mechanism for isolation of the deep water.
sentence_132: Below the pycnocline is the Deep Water mass, where salinity increases to 22.3 PSU and temperatures rise to around 8.9 °C.
sentence_133: The hydrochemical environment shifts from oxygenated to anoxic, as bacterial decomposition of sunken biomass utilizes all of the free oxygen.
sentence_134: Weak [[Geothermal_heating|geothermal heating]] and long [[Residence_time_(fluid_dynamics)|residence time]] create a very thick convective bottom layer.
sentence_135: The [[Black_Sea_undersea_river|Black Sea undersea river]] is a current of particularly saline water flowing through the Bosporus Strait and along the seabed of the Black Sea.
sentence_136: The discovery of the river announced on August 1, 2010, was made by scientists at the [[University_of_Leeds|University of Leeds]] and is the first of its kind in the world.
sentence_137: The undersea river stems from salty water spilling through the Bosporus Strait from the Mediterranean Sea into the Black Sea, where the water has a lower salt content.
sentence_138: Because of the anoxic water at depth, organic matter, including [[Human_impact_on_the_environment|anthropogenic]] artifacts such as boat hulls, are well preserved.
sentence_139: During periods of high surface productivity, short-lived [[Algae|algal]] blooms form organic rich layers known as [[Sapropel|sapropels]].
sentence_140: Scientists have reported an annual [[Phytoplankton|phytoplankton]] bloom that can be seen in many NASA images of the region.
sentence_141: As a result of these characteristics the Black Sea has gained interest from the field of [[Marine_archaeology|marine archaeology]] as ancient shipwrecks in excellent states of preservation have been discovered, such as the [[Byzantine|Byzantine]] wreck [[Sinop_D|Sinop D]], located in the anoxic layer off the coast of [[Sinop,_Turkey|Sinop, Turkey]].
sentence_142: Modelling shows that, in the event of an [[Asteroid_impact|asteroid impact]] on the Black Sea, the release of [[Hydrogen_sulfide|hydrogen sulfide]] clouds would pose a threat to health—and perhaps even life—for people living on the Black Sea coast.
sentence_143: There have been isolated reports of flares on the Black Sea occurring during thunderstorms, possibly caused by lightning igniting combustible gas seeping up from the sea depths.
sentence_144: See also: [[List_of_fish_of_the_Black_Sea|List of fish of the Black Sea]]
sentence_145: The Black Sea supports an active and dynamic marine ecosystem, dominated by species suited to the [[Brackish|brackish]], nutrient-rich, conditions.
sentence_146: As with all marine food webs, the Black Sea features a range of [[Trophic_level|trophic]] groups, with [[Autotrophic|autotrophic]] algae, including [[Diatoms|diatoms]] and [[Dinoflagellates|dinoflagellates]], acting as primary producers.
sentence_147: The fluvial systems draining Eurasia and central Europe introduce large volumes of sediment and dissolved nutrients into the Black Sea, but the distribution of these nutrients is controlled by the degree of physiochemical stratification, which is, in turn, dictated by seasonal physiographic development.
sentence_148: During winter, strong wind promotes convective overturning and upwelling of nutrients, while high summer temperatures result in a marked vertical stratification and a warm, shallow mixed layer.
sentence_149: Day length and [[Insolation|insolation]] intensity also controls the extent of the [[Photic_zone|photic zone]].
sentence_150: Subsurface productivity is limited by nutrient availability, as the anoxic bottom waters act as a sink for reduced nitrate, in the form of ammonia.
sentence_151: The [[Benthic|benthic]] zone also plays an important role in Black Sea nutrient cycling, as chemosynthetic organisms and anoxic geochemical pathways recycle nutrients which can be upwelled to the photic zone, enhancing productivity.
sentence_152: In total, Black Sea's biodiversity contains around one-third of Mediterranean's and is experiencing natural and artificial invasions or Mediterranizations.
sentence_153: The main phytoplankton groups present in the Black Sea are [[Dinoflagellates|dinoflagellates]], [[Diatoms|diatoms]], [[Coccolithophores|coccolithophores]] and [[Cyanobacteria|cyanobacteria]].
sentence_154: Generally, the annual cycle of phytoplankton development comprises significant diatom and dinoflagellate-dominated spring production, followed by a weaker mixed assemblage of community development below the seasonal thermocline during summer months and surface-intensified autumn production.
sentence_155: This pattern of productivity is also augmented by an [[Emiliania_huxleyi|Emiliania huxleyi]] bloom during the late spring and summer months.

list.value: Annual dinoflagellate distribution is defined by an extended bloom period in subsurface waters during the late spring and summer. In November, subsurface plankton production is combined with surface production, due to vertical mixing of water masses and nutrients such as [[Nitrite|nitrite]]. The major bloom-forming dinoflagellate species in the Black Sea is [[Gymnodinium|Gymnodinium]] sp. Estimates of dinoflagellate diversity in the Black Sea range from 193 to 267 species. This level of species richness is relatively low in comparison to the Mediterranean Sea, which is attributable to the brackish conditions, low water transparency and presence of [[Anoxic_waters|anoxic]] bottom waters. It is also possible that the low winter temperatures below 4 °C (39 °F) of the Black Sea prevent [[Thermophilous|thermophilous]] species from becoming established. The relatively high organic matter content of Black Sea surface water favor the development of [[Heterotrophic|heterotrophic]] (an organism that uses organic carbon for growth) and mixotrophic dinoflagellates species (able to exploit different trophic pathways), relative to autotrophs. Despite its unique hydrographic setting, there are no confirmed [[Endemism|endemic]] dinoflagellate species in the Black Sea.

The Black Sea is populated by many species of the marine diatom, which commonly exist as colonies of [[Unicellular|unicellular]], non-motile auto- and [[Heterotrophic|heterotrophic]] [[Algae|algae]]. The life-cycle of most diatoms can be described as 'boom and bust' and the Black Sea is no exception, with diatom blooms occurring in surface waters throughout the year, most reliably during March. In simple terms, the phase of rapid population growth in diatoms is caused by the in-wash of silicon-bearing terrestrial sediments, and when the supply of silicon is exhausted, the diatoms begin to sink out of the photic zone and produce resting [[Cysts|cysts]]. Additional factors such as predation by zooplankton and [[Ammonium|ammonium]]-based regenerated production also have a role to play in the annual diatom cycle. Typically, Proboscia alata blooms during spring and Pseudosolenia calcar-avis blooms during the autumn.

Coccolithophores are a type of [[Motility|motile]], [[Autotrophic|autotrophic]] [[Phytoplankton|phytoplankton]] that produce CaCO3 plates, known as [[Coccoliths|coccoliths]], as part of their life cycle. In the Black Sea, the main period of [[Coccolithophore|coccolithophore]] growth occurs after the bulk of the dinoflagellate growth has taken place. In May, the dinoflagellates move below the seasonal [[Thermocline|thermocline]], into deeper waters, where more nutrients are available. This permits coccolithophores to utilize the nutrients in the upper waters, and by the end of May, with favorable light and temperature conditions, growth rates reach their highest. The major bloom-forming species is [[Emiliania_huxleyi|Emiliania huxleyi]], which is also responsible for the release of [[Dimethyl_sulfide|dimethyl sulfide]] into the atmosphere. Overall, coccolithophore diversity is low in the Black Sea, and although recent sediments are dominated by E. huxleyi, Braarudosphaera bigelowii, [[Holocene|Holocene]] sediments have also been shown to contain Helicopondosphaera and Discolithina species.

Cyanobacteria are a phylum of [[Picoplankton|picoplanktonic]] (plankton ranging in size from 0.2 to 2.0 [[Micrometre|µm]]) [[Bacteria|bacteria]] that obtain their energy via [[Photosynthesis|photosynthesis]], and are present throughout the world's oceans. They exhibit a range of morphologies, including filamentous colonies and [[Biofilms|biofilms]]. In the Black Sea, several species are present, and as an example, Synechococcus spp. can be found throughout the photic zone, although concentration decreases with increasing depth. Other factors which exert an influence on distribution include nutrient availability, predation, and salinity.

The Black Sea along with the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] is part of the Zebra mussel's native range. The mussel has been accidentally introduced around the world and become an [[Invasive_species|invasive species]] where it has been introduced.

The Common Carp's native range extends to The Black Sea along with the Caspian Sea and [[Aral_Sea|Aral Sea]]. Like the Zebra mussel the Common Carp is an invasive species when introduced to other habitats.

Is another native fish that is also found in the Caspian Sea. It preys upon Zebra mussels. Like the mussels and common carp it has become invasive when introduced to other environments, like the [[Great_Lakes|Great Lakes]].

Marine mammals present within the basin include two species of dolphins ([[Common_dolphin|common]] and [[Bottlenose_dolphin|bottlenose]]) and [[Harbour_porpoise|harbour porpoise]] inhabit the sea although all of these are endangered due to pressures and impacts by human activities. All the three species have been classified as a distinct subspecies from those in the Mediterranean and in Atlantic Seas and endemic to Black and Azov Seas, and are more active during nights in Turkish Straits. However, construction of the [[Crimean_Bridge_(Crimea)|Crimean Bridge]] caused increases in nutrients and planktons in the waters, attracting large numbers of fish and more than 1,000 bottlenose dolphins. On the other hand, however, others claim that construction may cause devastating damages on ecosystem including dolphins.

Critically endangered [[Mediterranean_monk_seal|Mediterranean monk seals]] were historically abundant in Black Sea, and are regarded to have become extinct from the basin in 1997. Monk seals were present at the [[Snake_Island_(Black_Sea)|Snake Island]] until 1950s, and several locations such as the Danube Plavni Nature Reserve and [[Doğankent|Doğankent]] were last of [[Hauling-out|hauling-out]] sites in post-1990. Very few animals still thrive in the [[Sea_of_Marmara|Sea of Marmara]].
Ongoing Mediterranizations may or may not boost in increases of cetacean diversity in Turkish Straits hence in Black and Azov basins.

Various species of [[Pinniped|pinnipeds]], [[Sea_otter|sea otter]], and [[Beluga_whale|beluga whales]] were introduced into the Black Sea by mankind and later escaped either by accidental or purported causes. Of these, [[Grey_seal|grey seal]] and beluga whales have been recorded with successful, long-term occurrences.

[[Great_white_shark|Great white sharks]] are known to reach into the Sea of Marmara and Bosporus Strait and [[Basking_shark|basking shark]] into Dardanelles although it is unclear whether or not these sharks may reach into the Black and Azov basins.

sentence_156: Since the 1960s, rapid industrial expansion along the Black Sea coast line and the construction of a major dam has significantly increased annual variability in the N:P:Si ratio in the basin.
sentence_157: In coastal areas, the biological effect of these changes has been an increase in the frequency of monospecific phytoplankton blooms, with diatom bloom frequency increasing by a factor of 2.5 and non-diatom bloom frequency increasing by a factor of 6.
sentence_158: The non-diatoms, such as the prymnesiophytes Emiliania huxleyi (coccolithophore), Chromulina sp., and the Euglenophyte Eutreptia lanowii are able to out-compete diatom species because of the limited availability of Si, a necessary constituent of diatom frustules.
sentence_159: As a consequence of these blooms, benthic macrophyte populations were deprived of light, while anoxia caused mass mortality in marine animals.
sentence_160: The decline in macrophytes was further compounded by overfishing during the 1970s, while the invasive ctenophore Mnemiopsis reduced the biomass of copepods and other zooplankton in the late 1980s.
sentence_161: Additionally, an alien species—the [[Warty_comb_jelly|warty comb jelly]] (Mnemiopsis leidyi)—was able to establish itself in the basin, exploding from a few individuals to estimated biomass of one billion metric tons.
sentence_162: The change in species composition in Black Sea waters also has consequences for hydrochemistry, as Ca-producing coccolithophores influence salinity and pH, although these ramifications have yet to be fully quantified.
sentence_163: In central Black Sea waters, Si levels were also significantly reduced, due to a decrease in the flux of Si associated with advection across isopycnal surfaces.
sentence_164: This phenomenon demonstrates the potential for localized alterations in Black Sea nutrient input to have basin-wide effects.
sentence_165: Pollution reduction and regulation efforts have led to a partial recovery of the Black Sea ecosystem during the 1990s, and an EU monitoring exercise, 'EROS21', revealed decreased N and P values, relative to the 1989 peak.
sentence_166: Recently, scientists have noted signs of ecological recovery, in part due to the construction of new sewage treatment plants in Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria in connection with membership in the European Union.
sentence_167: Mnemiopsis leidyi populations have been checked with the arrival of another alien species which feeds on them.
sentence_168: In the past, the range of the [[Asiatic_lion|Asiatic lion]] extended from [[South_Asia|South Asia]] to the [[Balkans|Balkans]], possibly up to the Danube.
sentence_169: Places like Turkey and the [[Trans-Caucasus|Trans-Caucasus]] were in this range.
sentence_170: The [[Caspian_tiger|Caspian tiger]] occurred in [[Eastern_Anatolia_Region|eastern Turkey]] and the [[Caucasus|Caucasus]], at least.
sentence_171: The lyuti zver (Old East Slavic for "fierce animal") that was encountered by [[Vladimir_II_Monomakh|Vladimir II Monomakh]], Velikiy Kniaz of [[Kievan_Rus'|Kievan Rus']] (which ranged to the Black Sea in the south), may have been a tiger or [[Leopard|leopard]], rather than a [[Steppe_wolf|wolf]] or [[Eurasian_lynx|lynx]], due to the way it behaved towards him and his [[Horse|horse]].
sentence_172: Short-term climatic variation in the Black Sea region is significantly influenced by the operation of the North Atlantic oscillation, the climatic mechanisms resulting from the interaction between the north Atlantic and mid-latitude air masses.
sentence_173: While the exact mechanisms causing the North Atlantic Oscillation remain unclear, it is thought the climate conditions established in western Europe mediate the heat and precipitation fluxes reaching Central Europe and Eurasia, regulating the formation of winter [[Cyclones|cyclones]], which are largely responsible for regional [[Precipitation_(meteorology)|precipitation]] inputs and influence Mediterranean Sea Surface Temperatures (SST's).
sentence_174: The relative strength of these systems also limits the amount of cold air arriving from northern regions during winter.
sentence_175: Other influencing factors include the regional topography, as depressions and storms systems arriving from the [[Mediterranean|Mediterranean]] are funneled through the low land around the Bosporus, [[Pontic_Mountains|Pontic]] and Caucasus mountain ranges acting as waveguides, limiting the speed and paths of cyclones passing through the region.
sentence_176: Main article: [[List_of_islands_in_the_Black_Sea|List of islands in the Black Sea]]
sentence_177: The Black Sea is connected to the [[World_Ocean|World Ocean]] by a chain of two shallow straits, the [[Dardanelles|Dardanelles]] and the [[Bosporus|Bosporus]].
sentence_178: The Dardanelles is 55 m (180 ft) deep and the Bosporus is as shallow as 36 m (118 ft).
sentence_179: By comparison, at the height of the last [[Quaternary_glaciation|ice age]], sea levels were more than 100 m (330 ft) lower than they are now.
sentence_180: There is also evidence that water levels in the Black Sea were considerably lower at some point during the post-glacial period.
sentence_181: Some researchers theorize that the Black Sea had been a landlocked freshwater lake (at least in upper layers) during the last glaciation and for some time after.
sentence_182: In the aftermath of the last glacial period, water levels in the Black Sea and the Aegean Sea rose independently until they were high enough to exchange water.
sentence_183: The exact timeline of this development is still subject to debate.
sentence_184: One possibility is that the Black Sea filled first, with excess freshwater flowing over the Bosporus sill and eventually into the Mediterranean Sea.
sentence_185: There are also catastrophic scenarios, such as the "[[Black_Sea_deluge_theory|Black Sea deluge theory]]" put forward by William Ryan, [[Walter_Pitman_(geologist)|Walter Pitman]] and .
sentence_186: Main article: [[Black_Sea_deluge_hypothesis|Black Sea deluge hypothesis]]
sentence_187: The Black Sea deluge is a hypothesized catastrophic rise in the level of the Black Sea circa 5600 BC due to waters from the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]] breaching a sill in the [[Bosporus|Bosporus]] Strait.
sentence_188: The hypothesis was headlined when [[The_New_York_Times|The New York Times]] published it in December 1996, shortly before it was published in an [[Academic_journal|academic journal]].
sentence_189: While it is agreed that the sequence of events described did occur, there is debate over the suddenness, dating, and magnitude of the events.
sentence_190: Relevant to the hypothesis is that its description has led some to connect this catastrophe with prehistoric [[Deluge_(mythology)|flood myths]].
sentence_191: The Black Sea was a busy waterway on the crossroads of the ancient world: the Balkans to the west, the Eurasian steppes to the north, the Caucasus and Central Asia to the east, Asia Minor and Mesopotamia to the south, and Greece to the south-west.
sentence_192: The [[Varna_Necropolis|oldest processed gold in the world]] was found in [[Varna|Varna]], Bulgaria, and [[Greek_mythology|Greek mythology]] portrays the [[Argonauts|Argonauts]] as sailing on the Black Sea.
sentence_193: The land at the eastern end of the Black Sea, [[Colchis|Colchis]], (now [[Georgia_(country)|Georgia]]), marked for the Greeks the edge of the known world.
sentence_194: The steppes to the north of the Black Sea have been suggested as the original homeland (Urheimat) of the speakers of the [[Proto-Indo-European_language|Proto-Indo-European language]], (PIE) the progenitor of the [[Indo-European_languages|Indo-European language]] family, by some scholars such as [[Marija_Gimbutas|Marija Gimbutas]]; others move the homeland further east towards the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]], yet others to [[Anatolia|Anatolia]].
sentence_195: Greek presence in the Black Sea began at least as early as the 9th century BC with [[Greek_colonisation|colonization]] of the Black Sea's southern coast.
sentence_196: By 500 BC, permanent Greek communities existed all around the Black Sea and a lucrative trade network connected the entirety of the Black Sea to the wider Mediterranean.
sentence_197: While Greek colonies generally maintained very close cultural ties to their founding [[Polis|polis]], Greek colonies in the Black Sea began to develop their own Black Sea Greek culture, know today as [[Pontic_Greeks|Pontic]].
sentence_198: The coastal community of Black Sea Greeks remained a prominent part of the Greek World for centuries.
sentence_199: The Black Sea became a virtual Ottoman Navy lake within five years of [[Republic_of_Genoa|Genoa]] losing the [[Crimea|Crimean Peninsula]] in 1479, after which the only Western merchant vessels to sail its waters were those of [[Venice|Venice]]'s old rival Ragusa.
sentence_200: This restriction was challenged by the [[Russian_Navy|Russian Navy]] from 1783 until the relaxation of export controls in 1789 because of the [[French_Revolution|French Revolution]].
sentence_201: The Black Sea was a significant naval theatre of [[Naval_warfare_of_World_War_I#Black_Sea|World War I]] and saw both naval and land battles during [[Eastern_Front_(World_War_II)|World War II]].
sentence_202: Ancient trade routes in the region are currently being extensively studied by scientists, as the Black Sea was sailed by [[Hittites|Hittites]], [[Carians|Carians]], [[Colchis|Colchians]], [[Thracians|Thracians]], [[Ancient_Greeks|Greeks]], [[Achaemenid_Empire|Persians]], [[Cimmerians|Cimmerians]], [[Scythians|Scythians]], [[Ancient_Rome|Romans]], [[Byzantine_Greeks|Byzantines]], [[Goths|Goths]], [[Huns|Huns]], [[Avars_(Carpathians)|Avars]], [[Slavs|Slavs]], [[Varangians|Varangians]], [[Crusaders|Crusaders]], [[Republic_of_Venice|Venetians]], [[Republic_of_Genoa|Genoese]], [[Colchis|Georgians]], [[Tatars|Tatars]] and Ottomans.
sentence_203: Perhaps the most promising areas in deepwater archaeology are the quest for submerged prehistoric settlements in the continental shelf and for ancient shipwrecks in the anoxic zone, which are expected to be exceptionally well preserved due to the absence of oxygen.
sentence_204: This concentration of [[Historical_powers|historical powers]], combined with the preservative qualities of the deep [[Anoxic_waters|anoxic waters]] of the Black Sea, has attracted increased interest from [[Marine_archaeology|marine archaeologists]] who have begun to discover a large number of ancient ships and organic remains in a high state of preservation.
sentence_205: According to NATO, the Black sea is a strategic corridor that provides smuggling channels for moving legal and illegal goods including drugs, radioactive materials, and counterfeit goods that can be used to finance terrorism.
sentence_206: According to the [[International_Transport_Workers'_Federation|International Transport Workers' Federation]] 2013 study, there were at least 30 operating merchant [[Seaport|seaports]] in the Black Sea (including at least 12 in [[Ukraine|Ukraine]]).
sentence_207: According to the International Transport Workers' Federation 2013 study, there were around 2,400 commercial vessels operating in the Black Sea.
sentence_208: [[European_anchovy|Anchovy]]: the Turkish commercial fishing fleet catches around 300,000 tons per year on average, and fishery carried out mainly in winter and the highest portion of the stock is caught between November and December.
sentence_209: Since the 1980s, the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]] started offshore drilling for [[Petroleum|petroleum]] in the sea's western portion (adjoining [[Ukraine|Ukraine]]'s coast).
sentence_210: Independent Ukraine continued and intensified that effort within its [[Exclusive_economic_zone|exclusive economic zone]], inviting major international oil companies for exploration.
sentence_211: Discovery of the new, massive oilfields in the area stimulated an influx of foreign investments.
sentence_212: It also provoked a short-term peaceful territorial dispute with [[Romania|Romania]] which was resolved in 2011 by an international court redefining the exclusive economic zones between the two countries.
sentence_213: In the years following the end of the [[Cold_War|Cold War]], the popularity of the Black Sea as a [[Tourism|tourist]] destination steadily increased.
sentence_214: Tourism at Black Sea resorts became one of the region's growth industries.
sentence_215: The following is a list of notable Black Sea resort towns:

section_37.value: International and military use of the Straits

sentence_216: The [[Montreux_Convention_Regarding_the_Regime_of_the_Turkish_Straits|1936 Montreux Convention]] provides for free passage of civilian ships between the international waters of the Black and the Mediterranean Seas.
sentence_217: However, a single country (Turkey) has complete control over the straits connecting the two seas.
sentence_218: Military ships are separate categories from civilian ships and they can only pass through the straits if the ship is belonging to a Black Seapower.
sentence_219: Other military ships have the right to pass through the straits if they are not in a war against Turkey and they can stay in the Black Sea basin for a limited time.
sentence_220: The 1982 amendments to the Montreux Convention allow Turkey to close the Straits at its discretion in both wartime and peacetime.
sentence_221: The 1936 Montreux Convention governs the passage of vessels between the Black, the Mediterranean and Aegean Seas and the presence of military vessels belonging to non-[[Littoral|littoral]] states in the Black Sea waters.
sentence_222: In December 2018, the [[Kerch_Strait_incident|Kerch Strait incident]] took place.
sentence_223: The Russian Navy and Coast guard took control of three ships belonging to their counterparts.
sentence_224: The ships were trying to enter the Black Sea
sentence_225: Main articles: [[Black_Sea_Euroregion|Black Sea Euroregion]], [[Superior_Prut_and_Lower_Danube|Superior Prut and Lower Danube]], [[Black_Sea_Games|Black Sea Games]], and Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation

title: Andorra
sentence_0: Not to be confused with the Italian town of [[Andora|Andora]].
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Andorra_(disambiguation)|Andorra (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: Andorra ([[English|/ænˈdɔːrə/]] (listen), also [[British_English|UK]]: [[English|/ænˈdɒrə/]]; Catalan: [[Catalan|[ənˈdorə]]), officially the Principality of Andorra ([[Catalan_language|Catalan]]: Principat d'Andorra), is a sovereign landlocked [[Microstate|microstate]] on the [[Iberian_Peninsula|Iberian Peninsula]], in the eastern [[Pyrenees|Pyrenees]], bordered by [[France|France]] to the north and [[Spain|Spain]] to the south.
sentence_3: Believed to have been created by [[Charlemagne|Charlemagne]], Andorra was ruled by the [[Count_of_Urgell|count of Urgell]] until 988, when it was transferred to the Roman Catholic Diocese of Urgell.
sentence_4: The present principality was formed by [[Paréage_of_Andorra_1278|a charter in 1278]].
sentence_5: It is known as a principality as it is a diarchy headed by two princes: the Bishop of Urgell in Catalonia, Spain, and the [[President_of_the_French_Republic|President of the French Republic]].
sentence_6: Andorra is the [[European_microstates|sixth-smallest nation in Europe]], having an area of 468 square kilometres (181 sq mi) and a population of approximately 77,006.
sentence_7: The [[Andorran_people|Andorran people]] are a [[Italic_peoples|Romance]] ethnic group of originally [[Catalans|Catalan]] descent.
sentence_8: Andorra is the 16th-smallest country in the world by land and the 11th-smallest by population.
sentence_9: Its capital, [[Andorra_la_Vella|Andorra la Vella]], is the highest capital city in Europe, at an elevation of 1,023 metres (3,356 feet) above sea level.
sentence_10: The official language is [[Catalan_language|Catalan]], but Spanish, Portuguese, and French are also commonly spoken.
sentence_11: Tourism in Andorra sees an estimated 10.2 million visitors annually.
sentence_12: Andorra is not a member of the [[European_Union|European Union]], but the [[Euro|euro]] is its official currency.
sentence_13: It has been a member of the [[United_Nations|United Nations]] since 1993.
sentence_14: In 2013, Andorra had [[List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy|the highest life expectancy in the world]] at 81 years, according to the [[Global_Burden_of_Disease_Study|Global Burden of Disease Study]].
sentence_15: The origin of the word Andorra is unknown, although several hypotheses have been formulated.
sentence_16: The oldest derivation of the word Andorra is from the Greek historian Polybius ([[The_Histories_(Polybius)|The Histories]] III, 35, 1) who describes the Andosins, an [[Iberians|Iberian]] [[Pre-Roman_peoples_of_the_Iberian_Peninsula|Pre-Roman tribe]], as historically located in the valleys of Andorra and facing the [[Ancient_Carthage|Carthaginian]] army in its passage through the Pyrenees during the [[Punic_Wars|Punic Wars]].
sentence_17: The word Andosini or Andosins (Ἀνδοσίνοι) may derive from the [[Basque_language|Basque]] handia whose meaning is "big" or "giant".
sentence_18: The Andorran [[Toponymy|toponymy]] shows evidence of Basque language in the area.
sentence_19: Another theory suggests that the word Andorra may derive from the old word Anorra that contains the Basque word ur (water).
sentence_20: Another theory suggests that Andorra may derive from [[Arabic_language|Arabic]]: الدارة‎, [[Romanization_of_Arabic|romanized]]: al-darra, meaning "the thickly wooded place".
sentence_21: When the [[Arabs|Arabs]] and [[Moors|Moors]] conquered the Iberian Peninsula, the valleys of the High Pyrenees were covered by large tracts of forest.
sentence_22: These regions were not administered by Muslims, because of the geographic difficulty of direct rule.
sentence_23: Other theories suggest that the term derives from the [[Navarro-Aragonese|Navarro-Aragonese]] andurrial, which means "land covered with bushes" or "scrubland".
sentence_24: The [[Folk_etymology|folk etymology]] holds that [[Charlemagne|Charlemagne]] had named the region as a reference to the Biblical [[Canaan|Canaanite]] valley of [[Endor_(village)|Endor]] or [[Endor_(village)|Andor]] (where the [[Midianites|Midianites]] had been defeated), a name bestowed by his heir and son [[Louis_le_Debonnaire|Louis le Debonnaire]] after defeating the Moors in the "wild valleys of Hell".
sentence_25: Main article: History of Andorra
sentence_26: La Balma de la [[La_Margineda|Margineda]], found by archaeologists at [[Sant_Julià_de_Lòria|Sant Julià de Lòria]], was settled in 9,500 BC as a passing place between the two sides of the Pyrenees.
sentence_27: The seasonal camp was perfectly located for hunting and fishing by the groups of hunter-gatherers from [[Ariège_(river)|Ariege]] and [[Segre_(river)|Segre]].
sentence_28: During the [[Neolithic_Age|Neolithic Age]], a group of people moved to the [[Madriu-Perafita-Claror_Valley|Valley of Madriu]] (the present-day Natural Parc located in [[Escaldes-Engordany|Escaldes-Engordany]] declared [[UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]]) as a permanent camp in 6640 BC.
sentence_29: The population of the valley grew cereals, raised domestic livestock, and developed a commercial trade with people from the [[Sègre_(department)|Segre]] and [[Occitania|Occitania]].
sentence_30: Other archaeological deposits include the Tombs of [[Segudet|Segudet]] ([[Ordino|Ordino]]) and Feixa del Moro (Sant Julia de Loria) both dated in 4900–4300 BC as an example of the [[Urnfield_culture|Urn culture]] in Andorra.
sentence_31: The model of small settlements began to evolve to a complex urbanism during the [[Bronze_Age|Bronze Age]].
sentence_32: [[Metallurgy|Metallurgical]] items of iron, ancient coins, and relicaries can be found in the [[Sanctuary|ancient sanctuaries]] scattered around the country.
sentence_33: The sanctuary of Roc de les Bruixes (Stone of the Witches) is perhaps the most important archeological complex of this age in Andorra, located in the parish of [[Canillo|Canillo]], about the rituals of funerals, ancient scripture and engraved stone [[Mural|murals]].
sentence_34: The inhabitants of the valleys were traditionally associated with the [[Iberians|Iberians]] and historically located in Andorra as the Iberian tribe Andosins or Andosini (Ἀνδοσίνους) during the 7th and 2nd centuries BC.
sentence_35: Influenced by the [[Aquitanian_language|Aquitanian]], [[Basque_language|Basque]] and [[Iberian_languages|Iberian languages]], the locals developed some current toponyms.
sentence_36: Early writings and documents relating to this group of people goes back to the second century BC by the Greek writer Polybius in his Histories during the [[Punic_Wars|Punic Wars]].
sentence_37: Some of the most significant remains of this era are the Castle of the Roc d'Enclar (part of the early Marca Hispanica), l'Anxiu in [[Les_Escaldes|Les Escaldes]] and Roc de L'Oral in [[Encamp|Encamp]].
sentence_38: The presence of [[Roman_Empire|Roman]] influence is recorded from the 2nd century BC to the 5th century AD.
sentence_39: The places found with more Roman presence are in Camp Vermell (Red Field) in Sant Julia de Loria, and in some places in Encamp, as well as in the Roc d'Enclar.
sentence_40: People continued trading, mainly with wine and cereals, with the Roman cities of [[Urgellet|Urgellet]] (the present-day [[La_Seu_d'Urgell|La Seu d'Urgell]]) and all across Segre through the [[Roman_roads|via romana]] Strata Ceretana (also known as Strata Confluetana).

section_4.value: Visigoths and Carolingians: the legend of Charlemagne

sentence_41: After the [[Fall_of_the_Roman_Empire|fall of the Roman Empire]], Andorra came under the influence of the [[Visigothic_Kingdom|Visigoths]], not remotely from the [[History_of_Toledo,_Spain#Visigothic_Toledo|Kingdom of Toledo]], but locally from the Diocese of Urgell.
sentence_42: The Visigoths remained in the valleys for 200 years, during which time Christianity spread.
sentence_43: When the Muslim Empire of Al-Andalus replaced the ruling Visigoths in most of the Iberian Peninsula, Andorra was sheltered from these invaders by the [[Francia|Franks]].
sentence_44: Tradition holds that Charles the Great (Charlemagne) granted a charter to the Andorran people for a contingent of five thousand soldiers under the command of Marc Almugaver, in return for fighting against the [[Moors|Moors]] near [[Porté-Puymorens|Porté-Puymorens]] ([[Cerdanya|Cerdanya]]).
sentence_45: Andorra remained part of the Frankish Marca Hispanica, the buffer-zone between the [[Francia|Frankish Empire]] and the Muslim territories, Andorra being part of the territory ruled by the [[Counts_of_Urgell|Count of Urgell]] and eventually by the bishop of the Diocese of Urgell.
sentence_46: Also tradition holds that it was guaranteed by the son of Charlemagne, [[Louis_the_Pious|Louis the Pious]], writing the Carta de Poblament or a local [[Municipal_charter|municipal charter]] circa 805.
sentence_47: In 988, [[Borrell_II|Borrell II]], Count of Urgell, gave the Andorran valleys to the Diocese of Urgell in exchange for land in Cerdanya.
sentence_48: Since then, the Bishop of Urgell, based in Seu d'Urgell, has been [[Co-Princes_of_Andorra|Co-prince]] of Andorra.
sentence_49: The first document that mentions Andorra as a territory is the Acta de Consagració i Dotació de la Catedral de la Seu d'Urgell (Deed of Consecration and Endowment of the Cathedral of La Seu d'Urgell).
sentence_50: The old document dated from 839 depicts the six old parishes of the Andorran valleys and therefore the administrative division of the country.

section_5.value: Medieval Age: The Paréages and the founding of the Co-Principality

sentence_51: Before 1095, Andorra did not have any type of military protection and the Bishop of Urgell, who knew that the count of Urgell wanted to reclaim the Andorran valleys, asked the lord of Caboet for help and protection.
sentence_52: In 1095, the Lord of Caboet and the bishop of Urgell signed under oath a declaration of their co-sovereignty over Andorra.
sentence_53: Arnalda, daughter of Arnau of Caboet, married the viscount of Castellbò.
sentence_54: Their daughter, Ermessenda, married the count of Foix, [[Roger-Bernard_II,_Count_of_Foix|Roger-Bernard II]].
sentence_55: Roger-Bernard II and Ermessenda shared ruled over Andorra with the bishop of Urgell.
sentence_56: In the 13th century, a military dispute arose between the bishop of Urgell and the count of Foix as aftermath of the [[Cathar_Crusade|Cathar Crusade]].
sentence_57: The conflict was resolved in 1278 with the mediation of the king of Aragon, [[Peter_II_of_Aragon|Peter II]], between the bishop and the count, by the signing of the [[Paréage_of_Andorra_1278|first paréage]] which provided that Andorra's sovereignty be shared between the count of Foix (whose title would ultimately transfer to the French head of state) and the bishop of Urgell, in Catalonia.
sentence_58: This gave the principality its territory and political form.
sentence_59: A second paréage was signed in 1288 after a dispute when the count of Foix ordered the construction of a castle in Roc d'Enclar.
sentence_60: The document was ratified by the noble notary [[County_of_Cerdanya|Jaume Orig of Puigcerdà]] and the construction of military structures in the country was prohibited.
sentence_61: In 1364 the political organization of the country named the figure of the [[Syndic|syndic]] (now spokesman and president of the parliament) as representative of the Andorrans to their co-princes making possible the creation of local departments (comuns, quarts and veïnats).
sentence_62: After being ratified by Bishop Francesc Tovia and Count [[John_I,_Count_of_Foix|John I]], the Consell de la Terra or [[General_Council_(Andorra)|Consell General de les Valls]] (General Council of the Valleys) was founded in 1419, the second oldest parliament in Europe.
sentence_63: The syndic Andreu d'Alàs and the General Council organized the creation of the [[Politics_of_Andorra#Judicial_branch|Justice Courts]] (La Cort de Justicia) in 1433 with the co-Princes and the collection of taxes like foc i lloc (literally fire and site, a national tax active since then).
sentence_64: Although there are remains of ecclesiastical works dating before the 9th century (Sant Vicenç d'Enclar or [[Església_de_Santa_Coloma|Església de Santa Coloma]]), Andorra developed exquisite [[Romanesque_Art_and_Architecture|Romanesque Art]] during the 9th through 14th centuries, particularly in the construction of churches, bridges, religious murals and statues of the [[Virgin_and_Child|Virgin and Child]] (Our Lady of Meritxell being the most important).
