sentence_65: Nowadays, the [[List_of_regional_characteristics_of_Romanesque_churches#Romanesque_churches_in_Spain,_Portugal_and_Andorra|Romanesque]] buildings that form part of Andorra's cultural heritage stand out in a remarkable way, with an emphasis on [[Església_de_Sant_Esteve|Església de Sant Esteve]], [[Sant_Joan_de_Caselles|Sant Joan de Caselles]], [[Església_de_Sant_Miquel_d'Engolasters|Església de Sant Miquel d'Engolasters]], [[Sant_Martí_de_la_Cortinada|Sant Martí de la Cortinada]] and the medieval bridges of [[Pont_de_la_Margineda|Margineda]] and [[Pont_dels_Escalls|Escalls]] among many others.
sentence_66: The Catalan Pyrenees were embryonic of the [[Catalan_language|Catalan language]] at the end of the 11th century.
sentence_67: Andorra was influenced by this language, which was adopted locally decades before it expanded to the rest of the Crown of Aragon.
sentence_68: The local population based its economy during the Middle Ages in livestock and agriculture, as well as in furs and weavers.
sentence_69: Later, at the end of the 11th century, the first [[Bloomery#Medieval_Europe|iron foundries]] began to appear in Northern Parishes like [[Ordino|Ordino]], much appreciated by the master artisans who developed the art of the forges, an important economic activity in the country from the 15th century.
sentence_70: In 1601 the [[Andorra#Law_and_criminal_justice|Tribunal de Corts]] (High Court of Justice) was created as a result of [[Huguenot_rebellions|Huguenot rebellions]] in France, [[Spanish_Inquisition|Inquisition]] courts coming from Spain and witchcraft-related beliefs native to the area, in the context of the [[Reformation|Reformation]] and Counter-Reformation.
sentence_71: With the passage of time, the co-title to Andorra passed to the kings of [[Kingdom_of_Navarre|Navarre]].
sentence_72: After [[Henry_IV_of_France|Henry III of Navarre]] became [[King_of_France|king of France]], he issued an edict in 1607 that established the head of the French state and the bishop of Urgell as [[Co-Princes_of_Andorra|co-princes of Andorra]], a political arrangement that continues up to the present time.
sentence_73: During 1617, communal councils form the sometent (popular militia or army) to deal with the rise of bandolerisme ([[Brigandage|brigandage]]) and the Consell de la Terra was defined and structured in terms of its composition, organization and competences current today.
sentence_74: Andorra continued with the same economic system that it had during the 12th–14th centuries with a large production of metallurgy (fargues, a system similar to Farga Catalana) and with the introduction of tobacco circa 1692 and import trade.
sentence_75: The fair of Andorra la Vella was ratified by the co-princes in 1371 and 1448 being the most important annual national festival commercially ever since.
sentence_76: The country had a unique and experienced [[Guild|guild]] of weavers, Confraria de Paraires i Teixidors, located in [[Escaldes-Engordany|Escaldes-Engordany]] founded in 1604 taking advantage of the thermal waters of the area.
sentence_77: By this time, the country was characterized by the social system of prohoms (wealthy society) and casalers (rest of the population with smaller economic acquisition), deriving from the tradition of [[Pubilla|pubilla]] and [[Heir|hereu]].
sentence_78: Three centuries after its foundation the Consell de la Terra located its headquarters and the Tribunal de Corts in [[Casa_de_la_Vall|Casa de la Vall]] in 1702.
sentence_79: The manor house built in 1580 served as a noble fortress of the Busquets family.
sentence_80: Inside the parliament was placed the Closet of the six keys (Armari de les sis claus) representative of each Andorran parish and where the Andorran constitution and other documents and laws were kept later on.
sentence_81: In both the [[Reapers'_War|Reapers' War]] and the [[War_of_the_Spanish_Succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], the Andorran people (although professing to be a neutral country) supported the [[Catalans|Catalans]] who saw their [[Catalan_constitutions|rights]] reduced in [[Nueva_Planta_decrees|1716]].
sentence_82: The reaction was the promotion of Catalan writings in Andorra, with cultural works such as the Book of Privileges (Llibre de Privilegis de 1674), Manual Digest (1748) by Antoni Fiter i Rossell or the Polità andorrà (1763) by Antoni Puig.

section_7.value: 19th century: the New Reform and the Andorran Question

sentence_83: After the [[French_Revolution|French Revolution]], [[Napoleon_I|Napoleon I]] reestablished the Co-Principate in 1809 and removed the French medieval title.
sentence_84: In 1812–1813, the [[First_French_Empire|First French Empire]] annexed Catalonia during the [[Peninsular_War|Peninsular War]] (Guerra Peninsular) and divided the region into four [[Département|départements]], with Andorra as a part of the district of [[Puigcerdà|Puigcerdà]].
sentence_85: In 1814, an imperial decree reestablished the independence and economy of Andorra.
sentence_86: During this period, Andorra's late medieval institutions and rural culture remained largely unchanged.
sentence_87: In 1866, the [[Syndic|syndic]] [[Guillem_d'Areny-Plandolit|Guillem d'Areny-Plandolit]] led the reformist group in a Council General of 24 members elected by suffrage limited to heads of families.
sentence_88: The Council General replaced the aristocratic oligarchy that previously ruled the state.
sentence_89: The New Reform (Nova Reforma) began after ratification by both Co-Princes and established the basis of the constitution and symbols—such as the [[Flag_of_Andorra|tricolor flag]]—of Andorra.
sentence_90: A new [[Service_economy|service economy]] arose as a demand of the valley inhabitants and began to build infrastructure such as hotels, spa resorts, roads and telegraph lines.
sentence_91: The authorities of the Co-Princes banned casinos and betting houses throughout the country.
sentence_92: The ban resulted in an economic conflict for the Andorran people.
sentence_93: The conflict led to the so-called revolution of 1881, when revolutionaries assaulted the house of the syndic on 8 December 1880, and established the Provisional Revolutionary Council led by Joan Pla i Calvo and Pere Baró i Mas.
sentence_94: The Provisional Revolutionary Council allowed for the construction of casinos and spas by foreign companies.
sentence_95: From 7 to 9 June 1881, the loyalists of [[Canillo|Canillo]] and [[Encamp|Encamp]] reconquered the parishes of [[Ordino|Ordino]] and [[La_Massana|La Massana]] by establishing contact with the revolutionary forces in [[Escaldes-Engordany|Escaldes-Engordany]].
sentence_96: After a day of combat the [[Pont_dels_Escalls|Treaty of the Bridge of Escalls]] was signed on 10 June.
sentence_97: The council was replaced and new elections were held.
sentence_98: The economic situation worsened, as the populace was divided over the Qüestió d'Andorra – the "Andorran Question" in relation to the [[Eastern_Question|Eastern Question]]).
sentence_99: The struggles continued between pro-bishops, pro-French, and nationalists based on the troubles of Canillo in 1882 and 1885.
sentence_100: Andorra participated in the cultural movement of the Catalan [[Renaixença|Renaixença]].
sentence_101: Between 1882 and 1887, the first academic schools were formed where trilingualism coexisted with the official language, Catalan.
sentence_102: [[Romanticism|Romantic]] authors from France and Spain reported the awakening of the [[Romantic_nationalism|national consciousness]] of the country.
sentence_103: Jacint Verdaguer lived in Ordino during the 1880s where he wrote and shared works related to the Renaixença with writer and photographer, [[Casa_Rossell|Joaquim de Riba]].
sentence_104: In 1848, [[Fromental_Halévy|Fromental Halévy]] had premiered the opera [[Le_val_d'Andorre|Le Val d'Andorre]] to great success in Europe, where the national consciousness of the valleys was exposed in the romantic work during the Peninsular War.

section_8.value: 20th and 21st century: Modernisation of the country and the Constitutional Andorra

sentence_105: Andorra declared war on [[Imperial_Germany|Imperial Germany]] during World War I, but did not take part directly in the fighting.
sentence_106: Some Andorrans volunteered to take part in the conflict as part of the [[Marching_Regiment_of_the_Foreign_Legion|French Legions]].
sentence_107: It remained in an official state of [[Belligerency|belligerency]] until 1958 as it was not included in the [[Treaty_of_Versailles|Treaty of Versailles]].
sentence_108: In 1933, France occupied Andorra following social unrest which occurred before elections due to the [[Andorran_Revolution|Revolution of 1933]] and the FHASA strikes (Vagues de FHASA); the revolt led by [[Young_Andorrans|Joves Andorrans]] (a [[Trade_union|labour union group]] related to the Spanish [[Confederación_Nacional_del_Trabajo|CNT]] and [[Federación_Anarquista_Ibérica|FAI]]) called for political reforms, the [[Universal_suffrage|universal suffrage vote]] of all Andorrans and acted in defense of the rights of local and foreign workers during the construction of FHASA's hydroelectric power station in [[Encamp|Encamp]].
sentence_109: On 5 April 1933 Joves Andorrans seized the Andorran Parliament.
sentence_110: These actions were preceded by the arrival of Colonel René-Jules Baulard with 50 [[National_Gendarmerie|gendarmes]] and the mobilization of 200 local militias or sometent led by the Síndic Francesc Cairat.
sentence_111: On 6 July 1934, adventurer and nobleman [[Boris_Skossyreff|Boris Skossyreff]], with his promise of freedoms and modernization of the country and wealth through the establishment of a tax haven and foreign investments, received the support of the members of the General Council to proclaim himself the sovereign of Andorra.
sentence_112: On 8 July 1934 Boris issued a proclamation in Urgell, declaring himself Boris I, King of Andorra, simultaneously declaring war on the Bishop of Urgell and approving the King's constitution on 10 July.
sentence_113: He was arrested by the Co-Prince and Bishop Justí Guitart i Vilardebó and their authorities on 20 July and ultimately expelled from Spain.
sentence_114: From 1936 until 1940, a French military detachment of Garde Mobile led by well-known Colonel René-Jules Baulard was garrisoned in Andorra to secure the principality against disruption from the [[Spanish_Civil_War|Spanish Civil War]] and Francoist Spain and also face the rise of [[Republicanism|Republicanism]] in the aftermath of the 1933 Revolution.
sentence_115: During the Spanish Civil War, the inhabitants of Andorra welcomed refugees from both sides, and many of them settled permanently in the country thus contributing to the subsequent economic boom and the entry into the [[Neoliberalism|capitalist era]] of Andorra.
sentence_116: Francoist troops reached the Andorran border in the later stages of the war.
sentence_117: During World War II, Andorra remained neutral and was an important smuggling route between [[Vichy_France|Vichy France]] and Francoist Spain, two fascist states.
sentence_118: Many Andorrans criticized the passivity of the General Council for impeding both the entry and expulsion of foreigners and refugees, committing economic crimes, reducing the rights of citizens and being sympathetic to Francoism.
sentence_119: General Council members justified the council's political and diplomatic actions as necessary for Andorra's survival and the protection of its sovereignty.
sentence_120: Andorra was relatively unscathed by the two world wars and the Spanish Civil War.
sentence_121: Certain [[Resistance_during_World_War_II|groups]] organized themselves to help victims of oppression in Nazi-occupied countries, while participating in smuggling to help Andorra survive.
sentence_122: Among the groups that were most prominent there was the [[Hostal_Palanques|Hostal Palanques]] Evasion Network Command.
sentence_123: The Evasion Network Command, in contact with the British [[Mi6|Mi6]], helped almost 400 fugitives, among whom were [[Allies_of_World_War_II|Allied]] military personnel.
sentence_124: The Command remained active between 1941 and 1944, although there were struggles with [[Axis_powers|pro-Axis]] informers and [[Gestapo|Gestapo]] agents within Andorra.
sentence_125: In the capital city there was a smuggling [[Black_market|black market]] network of propaganda, culture and cinematic art not prone to totalitarian regimes, promulgated in some places as the Hotel Mirador or the Casino Hotel, as a meeting place for people of ideologies close to Andorran and Spanish Republicanism, and Free France.
sentence_126: The network was maintained after the war, when film societies were formed, where movies, music and books [[Censorship_in_Francoist_Spain|censored in Franco's Spain]] were imported, thus becoming an anti-censorship attraction for the Catalan or foreign public even within Andorra.
sentence_127: Andorran Group (Agrupament Andorrà), an [[Anti-fascism|anti-fascist organization]] linked to the Occitanie's [[French_Resistance|French Resistance]], accused the French representative (veguer) of [[Collaboration_with_the_Axis_Powers|collaboration with Nazism]].
sentence_128: The Andorran opening to the [[Capitalist_economy|capitalist economy]] resulted in two axes: mass tourism and the country's tax exemption.
sentence_129: The first steps toward the capitalist boom date from the 1930s, with the construction of FHASA and the creation of professional banking with Banc Agrícol (1930) and [[Crèdit_Andorrà|Crèdit Andorrà]] (1949), later with [[Mora_Banc_Grup|Banca Mora]] (1952), [[Banca_Privada_d'Andorra|Banca Cassany]] (1958) and SOBANCA (1960).
sentence_130: Shortly after activities such as skiing and shopping become a tourist attraction, with the inauguration of ski resorts and cultural entities in the late 1930s.
sentence_131: All in all, a renovated hotel industry has developed.
sentence_132: In April 1968 a social health insurance system was created ([[Caixa_Andorrana_de_Seguretat_Social|CASS]]).
sentence_133: The Andorran Government necessarily involved planning, projection and forecasts for the future: with the official visit of the French co-prince [[Charles_de_Gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]] in 1967 and 1969, it was given approval for the economic boom and national demands within the framework of human rights and international openness.
sentence_134: Andorra lived an era commonly known as "Andorran dream" (in relation to the [[American_Dream|American dream]]) along with the [[Trente_Glorieuses|Trente Glorieuses]]: the [[Mass_culture|mass culture]] rooted the country experiencing radical changes in the economy and culture.
sentence_135: Proof of this event was [[Ràdio_Andorra|Ràdio Andorra]], number one transmitter musical radio station in Europe on this period, with guests and speakers of great importance promoting musical hits of Chanson française, [[Swing_(dance)|Swing]], [[Rhythm_&_blues|Rhythm & blues]], [[Jazz|Jazz]], [[Rock_and_roll|Rock & roll]] or [[Country_music|American Country music]].
sentence_136: So much so that Andorra achieved a [[GDP|GDP]] per capita and a life expectancy higher than the most standard countries of the current economy.
sentence_137: Given its relative isolation, Andorra has existed outside the mainstream of European history, with few ties to countries other than France, Spain and Portugal.
sentence_138: In recent times, however, its thriving tourist industry along with developments in transport and communications have removed the country from its isolation.
sentence_139: Since 1976 the country sees the need to reform Andorran institutions due to the anachronisms in the field of sovereignty, human rights and the balance of powers as well as the need to adapt legislation to modern demands.
sentence_140: In 1982 a first separation of powers took place when instituting the Govern d'Andorra, under the name of Executive Board (Consell Executiu), chaired by the first prime minister [[Òscar_Ribas_Reig|Òscar Ribas Reig]] with the approval of the Co-Princes.
sentence_141: In 1989 the Principality signed an agreement with the [[European_Economic_Community|European Economic Community]] to regularize trade relations.
sentence_142: Its political system was modernized in 1993 after the [[Andorran_constitutional_referendum,_1993|Andorran constitutional referendum]], when the constitution was drafted by the Co-Princes and the General Council and approved on 14 March by 74.2% of voters, with a 76% turnout.
sentence_143: The [[Andorran_parliamentary_election,_1993|first elections]] under the new constitution were held later in the year.
sentence_144: The same year Andorra became a member of the [[United_Nations|United Nations]] and the [[Council_of_Europe|Council of Europe]].
sentence_145: Andorra formalized diplomatic relations with the United States in 1996 participating in the 51st [[UN_General_Assembly|UN General Assembly]], a very important fact in view of the normalization that the country aspired to.
sentence_146: First General Syndic Marc Forné took part on a speech in Catalan in the General Assembly to defend the reform of the organization, and after three days Forné took part in the parliamentary assembly of the Council of Europe to defend the linguistic rights and the economy of Andorra.
sentence_147: In mid-2006 the monetary agreement with the European Union is formalized, which allows Andorra to use the [[Euro|euro]] in an official way, as well as coin its own Euro currency.
sentence_148: Main article: Politics of Andorra
sentence_149: Main article: [[Co-princes_of_Andorra|Co-princes of Andorra]]
sentence_150: Andorra is a parliamentary co-principality with the president of France and the Catholic bishop of Urgell (Catalonia, Spain) as co-princes.
sentence_151: This peculiarity makes the president of France, in his capacity as [[Prince_of_Andorra|prince of Andorra]], an elected monarch, although he is not elected by a popular vote of the Andorran people.
sentence_152: The politics of Andorra take place in a framework of a [[Parliamentary_system|parliamentary]] [[Representative_democracy|representative democracy]], whereby the [[List_of_heads_of_government_of_Andorra|head of government]] is the chief executive, and of a multi-party system.
sentence_153: The current head of government is [[Xavier_Espot_Zamora|Xavier Espot Zamora]] of the [[Democrats_for_Andorra|Democrats for Andorra]] (DA).
sentence_154: Executive power is exercised by the government.
sentence_155: Legislative power is vested in both government and parliament.
sentence_156: The Parliament of Andorra is known as the General Council.
sentence_157: The General Council consists of between 28 and 42 councillors.
sentence_158: The councillors serve for four-year terms, and elections are held between the 30th and 40th days following the dissolution of the previous Council.
sentence_159: Half are elected in equal numbers by each of the seven administrative parishes, and the other half of the councillors are elected in a single national constituency.
sentence_160: Fifteen days after the election, the councillors hold their inauguration.
sentence_161: During this session, the Syndic General, who is the head of the General Council, and the Subsyndic General, his assistant, are elected.
sentence_162: Eight days later, the Council convenes once more.
sentence_163: During this session the head of government is chosen from among the councillors.
sentence_164: Candidates can be proposed by a minimum of one-fifth of the councillors.
sentence_165: The Council then elects the candidate with the absolute majority of votes to be head of government.
sentence_166: The Syndic General then notifies the co-princes, who in turn appoint the elected candidate as the head of government of Andorra.
sentence_167: The General Council is also responsible for proposing and passing laws.
sentence_168: Bills may be presented to the council as Private Members' Bills by three of the local Parish Councils jointly or by at least one tenth of the citizens of Andorra.
sentence_169: The council also approves the annual budget of the principality.
sentence_170: The government must submit the proposed budget for parliamentary approval at least two months before the previous budget expires.
sentence_171: If the budget is not approved by the first day of the next year, the previous budget is extended until a new one is approved.
sentence_172: Once any bill is approved, the Syndic General is responsible for presenting it to the Co-Princes so that they may sign and enact it.
sentence_173: If the head of government is not satisfied with the council, he may request that the co-princes dissolve the council and order new elections.
sentence_174: In turn, the councillors have the power to remove the head of government from office.
sentence_175: After a motion of censure is approved by at least one-fifth of the councillors, the council will vote and if it receives the absolute majority of votes, the head of government is removed.
sentence_176: Main article: [[Law_of_Andorra|Law of Andorra]]
sentence_177: The judiciary is composed of the Magistrates Court, the Criminal Law Court, the High Court of Andorra, and the Constitutional Court.
sentence_178: The High Court of Justice is composed of five judges: one appointed by the head of government, one each by the co-princes, one by the Syndic General, and one by the judges and magistrates.
sentence_179: It is presided over by the member appointed by the Syndic General and the judges hold office for six-year terms.
sentence_180: The magistrates and judges are appointed by the High Court, as is the president of the Criminal Law Court.
sentence_181: The High Court also appoints members of the Office of the Attorney General.
sentence_182: The Constitutional Court is responsible for interpreting the Constitution and reviewing all appeals of unconstitutionality against laws and treaties.
sentence_183: It is composed of four judges, one appointed by each of the co-princes and two by the General Council.
sentence_184: They serve eight-year terms.
sentence_185: The Court is presided over by one of the judges on a two-year rotation so that each judge at one point will preside over the Court.
sentence_186: Main article: [[Foreign_relations_of_Andorra|Foreign relations of Andorra]]
sentence_187: Andorra does not have its own armed forces, although there is a small ceremonial army.
sentence_188: Responsibility for defending the nation rests primarily with France and Spain.
sentence_189: However, in case of emergencies or natural disasters, the Sometent (an alarm) is called and all able-bodied men between 21 and 60 of Andorran nationality must serve.
sentence_190: This is why all Andorrans, and especially the head of each house (usually the eldest able-bodied man of a house) should, by law, keep a rifle, even though the law also states that the police will offer a firearm in case of need.
sentence_191: Andorra is a full member of the United Nations (UN), the [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] (OSCE), and has a special agreement with the [[European_Union|European Union]] (EU), it also has observer status at the [[World_Trade_Organization|World Trade Organization]] (WTO).
sentence_192: On 16 October 2020, Andorra became the 190th member of the [[International_Monetary_Fund|International Monetary Fund]] (IMF), during the [[COVID-19_pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]].
sentence_193: Andorra has a small army, which has historically been raised or reconstituted at various dates, but has never in modern times amounted to a standing army.
sentence_194: The basic principle of Andorran defence is that all able-bodied men are available to fight if called upon by the sounding of the Sometent.
sentence_195: Being a [[Landlocked_country|landlocked country]], Andorra has no navy.
sentence_196: Before World War I, Andorra maintained an armed force of about 600 part-time militiamen under the supervision of a Captain (Capità or Cap de Sometent) and a Lieutenant (Desener or Lloctinent del Capità).
sentence_197: This body was not liable for service outside the principality and was commanded by two officials (veguers) appointed by France and the Bishop of Urgell.
sentence_198: Despite not being involved in any fighting during the First World War, Andorra was technically the longest combatant, as the country was left out of the [[Versailles_Peace_Conference|Versailles Peace Conference]], [[De_jure|technically]] remaining at war with Germany from its original declaration of war in 1914 until 24 September 1958 when Andorra officially declared peace with Germany.
sentence_199: In the modern era, the army has consisted of a very small body of volunteers willing to undertake ceremonial duties.
sentence_200: Uniforms and weaponry were handed down from generation to generation within families and communities.
sentence_201: The army's role in internal security was largely taken over by the formation of the [[Police_Corps_of_Andorra|Police Corps of Andorra]] in 1931.
sentence_202: Brief civil disorder associated with the elections of 1933 led to assistance being sought from the French [[National_Gendarmerie|National Gendarmerie]], with a detachment resident in Andorra for two months under the command of René-Jules Baulard.
sentence_203: The Andorran Police was reformed in the following year, with eleven soldiers appointed to supervisory roles.
sentence_204: The force consisted of six Corporals, one for each parish (although there are currently seven parishes, there were only six until 1978), plus four junior staff officers to co-ordinate action, and a commander with the rank of major.
sentence_205: It was the responsibility of the six corporals, each in his own parish, to be able to raise a fighting force from among the able-bodied men of the parish.
sentence_206: Today a small, twelve-man ceremonial unit remains the only permanent section of the Sometent, but all able-bodied men remain technically available for military service, with a requirement for each family to have access to a firearm.
sentence_207: A shotgun per household is unregulated.
sentence_208: Rifles and pistols require a license.
sentence_209: The army has not fought for more than 700 years, and its main responsibility is to present the [[Flag_of_Andorra|flag of Andorra]] at official ceremonial functions.
sentence_210: According to Marc Forné Molné, Andorra's military budget is strictly from voluntary donations, and the availability of full-time volunteers.
sentence_211: In more recent times there has only been a general emergency call to the popular army of Sometent during the floods of 1982 in the Catalan Pyrenees, where 12 citizens perished in Andorra, to help the population and establish a public order along with the Local Police units.
sentence_212: Main article: [[Police_Corps_of_Andorra|Police Corps of Andorra]]
sentence_213: Andorra maintains a small but modern and well-equipped internal police force, with around 240 police officers supported by civilian assistants.
sentence_214: The principal services supplied by the corps are uniformed community policing, criminal detection, border control, and traffic policing.
sentence_215: There are also small specialist units including police dogs, mountain rescue, and a bomb disposal team.
sentence_216: The Grup d'Intervenció Policia d'Andorra (GIPA) is a small special forces unit trained in [[Counter-terrorism|counter-terrorism]], and [[Hostage_negotiator|hostage recovery]] tasks.
sentence_217: Although it is the closest in style to an active military force, it is part of the [[Police_Corps_of_Andorra|Police Corps]], and not the [[Military_of_Andorra|army]].
sentence_218: As terrorist and hostage situations are a rare threat to the country, the GIPA is commonly assigned to prisoner escort duties, and at other times to routine policing.
sentence_219: The Andorran Fire Brigade, with headquarters at [[Santa_Coloma_d'Andorra|Santa Coloma]], operates from four modern fire stations, and has a staff of around 120 firefighters.
sentence_220: The service is equipped with 16 heavy appliances (fire tenders, turntable ladders, and specialist four-wheel drive vehicles), four light support vehicles (cars and vans) and four ambulances.
sentence_221: Historically, the families of the six ancient parishes of Andorra maintained local arrangements to assist each other in fighting fires.
sentence_222: The first fire pump purchased by the government was acquired in 1943.
sentence_223: Serious fires which lasted for two days in December 1959 led to calls for a permanent fire service, and the Andorran Fire Brigade was formed on 21 April 1961.
sentence_224: The fire service maintains full-time cover with five fire crews on duty at any time: two at the brigade's headquarters in Santa Coloma, and one crew at each of the other three fire stations.
sentence_225: Main articles: [[Geography_of_Andorra|Geography of Andorra]] and [[Geology_of_Andorra|Geology of Andorra]]
sentence_226: Main article: Parishes of Andorra
sentence_227: Andorra consists of seven parishes:
sentence_228: Due to its location in the eastern [[Pyrenees|Pyrenees]] mountain range, Andorra consists predominantly of rugged mountains, the highest being the [[Coma_Pedrosa|Coma Pedrosa]] at 2,942 metres (9,652 ft), and the average elevation of Andorra is 1,996 metres (6,549 ft).
sentence_229: These are dissected by three narrow valleys in a Y shape that combine into one as the main stream, the [[Gran_Valira|Gran Valira]] river, leaves the country for Spain (at Andorra's lowest point of 840 m or 2,756 ft).
sentence_230: Andorra's land area is 468 km (181 sq mi).
sentence_231: [[Phytogeography|Phytogeographically]], Andorra belongs to the Atlantic European province of the Circumboreal Region within the Boreal Kingdom.
sentence_232: According to the WWF, the territory of Andorra belongs to the [[Ecoregion|ecoregion]] of Pyrenees conifer and mixed forests.
sentence_233: Andorra has [[Alpine_climate|alpine]], continental and [[Oceanic_climate|oceanic climates]], depending on altitude.
sentence_234: Its higher elevation means there is, on average, more snow in winter and it is slightly cooler in summer.
sentence_235: The diversity of landmarks, the different orientation of the valleys and the irregularity relief typical of the [[Mediterranean_climate|Mediterranean climates]] make the country have a great diversity of microclimates that hinder the general dominance of the [[Mountain_climate|high mountain climate]].
sentence_236: The great differences of altitude in the minimum and maximum points, together with the influence of a Mediterranean climate, develop the climate of the Andorran Pyrenees.
sentence_237: When in precipitation, a global model characterized by convective and abundant rains can be defined during spring and summer, which can last until autumn (May, June and August are usually the rainiest months); In winter, however, it is less rainy, except in the highlands, subject to the influence of fronts from the [[Atlantic_Europe|Atlantic]], which explains the great amount of snowfall in the Andorran mountains.
sentence_238: The temperature regime is characterized, broadly, by a temperate summer and a long and cold winter; in accordance with the mountainous condition of the Principality.
sentence_239: Main article: [[Economy_of_Andorra|Economy of Andorra]]
sentence_240: Tourism, the mainstay of Andorra's tiny, well-to-do economy, accounts for roughly 80% of GDP.
sentence_241: An estimated 10.2 million tourists visit annually, attracted by Andorra's [[Duty-free_shopping|duty-free]] status and by its summer and winter resorts.
sentence_242: One of the main sources of income in Andorra is tourism from ski resorts which total over 175 km (109 mi) of ski ground.
sentence_243: The sport brings in over 7 million visitors annually and an estimated 340 million euros per year, sustaining 2,000 direct and 10,000 indirect jobs at present since 2007.
sentence_244: The banking sector, with its [[Tax_haven|tax haven]] status, also contributes substantially to the economy with revenues raised exclusively through import tariffs (the financial and insurance sector accounts for approximately 19% of GDP).
sentence_245: However, during the [[European_sovereign-debt_crisis|European sovereign-debt crisis]] of the 21st century, the tourist industry suffered a decline, partly caused by a drop in the prices of goods in Spain, undercutting [[Duty-free_shop|duty-free shopping]] and increasing unemployment.
sentence_246: On 1 January 2012, a business tax of 10% was introduced, followed by a sales tax of 2% a year later, which raised just over 14 million euros in its first quarter.
sentence_247: Agricultural production is limited; only 5% of the land is arable, and most food has to be imported.
sentence_248: Some tobacco is grown locally.
sentence_249: The principal livestock activity is domestic sheep raising.
sentence_250: Manufacturing output consists mainly of cigarettes, cigars, and furniture.
sentence_251: Andorra's natural resources include hydroelectric power, mineral water, timber, iron ore, and lead.
sentence_252: Andorra is not a member of the European Union, but enjoys a [[Andorra–European_Union_relations|special relationship]] with it, such as being treated as an EU member for trade in manufactured goods (no tariffs) and as a non-EU member for agricultural products.
sentence_253: Andorra lacked a currency of its own and used both the [[French_franc|French franc]] and the [[Spanish_peseta|Spanish peseta]] in banking transactions until 31 December 1999, when both currencies were replaced by the EU's single currency, the euro.
sentence_254: Coins and notes of both the franc and the peseta remained legal tender in Andorra until 31 December 2002.
sentence_255: Andorra negotiated to issue its own euro coins, beginning in 2014.
sentence_256: Andorra has traditionally had one of the world's lowest unemployment rates.
sentence_257: In 2019 it stood at 2%.
sentence_258: On 31 May 2013, it was announced that Andorra intended to legislate for the introduction of an income tax by the end of June, against a background of increasing dissatisfaction with the existence of tax havens among EU members.
sentence_259: The announcement was made following a meeting in Paris between the Head of Government [[Antoni_Marti|Antoni Marti]] and the French President and Prince of Andorra [[François_Hollande|François Hollande]].
sentence_260: Hollande welcomed the move as part of a process of Andorra "bringing its taxation in line with international standards".
sentence_261: By the mid-2010s, the financial system comprised five banking groups, one specialised credit entity, eight investment undertaking management entities, three asset management companies, and 29 insurance companies, 14 of which are branches of foreign insurance companies authorised to operate in the principality.
sentence_262: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Andorra|Demographics of Andorra]]
sentence_263: The population of Andorra is estimated at 77,006 (2018).
sentence_264: The [[Andorran_people|Andorrans]] are a Romance [[Ethnic_group|ethnic group]] of originally [[Catalans|Catalan]] descent.
sentence_265: The population has grown from 5,000 in 1900.
sentence_266: Two-thirds of residents lack Andorran nationality and do not have the right to vote in communal elections.
sentence_267: Moreover, they are not allowed to be elected as prime minister or to own more than 33% of the capital stock of a privately held company.
sentence_268: Main article: Languages of Andorra
sentence_269: The historic and [[Official_language|official language]] is [[Catalan_language|Catalan]], a Romance language.
sentence_270: The Andorran government encourages the use of Catalan.
sentence_271: It funds a Commission for Catalan [[Toponymy|Toponymy]] in Andorra (Catalan: Comissió de Toponímia d'Andorra), and provides free Catalan classes to assist immigrants.
sentence_272: Andorran television and radio stations use Catalan.
sentence_273: Because of immigration, historical links, and close geographic proximity, Spanish, Portuguese and French are commonly spoken.
sentence_274: Most Andorran residents can speak one or more of these, in addition to Catalan.
sentence_275: English is less commonly spoken among the general population, though it is understood to varying degrees in the major tourist resorts.
sentence_276: Andorra is one of only four European countries (together with France, [[Monaco|Monaco]], and [[Turkey|Turkey]]) that have never signed the [[Framework_Convention_for_the_Protection_of_National_Minorities|Council of Europe Framework Convention on National Minorities]].
sentence_277: According to the Observatori Social d'Andorra, the linguistic usage in Andorra is as follows:
sentence_278: The population of Andorra is predominantly (88.2%) Catholic.
sentence_279: Their patron saint is Our Lady of Meritxell.
sentence_280: Though it is not an official state religion, the constitution acknowledges a special relationship with the Catholic Church, offering some special privileges to that group.
sentence_281: Other Christian denominations include the [[Anglican_Church|Anglican Church]], the [[Unification_Church|Unification Church]], the New Apostolic Church, and [[Jehovah's_Witnesses|Jehovah's Witnesses]].
sentence_282: The small [[Islam_in_Andorra|Muslim community]] is primarily made up of North African immigrants.
sentence_283: There is a small community of [[Hinduism|Hindus]] and [[Bahá'í_Faith_in_Andorra|Bahá'ís]], and roughly 100 Jews live in Andorra.
sentence_284: (See [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Andorra|History of the Jews in Andorra]].)
sentence_285: Main article: [[List_of_cities_in_Andorra|List of cities in Andorra]]
sentence_286: Children between the ages of 6 and 16 are required by law to have full-time education.
sentence_287: Education up to secondary level is provided free of charge by the government.
sentence_288: There are three systems of school, Andorran, French and Spanish, which use Catalan, French and Spanish languages respectively, as the main language of instruction.
sentence_289: Parents may choose which system their children attend.
sentence_290: All schools are built and maintained by Andorran authorities, but teachers in the French and Spanish schools are paid for the most part by France and Spain.
sentence_291: 39% of Andorran children attend Andorran schools, 33% attend French schools, and 28% Spanish schools.
sentence_292: The Universitat d'Andorra (UdA) is the state public university and is the only university in Andorra.
sentence_293: It was established in 1997.
sentence_294: The university provides first-level degrees in nursing, computer science, business administration, and educational sciences, in addition to higher professional education courses.
sentence_295: The only two graduate schools in Andorra are the Nursing School and the School of Computer Science, the latter having a PhD programme.
sentence_296: The geographical complexity of the country as well as the small number of students prevents the University of Andorra from developing a full academic programme, and it serves principally as a centre for virtual studies, connected to Spanish and French universities.
sentence_297: The Virtual Studies Centre (Centre d'Estudis Virtuals) at the University runs approximately 20 different academic degrees at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels in fields including tourism, law, Catalan [[Philology|philology]], humanities, psychology, political sciences, audiovisual communication, telecommunications engineering, and East Asia studies.
sentence_298: The centre also runs various postgraduate programmes and continuing-education courses for professionals.
sentence_299: Main article: [[Transport_in_Andorra|Transport in Andorra]]
sentence_300: See also: [[Andorra–La_Seu_d'Urgell_Airport|Andorra–La Seu d'Urgell Airport]]
sentence_301: Until the 20th century, Andorra had very limited transport links to the outside world, and development of the country was affected by its physical isolation.
sentence_302: Even now, the nearest major airports at Toulouse and Barcelona are both three hours' drive from Andorra.
sentence_303: Andorra has a road network of 279 km (173 mi), of which 76 km (47 mi) is unpaved.
sentence_304: The two main roads out of [[Andorra_la_Vella|Andorra la Vella]] are the CG-1 to the Spanish border near [[Sant_Julià_de_Lòria|Sant Julia de Loria]], and the CG-2 to the French border via the Envalira Tunnel near [[El_Pas_de_la_Casa|El Pas de la Casa]].
sentence_305: Bus services cover all metropolitan areas and many rural communities, with services on most major routes running half-hourly or more frequently during peak travel times.
sentence_306: There are frequent long-distance bus services from Andorra to [[Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Toulouse|Toulouse]], plus a daily tour from the former city.
sentence_307: Bus services mostly are run by private companies, but some local ones are operated by the government.
sentence_308: There are no airports for fixed-wing aircraft within Andorra's borders but there are, however, heliports in [[La_Massana|La Massana]] (Camí Heliport), Arinsal and [[Escaldes-Engordany|Escaldes-Engordany]] with commercial helicopter services and an airport located in the neighbouring Spanish comarca of [[Alt_Urgell|Alt Urgell]], 12 kilometres (7.5 miles) south of the Andorran-Spanish border.
sentence_309: Since July 2015, [[Andorra–La_Seu_d'Urgell_Airport|Andorra–La Seu d'Urgell Airport]] has operated commercial flights to [[Adolfo_Suárez_Madrid–Barajas_Airport|Madrid]] and [[Palma_de_Mallorca_Airport|Palma de Mallorca]], and is the [[Airline_hub|main hub]] for [[Air_Andorra|Air Andorra]] and [[Andorra_Airlines|Andorra Airlines]].
sentence_310: As of 11 July 2018, there are no regular commercial flights at the airport.
sentence_311: Nearby airports located in Spain and France provide access to international flights for the principality.
sentence_312: The nearest airports are at [[Perpignan–Rivesaltes_Airport|Perpignan]], France (156 kilometres or 97 miles from Andorra) and [[Lleida-Alguaire_Airport|Lleida]], Spain (160 kilometres or 99 miles from Andorra).
sentence_313: The largest nearby airports are at Toulouse, France (165 kilometres or 103 miles from Andorra) and Barcelona, Spain (215 kilometres or 134 miles from Andorra).
sentence_314: There are hourly bus services from both Barcelona and Toulouse airports to Andorra.
sentence_315: The nearest railway station is [[L'Hospitalet-près-l'Andorre|L'Hospitalet-près-l'Andorre]] 10 km (6 mi) east of Andorra which is on the 1,435 mm (4 ft 8 ⁄2 in)[[Standard_gauge|-gauge]] line from [[Latour-de-Carol|Latour-de-Carol]] (25 km or 16 mi) southeast of Andorra, to [[Toulouse|Toulouse]] and on to Paris by the French [[TGV|high-speed trains]].
sentence_316: This line is operated by the [[SNCF|SNCF]].
sentence_317: Latour-de-Carol has a scenic 1,000 mm (3 ft 3 ⁄8 in) [[Metre_gauge|metre gauge]] trainline to [[Villefranche-de-Conflent|Villefranche-de-Conflent]], as well as the SNCF's 1,435 mm gauge line connecting to [[Perpignan|Perpignan]], and the [[RENFE|RENFE's]] 1,668 mm (5 ft 5 ⁄32 in) [[Iberian_gauge|-gauge]] line to Barcelona.
sentence_318: There are also direct [[Intercités#Night_trains|Intercités de Nuit]] trains between L'Hospitalet-près-l'Andorre and Paris on certain dates.
sentence_319: Main article: [[Telecommunications_in_Andorra|Telecommunications in Andorra]]
sentence_320: See also: [[Andorra_Telecom|Andorra Telecom]]
sentence_321: In Andorra, mobile and fixed telephone and internet services are operated exclusively by the Andorran national telecommunications company, SOM, also known as [[Andorra_Telecom|Andorra Telecom]] (STA).
sentence_322: The same company also manages the technical infrastructure for national broadcasting of digital television and radio.
sentence_323: In 2010 Andorra became the first country to provide a direct [[Optical_fiber|optical fiber]] link to all homes ([[FTTx|FTTH]]) and businesses.
sentence_324: The first commercial radio station to broadcast was [[Radio_Andorra|Radio Andorra]], which was active from 1939 to 1981.
sentence_325: On 12 October 1989, the General Council established radio and television as essential public services creating and managing the entity ORTA, becoming on 13 April 2000, in the public company [[Ràdio_i_Televisió_d'Andorra|Ràdio i Televisió d'Andorra]] (RTVA).
sentence_326: In 1990, the public radio was founded on the Radio Nacional d'Andorra.
sentence_327: As an autochthonous television channel, there is only the national public television network Andorra Televisió, created in 1995.
sentence_328: Additional TV and radio stations from Spain and France are available via digital terrestrial television and IPTV.
sentence_329: There are three national newspapers, [[Diari_d'Andorra|Diari d'Andorra]], [[El_Periòdic_d'Andorra|El Periòdic d'Andorra]], and [[Bondia_(newspaper)|Bondia]] as well as several local newspapers.
sentence_330: The history of the Andorran press begins in the period between 1917 and 1937 with the appearance of several periodicals papers such as Les Valls d'Andorra (1917), Nova Andorra (1932) and Andorra Agrícola (1933).
sentence_331: In 1974, the Poble Andorrà became the first regular newspaper in Andorra.
sentence_332: There is also an [[Amateur_radio|amateur radio]] society and news agency ANA with independent management.
sentence_333: Main article: Culture of Andorra
sentence_334: See also: [[Music_of_Andorra|Music of Andorra]]
sentence_335: The official and historic language is [[Catalan_language|Catalan]].
sentence_336: Thus the culture is Catalan, with its own specificity.
sentence_337: Andorra is home to folk dances like the contrapàs and marratxa, which survive in [[Sant_Julià_de_Lòria|Sant Julià de Lòria]] especially.
sentence_338: Andorran folk music has similarities to the music of its neighbours, but is especially [[Music_of_Catalonia|Catalan]] in character, especially in the presence of dances such as the [[Sardana|sardana]].
sentence_339: Other Andorran folk dances include contrapàs in [[Andorra_la_Vella|Andorra la Vella]] and Saint Anne's dance in Escaldes-Engordany.
sentence_340: Andorra's national holiday is Our Lady of Meritxell Day, 8 September.
sentence_341: Among the more important festivals and traditions are the [[Canòlic|Canólich Gathering]] in May, the Roser d'Ordino in July, the Meritxell Day (National Day of Andorra), the Andorra la Vella Fair, the [[Sant_Jordi|Sant Jordi Day]], the Santa Llúcia Fair, the Festivity from La Candelera to Canillo, the [[Carnival|Carnival]] of Encamp, the sung of caramelles, the Festivity of [[Saint_Stephen|Sant Esteve]] and the Festa del Poble.
sentence_342: Andorra participated regularly in the [[Eurovision_Song_Contest|Eurovision Song Contest]] between 2004 and 2009, being the only [[List_of_countries_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest|participating country]] presenting songs in [[Catalan_language|Catalan]].
sentence_343: In popular folklore, the best-known Andorran legends are the legend of Charlemagne, according to which this Frankish King would have founded the country, the White Lady of [[Auvinyà|Auvinyà]], the [[El_buner_d'Ordino|Buner d'Ordino]], the legend of [[Engolasters|Engolasters Lake]] and the legend of Our Lady of Meritxell.
sentence_344: Andorran gastronomy is mainly [[Catalan_cuisine|Catalan]], although it has also adopted other elements of [[French_cuisine|French]] and Italian cuisines.
sentence_345: The cuisine of the country has similar characteristics with the neighbors of the [[Cerdanya|Cerdanya]] and the [[Alt_Urgell|Alt Urgell]], with whom it has a strong cultural ties.
sentence_346: Andorra's cuisine is marked by its nature as mountain valleys.
sentence_347: Typical dishes of the country are the quince [[Aioli|all-i-oli]], the duck with winter pear, the lamb in the oven with nuts, pork civet, the massegada cake, the escarole with pear trees, confited duck and mushrooms, escudella, spinach with raisins and pine nuts, jelly marmalade, stuffed murgues (mushrooms) with pork, [[Dandelion|dandelion]] salad and the Andorran trout of river.
sentence_348: To drink, the mulled wine and [[Beer|beer]] are also popular.
sentence_349: Some of the dishes are very common in the [[Alt_Pirineu_i_Aran|mountainous regions of Catalonia]], such as [[Trinxat|trinxat]], [[Embutido|embotits]], cooked snails, rice with mushrooms, mountain rice and [[Mató|mató]].
sentence_350: Pre-Romanesque and Romanesque art are one of the most important artistic manifestations and characteristics of the Principality.
sentence_351: The Romanesque one allows to know the formation of the parochial communities, the relations of (social and political) power and the national culture.
sentence_352: There are a total of forty Romanesque churches that stand out as being small austere ornamentation constructions, as well as [[Romanesque_architecture|bridges]], fortresses and manor houses of the same period.
sentence_353: Summer solstice fire festivals in the Pyrenees was included as [[Intangible_cultural_heritage|UNESCO Intangible cultural heritage]] in 2015.
sentence_354: Also the [[Madriu-Perafita-Claror_Valley|Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley]] became Andorra's first, and to date its only, [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] [[World_Heritage_Site|World Heritage Site]] in 2004, with a small extension in 2006.
sentence_355: Andorra is famous for the practice of [[Winter_sports|winter sports]].
sentence_356: Andorra has the largest territory of ski slopes in the [[Pyrenees|Pyrenees]] (3100 hectares and about 350 km of slopes) and two ski resorts.
sentence_357: Grandvalira is the largest and most popular resort.
sentence_358: Other popular sports played in Andorra include [[Association_football|football]], [[Rugby_union|rugby union]], basketball, and [[Roller_hockey_(quad)|roller hockey]].
sentence_359: For [[Roller_hockey_(quad)|roller hockey]], [[Andorra_national_roller_hockey_team|Andorra]] usually plays in [[CERH_European_Roller_Hockey_Championship|CERH Euro Cup]] and in [[FIRS_Roller_Hockey_World_Cup|FIRS Roller Hockey World Cup]].
sentence_360: In 2011, Andorra was the host country to the [[2011_European_League_Final_Eight|2011 European League Final Eight]].
sentence_361: The country is represented in association football by the [[Andorra_national_football_team|Andorra national football team]].
sentence_362: The team gained its first competitive win in a European Championship qualifier on 11 October 2019, against Moldova.
sentence_363: Football is governed in Andorra by the [[Andorran_Football_Federation|Andorran Football Federation]] - founded in 1994, it organizes the national competitions of association football ([[Primera_Divisió|Primera Divisió]], [[Copa_Constitució|Copa Constitució]] and [[Andorran_Supercup|Supercopa]]) and [[Futsal|futsal]].
sentence_364: Andorra was admitted to [[UEFA|UEFA]] and [[FIFA|FIFA]] in the same year, 1996.
sentence_365: [[FC_Andorra|FC Andorra]], a club based in [[Andorra_la_Vella|Andorra la Vella]] founded in 1942, compete in the [[Spanish_football_league_system|Spanish football league system]].
sentence_366: [[Rugby_union|Rugby]] is a traditional sport in Andorra, mainly influenced by the popularity in southern France.
sentence_367: The Andorra national rugby union team, nicknamed Els Isards, plays on the international stage in [[Rugby_union|rugby union]] and [[Rugby_sevens|rugby sevens]].
sentence_368: VPC Andorra XV is a rugby team based in Andorra la Vella actually playing in the French championship.
sentence_369: Basketball popularity has increased in the country since the 1990s, when the Andorran team [[BC_Andorra|BC Andorra]] played in the top league of Spain ([[Liga_ACB|Liga ACB]]).
sentence_370: After 18 years the club returned to the top league in 2014.
sentence_371: Other sports practised in Andorra include cycling, volleyball, judo, Australian Rules football, handball, swimming, gymnastics, tennis, and motorsports.
sentence_372: In 2012, Andorra raised its first national cricket team and played a home match against the Dutch Fellowship of Fairly Odd Places Cricket Club, the first match played in the history of Andorra at an altitude of 1,300 metres (4,300 ft).
sentence_373: Andorra first participated at the [[Olympic_Games|Olympic Games]] in 1976.
sentence_374: The country has appeared in every [[Winter_Olympic|Winter Olympic]] Games since 1976.
sentence_375: Andorra competes in the [[Games_of_the_Small_States_of_Europe|Games of the Small States of Europe]], being twice the host country in [[1991_Games_of_the_Small_States_of_Europe|1991]] and [[2005_Games_of_the_Small_States_of_Europe|2005]].
sentence_376: As one of the [[Catalan_Countries|Catalan Countries]], Andorra is home to a team of [[Castell|castellers]], or Catalan human tower builders.
sentence_377: The Castellers d'Andorra [], based in the town of [[Santa_Coloma_d'Andorra|Santa Coloma d'Andorra]], are recognized by the Coordinadora de Colles Castelleres de Catalunya [], the governing body of castells.

title: Ankara
sentence_0: "Ancyra" redirects here.
sentence_1: For the insect genus, see [[Ancyra_(genus)|Ancyra (genus)]].
sentence_2: For the archdiocese, see [[Ancyra_(Catholic_titular_see)|Ancyra (Catholic titular see)]].
sentence_3: For other uses, see [[Ankara_(disambiguation)|Ankara (disambiguation)]].
sentence_4: Ankara ([[English|/ˈæŋkərə/]] ANK-ə-rə, also [[American_English|US]]: [[English|/ˈɑːŋ-/]] AHNK-ə-rə, Turkish: [[Turkish|[ˈaŋkaɾa]] (listen)), historically known as Ancyra ([[English|/ænˈsaɪrə/]] an-SY-rə) and Angora ([[English|/æŋˈɡɔːrə/]] ang-GOR-ə, also [[American_English|US]]: [[English|/ˈæŋɡərə/]] ANG-gə-rə), is the [[List_of_national_capitals|capital]] of [[Turkey|Turkey]].
sentence_5: Located in the [[Central_Anatolia_Region|central part]] of [[Anatolia|Anatolia]], the city has a population of 4.5 million in its urban centre and over 5.6 million in [[Ankara_Province|Ankara Province]], making it Turkey's [[List_of_cities_in_Turkey|second-largest city]] after [[Istanbul|Istanbul]].
sentence_6: Serving as the capital of the ancient [[Celts|Celtic]] state of [[Galatia|Galatia]] (280–64 BC), and later of the [[Roman_Empire|Roman]] province with the [[Galatia_(Roman_province)|same name]] (25 BC–7th century), the city is very old with various [[Hattians|Hattian]], [[Hittites|Hittite]], Lydian, Phrygian, [[Galatians_(people)|Galatian]], [[Hellenistic_civilization|Greek]], [[Achaemenid_Empire|Persian]], [[Ancient_Rome|Roman]], [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantine]], and [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman]] [[Archaeological_site|archaeological sites]].
sentence_7: The Ottomans made the city the capital first of the [[Anatolia_Eyalet|Anatolia Eyalet]] (1393–late 15th century), and then the [[Angora_Vilayet|Angora Vilayet]] (1867–1922).
sentence_8: The historical center of Ankara is a rocky hill rising 150 m (500 ft) over the left bank of the [[Ankara_River|Ankara River]], a tributary of the [[Sakarya_River|Sakarya River]].
sentence_9: The hill remains crowned by the ruins of [[Ankara_Castle|Ankara Castle]].
sentence_10: Although few of its outworks have survived, there are well-preserved examples of [[Roman_architecture|Roman]] and [[Ottoman_architecture|Ottoman architecture]] throughout the city, the most remarkable being the 20 BC [[Augusteum|Temple of Augustus and Rome]] that boasts the [[Monumentum_Ancyranum|Monumentum Ancyranum]], the inscription recording the [[Res_Gestae_Divi_Augusti|Res Gestae Divi Augusti]].
sentence_11: On 23 April 1920, the [[Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey|Grand National Assembly of Turkey]] was established in Ankara, which became the headquarters of the Turkish National Movement during the [[Turkish_War_of_Independence|Turkish War of Independence]].
sentence_12: Ankara became the new Turkish capital upon the establishment of the Republic on 29 October 1923, succeeding in this role the former Turkish capital Istanbul (Constantinople) following the [[Defeat_and_dissolution_of_the_Ottoman_Empire|fall of the Ottoman Empire]].
sentence_13: The [[Government_of_Turkey|government]] is a prominent employer, but Ankara is also an important commercial and industrial city, located at the centre of Turkey's road and railway networks.
sentence_14: The city gave its name to the [[Angora_wool|Angora wool]] shorn from [[Angora_rabbit|Angora rabbits]], the long-haired [[Angora_goat|Angora goat]] (the source of [[Mohair|mohair]]), and the [[Turkish_Angora|Angora cat]].
sentence_15: The area is also known for its pears, honey and [[Muscat_(grape_and_wine)|muscat]] grapes.
sentence_16: Although situated in one of the driest regions of Turkey and surrounded mostly by steppe vegetation (except for the forested areas on the southern periphery), Ankara can be considered a green city in terms of green areas per inhabitant, at 72 square metres (775 square feet) per head.
sentence_17: The orthography of the name Ankara has varied over the ages.
sentence_18: It has been identified with the [[Hittites|Hittite]] cult center Ankuwaš, although this remains a matter of debate.
sentence_19: In classical antiquity and during the medieval period, the city was known as Ánkyra (Ἄγκυρα, lit "[[Anchor|anchor]]") in Greek and Ancyra in [[Latin|Latin]]; the [[Galatian_language|Galatian Celtic]] name was probably a similar variant.
sentence_20: Following its annexation by the [[Seljuk_Turks|Seljuk Turks]] in 1073, the city became known in many European languages as Angora; it was also known in [[Ottoman_Turkish_language|Ottoman Turkish]] as Engürü.
sentence_21: The form "Angora" is preserved in the names of breeds of many different kinds of animals, and in the names of several locations in the US (see [[Angora_(disambiguation)|Angora]]).
sentence_22: The city has exported [[Mohair|mohair]] (from the [[Angora_goat|Angora goat]]) and [[Angora_wool|Angora wool]] (from the [[Angora_rabbit|Angora rabbit]]) internationally for centuries.
sentence_23: In the 19th century, the city also exported substantial amounts of [[Goatskin_(material)|goat]] and cat skins, [[Gum_arabic|gum]], [[Beeswax|wax]], [[Honey|honey]], berries, and [[Madder_root|madder root]].
sentence_24: It was connected to [[Istanbul|Istanbul]] by railway before the [[First_World_War|First World War]], continuing to export mohair, wool, berries, and [[Grain|grain]].
sentence_25: The [[Central_Anatolia_Region|Central Anatolia Region]] is one of the primary locations of grape and [[Turkish_wine|wine production in Turkey]], and Ankara is particularly famous for its Kalecik Karası and [[Muscat_(grape_and_wine)|Muscat grapes]]; and its [[Kavaklıdere_(winery)|Kavaklıdere wine]], which is produced in the [[Kavaklıdere,_Ankara|Kavaklıdere]] neighbourhood within the [[Çankaya,_Ankara|Çankaya]] district of the city.
sentence_26: Ankara is also famous for its pears.
sentence_27: Another renowned natural product of Ankara is its indigenous type of [[Honey|honey]] (Ankara Balı) which is known for its light color and is mostly produced by the [[Atatürk_Forest_Farm_and_Zoo|Atatürk Forest Farm and Zoo]] in the Gazi district, and by other facilities in the Elmadağ, Çubuk and Beypazarı districts.
sentence_28: [[Çubuk-1_Dam|Çubuk-1]] and [[Çubuk-2_Dam|Çubuk-2]] [[Dam|dams]] on the Çubuk Brook in Ankara were among the first dams constructed in the Turkish Republic.
sentence_29: Ankara is the center of the state-owned and private Turkish defence and [[Aerospace_manufacturer|aerospace]] companies, where the industrial plants and headquarters of the [[Turkish_Aerospace_Industries|Turkish Aerospace Industries]], [[Mechanical_and_Chemical_Industry_Corporation_(Turkey)|MKE]], ASELSAN, HAVELSAN, [[ROKETSAN|ROKETSAN]], FNSS, [[Nurol_Makina|Nurol Makina]], and numerous other firms are located.
sentence_30: Exports to foreign countries from these defence and aerospace firms have steadily increased in the past decades.
sentence_31: The [[International_Defence_Industry_Fair|IDEF]] in Ankara is one of the largest international expositions of the global arms industry.
sentence_32: A number of the global [[Automotive_industry|automotive companies]] also have production facilities in Ankara, such as the German bus and truck manufacturer [[MAN_SE|MAN SE]].
sentence_33: Ankara hosts the [[OSTIM_Industrial_Zone|OSTIM Industrial Zone]], Turkey's largest [[Industrial_park|industrial park]].
sentence_34: A large percentage of the complicated employment in Ankara is provided by the state institutions; such as the [[Ministry_(government_department)|ministries]], subministries, and other administrative bodies of the Turkish government.
sentence_35: There are also many foreign citizens working as diplomats or clerks in the embassies of their respective countries.
sentence_36: Ankara and [[Ankara_Province|its province]] are located in the [[Central_Anatolia_Region|Central Anatolia Region]] of Turkey.
sentence_37: The Çubuk Brook flows through the city center of Ankara.
sentence_38: It is connected in the western suburbs of the city to the [[Ankara_River|Ankara River]], which is a [[Tributary|tributary]] of the [[Sakarya_River|Sakarya River]].
sentence_39: Ankara has a [[Cold_semi-arid_climate|cold semi-arid climate]] ([[Köppen_climate_classification|Köppen climate classification]]: BSk).
sentence_40: Under the Trewartha climate classification, Ankara has a middle latitude steppe climate (BSk).
sentence_41: Due to its elevation and inland location, Ankara has cold and snowy winters, and hot and dry summers.
sentence_42: Rainfall occurs mostly during the spring and autumn.
sentence_43: The city lies in [[USDA|USDA]] [[Hardiness_zone|Hardiness zone]] 7b, and its annual average precipitation is fairly low at 388 millimeters (15 in), nevertheless precipitation can be observed throughout the year.
sentence_44: Monthly mean temperatures range from 0.3 °C (32.5 °F) in January to 23.5 °C (74.3 °F) in July, with an annual mean of 12.02 °C (53.6 °F).
sentence_45: Ankara had a population of 75,000 in 1927.
sentence_46: As of 2019, Ankara Province has a population of 5,639,076.
sentence_47: When Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923, it was designated as a planned city for 500,000 future inhabitants.
sentence_48: During the 1920s, 1930s and 1940s, the city grew in a planned and orderly pace.
sentence_49: However, from the 1950s onward, the city grew much faster than envisioned, because unemployment and poverty forced people to migrate from the countryside into the city in order to seek a better standard of living.
sentence_50: As a result, many illegal houses called [[Gecekondu|gecekondu]] were built around the city, causing the unplanned and uncontrolled urban landscape of Ankara, as not enough planned housing could be built fast enough.
sentence_51: Although precariously built, the vast majority of them have electricity, running water and modern household amenities.
sentence_52: Nevertheless, many of these gecekondus have been replaced by huge public housing projects in the form of [[Tower_block|tower blocks]] such as Elvankent, [[Eryaman,_Etimesgut|Eryaman]] and [[Güzelkent,_Etimesgut|Güzelkent]]; and also as mass housing compounds for military and civil service accommodation.
sentence_53: Although many gecekondus still remain, they too are gradually being replaced by mass housing compounds, as empty land plots in the city of Ankara for new construction projects are becoming impossible to find.
sentence_54: Çorum and Yozgat, which are located in Central Anatolia and whose population is decreasing, are the provinces with the highest net migration to Ankara.
sentence_55: About one third of the Central Anatolia population of 15,608,868 people resides in Ankara.
sentence_56: The population of Ankara has a higher education level than the country average.
sentence_57: According to 2008 data, 15-years-higher literacy rate creates 88% of the total provincial population (91% in men and 86% in women).
sentence_58: This ratio was 83% for Turkey (88% males, 79% females).
sentence_59: This difference is particularly evident in the university educated segment of the population.
sentence_60: The ratio of university and high school graduates to total population is 10.6% in Ankara, while 5.4% in Turkey.
sentence_61: See also: [[Ankara_Metro|Ankara Metro]], [[Ankara_Central_Station|Ankara Central Station]], and [[Esenboğa_International_Airport|Esenboğa International Airport]]
sentence_62: The Electricity, Gas, Bus General Directorate (EGO) operates the [[Ankara_Metro|Ankara Metro]] and other forms of public transportation.
sentence_63: Ankara is served by a suburban rail named [[Ankaray|Ankaray]] (A1) and three [[Rapid_transit|subway]] lines (M1, M2, M3) of the Ankara Metro with about 300,000 total daily commuters, while an additional subway line (M4) is under construction.
sentence_64: A 3.2 km (2.0 mi) long [[Gondola_lift|gondola lift]] with four stations connects the district of Şentepe to the [[Yenimahalle,_Ankara|Yenimahalle metro station]].
sentence_65: The [[Ankara_Central_Station|Ankara Central Station]] is a major rail hub in Turkey.
sentence_66: The [[Turkish_State_Railways|Turkish State Railways]] operates passenger train service from Ankara to other major cities, such as: [[Istanbul|Istanbul]], [[Eskişehir|Eskişehir]], [[Balıkesir|Balıkesir]], [[Kütahya|Kütahya]], İzmir, [[Kayseri|Kayseri]], [[Adana|Adana]], [[Kars|Kars]], [[Elâzığ|Elâzığ]], [[Malatya|Malatya]], [[Diyarbakır|Diyarbakır]], [[Karabük|Karabük]], [[Zonguldak|Zonguldak]] and [[Sivas|Sivas]].
sentence_67: Commuter rail also runs between the stations of [[Sincan-Kayaş_Line|Sincan and Kayaş]].
sentence_68: On 13 March 2009, the new [[Yüksek_Hızlı_Tren|Yüksek Hızlı Tren]] (YHT) [[High-speed_rail_in_Turkey|high-speed rail service]] began operation between Ankara and Eskişehir.
sentence_69: On 23 August 2011, another YHT high-speed line commercially started its service [[Ankara-Konya_high-speed_railway|between Ankara and Konya]].
sentence_70: On 25 July 2014, the [[Ankara-Istanbul_high-speed_railway|Ankara–Istanbul high-speed line]] of YHT entered service.
sentence_71: [[Esenboğa_International_Airport|Esenboğa International Airport]], located in the north-east of the city, is Ankara's main airport.
sentence_72: The average amount of time people spend commuting on public transit in Ankara on a weekday is 71 minutes.
sentence_73: 17% of public transit passengers, ride for more than two hours every day.
sentence_74: The average amount of time people wait at a stop or station for public transit is sixteen minutes, while 28% of users wait for over twenty minutes on average every day.
sentence_75: The average distance people usually ride in a single trip with public transit is 9.9 km (6.2 mi), while 27% travel for over 12 km (7.5 mi) in a single direction.
sentence_76: Ankara is politically a triple battleground between the ruling conservative [[Justice_and_Development_Party_(Turkey)|Justice and Development Party]] (AKP), the opposition [[Kemalism|Kemalist]] centre-left [[Republican_People's_Party_(Turkey)|Republican People's Party]] (CHP) and the nationalist far-right [[Nationalist_Movement_Party|Nationalist Movement Party]] (MHP).
sentence_77: The [[Ankara_Province|province of Ankara]] is divided into 25 districts.
sentence_78: The CHP's key and almost only political stronghold in Ankara lies within the central area of [[Çankaya,_Ankara_(district)|Çankaya]], which is the city's most populous district.
sentence_79: While the CHP has always gained between 60 and 70% of the vote in Çankaya since 2002, political support elsewhere throughout Ankara is minimal.
sentence_80: The high population within Çankaya, as well as [[Yenimahalle|Yenimahalle]] to an extent, has allowed the CHP to take overall second place behind the AKP in both local and general elections, with the MHP a close third, despite the fact that the MHP is politically stronger than the CHP in almost every other district.
sentence_81: Overall, the AKP enjoys the most support throughout the city.
sentence_82: The electorate of Ankara thus tend to vote in favour of the political right, far more so than the other main cities of [[Istanbul|Istanbul]] and [[Ä°zmir|Ä°zmir]].
sentence_83: In retrospect, the [[2013–14_protests_in_Turkey|2013–14 protests against the AKP government]] were particularly strong in Ankara, proving to be fatal on multiple occasions.
sentence_84: The city suffered from a series of terrorist attacks in 2015 and 2016, most notably on [[2015_Ankara_bombings|10 October 2015]]; [[February_2016_Ankara_bombing|17 February 2016]]; [[March_2016_Ankara_bombing|13 March 2016]]; and [[2016_Turkish_coup_d'état_attempt|15 July 2016]].
sentence_85: [[Melih_Gökçek|Melih Gökçek]] was the Metropolitan Mayor of Ankara between 1994 and 2017.
sentence_86: Initially elected in the [[1994_Turkish_local_elections|1994 local elections]], he was re-elected in [[1999_Turkish_local_elections|1999]], [[2004_Turkish_local_elections|2004]] and [[2009_Turkish_local_elections|2009]].
sentence_87: In the [[2014_Turkish_local_elections|2014 local elections]], Gökçek stood for a fifth term.
sentence_88: The MHP's metropolitan mayoral candidate for the 2009 local elections, [[Mansur_Yavaş|Mansur Yavaş]], stood as the CHP's candidate against Gökçek in 2014.
sentence_89: In a heavily controversial election, Gökçek was declared the winner by just 1% ahead of Yavaş amid allegations of systematic electoral fraud.
sentence_90: With the [[Supreme_Electoral_Council_of_Turkey|Supreme Electoral Council]] and courts rejecting his appeals, Yavaş declared his intention to take the irregularities to the [[European_Court_of_Human_Rights|European Court of Human Rights]].
sentence_91: Although Gökçek was inaugurated for a fifth term, most election observers believe that Yavaş was the winner of the election.
sentence_92: Gökçek resigned on 28 October 2017 and was replaced by the former mayor of [[Sincan,_Ankara|Sincan]] district, [[Mustafa_Tuna|Mustafa Tuna]].
sentence_93: Since 8 April 2019, the Mayor of Ankara is [[Mansur_Yavaş|Mansur Yavaş]] from the [[Republican_People's_Party_(Turkey)|Republican People's Party (CHP)]], who won the [[2019_Ankara_mayoral_election|mayoral election in 2019]].
sentence_94: The foundations of the [[Ankara_Castle|Ankara castle and citadel]] were laid by the Galatians on a prominent [[Lava|lava]] outcrop (), and the rest was completed by the Romans.
sentence_95: The Byzantines and Seljuks further made restorations and additions.
sentence_96: The area around and inside the citadel, being the oldest part of Ankara, contains many fine examples of traditional architecture.
sentence_97: There are also recreational areas to relax.
sentence_98: Many restored traditional Turkish houses inside the citadel area have found new life as restaurants, serving local cuisine.
sentence_99: The citadel was depicted in various Turkish banknotes during 1927–1952 and 1983–1989.
sentence_100: The remains, the stage, and the backstage of the Roman theatre can be seen outside [[Ankara_Castle|the castle]].
sentence_101: Roman statues that were found here are exhibited in the [[Museum_of_Anatolian_Civilizations|Museum of Anatolian Civilizations]].
sentence_102: The seating area is still under excavation.
sentence_103: Main article: [[Monumentum_Ancyranum|Monumentum Ancyranum]]
sentence_104: The Augusteum, now known as the Temple of Augustus and Rome, was built 25 x 20 BC following the conquest of Central Anatolia by the [[Roman_Empire|Roman Empire]].
sentence_105: Ancyra then formed the capital of the new province of [[Galatia|Galatia]].
sentence_106: After the death of [[Augustus|Augustus]] in AD 14, a copy of the text of the [[Res_Gestae_Divi_Augusti|Res Gestae Divi Augusti]] (the [[Monumentum_Ancyranum|Monumentum Ancyranum]]) was inscribed on the interior of the temple's pronaos in Latin and a Greek translation on an exterior wall of the cella.
sentence_107: The temple on the ancient acropolis of Ancyra was enlarged in the 2nd century and converted into a church in the 5th century.
sentence_108: It is located in the Ulus quarter of the city.
sentence_109: It was subsequently publicized by the [[Austrian_Empire|Austrian]] ambassador [[Ogier_Ghiselin_de_Busbecq|Ogier Ghiselin de Busbecq]] in the 16th century.
sentence_110: The [[Roman_Baths_of_Ankara|Roman Baths of Ankara]] have all the typical features of a classical [[Thermae|Roman bath complex]]: a [[Frigidarium|frigidarium]] (cold room), a [[Tepidarium|tepidarium]] (warm room) and a [[Caldarium|caldarium]] (hot room).
sentence_111: The baths were built during the reign of the Roman emperor [[Caracalla|Caracalla]] in the early 3rd century to honor [[Asclepius|Asclepios]], the God of Medicine.
sentence_112: Today, only the basement and first floors remain.
sentence_113: It is situated in the Ulus quarter.
sentence_114: The [[Roman_Road_of_Ankara|Roman Road of Ankara]] or Cardo Maximus was found in 1995 by Turkish archaeologist Cevdet Bayburtluoğlu.
sentence_115: It is 216 metres (709 feet) long and 6.7 metres (22.0 feet) wide.
sentence_116: Many ancient artifacts were discovered during the excavations along the road and most of them are displayed at the [[Museum_of_Anatolian_Civilizations|Museum of Anatolian Civilizations]].
sentence_117: The Column of Julian or Julianus, now in the Ulus district, was erected in honor of the Roman emperor [[Julian_the_Apostate|Julian the Apostate]]'s visit to Ancyra in 362.
sentence_118: [[Kocatepe_Mosque|Kocatepe Mosque]] is the largest mosque in the city.
sentence_119: Located in the Kocatepe quarter, it was constructed between 1967 and 1987 in classical [[Ottoman_architecture|Ottoman style]] with four minarets.
sentence_120: Its size and prominent location have made it a landmark for the city.
sentence_121: Ahmet Hamdi Akseki Mosque is located near the Presidency of Religious Affairs on the [[Eskişehir|Eskişehir]] Road.
sentence_122: Built in the Turkish neoclassical style, it is one of the largest new mosques in the city, completed and opened in 2013.
sentence_123: It can accommodate 6 thousand people during general prayers, and up to 30 thousand people during funeral prayers.
sentence_124: The mosque was decorated with [[Sultanate_of_Rum|Anatolian]] [[Seljuk_architecture|Seljuk style]] patterns.
sentence_125: It is the largest Ottoman mosque in Ankara and was built by the famous architect Sinan in the 16th century.
sentence_126: The mimber (pulpit) and mihrap (prayer niche) are of white marble, and the mosque itself is of Ankara stone, an example of very fine workmanship.
sentence_127: This mosque, in the Ulus quarter next to the [[Monumentum_Ancyranum|Temple of Augustus]], was built in the early 15th century in [[Seljuk_architecture|Seljuk style]] by an unknown architect.
sentence_128: It was subsequently restored by architect [[Mimar_Sinan|Mimar Sinan]] in the 16th century, with [[Kütahya|Kütahya]] tiles being added in the 18th century.
sentence_129: The mosque was built in honor of [[Hacı_Bayram-ı_Veli|Hacı Bayram-ı Veli]], whose tomb is next to the mosque, two years before his death (1427–28).
sentence_130: The usable space inside this mosque is 437 m (4,704 sq ft) on the first floor and 263 m (2,831 sq ft) on the second floor.
sentence_131: It was founded in the Ulus quarter near the Ankara Citadel and was constructed by the Ahi fraternity during the late 14th and early 15th centuries.
sentence_132: The finely carved walnut mimber (pulpit) is of particular interest.
sentence_133: The Alâeddin Mosque is the oldest mosque in Ankara.
sentence_134: It has a [[Wood_carving|carved]] [[Juglans|walnut]] [[Minbar|mimber]], the inscription on which records that the mosque was completed in early [[Islamic_calendar|AH 574]] (which corresponds to the summer of 1178 AD) and was built by the [[Seljuk_dynasty|Seljuk]] prince Muhiddin Mesud Şah (d. 1204), the [[Bey|Bey]] of Ankara, who was the son of the [[Anatolian_Seljuk_Sultanate|Anatolian Seljuk sultan]] Kılıç Arslan II (reigned 1156–1192.)
sentence_135: The [[Victory_Monument_(Ankara)|Victory Monument]] ([[Turkish_language|Turkish]]: ) was crafted by Austrian sculptor Heinrich Krippel in 1925 and was erected in 1927 at [[Ulus_Square|Ulus Square]].
sentence_136: The monument is made of [[Marble|marble]] and [[Bronze|bronze]] and features an [[Equestrian_statue|equestrian statue]] of [[Mustafa_Kemal_Atatürk|Mustafa Kemal Atatürk]], who wears a Republic era modern military uniform, with the rank [[Field_Marshal|Field Marshal]].
sentence_137: Located at Zafer Square ([[Turkish_language|Turkish]]: Zafer Meydanı), the [[Marble|marble]] and [[Bronze|bronze]] statue was crafted by the renowned Italian sculptor Pietro Canonica in 1927 and depicts a standing Atatürk who wears a Republic era modern military uniform, with the rank [[Field_Marshal|Field Marshal]].

section_27.value: Monument to a Secure, Confident Future

sentence_138: This monument, located in Güven Park near Kızılay Square, was erected in 1935 and bears Atatürk's advice to his people: "Turk!
sentence_139: Be proud, work hard, and believe in yourself."
sentence_140: The monument was depicted on the reverse of the Turkish 5 [[Turkish_lira|lira]] banknote of 1937–1952 and of the 1000 lira banknotes of 1939–1946.
sentence_141: Erected in 1978 at [[Sıhhiye_Square|Sıhhiye Square]], this impressive monument symbolizes the [[Hattians|Hatti]] Sun Disc (which was later adopted by the [[Hittites|Hittites]]) and commemorates Anatolia's earliest known civilization.
sentence_142: The Hatti Sun Disc has been used in the previous logo of Ankara Metropolitan Municipality.
sentence_143: It was also used in the previous logo of the Ministry of Culture & Tourism.
sentence_144: [[Suluhan|Suluhan]] is a historical Inn in Ankara.
sentence_145: It is also called the Hasanpaşa Han.
sentence_146: It is about 400 meters (1,300 ft) southeast of [[Ulus_Square|Ulus Square]] and situated in the Hacıdoğan neighbourhood.
sentence_147: According to the vakfiye (inscription) of the building, the Ottoman era han was commissioned by Hasan Pasha, a regional [[Beylerbey|beylerbey]], and was constructed between 1508 and 1511, during the final years of the reign of Sultan [[Bayezid_II|Bayezid II]].
sentence_148: There are 102 rooms (now shops) which face the two yards.
sentence_149: In each room there is a window, a niche and a chimney.
sentence_150: [[Çengelhan_Rahmi_Koç_Museum|Çengelhan Rahmi Koç Museum]] is a museum of industrial technology situated in , an Ottoman era Inn which was completed in 1523, during the early years of the reign of Sultan [[Suleiman_the_Magnificent|Suleiman the Magnificent]].
sentence_151: The exhibits include industrial/technological artifacts from the 1850s onwards.
sentence_152: There are also sections about Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of modern Turkey; Vehbi Koç, Rahmi Koç's father and one of the first industrialists of Turkey, and Ankara city.
sentence_153: Foreign visitors to Ankara usually like to visit the old shops in Çıkrıkçılar Yokuşu (Weavers' Road) near Ulus, where myriad things ranging from traditional fabrics, hand-woven carpets and leather products can be found at bargain prices.
sentence_154: Bakırcılar Çarşısı (Bazaar of Coppersmiths) is particularly popular, and many interesting items, not just of copper, can be found here like jewelry, carpets, costumes, antiques and embroidery.
sentence_155: Up the hill to the castle gate, there are many shops selling a huge and fresh collection of spices, dried fruits, nuts, and other produce.
