sentence_418: In 2007, a 30-year lease was granted for the [[Mes_Aynak#Copper_Mine|Aynak]] copper mine to the [[China_Metallurgical_Group|China Metallurgical Group]] for $3 billion, making it the biggest foreign investment and private business venture in Afghanistan's history.
sentence_419: The state-run [[Steel_Authority_of_India|Steel Authority of India]] won the mining rights to develop the huge Hajigak iron ore deposit in central Afghanistan.
sentence_420: Government officials estimate that 30% of the country's untapped mineral deposits are worth at least $1 trillion.
sentence_421: One official asserted that "this will become the backbone of the Afghan economy" and a Pentagon memo stated that Afghanistan could become the "Saudi Arabia of lithium".
sentence_422: In a 2011 news story, the [[The_Christian_Science_Monitor|CSM]] reported, "The United States and other Western nations that have borne the brunt of the cost of the Afghan war have been conspicuously absent from the bidding process on Afghanistan's mineral deposits, leaving it mostly to regional powers."
sentence_423: Access to biocapacity in Afghanistan is lower than world average.
sentence_424: In 2016, Afghanistan had 0.43 global hectares of biocapacity per person within its territory, much less than the world average of 1.6 global hectares per person.
sentence_425: In 2016 Afghanistan used 0.73 global hectares of biocapacity per person - their [[Ecological_footprint|ecological footprint]] of consumption.
sentence_426: This means they use just under double as much biocapacity as Afghanistan contains.
sentence_427: As a result, Afghanistan is running a biocapacity deficit.
sentence_428: Main articles: [[Energy_in_Afghanistan|Energy in Afghanistan]] and [[Renewable_energy_in_Afghanistan|Renewable energy in Afghanistan]]
sentence_429: According to the [[World_Bank|World Bank]], 98% of the rural population have access to electricity in 2018, up from 28% in 2008.
sentence_430: Overall the figure stands at 98.7%.
sentence_431: As of 2016, Afghanistan produces 1,400 [[Megawatt|megawatts]] of power, but still imports the majority of electricity via transmission lines from Iran and the Central Asian states.
sentence_432: The majority of electricity production is via hydropower, helped by the amount of rivers and streams that flow from the mountains.
sentence_433: However electricity is not always reliable and blackouts happen, including in Kabul.
sentence_434: In recent years an increasing number of [[Solar_power|solar]], [[Biomass|biomass]] and wind power plants have been constructed.
sentence_435: Currently under development are the [[CASA-1000|CASA-1000]] project which will transmit electricity from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, and the [[Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India_pipeline|Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India]] (TAPI) gas pipeline.
sentence_436: Power is managed by the Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS, Afghanistan Electricity Company).
sentence_437: Important dams include the [[Kajaki_Dam|Kajaki Dam]], [[Dahla_Dam|Dahla Dam]], and the [[Sardeh_Band_Dam|Sardeh Band Dam]].
sentence_438: Main article: Tourism in Afghanistan
sentence_439: Tourism is a small industry in Afghanistan due to security issues.
sentence_440: Nevertheless, some 20,000 foreign tourists visit the country annually as of 2016.
sentence_441: In particular an important region for domestic and international tourism is the picturesque [[Bamyan|Bamyan]] Valley, which includes lakes, canyons and historical sites, helped by the fact it is in a safe area away from insurgent activity.
sentence_442: Smaller numbers visit and trek in regions such as the [[Wakhan|Wakhan]] Valley, which is also one of the world's most remote communities.
sentence_443: From the late 1960s onwards, Afghanistan was a popular stop on the famous [[Hippie_trail|Hippie trail]], attracting many Europeans and Americans.
sentence_444: Coming from Iran, the trail traveled through various Afghan provinces and cities including [[Herat|Herat]], [[Kandahar|Kandahar]] and [[Kabul|Kabul]] before crossing to northern Pakistan, northern India, and [[Nepal|Nepal]].
sentence_445: Tourism peaked in 1977, the year before the start of political instability and armed conflict.
sentence_446: The city of [[Ghazni|Ghazni]] has significant history and historical sites, and together with [[Bamyan|Bamyan]] city have in recent years been voted Islamic Cultural Capital and South Asia Cultural Capital respectively.
sentence_447: The cities of [[Herat|Herat]], [[Kandahar|Kandahar]], [[Balkh|Balkh]], and [[Zaranj|Zaranj]] are also very historic.
sentence_448: The [[Minaret_of_Jam|Minaret of Jam]] in the [[Hari_River,_Afghanistan|Hari River]] valley is a [[World_Heritage_Site|UNESCO World Heritage site]].
sentence_449: A cloak reputedly worn by Islam's prophet [[Muhammad|Muhammad]] is kept inside the [[Shrine_of_the_Cloak|Shrine of the Cloak]] in Kandahar, a city founded by [[Alexander_the_Great|Alexander]] and the first capital of Afghanistan.
sentence_450: The [[Citadel_of_Herat|citadel of Alexander]] in the western city of Herat has been renovated in recent years and is a popular attraction.
sentence_451: In the north of the country is the [[Shrine_of_Ali|Shrine of Ali]], believed by many to be the location where [[Ali|Ali]] was buried.
sentence_452: The [[National_Museum_of_Afghanistan|National Museum of Afghanistan]] is located in Kabul and hosts a large number of Buddhist, [[Bactria|Bactrian]] Greek and early Islamic antiquities; the museum suffered greatly by civil war but has been slowly restoring since the early 2000s.
sentence_453: Main article: [[Communications_in_Afghanistan|Communications in Afghanistan]]
sentence_454: Telecommunication services in Afghanistan are provided by [[Afghan_Telecom|Afghan Telecom]], [[Afghan_Wireless|Afghan Wireless]], [[Etisalat|Etisalat]], [[MTN_Group|MTN Group]], and [[Roshan_(telco)|Roshan]].
sentence_455: The country uses its own space [[Satellite|satellite]] called [[Afghansat_1|Afghansat 1]], which provides services to millions of phone, internet, and television subscribers.
sentence_456: By 2001 following years of civil war, telecommunications was virtually a non-existent sector, but by 2016 it had grown to a $2 billion industry, with 22 million mobile phone subscribers and 5 million internet users.
sentence_457: The sector employs at least 120,000 people nationwide.
sentence_458: Main article: [[Transport_in_Afghanistan|Transport in Afghanistan]]
sentence_459: See also: [[List_of_airports_in_Afghanistan|List of airports in Afghanistan]] and [[Rail_transport_in_Afghanistan|Rail transport in Afghanistan]]
sentence_460: Due to Afghanistan's geography, transport between various parts of the country have historically been difficult.
sentence_461: The backbone of Afghanistan's road network is [[Highway_1_(Afghanistan)|Highway 1]], often called the "Ring Road", which extends for 2,210 kilometers (1,370 mi) and connects five major cities: Kabul, Ghazni, Kandahar, Herat and Mazar-i-Sharif, with spurs to Kunduz and Jalalabad and various border crossings, while skirting around the mountains of the Hindu Kush.
sentence_462: The Ring Road is crucially important for domestic and international trade and the economy.
sentence_463: A key portion of the Ring Road is the [[Salang_Tunnel|Salang Tunnel]], completed in 1964, which facilitates travel through the Hindu Kush mountain range and connects northern and southern Afghanistan.
sentence_464: It is the only land route that connects Central Asia to the [[Indian_subcontinent|Indian subcontinent]].
sentence_465: Several mountain passes allow travel between the Hindu Kush in other areas.
sentence_466: Serious traffic accidents are common on Afghan roads and highways, particularly on the [[Kabul–Kandahar_Highway|Kabul–Kandahar]] and the [[Kabul–Jalalabad_Road|Kabul–Jalalabad Road]].
sentence_467: Traveling by bus in Afghanistan remains dangerous due to militant activities.
sentence_468: Air transport in Afghanistan is provided by the national carrier, [[Ariana_Afghan_Airlines|Ariana Afghan Airlines]], and by the private company [[Kam_Air|Kam Air]].
sentence_469: Airlines from a number of countries also provide flights in and out of the country.
sentence_470: These include [[Air_India|Air India]], [[Emirates_(airline)|Emirates]], [[Gulf_Air|Gulf Air]], [[Iran_Aseman_Airlines|Iran Aseman Airlines]], Pakistan International Airlines, and [[Turkish_Airlines|Turkish Airlines]].
sentence_471: The country has four international airports: [[Hamid_Karzai_International_Airport|Hamid Karzai International Airport]] (formerly Kabul International Airport), [[Kandahar_International_Airport|Kandahar International Airport]], [[Herat_International_Airport|Herat International Airport]], and [[Mazar-e_Sharif_International_Airport|Mazar-e Sharif International Airport]].
sentence_472: Including domestic airports, there are 43.
sentence_473: [[Bagram_Air_Base|Bagram Air Base]] is a major military airfield.
sentence_474: The country has three rail links: one, a 75-kilometer (47 mi) line from [[Mazar-i-Sharif|Mazar-i-Sharif]] to the [[Afghanistan–Uzbekistan_Friendship_Bridge|Uzbekistan border]]; a 10-kilometer (6.2 mi) long line from [[Toraghundi|Toraghundi]] to the [[Turkmenistan|Turkmenistan]] border (where it continues as part of [[Türkmendemirýollary|Turkmen Railways]]); and a short link from [[Aqina|Aqina]] across the Turkmen border to [[Kerki|Kerki]], which is planned to be extended further across Afghanistan.
sentence_475: These lines are used for freight only and there is no passenger service.
sentence_476: A rail line between [[Khaf,_Iran|Khaf]], Iran and [[Herat|Herat]], western Afghanistan, intended for both freight and passengers, is under construction as of 2019.
sentence_477: About 125 kilometers (78 mi) of the line will lie on the Afghan side.
sentence_478: There are various proposals for the construction of additional rail lines in the country.
sentence_479: Private vehicle ownership has increased substantially since the early 2000s.
sentence_480: Taxis are yellow in color and consist of both cars and [[Auto_rickshaw|auto rickshaws]].
sentence_481: In rural Afghanistan, villagers often use [[Donkey|donkeys]], [[Mule|mules]] or [[Horse|horses]] to transport or carry goods.
sentence_482: [[Camel|Camels]] are primarily used by the [[Kochi|Kochi]] nomads.
sentence_483: Bicycles are popular throughout Afghanistan.
sentence_484: Main article: [[Education_in_Afghanistan|Education in Afghanistan]]
sentence_485: [[Education_in_Afghanistan|Education in Afghanistan]] includes [[K–12_(education)|K–12]] and higher education, which is overseen by the [[Ministry_of_Education_(Afghanistan)|Ministry of Education]] and the [[Ministry_of_Higher_Education_(Afghanistan)|Ministry of Higher Education]].
sentence_486: There are over 16,000 schools in the country and roughly 9 million students.
sentence_487: Of this, about 60% are males and 40% females.
sentence_488: Over 174,000 students are enrolled in different [[List_of_universities_in_Afghanistan|universities]] around the country.
sentence_489: About 21% of these are females.
sentence_490: Former Education Minister [[Ghulam_Farooq_Wardak|Ghulam Farooq Wardak]] had stated that construction of 8,000 schools is required for the remaining children who are deprived of formal learning.
sentence_491: The top universities in Afghanistan are the American University of Afghanistan (AUAF) followed by [[Kabul_University|Kabul University]] (KU), both of which are located in Kabul.
sentence_492: The [[National_Military_Academy_of_Afghanistan|National Military Academy of Afghanistan]], modeled after the [[United_States_Military_Academy|United States Military Academy]] at West Point, is a four-year military development institution dedicated to graduating officers for the [[Afghan_Armed_Forces|Afghan Armed Forces]].
sentence_493: The [[Afghan_Defense_University|Afghan Defense University]] was constructed near [[Qargha_Reservoir|Qargha]] in Kabul.
sentence_494: Major universities outside of Kabul include [[Kandahar_University|Kandahar University]] in the south, [[Herat_University|Herat University]] in the northwest, [[Balkh_University|Balkh University]] and Kunduz University in the north, Nangarhar University and [[Khost_University|Khost University]] in the east.
sentence_495: The United States is building six faculties of education and five provincial teacher training colleges around the country, two large secondary schools in Kabul, and one school in Jalalabad.
sentence_496: Kabul University was founded in 1932 and is a respected institute that played a significant part in the country's education; from the 1960s the Kabul University was also a hotbed of radical political ideologies such as Marxism and Islamism, which played major parts in society, politics and the war that began in 1978.
sentence_497: As of 2018 the literacy rate of the population age 15 and older is 43.02% (males 55.48% and females 29.81%).
sentence_498: The Afghan National Security Forces are provided with mandatory literacy courses.
sentence_499: Main article: [[Health_in_Afghanistan|Health in Afghanistan]]
sentence_500: According to the [[Human_Development_Index|Human Development Index]], Afghanistan is the [[List_of_countries_by_Human_Development_Index|15th least developed country in the world]].
sentence_501: The average [[List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy|life expectancy]] is estimated to be around 60 years.
sentence_502: The country's [[Maternal_mortality|maternal mortality]] rate is 396 deaths/100,000 live births and its [[Infant_mortality|infant mortality]] rate is 66 to 112.8 deaths in every 1,000 live births.
sentence_503: The [[Ministry_of_Public_Health_(Afghanistan)|Ministry of Public Health]] plans to cut the infant mortality rate to 400 for every 100,000 live births before 2020.
sentence_504: The country has more than 3,000 [[Midwifery|midwives]], with an additional 300 to 400 being trained each year.
sentence_505: There are over 100 [[List_of_hospitals_in_Afghanistan|hospitals in Afghanistan]], with the most advanced treatments being available in Kabul.
sentence_506: The French Medical Institute for Children and [[Indira_Gandhi_Children's_Hospital|Indira Gandhi Children's Hospital]] in Kabul are the leading [[Children's_hospital|children's hospitals]] in the country.
sentence_507: Some of the other leading hospitals in Kabul include the [[Jamhuriat_Hospital|Jamhuriat Hospital]] and [[Jinnah_Hospital_(Kabul)|Jinnah Hospital]].
sentence_508: In spite of all this, many Afghans travel to Pakistan and India for advanced treatment.
sentence_509: It was reported in 2006 that nearly 60% of the Afghan population lives within a two-hour walk of the nearest health facility.
sentence_510: [[Disability|Disability]] rate is also high in Afghanistan due to the decades of war.
sentence_511: It was reported recently that about 80,000 people are missing limbs.
sentence_512: Non-governmental charities such as [[Save_the_Children|Save the Children]] and [[Mahboba's_Promise|Mahboba's Promise]] assist orphans in association with governmental structures.
sentence_513: [[Demographic_and_Health_Surveys|Demographic and Health Surveys]] is working with the Indian Institute of Health Management Research and others to conduct a survey in Afghanistan focusing on [[Maternal_death|maternal death]], among other things.
sentence_515: Afghanistan is a predominantly tribal society, with different regions of the country having their own cultures as a result of differing ethnicities and geographic obstacles that makes much of the country remote.
sentence_516: Family is the mainstay of Afghan society and families are often headed by a [[Patriarch|patriarch]].
sentence_517: In the southern and eastern region, the people live according to the [[Pashtun_culture|Pashtun culture]] by following Pashtunwali (the Pashtun way).
sentence_518: Key tenets of Pashtunwali include [[Melmastia|hospitality]], the provision of [[Nanawatai|sanctuary]] to those seeking refuge, and revenge for the shedding of blood.
sentence_519: The Pashtuns (and Baloch) are largely connected to the culture of South Asia.
sentence_520: The remaining Afghans are culturally Persian and [[Turkic_peoples|Turkic]].
sentence_521: Some non-Pashtuns who live in proximity with Pashtuns have adopted Pashtunwali in a process called [[Pashtunization|Pashtunization]], while some Pashtuns have been Persianized.
sentence_522: Those who have lived in Pakistan and Iran over the last 30 years have been further influenced by the cultures of those neighboring nations.
sentence_523: The Afghan people are known to be strongly religious.
sentence_524: Afghans, particularly Pashtuns, are noted for their tribal solidarity and high regard for personal honor.
sentence_525: One writer considers the tribal system to be the best way of organizing large groups of people in a country that is geographically difficult, and in a society that, from a materialistic point of view, has an uncomplicated lifestyle.
sentence_526: There are various [[Ethnic_groups_in_Afghanistan|Afghan tribes]], and an estimated 2–3 million [[Kochi_people|nomads]].
sentence_527: Afghan culture is deeply [[Islamic_culture|Islamic]], but pre-Islamic practices persist.
sentence_528: One example is [[Bacha_bazi|bacha bazi]], a term for activities involving sexual relations between older men and younger adolescent men, or boys.
sentence_529: [[Child_marriage_in_Afghanistan|Child marriage]] is prevalent in Afghanistan; the legal age for marriage is 16.
sentence_530: The most preferred marriage in Afghan society is to one's [[Parallel_and_cross_cousins|parallel cousin]], and the groom is often expected to pay a [[Bride_price|bride price]].
sentence_531: In the villages, families typically occupy [[Mudbrick|mudbrick]] houses, or compounds with mudbrick or stone walled houses.
sentence_532: Villages typically have a headman (malik), a master for water disribution (mirab) and a religious teacher (mullah).
sentence_533: Men would typically work on the fields, joined by women during harvest.
sentence_534: About 15% of the population are [[Nomadic|nomadic]], locally called [[Kochi|kochis]].
sentence_535: When nomads pass villages they often buy supplies such as tea, wheat and [[Kerosene|kerosene]] from the villagers; villagers buy [[Wool|wool]] and milk from the nomads.
sentence_536: [[Afghan_clothing|Afghan clothing]] for both men and women typically consists of various forms of [[Shalwar_kameez|shalwar kameez]], especially [[Perahan_tunban|perahan tunban]] and [[Khet_partug|khet partug]].
sentence_537: Women would normally wear a [[Chador|chador]] for head covering; some women, typically from highly conservative communities, wear the [[Burqa|burqa]], a full body covering.
sentence_538: These were worn by some women of the Pashtun community well before Islam came to the region, but the [[Taliban|Taliban]] enforced this dress on women when they were in power.
sentence_539: Another popular dress is the chapan which acts as a coat.
sentence_540: The [[Karakul_(hat)|karakul]] is a hat made from the fur of a specific regional breed of sheep.
sentence_541: It was favored by former kings of Afghanistan and became known to much of the world in the 21st century when it was constantly worn by President [[Hamid_Karzai|Hamid Karzai]].
sentence_542: The [[Pakol|pakol]] is another traditional hat originating from the far east of the country; it was popularly worn by the guerilla leader [[Ahmad_Shah_Massoud|Ahmad Shah Massoud]].
sentence_543: The Mazari hat originates from northern Afghanistan.
sentence_545: The nation has a complex history that has survived either in its current cultures or in the form of various languages and monuments.
sentence_546: Afghanistan contains many remnants from all ages, including [[Ancient_Greece|Greek]] and [[Buddhist|Buddhist]] stupas, monasteries, monuments, temples and Islamic minarets.
sentence_547: Among the most well known are the [[Great_Mosque_of_Herat|Great Mosque of Herat]], the [[Blue_Mosque_(Mazar-i-Sharif)|Blue Mosque]], the [[Minaret_of_Jam|Minaret of Jam]], the [[Chil_Zena|Chil Zena]], the Qala-i Bost in [[Lashkargah|Lashkargah]], the ancient Greek city of [[Ai-Khanoum|Ai-Khanoum]].
sentence_548: However, many of its historic monuments have been damaged in modern times due to the civil wars.
sentence_549: The two famous [[Buddhas_of_Bamiyan|Buddhas of Bamiyan]] were destroyed by the Taliban, who regarded them as [[Idolatry|idolatrous]].
sentence_550: Despite that, archaeologists are still finding Buddhist relics in different parts of the country, some of them dating back to the 2nd century.
sentence_551: As there was no colonialism in the modern era in Afghanistan, European-style architecture is rare; most notably the Victory Arch at [[Paghman|Paghman]], and the [[Darul_Aman_Palace|Darul Aman Palace]] in Kabul, were built in this style in the 1920s by the Afghans themselves.
sentence_553: Carpet [[Weaving|weaving]] is an ancient practice in Afghanistan, and many of these are still [[Handicraft|handmade]] by tribal and nomadic people today.
sentence_554: Carpets have been produced in the region for thousands of years and traditionally done by women.
sentence_555: Some crafters express their feelings through the designs of rugs; for example after the outbreak of the [[Soviet-Afghan_War|Soviet-Afghan War]], "[[War_rugs|war rugs]]" were created with designs representing pain and misery caused by the conflict.
sentence_556: Every province has its own specific characteristics in making rugs.
sentence_557: In some of the Turkic-populated areas in the north-west, bride and wedding ceremony prices are driven by the bride's weaving skills.
sentence_558: [[Pottery|Pottery]] has been crafted in Afghanistan for millennia.
sentence_559: The village of [[Istalif|Istalif]], north of Kabul, is in particular a major center, known for its unique turquoise and green pottery, and their methods of crafting have remained the same for centuries.
sentence_560: Much of [[Lapis_lazuli|lapis lazuli]] stones were earthed in modern-day Afghanistan which were used in [[Chinese_porcelain|Chinese porcelain]] as [[Cobalt_blue|cobalt blue]], later used in ancient Mesopotamia and [[Turkey|Turkey]].
sentence_561: The lands of Afghanistan have a long history of art, with the world's earliest known usage of oil painting found in cave murals in the country.
sentence_562: A notable art style that developed in Afghanistan and eastern Pakistan is [[Gandhara_Art|Gandhara Art]], produced by a fusion of Greco-Roman art and Buddhist art between the 1st and 7th centuries CE.
sentence_563: Later eras saw increased use of the [[Persian_miniature|Persian miniature]] style, with [[Kamāl_ud-Dīn_Behzād|Kamaleddin Behzad]] of [[Herat|Herat]] being one of the most notable miniature artists of the [[Timurid_dynasty|Timurid]] and early [[Safavid_dynasty|Safavid]] periods.
sentence_564: Since the 1900s, the nation began to use Western techniques in art.
sentence_565: [[Abdul_Ghafoor_Breshna|Abdul Ghafoor Breshna]] was a prominent Afghan painter and sketch artist from Kabul during the 20th century.
sentence_567: Afghanistan has around 350 [[List_of_radio_stations_in_Afghanistan|radio stations]] and over 200 television stations.
sentence_568: Radio Television Afghanistan, originating from 1925, is the state public broadcaster.
sentence_569: Television programs began airing in the 1970s and today there are many private television channels such as [[TOLO_(TV_channel)|TOLO]] and Shamshad TV.
sentence_570: The first Afghan newspaper was published in 1873, and there are hundreds of print outlets today.
sentence_571: By the 1920s, Radio Kabul was broadcasting local radio services.
sentence_572: [[Voice_of_America|Voice of America]], [[BBC_World_Service|BBC]], and [[Radio_Liberty|Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]] (RFE/RL) broadcast in both of Afghanistan's official languages on radio.
sentence_573: Press restrictions have been gradually relaxed and private media diversified since 2002, after more than two decades of tight controls.
sentence_574: Afghans have long been accustomed to watching Indian [[Bollywood|Bollywood]] films and listening to its [[Filmi|filmi]] songs.
sentence_575: It has been claimed that Afghanistan is among the biggest markets for the Hindi film industry.
sentence_576: The stereotypes of Afghans in India ([[Kabul|Kabuliwala]] or Pathani) has also been represented in some Bollywood films by actors.
sentence_577: Many Bollywood film stars have roots in Afghanistan, including [[Salman_Khan|Salman Khan]], [[Saif_Ali_Khan|Saif Ali Khan]], [[Shah_Rukh_Khan|Shah Rukh Khan]], [[Aamir_Khan|Aamir Khan]], [[Feroz_Khan_(Indian_actor)|Feroz Khan]], [[Kader_Khan|Kader Khan]], Naseeruddin Shah, [[Zarine_Khan|Zarine Khan]], [[Celina_Jaitly|Celina Jaitly]], and a number of others.
sentence_578: Several Bollywood films have been shot inside Afghanistan, including [[Dharmatma|Dharmatma]], [[Khuda_Gawah|Khuda Gawah]], [[Escape_from_Taliban|Escape from Taliban]], and [[Kabul_Express|Kabul Express]].
sentence_580: Afghan classical music has close historical links with [[Indian_classical_music|Indian classical music]] and use the same Hindustani terminology and theories like [[Raga|raga]].
sentence_581: Genres of this style of music include ghazal (poetic music) and instruments such as the Indian [[Tabla|tabla]], sitar and [[Harmonium|harmonium]], and local instruments like [[Zerbaghali|zerbaghali]], as well as [[Dayereh|dayereh]] and [[Tanbur|tanbur]] which are also known in Central Asia, the Caucusus and the Middle East.
sentence_582: The [[Rubab_(instrument)|rubab]] is the country's national instrument and precurses the Indian sarod instrument.
sentence_583: Some of the famous artists of classical music include [[Ustad_Sarahang|Ustad Sarahang]] and Sarban.
sentence_584: Pop music developed in the 1950s through Radio Kabul and was influential in social change.
sentence_585: During this time female artists also started appearing, at first [[Mermon_Parwin|Mermon Parwin]].
sentence_586: Perhaps the most famous artist of this genre was [[Ahmad_Zahir|Ahmad Zahir]], who synthesized many genres and continues to be renowned for his voice and rich lyrics long after his death in 1979.
sentence_587: Other notable masters of traditional or popular Afghan music include [[Nashenas|Nashenas]], [[Ubaidullah_Jan|Ubaidullah Jan]], Mahwash, Ahmad Wali, [[Farhad_Darya|Farhad Darya]], and Naghma.
sentence_588: [[Attan|Attan]] is the national dance of Afghanistan, a group dance popularly performed by Afghans of all backgrounds.
sentence_589: The dance is considered part of Afghan identity.
sentence_591: Afghan cuisine is largely based upon the nation's chief crops, such as wheat, maize, [[Barley|barley]] and rice.
sentence_592: Accompanying these staples are native fruits and vegetables as well as dairy products such as milk, [[Yogurt|yogurt]] and [[Whey|whey]].
sentence_593: Kabuli palaw is the [[National_dish|national dish]] of Afghanistan.
sentence_594: The nation's culinary specialties reflect its ethnic and geographic diversity.
sentence_595: Afghanistan is known for its high quality [[Pomegranate_production_in_Afghanistan|pomegranates]], grapes, and sweet melons.
sentence_596: Tea is a favorite drink among Afghans, and they typically eat [[Naan|naan]] breads, yoghurts, rice and meat in a typical diet.
sentence_598: Classic [[Persian_literature|Persian]] and [[Pashto_literature_and_poetry|Pashto poetry]] are a cherished part of Afghan culture.
sentence_599: Poetry has always been one of the major educational pillars in the region, to the level that it has integrated itself into culture.
sentence_600: One of the poetic styles is called [[Landay_(poetry)|landay]].
sentence_601: A popular theme in Afghan folklore and mythology are [[Dev_(mythology)|devs]], monstrous creatures.
sentence_602: Thursdays are traditionally "poetry night" in the city of [[Herat|Herat]] when men, women and children gather and recite both ancient and modern poems.
sentence_603: The Afghan region has produced countless Persian-speaking poets and writers from the Middle Ages to the present day, among which three mystical authors are considered true national glories (although claimed with equal ardor by Iran), namely: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari of Herat, a great mystic and [[Sufi|Sufi]] saint in the 11th century, [[Sanai|Sanai]] of Ghazni, author of mystical poems in the 12th century, and, finally, [[Rumi|Rumi]] of Balkh, in the 13th century, considered the persophonist throughout the world as the greatest mystical poet of the entire Muslim world.
sentence_604: The Afghan Pashto literature, although quantitatively remarkable and in great growth in the last century, has always had an essentially local meaning and importance, feeling the influence of both Persian literature and the contiguous literatures of India.
sentence_605: Both main literatures, from the second half of the nineteenth century, have shown themselves to be sensitive to genres (novel, theater), movements and stylistic features imported from Europe.
sentence_606: [[Khushal_Khan_Khattak|Khushal Khan Khattak]] of the 17th century is considered the national poet.
sentence_607: Other notable poets include Rabi'a Balkhi, [[Jami|Jami]], Rahman Baba, [[Khalilullah_Khalili|Khalilullah Khalili]], and [[Parween_Pazhwak|Parween Pazhwak]].
sentence_608: Afghanistan's official New Year starts with [[Nowruz|Nowruz]], an ancient tradition that started as a [[Zoroastrian|Zoroastrian]] celebration in present-day Iran, and with which it shares the annual celebration along with several other countries.
sentence_609: It occurs every year at the [[Equinox|vernal equinox]].
sentence_610: [[Nauruz_in_Afghanistan|In Afghanistan]], Nowruz is typically celebrated with music and dance, as well as holding buzkashi tournaments.
sentence_611: [[Yaldā_Night|Yaldā]], another nationally celebrated ancient tradition, commemorates the ancient goddess [[Mithra|Mithra]] and marks the longest night of the year on the eve of the [[Winter_solstice|winter solstice]] (čelle ye zemestān; usually falling on 20 or 21 December), during which families gather together to recite poetry and eat fruits—particularly the red fruits watermelon and [[Pomegranate|pomegranate]], as well as [[Mixed_nuts|mixed nuts]].
sentence_612: Religious festivals are also celebrated; as a predominantly Muslim country, Islamic events and festivals such as [[Ramadan|Ramadan]], [[Eid_al-Fitr|Eid al-Fitr]] and [[Ashura|Ashura]] are widely celebrated annually in Afghanistan.
sentence_613: The Sikh festival of [[Vaisakhi|Vaisakhi]] is celebrated by the Sikh community and the Hindu festival [[Diwali|Diwali]] by the Hindu community.
sentence_614: [[Afghan_Independence_Day|National Independence Day]] is celebrated on 19 August to mark the [[Anglo-Afghan_Treaty_of_1919|Anglo-Afghan Treaty of 1919]] under King [[Amanullah_Khan|Amanullah Khan]] and the country's full independence.
sentence_615: Several international celebrations are also officially held in Afghanistan, such as [[International_Workers'_Day|International Workers' Day]] and [[International_Women's_Day|International Women's Day]].
sentence_616: Some regional festivals include the Pamir Festival, which celebrates the culture of the [[Wakhi_people|Wakhi]] and [[Kyrgyz_people|Kyrgyz]] peoples, the Red Flower Festival (during Nowruz) in [[Mazar-i-Sharif|Mazar-i-Sharif]] and the Damboora Festival in [[Bamyan_Province|Bamyan Province]].
sentence_618: Sport in Afghanistan is managed by the [[Afghan_Sports_Federation|Afghan Sports Federation]].
sentence_619: [[Cricket|Cricket]] and association football are the two most popular sports in the country.
sentence_620: The Afghan Sports Federation promotes cricket, association football, basketball, volleyball, [[Golf|golf]], [[Team_handball|handball]], [[Boxing|boxing]], [[Taekwondo|taekwondo]], [[Olympic_weightlifting|weightlifting]], bodybuilding, [[Track_and_field|track and field]], skating, bowling, [[Snooker|snooker]], [[Chess|chess]], and other sports.
sentence_621: Afghanistan's sports teams are increasingly celebrating titles at international events.
sentence_622: Its [[Afghanistan_national_basketball_team|basketball team]] won the first team sports title at the [[2010_South_Asian_Games|2010 South Asian Games]].
sentence_623: Later that year, the country's [[Afghanistan_national_cricket_team|cricket team]] followed as it won the [[2009–10_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup|2009–10 ICC Intercontinental Cup]].
sentence_624: In 2012, the country's [[Afghanistan_national_3x3_team|3x3 basketball team]] won the gold medal at the [[3-on-3_basketball_at_the_2012_Asian_Beach_Games|2012 Asian Beach Games]].
sentence_625: In 2013, Afghanistan's [[Afghanistan_national_football_team|football team]] followed as it won the [[SAFF_Championship|SAFF Championship]].
sentence_626: The [[Afghanistan_national_cricket_team|Afghan national cricket team]], which was formed in 2001, participated in the [[2009_ICC_World_Cup_Qualifier|2009 ICC World Cup Qualifier]], [[2010_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_One|2010 ICC World Cricket League Division One]] and the [[2010_ICC_World_Twenty20|2010 ICC World Twenty20]].
sentence_627: It won the [[ACC_Twenty20_Cup|ACC Twenty20 Cup]] in 2007, 2009, 2011 and 2013.
sentence_628: The team eventually made it and played in the [[2015_Cricket_World_Cup|2015 Cricket World Cup]].
sentence_629: The [[Afghanistan_Cricket_Board|Afghanistan Cricket Board]] (ACB) is the official governing body of the sport and is headquartered in Kabul.
sentence_630: The [[Alokozay_Kabul_International_Cricket_Ground|Alokozay Kabul International Cricket Ground]] serves as the nation's main cricket stadium.
sentence_631: There are several other stadiums throughout the country, including the [[Ghazi_Amanullah_Khan_International_Cricket_Stadium|Ghazi Amanullah Khan International Cricket Stadium]] near [[Jalalabad|Jalalabad]].
sentence_632: Domestically, cricket is played between teams from different provinces.
sentence_633: The [[Afghanistan_national_football_team|Afghanistan national football team]] has been competing in international [[Association_football|football]] since 1941.
sentence_634: The national team plays its home games at the [[Ghazi_Stadium|Ghazi Stadium]] in Kabul, while [[Football_in_Afghanistan|football in Afghanistan]] is governed by the [[Afghanistan_Football_Federation|Afghanistan Football Federation]].
sentence_635: The national team has never competed or qualified for the [[FIFA_World_Cup|FIFA World Cup]] but has recently won an international football trophy in 2013.
sentence_636: The country also has a national team in the sport of futsal, a 5-a-side variation of football.
sentence_637: The traditional and the national sport of Afghanistan is buzkashi, mainly popular in the north, but also having a following in other parts of the country.
sentence_638: It is similar to [[Polo|polo]], played by horsemen in two teams, each trying to grab and hold a goat carcass.
sentence_639: The [[Afghan_Hound|Afghan Hound]] (a type of running dog) originated in Afghanistan and was formerly used in [[Wolf_hunting_with_dogs|wolf hunting]].
sentence_640: In 2002, traveler [[Rory_Stewart|Rory Stewart]] reported that dogs were still used for wolf hunting in remote areas.

title: Art Deco
sentence_0: Art Deco, sometimes referred to as Deco, is a style of visual arts, architecture and design that first appeared in France just before [[World_War_I|World War I]].
sentence_1: Art Deco influenced the design of buildings, furniture, jewelry, fashion, cars, movie theatres, trains, [[Ocean_liner|ocean liners]], and everyday objects such as radios and vacuum cleaners.
sentence_2: It took its name, short for Arts Décoratifs, from the [[International_Exhibition_of_Modern_Decorative_and_Industrial_Arts|Exposition internationale des arts décoratifs et industriels modernes]] (International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts) held in Paris in 1925.
sentence_3: It combined modern styles with fine craftsmanship and rich materials.
sentence_4: During its heyday, Art Deco represented luxury, glamour, exuberance, and faith in social and technological progress.
sentence_5: From its outset, Art Deco was influenced by the bold geometric forms of [[Cubism|Cubism]] and the [[Vienna_Secession|Vienna Secession]]; the bright colors of [[Fauvism|Fauvism]] and of the [[Ballets_Russes|Ballets Russes]]; the updated craftsmanship of the furniture of the eras of [[Louis_Philippe_I|Louis Philippe I]] and [[Louis_XVI|Louis XVI]]; and the exotic styles of [[Chinese_art|China]] and [[Japanese_art|Japan]], [[Indian_art|India]], [[Persian_art|Persia]], [[Art_of_ancient_Egypt|ancient Egypt]] and [[Ancient_Maya_art|Maya art]].
sentence_6: It featured rare and expensive materials, such as ebony and ivory, and exquisite craftsmanship.
sentence_7: The [[Chrysler_Building|Chrysler Building]] and [[Art_Deco_architecture_of_New_York_City|other skyscrapers of New York City built during the 1920s and 1930s]] are monuments of the Art Deco style.
sentence_8: In the 1930s, during the [[Great_Depression|Great Depression]], Art Deco became more subdued.
sentence_9: New materials arrived, including [[Chrome_plating|chrome plating]], stainless steel, and [[Plastic|plastic]].
sentence_10: A sleeker form of the style, called [[Streamline_Moderne|Streamline Moderne]], appeared in the 1930s; it featured curving forms and smooth, polished surfaces.
sentence_11: Art Deco is one of the first truly international styles, but its dominance ended with the beginning of [[World_War_II|World War II]] and the rise of the strictly functional and unadorned styles of [[Modern_architecture|modern architecture]] and the [[International_Style_(architecture)|International Style]] of architecture that followed.
sentence_12: Art Deco took its name, short for arts décoratifs, from the [[Exposition_Internationale_des_Arts_Décoratifs_et_Industriels_Modernes|Exposition Internationale des Arts Décoratifs et Industriels Modernes]] held in Paris in 1925, though the diverse styles that characterize Art Deco had already appeared in [[Paris|Paris]] and [[Brussels|Brussels]] before [[World_War_I|World War I]].
sentence_13: The term arts décoratifs was first used in France in 1858; published in the Bulletin de la Société française de photographie.
sentence_14: In 1868, [[Le_Figaro|Le Figaro]] newspaper used the term objets d'art décoratifs with respect to objects for stage scenery created for the [[Salle_Le_Peletier|Théâtre de l'Opéra]].
sentence_15: In 1875, furniture designers, textile, jewelry and glass designers, and other craftsmen were officially given the status of artists by the French government.
sentence_16: In response to this, the École royale gratuite de dessin (Royal Free School of Design), founded in 1766 under King [[Louis_XVI_of_France|Louis XVI]] to train artists and artisans in crafts relating to the fine arts, was renamed the École nationale des arts décoratifs (National School of Decorative Arts).
sentence_17: It took its present name of ENSAD (École nationale supérieure des arts décoratifs) in 1927.
sentence_18: During the 1925 Exposition, architect Le Corbusier wrote a series of articles about the exhibition for his magazine L'Esprit Nouveau, under the title "1925 EXPO.
sentence_19: ARTS.
sentence_20: DÉCO.
sentence_21: ", which were combined into a book, L'art décoratif d'aujourd'hui (Decorative Art Today).
sentence_22: The book was a spirited attack on the excesses of the colourful and lavish objects at the Exposition; and on the idea that practical objects such as furniture should not have any decoration at all; his conclusion was that "Modern decoration has no decoration".
sentence_23: The actual phrase art déco did not appear in print until 1966, when it featured in the title of the first modern exhibition on the subject, held by the Museum of Decorative Arts in Paris, Les Années 25 : Art déco, Bauhaus, Stijl, Esprit nouveau, which covered the variety of major styles in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentence_24: The term art déco was then used in a 1966 newspaper article by Hillary Gelson in [[The_Times|The Times]] (London, 12 November), describing the different styles at the exhibit.
sentence_25: Art Deco gained currency as a broadly applied stylistic label in 1968 when historian [[Bevis_Hillier|Bevis Hillier]] published the first major academic book on the style: [[Art_Deco_of_the_20s_and_30s|Art Deco of the 20s and 30s]].
sentence_26: Hillier noted that the term was already being used by art dealers and cites The Times (2 November 1966) and an essay named Les Arts Déco in [[Elle_(magazine)|Elle]] magazine (November 1967) as examples of prior usage.
sentence_27: In 1971, Hillier organized an exhibition at the [[Minneapolis_Institute_of_Arts|Minneapolis Institute of Arts]], which he details in his book about it, The World of Art Deco.
sentence_28: The emergence of Art Deco was closely connected with the rise in status of decorative artists, who until late in the 19th century had been considered simply as artisans.
sentence_29: The term arts décoratifs had been invented in 1875, giving the designers of furniture, textiles, and other decoration official status.
sentence_30: The Société des artistes décorateurs (Society of Decorative Artists), or SAD, was founded in 1901, and decorative artists were given the same rights of authorship as painters and sculptors.
sentence_31: A similar movement developed in Italy.
sentence_32: The first international exhibition devoted entirely to the decorative arts, the [[Prima_Esposizione_Internazionale_d'Arte_Decorativa_Moderna|Esposizione Internazionale d'Arte Decorativa Moderna]], was held in [[Turin|Turin]] in 1902.
sentence_33: Several new magazines devoted to decorative arts were founded in Paris, including Arts et décoration and L'Art décoratif moderne.
sentence_34: Decorative arts sections were introduced into the annual salons of the Sociéte des artistes français, and later in the [[Salon_d'Automne|Salon d'Automne]].
sentence_35: French nationalism also played a part in the resurgence of decorative arts; French designers felt challenged by the increasing exports of less expensive German furnishings.
sentence_36: In 1911, the SAD proposed the holding of a major new international exposition of decorative arts in 1912.
sentence_37: No copies of old styles were to be permitted; only modern works.
sentence_38: The exhibit was postponed until 1914, then, because of the war, postponed until 1925, when it gave its name to the whole family of styles known as "Déco".
sentence_39: Parisian department stores and fashion designers also played an important part in the rise of Art Deco.
sentence_40: Established enterprises such as silverware firm [[Christofle|Christofle]], glass designer [[René_Lalique|René Lalique]], and the jewelers [[Louis_Cartier|Louis Cartier]] and [[Boucheron|Boucheron]], who all began designing products in more modern styles.
sentence_41: Beginning in 1900, department stores had recruited decorative artists to work in their design studios.
sentence_42: The decoration of the 1912 Salon d'Automne had been entrusted to the department store [[Printemps|Printemps]].
sentence_43: During the same year Printemps created its own workshop called Primavera.
sentence_44: By 1920 Primavera employed more than three hundred artists.
sentence_45: The styles ranged from the updated versions of Louis XIV, Louis XVI, and especially Louis Philippe furniture made by [[Louis_Süe|Louis Süe]] and the Primavera workshop, to more modern forms from the workshop of the Au Louvre department store.
sentence_46: Other designers, including [[Émile-Jacques_Ruhlmann|Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann]] and Paul Foliot refused to use mass production, and insisted that each piece be made individually by hand.
sentence_47: The early Art Deco style featured luxurious and exotic materials such as ebony, [[Ivory|ivory]] and [[Silk|silk]], very bright colors and stylized [[Motif_(visual_arts)|motifs]], particularly baskets and bouquets of flowers of all colors, giving a modernist look.
sentence_48: The architects of the [[Vienna_Secession|Vienna Secession]] (formed 1897), especially [[Josef_Hoffmann|Josef Hoffmann]], had a notable influence on Art Deco.
sentence_49: His [[Stoclet_Palace|Stoclet Palace]] in Brussels (1905–1911), was a prototype of the Art Deco style, featuring geometric volumes, symmetry, straight lines, concrete covered with marble plaques, finely-sculpted ornament, and lavish interiors, including mosaic friezes by [[Gustav_Klimt|Gustav Klimt]].
sentence_50: Hoffmann was also a founder of the Wiener Werkstätte (1903–1932), an association of craftsmen and interior designers working in the new style.
sentence_51: This became the model for the Compagnie des arts français, created in 1919, which brought together [[André_Mare|André Mare]], and [[Louis_Süe|Louis Süe]], the first leading French Art Deco designers and decorators.
sentence_52: New materials and technologies, especially [[Reinforced_concrete|reinforced concrete]], were key to the development and appearance of Art Deco.
sentence_53: The first concrete house was built in 1853 Paris suburbs by [[François_Coignet|François Coignet]].
sentence_54: In 1877 [[Joseph_Monier|Joseph Monier]] introduced the idea of strengthening the concrete with a mesh of iron rods in a grill pattern.
sentence_55: In 1893 [[Auguste_Perret|Auguste Perret]] built the first concrete garage in Paris, then an apartment building, house, then, in 1913, the [[Théâtre_des_Champs-Élysées|Théâtre des Champs-Élysées]].
sentence_56: The theatre was denounced by one critic as the "Zeppelin of Avenue Montaigne", an alleged Germanic influence, copied from the [[Vienna_Secession|Vienna Secession]].
sentence_57: Thereafter, the majority of Art Deco buildings were made of reinforced concrete, which gave greater freedom of form and less need for reinforcing pillars and columns.
sentence_58: Perret was also a pioneer in covering the concrete with ceramic tiles, both for protection and decoration.
sentence_59: The architect Le Corbusier first learned the uses of reinforced concrete working as a draftsman in Perret's studio.
sentence_60: Other new technologies that were important to Art Deco were new methods in producing plate glass, which was less expensive and allowed much larger and stronger windows, and for mass-producing [[Aluminum|aluminum]], which was used for building and window frames and later, by Corbusier and others, for lightweight furniture.
sentence_61: The [[Théâtre_des_Champs-Élysées|Théâtre des Champs-Élysées]] (1910–1913), by [[Auguste_Perret|Auguste Perret]], was the first landmark Art Deco building completed in Paris.
sentence_62: Previously, [[Reinforced_concrete|reinforced concrete]] had been used only for industrial and apartment buildings, Perret had built the first modern reinforced-concrete apartment building in Paris on rue Benjamin Franklin in 1903–04.
sentence_63: [[Henri_Sauvage|Henri Sauvage]], another important future Art Deco architect, built another in 1904 at 7, rue Trétaigne (1904).
sentence_64: From 1908 to 1910, the 21-year-old Le Corbusier worked as a draftsman in Perret's office, learning the techniques of concrete construction.
sentence_65: Perret's building had clean rectangular form, geometric decoration and straight lines, the future trademarks of Art Deco.
sentence_66: The decor of the theater was also revolutionary; the facade was decorated with [[High-relief|high reliefs]] by [[Antoine_Bourdelle|Antoine Bourdelle]], a dome by [[Maurice_Denis|Maurice Denis]], paintings by [[Édouard_Vuillard|Édouard Vuillard]], and an Art Deco curtain by [[Ker-Xavier_Roussel|Ker-Xavier Roussel]].
sentence_67: The theater became famous as the venue for many of the first performances of the [[Ballets_Russes|Ballets Russes]].
sentence_68: Perret and Sauvage became the leading Art Deco architects in Paris in the 1920s.
sentence_69: At its birth between 1910 and 1914, Art Deco was an explosion of colors, featuring bright and often clashing hues, frequently in floral designs, presented in furniture upholstery, carpets, screens, wallpaper and fabrics.
sentence_70: Many colorful works, including chairs and a table by [[Maurice_Dufrêne|Maurice Dufrêne]] and a bright Gobelin carpet by [[Paul_Follot|Paul Follot]] were presented at the 1912 [[Société_des_artistes_décorateurs|Salon des artistes décorateurs]].
sentence_71: In 1912–1913 designer [[Adrien_Karbowsky|Adrien Karbowsky]] made a floral chair with a parrot design for the hunting lodge of art collector [[Jacques_Doucet_(fashion_designer)|Jacques Doucet]].
sentence_72: The furniture designers Louis Süe and [[André_Mare|André Mare]] made their first appearance at the 1912 exhibit, under the name of the Atelier français, combining colorful fabrics with exotic and expensive materials, including ebony and ivory.
sentence_73: After World War I, they became one of the most prominent French interior design firms, producing the furniture for the first-class salons and cabins of the French transatlantic [[Ocean_liner|ocean liners]].
sentence_74: The vivid colors of Art Deco came from many sources, including the exotic set designs by [[Léon_Bakst|Léon Bakst]] for the [[Ballets_Russes|Ballets Russes]], which caused a sensation in Paris just before World War I.
sentence_75: Some of the colors were inspired by the earlier [[Fauvism|Fauvism]] movement led by [[Henri_Matisse|Henri Matisse]]; others by the [[Orphism_(art)|Orphism]] of painters such as [[Sonia_Delaunay|Sonia Delaunay]]; others by the movement known as the Nabis, and in the work of symbolist painter Odilon Redon, who designed fireplace screens and other decorative objects.
sentence_76: Bright colors were a feature of the work of fashion designer [[Paul_Poiret|Paul Poiret]], whose work influenced both Art Deco fashion and interior design.
sentence_77: The [[Art_movement|art movement]] known as [[Cubism|Cubism]] appeared in France between 1907 and 1912, influencing the development of Art Deco.
sentence_78: In Art Deco Complete: The Definitive Guide to the Decorative Arts of the 1920s and 1930s Alastair Duncan writes "Cubism, in some bastardized form or other, became the lingua franca of the era's decorative artists."
sentence_79: The Cubists, themselves under the influence of [[Paul_Cézanne|Paul Cézanne]], were interested in the simplification of forms to their geometric essentials: the cylinder, the sphere, the cone.
sentence_80: In 1912, the artists of the [[Section_d'Or|Section d'Or]] exhibited works considerably more accessible to the general public than the analytical Cubism of Picasso and Braque.
sentence_81: The Cubist vocabulary was poised to attract fashion, furniture and interior designers.
sentence_82: The 1912 writings of [[André_Vera|André Vera]], Le Nouveau style, published in the journal L'Art décoratif, expressed the rejection of [[Art_Nouveau|Art Nouveau]] forms (asymmetric, polychrome and picturesque) and called for simplicité volontaire, symétrie manifeste, l'ordre et l'harmonie, themes that would eventually become common within Art Deco; though the Deco style was often extremely colorful and often complex.
sentence_83: In the Art Décoratif section of the 1912 Salon d'Automne, an architectural installation was exhibited known as the [[La_Maison_Cubiste|La Maison Cubiste]].
sentence_84: The facade was designed by [[Raymond_Duchamp-Villon|Raymond Duchamp-Villon]].
sentence_85: The decor of the house was by [[André_Mare|André Mare]].
sentence_86: La Maison Cubiste was a furnished installation with a facade, a staircase, wrought iron banisters, a bedroom, a living room—the Salon Bourgeois, where paintings by [[Albert_Gleizes|Albert Gleizes]], [[Jean_Metzinger|Jean Metzinger]], [[Marie_Laurencin|Marie Laurencin]], [[Marcel_Duchamp|Marcel Duchamp]], [[Fernand_Léger|Fernand Léger]] and [[Roger_de_La_Fresnaye|Roger de La Fresnaye]] were hung.
sentence_87: Thousands of spectators at the salon passed through the full-scale model.
sentence_88: The facade of the house, designed by Duchamp-Villon, was not very radical by modern standards; the lintels and pediments had prismatic shapes, but otherwise the facade resembled an ordinary house of the period.
sentence_89: For the two rooms, Mare designed the wallpaper, which featured stylized roses and floral patterns, along with upholstery, furniture and carpets, all with flamboyant and colorful motifs.
sentence_90: It was a distinct break from traditional decor.
sentence_91: The critic Emile Sedeyn described Mare's work in the magazine Art et Décoration: "He does not embarrass himself with simplicity, for he multiplies flowers wherever they can be put.
sentence_92: The effect he seeks is obviously one of picturesqueness and gaiety.
sentence_93: He achieves it."
sentence_94: The Cubist element was provided by the paintings.
sentence_95: The installation was attacked by some critics as extremely radical, which helped make for its success.
sentence_96: This architectural installation was subsequently exhibited at the 1913 [[Armory_Show|Armory Show]], New York City, Chicago and Boston.
sentence_97: Thanks largely to the exhibition, the term "Cubist" began to be applied to anything modern, from women's haircuts to clothing to theater [[Performance|performances]].
sentence_98: The Cubist influence continued within Art Deco, even as Deco branched out in many other directions.
sentence_99: In 1927, Cubists [[Joseph_Csaky|Joseph Csaky]], [[Jacques_Lipchitz|Jacques Lipchitz]], [[Louis_Marcoussis|Louis Marcoussis]], [[Henri_Laurens|Henri Laurens]], the sculptor [[Gustave_Miklos|Gustave Miklos]], and others collaborated in the decoration of a Studio House, rue Saint-James, [[Neuilly-sur-Seine|Neuilly-sur-Seine]], designed by the architect Paul Ruaud and owned by the French fashion designer Jacques Doucet, also a collector of [[Post-Impressionist|Post-Impressionist]] art by Henri Matisse and Cubist paintings (including [[Les_Demoiselles_d'Avignon|Les Demoiselles d'Avignon]], which he bought directly from Picasso's studio).
sentence_100: Laurens designed the fountain, Csaky designed Doucet's staircase, Lipchitz made the fireplace mantel, and Marcoussis made a Cubist rug.
sentence_101: Besides the Cubist artists, Doucet brought in other Deco interior designers to help in decorating the house, including Pierre Legrain, who was in charge of organizing the decoration, and [[Paul_Iribe|Paul Iribe]], Marcel Coard, [[André_Groult|André Groult]], [[Eileen_Gray|Eileen Gray]] and Rose Adler to provide furniture.
sentence_102: The decor included massive pieces made of macassar ebony, inspired by African art, and furniture covered with Morocco leather, crocodile skin and snakeskin, and patterns taken from African designs.
sentence_103: Art Deco was not a single style, but a collection of different and sometimes contradictory styles.
sentence_104: In architecture, Art Deco was the successor to and reaction against Art Nouveau, a style which flourished in Europe between 1895 and 1900, and also gradually replaced the [[Beaux-Arts_architecture|Beaux-Arts]] and neoclassical that were predominant in European and American architecture.
sentence_105: In 1905 Eugène Grasset wrote and published Méthode de Composition Ornementale, Éléments Rectilignes, in which he systematically explored the decorative (ornamental) aspects of geometric elements, forms, motifs and their variations, in contrast with (and as a departure from) the undulating Art Nouveau style of [[Hector_Guimard|Hector Guimard]], so popular in Paris a few years earlier.
sentence_106: Grasset stressed the principle that various simple geometric shapes like triangles and squares are the basis of all compositional arrangements.
sentence_107: The reinforced-concrete buildings of Auguste Perret and Henri Sauvage, and particularly the [[Théâtre_des_Champs-Élysées|Théâtre des Champs-Élysées]], offered a new form of construction and decoration which was copied worldwide.
sentence_108: In decoration, many different styles were borrowed and used by Art Deco.
sentence_109: They included pre-modern art from around the world and observable at the [[Musée_du_Louvre|Musée du Louvre]], [[Musée_de_l'Homme|Musée de l'Homme]] and the [[Musée_national_des_Arts_d'Afrique_et_d'Océanie|Musée national des Arts d'Afrique et d'Océanie]].
sentence_110: There was also popular interest in archeology due to excavations at [[Pompeii|Pompeii]], [[Troy|Troy]], and the tomb of the 18th dynasty Pharaoh [[Tutankhamun|Tutankhamun]].
sentence_111: Artists and designers integrated motifs from [[Ancient_Egypt|ancient Egypt]], Mesopotamia, [[Ancient_Greece|Greece]], [[Ancient_Rome|Rome]], Asia, [[Mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]] and [[Oceania|Oceania]] with [[Machine_Age|Machine Age]] elements.
sentence_112: Other styles borrowed included Russian [[Constructivism_(art)|Constructivism]] and Italian [[Futurism|Futurism]], as well as Orphism, [[Functionalism_(architecture)|Functionalism]], and [[Modernism|Modernism]] in general.
sentence_113: Art Deco also used the clashing colors and designs of Fauvism, notably in the work of Henri Matisse and [[André_Derain|André Derain]], inspired the designs of art deco textiles, wallpaper, and painted ceramics.
sentence_114: It took ideas from the high fashion vocabulary of the period, which featured geometric designs, chevrons, zigzags, and stylized bouquets of flowers.
sentence_115: It was influenced by discoveries in [[Egyptology|Egyptology]], and growing interest in the Orient and in African art.
sentence_116: From 1925 onwards, it was often inspired by a passion for new machines, such as airships, automobiles and ocean liners, and by 1930 this influence resulted in the style called [[Streamline_Moderne|Streamline Moderne]].
sentence_117: Art Deco was associated with both luxury and modernity; it combined very expensive materials and exquisite craftsmanship put into modernistic forms.
sentence_118: Nothing was cheap about Art Deco: pieces of furniture included ivory and silver inlays, and pieces of Art Deco jewelry combined diamonds with platinum, jade, and other precious materials.
sentence_119: The style was used to decorate the first-class salons of ocean liners, deluxe trains, and skyscrapers.
sentence_120: It was used around the world to decorate the great movie palaces of the late 1920s and 1930s.
sentence_121: Later, after the [[Great_Depression|Great Depression]], the style changed and became more sober.
sentence_122: A good example of the luxury style of Art Deco is the boudoir of the fashion designer [[Jeanne_Lanvin|Jeanne Lanvin]], designed by [[Armand-Albert_Rateau|Armand-Albert Rateau]] (1882–1938) made between 1922–25.
sentence_123: It was located in her house at 16 rue Barbet de Jouy, in Paris, which was demolished in 1965.
sentence_124: The room was reconstructed in the Museum of Decorative Arts in Paris.
sentence_125: The walls are covered with molded lambris below sculpted bas-reliefs in stucco.
sentence_126: The alcove is framed with columns of marble on with bases and a plinth of sculpted wood.
sentence_127: The floor is of white and black marble, and in the cabinets decorative objects are displayed against a background of blue silk.
sentence_128: Her bathroom had a tub and washstand made of sienna marble, with a wall of carved stucco and bronze fittings.
sentence_129: By 1928 the style had become more comfortable, with deep leather club chairs.
sentence_130: The study designed by the Paris firm of Alavoine for an American businessman in 1928–30, now in the [[Brooklyn_Museum|Brooklyn Museum]].
sentence_131: By the 1930s, the style had been somewhat simplified, but it was still extravagant.
sentence_132: In 1932 the decorator Paul Ruoud made the Glass Salon for Suzanne Talbot.
sentence_133: It featured a serpentine armchair and two tubular armchairs by Eileen Gray, a floor of mat silvered glass slabs, a panel of abstract patterns in silver and black lacquer, and an assortment of animal skins.

section_10.value: International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts (1925)

sentence_134: Main article: [[International_Exhibition_of_Modern_Decorative_and_Industrial_Arts|International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts]]
sentence_135: The event that marked the zenith of the style and gave it its name was the [[International_Exhibition_of_Modern_Decorative_and_Industrial_Arts|International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts]] which took place in Paris from April to October in 1925.
sentence_136: This was officially sponsored by the French government, and covered a site in Paris of 55 acres, running from the [[Grand_Palais|Grand Palais]] on the right bank to [[Les_Invalides|Les Invalides]] on the left bank, and along the banks of the Seine.
sentence_137: The Grand Palais, the largest hall in the city, was filled with exhibits of decorative arts from the participating countries.
sentence_138: There were 15,000 exhibitors from twenty different countries, including England, Italy, Spain, Poland, Czechoslovakia, Belgium, Japan, and the new [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]], though Germany was not invited because of tensions after the war and the United States, misunderstanding the purpose of the exhibit, declined to participate.
sentence_139: It was visited by sixteen million people during its seven-month run.
sentence_140: The rules of the exhibition required that all work be modern; no historical styles were allowed.
sentence_141: The main purpose of the Exhibit was to promote the French manufacturers of luxury furniture, porcelain, glass, metal work, textiles and other decorative products.
sentence_142: To further promote the products, all the major Paris department stores and major designers had their own pavilions.
sentence_143: The Exposition had a secondary purpose in promoting products from French colonies in Africa and Asia, including ivory and exotic woods.
sentence_144: The Hôtel du Collectionneur was a popular attraction at the Exposition; it displayed the new furniture designs of Emile-Jacques Ruhlmann, as well as Art Deco fabrics, carpets, and a painting by [[Jean_Dupas|Jean Dupas]].
sentence_145: The interior design followed the same principles of symmetry and geometric forms which set it apart from Art Nouveau, and bright colors, fine craftsmanship rare and expensive materials which set it apart from the strict functionality of the Modernist style.
sentence_146: While most of the pavilions were lavishly decorated and filled with hand-made luxury furniture, two pavilions, those of the Soviet Union and Pavilion du Nouveau Esprit, built by the magazine of that name run by Le Corbusier, were built in an austere style with plain white walls and no decoration; they were among the earliest examples of [[Modernist_architecture|modernist architecture]].
sentence_147: American skyscrapers marked the summit of the Art Deco style; they became the tallest and most recognizable modern buildings in the world.
sentence_148: They were designed to show the prestige of their builders through their height, their shape, their color, and their dramatic illumination at night.
sentence_149: The [[American_Radiator_Building|American Radiator Building]] by [[Raymond_Hood|Raymond Hood]] (1924) combined Gothic and Deco modern elements in the design of the building.
sentence_150: Black brick on the frontage of the building (symbolizing coal) was selected to give an idea of solidity and to give the building a solid mass.
sentence_151: Other parts of the facade were covered in gold bricks (symbolizing fire), and the entry was decorated with marble and black mirrors.
sentence_152: Another early Art Deco skyscraper was Detroit's [[Guardian_Building|Guardian Building]], which opened in 1929.
sentence_153: Designed by modernist [[Wirt_C._Rowland|Wirt C. Rowland]], the building was the first to employ stainless steel as a decorative element, and the extensive use of colored designs in place of traditional ornaments.
sentence_154: New York City's skyline was radically changed by the [[Chrysler_Building|Chrysler Building]] in Manhattan (completed in 1930), designed by [[William_Van_Alen|William Van Alen]].
sentence_155: It was a giant seventy-seven-floor tall advertisement for Chrysler automobiles.
sentence_156: The top was crowned by a stainless steel spire, and was ornamented by deco "gargoyles" in the form of stainless steel radiator cap decorations.
sentence_157: The base of the tower, thirty-three stories above the street, was decorated with colorful art deco friezes, and the lobby was decorated with art deco symbols and images expressing modernity.
sentence_158: The Chrysler Building was followed by the [[Empire_State_Building|Empire State Building]] by [[William_F._Lamb|William F. Lamb]] (1931) and the [[RCA_Building|RCA Building]] (now 30 Rockefeller Plaza) by Raymond Hood (1933) which together completely changed New York City's skyline.
sentence_159: The tops of the buildings were decorated with Art Deco crowns and spires covered with stainless steel, and, in the case of the Chrysler building, with Art Deco gargoyles modeled after radiator ornaments, while the entrances and lobbies were lavishly decorated with Art Deco sculpture, ceramics, and design.
sentence_160: Similar buildings, though not quite as tall, soon appeared in Chicago and other large American cities.
sentence_161: The Chrysler Building was soon surpassed in height by the Empire State Building, in a slightly less lavish Deco style.
sentence_162: Rockefeller Center added a new design element: several tall building grouped around an open plaza, with a fountain in the center.
sentence_163: In 1925, two different competing schools coexisted within Art Deco: the traditionalists, who had founded the Society of Decorative Artists; included the furniture designer Emile-Jacques Ruhlmann, Jean Dunard, the sculptor Antoine Bourdelle, and designer Paul Poiret; they combined modern forms with traditional craftsmanship and expensive materials.
sentence_164: On the other side were the modernists, who increasingly rejected the past and wanted a style based upon advances in new technologies, simplicity, a lack of decoration, inexpensive materials, and mass production.
sentence_165: The modernists founded their own organization, [[The_French_Union_of_Modern_Artists|The French Union of Modern Artists]], in 1929.
sentence_166: Its members included architects [[Pierre_Chareau|Pierre Chareau]], [[Francis_Jourdain|Francis Jourdain]], [[Robert_Mallet-Stevens|Robert Mallet-Stevens]], Corbusier, and, in the Soviet Union, [[Konstantin_Melnikov|Konstantin Melnikov]]; the Irish designer Eileen Gray, and French designer Sonia Delaunay, the jewelers [[Jean_Fouquet|Jean Fouquet]] and [[Jean_Puiforcat|Jean Puiforcat]].
sentence_167: They fiercely attacked the traditional art deco style, which they said was created only for the wealthy, and insisted that well-constructed buildings should be available to everyone, and that form should follow function.
sentence_168: The beauty of an object or building resided in whether it was perfectly fit to fulfill its function.
sentence_169: Modern industrial methods meant that furniture and buildings could be mass-produced, not made by hand.
sentence_170: The Art Deco interior designer Paul Follot defended Art Deco in this way: "We know that man is never content with the indispensable and that the superfluous is always needed...If not, we would have to get rid of music, flowers, and perfumes..!"
sentence_171: However, Le Corbusier was a brilliant publicist for modernist architecture; he stated that a house was simply "a machine to live in", and tirelessly promoted the idea that Art Deco was the past and modernism was the future.
sentence_172: Le Corbusier's ideas were gradually adopted by architecture schools, and the aesthetics of Art Deco were abandoned.
sentence_173: The same features that made Art Deco popular in the beginning, its craftsmanship, rich materials and ornament, led to its decline.
sentence_174: The Great Depression that began in the United States in 1929, and reached Europe shortly afterwards, greatly reduced the number of wealthy clients who could pay for the furnishings and art objects.
sentence_175: In the Depression economic climate, few companies were ready to build new skyscrapers.
sentence_176: Even the Ruhlmann firm resorted to producing pieces of furniture in series, rather than individual hand-made items.
sentence_177: The last buildings built in Paris in the new style were the Museum of Public Works by Auguste Perret (now the French Economic, Social and Environmental Council) and the Palais de Chaillot by [[Louis-Hippolyte_Boileau|Louis-Hippolyte Boileau]], Jacques Carlu and [[Léon_Azéma|Léon Azéma]], and the [[Palais_de_Tokyo|Palais de Tokyo]] of the [[Exposition_Internationale_des_Arts_et_Techniques_dans_la_Vie_Moderne|1937 Paris International Exposition]]; they looked out at the grandiose pavilion of Nazi Germany, designed by [[Albert_Speer|Albert Speer]], which faced the equally grandiose socialist-realist pavilion of Stalin's Soviet Union.
sentence_178: After World War II, the dominant architectural style became the International Style pioneered by Le Corbusier, and Mies Van der Rohe.
sentence_179: A handful of Art Deco hotels were built in [[Miami_Beach,_Florida|Miami Beach]] after World War II, but elsewhere the style largely vanished, except in industrial design, where it continued to be used in automobile styling and products such as jukeboxes.
sentence_180: In the 1960s, it experienced a modest academic revival, thanks in part to the writings of architectural historians such as Bevis Hillier.
sentence_181: In the 1970s efforts were made in the United States and Europe to preserve the best examples of Art Deco architecture, and many buildings were restored and repurposed.
sentence_182: [[Postmodern_architecture|Postmodern architecture]], which first appeared in the 1980s, like Art Deco, often includes purely decorative features.
sentence_183: Deco continues to inspire designers, and is often used in contemporary fashion, jewelry, and toiletries.
sentence_184: There was no section set aside for painting at the 1925 Exposition.
sentence_185: Art deco painting was by definition decorative, designed to decorate a room or work of architecture, so few painters worked exclusively in the style, but two painters are closely associated with Art Deco.
sentence_186: Jean Dupas painted Art Deco murals for the Bordeaux Pavilion at the 1925 Decorative Arts Exposition in Paris, and also painted the picture over the fireplace in the Maison de la Collectioneur exhibit at the 1925 Exposition, which featured furniture by Ruhlmann and other prominent Art Deco designers.
sentence_187: His murals were also prominent in the decor of the French ocean liner [[SS_Normandie|SS Normandie]].
sentence_188: His work was purely decorative, designed as a background or accompaniment to other elements of the decor.
sentence_189: The other painter closely associated with the style is [[Tamara_de_Lempicka|Tamara de Lempicka]].
sentence_190: Born in Poland, she emigrated to Paris after the [[Russian_Revolution|Russian Revolution]].
sentence_191: She studied under [[Maurice_Denis|Maurice Denis]] and [[André_Lhote|André Lhote]], and borrowed many elements from their styles.
sentence_192: She painted portraits in a realistic, dynamic and colorful Art Deco style.
sentence_193: In the 1930s a dramatic new form of Art Deco painting appeared in the United States.
sentence_194: During the Great Depression, the [[Federal_Art_Project|Federal Art Project]] of the [[Works_Progress_Administration|Works Progress Administration]] was created to give work to unemployed artists.
sentence_195: Many were given the task of decorating government buildings, hospitals and schools.
sentence_196: There was no specific art deco style used in the murals; artists engaged to paint murals in government buildings came from many different schools, from American regionalism to [[Social_realism|social realism]]; they included [[Reginald_Marsh_(artist)|Reginald Marsh]], [[Rockwell_Kent|Rockwell Kent]] and the Mexican painter [[Diego_Rivera|Diego Rivera]].
sentence_197: The murals were Art Deco because they were all decorative and related to the activities in the building or city where they were painted: Reginald Marsh and Rockwell Kent both decorated U.S. postal buildings, and showed postal employees at work while Diego Rivera depicted automobile factory workers for the [[Detroit_Institute_of_Arts|Detroit Institute of Arts]].
sentence_198: Diego Rivera's mural [[Man_at_the_Crossroads|Man at the Crossroads]] (1933) for Rockefeller Center featured an unauthorized portrait of [[Lenin|Lenin]].
sentence_199: When Rivera refused to remove Lenin, the painting was destroyed and a new mural was painted by the Spanish artist [[Josep_Maria_Sert|Josep Maria Sert]].
sentence_200: Sculpture was a very common and integral feature of Art Deco architecture.
sentence_201: In France, allegorical bas-reliefs representing dance and music by [[Antoine_Bourdelle|Antoine Bourdelle]] decorated the earliest Art Deco landmark in Paris, the [[Théâtre_des_Champs-Élysées|Théâtre des Champs-Élysées]], in 1912.
sentence_202: 1925 had major sculptural works placed around the site, pavilions were decorated with sculptural friezes, and several pavilions devoted to smaller studio sculpture.
sentence_203: In the 1930s, a large group of prominent sculptors made works for the 1937 [[Exposition_Internationale_des_Arts_et_Techniques_dans_la_Vie_Moderne|Exposition Internationale des Arts et Techniques dans la Vie Moderne]] at Chaillot.
sentence_204: [[Alfred_Janniot|Alfred Janniot]] made the relief sculptures on the façade of the Palais de Tokyo.
sentence_205: The [[Musée_d'Art_Moderne_de_la_Ville_de_Paris|Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris]], and the esplanade in front of the Palais de Chaillot, facing the Eiffel Tower, was crowded with new statuary by [[Charles_Malfray|Charles Malfray]], Henry Arnold, and many others.
sentence_206: Public art deco sculpture was almost always representational, usually of heroic or allegorical figures related to the purpose of the building or room.
sentence_207: The themes were usually selected by the patrons, not the artist.
sentence_208: Abstract sculpture for decoration was extremely rare.
sentence_209: In the United States, the most prominent Art Deco sculptor for public art was [[Paul_Manship|Paul Manship]], who updated classical and mythological subjects and themes in an Art Deco style.
sentence_210: His most famous work was the statue of [[Prometheus_(Manship)|Prometheus]] at [[Rockefeller_Center|Rockefeller Center]] in New York City, a 20th-century adaptation of a classical subject.
sentence_211: Other important works for Rockefeller Center were made by [[Lee_Lawrie|Lee Lawrie]], including the sculptural facade and the [[Atlas_(statue)|Atlas statue]].
sentence_212: During the [[Great_Depression|Great Depression]] in the United States, many sculptors were commissioned to make works for the decoration of federal government buildings, with funds provided by the WPA, or [[Works_Progress_Administration|Works Progress Administration]].
sentence_213: They included sculptor Sidney Biehler Waugh, who created stylized and idealized images of workers and their tasks for federal government office buildings.
sentence_214: In San Francisco, [[Ralph_Stackpole|Ralph Stackpole]] provided sculpture for the facade of the new [[San_Francisco_Stock_Exchange|San Francisco Stock Exchange]] building.
sentence_215: In Washington DC, [[Michael_Lantz|Michael Lantz]] made works for the [[Federal_Trade_Commission|Federal Trade Commission]] building.
sentence_216: In Britain, Deco public statuary was made by [[Eric_Gill|Eric Gill]] for the [[BBC_Broadcasting_House|BBC Broadcasting House]], while Ronald Atkinson decorated the lobby of the former [[Daily_Express_Building,_London|Daily Express Building]] in London (1932).
sentence_217: One of the best known and certainly the largest public Art Deco sculpture is the [[Christ_the_Redeemer_(statue)|Christ the Redeemer]] by the French sculptor [[Paul_Landowski|Paul Landowski]], completed between 1922 and 1931, located on a mountain top overlooking [[Rio_de_Janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil.
sentence_218: Many early Art Deco sculptures were small, designed to decorate salons.
sentence_219: One genre of this sculpture was called the [[Chryselephantine|Chryselephantine]] statuette, named for a style of ancient Greek temple statues made of gold and ivory.
sentence_220: They were sometimes made of bronze, or sometimes with much more lavish materials, such as ivory, [[Onyx|onyx]], alabaster, and gold leaf.
sentence_221: One of the best-known Art Deco salon sculptors was the Romanian-born [[Demétre_Chiparus|Demétre Chiparus]], who produced colorful small sculptures of dancers.
sentence_222: Other notable salon sculptors included [[Ferdinand_Preiss|Ferdinand Preiss]], [[Josef_Lorenzl|Josef Lorenzl]], Alexander Kelety, Dorothea Charol and Gustav Schmidtcassel.
sentence_223: Another important American sculptor in the studio format was [[Harriet_Whitney_Frishmuth|Harriet Whitney Frishmuth]], who had studied with [[Auguste_Rodin|Auguste Rodin]] in Paris.
sentence_224: Pierre Le Paguays was a prominent Art Deco studio sculptor, whose work was shown at the 1925 Exposition.
sentence_225: He worked with bronze, marble, ivory, onyx, gold, [[Alabaster|alabaster]] and other precious materials.
sentence_226: [[François_Pompon|François Pompon]] was a pioneer of modern stylized [[Animalier|animalier]] sculpture.
sentence_227: He was not fully recognized for his artistic accomplishments until the age of 67 at the Salon d'Automne of 1922 with the work Ours blanc, also known as The White Bear, now in the [[Musée_d'Orsay|Musée d'Orsay]] in Paris.
sentence_228: Parallel with these Art Deco sculptors, more avant-garde and abstract modernist sculptors were at work in Paris and New York City.
sentence_229: The most prominent were [[Constantin_Brâncuși|Constantin Brâncuși]], [[Joseph_Csaky|Joseph Csaky]], [[Alexander_Archipenko|Alexander Archipenko]], [[Henri_Laurens|Henri Laurens]], [[Jacques_Lipchitz|Jacques Lipchitz]], [[Gustave_Miklos|Gustave Miklos]], [[Jean_Lambert-Rucki|Jean Lambert-Rucki]], [[Jan_et_Joël_Martel|Jan et Joël Martel]], [[Chana_Orloff|Chana Orloff]] and Pablo Gargallo.
sentence_230: The Art Deco style appeared early in the graphic arts, in the years just before World War I.
sentence_231: It appeared in Paris in the posters and the costume designs of Léon Bakst for the Ballets Russes, and in the catalogs of the fashion designers Paul Poiret.
sentence_232: The illustrations of Georges Barbier, and Georges Lepape and the images in the fashion magazine La Gazette du bon ton perfectly captured the elegance and sensuality of the style.
sentence_233: In the 1920s, the look changed; the fashions stressed were more casual, sportive and daring, with the woman models usually smoking cigarettes.
sentence_234: American fashion magazines such as [[Vogue_(magazine)|Vogue]], [[Vanity_Fair_(magazine)|Vanity Fair]] and [[Harper's_Bazaar|Harper's Bazaar]] quickly picked up the new style and popularized it in the United States.
sentence_235: It also influenced the work of American book illustrators such as Rockwell Kent.
sentence_236: In Germany, the most famous poster artist of the period was [[Ludwig_Hohlwein|Ludwig Hohlwein]], who created colorful and dramatic posters for music festivals, beers, and, late in his career, for the Nazi Party.
