sentence_237: During the Art Nouveau period, posters usually advertised theatrical products or cabarets.
sentence_238: In the 1920s, travel posters, made for steamship lines and airlines, became extremely popular.
sentence_239: The style changed notably in the 1920s, to focus attention on the product being advertised.
sentence_240: The images became simpler, precise, more linear, more dynamic, and were often placed against a single color background.
sentence_241: In France popular Art Deco designers included, Charles Loupot and [[Paul_Colin_(artist)|Paul Colin]], who became famous for his posters of American singer and dancer [[Josephine_Baker|Josephine Baker]].
sentence_242: Jean Carlu designed posters for Charlie Chaplin movies, soaps, and theaters; in the late 1930s he emigrated to the United States, where, during the World War, he designed posters to encourage war production.
sentence_243: The designer Charles Gesmar became famous making posters for the singer [[Mistinguett|Mistinguett]] and for [[Air_France|Air France]].
sentence_244: Among the best known French Art Deco poster designers was [[Cassandre_(artist)|Cassandre]], who made the celebrated poster of the ocean liner SS Normandie in 1935.
sentence_245: In the 1930s a new genre of posters appeared in the United States during the Great Depression.
sentence_246: The Federal Art Project hired American artists to create posters to promote tourism and cultural events.
sentence_247: "Art Deco Architecture" redirects here.
sentence_248: For the book by Patricia Bayer, see Art Deco Architecture: Design, Decoration and Detail from the Twenties and Thirties.
sentence_249: Further information: [[Art_Deco_architecture_of_New_York_City|Art Deco architecture of New York City]], [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture|List of Art Deco architecture]], and [[List_of_Art_Deco_buildings_in_Sydney|List of Art Deco buildings in Sydney]]
sentence_250: The architectural style of art deco made its debut in Paris in 1903–04, with the construction of two apartment buildings in Paris, one by Auguste Perret on rue Benjamin Franklin and the other on rue Trétaigne by Henri Sauvage.
sentence_251: The two young architects used reinforced concrete for the first time in Paris residential buildings; the new buildings had clean lines, rectangular forms, and no decoration on the facades; they marked a clean break with the [[Art_Nouveau|art nouveau]] style.
sentence_252: Between 1910 and 1913, Perret used his experience in concrete apartment buildings to construct the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées, 15 [[Avenue_Montaigne|avenue Montaigne]].
sentence_253: Between 1925 and 1928 he constructed the new art deco facade of the [[La_Samaritaine|La Samaritaine]] department store in Paris.
sentence_254: After the First World War, art deco buildings of steel and reinforced concrete began to appear in large cities across Europe and the United States.
sentence_255: In the United States the style was most commonly used for office buildings, government buildings, movie theaters, and railroad stations.
sentence_256: It sometimes was combined with other styles; [[Los_Angeles_City_Hall|Los Angeles City Hall]] combined Art Deco with a roof based on the ancient Greek [[Mausoleum_at_Halicarnassus|Mausoleum at Halicarnassus]], while the [[Los_Angeles_railroad_station|Los Angeles railroad station]] combined Deco with Spanish mission architecture.
sentence_257: Art Deco elements also appeared in engineering projects, including the towers of the [[Golden_Gate_Bridge|Golden Gate Bridge]] and the intake towers of [[Hoover_Dam|Hoover Dam]].
sentence_258: In the 1920s and 1930s it became a truly international style, with examples including the [[Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes|Palacio de Bellas Artes]] (Palace of Fine Arts) in [[Mexico_City|Mexico City]] by Federico Mariscal [], the [[Mayakovskaya_(Moscow_Metro)|Mayakovskaya Metro Station]] in [[Moscow|Moscow]] and the [[National_Diet_Building|National Diet Building]] in Tokyo by Watanabe Fukuzo.
sentence_259: The Art Deco style was not limited to buildings on land; the ocean liner SS Normandie, whose first voyage was in 1935, featured Art Deco design, including a dining room whose ceiling and decoration were made of glass by [[Lalique|Lalique]].
sentence_260: The grand showcases of Art deco interior design were the lobbies of government buildings, theaters, and particularly office buildings.
sentence_261: Interiors were extremely colorful and dynamic, combining sculpture, murals, and ornate geometric design in marble, glass, ceramics and stainless steel.
sentence_262: An early example was the [[Fisher_Building|Fisher Building]] in Detroit, by [[Joseph_Nathaniel_French|Joseph Nathaniel French]]; the lobby was highly decorated with sculpture and ceramics.
sentence_263: The [[Guardian_Building|Guardian Building]] (originally the Union Trust Building) in Detroit, by [[Wirt_Rowland|Wirt Rowland]] (1929), decorated with red and black marble and brightly colored ceramics, highlighted by highly polished steel elevator doors and counters.
sentence_264: The sculptural decoration installed in the walls illustrated the virtues of industry and saving; the building was immediately termed the "Cathedral of Commerce".
sentence_265: The Medical and Dental Building called [[450_Sutter_Street|450 Sutter Street]] in San Francisco by [[Timothy_Pflueger|Timothy Pflueger]] was inspired by [[Maya_civilization|Mayan]] architecture, in a highly stylized form; it used pyramid shapes, and the interior walls were covered highly stylized rows of hieroglyphs.
sentence_266: In France, the best example of an Art Deco interior during period was the [[Palais_de_la_Porte_Dorée|Palais de la Porte Dorée]] (1931) by [[Albert_Laprade|Albert Laprade]], Léon Jaussely and [[Léon_Bazin|Léon Bazin]].
sentence_267: The building (now the National Museum of Immigration, with an aquarium in the basement) was built for the [[Paris_Colonial_Exposition|Paris Colonial Exposition]] of 1931, to celebrate the people and products of French colonies.
sentence_268: The exterior facade was entirely covered with sculpture, and the lobby created an Art Deco harmony with a wood parquet floor in a geometric pattern, a mural depicting the people of French colonies; and a harmonious composition of vertical doors and horizontal balconies.
sentence_269: Many of the best surviving examples of Art Deco are movie theaters built in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentence_270: The Art Deco period coincided with the conversion of silent films to sound, and movie companies built enormous theaters in major cities to capture the huge audience that came to see movies.
sentence_271: Movie palaces in the 1920s often combined exotic themes with art deco style; [[Grauman's_Egyptian_Theatre|Grauman's Egyptian Theatre]] in Hollywood (1922) was inspired by ancient Egyptian [[Tomb|tombs]] and [[Pyramid|pyramids]], while the [[Fox_Theater_(Bakersfield,_California)|Fox Theater]] in Bakersfield, California attached a tower in California Mission style to an Art Deco hall.
sentence_272: The largest of all is [[Radio_City_Music_Hall|Radio City Music Hall]] in New York City, which opened in 1932.
sentence_273: Originally designed as a stage theater, it quickly transformed into a movie theater, which could seat 6,015 persons.
sentence_274: The interior design by [[Donald_Deskey|Donald Deskey]] used glass, aluminum, chrome, and leather to create a colorful escape from reality.
sentence_275: The [[Paramount_Theatre_(Oakland,_California)|Paramount Theatre]] in Oakland, California, by Timothy Pflueger, had a colorful ceramic facade a lobby four stories high, and separate Art Deco smoking rooms for gentlemen and ladies.
sentence_276: Similar grand palaces appeared in Europe.
sentence_277: The [[Grand_Rex|Grand Rex]] in Paris (1932), with its imposing tower, was the largest movie theater in Europe.
sentence_278: The [[Gaumont_State_Cinema|Gaumont State Cinema]] in London (1937) had a tower modeled after the Empire State building, covered with cream-colored ceramic tiles and an interior in an Art Deco-Italian Renaissance style.
sentence_279: The [[Paramount_(Shanghai)|Paramount]] Theater in [[Shanghai|Shanghai]], China (1933) was originally built as a dance hall called The gate of 100 pleasures; it was converted to a movie theater after the Communist Revolution in 1949, and now is a ballroom and disco.
sentence_280: In the 1930s Italian architects built a small movie palace, the Cinema Impero, in [[Asmara|Asmara]] in what is now [[Eritrea|Eritrea]].
sentence_281: Today, many of the movie theaters have been subdivided into multiplexes, but others have been restored and are used as cultural centers in their communities.
sentence_282: See also: [[Streamline_Moderne|Streamline Moderne]]
sentence_283: In the late 1930s, a new variety of Art Deco architecture became common; it was called [[Streamline_Moderne|Streamline Moderne]] or simply Streamline, or, in France, the Style Paqueboat, or Ocean Liner style.
sentence_284: Buildings in the style had rounded corners and long horizontal lines; they were built of reinforced concrete, and were almost always white; and they sometimes had nautical features, such as railings that resembled those on a ship.
sentence_285: The rounded corner was not entirely new; it had appeared in Berlin in 1923 in the [[Mossehaus|Mossehaus]] by [[Erich_Mendelsohn|Erich Mendelsohn]], and later in the [[Hoover_Building|Hoover Building]], an industrial complex in the London suburb of [[Perivale|Perivale]].
sentence_286: In the United States, it became most closely associated with transport; Streamline moderne was rare in office buildings, but was often used for bus stations and airport terminals, such as the terminal at La Guardia airport in New York City that handled the first transatlantic flights, via the PanAm clipper flying boats; and in roadside architecture, such as gas stations and diners.
sentence_287: In the late 1930s a series of diners, modeled after streamlined railroad cars, were produced and installed in towns in New England; at least two examples still remain and are now registered historic buildings.
sentence_288: Decoration in the Art Deco period went through several distinct phases.
sentence_289: Between 1910 and 1920, as Art Nouveau was exhausted, design styles saw a return to tradition, particularly in the work of Paul Iribe.
sentence_290: In 1912 André Vera published an essay in the magazine L'Art Décoratif calling for a return to the craftsmanship and materials of earlier centuries, and using a new repertoire of forms taken from nature, particularly baskets and garlands of fruit and flowers.
sentence_291: A second tendency of Art Deco, also from 1910 to 1920, was inspired by the bright colors of the artistic movement known as the [[Fauvism|Fauves]] and by the colorful costumes and sets of the Ballets Russes.
sentence_292: This style was often expressed with exotic materials such as sharkskin, mother of pearl, ivory, tinted leather, lacquered and painted wood, and decorative inlays on furniture that emphasized its geometry.
sentence_293: This period of the style reached its high point in the 1925 Paris Exposition of Decorative Arts.
sentence_294: In the late 1920s and the 1930s, the decorative style changed, inspired by new materials and technologies.
sentence_295: It became sleeker and less ornamental.
sentence_296: Furniture, like architecture, began to have rounded edges and to take on a polished, streamlined look, taken from the streamline modern style.
sentence_297: New materials, such as chrome-plated steel, aluminum and [[Bakelite|bakelite]], an early form of plastic, began to appear in furniture and decoration.
sentence_298: Throughout the Art Deco period, and particularly in the 1930s, the motifs of the decor expressed the function of the building.
sentence_299: Theaters were decorated with sculpture which illustrated music, dance, and excitement; power companies showed sunrises, the Chrysler building showed stylized hood ornaments; The friezes of Palais de la Porte Dorée at the 1931 Paris Colonial Exposition showed the faces of the different nationalities of French colonies.
sentence_300: The Streamline style made it appear that the building itself was in motion.
sentence_301: The WPA murals of the 1930s featured ordinary people; factory workers, postal workers, families and farmers, in place of classical heroes.
sentence_302: French furniture from 1910 until the early 1920s was largely an updating of French traditional furniture styles, and the art nouveau designs of [[Louis_Majorelle|Louis Majorelle]], [[Charles_Plumet|Charles Plumet]] and other manufacturers.
sentence_303: French furniture manufacturers felt threatened by the growing popularity of German manufacturers and styles, particularly the [[Biedermeier|Biedermeier]] style, which was simple and clean-lined.
sentence_304: The French designer Frantz Jourdain, the President of the Paris Salon d'Automne, invited designers from Munich to participate in the 1910 Salon.
sentence_305: French designers saw the new German style, and decided to meet the German challenge.
sentence_306: The French designers decided to present new French styles in the Salon of 1912.
sentence_307: The rules of the Salon indicated that only modern styles would be permitted.
sentence_308: All of the major French furniture designers took part in Salon: Paul Follot, Paul Iribe, Maurice Dufrêne, André Groult, André Mare and Louis Suë took part, presenting new works that updated the traditional French styles of Louis XVI and [[Louis_Philippe|Louis Philippe]] with more angular corners inspired by Cubism and brighter colors inspired by Fauvism and the Nabis.
sentence_309: The painter [[André_Mare|André Mare]] and furniture designer [[Louis_Süe|Louis Süe]] both participated the 1912 Salon.
sentence_310: After the war the two men joined together to form their own company, formally called the Compagnie des Arts Française, but usually known simply as Suë and Mare.
sentence_311: Unlike the prominent art nouveau designers like Louis Majorelle, who personally designed every piece, they assembled a team of skilled craftsmen and produced complete interior designs, including furniture, glassware, carpets, ceramics, wallpaper and lighting.
sentence_312: Their work featured bright colors and furniture and fine woods, such ebony encrusted with mother of pearl, abalone and silvered metal to create bouquets of flowers.
sentence_313: They designed everything from the interiors of ocean liners to perfume bottles for the label of [[Jean_Patou|Jean Patou]].The firm prospered in the early 1920s, but the two men were better craftsmen than businessmen.
sentence_314: The firm was sold in 1928, and both men left.
sentence_315: The most prominent furniture designer at the 1925 Decorative Arts Exposition was [[Émile-Jacques_Ruhlmann|Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann]], from Alsace.
sentence_316: He first exhibited his works at the 1913 Autumn Salon, then had his own pavilion, the "House of the Rich Collector", at the 1925 Exposition.
sentence_317: He used only most rare and expensive materials, including ebony, [[Mahogany|mahogany]], rosewood, [[Ambon_Island|ambon]] and other exotic woods, decorated with inlays of ivory, tortoise shell, mother of pearl, Little pompoms of silk decorated the handles of drawers of the cabinets.
sentence_318: His furniture was based upon 18th-century models, but simplified and reshaped.
sentence_319: In all of his work, the interior structure of the furniture was completely concealed.
sentence_320: The framework usually of oak, was completely covered with an overlay of thin strips of wood, then covered by a second layer of strips of rare and expensive woods.
sentence_321: This was then covered with a veneer and polished, so that the piece looked as if it had been cut out of a single block of wood.
sentence_322: Contrast to the dark wood was provided by inlays of ivory, and ivory key plates and handles.
sentence_323: According to Ruhlmann, armchairs had to be designed differently according to the functions of the rooms where they appeared; living room armchairs were designed to be welcoming, office chairs comfortable, and salon chairs voluptuous.
sentence_324: Only a small number of pieces of each design of furniture was made, and the average price of one of his beds or cabinets was greater than the price of an average house.
sentence_325: [[Jules_Leleu|Jules Leleu]] was a traditional furniture designer who moved smoothly into Art Deco in the 1920s; he designed the furniture for the dining room of the [[Élysée_Palace|Élysée Palace]], and for the first-class cabins of the steamship Normandie.
sentence_326: his style was characterized by the use of ebony, Macassar wood, walnut, with decoration of plaques of ivory and mother of pearl.
sentence_327: He introduced the style of lacquered art deco furniture at the end of in the late 1920s, and in the late 1930s introduced furniture made of metal with panels of smoked glass.
sentence_328: In Italy, the designer [[Gio_Ponti|Gio Ponti]] was famous for his streamlined designs.
sentence_329: The costly and exotic furniture of Ruhlmann and other traditionalists infuriated modernists, including the architect Le Corbusier, causing him to write a famous series of articles denouncing the arts décoratif style.
sentence_330: He attacked furniture made only for the rich, and called upon designers to create furniture made with inexpensive materials and modern style, which ordinary people could afford.
sentence_331: He designed his own chairs, created to be inexpensive and mass-produced.
sentence_332: In the 1930s, furniture designs adapted to the form, with smoother surfaces and curved forms.
sentence_333: The masters of the late style included Donald Deskey was one of the most influential designers; he created the interior of the Radio City Music Hall.
sentence_334: He used a mixture of traditional and very modern materials, including aluminum, chrome, and bakelite, an early form of plastic.
sentence_335: The [[Waterfall_style|Waterfall style]] was popular the 1930s and 1940s, the most prevalent Art Deco form of furniture at the time.
sentence_336: Pieces were typically of plywood finished with blond veneer and with rounded edges, resembling a waterfall.
sentence_337: Main article: [[Streamline_Moderne|Streamline Moderne]]
sentence_338: Streamline was a variety of Art Deco which emerged during the mid-1930s.
sentence_339: It was influenced by modern [[Aerodynamics|aerodynamic]] principles developed for aviation and [[Ballistics|ballistics]] to reduce aerodynamic drag at high velocities.
sentence_340: The bullet shapes were applied by designers to cars, trains, ships, and even objects not intended to move, such as [[Refrigerator|refrigerators]], [[Fuel_dispenser|gas pumps]], and buildings.
sentence_341: One of the first production vehicles in this style was the Chrysler Airflow of 1933.
sentence_342: It was unsuccessful commercially, but the beauty and functionality of its design set a precedent; meant modernity.
sentence_343: It continued to be used in car design well after World War II.
sentence_344: New industrial materials began to influence design of cars and household objects.
sentence_345: These included [[Aluminum|aluminum]], [[Chrome_plating|chrome]], and [[Bakelite|bakelite]], an early form of plastic.
sentence_346: Bakelite could be easily molded into different forms, and soon was used in telephones, radios and other appliances.
sentence_347: Ocean liners also adopted a style of Art Deco, known in French as the Style Paquebot, or "Ocean Liner Style".
sentence_348: The most famous example was the SS Normandie, which made its first transatlantic trip in 1935.
sentence_349: It was designed particularly to bring wealthy Americans to Paris to shop.
sentence_350: The cabins and salons featured the latest Art Deco furnishings and decoration.
sentence_351: The Grand Salon of the ship, which was the restaurant for first-class passengers, was bigger than the Hall of Mirrors of the [[Palace_of_Versailles|Palace of Versailles]].
sentence_352: It was illuminated by electric lights within twelve pillars of Lalique crystal; thirty-six matching pillars lined the walls.
sentence_353: This was one of the earliest examples of illumination being directly integrated into architecture.
sentence_354: The style of ships was soon adapted to buildings.
sentence_355: A notable example is found on the San Francisco waterfront, where the Maritime Museum building, built as a public bath in 1937, resembles a ferryboat, with ship railings and rounded corners.
sentence_356: The Star Ferry Terminal in Hong Kong also used a variation of the style.
sentence_357: Textiles were an important part of the Art Deco style, in the form of colorful wallpaper, upholstery and carpets, In the 1920s, designers were inspired by the stage sets of the [[Ballets_Russes|Ballets Russes]], fabric designs and costumes from [[Léon_Bakst|Léon Bakst]] and creations by the Wiener Werkstätte.
sentence_358: The early interior designs of [[André_Mare|André Mare]] featured brightly colored and highly stylized garlands of roses and flowers, which decorated the walls, floors, and furniture.
sentence_359: Stylized Floral motifs also dominated the work of [[Raoul_Dufy|Raoul Dufy]] and [[Paul_Poiret|Paul Poiret]], and in the furniture designs of J.E. Ruhlmann.
sentence_360: The floral carpet was reinvented in Deco style by [[Paul_Poiret|Paul Poiret]].
sentence_361: The use of the style was greatly enhanced by the introduction of the pochoir stencil-based printing system, which allowed designers to achieve crispness of lines and very vivid colors.
sentence_362: Art Deco forms appeared in the clothing of [[Paul_Poiret|Paul Poiret]], [[Charles_Worth|Charles Worth]] and [[Jean_Patou|Jean Patou]].
sentence_363: After World War I, exports of clothing and fabrics became one of the most important currency earners of France.
sentence_364: Late Art Deco wallpaper and textiles sometimes featured stylized industrial scenes, cityscapes, locomotives and other modern themes, as well as stylized female figures, metallic colors and geometric designs.
sentence_365: Fashion changed dramatically during the Art Deco period, thanks in particular to designers [[Paul_Poiret|Paul Poiret]] and later [[Coco_Chanel|Coco Chanel]].
sentence_366: Poiret introduced an important innovation to fashion design, the concept of [[Drapery|draping]], a departure from the tailoring and pattern-making of the past.
sentence_367: He designed clothing cut along straight lines and constructed of rectangular motifs.
sentence_368: His styles offered structural simplicity The corseted look and formal styles of the previous period were abandoned, and fashion became more practical, and streamlined.
sentence_369: with the use of new materials, brighter colors and printed designs.
sentence_370: The designer [[Coco_Chanel|Coco Chanel]] continued the transition, popularizing the style of sporty, casual chic.
sentence_371: In the 1920s and 1930s, designers including René Lalique and Cartier tried to reduce the traditional dominance of [[Diamonds|diamonds]] by introducing more colorful gemstones, such as small emeralds, rubies and sapphires.
sentence_372: They also placed greater emphasis on very elaborate and elegant settings, featuring less-expensive materials such as enamel, glass, horn and ivory.
sentence_373: Diamonds themselves were cut in less traditional forms; the 1925 Exposition saw many diamonds cut in the form of tiny rods or matchsticks.
sentence_374: The settings for diamonds also changed; More and more often jewelers used [[Platinum|platinum]] instead of gold, since it was strong and flexible, and could set clusters of stones.
sentence_375: Jewelers also began to use more dark materials, such as enamels and black [[Onyx|onyx]], which provided a higher contrast with diamonds.
sentence_376: Jewelry became much more colorful and varied in style.
sentence_377: Cartier and the firm of Boucheron combined diamonds with colorful other gemstones cut into the form of leaves, fruit or flowers, to make brooches, rings, earrings, clips and pendants.
sentence_378: Far Eastern themes also became popular; plaques of jade and coral were combined with platinum and diamonds, and vanity cases, cigarette cases and powder boxes were decorated with Japanese and Chinese landscapes made with mother of pearl, enamel and lacquer.
sentence_379: Rapidly changing fashions in clothing brought new styles of jewelry.
sentence_380: Sleeveless dresses of the 1920s meant that arms needed decoration, and designers quickly created bracelets of gold, silver and platinum encrusted with lapis-lazuli, onyx, coral, and other colorful stones; Other bracelets were intended for the upper arms, and several bracelets were often worn at the same time.
sentence_381: The short haircuts of women in the twenties called for elaborate deco earring designs.
sentence_382: As women began to smoke in public, designers created very ornate cigarette cases and ivory cigarette holders.
sentence_383: The invention of the wrist-watch before World War I inspired jewelers to create extraordinary decorated watches, encrusted with diamonds and plated with enamel, gold and silver.
sentence_384: Pendant watches, hanging from a ribbon, also became fashionable.
sentence_385: The established jewelry houses of Paris in the period, Cartier, [[Chaumet|Chaumet]], Georges Fouquet, [[Mauboussin|Mauboussin]], and [[Van_Cleef_&_Arpels|Van Cleef & Arpels]] all created jewelry and objects in the new fashion.
sentence_386: The firm of Chaumet made highly geometric cigarette boxes, cigarette lighters, pillboxes and notebooks, made of hard stones decorated with [[Jade|jade]], [[Lapis_lazuli|lapis lazuli]], diamonds and sapphires.
sentence_387: They were joined by many young new designers, each with his own idea of deco.
sentence_388: [[Raymond_Templier|Raymond Templier]] designed pieces with highly intricate geometric patterns, including silver earrings that looked like skyscrapers.
sentence_389: Gerard Sandoz was only 18 when he started to design jewelry in 1921; he designed many celebrated pieces based on the smooth and polished look of modern machinery.
sentence_390: The glass designer René Lalique also entered the field, creating pendants of fruit, flowers, frogs, fairies or mermaids made of sculpted glass in bright colors, hanging on cords of silk with tassels.
sentence_391: The jeweler Paul Brandt contrasted rectangular and triangular patterns, and embedded pearls in lines on onyx plaques.
sentence_392: [[Jean_Despres|Jean Despres]] made necklaces of contrasting colors by bringing together silver and black lacquer, or gold with lapis lazuli.
sentence_393: Many of his designs looked like highly polished pieces of machines.
sentence_394: [[Jean_Dunand|Jean Dunand]] was also inspired by modern machinery, combined with bright reds and blacks contrasting with polished metal.
sentence_395: Like the Art Nouveau period before it, Art Deco was an exceptional period for fine glass and other decorative objects, designed to fit their architectural surroundings.
sentence_396: The most famous producer of glass objects was René Lalique, whose works, from vases to hood ornaments for automobiles, became symbols of the period.
sentence_397: He had made ventures into glass before World War I, designing bottles for the perfumes of [[François_Coty|François Coty]], but he did not begin serious production of art glass until after World War I.
sentence_398: In 1918, at the age of 58, he bought a large glass works in Combs-la-Ville and began to manufacture both artistic and practical glass objects.
sentence_399: He treated glass as a form of sculpture, and created statuettes, vases, bowls, lamps and ornaments.
sentence_400: He used demi-crystal rather than lead crystal, which was softer and easier to form, though not as lustrous.
sentence_401: He sometimes used colored glass, but more often used opalescent glass, where part or the whole of the outer surface was stained with a wash. Lalique provided the decorative glass panels, lights and illuminated glass ceilings for the ocean liners SS Île de France in 1927 and the SS Normandie in 1935, and for some of the first-class sleeping cars of the French railroads.
sentence_402: At the 1925 Exposition of Decorative Arts, he had his own pavilion, designed a dining room with a table settling and matching glass ceiling for the Sèvres Pavilion, and designed a glass fountain for the courtyard of the Cours des Métier, a slender glass column which spouted water from the sides and was illuminated at night.
sentence_403: Other notable Art Deco glass manufacturers included Marius-Ernest Sabino, who specialized in figurines, vases, bowls, and glass sculptures of fish, nudes, and animals.
sentence_404: For these he often used an opalescent glass which could change from white to blue to amber, depending upon the light.
sentence_405: His vases and bowls featured molded friezes of animals, nudes or busts of women with fruit or flowers.
sentence_406: His work was less subtle but more colorful than that of Lalique.
sentence_407: Other notable Deco glass designers included Edmond Etling, who also used bright opalescent colors, often with geometric patterns and sculpted nudes; Albert Simonet, and Aristide Colotte and [[Maurice_Marinot|Maurice Marinot]], who was known for his deeply etched sculptural bottles and vases.
sentence_408: The firm of [[Daum_(studio)|Daum]] from the city of [[Nancy,_France|Nancy]], which had been famous for its Art Nouveau glass, produced a line of Deco vases and glass sculpture, solid, geometric and chunky in form.
sentence_409: More delicate multicolored works were made by Gabriel Argy-Rousseau, who produced delicately colored vases with sculpted butterflies and nymphs, and Francois Decorchemont, whose vases were streaked and marbled.
sentence_410: The Great Depression ruined a large part of the decorative glass industry, which depended upon wealthy clients.
sentence_411: Some artists turned to designing stained glass windows for churches.
sentence_412: In 1937, the Steuben glass company began the practice of commissioning famous artists to produce glassware.
sentence_413: [[Louis_Majorelle|Louis Majorelle]], famous for his Art Nouveau furniture, designed a remarkable Art Deco stained glass window portraying steel workers for the offices of the [[Aciéries_de_Longwy|Aciéries de Longwy]], a steel mill in [[Longwy|Longwy]], France.
sentence_414: [[Amiens_Cathedral|Amiens Cathedral]] has a rare example of Art Deco stained glass windows in the Chapel of the Sacred Heart, made in 1932-34 by the Paris glass artist [[Jean_Gaudin_(glass_artist)|Jean Gaudin]] based on drawings by Jacques Le Breton.
sentence_415: Art Deco artists produced a wide variety of practical objects in the Art Deco style, made of industrial materials from traditional wrought iron to chrome-plated steel.
sentence_416: The American artist [[Norman_Bel_Geddes|Norman Bel Geddes]] designed a cocktail set resembling a skyscraper made of chrome-plated steel.
sentence_417: Raymond Subes designed an elegant metal grille for the entrance of the Palais de la Porte Dorée, the centerpiece of the 1931 Paris Colonial Exposition.
sentence_418: The French sculptor [[Jean_Dunand|Jean Dunand]] produced magnificent doors on the theme "The Hunt", covered with gold leaf and paint on plaster (1935).
sentence_419: Art Deco visuals and imagery was used in multiple [[Animated_film|animated films]] including Batman, [[Night_Hood|Night Hood]], [[All's_Fair_at_the_Fair|All's Fair at the Fair]], Merry Mannequins, [[Page_Miss_Glory_(1936_film)|Page Miss Glory]], [[Fantasia_(1940_film)|Fantasia]] and [[Sleeping_Beauty_(1959_film)|Sleeping Beauty]].

section_30.value: Art Deco architecture around the world

sentence_420: Art Deco architecture began in Europe, but by 1939 there were examples in large cities on every continent and in almost every country.
sentence_421: This is a selection of prominent buildings on each continent.
sentence_422: (For a comprehensive of existing buildings by country, see [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture|List of Art Deco architecture]].)
sentence_423: See also: [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#Africa|List of Art Deco architecture § Africa]]
sentence_424: Most Art Deco buildings in Africa were built during European colonial rule, and often designed by Italian and French architects.
sentence_425: See also: [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#Asia|List of Art Deco architecture § Asia]]
sentence_426: See also: [[List_of_Art_Deco_buildings_in_Sydney|List of Art Deco buildings in Sydney]], [[List_of_Art_Deco_buildings_in_Melbourne|List of Art Deco buildings in Melbourne]], List of Art Deco buildings in Tasmania, [[List_of_Art_Deco_buildings_in_Perth|List of Art Deco buildings in Perth]], and [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#Oceania|List of Art Deco architecture § Oceania]]
sentence_427: Melbourne and Sydney, Australia, have several notable Art Deco buildings, including the [[Manchester_Unity_Building|Manchester Unity Building]] and the former [[Russell_Street_Police_Headquarters|Russell Street Police Headquarters]] in Melbourne, the Castlemaine Art Museum in [[Castlemaine,_Victoria|Castlemaine]], central Victoria and the [[Grace_Building,_Sydney|Grace Building]], [[AWA_Tower|AWA Tower]] and [[Anzac_Memorial|Anzac Memorial]] in Sydney.
sentence_428: Several towns in New Zealand, including [[Napier,_New_Zealand|Napier]] and [[Hastings,_New_Zealand|Hastings]] were rebuilt in Art Deco style after the [[1931_Hawke's_Bay_earthquake|1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake]], and many of the buildings have been protected and restored.
sentence_429: Napier has been nominated for UNESCO [[World_Heritage_Site|World Heritage Site]] status, the first cultural site in New Zealand to be nominated.
sentence_430: [[Wellington|Wellington]] has retained a sizeable number of Art Deco buildings.

section_34.value: Canada, Mexico, and the United States

sentence_431: See also: [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#North_America|List of Art Deco architecture § North America]], [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#United_States|List of Art Deco architecture § United States]], and [[Art_Deco_in_the_United_States|Art Deco in the United States]]
sentence_432: In Canada, surviving Art Deco structures are mainly in the major cities; [[Montreal|Montreal]], [[Toronto|Toronto]], [[Hamilton,_Ontario|Hamilton, Ontario]], and [[Vancouver|Vancouver]].
sentence_433: They range from public buildings like [[Vancouver_City_Hall|Vancouver City Hall]] to commercial buildings ([[College_Park_(Toronto)|College Park]]) to public works ([[R._C._Harris_Water_Treatment_Plant|R.
sentence_434: C. Harris Water Treatment Plant]]).
sentence_435: In Mexico, the most imposing Art Deco example is interior of the [[Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes|Palacio de Bellas Artes]] (Palace of Fine Arts), finished in 1934 with its elaborate decor and murals.
sentence_436: Examples of Art Deco residential architecture can be found in the [[Condesa|Condesa]] neighborhood, many designed by [[Francisco_J._Serrano|Francisco J. Serrano]].
sentence_437: In the United States, Art Deco buildings are found from coast to coast, in all the major cities.
sentence_438: It was most widely used for office buildings, train stations, airport terminals, and movie theaters; residential buildings are rare.
sentence_439: During the 1920s and 1930s architects in the [[Southwestern_United_States|Southwestern United States]], particularly in the US state of [[New_Mexico|New Mexico]], combined [[Pueblo_Revival_architecture|Pueblo revival]] with Art Deco to create [[Pueblo_Deco_architecture|Pueblo Deco]], as seen in the [[KiMo_Theater|KiMo Theater]] in [[Albuquerque,_New_Mexico|Albuquerque]].
sentence_440: In the 1930s, the more austere streamline style became popular.
sentence_441: Many buildings were demolished between 1945 and the late 1960s, but then efforts began to protect the best examples.
sentence_442: The City of Miami Beach established the [[Miami_Beach_Architectural_District|Miami Beach Architectural District]] to preserve the colorful collection of Art Deco buildings found there.
sentence_443: See also: List of Art Deco architecture § Central America / Caribbean
sentence_444: Art Deco buildings can be found throughout Central America.
sentence_445: A particularly rich collection is found in [[Cuba|Cuba]], built largely for the large number of tourists who came to the island from the United States.
sentence_446: One such building is the [[López_Serrano_Building|López Serrano]] built between 1929 and 1932 in the Vedado section of [[Havana|Havana]].
sentence_447: See also: [[Art_Deco_in_Paris|Art Deco in Paris]], Art Deco in Brussels, and [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#Europe|List of Art Deco architecture § Europe]]
sentence_448: The architectural style first appeared in Paris with the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées (1910–13) by Auguste Perret but then spread rapidly around Europe, until examples could be found in nearly every large city, from London to Moscow.
sentence_449: In Germany two variations of Art Deco flourished in the 1920s and 30s: The [[New_Objectivity_(architecture)|Neue Sachlichkeit]] style and [[Expressionist_architecture|Expressionist architecture]].
sentence_450: Notable examples include Erich Mendelsohn's Mossehaus and Schaubühne theater in [[Berlin|Berlin]], Fritz Höger's [[Chilehaus|Chilehaus]] in [[Hamburg|Hamburg]] and his [[Kirche_am_Hohenzollernplatz|Kirche am Hohenzollernplatz]] in Berlin, the Anzeiger Tower in [[Hanover|Hanover]] and the Borsig Tower in Berlin.
sentence_451: One of the largest Art Deco buildings in Western Europe is the [[Basilica_of_the_Sacred_Heart,_Brussels|National Basilica of the Sacred Heart]] in [[Koekelberg|Koekelberg]], Brussels.
sentence_452: In 1925, architect Albert van Huffel won the Grand Prize for Architecture with his scale model of the basilica at the Exposition Internationale des Arts Décoratifs et Industriels Modernes in Paris.
sentence_453: Spain and Portugal have some striking examples of Art Deco buildings, particularly movie theaters.
sentence_454: Examples in Portugal are the Capitólio Theater (1931) and the Éden Cine-Theater (1937) in [[Lisbon|Lisbon]], the [[Rivoli_Theatre_(Portugal)|Rivoli Theater]] (1937) and the [[Coliseu_do_Porto|Coliseu]] (1941) in [[Porto|Porto]] and the Rosa Damasceno Theater (1937) in [[Santarém,_Portugal|Santarém]].
sentence_455: An example in Spain is the Cine Rialto in Valencia (1939).
sentence_456: During the 1930s, Art Deco had a noticeable effect on house design in the United Kingdom, as well as the design of various public buildings.
sentence_457: Straight, white-rendered house frontages rising to flat roofs, sharply geometric door surrounds and tall windows, as well as convex-curved metal corner windows, were all characteristic of that period.
sentence_458: The [[London_Underground|London Underground]] is famous for many examples of Art Deco architecture, and there are a number of buildings in the style situated along the [[Golden_Mile_(Brentford)|Golden Mile]] in Brentford.
sentence_459: Also in West London is the Hoover Building, which was originally built for [[The_Hoover_Company|The Hoover Company]] and was converted into a superstore in the early 1990s.
sentence_460: Bucharest, Romania Bucharest once known as the "Little Paris" of the 19th century engages in a new adventure after the first world war, together with the new trends and progress of technology, thus redirecting its inspiration towards a further horizon, New York City.
sentence_461: The 1930s bring a new fashion brought by a newer generation which echoes in the cinema, theater, dancing styles, art and architecture.
sentence_462: Bucharest during the 1930s was marked by more and more art deco architecture from the bigger boulevards like Magheru street to the private houses and smaller neighborhoods.
sentence_463: One of the first landmarks of modern Bucharest is considered The Palace of Telephones which would be the first skyscraper of the city.
sentence_464: It was the tallest building between 1933 and the 1970s, with a height of 52.5 m. The architects were Louis Weeks and Edmond Van Saanen and engineer Walter Troy.
sentence_465: The art deco monuments are a crucial part of the entire character of Bucharest since they describe and mark an important period from history, the interbellic life (WW1-WW2).
sentence_466: Unfortunately, most of the buildings from those years are prone to catastrophes, Bucharest being in danger of another earthquake, very common for its geographic region.
sentence_467: It is truly important to protect the art deco patrimony in Bucharest and preserve another great and essential art deco capital from Europe.
sentence_468: See also: [[Art_Deco_in_Mumbai|Art Deco in Mumbai]]
sentence_469: The Indian Institute of Architects, founded in Mumbai in 1929, played a prominent role in propagating the Art Deco movement.
sentence_470: In November 1937, this institute organized the 'Ideal Home Exhibition' held in the Town Hall in Mumbai which spanned over 12 days and attracted about one hundred thousand visitors.
sentence_471: As a result, it was declared a success by the 'Journal of the Indian Institute of Architects'.
sentence_472: The exhibits displayed the 'ideal', or better described as the most 'modern' arrangements for various parts of the house, paying close detail to avoid architectural blunders and present the most efficient and well-thought-out models.
sentence_473: The exhibition focused on various elements of a home ranging from furniture, elements of interior decoration as well as radios and refrigerators using new and scientifically relevant materials and methods.
sentence_474: Guided by their desire to emulate the west, the Indian architects were fascinated by the industrial modernity that Art Deco offered.
sentence_475: The western elites were the first to experiment with the technologically advanced facets of Art Deco, and architects began the process of transformation by the early 1930s.
sentence_476: Mumbai's expanding port commerce in the 1930s resulted in the growth of educated middle class population.
sentence_477: It also saw an increase of people migrating to Mumbai in search of job opportunities.
sentence_478: This led to the pressing need for new developments through Land Reclamation Schemes and construction of new public and residential buildings.
sentence_479: Parallelly, the changing political climate in the country and the aspirational quality of the Art Deco aesthetics led to a whole-hearted acceptance of the building style in the city's development.
sentence_480: Most of the buildings from this period can be seen spread throughout the city neighbourhoods in areas such as Churchgate, Colaba, Fort, Mohammed Ali Road, Cumbala Hill, Dadar, Matunga, Bandra and Chembur.
sentence_481: See also: [[List_of_Art_Deco_architecture#South_America|List of Art Deco architecture § South America]]
sentence_482: Art Deco in South America is especially present in countries which received a great wave of immigration in the first half of the 20th century, with notable works in their richest cities, like [[São_Paulo|São Paulo]] and [[Rio_de_Janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in Brazil and [[Buenos_Aires|Buenos Aires]] in Argentina.
sentence_483: The [[Kavanagh_building|Kavanagh building]] in Buenos Aires (1934), by Sánchez, Lagos and de la Torre, was the tallest reinforced-concrete structure when it was completed, and is a notable example of late Art Deco style.
sentence_484: In many cities, efforts have been made to protect the remaining Art Deco buildings.
sentence_485: In many U.S. cities, historic art deco movie theaters have been preserved and turned into cultural centers.
sentence_486: Even more modest art deco buildings have been preserved as part of America's architectural heritage; an art deco cafe and gas station along Route 66 in Shamrock, Texas is an historic monument.
sentence_487: The Miami Beach Architectural District protects several hundred old buildings, and requires that new buildings comply with the style.
sentence_488: In [[Havana|Havana]], Cuba, many Art Deco buildings have badly deteriorated.
sentence_489: Efforts are underway to bring the buildings back to their original color and appearance.
sentence_490: In the 21st century, modern variants of Art Deco, called Neo Art Deco (or Neo-Art Deco), have appeared in some American cities, inspired by the classic Art Deco buildings of the 1920s and 1930s.
sentence_491: Examples include the NBC Tower in Chicago, inspired by [[30_Rockefeller_Plaza|30 Rockefeller Plaza]] in New York City; and [[Smith_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts|Smith Center for the Performing Arts]] in Las Vegas, Nevada, which includes art deco features from [[Hoover_Dam|Hoover Dam]], fifty miles away.

title: Antlia
sentence_0: Antlia ([[English|/ˈæntliə/]]; from Ancient Greek ἀντλία) is a [[Constellation|constellation]] in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
sentence_1: Its name means "[[Pump|pump]]" in [[Latin|Latin]] and [[Greek_language|Greek]]; it represents an [[Air_pump|air pump]].
sentence_2: Originally Antlia Pneumatica, the constellation was established by [[Nicolas-Louis_de_Lacaille|Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille]] in the 18th century.
sentence_3: Its non-specific (single-word) name, already in limited use, was preferred by [[John_Herschel|John Herschel]] then welcomed by the astronomic community which officially accepted this.
sentence_4: North of stars forming some of the sails of the ship [[Argo_Navis|Argo Navis]] (the constellation [[Vela_(constellation)|Vela]]), Antlia is completely visible from latitudes south of [[49th_parallel_north|49 degrees north]].
sentence_5: Antlia is a faint constellation; its brightest star is [[Alpha_Antliae|Alpha Antliae]], an orange [[Giant_star|giant]] that is a suspected variable star, ranging between [[Apparent_magnitude|apparent magnitudes]] 4.22 and 4.29.
sentence_6: [[S_Antliae|S Antliae]] is an [[Binary_star#Eclipsing_binaries|eclipsing binary]] star system, changing in brightness as one star passes in front of the other.
sentence_7: Sharing a [[Common_envelope|common envelope]], the stars are so close they will one day merge to form a single star.
sentence_8: Two star systems with known exoplanets, [[HD_93083|HD 93083]] and [[WASP-66|WASP-66]], lie within Antlia, as do [[NGC_2997|NGC 2997]], a [[Spiral_galaxy|spiral galaxy]], and the [[Antlia_Dwarf|Antlia Dwarf Galaxy]].
sentence_9: The French astronomer [[Nicolas-Louis_de_Lacaille|Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille]] first described the constellation in French as la Machine Pneumatique (the Pneumatic Machine) in 1751–52, commemorating the [[Air_pump|air pump]] invented by the French physicist Denis Papin.
sentence_10: De Lacaille had observed and catalogued almost 10,000 southern stars during a two-year stay at the Cape of Good Hope, devising fourteen new constellations in uncharted regions of the Southern Celestial Hemisphere not visible from Europe.
sentence_11: He named all but one in honour of instruments that symbolised the [[Age_of_Enlightenment|Age of Enlightenment]].
sentence_12: Lacaille depicted Antlia as a single-cylinder vacuum pump used in Papin's initial experiments, while German astronomer [[Johann_Elert_Bode|Johann Bode]] chose the more advanced double-cylinder version.
sentence_13: Lacaille [[Latin|Latinised]] the name to Antlia pneumatica on his 1763 chart.
sentence_14: English astronomer [[John_Herschel|John Herschel]] proposed shrinking the name to one word in 1844, noting that Lacaille himself had abbreviated his constellations thus on occasion.
sentence_15: This was universally adopted.
sentence_16: The [[International_Astronomical_Union|International Astronomical Union]] adopted it as one of the [[88_modern_constellations|88 modern constellations]] in 1922.
sentence_17: Although visible to the Ancient Greeks, Antlia's stars were too faint to have been commonly recognised as a figurative object, or part of one, in ancient asterisms.
sentence_18: The stars that now comprise Antlia are in a zone of the sky associated with the asterism/old constellation [[Argo_Navis|Argo Navis]], the ship, the Argo, of the Argonauts, in its latter centuries.
sentence_19: This, due to its immense size, was split into hull, poop deck and sails by Lacaille in 1763.
sentence_20: Ridpath reports that due to their faintness, the stars of Antlia did not make up part of the classical depiction of Argo Navis.
sentence_21: [[Chinese_astronomy|Chinese astronomers]] were able to view what is modern Antlia from their latitudes, and incorporated its stars into two different constellations.
sentence_22: Several stars in the southern part of Antlia were a portion of "Dong'ou", which represented an area in southern China.
sentence_23: Furthermore, [[Epsilon_Antliae|Epsilon]], [[Eta_Antliae|Eta]], and [[Theta_Antliae|Theta Antliae]] were incorporated into the celestial temple, which also contained stars from modern [[Pyxis|Pyxis]].
sentence_24: Covering 238.9 square degrees and hence 0.579% of the sky, Antlia ranks 62nd of the [[88_modern_constellations|88 modern constellations]] by area.
sentence_25: Its position in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere means that the whole [[Constellation|constellation]] is visible to observers south of [[49th_parallel_north|49°N]].
sentence_26: [[Hydra_(constellation)|Hydra]] the sea snake runs along the length of its northern border, while [[Pyxis|Pyxis]] the compass, [[Vela_(constellation)|Vela]] the sails, and [[Centaurus|Centaurus]] the centaur line it to the west, south and east respectively.
sentence_27: The three-letter abbreviation for the constellation, as adopted by the International Astronomical Union, is "Ant".
sentence_28: The official constellation boundaries, as set by Belgian astronomer [[Eugène_Joseph_Delporte|Eugène Delporte]] in 1930, are defined by a polygon with an east side, south side and ten other sides (facing the two other cardinal compass points) (illustrated in infobox at top-right).
sentence_29: In the [[Equatorial_coordinate_system|equatorial coordinate system]], the [[Right_ascension|right ascension]] coordinates of these borders lie between 09 26.5 and 11 05.6 , while the [[Declination|declination]] coordinates are between −24.54° and −40.42°.
sentence_30: See also: [[List_of_stars_in_Antlia|List of stars in Antlia]]
sentence_31: Lacaille gave nine stars Bayer designations, labelling them Alpha through to Theta, combining two stars next to each other as Zeta.
sentence_32: Gould later added a tenth, [[Iota_Antliae|Iota Antliae]].
sentence_33: Beta and Gamma Antliae (now [[HR_4339|HR 4339]] and [[HD_90156|HD 90156]]) ended up in the neighbouring constellation Hydra once the constellation boundaries were delineated in 1930.
sentence_34: Within the constellation's borders, there are 42 stars brighter than or equal to [[Apparent_magnitude|apparent magnitude]] 6.5.
sentence_35: The constellation's two brightest stars—[[Alpha_Antliae|Alpha]] and [[Epsilon_Antliae|Epsilon Antliae]]—shine with a reddish tinge.
sentence_36: Alpha is an orange [[Giant_star|giant]] of [[Stellar_classification#Spectral_types|spectral type]] [[Stellar_classification#Class_K|K4III]] that is a suspected variable star, ranging between [[Apparent_magnitude|apparent magnitudes]] 4.22 and 4.29.
sentence_37: It is located 320 ± 10 [[Light-year|light-years]] away from Earth.
sentence_38: Estimated to be shining with around 480 to 555 times the [[Luminosity|luminosity]] of the Sun, it is most likely an ageing star that is brightening and on its way to becoming a [[Mira_variable|Mira variable]] star, having converted all its core fuel into carbon.
sentence_39: Located 590 ± 30 light-years from Earth, Epsilon Antliae is an evolved orange giant star of spectral type K3 IIIa, that has swollen to have a diameter about 69 times that of the Sun, and a luminosity of around 1279 Suns.
sentence_40: It is slightly variable.
sentence_41: At the other end of Antlia, [[Iota_Antliae|Iota Antliae]] is likewise an orange giant of spectral type K1 III.
sentence_42: It is 202 ± 2 light-years distant.
sentence_43: Located near Alpha is [[Delta_Antliae|Delta Antliae]], a [[Binary_star|binary star]], 450 ± 10 light-years distant from Earth.
sentence_44: The primary is a [[B-type_main_sequence_star|blue-white main sequence star]] of spectral type [[Stellar_classification#Class_B|B9.5V]] and magnitude 5.6, and the secondary is a [[F-type_main_sequence_star|yellow-white main sequence star]] of spectral type [[Stellar_classification#Class_F|F9Ve]] and magnitude 9.6.
sentence_45: [[Zeta_Antliae|Zeta Antliae]] is a wide optical [[Double_star|double star]].
sentence_46: The brighter star—[[Zeta1_Antliae|Zeta Antliae]]—is 410 ± 40 light-years distant and has a magnitude of 5.74, though it is a true binary star system composed of two [[A-type_main_sequence_star|white main sequence stars]] of magnitudes 6.20 and 7.01 that are separated by 8.042 [[Arcsecond|arcseconds]].
sentence_47: The fainter star—[[Zeta2_Antliae|Zeta Antliae]]—is 386 ± 5 light-years distant and of magnitude 5.9.
sentence_48: [[Eta_Antliae|Eta Antliae]] is another double composed of a yellow white star of spectral type F1V and magnitude 5.31, with a companion of magnitude 11.3.
sentence_49: [[Theta_Antliae|Theta Antliae]] is likewise double, most likely composed of an [[A-type_main_sequence_star|A-type main sequence star]] and a yellow giant.
sentence_50: [[S_Antliae|S Antliae]] is an [[Eclipsing_binary|eclipsing binary]] star system that varies in apparent magnitude from 6.27 to 6.83 over a period of 15.6 hours.
sentence_51: The system is classed as a [[W_Ursae_Majoris_variable|W Ursae Majoris variable]]—the primary is hotter than the secondary and the drop in magnitude is caused by the latter passing in front of the former.
sentence_52: Calculating the properties of the component stars from the orbital period indicates that the primary star has a mass 1.94 times and a diameter 2.026 times that of the Sun, and the secondary has a mass 0.76 times and a diameter 1.322 times that of the Sun.
sentence_53: The two stars have similar [[Luminosity|luminosity]] and [[Stellar_classification|spectral type]] as they have a [[Common_envelope|common envelope]] and share stellar material.
sentence_54: The system is thought to be around 5–6 billion years old.
sentence_55: The two stars will eventually merge to form a single fast-spinning star.
sentence_56: [[T_Antliae|T Antliae]] is a [[Yellow_supergiant|yellow-white supergiant]] of spectral type F6Iab and [[Classical_Cepheid_variable|Classical Cepheid variable]] ranging between magnitude 8.88 and 9.82 over 5.9 days.
sentence_57: [[U_Antliae|U Antliae]] is a red [[Stellar_classification|C-type]] [[Carbon_star|carbon star]] and is an irregular variable that ranges between magnitudes 5.27 and 6.04.
sentence_58: At 910 ± 50 light-years distant, it is around 5819 times as luminous as the Sun.
sentence_59: [[BF_Antliae|BF Antliae]] is a [[Delta_Scuti_variable|Delta Scuti variable]] that varies by 0.01 of a magnitude.
sentence_60: [[HR_4049|HR 4049]], also known as AG Antliae, is an unusual hot variable ageing star of spectral type B9.5Ib-II.
sentence_61: It is undergoing intense loss of mass and is a unique variable that does not belong to any class of known variable star, ranging between magnitudes 5.29 and 5.83 with a period of 429 days.
sentence_62: It is around 6000 light-years away from Earth.
sentence_63: [[UX_Antliae|UX Antliae]] is an [[R_Coronae_Borealis_variable|R Coronae Borealis variable]] with a baseline apparent magnitude of around 11.85, with irregular dimmings down to below magnitude 18.0.
sentence_64: A luminous and remote star, it is a [[Supergiant|supergiant]] with a spectrum resembling that of a yellow-white F-type star but it has almost no hydrogen.
sentence_65: [[HD_93083|HD 93083]] is an orange dwarf star of spectral type K3V that is smaller and cooler than the Sun.
sentence_66: It has a planet that was discovered by the [[Radial_velocity_method|radial velocity method]] with the [[High_Accuracy_Radial_Velocity_Planet_Searcher|HARPS spectrograph]] in 2005.
sentence_67: About as massive as Saturn, the planet orbits its star with a period of 143 days at a mean distance of 0.477 AU.
sentence_68: [[WASP-66|WASP-66]] is a sunlike star of spectral type F4V. A planet with 2.3 times the mass of Jupiter orbits it every 4 days, discovered by the transit method in 2012.
sentence_69: [[DEN_1048-3956|DEN 1048-3956]] is a [[Brown_dwarf|brown dwarf]] of spectral type M8 located around 13 light-years distant from Earth.
sentence_70: At magnitude 17 it is much too faint to be seen with the unaided eye.
sentence_71: It has a surface temperature of about 2500 K. Two powerful [[Solar_flare|flares]] lasting 4–5 minutes each were detected in 2002.
sentence_72: [[2MASS_0939-2448|2MASS 0939-2448]] is a system of two cool and faint brown dwarfs, probably with effective temperatures of about 500 and 700 K and masses of about 25 and 40 times that of Jupiter, though it is also possible that both objects have temperatures of 600 K and 30 Jupiter masses.
sentence_73: Antlia contains many faint galaxies, the brightest of which is [[NGC_2997|NGC 2997]] at magnitude 10.6.
sentence_74: It is a loosely wound face-on [[Spiral_galaxy|spiral galaxy]] of type [[Galaxy_morphological_classification|Sc]].
sentence_75: Though nondescript in most amateur telescopes, it presents bright clusters of young stars and many dark dust lanes in photographs.
sentence_76: Discovered in 1997, the [[Antlia_Dwarf|Antlia Dwarf]] is a 14.8 [[Dwarf_spheroidal_galaxy|dwarf spheroidal galaxy]] that belongs to the [[Local_Group|Local Group]] of galaxies.
sentence_77: In 2018 the discovery was announced of a very low [[Surface_brightness|surface brightness]] galaxy near Epsilon Antliae, [[Antlia_2|Antlia 2]], which is a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
sentence_78: The [[Antlia_Cluster|Antlia Cluster]], also known as Abell S0636, is a [[Galaxy_cluster|cluster of galaxies]] located in the [[Hydra-Centaurus_Supercluster|Hydra-Centaurus Supercluster]].
sentence_79: It is the third nearest to the [[Local_Group|Local Group]] after the [[Virgo_Cluster|Virgo Cluster]] and the [[Fornax_Cluster|Fornax Cluster]].
sentence_80: The cluster's distance from earth is 40.5 [[Parsec#Megaparsecs_and_gigaparsecs|Mpc]] (132.1 [[Light-year#Definitions|Mly]]) to 40.9 Mpc (133.4 Mly) Located in the southeastern corner of the constellation, it boasts the giant elliptical galaxies [[NGC_3268|NGC 3268]] and [[NGC_3258|NGC 3258]] as the main members of a southern and northern subgroup respectively, and contains around 234 galaxies in total.

title: A.S. Roma
sentence_0: This article is about the men's football club.
sentence_1: For the women's football club, see [[A.S._Roma_Women|A.S.
sentence_2: Roma Women]].
sentence_3: For other uses, see [[Roma_(disambiguation)#Sports|Roma (disambiguation) § Sports]].
sentence_4: Associazione Sportiva Roma ([[Borsa_Italiana|BIT]]: , [[London_Stock_Exchange|LSE]]: ; Rome Sport Association), commonly referred to as Roma (Italian pronunciation: [[Italian|[ˈroːma]]), is an [[Football_in_Italy|Italian]] professional [[Association_football|football]] [[List_of_football_clubs_in_Italy|club]] based in [[Rome|Rome]].
sentence_5: Founded by a merger in 1927, Roma have participated in the top-tier of Italian football for all of their existence except for [[1951–52_Serie_B|1951–52]] season.
sentence_6: Roma have won [[Serie_A|Serie A]] three times, in [[1941–42_Serie_A|1941–42]], [[1982–83_Serie_A|1982–83]] and [[2000–01_Serie_A|2000–01]], as well as winning nine [[Coppa_Italia|Coppa Italia]] titles and two [[Supercoppa_Italiana|Supercoppa Italiana]] titles.
sentence_7: In European competitions, Roma won the [[Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup|Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] in [[1960–61_Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup|1960–61]] and were runners-up in the [[1983–84_European_Cup|1983–84 European Cup]] and the [[1990–91_UEFA_Cup|1990–91 UEFA Cup]].
sentence_8: Fifteen players have won the [[FIFA_World_Cup|FIFA World Cup]] while playing at Roma: Ferraris, Guaita and Masetti (1934); Donati, Monzeglio and Serantoni (1938); [[Bruno_Conti|Bruno Conti]] (1982); [[Rudi_Voller|Rudi Voller]] and Berthold (1990); Aldair (1994); Candela (1998); [[Cafu|Cafu]] (2002); [[Daniele_De_Rossi|Daniele De Rossi]], [[Simone_Perrotta|Simone Perrotta]] and [[Francesco_Totti|Francesco Totti]] (2006).
sentence_9: Since 1953, Roma have played their home matches at the Stadio Olimpico, a venue they share with city rivals [[S.S._Lazio|Lazio]].
sentence_10: With a capacity of over 72,000, it is the second-largest of its kind in Italy, with only the [[San_Siro|San Siro]] able to seat more.
sentence_11: The club plan to move to a [[Stadio_della_Roma|new stadium]], though this is yet to start construction.
sentence_12: The club's home colours are [[Carmine_(color)|carmine red]] and [[Golden_yellow|golden yellow]], which gives Roma their nickname "I Giallorossi" ("The Yellow and Reds").
sentence_13: These colours have often been combined with white shorts.
sentence_14: Their club badge features a she-wolf, an allusion to the [[Founding_of_Rome|founding myth of Rome]].
sentence_15: Main article: [[History_of_A.S._Roma|History of A.S. Roma]]
sentence_16: A.S. Roma was founded in the spring of 1927 when Italo Foschi initiated the merger of three older [[Italian_Football_Championship|Italian Football Championship]] clubs from the city of Rome: [[Roman_F.C.|Roman FC]], [[S.S._Alba-Audace_Roma|SS Alba-Audace]] and [[Fortitudo-Pro_Roma_S.G.S.|Fortitudo-Pro Roma SGS]].
sentence_17: Italo Foschi was an important Roman representative of the ruling [[National_Fascist_Party|National Fascist Party]].
sentence_18: The purpose of the merger was to give the Italian capital a strong club to rival that of the more dominant Northern Italian clubs of the time.
sentence_19: The only major Roman club to resist the merger was [[S.S._Lazio|Lazio]] because of the intervention of the army General Vaccaro, a member of the club and executive of Italian Football Federation.
sentence_20: All three founding clubs were [[Serie_B|relegated]], but the fascist-aligned FIGC bet over the capacity of the new team to give a stronger representation to the capital of Italy, and they were awarded a [[Wild_card_(sports)|wild card]] for the [[Divisione_Nazionale|Divisione Nazionale]], the [[Serie_A|Serie A]] forerunner.
sentence_21: The club played its earliest seasons at the Motovelodromo Appio stadium, before settling in the working-class streets of [[Testaccio|Testaccio]], where it built an all-wooden ground Campo Testaccio; this was opened in November 1929.
sentence_22: An early season in which Roma made a large mark was the [[1930–31_Serie_A|1930–31]] championship, where the club finished as runners-up behind [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]].
sentence_23: Captain [[Attilio_Ferraris|Attilio Ferraris]], along with [[Guido_Masetti|Guido Masetti]], [[Fulvio_Bernardini|Fulvio Bernardini]] and [[Rodolfo_Volk|Rodolfo Volk]], were highly important players during this period.
sentence_24: After a slump in league form and the departure of high key players, Roma eventually rebuilt their squad adding goalscorers such as the Argentine [[Enrique_Guaita|Enrique Guaita]].
sentence_25: Under the management of [[Luigi_Barbesino|Luigi Barbesino]], the Roman club came close to their first title in [[1935–36_Serie_A|1935–36]], finishing just one point behind champions [[Bologna_F.C._1909|Bologna]].
sentence_26: Roma returned to form after being inconsistent for much of the late 1930s.
sentence_27: Roma recorded an unexpected title triumph in the [[1941–42_Serie_A|1941–42 season]] by winning their first ever Scudetto title.
sentence_28: The 18 goals scored by local player [[Amedeo_Amadei|Amedeo Amadei]] were essential to the [[Alfréd_Schaffer|Alfréd Schaffer]]-coached Roma side winning the title.
sentence_29: At the time, Italy was involved in [[World_War_II|World War II]] and Roma were playing at the [[Stadio_Nazionale_PNF|Stadio del Partito Nazionale Fascista]].
sentence_30: In the years just after the war, Roma were unable to recapture their league stature from the early 1940s.
sentence_31: Roma finished in the lower half of Serie A for five seasons in a row, before eventually succumbing to their only ever relegation to [[Serie_B|Serie B]] at the end of the [[1950–51_Serie_A|1950–51 season]], around a decade after their championship victory.
sentence_32: Under future [[Italy_national_football_team|Italy national team]] manager [[Giuseppe_Viani|Giuseppe Viani]], promotion straight back up was achieved.
sentence_33: After returning to the Serie A, Roma managed to stabilise themselves as a top half club again with players such as [[Egisto_Pandolfini|Egisto Pandolfini]], [[Dino_Da_Costa|Dino Da Costa]] and Dane [[Helge_Bronée|Helge Bronée]].
sentence_34: Their best finish of this period was under the management of Englishman Jesse Carver, when in [[1954–55_Serie_A|1954–55]], they finished as runners-up after [[Udinese_Calcio|Udinese]], who originally finished second were relegated for corruption.
sentence_35: Although Roma were unable to break into the top four during the following decade, they did achieve some measure of cup success.
sentence_36: Their first honour outside of Italy was recorded in [[1960–61_Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup|1960–61]] when Roma won the [[Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup|Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] by defeating [[Birmingham_City_F.C.|Birmingham City]] 4–2 in the finals.
sentence_37: A few years later, Roma won their first [[Coppa_Italia|Coppa Italia]] trophy in 1963–64 after defeating [[Torino_F.C.|Torino]] 1–0.
sentence_38: Their lowest point came during the 1964–65 season, when manager [[Juan_Carlos_Lorenzo|Juan Carlos Lorenzo]] announced the club could not pay its players and was unlikely to be able to afford to travel to [[Vicenza|Vicenza]] to fulfil its next fixture.
sentence_39: Supporters kept the club going with a fundraiser at the Sistine Theatre and bankruptcy was avoided with the election of a new club president [[Franco_Evangelisti_(politician)|Franco Evangelisti]].
sentence_40: Their second Coppa Italia trophy was won in 1968–69, when it competed in a small, league-like system.
sentence_41: [[Giacomo_Losi|Giacomo Losi]] set a Roma appearance record in 1969 with 450 appearances in all competitions, a record that would last 38 years.
sentence_42: Roma were able to add another cup to their collection in 1972, with a 3–1 victory over [[Blackpool_F.C.|Blackpool]] in the [[Anglo-Italian_Cup|Anglo-Italian Cup]].
sentence_43: During much of the 1970s, Roma's appearance in the top half of Serie A was sporadic.
sentence_44: The best place the club were able to achieve during the decade was third in [[1974–75_Serie_A|1974–75]].
sentence_45: Notable players who turned out for the club during this period included midfielders [[Giancarlo_De_Sisti|Giancarlo De Sisti]] and [[Francesco_Rocca|Francesco Rocca]].
sentence_46: The dawning of a newly successful era in Roma's footballing history was brought in with another Coppa Italia victory, they defeated Torino on penalties to win the 1979–80 edition.
sentence_47: Roma would reach heights in the league which they had not touched since the 1940s by narrowly and controversially finishing as runners-up to [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]] in [[1980–81_Serie_A|1980–81]].
sentence_48: Former [[A.C._Milan|Milan]] player [[Nils_Liedholm|Nils Liedholm]] was the manager at the time, with players such as [[Bruno_Conti|Bruno Conti]], Agostino Di Bartolomei, [[Roberto_Pruzzo|Roberto Pruzzo]] and [[Paulo_Roberto_Falcão|Falcão]].
sentence_49: The second Scudetto did not elude Roma for much longer.
sentence_50: In [[1982–83_Serie_A|1982–83]], the Roman club won the title for the first time in 41 years, amidst celebrations in the capital.
sentence_51: The [[1983–84_Serie_A|following season]], Roma finished as runners-up in Italy and collected a Coppa Italia title, they also finished as runners-up in the [[UEFA_Champions_League|European Cup]] final of [[1984_European_Cup_Final|1984]].
sentence_52: The European Cup final with [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool]] ended in a 1–1 draw with a goal from Pruzzo, but Roma eventually lost in the penalty shoot-out.
sentence_53: Roma's successful run in the 1980s would finish with a runners-up spot in [[1985–86_Serie_A|1985–86]] and a Coppa Italia victory, beating out [[U.C._Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] 3–2.
sentence_54: After, a comparative decline began in the league, one of the few league highs from the following period being a third-place finish in [[1987–88_Serie_A|1987–88]].
sentence_55: At the start of the 1990s, the club was involved in an all-Italian [[1991_UEFA_Cup_Final|UEFA Cup final]], where they lost 2–1 to [[Inter_Milan|Internazionale]] in [[1990–91_UEFA_Cup|1991]].
sentence_56: The same season, the club won its [[1990–91_Coppa_Italia|seventh]] Coppa Italia and ended runners-up to Sampdoria in the [[Supercoppa_Italiana|Supercoppa Italiana]].
sentence_57: Aside from finishing runners-up to Torino in a Coppa Italia final, the rest of the decade was largely sub-par in the history of Roma, particularly in the league, where the highest they could manage was fourth in [[1997–98_Serie_A|1997–98]].
sentence_58: The early 1990s also saw the emergence of homegrown striker [[Francesco_Totti|Francesco Totti]], who would go on to be an important member of the team and the club's iconic captain.
sentence_59: Roma returned to form in the 2000s, beginning the decade in great style by winning their third ever Serie A title in [[2000–01_Serie_A|2000–01]].
sentence_60: The Scudetto was won on the last day of the season after defeating [[Parma_Calcio_1913|Parma]] 3–1, edging Juventus by two points.
sentence_61: The club's captain, Francesco Totti, was a large reason for the title victory and he would become one of the main heroes in the club's history, going on to break several [[A.S._Roma_statistics_and_records|club records]].
sentence_62: Other important players during this period included [[Aldair|Aldair]], [[Cafu|Cafu]], [[Gabriel_Batistuta|Gabriel Batistuta]] and [[Vincenzo_Montella|Vincenzo Montella]].
sentence_63: The club attempted to defend the title in the [[2001–02_Serie_A|following season]] but ended as runners-up to Juventus by one point.
sentence_64: This would be the start of Roma finishing as runners-up several times in both Serie A and [[Coppa_Italia|Coppa Italia]] during the 2000s – they lost out 4–2 to [[A.C._Milan|Milan]] in the Coppa Italia final of [[2002–03_Coppa_Italia|2003]] and lost to Milan again by finishing second in Serie A for the [[2003–04_Serie_A|2003–04 season]].
sentence_65: The club also re-capitalized several time in 2003–04 season.
sentence_66: In November 2003, €37.5 million was injected by "Roma 2000" to cover the half-year loss and loss carried from previous year.
sentence_67: and again on 30 June for €44.57 million.
sentence_68: Through stock market, a further €19.850 million of new shares issued, and at the year end, the share capital was €19.878 million, which was unchanged as of 2011.
sentence_69: The following season also saw the departure of [[Walter_Samuel|Walter Samuel]] for €25 million and [[Emerson_(footballer,_born_1976)|Emerson]] for €28 million, which decreased the strength of the squad.
sentence_70: The Giallorossi therefore finished in eighth place, one of the worst of recent seasons.
sentence_71: On 9 July 2006, Roma's Francesco Totti, [[Daniele_De_Rossi|Daniele De Rossi]] and [[Simone_Perrotta|Simone Perrotta]] were part of the Italy national team which defeated [[France_national_football_team|France]] in the [[2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Final|2006 FIFA World Cup Final]].
sentence_72: A Serie A scandal was revealed during 2006; Roma were not one of the teams involved.
sentence_73: After punishments were issued, Roma was re-classified as runners-up for [[2005–06_Serie_A|2005–06]], the same season they finished second in the Coppa Italia losing to Internazionale.
sentence_74: In the two following seasons, [[2006–07_Serie_A|2006–07]] and [[2007–08_Serie_A|2007–08]], Roma finished as Serie A runners-up, meaning that in the 2000s, Roma have finished in the top two positions more than any other decade in their history.
sentence_75: Meanwhile, in the UEFA Champions League during both of these seasons, they reached the quarter-finals before going out to [[Manchester_United_F.C.|Manchester United]].
sentence_76: Despite the sloppy start in the [[2008–09_UEFA_Champions_League|2008–09 Champions League]], Roma managed to reach the knockout stage ahead of [[Chelsea_F.C.|Chelsea]] in their group, thus finishing for the first time in their history as winners of the group stage.
sentence_77: However, the Giallorossi, would lose to [[Arsenal_F.C.|Arsenal]] in the knockout stage on penalty kicks, ending their Champions League campaign.
sentence_78: After a disappointing start to the [[2009–10_A.S._Roma_season|2009–10 season]], [[Claudio_Ranieri|Claudio Ranieri]] replaced [[Luciano_Spalletti|Luciano Spalletti]] as head coach.
sentence_79: At the time of the switch, Roma lay bottom of the Serie A table after losses to Juventus and [[Genoa_C.F.C.|Genoa]].
sentence_80: Despite this setback, Roma would later embark on an incredible unbeaten streak of 24 matches in the league – with the last of the 24 being a 2–1 win over rivals Lazio, whereby Roma came from 1–0 down at half-time to defeat their city rivals after Ranieri courageously substituted both Totti and De Rossi at the interval.
sentence_81: The Giallorossi were on top of the table at one point, before a loss to Sampdoria later in the season.
sentence_82: Roma would finish runners-up to Internazionale yet again in both Serie A and the Coppa Italia.
sentence_83: This rounded out a highly successful decade in Roma's history, following somewhat mediocre results of the 1990s.
sentence_84: During the 2000s, Roma had finally recaptured the Scudetto, two Coppa Italia trophies, and their first two Supercoppa Italiana titles.
sentence_85: Other notable contributions to the club's history have included a return to the Champions League quarter-finals (in the [[2006–07_UEFA_Champions_League|2006–07]] and [[2007–08_UEFA_Champions_League|2007–08]] editions) since 1984, six runners up positions in the league, four Coppa Italia finals and three Supercoppa finals – marking Roma's greatest ever decade.
sentence_86: In the summer of 2010, the Sensi family agreed to relinquish their control of Roma as part of a debt-settlement agreement.
sentence_87: This brought an end to the presidential reign of the Sensi family, who had presided over the club since 1993.
sentence_88: Until a new owner was appointed, Rosella Sensi would continue her directorial role of the club.
sentence_89: The [[2010–11_A.S._Roma_season|2010–11 season]] had once again seen Roma start off with mixed fortunes on both a domestic and European level.
sentence_90: These included losses against [[Cagliari_Calcio|Cagliari]], [[Brescia_Calcio|Brescia]] and a 2–0 defeat against [[FC_Bayern_Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the group stages of the Champions League, a match which saw manager [[Claudio_Ranieri|Claudio Ranieri]] openly criticized by his players.
sentence_91: However, these were accompanied by victories against Inter and a sensational victory against Bayern Munich in the return fixture, which saw Roma fight back from 0–2 down at half-time to emerge as 3–2 winners.
sentence_92: Following a series of poor results which saw Roma engage in a winless-streak of five consecutive matches, Ranieri resigned as head coach in February 2011, and former striker [[Vincenzo_Montella|Vincenzo Montella]] was appointed as caretaker manager until the end of the season.
sentence_93: It was also during this season that Roma icon Francesco Totti scored his 200th Serie A goal against [[ACF_Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in March 2011, becoming only the sixth ever player to achieve such a feat.
sentence_94: On 16 April 2011, the takeover contract was closed with an American investment group led by [[Thomas_R._DiBenedetto|Thomas R. DiBenedetto]], with [[James_Pallotta|James Pallotta]], Michael Ruane and Richard D'Amore as partners.
sentence_95: DiBenedetto became the 22nd president of the club, serving from 27 September 2011 to 27 August 2012 and was succeeded by Pallotta.
sentence_96: The new intermediate holding company, NEEP Roma Holding, was 60% owned by American's "AS Roma SPV, LLC" and the rest (40%) was retained by the creditor of Sensi, [[UniCredit|UniCredit]].
sentence_97: In turn, NEEP owned all shares held previously by Sensi (about 67%) with the rest free float in the stock market.
sentence_98: UniCredit later disinvested NEEP Roma Holding to sell to "AS Roma SPV, LLC" and Pallotta.
sentence_99: The new ownership immediately went into effect by making significant changes in the club, hiring [[Walter_Sabatini|Walter Sabatini]] as director of football and former [[Spain_national_football_team|Spanish international]] and [[FC_Barcelona_B|Barcelona B]] coach [[Luis_Enrique_(footballer)|Luis Enrique]] as manager.
sentence_100: The first high-profile player signings from the duo were attacking midfielder [[Erik_Lamela|Erik Lamela]] from [[Club_Atlético_River_Plate|River Plate]], forward [[Bojan_Krkić|Bojan]] from [[FC_Barcelona|Barcelona]], goalkeeper [[Maarten_Stekelenburg|Maarten Stekelenburg]] from [[AFC_Ajax|Ajax]] and unattached defender [[Gabriel_Heinze|Gabriel Heinze]].
sentence_101: The club also sold and released defender [[John_Arne_Riise|John Arne Riise]], goalkeeper [[Doni_(footballer)|Doni]] and forwards [[Jérémy_Ménez|Jérémy Ménez]] and [[Mirko_Vučinić|Mirko Vučinić]].
sentence_102: At the financial level, the company had recapitalised for more than €100 million, the last recapitalisation occurring in the early 2000s.
sentence_103: Roma, however, was eliminated from [[2011–12_UEFA_Europa_League|2011–12 UEFA Europa League]] play-off round.
sentence_104: After the formal takeover on 18 August, Roma bought forward [[Dani_Osvaldo|Dani Osvaldo]], midfielders [[Miralem_Pjanić|Miralem Pjanić]] and [[Fernando_Gago|Fernando Gago]] and defender [[Simon_Kjær|Simon Kjær]], as well as youngster [[Fabio_Borini|Fabio Borini]], which cost the club more than €40 million.
sentence_105: In 2012, Pallotta became the new president.
sentence_106: The 2012–13 pre-season started with the June hiring of former manager [[Zdeněk_Zeman|Zdeněk Zeman]].
sentence_107: Zeman replaced Luis Enrique who resigned at the end of the 2011–12 season.
sentence_108: Luis Enrique's lone season reign had seen the disappointing loss to Slovan Bratislava in the [[2011–12_UEFA_Europa_League|UEFA Europa League]], as well as the inability to qualify for international competitions for the 2012–13 season.
sentence_109: Roma eventually finished seventh, losing the [[2012–13_UEFA_Europa_League|Europa League]] chase to rivals Lazio, [[S.S.C._Napoli|Napoli]] and Internazionale.
sentence_110: Zeman brought back his high-scoring 4–3–3 formation and his hard working ethic which successfully guided former team [[Delfino_Pescara_1936|Pescara]] to the Serie A.
sentence_111: However, he was sacked on 2 February 2013.
sentence_112: He was replaced by caretaker manager [[Aurelio_Andreazzoli|Aurelio Andreazzoli]], whose reign saw the continuation of a disappointing season, with the team ending up in sixth place in Serie A, while also losing 1–0 to rivals Lazio in the [[2012–13_Coppa_Italia|Coppa Italia]] final.
sentence_113: As a result, Roma missed out on European competition for the second-straight season.
sentence_114: On 12 June 2013, Pallotta announced that [[Rudi_Garcia|Rudi Garcia]] had been appointed the new manager of Roma.
