sentence_115: He enjoyed a fantastic start to his Roma career, winning his first ten matches (an all-time Serie A record) including a 2–0 derby win against Lazio, a 0–3 victory away to Internazionale and a 2–0 home win over title rivals Napoli.
sentence_116: During this run, Roma scored 24 times while conceding just once, away to Parma.
sentence_117: The 2013–14 season saw one of Roma's best ever in Serie A, the club tallying an impressive 85 points and finishing second to Juventus, who won the league with a record-breaking 102 points.
sentence_118: Roma's defence was significantly better than in previous seasons, with only 25 goals conceded and a total of 21 clean sheets, including nine in their first ten matches.
sentence_119: In 2014–15, Roma finished second behind Juventus for the second consecutive season after a poor run of form in 2015.
sentence_120: At the end of season the club was sanctioned for loss making and breaking UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations.
sentence_121: On 13 January 2016, Garcia was sacked after a run of one win in seven Serie A matches.
sentence_122: [[Luciano_Spalletti|Luciano Spalletti]] was subsequently appointed manager of Roma for his second spell.
sentence_123: On 21 February, Totti publicly criticised Spalletti due to his own lack of playing-time since returning from injury.
sentence_124: Consequently, Totti was subsequently dropped by Spalletti for Roma's 5–0 win over [[U.S._Città_di_Palermo|Palermo]], with the decision causing an uproar among the fans and in the media.
sentence_125: After their initial disagreements, Spalletti began to use Totti as an immediate impact substitute, which proved to be an effective decision, as the Roma number 10 rediscovered his form and contributed with four goals and one assist after coming off the bench in five consecutive Serie A matches.
sentence_126: As a result, Spalletti was able to lead Roma from a mid-table spot to a third-place finish in [[2015–16_Serie_A|Serie A]], clinching the [[2016–17_UEFA_Champions_League|UEFA Champions League]] play-off spot.
sentence_127: During the summer of 2016, Roma lost star midfielder [[Miralem_Pjanić|Miralem Pjanić]] to rivals Juventus to improve its financial position.
sentence_128: On 27 April 2017, Roma appointed [[Sevilla_FC|Sevilla FC]]'s Sporting director [[Monchi|Monchi]] as their new sporting director.
sentence_129: On 28 May 2017, on the last day of the [[2016–17_A.S._Roma_season|2016–17 season]], Francesco Totti made his 786th and final appearance for Roma before retiring in a 3–2 home win against [[Genoa_C.F.C.|Genoa]], coming on as a substitute for [[Mohamed_Salah|Mohamed Salah]] in the 54th minute and received a standing ovation from the fans.
sentence_130: The win saw Roma finish second in Serie A behind Juventus.
sentence_131: Following Totti's retirement, [[Daniele_De_Rossi|Daniele De Rossi]] became club captain and signed a new two-year contract.
sentence_132: On 13 June 2017, former Roma player [[Eusebio_Di_Francesco|Eusebio Di Francesco]] was appointed as the club's new manager, replacing Spalletti, who had left the club to take charge of Internazionale.
sentence_133: Roma again lost a key player during the summer transfer window, with [[Mohamed_Salah|Mohamed Salah]] joining [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool F.C.]] for a fee of 39m euro (£34m).
sentence_134: Several new players joined the club, including a club record deal for [[Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] striker [[Patrik_Schick|Patrik Schick]] and [[Aleksandar_Kolarov|Aleksandar Kolarov]] in a €5m (£4.4m) move from [[Manchester_City_F.C.|Manchester City]] Di Francesco also brought in [[Gregoire_Defrel|Gregoire Defrel]] from his previous club [[Sassuolo_Calcio|Sassuolo]] in an €18 million deal.
sentence_135: On 5 December 2017 the [[Stadio_della_Roma|Stadio della Roma]] project, after experiencing five years worth of delays due to conflicting interests from various parties in the Roman city government, was given the go-ahead to begin construction.
sentence_136: It is slated to open in time for the 2020–21 season and will replace the Stadio Olimpico as Roma's ground.
sentence_137: In the [[2017–18_UEFA_Champions_League|2017–18 UEFA Champions League]] group stage, Roma were drawn in a tough Group C with [[Chelsea_F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Atlético_Madrid|Atletico Madrid]] and [[Qarabağ_FK|Qarabag]].
sentence_138: However, after performing strongly in the group stage, including a 3–0 home victory against Chelsea, Roma progressed to the knockout stages as Group C winners after [[Diego_Perotti|Diego Perotti]]'s lone goal in a 1–0 win over Qarabag.
sentence_139: After progressing past [[Shakhtar_Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in the Round of 16, Roma were drawn against [[FC_Barcelona|FC Barcelona]] in the quarter-finals.
sentence_140: On 4 April 2018, Roma were defeated 4–1 away to Barcelona at the [[Camp_Nou|Camp Nou]] in the first leg, after own goals from [[Daniele_De_Rossi|Daniele De Rossi]] and [[Kostas_Manolas|Kostas Manolas]], although [[Edin_Džeko|Edin Džeko]] provided a late glimmer of hope by scoring an away goal.
sentence_141: On 10 April, Roma pulled off a sensational second-leg comeback at the Stadio Olimpico to beat Barcelona 3-0 and reach the Champions League semi-finals on away goals.
sentence_142: An early goal from [[Edin_Džeko|Edin Džeko]] and a 58th-minute penalty from De Rossi had left the Giallorossi needing to score one more goal to progress before Manolas scored the crucial third goal, heading in at the near post with eight minutes remaining.
sentence_143: By doing so, Roma became only the third team in Champions League history to overturn a first-leg defeat of three goals or more and reached the final four of the competition for the first time since [[1983–84_European_Cup|1984]].
sentence_144: Roma were subsequently drawn against [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool]], the team that had defeated them in the [[1984_European_Cup_Final|1984 European Cup Final]], in the semi-finals.
sentence_145: Liverpool would go on to win the tie 7–6 on aggregate.
sentence_146: Roma ended the 2017–2018 season in 3rd place on 77 points, qualifying for the following seasons Champions League.
sentence_147: In the summer of 2018, Roma were busy in the transfer market, in large parts thanks to the €83 million they received from reaching the Champions League semi finals, as well as selling Alisson for a world record €72 million including bonuses to Liverpool.
sentence_148: In a very busy window, Roma spent €150 million to sign the likes of Shick, Nzonzi, Pastore, Kluivert, Defrel and more, while selling their 2 starting midfielders from the previous season, Nainggolan and Strootman.
sentence_149: The 2018-2019 Serie A season was a disappointment for Roma as they spent the first half of the season bouncing between 6th and 10th place.
sentence_150: This was compounded by the fact that many of the new signings failed to make an impact.
sentence_151: After Roma were eliminated against Porto 4–3 on aggregate in the Champions League round of 16, Di Francesco was sacked and replaced by Claudio Ranieri who served as caretaker manager.
sentence_152: The following day, sporting director Monchi stepped down.
sentence_153: He stated: "I left Roma for a simple reason: I realized that the owners' ideas were different to mine.
sentence_154: The President thought it was better to go to the right, I thought it was better to go to the left".
sentence_155: James Pallotta hit back saying "I gave him [Monchi] 100 percent control to appoint the coach he wanted, to employ the assistant coaches and the performance staff, to manage the scouting and to bring in the players he wanted.
sentence_156: If you look at our results and our performances, it's clear that this hasn't worked.
sentence_157: He asked me to trust him and let him do it his way.
sentence_158: We gave him complete control and now we have more injuries than we've ever had and are in danger of missing out on finishing in the top 3 for the first time since 2014."
sentence_159: In Monchi's 2 years at the club, he spent £208 million on 21 signings, however within 2 years, only 12 of his signings remained at the club.
sentence_160: Under Ranieri results improved, however Roma failed to qualify for the Champions League, finishing in 6th place on 66 points.
sentence_161: On 11 June 2019, Roma appointed Paulo Fonseca as their new manager.
sentence_162: In December 2019, AS Roma SPV LLC was in final negotiations to sell the team for $872 million, to American businessman [[Dan_Friedkin|Dan Friedkin]], however negotiations stalled during the [[COVID-19_pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]].
sentence_163: On August 6, 2020, Friedkin signed the preliminary contract to agree to pay $591 million to Pallotta, the main shareholder of Roma.
sentence_164: Roma's colours of [[Carmine_(color)|carmine red]] with a [[Golden_yellow|golden yellow]] trim represents the traditional colours of Rome, the official seal of the [[Comune_di_Roma|Comune di Roma]] features the same colours.
sentence_165: The gold and the purple-red represent [[Roman_Empire|Roman imperial]] dignity.
sentence_166: White shorts and black socks are usually worn with the red shirt, however in particularly high key matches, the shorts and socks are the same colour as the home shirt.
sentence_167: The kit itself was originally worn by [[Roman_F.C.|Roman Football Club]]; one of the three clubs who merged to form the current incarnation in 1927.
sentence_168: Because of the colours they wear, Roma are often nicknamed i giallorossi meaning the yellow-reds.
sentence_169: Roma's away kit is traditionally white, with a third kit changing colour from time to time.
sentence_170: A popular nickname for the club is "i lupi" ("the wolves") – the animal has always featured on the club's badge in different forms throughout their history.
sentence_171: The emblem of the team is currently the one which was used when the club was first founded.
sentence_172: It portrays the female wolf with the two infant brothers [[Romulus_and_Remus|Romulus and Remus]], illustrating the [[Founding_of_Rome|myth of the founding of Rome]], superimposed on a bipartite golden yellow over maroon red shield.
sentence_173: In the myth from which the club takes their nickname and logo, the twins (sons of [[Mars_(god)|Mars]] and [[Rhea_Silvia|Rhea Silvia]]) are thrown into the river [[Tiber|Tiber]] by their uncle [[Amulius|Amulius]].
sentence_174: A she-wolf then saved the twins and looked after them.
sentence_175: Eventually, the two twins took revenge on Amulius before falling-out themselves – [[Romulus|Romulus]] killed [[Remus|Remus]] and was thus made king of a new city named in his honour, Rome.

sentence_176: Main articles: Stadio Olimpico, [[Campo_Testaccio|Campo Testaccio]], [[Stadio_Nazionale_PNF|Stadio Nazionale PNF]], and [[Stadio_Flaminio|Stadio Flaminio]]
sentence_177: The first sport facility Roma used was the Motovelodromo Appio, previously used by [[S.S._Alba-Audace_Roma|Alba-Audace]].
sentence_178: Roma only played the [[1927–28_Divisione_Nazionale|1927–28 season]] there until they moved to [[Campo_Testaccio|Campo Testaccio]] the very next season.
sentence_179: Campo Testaccio was used through 1929 to 1940.
sentence_180: The team moved later to the [[Stadio_Nazionale_PNF|Stadio Nazionale del PNF]], where they spent 13 years before moving once again.
sentence_181: In the 1953–54 season, Roma moved to the Olympic arena, Stadio Olimpico, which it shares with Lazio.
sentence_182: The arena has undergone several changes over the years.
sentence_183: The most significant change took place in the nineties when Stadio Olimpico was demolished and then reconstructed to for the [[1990_FIFA_World_Cup|1990 FIFA World Cup]], held in Italy.
sentence_184: Roma have played almost every season since 1953–54, with exception of the 1989–90 seasons due to the reconstruction of Stadio Olimpico.
sentence_185: That year, Roma played its home matches at [[Stadio_Flaminio|Stadio Flaminio]].
sentence_186: On 30 December 2012, Roma club president [[James_Pallotta|James Pallotta]] announced the construction of a new stadium in the [[Tor_di_Valle|Tor di Valle]] area of Rome.
sentence_187: The new stadium, [[Stadio_della_Roma|Stadio della Roma]], will have a capacity of 52,500 spectators.
sentence_188: On 2 February 2017, the [[Lazio|Region of Lazio]] and the mayor of Rome rejected the proposal to build a new stadium.
sentence_189: However, it was later approved on 24 February after final review of the stadium's design adjustments.
sentence_190: In August 2017, the stadium suffered another delay, forcing Roma to renew their lease with the Stadio Olimpico until 2020.
sentence_191: It is presently uncertain when the stadium will open.
sentence_192: On 5 December 2017 the [[Stadio_della_Roma|Stadio della Roma]] project, after experiencing five years worth of delays due to conflicting interests from various parties in the Roman city government, was given the go-ahead to begin construction.
sentence_193: It is slated to open in time for the 2020–21 season and will replace the Stadio Olimpico as Roma's ground.
sentence_194: As of 2020, the club has yet to be given the go ahead to build a new stadium.

sentence_195: A sports centre located in at kilometre 3600 in south-east of Rome was purchased on 22 July 1977 by then club president Gaetano Anzalone.
sentence_196: It was opened on 23 July 1979 as Anzalone's final act as president.
sentence_197: The complex had its first expansion in 1984 when the club was handled by Dino Viola and another in 1998 under the chairmanship of Franco Sensi.
sentence_198: The centre's official name is the Fulvio Bernardini di Trigoria, named after club icon [[Fulvio_Bernardini|Fulvio Bernardini]].
sentence_199: The centre is also known for hosting the [[Argentina_national_football_team|Argentina national team]] during the [[1990_FIFA_World_Cup|1990 FIFA World Cup]], held in Italy.
sentence_200: Roma is the fifth-most supported football club in Italy – behind Juventus, Internazionale, [[A.C._Milan|A.C.
sentence_201: Milan]] and [[S.S.C._Napoli|Napoli]] – with approximately 7% of Italian football fans supporting the club, according to the Doxa Institute-L'Espresso's research of April 2006.
sentence_202: Historically, the largest section of Roma supporters in the city of Rome have come from the [[Inner_city|inner-city]], especially [[Testaccio|Testaccio]].
sentence_203: The traditional [[Ultras|ultras]] group of the club was Commando Ultrà Curva Sud commonly abbreviated as CUCS.
sentence_204: This group was founded by the merger of many smaller groups and was considered one of the most historic in the history of [[European_football|European football]].
sentence_205: However, by the mid-1990s, CUCS had been usurped by rival factions and ultimately broke up.
sentence_206: Since that time, the [[Curva_(stadia)|Curva]] Sud of the Stadio Olimpico has been controlled by more right-wing groups, including A.S. Roma Ultras, Boys and Giovinezza, among others.
sentence_207: However, the oldest group, Fedayn, is apolitical, and politics is not the main identity of Roma, just a part of their overall identity.
sentence_208: Besides ultras groups, it is believed Roma fans support the [[Left-wing_politics|left]] as opposed to Lazio supporters, which are notoriously proud of their right-wing affiliation.
sentence_209: In November 2015, Roma's ultras and their Lazio counterparts boycotted Roma's 1–0 victory in the [[Derby_della_Capitale|Derby della Capitale]] in protest at new safety measures imposed at the Stadio Olimpico.
sentence_210: The measures – imposed by Rome's prefect, Franco Gabrielli – had involved plastic glass dividing walls being installed in both the Curva Sud and Curva Nord, splitting the sections behind each goal in two.
sentence_211: Both sets of ultras continued their protests for the rest of the season, including during Roma's 4–1 victory in the return fixture.
sentence_212: Lazio's ultras returned to the Curva Nord for Roma's 1–4 victory in December 2016, but the Roma ultras continue to boycott matches.
sentence_213: The most known club anthem is "Roma (non-si discute, si ama)", also known as "Roma Roma", by singer [[Antonello_Venditti|Antonello Venditti]].
sentence_214: The title roughly means, "Roma is not to be questioned, it is to be loved," and it is sung before each match.
sentence_215: The song "Grazie Roma", by the same singer, is played at the end of victorious home matches.
sentence_216: Recently, the main riff of [[The_White_Stripes|The White Stripes]]' song "[[Seven_Nation_Army|Seven Nation Army]]" has also become widely popular at matches.
sentence_217: In Italian football, Roma is a club with many rivalries; first and foremost is their rivalry with Lazio, the club with whom they share the Stadio Olimpico.
sentence_218: The derby between the two is called the [[Derby_della_Capitale|Derby della Capitale]], it is amongst the most heated and emotional footballing rivalries in the world.
sentence_219: The fixture has seen some occasional instances of violence in the past, including the death of Lazio fan Vincenzo Paparelli in [[1979–80_Serie_A|1979–80]] as a result of an [[Flare_gun|emergency flare]] fired from the Curva Sud, and the abandonment of a match in March 2004 following unfounded rumours of a fatality which led to violence outside the stadium.
sentence_220: Against Napoli, Roma also compete in the [[Derby_del_Sole|Derby del Sole]], meaning the "Derby of the Sun".
sentence_221: Nowadays, fans also consider other Serie A giants like Juventus (a rivalry born especially in the 1980s), Milan and Internazionale (increased in recent years) among their rivals, as these four compete for the top four spots in the league table to secure a spot in the UEFA Champions League.
sentence_222: Rivalries with other teams have escalated into serious violence.
sentence_223: A group of ultras who label themselves the Fedayn — 'the devotees' — after a group of long-forgotten Iranian guerrilla fighters are regarded to be responsible for the organised hooliganism.
sentence_224: In 2014 Daniele De Santis, a Roma ultra, was convicted of shooting Ciro Esposito and two others during clashes with Napoli fans who were in Rome for their club's [[2014_Coppa_Italia_Final|Coppa Italia final]] against Fiorentina.
sentence_225: Esposito died of his wounds.
sentence_226: De Santis was sentenced to 26 years in prison, later reduced to 16 years on appeal.
sentence_227: Roma ultras have displayed banners celebrating De Santis.
sentence_228: There have been multiple instances of Roma [[Ultras|ultras]] attacking supporters of foreign clubs when playing in Rome.
sentence_229: These attacks have regularly featured the Roma ultras using knives, poles, flares, bottles and stones on unarmed foreign supporters, resulting in multiple hospitalisations.
sentence_230: Home games against Liverpool in 1984 and 2001, Middlesbrough in 2006, [[2007_A.S._Roma–Manchester_United_F.C._conflict|Manchester United in 2007]], Arsenal in 2009, Tottenham Hotspur in 2012, and Chelsea in 2017 have all resulted in multiple stabbings and other injuries to foreign supporters.
sentence_231: In 2018 Roma ultras travelling to an away game at Liverpool attacked home supporters, resulting in a home supporter being critically injured.

sentence_259: [[Francesco_Totti|Francesco Totti]] currently holds Roma's official appearance record, having made 786 appearances in all competitions, over the course of 25 seasons from 1993 until 2017.
sentence_260: He also holds the record for Serie A appearances with 619, as he passed [[Giacomo_Losi|Giacomo Losi]] on 1 March 2008 during a home match against Parma.
sentence_261: Including all competitions, Totti is the all-time leading goalscorer for Roma with 307 goals since joining the club, 250 of which were scored in Serie A (another Roma record).
sentence_262: [[Roberto_Pruzzo|Roberto Pruzzo]], who was the all-time topscorer since 1988, comes in second in all competitions with 138.

sentence_264: Not only was Volk the league's top scorer that year, he also set a Roma record for most goals scored in a season which would later be matched by [[Edin_Džeko|Edin Džeko]] in [[2016–17_A.S._Roma_season|2016–17]].
sentence_265: Its major founders Fortitudo and Alba having been relegated at the end of 1926–27 campaign, new-founded Roma had to take part to Southern First Division championship (Serie B) for its inaugural season.
sentence_266: Nevertheless, the FIGC decided on a special enlargement of first level division re-admitting AS Roma and SSC Napoli.

title: Azerbaijan
sentence_0: This article is about the independent country in the Caucasus.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Azerbaijan_(disambiguation)|Azerbaijan (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: Azerbaijan ([[British_English|UK]]: [[English|/ˌæzərbaɪˈdʒɑːn, -ˈʒɑːn/]] (listen), [[American_English|US]]: [[English|/ˌɑːzərbaɪˈdʒɑːn, ˌæz-/]]; [[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]]: Azərbaycan [[Azerbaijani|[ɑːzæɾbɑjˈd͡ʒɑn]]), officially the Republic of Azerbaijan ([[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]]: Azərbaycan Respublikası [[Azerbaijani|[ɑːzæɾbɑjˈd͡ʒɑn ɾespublikɑˈsɯ]]), is a country in the [[Transcaucasia|Caucasus]] region of [[Eurasia|Eurasia]].
sentence_3: Located at the crossroads of [[Eastern_Europe|Eastern Europe]] and [[Western_Asia|Western Asia]], it is bounded by the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] to the east, the [[Russia|Russian]] republic of [[Dagestan|Dagestan]] to the north, [[Georgia_(country)|Georgia]] to the northwest, [[Armenia|Armenia]] and [[Turkey|Turkey]] to the west, and [[Iran|Iran]] to the south.
sentence_4: The [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] proclaimed its independence from the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] in 1918 and became the first secular democratic Muslim-majority state.
sentence_5: In 1920, the country was incorporated into the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]] as the [[Azerbaijan_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic]].
sentence_6: The modern Republic of Azerbaijan proclaimed its independence on 30 August 1991, shortly before the dissolution of the USSR in the same year.
sentence_7: In September 1991, the Armenian majority of the disputed [[Nagorno-Karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]] region seceded to form the [[Republic_of_Artsakh|Republic of Artsakh]].
sentence_8: The region and [[Armenian-controlled_territories_surrounding_Nagorno-Karabakh|seven surrounding districts]], internationally recognized as part of Azerbaijan pending a solution to the status of the Nagorno-Karabakh through negotiations facilitated by the [[OSCE|OSCE]], became de facto independent with the end of the [[First_Nagorno-Karabakh_War|First Nagorno-Karabakh War]] in 1994.
sentence_9: Following the [[2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_war|2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war]], the seven districts and parts of [[Nagorno-Karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]] were returned to Azerbaijani rule.
sentence_10: Azerbaijan is a [[Unitary_state|unitary]] semi-presidential [[Republic|republic]].
sentence_11: It is one of six independent [[List_of_Turkic_dynasties_and_countries#Current_independent_states|Turkic states]] and an active member of the [[Turkic_Council|Turkic Council]] and the [[International_Organization_of_Turkic_Culture|TÜRKSOY]] community.
sentence_12: Azerbaijan has diplomatic relations with 182 countries and holds membership in 38 international organizations, including the [[United_Nations|United Nations]] (since 1992), the [[Council_of_Europe|Council of Europe]], the [[Non-Aligned_Movement|Non-Aligned Movement]], the [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|OSCE]], and the [[NATO|NATO]] [[Partnership_for_Peace|Partnership for Peace]] (PfP) program.
sentence_13: It is one of the founding members of [[GUAM_Organization_for_Democracy_and_Economic_Development|GUAM]], the [[Commonwealth_of_Independent_States|Commonwealth of Independent States]] (CIS) and the [[Organisation_for_the_Prohibition_of_Chemical_Weapons|Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons]].
sentence_14: Azerbaijan also holds observer status in the [[World_Trade_Organization|World Trade Organization]].
sentence_15: While around 97% of the population is [[Muslim|Muslim]], the [[Constitution_of_Azerbaijan|Constitution of Azerbaijan]] does not declare an official religion and all major political forces in the country are [[Secularism|secularist]].
sentence_16: Azerbaijan is a [[Developing_country|developing country]] and ranks 87th on the [[Human_Development_Index|Human Development Index]].
sentence_17: It has a high rate of [[Economic_development|economic development]] and [[Literacy_rate|literacy]], as well as a low rate of [[List_of_countries_by_unemployment_rate|unemployment]].
sentence_18: However, the ruling party, the [[New_Azerbaijan_Party|New Azerbaijan Party]], in power since 1993, has been accused of authoritarian leadership and the deterioration of the country's [[Human_rights_in_Azerbaijan|human rights record]], including increasing restrictions on civil liberties, particularly on [[Media_freedom_in_Azerbaijan|press freedom]] and political repression.
sentence_19: Further information: [[Atropatene|Atropatene]], [[Caucasian_Albania|Caucasian Albania]], and [[Azerbaijan_(toponym)|Azerbaijan (toponym)]]
sentence_20: According to a modern etymology, the term Azerbaijan derives from that of [[Atropates|Atropates]], a [[Persian_people|Persian]] [[Satrap|satrap]] under the [[Achaemenid_Empire|Achaemenid Empire]], who was later reinstated as the satrap of [[Medes|Media]] under [[Alexander_the_Great|Alexander the Great]].
sentence_21: The original etymology of this name is thought to have its roots in the once-dominant [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]].
sentence_22: In the [[Avesta|Avesta]]'s Frawardin [[Yasht|Yasht]] ("Hymn to the Guardian Angels"), there is a mention of âterepâtahe ashaonô fravashîm ýazamaide, which literally translates from [[Avestan|Avestan]] as "we worship the [[Fravashi|fravashi]] of the holy [[Atropatene|Atropatene]]."
sentence_23: The name "Atropates" itself is the Greek transliteration of an Old Iranian, probably [[Median_language|Median]], compounded name with the meaning "Protected by the (Holy) Fire" or "The Land of the (Holy) Fire".
sentence_24: The Greek name was mentioned by [[Diodorus_Siculus|Diodorus Siculus]] and [[Strabo|Strabo]].
sentence_25: Over the span of millennia, the name evolved to Āturpātākān ([[Middle_Persian|Middle Persian]]), then to Ādharbādhagān, Ādharbāyagān, Āzarbāydjān (New Persian) and present-day Azerbaijan.
sentence_26: The name Azerbaijan was first adopted for the area of the present-day Republic of Azerbaijan by the government of [[Musavat|Musavat]] in 1918, after the [[Russian_Revolution|collapse of the Russian Empire]], when the independent [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] was established.
sentence_27: Until then, the designation had been used exclusively to identify the [[Azerbaijan_(Iran)|adjacent region of contemporary northwestern Iran]], while the area of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic was formerly referred to as [[Arran_(Caucasus)|Arran]] and [[Shirvan|Shirvan]].
sentence_28: On that basis Iran protested the newly adopted country name.
sentence_29: During the Soviet rule, the country was also spelled in Latin from the [[Russian_transliteration|Russian transliteration]] as Azerbaydzhan (Russian: Азербайджа́н).
sentence_30: The country's name was also spelled in Cyrillic script from 1940 to 1991 as "Азәрбајҹан".
sentence_31: Main article: [[History_of_Azerbaijan|History of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_32: Further information: [[Caucasian_Albania|Caucasian Albania]]
sentence_33: The earliest evidence of human settlement in the territory of Azerbaijan dates back to the late [[Stone_Age|Stone Age]] and is related to the [[Guruchay_culture|Guruchay culture]] of [[Azokh_Cave|Azokh Cave]].
sentence_34: Early settlements included the [[Scythia|Scythians]] during the 9th century BC.
sentence_35: Following the Scythians, Iranian [[Medes|Medes]] came to dominate the area to the south of the [[Aras_(river)|Aras river]].
sentence_36: The Medes forged a vast empire between 900 and 700 BC, which was integrated into the [[Achaemenid_Empire|Achaemenid Empire]] around 550 BC.
sentence_37: The area was conquered by the Achaemenids leading to the spread of [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]].

section_3.value: From the Sasanid period to the Safavid period

sentence_38: The [[Sasanian_Empire|Sasanian Empire]] turned [[Caucasian_Albania|Caucasian Albania]] into a vassal state in 252, while King [[Urnayr|Urnayr]] officially adopted [[Christianity|Christianity]] as the state religion in the 4th century.
sentence_39: Despite Sassanid rule, [[Caucasian_Albania|Albania]] remained an entity in the region until the 9th century, while fully subordinate to Sassanid Iran, and retained its monarchy.
sentence_40: Despite being one of the chief vassals of the Sasanian emperor, the Albanian king had only a semblance of authority, and the Sasanian [[Marzban|marzban]] (military governor) held most civil, religious, and military authority.
sentence_41: In the first half of the 7th century, [[Caucasian_Albania|Caucasian Albania]], as a vassal of the Sasanians, came under nominal Muslim rule due to the [[Muslim_conquest_of_Persia|Muslim conquest of Persia]].
sentence_42: The [[Umayyad_Caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]] repulsed both the Sasanians and [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantines]] from [[Transcaucasia|Transcaucasia]] and turned [[Caucasian_Albania|Caucasian Albania]] into a vassal state after Christian resistance led by King [[Javanshir|Javanshir]], was suppressed in 667.
sentence_43: The power vacuum left by the decline of the [[Abbasid_Caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]] was filled by numerous local dynasties such as the [[Sallarid_dynasty|Sallarids]], [[Sajid_dynasty|Sajids]], and [[Shaddadids|Shaddadids]].
sentence_44: At the beginning of the 11th century, the territory was gradually seized by the waves of [[Oghuz_Turks|Oghuz Turks]] from [[Central_Asia|Central Asia]], who adopted a [[Turkoman_(ethnonym)|Turkoman]] ethnonym at the time.
sentence_45: The first of these Turkic dynasties established was the [[Seljuk_Empire|Seljuk Empire]], who entered the area now known as Azerbaijan by 1067.
sentence_46: The pre-Turkic population that lived on the territory of modern Azerbaijan spoke several [[Indo-European_languages|Indo-European]] and Caucasian languages, among them [[Armenian_language|Armenian]] and an [[Iranian_languages|Iranian language]], [[Old_Azeri_language|Old Azeri]], which was gradually replaced by a [[Turkic_languages|Turkic language]], the early precursor of the [[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani language]] of today.
sentence_47: Some linguists have also stated that the [[Tat_language_(Caucasus)|Tati dialects]] of [[Azerbaijan_(Iran)|Iranian Azerbaijan]] and the Republic of Azerbaijan, like those spoken by the [[Tat_people_(Caucasus)|Tats]], are descended from Old Azeri.
sentence_48: Locally, the possessions of the subsequent Seljuk Empire were ruled by [[Eldiguzids|Eldiguzids]], technically vassals of the Seljuk sultans, but sometimes de facto rulers themselves.
sentence_49: Under the Seljuks, local poets such as [[Nizami_Ganjavi|Nizami Ganjavi]] and [[Khaqani|Khaqani]] gave rise to a blossoming of [[Persian_literature|Persian literature]] on the territory of present-day Azerbaijan.
sentence_50: The local dynasty of the [[Shirvanshah|Shirvanshahs]] became a [[Vassal|vassal]] state of [[Timurid_Empire|Timur's Empire]], and assisted him in his war with the ruler of the [[Golden_Horde|Golden Horde]] [[Tokhtamysh|Tokhtamysh]].
sentence_51: Following Timur's death, two independent and rival states emerged: [[Kara_Koyunlu|Kara Koyunlu]] and [[Aq_Qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]].
sentence_52: The Shirvanshahs returned, maintaining for numerous centuries to come a high degree of autonomy as local rulers and vassals as they had done since 861.
sentence_53: In 1501, the [[Safavid_dynasty|Safavid dynasty]] of Iran subdued the Shirvanshahs and gained its possessions.
sentence_54: In the course of the next century, the Safavids [[Safavid_conversion_of_Iran_to_Shia_Islam|converted the formerly Sunni population to Shia Islam]], as they did with the population in what is modern-day Iran.
sentence_55: The Safavids allowed the Shirvanshahs to remain in power, under Safavid suzerainty, until 1538, when Safavid king [[Tahmasp_I|Tahmasp I]] (r. 1524–1576) completely deposed them, and made the area into the Safavid province of [[Safavid_Shirvan|Shirvan]].
sentence_56: The Sunni Ottomans briefly managed to occupy parts of present-day Azerbaijan as a result of the [[Ottoman-Safavid_War_(1578-1590)|Ottoman-Safavid War of 1578–1590]]; by the early 17th century, they were ousted by Safavid Iranian ruler [[Abbas_I_of_Persia|Abbas I]] (r. 1588–1629).
sentence_57: In the wake of the demise of the Safavid Empire, Baku and its environs were briefly occupied by the Russians as a consequence of the [[Russo-Persian_War_(1722–23)|Russo-Persian War of 1722–1723]].
sentence_58: Despite brief intermissions such as these by Safavid Iran's neighboring rivals, the land of what is today Azerbaijan remained under Iranian rule from the earliest advent of the Safavids up to the course of the 19th century.
sentence_59: Main articles: [[Russo-Persian_Wars|Russo-Persian Wars]], [[Treaty_of_Gulistan|Treaty of Gulistan]], and [[Treaty_of_Turkmenchay|Treaty of Turkmenchay]]
sentence_60: See also: [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]], [[Azerbaijan_SSR|Azerbaijan SSR]], and [[Operation_Edelweiss|Operation Edelweiss]]
sentence_61: After the [[Safavid|Safavids]], the area was ruled by the Iranian [[Afsharid_dynasty|Afsharid dynasty]].
sentence_62: After the death of [[Nader_Shah|Nader Shah]] (r. 1736–1747), many of his former subjects capitalized on the eruption of instability.
sentence_63: Numerous self-ruling [[Khanates_of_the_Caucasus|khanates]] with various forms of autonomy emerged in the area.
sentence_64: The rulers of these khanates were directly related to the ruling dynasties of Iran, and were [[Vassals|vassals]] and [[Commoners|subjects]] of the Iranian shah.
sentence_65: The khanates exercised control over their affairs via international trade routes between Central Asia and the West.
sentence_66: Thereafter, the area was under the successive rule of the Iranian [[Zand_dynasty|Zands]] and [[Qajar_dynasty|Qajars]].
sentence_67: From the late 18th century, Imperial Russia switched to a more aggressive geo-political stance towards its two neighbors and rivals to the south, namely Iran and the Ottoman Empire.
sentence_68: Russia now actively tried to gain possession of the Caucasus region which was, for the most part, in the hands of Iran.
sentence_69: In 1804, the Russians [[Battle_of_Ganja_(1804)|invaded and sacked the Iranian town of Ganja]], sparking the [[Russo-Persian_War_(1804–13)|Russo-Persian War of 1804–1813]].
sentence_70: The militarily superior Russians ended the Russo-Persian War of 1804–1813 with a victory.
sentence_71: Following Qajar Iran's loss in the 1804–1813 war, it was forced to concede suzerainty over most of the khanates, along with Georgia and Dagestan to the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]], per the [[Treaty_of_Gulistan|Treaty of Gulistan]].
sentence_72: The area to the north of the river [[Aras_River|Aras]], amongst which territory lies the contemporary Republic of Azerbaijan, was Iranian territory until it was occupied by Russia in the 19th century.
sentence_73: About a decade later, in violation of the Gulistan treaty, the Russians invaded Iran's [[Erivan_Khanate|Erivan Khanate]].
sentence_74: This sparked the final bout of hostilities between the two, the [[Russo-Persian_War_(1826-1828)|Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828]].
sentence_75: The resulting [[Treaty_of_Turkmenchay|Treaty of Turkmenchay]], forced [[Qajar_dynasty|Qajar Iran]] to cede sovereignty over the Erivan Khanate, the [[Nakhchivan_Khanate|Nakhchivan Khanate]] and the remainder of the [[Lankaran_Khanate|Lankaran Khanate]], comprising the last parts of the soil of the contemporary Azerbaijani Republic that were still in Iranian hands.
sentence_76: After incorporation of all Caucasian territories from Iran into Russia, the new border between the two was set at the [[Aras_River|Aras River]], which, upon the Soviet Union's disintegration, subsequently became part of the border between Iran and the Azerbaijan Republic.
sentence_77: Qajar Iran was forced to cede its Caucasian territories to Russia in the 19th century, which thus included the territory of the modern-day Azerbaijan Republic, while as a result of that cession, the [[Azerbaijanis|Azerbaijani ethnic group]] is nowadays parted between two nations: Iran and Azerbaijan.
sentence_78: Nevertheless, the number of ethnic Azerbaijanis in Iran far outnumber those in neighboring Azerbaijan.
sentence_79: After the collapse of the Russian Empire during [[World_War_I|World War I]], the short-lived [[Transcaucasian_Democratic_Federative_Republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] was declared, constituting the present-day republics of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Armenia.
sentence_80: It was followed by the [[March_Days|March Days]] massacres that took place between 30 March and 2 April 1918 in the city of [[Baku|Baku]] and adjacent areas of the [[Baku_Governorate|Baku Governorate]] of the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]].
sentence_81: When the republic dissolved in May 1918, the leading [[Musavat|Musavat]] party declared independence as the [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] (ADR), adopting the name of "Azerbaijan" for the new republic; a name that prior to the proclamation of the ADR was solely used to refer to the adjacent [[Iranian_Azerbaijan|northwestern region of contemporary Iran]].
sentence_82: The ADR was the first modern parliamentary republic in the Muslim world.
sentence_83: Among the important accomplishments of the Parliament was the extension of suffrage to women, making Azerbaijan the first Muslim nation to grant women equal political rights with men.
sentence_84: Another important accomplishment of ADR was the establishment of [[Baku_State_University|Baku State University]], which was the first modern-type university founded in the Muslim East.
sentence_85: By March 1920, it was obvious that Soviet Russia would attack Baku.
sentence_86: [[Vladimir_Lenin|Vladimir Lenin]] said that the invasion was justified as [[Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic|Soviet Russia]] could not survive without Baku's [[Petroleum_industry_in_Azerbaijan|oil]].
sentence_87: Independent Azerbaijan lasted only 23 months until the [[Bolshevik|Bolshevik]] [[11th_Soviet_Red_Army|11th Soviet Red Army]] invaded it, establishing the [[Azerbaijan_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Azerbaijan SSR]] on 28 April 1920.
sentence_88: Although the bulk of the newly formed Azerbaijani army was engaged in putting down an Armenian revolt that had just broken out in [[Karabakh|Karabakh]], Azerbaijanis did not surrender their brief independence of 1918–20 quickly or easily.
sentence_89: As many as 20,000 Azerbaijani soldiers died resisting what was effectively a Russian reconquest.
sentence_90: On 13 October 1921, the Soviet republics of Russia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia signed an agreement with Turkey known as the [[Treaty_of_Kars|Treaty of Kars]].
sentence_91: The previously independent [[Republic_of_Aras|Republic of Aras]] would also become the [[Nakhichevan_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Nakhichevan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic]] within the Azerbaijan SSR by the treaty of Kars.
sentence_92: On the other hand, [[Armenia|Armenia]] was awarded the region of [[Syunik_Province|Zangezur]] and Turkey agreed to return [[Gyumri|Gyumri]] (then known as Alexandropol).
sentence_93: During [[World_War_II|World War II]], Azerbaijan played a crucial role in the strategic energy policy of the Soviet Union, with 80 percent of the Soviet Union's oil on the [[Eastern_Front_(World_War_II)|Eastern Front]] being supplied by Baku.
sentence_94: By the Decree of the [[Supreme_Soviet_of_the_USSR|Supreme Soviet of the USSR]] in February 1942, the commitment of more than 500 workers and employees of the [[Petroleum_industry|oil industry]] of Azerbaijan were awarded orders and medals.
sentence_95: [[Operation_Edelweiss|Operation Edelweiss]] carried out by the German [[Wehrmacht|Wehrmacht]] targeted Baku because of its importance as the energy (petroleum) dynamo of the USSR.
sentence_96: A fifth of all Azerbaijanis fought in the Second World War from 1941 to 1945.
sentence_97: Approximately 681,000 people with over 100,000 of them women went to the front, while the total population of Azerbaijan was 3.4 million at the time.
sentence_98: Some 250,000 people from Azerbaijan were killed on the front.
sentence_99: More than 130 Azerbaijanis were named [[Hero_of_the_Soviet_Union|Heroes of the Soviet Union]].
sentence_100: Azerbaijani Major-General [[Azi_Aslanov|Azi Aslanov]] was twice awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union.
sentence_101: Following the politics of glasnost, initiated by [[Mikhail_Gorbachev|Mikhail Gorbachev]], civil unrest and ethnic strife grew in various regions of the Soviet Union, including [[Nagorno-Karabakh_Autonomous_Oblast|Nagorno-Karabakh]], an autonomous region of the Azerbaijan SSR.
sentence_102: The disturbances in Azerbaijan, in response to Moscow's indifference to an already heated conflict, resulted in calls for independence and secession, which culminated in the [[Black_January|Black January]] events in Baku.
sentence_103: Later in 1990, the Supreme Council of the Azerbaijan SSR dropped the words "Soviet Socialist" from the title, adopted the "Declaration of Sovereignty of the Azerbaijan Republic" and restored the flag of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic as the state flag.
sentence_104: As a consequence of the [[1991_Soviet_coup_d'état_attempt|failed coup which occurred in August in Moscow]], on 18 October 1991, the Supreme Council of Azerbaijan adopted a Declaration of Independence which was affirmed by a nationwide referendum in December 1991, while the Soviet Union officially ceased to exist on 26 December 1991.
sentence_105: The country now celebrates its [[Independence_Day_(Azerbaijan)|Independence Day]] on 18 October.
sentence_106: The early years of independence were overshadowed by the [[First_Nagorno-Karabakh_war|First Nagorno-Karabakh war]] with the ethnic Armenian majority of Nagorno-Karabakh backed by Armenia.
sentence_107: By the end of the hostilities in 1994, Armenians controlled up to 14–16 percent of Azerbaijani territory, including Nagorno-Karabakh itself.
sentence_108: During the war many atrocities were committed including the [[Massacre|massacres]] at [[Malibeyli_and_Gushchular_Massacre|Malibeyli and Gushchular]], the [[Garadaghly_Massacre|Garadaghly massacre]], the and the [[Khojaly_massacre|Khojaly massacres]].
sentence_109: Furthermore, an estimated 30,000 people have been killed and more than a million people have been displaced.
sentence_110: Four [[United_Nations_Security_Council|United Nations Security Council]] Resolutions ([[United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_822|822]], [[United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_853|853]], [[United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_874|874]], and [[United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_884|884]]) demand for "the immediate withdrawal of all Armenian forces from all occupied territories of Azerbaijan."
sentence_111: Many Russians and Armenians left and fled Azerbaijan as refugees during the 1990s.
sentence_112: According to the 1970 census, there were 510,000 ethnic [[Russian_diaspora|Russians]] and 484,000 Armenians in Azerbaijan.
sentence_113: In 1993, democratically elected president [[Abulfaz_Elchibey|Abulfaz Elchibey]] was overthrown by a military insurrection led by Colonel [[Surat_Huseynov|Surat Huseynov]], which resulted in the rise to power of the former leader of [[Azerbaijan_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Soviet Azerbaijan]], [[Heydar_Aliyev|Heydar Aliyev]].
sentence_114: In 1994, Surat Huseynov, by that time the prime minister, attempted another military coup against Heydar Aliyev, but he was arrested and charged with treason.
sentence_115: A year later, in 1995, another [[1995_Azerbaijani_coup_d'état_attempt|coup]] was attempted against Aliyev, this time by the commander of the [[OMON|OMON]] special unit, Rovshan Javadov.
sentence_116: The coup was averted, resulting in the killing of the latter and disbanding of Azerbaijan's OMON units.
sentence_117: At the same time, the country was tainted by rampant corruption in the governing bureaucracy.
sentence_118: In October 1998, Aliyev was reelected for a second term.
sentence_119: Despite the much improved economy, particularly with the exploitation of the [[Azeri-Chirag-Guneshli|Azeri-Chirag-Guneshli oil field]] and [[Shah_Deniz_gas_field|Shah Deniz gas field]], Aliyev's presidency was criticized due to suspected election frauds, high levels of economic inequality and [[Corruption_in_Azerbaijan|domestic corruption]].
sentence_120: [[Ilham_Aliyev|Ilham Aliyev]], Heydar Aliyev's son, became chairman of the [[New_Azerbaijan_Party|New Azerbaijan Party]] as well as [[President_of_Azerbaijan|President of Azerbaijan]] when his father died in 2003.
sentence_121: He was [[Azerbaijani_presidential_election,_2013|reelected to a third term]] as president in October 2013.
sentence_122: On 27 September 2020, new clashes in the unresolved [[Nagorno-Karabakh_conflict|Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]] resumed along the [[Nagorno-Karabakh_Line_of_Contact|Nagorno-Karabakh Line of Contact]].
sentence_123: Both the armed forces of Azerbaijan and Armenia reported military and civilian casualties.
sentence_124: The [[2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_ceasefire_agreement|Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire agreement]] and the end of the six-week [[2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_war|war between Azerbaijan and Armenia]] was seen as a victory and was widely celebrated in Azerbaijan.
sentence_125: Main articles: [[Geography_of_Azerbaijan|Geography of Azerbaijan]], [[Environment_of_Azerbaijan|Environment of Azerbaijan]], [[State_reserves_of_Azerbaijan|State reserves of Azerbaijan]], and National parks of Azerbaijan
sentence_126: See also: [[Extreme_points_of_Azerbaijan|Extreme points of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_127: Geographically, Azerbaijan is located in the [[South_Caucasus|South Caucasus]] region of [[Eurasia|Eurasia]], straddling [[Southwest_Asia|Western Asia]] and Eastern Europe.
sentence_128: It lies between latitudes [[38th_parallel_north|38°]] and [[42nd_parallel_north|42° N]], and longitudes [[44th_meridian_east|44°]] and [[51st_meridian_east|51° E]].
sentence_129: The total length of Azerbaijan's [[List_of_land_border_lengths|land borders]] is 2,648 km (1,645 mi), of which 1,007 kilometers are with Armenia, 756 kilometers with Iran, 480 kilometers with Georgia, 390 kilometers with Russia and 15 kilometers with Turkey.
sentence_130: The [[Coast|coastline]] stretches for 800 km (497 mi), and the length of the widest area of the Azerbaijani section of the Caspian Sea is 456 km (283 mi).
sentence_131: The territory of Azerbaijan extends 400 km (249 mi) from north to south, and 500 km (311 mi) from west to east.
sentence_132: Three physical features dominate Azerbaijan: the Caspian Sea, whose shoreline forms a natural boundary to the east; the Greater Caucasus mountain range to the north; and the extensive flatlands at the country's center.
sentence_133: There are also three mountain ranges, the Greater and [[Lesser_Caucasus|Lesser Caucasus]], and the [[Talysh_Mountains|Talysh Mountains]], together covering approximately 40% of the country.
sentence_134: The highest peak of Azerbaijan is [[Mount_Bazardüzü|Mount Bazardüzü]] (4,466 m), while the lowest point lies in the Caspian Sea (−28 m).
sentence_135: Nearly half of all the [[Mud_volcano|mud volcanoes]] on Earth are concentrated in Azerbaijan, [[Mud_volcanoes_in_Azerbaijan|these volcanoes]] were also among nominees for the [[New7Wonders_of_Nature|New7Wonders of Nature]].
sentence_136: The main water sources are surface waters.
sentence_137: However, only 24 of the 8,350 rivers are greater than 100 km (62 mi) in length.
sentence_138: All the rivers drain into the Caspian Sea in the east of the country.
sentence_139: The largest lake is [[Lake_Sarysu|Sarysu]] (67 km), and the longest river is [[Kura_(Caspian_Sea)|Kur]] (1,515 km), which is [[Transboundary_river|transboundary]] with [[Armenia|Armenia]].
sentence_140: Azerbaijan has several islands along the Caspian sea, mostly located in the [[Baku_Archipelago|Baku Archipelago]].
sentence_141: Since the independence of Azerbaijan in 1991, the Azerbaijani government has taken measures to preserve the environment of Azerbaijan.
sentence_142: National protection of the environment accelerated after 2001 when the state budget increased due to new revenues provided by the [[Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan_pipeline|Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline]].
sentence_143: Within four years protected areas doubled and now makeup eight percent of the country's territory.
sentence_144: Since 2001 the government has set up seven large reserves and almost doubled the sector of the budget earmarked for environmental protection.
sentence_145: Main articles: [[Orography_of_Azerbaijan|Orography of Azerbaijan]], [[Climate_of_Azerbaijan|Climate of Azerbaijan]], and [[Water_bodies_of_Azerbaijan|Water bodies of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_146: Azerbaijan is home to a vast variety of landscapes.
sentence_147: Over half of Azerbaijan's landmass consists of mountain ridges, crests, highlands, and plateaus which rise up to hypsometric levels of 400–1000 meters (including the Middle and Lower lowlands), in some places (Talis, Jeyranchol-Ajinohur and Langabiz-Alat foreranges) up to 100–120 meters, and others from 0–50 meters and up ([[Qobustan,_Absheron|Qobustan, Absheron]]).
sentence_148: The rest of Azerbaijan's terrain consists of plains and lowlands.
sentence_149: Hypsometric marks within the Caucasus region vary from about −28 meters at the Caspian Sea shoreline up to 4,466 meters (Bazardüzü peak).
sentence_150: The formation of climate in Azerbaijan is influenced particularly by cold [[Arctic|arctic]] [[Air_mass|air masses]] of Scandinavian [[Anticyclone|anticyclone]], temperate air masses of [[Siberia|Siberian]] anticyclone, and Central Asian anticyclone.
sentence_151: Azerbaijan's diverse landscape affects the ways air masses enter the country.
sentence_152: The Greater Caucasus protects the country from direct influences of cold air masses coming from the north.
sentence_153: That leads to the formation of [[Subtropics|subtropical climate]] on most foothills and plains of the country.
sentence_154: Meanwhile, plains and foothills are characterized by high [[Sunlight|solar radiation]] rates.
sentence_155: 9 out of 11 existing [[Köppen_climate_classification|climate zones]] are present in Azerbaijan.
sentence_156: Both the absolute minimum temperature ( −33 °C or −27.4 °F ) and the absolute maximum temperature ( 46 °C or 114.8 °F ) were observed in [[Julfa_Rayon|Julfa]] and [[Ordubad_Rayon|Ordubad]] – regions of [[Nakhchivan_Autonomous_Republic|Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic]].
sentence_157: The maximum annual [[Precipitation_(meteorology)|precipitation]] falls in [[Lankaran|Lankaran]] (1,600 to 1,800 mm or 63 to 71 in) and the minimum in Absheron (200 to 350 mm or 7.9 to 13.8 in).
sentence_158: Rivers and lakes form the principal part of the water systems of Azerbaijan, they were formed over a long geological timeframe and changed significantly throughout that period.
sentence_159: This is particularly evidenced by remnants of ancient rivers found throughout the country.
sentence_160: The country's water systems are continually changing under the influence of natural forces and human introduced industrial activities.
sentence_161: Artificial rivers (canals) and ponds are a part of Azerbaijan's water systems.
sentence_162: In terms of water supply, Azerbaijan is below the average in the world with approximately 100,000 cubic metres (3,531,467 cubic feet) per year of water per square kilometer.
sentence_163: All big [[Reservoir|water reservoirs]] are built on Kur.
sentence_164: The hydrography of Azerbaijan basically belongs to the [[Caspian_Sea_basin|Caspian Sea basin]].
sentence_165: The [[Kura_(Caspian_Sea)|Kura]] and [[Aras_River|Aras]] are the major rivers in Azerbaijan, they run through the [[Kura-Aras_Lowland|Kura-Aras Lowland]].
sentence_166: The rivers that directly flow into the Caspian Sea, originate mainly from the north-eastern slope of the Major Caucasus and [[Talysh_Mountains|Talysh Mountains]] and run along the Samur–Devechi and Lankaran lowlands.
sentence_167: [[Yanar_Dag|Yanar Dag]], translated as "burning mountain", is a natural gas fire which blazes continuously on a hillside on the [[Absheron_Peninsula|Absheron Peninsula]] on the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] near [[Baku|Baku]], which itself is known as the "land of fire."
sentence_168: Flames jet out into the air from a thin, porous sandstone layer.
sentence_169: It is a tourist attraction to visitors to the Baku area.
sentence_170: Main article: [[Wildlife_of_Azerbaijan|Wildlife of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_171: Further information: [[Fauna_of_Azerbaijan|Fauna of Azerbaijan]] and [[Flora_of_Azerbaijan|Flora of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_172: The first reports on the richness and diversity of animal life in Azerbaijan can be found in travel notes of Eastern travelers.
sentence_173: Animal carvings on architectural monuments, ancient rocks, and stones survived up to the present times.
sentence_174: The first information on the flora and fauna of Azerbaijan was collected during the visits of naturalists to Azerbaijan in the 17th century.
sentence_175: There are 106 species of mammals, 97 species of fish, 363 species of birds, 10 species of amphibians and 52 species of reptiles which have been recorded and classified in Azerbaijan.
sentence_176: The national animal of Azerbaijan is the Karabakh horse, a mountain-steppe racing and riding horse endemic to Azerbaijan.
sentence_177: The Karabakh horse has a reputation for its good temper, speed, elegance and intelligence.
sentence_178: It is one of the oldest breeds, with ancestry dating to the ancient world.
sentence_179: However, today the horse is an endangered species.
sentence_180: Azerbaijan's flora consists of more than 4,500 species of [[Higher_plants|higher plants]].
sentence_181: Due to the unique climate in Azerbaijan, the flora is much richer in the number of species than the flora of the other republics of the South Caucasus.
sentence_182: 66 percent of the species growing in the whole [[Caucasus|Caucasus]] can be found in Azerbaijan.
sentence_183: Main article: Politics of Azerbaijan
sentence_184: See also: [[Elections_in_Azerbaijan|Elections in Azerbaijan]] and [[Human_rights_in_Azerbaijan|Human rights in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_185: The structural formation of Azerbaijan's political system was completed by the adoption of the new [[Constitution_of_Azerbaijan|Constitution]] on 12 November 1995.
sentence_186: According to Article 23 of the Constitution, the state symbols of the Azerbaijan Republic are the [[Flag_of_Azerbaijan|flag]], the [[Coat_of_arms_of_Azerbaijan|coat of arms]], and the [[National_Anthem_of_the_Republic_of_Azerbaijan|national anthem]].
sentence_187: The state power in Azerbaijan is limited only by law for internal issues, but for international affairs is additionally limited by the provisions of international agreements.
sentence_188: The Constitution of Azerbaijan states that it is a presidential republic with three branches of power – Executive, Legislative, and Judicial.
sentence_189: The legislative power is held by the [[Unicameralism|unicameral]] [[National_Assembly_of_Azerbaijan|National Assembly]] and the Supreme National Assembly in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.
sentence_190: The Parliament of Azerbaijan, called Milli Majlis, consists of 125 deputies elected based on majority vote, with a term of 5 years for each elected member.
sentence_191: The elections are held every five years, on the first Sunday of November.
sentence_192: The Parliament is not responsible for the formation of the government, but the Constitution requires the approval of the Cabinet of Ministers by Milli Majlis.
sentence_193: The [[New_Azerbaijan_Party|New Azerbaijan Party]], and independents loyal to the ruling government, currently hold almost all of the Parliament's 125 seats.
sentence_194: During the [[Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010|2010 Parliamentary election]], the opposition parties, [[Musavat|Musavat]] and Azerbaijani Popular Front Party, failed to win a single seat.
sentence_195: European observers [[Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010#Campaign_irregularities|found numerous irregularities]] in the run-up to the election and [[Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010#Election|on election day]].
sentence_196: The executive power is held by the [[President_of_Azerbaijan|President]], who is elected for a seven-year term by direct elections, and the [[Prime_Minister_of_Azerbaijan|Prime Minister]].
sentence_197: The president is authorized to form the Cabinet, a collective executive body, accountable to both the President and the National Assembly.
sentence_198: The Cabinet of Azerbaijan consists primarily of the prime minister, his deputies, and ministers.
sentence_199: The president does not have the right to dissolve the National Assembly but has the right to veto its decisions.
sentence_200: To override the presidential veto, the parliament must have a majority of 95 votes.
sentence_201: The judicial power is vested in the [[Constitutional_Court_of_Azerbaijan|Constitutional Court]], [[Supreme_Court_of_Azerbaijan|Supreme Court]], and the Economic Court.
sentence_202: The president nominates the judges in these courts.
sentence_203: The [[European_Commission_for_the_Efficiency_of_Justice|European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice]] (CEPEJ) report refers to the Azerbaijani justice model on the selection of new judges as best practice, reflecting the particular features and the course of development towards ensuring the independence and quality of the judiciary in a new democracy.
sentence_204: Azerbaijan's system of governance nominally can be called two-tiered.
sentence_205: The top or highest tier of the government is the Executive Power headed by President.
sentence_206: The President appoints the Cabinet of Ministers and other high-ranking officials.
sentence_207: The Local Executive Authority is merely a continuation of Executive Power.
sentence_208: The legal status of local state administration in Azerbaijan is determined by the Provision on Local Executive Authority (Yerli Icra Hakimiyati), adopted 16 June 1999.
sentence_209: In June 2012, the President approved the new Regulation, which granted additional powers to Local Executive Authorities, strengthening their dominant position in Azerbaijan's local affairs Chapter 9 of the Constitution of the Azerbaijan Republic addresses major issues of local self-government, such as the legal status of municipalities, types of local self-government bodies, their basic powers and relationships to other official entities.
sentence_210: The other nominal tier of governance is municipalities (Bələdiyə) and members of municipalities are elected by a general vote in Municipal elections every five years.
sentence_211: Currently, there are 1,607 municipalities across the country.
sentence_212: The Law on Municipal Elections and the Law on the Status of Municipalities were the first to be adopted in the field of local government (2 July 1999).
sentence_213: The Law on Municipal Service regulates the activities of municipal employees, their rights, duties, labor conditions and social benefits, and outlines the structure of the executive apparatus and the organization of municipal service.
sentence_214: The Law on the Status of Municipalities regulates the role and structure of municipal bodies and outlines state guarantees of legal and financial autonomy.
sentence_215: The law pays special attention to the adoption and execution of municipal programs concerning social protection, social and economic development, and the local environment.
sentence_216: The Security Council is the deliberative body under the president, and he organizes it according to the Constitution.
sentence_217: It was established on 10 April 1997.
sentence_218: The administrative department is not a part of the president's office but manages the financial, technical and pecuniary activities of both the president and his office.
sentence_219: Although Azerbaijan has held several elections since regaining its independence and it has many of the formal institutions of democracy, it remains classified as "not free" (on border with "partly free") by [[Freedom_House|Freedom House]].
sentence_220: In recent years, large numbers of Azerbaijani journalists, bloggers, lawyers, and human rights activists have been rounded up and jailed for their criticism of President Aliyev and government authorities.
sentence_221: A resolution adopted by the European Parliament in September 2015 described Azerbaijan as "having suffered the greatest decline in democratic governance in all of Eurasia over the past ten years," noting as well that its dialogue with the country on human rights has "not made any substantial progress."
sentence_222: On 17 March 2016, the President of Azerbaijan signed a decree pardoning more than a dozen of the persons regarded as political prisoners by some NGOs.
sentence_223: This decree was welcomed as a positive step by the US State Department.
sentence_224: On 16 March 2017 another pardon decree was signed, which led to the release of additional persons regarded as political prisoners.
sentence_225: Azerbaijan has been harshly criticized for bribing foreign officials and diplomats in order to promote its causes abroad and legitimize its elections at home, a practice which has been termed as [[Caviar_diplomacy|Caviar diplomacy]].
sentence_226: However, on 6 March 2017, [[European_strategic_intelligence_and_security_center|ESISC]] (European Strategic Intelligence and Security Center) published a report called "The Armenian Connection", in which it attacked human rights NGOs and research organisations criticising human rights violations and corruption in Azerbaijan.
sentence_227: [[European_strategic_intelligence_and_security_center|ESISC]] in that report asserted that the "Caviar Diplomacy" report elaborated by ESI aimed to create a climate of suspicion based on slander to form a network of MPs that would engage in a political war against Azerbaijan and that the network, composed of European PMs, Armenian officials, and some NGOs (Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, "Human Rights House Foundation", "Open Dialog, European Stability Initiative, and Helsinki Committee for Human Rights) was financed by the Soros Foundation.
sentence_228: According to Robert Coalson (Radio Free Europe), ESISC is a part of Baku's lobbying efforts to extend the use of front think tanks to shift public opinion.
sentence_229: Freedom Files Analytical Centre said that "The report is written in the worst traditions of authoritarian propaganda".
sentence_230: Main article: [[Foreign_relations_of_Azerbaijan|Foreign relations of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_231: See also: [[Azerbaijan_and_the_European_Union|Azerbaijan and the European Union]]
sentence_232: The short-lived Azerbaijan Democratic Republic succeeded in establishing diplomatic relations with six countries, sending diplomatic representatives to Germany and Finland.
sentence_233: The process of international recognition of Azerbaijan's independence from the collapsing Soviet Union lasted roughly one year.
sentence_234: The most recent country to recognize Azerbaijan was Bahrain, on 6 November 1996.
sentence_235: Full diplomatic relations, including mutual exchanges of missions, were first established with Turkey, Pakistan, the United States, Iran and Israel.
sentence_236: Azerbaijan has placed a particular emphasis on its "[[Special_relationship_(international_relations)|special relationship]]" with Turkey.
sentence_237: Azerbaijan has diplomatic relations with 158 countries so far and holds membership in 38 international organizations.
sentence_238: It holds observer status in the [[Non-Aligned_Movement|Non-Aligned Movement]] and [[World_Trade_Organization|World Trade Organization]] and is a correspondent at the [[International_Telecommunication_Union|International Telecommunication Union]].
sentence_239: On 9 May 2006 Azerbaijan was elected to membership in the newly established [[Human_Rights_Council|Human Rights Council]] by the [[United_Nations_General_Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].
sentence_240: The term of office began on 19 June 2006.
sentence_241: Azerbaijan was first elected as a non-permanent member of the [[United_Nations_Security_Council_election,_2011|UN Security Council in 2011]] with the support of 155 countries.
sentence_242: Foreign policy priorities of Azerbaijan include, first of all, the restoration of its territorial integrity; elimination of the consequences of occupation of Nagorno-Karabakh and seven other regions of Azerbaijan surrounding Nagorno-Karabakh; integration into European and Euro-Atlantic structure; contribution to international security; cooperation with international organizations; regional cooperation and bilateral relations; strengthening of defense capability; promotion of security by domestic policy means; strengthening of democracy; preservation of ethnic and religious tolerance; scientific, educational, and cultural policy and preservation of moral values; economic and social development; enhancing internal and border security; and migration, energy, and transportation security policy.
sentence_243: Azerbaijan is an active member of international coalitions fighting international terrorism.
sentence_244: Azerbaijan was one of the first countries to offer support after the [[September_11_attacks|September 11 attacks]].
sentence_245: The country is contributing to peacekeeping efforts in Kosovo, Afghanistan and Iraq.
sentence_246: Azerbaijan is an active member of [[NATO|NATO]]'s [[Partnership_for_Peace|Partnership for Peace]] program.
sentence_247: It also maintains good relations with the [[European_Union|European Union]] and could potentially one day apply for membership.
sentence_248: Main article: [[Administrative_divisions_of_Azerbaijan|Administrative divisions of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_249: Azerbaijan is divided into 10 economic regions; 66 [[Raion|rayons]] (rayonlar, singular rayon) and 77 cities (şəhərlər, singular şəhər) of which 12 are under the direct authority of the republic.
sentence_250: Moreover, Azerbaijan includes the Autonomous Republic (muxtar respublika) of [[Nakhchivan_Autonomous_Republic|Nakhchivan]].
sentence_251: The [[President_of_Azerbaijan|President of Azerbaijan]] appoints the governors of these units, while the government of Nakhchivan is elected and approved by the parliament of Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.
sentence_252: Note: The cities under the direct authority of the republic in italics.
sentence_253: Main article: [[Azerbaijani_Armed_Forces|Azerbaijani Armed Forces]]
sentence_254: The history of the modern Azerbaijan army dates back to [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] in 1918, when the National Army of the newly formed Azerbaijan Democratic Republic was created on 26 June 1918.
sentence_255: When Azerbaijan gained independence after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the Armed Forces of the Republic of Azerbaijan were created according to the Law on the Armed Forces of 9 October 1991.
sentence_256: The original date of the establishment of the short-lived National Army is celebrated as Army Day (26 June) in today's Azerbaijan.
sentence_257: As of 2002, Azerbaijan had 95,000 active personnel in its armed forces.
sentence_258: There are also 17,000 paramilitary troops.
sentence_259: The armed forces have three branches: the Land Forces, the [[Azerbaijani_Air_Forces|Air Forces]] and the [[Azerbaijan_Navy|Navy]].
sentence_260: Additionally the armed forces embrace several military sub-groups that can be involved in state defense when needed.
sentence_261: These are the [[Internal_Troops_(Azerbaijan)|Internal Troops]] of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the [[Azerbaijan_Border_Guard|State Border Service]], which includes the [[Azerbaijan_Coast_Guard|Coast Guard]] as well.
sentence_262: The [[Azerbaijan_National_Guard|Azerbaijan National Guard]] is a further paramilitary force.
sentence_263: It operates as a semi-independent entity of the Special State Protection Service, an agency subordinate to the President.
sentence_264: Azerbaijan adheres to the [[Treaty_on_Conventional_Armed_Forces_in_Europe|Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe]] and has signed all major international arms and weapons treaties.
sentence_265: Azerbaijan closely cooperates with [[NATO|NATO]] in programs such as [[Partnership_for_Peace|Partnership for Peace]] and [[Individual_Partnership_Action_Plan|Individual Partnership Action Plan]].
sentence_266: Azerbaijan has deployed 151 of its Peacekeeping Forces in Iraq and another 184 in Afghanistan.
sentence_267: The defense budget of Azerbaijan for 2011 was set at US$3.1 billion.
sentence_268: In addition to that, $1.36 billion was planned to be used for the needs of the [[Ministry_of_Defence_Industry_of_Azerbaijan|defense industry]], which bring up the total military budget to 4.6 billion.
sentence_269: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev said on 26 June 2011 that the defence spending reached $3.3 billion that year.
sentence_270: Azerbaijan's defense budget for 2013 is $3.7 billion.
sentence_271: Azerbaijani defense industry manufactures small arms, artillery systems, tanks, armors and [[Night_vision_device|noctovision devices]], aviation bombs, pilotless vehicles, various military vehicles and military planes and helicopters.
sentence_272: Main article: [[Economy_of_Azerbaijan|Economy of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_273: After gaining independence in 1991, Azerbaijan became a member of the [[International_Monetary_Fund|International Monetary Fund]], the [[World_Bank|World Bank]], the [[European_Bank_for_Reconstruction_and_Development|European Bank for Reconstruction and Development]], the [[Islamic_Development_Bank|Islamic Development Bank]], and the [[Asian_Development_Bank|Asian Development Bank]].
sentence_274: The banking system of Azerbaijan consists of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan, [[Commercial_bank|commercial banks]] and non-banking credit organizations.
sentence_275: The National (now Central) Bank was created in 1992 based on the Azerbaijan State Savings Bank, an affiliate of the former State Savings Bank of the USSR.
sentence_276: The Central Bank serves as Azerbaijan's central bank, empowered to issue the national currency, the [[Azerbaijani_manat|Azerbaijani manat]], and to supervise all commercial banks.
sentence_277: Two major commercial banks are [[Unibank_(Azerbaijan)|UniBank]] and the state-owned International Bank of Azerbaijan, run by Abbas Ibrahimov.
sentence_278: Pushed up by spending and demand growth, the 2007 Q1 inflation rate reached 16.6%.
sentence_279: Nominal incomes and monthly wages climbed 29% and 25% respectively against this figure, but price increases in the non-oil industry encouraged inflation.
sentence_280: Azerbaijan shows some signs of the so-called "[[Dutch_disease|Dutch disease]]" because of its fast-growing energy sector, which causes inflation and makes non-energy exports more expensive.
sentence_281: In the early 2000s the chronically high inflation was brought under control.
sentence_282: This led to the launch of a new currency, the new Azerbaijani manat, on 1 January 2006, to cement the economic reforms and erase the vestiges of an unstable economy.
sentence_283: In 2008, Azerbaijan was cited as one of the top 10 reformers by the World Bank's [[Doing_Business_Report|Doing Business Report]].
sentence_284: Azerbaijan is also ranked 57th in the [[Global_Competitiveness_Report|Global Competitiveness Report]] for 2010–2011, above other CIS countries.
sentence_285: By 2012 the [[Gross_domestic_product|GDP]] of Azerbaijan had increased 20-fold from its 1995 level.
sentence_286: According to [[World_Bank|World Bank]]'s [[Doing_Business_report|Doing Business report]] 2019, Azerbaijan improved its position in the Ease of doing business rank from 57 to 25.
sentence_287: As a result of implementing a record number of reforms mainly involving institutional changes among the 10 top improvers, to do business in Azerbaijan became easier, such as time and cost to get construction permit reduced significantly (time by 80 days and cost by 12.563 [[Azerbaijani_manat|AZN]]), process of connecting electricity grid rationalized, as well as getting credit simplified.
sentence_288: Main article: [[Energy_in_Azerbaijan|Energy in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_289: Further information: [[Petroleum_industry_in_Azerbaijan|Petroleum industry in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_290: Two-thirds of Azerbaijan is rich in oil and natural gas.
sentence_291: The history of the oil industry of Azerbaijan dates back to the ancient period.
sentence_292: Arabian historian and traveler Ahmed Al-Belaruri discussed the economy of the Absheron peninsula in antiquity, mentioning its oil in particular.
sentence_293: There are many [[Pipelines_in_Azerbaijan|pipelines in Azerbaijan]].
sentence_294: The goal of the [[Southern_Gas_Corridor|Southern Gas Corridor]], which connects the giant [[Shah_Deniz_gas_field|Shah Deniz gas field]] in Azerbaijan to Europe, is to reduce European Union's dependency on Russian gas.
sentence_295: The region of the [[Lesser_Caucasus|Lesser Caucasus]] accounts for most of the country's gold, silver, iron, copper, [[Titanium|titanium]], [[Chromium|chromium]], [[Manganese|manganese]], [[Cobalt|cobalt]], [[Molybdenum|molybdenum]], complex ore and [[Antimony|antimony]].
sentence_296: In September 1994, a 30-year contract was signed between the [[State_Oil_Company_of_Azerbaijan_Republic|State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic]] (SOCAR) and 13 oil companies, among them [[Amoco|Amoco]], [[BP|BP]], [[ExxonMobil|ExxonMobil]], [[Lukoil|Lukoil]] and [[Equinor|Equinor]].
sentence_297: As Western oil companies are able to tap deepwater oilfields untouched by the Soviet exploitation, Azerbaijan is considered one of the most important spots in the world for oil exploration and development.
sentence_298: Meanwhile, the State Oil Fund of Azerbaijan was established as an extra-budgetary fund to ensure [[Macroeconomy|macroeconomic]] stability, transparency in the management of oil revenue, and safeguarding of resources for future generations.
sentence_299: Access to biocapacity in Azerbaijan is less than world average.
sentence_300: In 2016, Azerbaijan had 0.8 global hectares of biocapacity per person within its territory, half the world average of 1.6 global hectares per person.
sentence_301: In 2016 Azerbaijan used 2.1 global hectares of biocapacity per person – their [[Ecological_footprint|ecological footprint]] of consumption.
sentence_302: This means they use more biocapacity than Azerbaijan contains.
sentence_303: As a result, Azerbaijan is running a biocapacity deficit.
sentence_304: Azeriqaz, a sub-company of SOCAR, intends to ensure full gasification of the country by 2021.
sentence_305: Azerbaijan is one of the sponsors of the east–west and north–south energy transport corridors.
sentence_306: [[Baku–Tbilisi–Kars_railway|Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway]] line will connect the Caspian region with Turkey, is expected to be completed in July 2017.
sentence_307: The [[Trans-Anatolian_gas_pipeline|Trans-Anatolian gas pipeline]] (TANAP) and [[Trans_Adriatic_Pipeline|Trans-Adriatic Pipeline]] (TAP) will deliver natural gas from Azerbaijan's Shah Deniz gas to Turkey and Europe.
sentence_308: Azerbaijan extended the agreement on development of [[Azeri–Chirag–Gunashli|ACG]] until 2050 according to the amended [[Production_sharing_agreement|PSA]] signed on 14 September 2017 by [[SOCAR|SOCAR]] and co-ventures ([[BP|BP]], [[Chevron_Corporation|Chevron]], [[Inpex|Inpex]], [[Equinor|Equinor]], [[ExxonMobil|ExxonMobil]], TP, ITOCHU and [[Oil_and_Natural_Gas_Corporation|ONGC Videsh]]).
sentence_309: Main article: Agriculture in Azerbaijan
sentence_310: Azerbaijan has the largest agricultural basin in the region.
sentence_311: About 54.9 percent of Azerbaijan is agricultural land.
sentence_312: At the beginning of 2007 there were 4,755,100 hectares of utilized agricultural area.
sentence_313: In the same year the total wood resources counted 136 million m³.
sentence_314: Azerbaijan's agricultural scientific research institutes are focused on meadows and pastures, horticulture and [[Subtropical|subtropical]] crops, green vegetables, [[Viticulture|viticulture]] and [[Azerbaijani_wine|wine-making]], cotton growing and [[Medicinal_plants|medicinal plants]].
sentence_315: In some areas it is profitable to grow grain, potatoes, [[Sugar_beet|sugar beets]], cotton and tobacco.
sentence_316: Livestock, dairy products, and wine and [[Distilled_spirit|spirits]] are also important farm products.
sentence_317: The Caspian [[Fishing_industry|fishing industry]] concentrates on the dwindling stocks of [[Sturgeon|sturgeon]] and [[Beluga_(sturgeon)|beluga]].
sentence_318: In 2002 the Azerbaijani [[Merchant_marine|merchant marine]] had 54 ships.
sentence_319: Some products previously imported from abroad have begun to be produced locally.
sentence_320: Among them are Coca-Cola by Coca-Cola Bottlers LTD., beer by Baki-Kastel, parquet by Nehir and oil pipes by EUPEC Pipe Coating Azerbaijan.
sentence_321: Main article: [[Tourism_in_Azerbaijan|Tourism in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_322: Tourism is an important part of the [[Economy_of_Azerbaijan|economy of Azerbaijan]].
sentence_323: The country was a well-known tourist spot in the 1980s.
sentence_324: However, the fall of the Soviet Union, and the [[First_Nagorno-Karabakh_War|First Nagorno-Karabakh War]] during the 1990s, damaged the tourist industry and the image of Azerbaijan as a tourist destination.
sentence_325: It was not until the 2000s that the tourism industry began to recover, and the country has since experienced a high rate of growth in the number of tourist visits and overnight stays.
sentence_326: In the recent years, Azerbaijan has also become a popular destination for religious, spa, and [[Azerbaijani_medical_tourism|health care tourism]].
sentence_327: During winter, the [[Shahdag_Mountain_Resort|Shahdag Mountain Resort]] offers skiing with state of the art facilities.
sentence_328: The government of Azerbaijan has set the development of Azerbaijan as an elite tourist destination as a top priority.
sentence_329: It is a national strategy to make tourism a major, if not the single largest, contributor to the Azerbaijani economy.
sentence_330: These activities are regulated by the [[Ministry_of_Culture_and_Tourism_(Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Culture and Tourism of Azerbaijan]].
sentence_331: There are 63 countries which have visa-free score.
sentence_332: E-visa – for a visit of foreigners of visa-required countries to the Republic of Azerbaijan.
sentence_333: According to Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Report 2015 of the World Economic Forum, Azerbaijan holds 84th place.
