sentence_334: According to a report by the World Travel and Tourism Council, Azerbaijan was among the top ten countries showing the strongest growth in visitor exports between 2010 and 2016, In addition, Azerbaijan placed first (46.1%) among countries with the fastest-developing travel and tourism economies, with strong indicators for inbound international visitor spending last year.
sentence_335: Main articles: [[Transportation_in_Azerbaijan|Transportation in Azerbaijan]] and [[Rail_transport_in_Azerbaijan|Rail transport in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_336: The convenient location of Azerbaijan on the crossroad of major international traffic arteries, such as the [[Silk_Road|Silk Road]] and the south–north corridor, highlights the strategic importance of transportation sector for the country's economy.
sentence_337: The transport sector in the country includes roads, railways, aviation, and maritime transport.
sentence_338: Azerbaijan is also an important economic hub in the transportation of raw materials.
sentence_339: The [[Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan_pipeline|Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline]] (BTC) became operational in May 2006 and extends more than 1,774 kilometers through the territories of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey.
sentence_340: The BTC is designed to transport up to 50 million tons of crude oil annually and carries oil from the Caspian Sea oilfields to global markets.
sentence_341: The [[South_Caucasus_Pipeline|South Caucasus Pipeline]], also stretching through the territory of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey, became operational at the end of 2006 and offers additional gas supplies to the European market from the [[Shah_Deniz_gas_field|Shah Deniz gas field]].
sentence_342: Shah Deniz is expected to produce up to 296 billion cubic meters of natural gas per year.
sentence_343: Azerbaijan also plays a major role in the EU-sponsored Silk Road Project.
sentence_344: In 2002, the Azerbaijani government established the Ministry of Transport with a broad range of policy and regulatory functions.
sentence_345: In the same year, the country became a member of the [[Vienna_Convention_on_Road_Traffic|Vienna Convention on Road Traffic]].
sentence_346: Priorities are upgrading the transport network and improving transportation services in order to better facilitate the development of other sectors of the economy.
sentence_347: The 2012 construction of [[Kars–Tbilisi–Baku_railway|Kars–Tbilisi–Baku railway]] was meant to improve transportation between Asia and Europe by connecting the railways of China and Kazakhstan in the east to the European railway system in the west via Turkey.
sentence_348: In 2010 [[Russian_gauge|Broad-gauge]] railways and electrified railways stretched for 2,918 km (1,813 mi) and 1,278 km (794 mi) respectively.
sentence_349: By 2010, there were 35 airports and one [[Heliport|heliport]].
sentence_350: Main articles: Science and technology in Azerbaijan, [[Communications_in_Azerbaijan|Communications in Azerbaijan]], [[Azerbaijan_National_Aerospace_Agency|Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency]], and [[List_of_Azerbaijani_inventions_and_discoveries|List of Azerbaijani inventions and discoveries]]
sentence_351: In the 21st century, a new oil and gas boom helped to improve the situation in Azerbaijan's science and technology sectors, and the government launched a campaign aimed at modernization and [[List_of_Azerbaijani_inventions_and_discoveries|innovation]].
sentence_352: The government estimates that profits from the information technology and communication industry will grow and become comparable to those from oil production.
sentence_353: Azerbaijan has a large and steadily growing Internet sector, mostly uninfluenced by the [[Financial_crisis_of_2007–2008|financial crisis of 2007–2008]]; rapid growth is forecast for at least five more years.
sentence_354: The country has also been making progress in developing its telecoms sector.
sentence_355: The Ministry of Communications & Information Technologies (MCIT), as well as being an operator through its role in Aztelekom, is both a policy-maker and regulator.
sentence_356: Public payphones are available for local calls and require the purchase of a token from the telephone exchange or some shops and kiosks.
sentence_357: Tokens allow a call of indefinite duration.
sentence_358: As of 2009, there were 1,397,000 main telephone lines and 1,485,000 internet users.
sentence_359: There are four [[GSM|GSM]] providers: Azercell, , Azerfon ([[Nar_Mobile|Nar Mobile]]), [[Nakhtel|Nakhtel]] mobile network operators and one [[CDMA|CDMA]].
sentence_360: In the 21st century a number of prominent Azerbaijani [[Geodynamics|geodynamics]] and [[Geotectonics|geotectonics]] scientists, inspired by the fundamental works of Elchin Khalilov and others, designed hundreds of earthquake prediction stations and earthquake-resistant buildings that now constitute the bulk of The Republican Center of Seismic Service.
sentence_361: The [[Azerbaijan_National_Aerospace_Agency|Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency]] launched its first satellite AzerSat 1 into orbit on 7 February 2013 from [[Guiana_Space_Centre|Guiana Space Centre]] in French Guiana at orbital positions 46° East.
sentence_362: The satellite covers Europe and a significant part of Asia and Africa and serves the transmission of TV and radio broadcasting as well as the Internet.
sentence_363: The launching of a satellite into orbit is Azerbaijan's first step in realizing its goal of becoming a nation with its own space industry, capable of successfully implementing more projects in the future.
sentence_364: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Azerbaijan|Demographics of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_365: Further information: [[Ethnic_minorities_in_Azerbaijan|Ethnic minorities in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_366: As of January 2019, 52.8% of Azerbaijan's total population of 9,981,457 is [[Urban_area|urban]], with the remaining 47.2% being rural.
sentence_367: 50.1% of the total population is female.
sentence_368: The [[Human_sex_ratio|sex ratio]] in the same year was 0.99 males per female.
sentence_369: The 2011 population growth-rate was 0.85%, compared to 1.09% worldwide.
sentence_370: A significant factor restricting population growth is a high level of migration.
sentence_371: In 2011 Azerbaijan saw a migration of −1.14/1,000 people.
sentence_372: The [[Azerbaijani_diaspora|Azerbaijani diaspora]] is found in 42 countries and in turn there are many centers for ethnic minorities inside Azerbaijan, including the [[Germans_in_Azerbaijan|German]] cultural society "Karelhaus", [[Slavic_peoples|Slavic]] cultural center, Azerbaijani-Israeli community, [[Kurdish_people|Kurdish]] cultural center, International [[Talysh_people|Talysh]] Association, [[Lezgins|Lezgin]] national center "Samur", Azerbaijani-[[Tatarstan|Tatar]] community, [[Crimean_Tatars|Crimean Tatars]] society, etc.
sentence_373: The ethnic composition of the population according to the 2009 population census: 91.6% [[Azerbaijani_people|Azerbaijanis]], 2.0% [[Lezgians|Lezgians]], 1.4% [[Armenians|Armenians]] (almost all Armenians live in the break-away region of [[Republic_of_Nagorno-Karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]]), 1.3% [[Russians|Russians]], 1.3% [[Talysh_people|Talysh]], 0.6% [[Caucasian_Avars|Avars]], 0.4% [[Turkish_people|Turks]], 0.3% [[Tatars|Tatars]], 0.3% [[Tat_people_(Caucasus)|Tats]], 0.2% [[Ukrainians|Ukrainians]], 0.1% [[Tsakhur_people|Tsakhurs]], 0.1% [[Georgians|Georgians]], 0.1% [[Jew|Jews]], 0.1% [[Kurdish_people|Kurds]], other 0.2%.
sentence_374: Main article: List of cities in Azerbaijan
sentence_375: In total, Azerbaijan has 78 cities, 63 city districts, and one special legal status city.
sentence_376: These are followed by 261 urban-type settlements and 4248 villages.
sentence_377: Main article: [[Languages_of_Azerbaijan|Languages of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_378: The official language is [[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]], which is a [[Turkic_languages|Turkic language]].
sentence_379: Azerbaijani is spoken by approximately 92% of the population as a mother tongue.
sentence_380: Russian and [[Armenian_language|Armenian]] (only in Nagorno-Karabakh) are also spoken, and each are the mother tongue of around 1.5% of the population respectively.
sentence_381: There are a dozen other minority languages spoken natively in the country.
sentence_382: Avar, [[Budukh_language|Budukh]], [[Georgian_language|Georgian]], [[Juhuri_language|Juhuri]], [[Khinalug_language|Khinalug]], [[Kryts_language|Kryts]], [[Lezgian_language|Lezgian]], [[Rutul_language|Rutul]], [[Talysh_language|Talysh]], [[Tat_language_(Caucasus)|Tat]], [[Tsakhur_language|Tsakhur]], and [[Udi_language|Udi]] are all spoken by small minorities.
sentence_383: Some of these language communities are very small and their numbers are decreasing.
sentence_384: Armenian was the majority language in Nagorno-Karabakh with around 76% in 1989.
sentence_385: After the first Nagorno-Karabakh war, the population is almost exclusively Armenian at around 95%.
sentence_386: Main articles: [[Religion_in_Azerbaijan|Religion in Azerbaijan]] and [[Irreligion_in_Azerbaijan|Irreligion in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_387: Azerbaijan is considered the most secular Muslim-majority country.
sentence_388: Around 97% of the population are Muslims.
sentence_389: 85% of the Muslims are [[Shia_Islam|Shia]] and 15% [[Sunni_Muslim|Sunni]]; the Republic of Azerbaijan has the second highest proportion of Shia Muslims of any country in the world.
sentence_390: Other faiths are practised by the country's various ethnic groups.
sentence_391: Under article 48 of its [[Constitution_of_Azerbaijan|Constitution]], Azerbaijan is a secular state and ensures religious freedom.
sentence_392: In a 2006–2008 [[Gallup_(company)|Gallup]] poll, only 21% of respondents from Azerbaijan stated that religion is an important part of their daily lives.
sentence_393: Of the nation's religious minorities, the estimated 280,000 Christians (3.1%) are mostly [[Russian_Orthodox_Church|Russian]] and [[Georgian_Orthodox_Church|Georgian]] [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|Orthodox]] and [[Armenian_Apostolic_Church|Armenian Apostolic]] (almost all Armenians live in the break-away region of Nagorno-Karabakh).
sentence_394: In 2003, there were 250 [[Roman_Catholics|Roman Catholics]].
sentence_395: Other Christian denominations as of 2002 include [[Lutheranism|Lutherans]], [[Baptists|Baptists]] and [[Molokan|Molokans]].
sentence_396: There is also a small [[Protestant|Protestant]] community.
sentence_397: Azerbaijan also has an ancient [[Jewish|Jewish]] population with a [[Mountain_Jews|2,000-year history]]; Jewish organizations estimate that 12,000 Jews remain in Azerbaijan.
sentence_398: Azerbaijan also is home to members of the [[Bahá'í_Faith|Bahá'í]], [[International_Society_for_Krishna_Consciousness|Hare Krishna]] and [[Jehovah's_Witnesses|Jehovah's Witnesses]] communities, as well as adherents of the other religious communities.
sentence_399: Some religious communities have been [[Freedom_of_religion_in_Azerbaijan#Restrictions_on_religious_freedom|unofficially restricted from religious freedom]].
sentence_400: A [[U.S._State_Department|U.S.
sentence_401: State Department]] report on the matter mentions detention of members of certain Muslim and Christian groups, and many groups have difficulty registering with the SCWRA.
sentence_402: Main article: [[Education_in_Azerbaijan|Education in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_403: A relatively high percentage of Azerbaijanis have obtained some form of higher education, most notably in scientific and technical subjects.
sentence_404: In the Soviet era, literacy and average education levels rose dramatically from their very low starting point, despite two changes in the standard alphabet, from [[Perso-Arabic_script|Perso-Arabic script]] to [[Latin_script|Latin]] in the 1920s and from Roman to [[Cyrillic|Cyrillic]] in the 1930s.
sentence_405: According to Soviet data, 100 percent of males and females (ages nine to forty-nine) were literate in 1970.
sentence_406: According to the [[United_Nations_Development_Program|United Nations Development Program]] Report 2009, the literacy rate in Azerbaijan is 99.5 percent.
sentence_407: Since independence, one of the first laws that Azerbaijan's Parliament passed to disassociate itself from the Soviet Union was to adopt a modified-Latin alphabet to replace Cyrillic.
sentence_408: Other than that the Azerbaijani system has undergone little structural change.
sentence_409: Initial alterations have included the reestablishment of religious education (banned during the Soviet period) and curriculum changes that have reemphasized the use of the Azerbaijani language and have eliminated ideological content.
sentence_410: In addition to elementary schools, the education institutions include thousands of preschools, general secondary schools, and vocational schools, including specialized secondary schools and technical schools.
sentence_411: Education through the ninth grade is compulsory.
sentence_412: Main articles: [[Culture_of_Azerbaijan|Culture of Azerbaijan]] and [[Literature_of_Azerbaijan|Literature of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_413: See also: [[UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_List_in_Azerbaijan|UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_414: The culture of Azerbaijan has developed as a result of many influences; that's why Azerbaijanis are, in many ways, bi-cultural.
sentence_415: Today, national traditions are well preserved in the country despite Western influences, including [[Globalization|globalized]] consumer culture.
sentence_416: Some of the main elements of the Azerbaijani culture are: music, literature, folk dances and art, cuisine, architecture, cinematography and [[Novruz_in_Azerbaijan|Novruz Bayram]].
sentence_417: The latter is derived from the traditional celebration of the New Year in the ancient Iranian religion of [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]].
sentence_418: Novruz is a family holiday.
sentence_419: The profile of Azerbaijan's population consists, as stated above, of Azerbaijanis, as well as other nationalities or ethnic groups, compactly living in various areas of the country.
sentence_420: Azerbaijani national and traditional dresses are the [[Chokha|Chokha]] and Papakhi.
sentence_421: There are radio broadcasts in Russian, [[Georgian_language|Georgian]], [[Kurdish_language|Kurdish]], [[Lezgian_language|Lezgian]] and [[Talysh_language|Talysh]] languages, which are financed from the state budget.
sentence_422: Some local radio stations in [[Balakən|Balakan]] and [[Khachmaz_(city)|Khachmaz]] organize broadcasts in Avar and [[Tat_language_(Caucasus)|Tat]].
sentence_423: In Baku several newspapers are published in Russian, Kurdish (Dengi Kurd), Lezgian (Samur) and Talysh languages.
sentence_424: Jewish society "Sokhnut" publishes the newspaper Aziz.
sentence_425: Main articles: [[Music_of_Azerbaijan|Music of Azerbaijan]] and [[Azerbaijani_dances|Azerbaijani dances]]
sentence_426: Music of Azerbaijan builds on [[Folk_music|folk traditions]] that reach back nearly a thousand years.
sentence_427: For centuries Azerbaijani music has evolved under the badge of monody, producing rhythmically diverse melodies.
sentence_428: Azerbaijani music has a branchy [[Musical_mode|mode]] system, where [[Chromaticism|chromatization]] of [[Major_and_minor|major and minor]] [[Musical_scale|scales]] is of great importance.
sentence_429: Among national musical instruments there are 14 string instruments, eight percussion instruments and six wind instruments.
sentence_430: According to [[The_New_Grove_Dictionary_of_Music_and_Musicians|The Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians]], "in terms of ethnicity, culture and religion the Azerbaijani are musically much closer to Iran than Turkey."
sentence_431: [[Mugham|Mugham]], [[Meykhana|meykhana]] and [[Art_of_Azerbaijani_ashiqs|ashiq art]] are among the many musical traditions of Azerbaijan.
sentence_432: Mugham is usually a suite with poetry and instrumental interludes.
sentence_433: When performing mugham, the singers have to transform their emotions into singing and music.
sentence_434: In contrast to the mugham traditions of Central Asian countries, Azerbaijani mugham is more free-form and less rigid; it is often compared to the improvised field of [[Jazz|jazz]].
sentence_435: [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] proclaimed the Azerbaijani mugham tradition a [[Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity|Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity]] on 7 November 2003.
sentence_436: Meykhana is a kind of traditional Azerbaijani distinctive folk unaccompanied song, usually performed by several people improvising on a particular subject.
sentence_437: Ashiq combines poetry, storytelling, dance, and vocal and instrumental music into a traditional performance art that stands as a symbol of Azerbaijani culture.
sentence_438: It is a mystic troubadour or traveling bard who sings and plays the [[Baglama|saz]].
sentence_439: This tradition has its origin in the [[Shamanistic|Shamanistic]] beliefs of ancient [[Turkic_peoples|Turkic peoples]].
sentence_440: Ashiqs' songs are semi-improvised around common bases.
sentence_441: Azerbaijan's ashiq art was included in the list of [[Intangible_Cultural_Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]] by the UNESCO on 30 September 2009.
sentence_442: Since the mid-1960s, Western-influenced [[Azerbaijani_pop_music|Azerbaijani pop music]], in its various forms, that has been growing in popularity in Azerbaijan, while genres such as [[Azerbaijani_rock|rock]] and [[Azerbaijani_hip_hop|hip hop]] are widely produced and enjoyed.
sentence_443: Azerbaijani pop and [[Azerbaijani_folk_music|Azerbaijani folk music]] arose with the international popularity of performers like [[Alim_Qasimov|Alim Qasimov]], Rashid Behbudov, [[Vagif_Mustafazadeh|Vagif Mustafazadeh]], [[Muslim_Magomayev_(musician)|Muslim Magomayev]], [[Shovkat_Alakbarova|Shovkat Alakbarova]] and [[Rubaba_Muradova|Rubaba Muradova]].
sentence_444: Azerbaijan is an enthusiastic participant in the Eurovision Song Contest.
sentence_445: Azerbaijan made its debut appearance at the 2008 [[Eurovision_Song_Contest_2008|Eurovision Song Contest]].
sentence_446: The country's [[Azerbaijan_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2009|entry]] gained third place in 2009 and fifth the following year.
sentence_447: Ell and Nikki won the first place at the [[Eurovision_Song_Contest_2011|Eurovision Song Contest 2011]] with the song "[[Running_Scared_(Eldar_&_Nigar_song)|Running Scared]]", entitling Azerbaijan to host the contest in [[Eurovision_Song_Contest_2012|2012]], in Baku.
sentence_448: They have qualified for every Grand Final up until the [[Eurovision_Song_Contest_2018|2018 edition of the contest]], entering with [[X_My_Heart_(song)|X My Heart]] by singer [[Aisel_(singer)|Aisel]].
sentence_449: There are dozens of Azerbaijani [[Folk_dance|folk dances]].
sentence_450: They are performed at formal celebrations and the dancers wear national clothes like the [[Chokha|Chokha]], which is well-preserved within the national dances.
sentence_451: Most dances have a very fast rhythm.
sentence_452: Main article: [[Azerbaijani_literature|Azerbaijani literature]]
sentence_453: Among the medieval authors born within the territorial limits of modern Azerbaijani Republic was Persian poet and philosopher [[Nizami_Ganjavi|Nizami]], called Ganjavi after his place of birth, [[Ganja,_Azerbaijan|Ganja]], who was the author of the [[Khamseh|Khamseh]] ("The Quintuplet"), composed of five romantic poems, including "The Treasure of Mysteries," "Khosrow and Shīrīn," and "Leyli and Mejnūn."
sentence_454: The earliest known figure in Azerbaijani literature was [[Izzeddin_Hasanoglu|Izzeddin Hasanoglu]], who composed a [[Diwan_(poetry)|divan]] consisting of Persian and Turkic ghazals.
sentence_455: In Persian ghazals he used his pen-name, while his Turkic ghazals were composed under his own name of Hasanoghlu.
sentence_456: Classical literature in Azerbaijani was formed in the 14th century based on the various Early Middle Ages dialects of [[Tabriz|Tabriz]] and [[Shirvan|Shirvan]].
sentence_457: Among the poets of this period were [[Kadi_Burhan_al-Din|Gazi Burhanaddin]], [[Jahan_Shah|Haqiqi]] (pen-name of [[Jahan_Shah|Jahan-shah Qara Qoyunlu]]), and Habibi.
sentence_458: The end of the 14th century was also the period of starting literary activity of [[Nesimi|Imadaddin Nesimi]], one of the greatest [[Turkic_language|Turkic]] [[Hurufi|Hurufi]] [[Mysticism|mystical]] poets of the late 14th and early 15th centuries and one of the most prominent early divan masters in Turkic literary history, who also composed poetry in [[Persian_language|Persian]] and [[Arabic_language|Arabic]].
sentence_459: The divan and ghazal styles were further developed by poets [[Qasem-e_Anvar|Qasem-e Anvar]], [[Fuzûlî|Fuzuli]] and [[Khatai|Khatai]] (pen-name of [[Safavid_dynasty|Safavid]] [[Shah_Ismail_I|Shah Ismail I]]).
sentence_460: The [[Book_of_Dede_Korkut|Book of Dede Korkut]] consists of two manuscripts copied in the 16th century, was not written earlier than the 15th century.
sentence_461: It is a collection of 12 stories reflecting the oral tradition of Oghuz nomads.
sentence_462: The 16th-century poet, Muhammed Fuzuli produced his timeless philosophical and lyrical Qazals in Arabic, Persian, and Azerbaijani.
sentence_463: Benefiting immensely from the fine literary traditions of his environment, and building upon the legacy of his predecessors, Fizuli was destined to become the leading literary figure of his society.
sentence_464: His major works include The Divan of Ghazals and The Qasidas.
sentence_465: In the same century, Azerbaijani literature further flourished with the development of [[Ashik|Ashik]] ([[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]]: Aşıq) poetic genre of bards.
sentence_466: During the same period, under the pen-name of Khatāī ([[Arabic_language|Arabic]]: خطائی‎ for sinner) Shah Ismail I wrote about 1400 verses in Azerbaijani, which were later published as his Divan.
sentence_467: A unique literary style known as qoshma ([[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]]: qoşma for improvization) was introduced in this period, and developed by Shah Ismail and later by his son and successor, Shah [[Tahmasp_I|Tahmasp I]].
sentence_468: In the span of the 17th and 18th centuries, Fizuli's unique genres as well [[Ashik|Ashik]] poetry were taken up by prominent poets and writers such as Qovsi of Tabriz, [[Abbas_II_of_Persia|Shah Abbas Sani]], , Nishat, [[Molla_Vali_Vidadi|Molla Vali Vidadi]], Molla Panah Vagif, Amani, Zafar and others.
sentence_469: Along with [[Turkish_people|Turks]], [[Turkmens|Turkmens]] and [[Uzbeks|Uzbeks]], [[Azerbaijanis|Azerbaijanis]] also celebrate the Epic of Koroglu (from [[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]]: kor oğlu for blind man's son), a legendary folk hero.
sentence_470: Several documented versions of Koroglu epic remain at the Institute for Manuscripts of the [[National_Academy_of_Sciences_of_Azerbaijan|National Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan]].
sentence_471: Modern literature in Azerbaijan is based on the Shirvani dialect mainly, while in Iran it is based on the Tabrizi one.
sentence_472: The first newspaper in Azerbaijani, [[Akinchi|Akinchi]] was published in 1875.
sentence_473: In the mid-19th century, it was taught in the schools of [[Baku|Baku]], [[Ganja_(city)|Ganja]], [[Shaki,_Azerbaijan|Shaki]], [[Tbilisi|Tbilisi]], and [[Yerevan|Yerevan]].
sentence_474: Since 1845, it was also taught in the University of Saint Petersburg in Russia.
sentence_475: Main article: [[Azerbaijani_folk_art|Azerbaijani folk art]]
sentence_476: Azerbaijanis have a rich and distinctive culture, a major part of which is [[Decorative_art|decorative]] and [[Applied_art|applied art]].
sentence_477: This form of art is represented by a wide range of handicrafts, such as chasing, jeweler, engraving in metal, carving in wood, stone, and bone, carpet-making, lasing, pattern weaving and printing, knitting and embroidery.
sentence_478: Each of these types of decorative art, evidence of the endowments of the Azerbaijan nation, is very much in favor here.
sentence_479: Many interesting facts pertaining to the development of arts and crafts in Azerbaijan were reported by numerous merchants, travelers, and diplomats who had visited these places at different times.
sentence_480: The [[Azerbaijani_rug|Azerbaijani carpet]] is a traditional handmade textile of various sizes, with a dense texture and a pile or pile-less surface, whose patterns are characteristic of Azerbaijan's many carpet-making regions.
sentence_481: In November 2010 the Azerbaijani carpet was proclaimed a [[Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity|Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage]] by [[UNESCO|UNESCO]].
sentence_482: Azerbaijan has been since ancient times known as a center of a large variety of crafts.
sentence_483: The archeological dig on the territory of Azerbaijan testifies to the well-developed agriculture, stock raising, metalworking, pottery, ceramics, and carpet-weaving that date as far back as to the 2nd millennium BC.
sentence_484: Archeological sites in Dashbulaq, Hasansu, Zayamchai, and Tovuzchai uncovered from the BTC pipeline have revealed early Iron Age artifacts.
sentence_485: Azerbaijani carpets can be categorized under several large groups and a multitude of subgroups.
sentence_486: Scientific research of the Azerbaijani carpet is connected with the name of [[Latif_Karimov|Latif Karimov]], a prominent scientist and artist.
sentence_487: It was his classification that related the four large groups of carpets with the four geographical zones of Azerbaijan, Guba-Shirvan, Ganja-Kazakh, Karabakh and Tabriz.
sentence_488: Main article: [[Azerbaijani_cuisine|Azerbaijani cuisine]]
sentence_489: The traditional cuisine is famous for an abundance of vegetables and greens used seasonally in the dishes.
sentence_490: Fresh herbs, including mint, cilantro (coriander), dill, basil, parsley, tarragon, leeks, chives, thyme, marjoram, green onion, and watercress, are very popular and often accompany main dishes on the table.
sentence_491: Climatic diversity and fertility of the land are reflected in the national dishes, which are based on fish from the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]], local meat (mainly mutton and beef), and an abundance of seasonal vegetables and greens.
sentence_492: Saffron-rice [[Plov|plov]] is the flagship food in Azerbaijan and black tea is the national beverage.
sentence_493: Azerbaijanis often use traditional [[Armudu|armudu]] (pear-shaped) glass as they have very strong [[Azerbaijani_tea_culture|tea culture]].
sentence_494: Popular traditional dishes include [[Bozbash|bozbash]] (lamb soup that exists in several regional varieties with the addition of different vegetables), [[Qutab|qutab]] (fried turnover with a filling of greens or minced meat) and [[Dushbara|dushbara]] (sort of dumplings of dough filled with ground meat and flavor).
sentence_495: Main article: [[Architecture_of_Azerbaijan|Architecture of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_496: Azerbaijani architecture typically combines elements of [[Eastern_world|East]] and [[Western_culture|West]].
sentence_497: Azerbaijiani architecture has heavy influences from Persian architecture.
sentence_498: Many ancient architectural treasures such as the [[Maiden_Tower_(Baku)|Maiden Tower]] and [[Palace_of_the_Shirvanshahs|Palace of the Shirvanshahs]] in the [[Baku|Walled City of Baku]] survive in modern Azerbaijan.
sentence_499: Entries submitted on the [[UNESCO_World_Heritage|UNESCO World Heritage]] tentative list include the [[Ateshgah_of_Baku|Ateshgah of Baku]], [[Momine_Khatun_Mausoleum|Momine Khatun Mausoleum]], [[Hirkan_National_Park|Hirkan National Park]], [[Binagadi_asphalt_lake|Binagadi asphalt lake]], [[Lökbatan_Mud_Volcano|Lökbatan Mud Volcano]], [[Shusha_State_Historical_and_Architectural_Reserve|Shusha State Historical and Architectural Reserve]], Baku Stage Mountain, Caspian Shore Defensive Constructions, Ordubad National Reserve and the [[Palace_of_Shaki_Khans|Palace of Shaki Khans]].
sentence_500: Among other architectural treasures are [[Quadrangular_castle_(Mardakan)|Quadrangular Castle]] in [[Mardakan|Mardakan]], [[Parigala|Parigala]] in [[Yuxarı_Çardaqlar|Yukhary Chardaglar]], a number of bridges spanning the Aras River, and several mausoleums.
sentence_501: In the 19th and early 20th centuries, little monumental architecture was created, but distinctive residences were built in Baku and elsewhere.
sentence_502: Among the most recent architectural monuments, the [[Baku_Metro|Baku subways]] are noted for their lavish decor.
sentence_503: The task for modern Azerbaijani architecture is diverse application of modern aesthetics, the search for an architect's own artistic style and inclusion of the existing historico-cultural environment.
sentence_504: Major projects such as [[Heydar_Aliyev_Cultural_Center|Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center]], [[Flame_Towers|Flame Towers]], [[Baku_Crystal_Hall|Baku Crystal Hall]], Baku White City and [[SOCAR_Tower|SOCAR Tower]] have transformed the country's skyline and promotes its contemporary identity.
sentence_505: Main article: [[Visual_arts_of_Azerbaijan|Visual arts of Azerbaijan]]
sentence_506: Azerbaijani art includes one of the oldest art objects in the world, which were discovered as [[Gamigaya_Petroglyphs|Gamigaya Petroglyphs]] in the territory of [[Ordubad_Rayon|Ordubad Rayon]] are dated back to the 1st to 4th centuries BC.
sentence_507: About 1500 dislodged and carved rock paintings with images of deer, goats, bulls, dogs, snakes, birds, fantastic beings and also people, carriages and various symbols had been found out on basalt rocks.
sentence_508: Norwegian ethnographer and adventurer [[Thor_Heyerdahl|Thor Heyerdahl]] was convinced that people from the area went to [[Scandinavia|Scandinavia]] in about 100 AD, took their boat building skills with them, and transmuted them into the Viking boats in Northern Europe.
sentence_509: Over the centuries, Azerbaijani art has gone through many stylistic changes.
sentence_510: Azerbaijani painting is traditionally characterized by a warmth of colour and light, as exemplified in the works of [[Azim_Azimzade|Azim Azimzade]] and [[Bahruz_Kangarli|Bahruz Kangarli]], and a preoccupation with religious figures and cultural motifs.
sentence_511: Azerbaijani painting enjoyed preeminence in Caucasus for hundreds of years, from the Romanesque and [[Culture_of_the_Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman]] periods, and through the [[Socialist_realism|Soviet]] and [[Baroque|Baroque]] periods, the latter two of which saw fruition in Azerbaijan.
sentence_512: Other notable artists who fall within these periods include [[Sattar_Bahlulzade|Sattar Bahlulzade]], [[Togrul_Narimanbekov|Togrul Narimanbekov]], [[Tahir_Salahov|Tahir Salahov]], [[Alakbar_Rezaguliyev|Alakbar Rezaguliyev]], [[Mirza_Gadim_Iravani|Mirza Gadim Iravani]], [[Mikayil_Abdullayev|Mikayil Abdullayev]] and [[Boyukagha_Mirzazade|Boyukagha Mirzazade]].
sentence_513: Main articles: [[Cinema_of_Azerbaijan|Cinema of Azerbaijan]], [[Azerbaijani_animation|Azerbaijani animation]], and [[Television_in_Azerbaijan|Television in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_514: The film industry in Azerbaijan dates back to 1898.
sentence_515: In fact, Azerbaijan was among the first countries involved in cinematography.
sentence_516: Therefore, it is not surprising that this apparatus soon showed up in [[Baku|Baku]] – at the start of the 20th century, this bay town on the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian]] was producing more than 50 percent of the world's supply of oil.
sentence_517: Just like today, the oil industry attracted foreigners eager to invest and to work.
sentence_518: In 1919, during the [[Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]], a documentary The Celebration of the Anniversary of Azerbaijani Independence was filmed on the first anniversary of Azerbaijan's independence from Russia, 27 May, and premiered in June 1919 at several theatres in Baku.
sentence_519: After the Soviet power was established in 1920, Nariman Narimanov, Chairman of the Revolutionary Committee of Azerbaijan, signed a decree nationalizing Azerbaijan's cinema.
sentence_520: This also influenced the creation of [[Azerbaijani_animation|Azerbaijani animation]].
sentence_521: In 1991, after Azerbaijan gained its independence from the Soviet Union, the first Baku International Film Festival East-West was held in Baku.
sentence_522: In December 2000, the former President of Azerbaijan, Heydar Aliyev, signed a decree proclaiming 2 August to be the professional holiday of filmmakers of Azerbaijan.
sentence_523: Today Azerbaijani filmmakers are again dealing with issues similar to those faced by cinematographers prior to the establishment of the Soviet Union in 1920.
sentence_524: Once again, both choices of content and sponsorship of films are largely left up to the initiative of the filmmaker.
sentence_525: Main articles: [[Media_of_Azerbaijan|Media of Azerbaijan]] and [[Media_freedom_in_Azerbaijan|Media freedom in Azerbaijan]]
sentence_526: There are three state-owned television channels: [[AzTV|AzTV]], [[Idman_Azerbaijan_TV|Idman TV]] and [[Medeniyyet_TV|Medeniyyet TV]].
sentence_527: There is one public channel and 6 private channels: [[Ä°ctimai_Television|Ä°ctimai Television]], [[Space_TV|Space TV]], [[Lider_TV|Lider TV]], [[Azad_Azerbaijan_TV|Azad Azerbaijan TV]], , and [[Region_TV|ARB]].
sentence_529: The [[Constitution_of_Azerbaijan|Constitution of Azerbaijan]] claims to guarantee freedom of speech, but this is denied in practice.
sentence_530: After several years of decline in press and media freedom, in 2014, the media environment in Azerbaijan deteriorated rapidly under a governmental campaign to silence any opposition and criticism, even while the country led the Committee of Ministers of the [[Council_of_Europe|Council of Europe]] (May–November 2014).
sentence_531: Spurious legal charges and impunity in violence against journalists have remained the norm.
sentence_532: All foreign broadcasts are banned in the country.
sentence_533: According to the 2013 [[Freedom_House|Freedom House]] [[Freedom_of_the_Press_(report)|Freedom of the Press report]], Azerbaijan's press freedom status is "not free," and Azerbaijan ranks 177th out of 196 countries.
sentence_534: Christianity is officially recognized, but in practice it is often oppressed.
sentence_535: All religious communities are required to register to be allowed to meet, under the risk of imprisonment.
sentence_537: "Racial discrimination contributes to the country's lack of religious freedom, since many of the Christians are ethnic Armenian or Russian, rather than Azeri Muslim."
sentence_538: [[Radio_Liberty|Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]] and [[Voice_of_America|Voice of America]] are banned in Azerbaijan.
sentence_539: Discrimination against [[LGBT_rights_in_Azerbaijan|LGBT people]] in Azerbaijan is widespread.
sentence_540: During the last few years, three journalists were killed and several prosecuted in trials described as unfair by international human rights organizations.
sentence_541: Azerbaijan had the biggest number of journalists imprisoned in Europe in 2015, according to the [[Committee_to_Protect_Journalists|Committee to Protect Journalists]], and is the 5th most censored country in the world, ahead of Iran and China.
sentence_542: Some critical journalists have been [[Misinformation_related_to_the_2019–20_coronavirus_pandemic#Combative_efforts|arrested]] for their coverage of the [[COVID-19_pandemic_in_Azerbaijan|COVID-19 pandemic in Azerbaijan]].
sentence_543: A report by an [[Amnesty_International|Amnesty International]] researcher in October 2015 points to '...the severe deterioration of human rights in Azerbaijan over the past few years.
sentence_544: Sadly Azerbaijan has been allowed to get away with unprecedented levels of repression and in the process almost wipe out its civil society'.
sentence_545: Amnesty's 2015/16 annual report on the country stated ' ... persecution of political dissent continued.
sentence_546: Human rights organizations remained unable to resume their work.
sentence_547: At least 18 prisoners of conscience remained in detention at the end of the year.
sentence_548: Reprisals against independent journalists and activists persisted both in the country and abroad, while their family members also faced harassment and arrests.
sentence_549: International human rights monitors were barred and expelled from the country.
sentence_550: Reports of torture and other ill-treatment persisted.
sentence_551: [[The_Guardian|The Guardian]] reported in April 2017 that "Azerbaijan's ruling elite operated a secret $2.9bn (£2.2bn) scheme to pay prominent Europeans, buy luxury goods and launder money through a network of opaque British companies ....
sentence_552: Leaked data shows that the Azerbaijani leadership, accused of serial human rights abuses, systemic corruption and rigging elections, made more than 16,000 covert payments from 2012 to 2014.
sentence_553: Some of this money went to politicians and journalists, as part of an international lobbying operation to deflect criticism of Azerbaijan's president, Ilham Aliyev, and to promote a positive image of his oil-rich country."
sentence_554: There was no suggestion that all recipients were aware of the source of the money as it arrived via a disguised route.
sentence_556: Freestyle wrestling has been traditionally regarded as Azerbaijan's national sport, in which Azerbaijan won up to [[Azerbaijan_at_the_Olympics|fourteen medals]], including four golds since joining the International Olympic Committee.
sentence_557: Currently, the most popular sports include [[Association_football|football]] and wrestling.
sentence_558: Football is the most popular sport in Azerbaijan, and the [[Association_of_Football_Federations_of_Azerbaijan|Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan]] with 9,122 registered players, is the largest sporting association in the country.
sentence_559: The [[Azerbaijan_national_football_team|national football team]] of Azerbaijan demonstrates relatively low performance in the international arena compared to the nation football clubs.
sentence_560: The most successful Azerbaijani football clubs are [[Neftchi_Baku_PFC|Neftchi Baku]], [[FK_Qarabağ|Qarabağ]], and [[Gabala_FK|Gabala]].
sentence_561: In [[2012–13_UEFA_Europa_League|2012]], Neftchi Baku became the first Azerbaijani team to advance to the group stage of a European competition, beating [[APOEL_F.C.|APOEL]] of Cyprus 4–2 on aggregate in the play-off round of the [[2012–13_UEFA_Europa_League|2012–13 UEFA Europa League]].
sentence_562: In [[2014–15_UEFA_Europa_League|2014]], Qarabağ became the second Azerbaijani club advancing to the group stage of [[UEFA_Europa_League|UEFA Europa League]].
sentence_563: In 2017, after beating [[F.C._Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] 2–2([[Away_goals_rule|a]]) in the play-off round of the [[2017–18_UEFA_Champions_League|UEFA Champions League]], Qarabağ became the first Azerbaijani club to reach the Group stage.
sentence_564: [[Futsal|Futsal]] is another popular sport in Azerbaijan.
sentence_565: The [[Azerbaijan_national_futsal_team|Azerbaijan national futsal team]] reached fourth place in the [[2010_UEFA_Futsal_Championship|2010 UEFA Futsal Championship]], while domestic club [[Araz_Naxçivan|Araz Naxçivan]] clinched bronze medals at the [[2009–10_UEFA_Futsal_Cup|2009–10 UEFA Futsal Cup]] and 2013–14 UEFA Futsal Cup.
sentence_566: Azerbaijan was the main sponsor of Spanish football club [[Atlético_de_Madrid|Atlético de Madrid]] during seasons 2013/2014 and 2014/2015, a partnership that the club described should 'promote the image of Azerbaijan in the world'.
sentence_567: Azerbaijan is one of the traditional powerhouses of world chess, having hosted many international chess tournaments and competitions and became European Team Chess Championship winners in 2009, 2013 and 2017. Notable chess players from country's chess schools that made a great impact on the game in world, includes [[Teimour_Radjabov|Teimour Radjabov]], [[Shahriyar_Mammadyarov|Shahriyar Mammadyarov]], [[Vladimir_Makogonov|Vladimir Makogonov]], [[Vugar_Gashimov|Vugar Gashimov]] and former [[World_Chess_Champion|World Chess Champion]] [[Garry_Kasparov|Garry Kasparov]].
sentence_568: As of 2014, country's home of [[Shamkir_Chess|Shamkir Chess]] a category 22 event and one of the highest rated tournaments of all time.
sentence_569: [[Backgammon|Backgammon]] also plays a major role in Azerbaijani culture.
sentence_570: The game is very popular in Azerbaijan and is widely played among the local public.
sentence_571: There are also different variations of backgammon developed and analyzed by Azerbaijani experts.
sentence_572: [[Azerbaijan_Women's_Volleyball_Super_League|Azerbaijan Women's Volleyball Super League]] is one of strongest women leagues in world.
sentence_573: Its women's national team came fourth at the [[2005_Women's_European_Volleyball_Championship|2005 European Championship]].
sentence_574: Over the last years, clubs like [[Rabita_Baku|Rabita Baku]] and [[Azerrail_Baku|Azerrail Baku]] achieved great success at European cups.
sentence_575: Azerbaijani volleyball players include likes of [[Valeriya_Korotenko|Valeriya Korotenko]], [[Oksana_Parkhomenko|Oksana Parkhomenko]], [[Inessa_Korkmaz|Inessa Korkmaz]], [[Natalya_Mammadova|Natalya Mammadova]] and [[Alla_Hasanova|Alla Hasanova]].
sentence_576: Other Azerbaijani athletes are [[Namig_Abdullayev|Namig Abdullayev]], [[Toghrul_Asgarov|Toghrul Asgarov]], [[Rovshan_Bayramov|Rovshan Bayramov]], [[Sharif_Sharifov|Sharif Sharifov]], [[Mariya_Stadnik|Mariya Stadnik]] and [[Farid_Mansurov|Farid Mansurov]] in [[Amateur_wrestling|wrestling]], [[Nazim_Huseynov|Nazim Huseynov]], [[Elnur_Mammadli|Elnur Mammadli]], [[Elkhan_Mammadov_(judoka)|Elkhan Mammadov]] and Rustam Orujov in judo, [[Rafael_Aghayev|Rafael Aghayev]] in [[Karate|karate]], [[Magomedrasul_Majidov|Magomedrasul Majidov]] and Aghasi Mammadov in [[Boxing|boxing]], [[Nizami_Pashayev|Nizami Pashayev]] in [[Olympic_weightlifting|Olympic weightlifting]], [[Azad_Asgarov|Azad Asgarov]] in pankration, [[Eduard_Mammadov|Eduard Mammadov]] in kickboxing, and [[K-1|K-1]] fighter [[Zabit_Samedov|Zabit Samedov]].
sentence_577: Azerbaijan has a [[Baku_City_Circuit|Formula One race-track]], made in June 2012, and the country hosted its first [[2016_European_Grand_Prix|Formula One Grand Prix]] on 19 June 2016 and the [[Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix|Azerbaijan Grand Prix]] in 2017, 2018 and 2019.
sentence_578: Other annual sporting events held in the country are the [[Baku_Cup|Baku Cup]] tennis tournament and the Tour d'Azerbaïdjan cycling race.
sentence_579: Azerbaijan hosted several major sport competitions since the late 2000s, including the [[2013_F1_Powerboat_World_Championship_season|2013 F1 Powerboat World Championship]], [[2012_FIFA_U-17_Women's_World_Cup|2012 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup]], [[2011_AIBA_World_Boxing_Championships|2011 AIBA World Boxing Championships]], [[2010_European_Wrestling_Championships|2010 European Wrestling Championships]], [[2009_Rhythmic_Gymnastics_European_Championships|2009 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships]], [[European_Taekwondo_Championships|2014 European Taekwondo Championships]], [[2014_Rhythmic_Gymnastics_European_Championships|2014 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships]], and [[42nd_Chess_Olympiad|2016 World Chess Olympiad]].
sentence_580: On 8 December 2012, [[Baku|Baku]] was selected to host the [[2015_European_Games|2015 European Games]], the first to be held in the competition's history.
sentence_581: Baku also hosted the fourth [[Islamic_Solidarity_Games|Islamic Solidarity Games]] in 2017, [[2019_European_Youth_Summer_Olympic_Festival|2019 European Youth Summer Olympic Festival]] and it is also one of the hosts of [[UEFA_Euro_2020|UEFA Euro 2020]].

title: The Bronx
sentence_0: "Bronx" redirects here.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Bronx_(disambiguation)|Bronx (disambiguation)]].
