sentence_2: Andhra Pradesh (English: [[English|/ˌɑːndrə prəˈdɛʃ/]] Telugu: [[Telugu|[ãːndʱrʌ prʌdeːɕ]] listen (help·)) is a [[States_and_union_territories_of_India|state]] in the south-eastern [[Coastal_India|coastal]] region of [[India|India]].
sentence_3: It is the [[List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_area|seventh-largest state by area]] covering an area of 162,975 km (62,925 sq mi) and [[List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population|tenth-most populous state]] with 49,386,799 inhabitants.
sentence_4: It is bordered by [[Telangana|Telangana]] to the north-west, Chhattisgarh to the north, [[Odisha|Odisha]] to the north-east, [[Tamil_Nadu|Tamil Nadu]] to the south, [[Karnataka|Karnataka]] to the west and the [[Bay_of_Bengal|Bay of Bengal]] to the east.
sentence_5: It has the second longest coastline in India after [[Gujarat|Gujarat]], of about 974 km (605 mi).
sentence_6: Andhra Pradesh is the first state to be formed on a [[States_Reorganisation_Act,_1956|linguistic basis]] in India on 1 October 1953.
sentence_7: Andhra Pradesh was once a major [[Buddhist_pilgrimage_sites_in_India|Buddhist pilgrimage site]] in India and a Buddhist learning center which can be seen in [[Buddhist_pilgrimage_sites_in_India|many sites]] in the state in the form of [[Buddhist_monastery|ruins]], [[Chaitya|chaityas]] and [[Stupa|stupas]] Andhra Pradesh is also known as the land of the world-famous diamond [[Koh-i-Noor|Koh-i-Noor]] and many other [[Golconda_diamonds|global known diamonds]] due to their presence in its [[Kollur_Mine|Kollur Mine]] once.
sentence_8: It is also known as the "rice bowl of India" for being a major producer of rice in India.
sentence_9: Its official language is [[Telugu_language|Telugu]]; one of the [[Classical_Languages_of_India|classical languages of India]], the [[List_of_languages_by_number_of_native_speakers_in_India|fourth most spoken language in India]] and the [[List_of_languages_by_number_of_native_speakers|11th-most spoken language in the world]].
sentence_10: Early inhabitants were known as the Andhras, tracing their history to the [[Vedic_period|Vedic period]] when they were mentioned in the 8th century BCE Rigvedic text [[Aitareya_Brahmana|Aitareya Brahmana]].
sentence_11: According to the [[Aitareya_Brahmana|Aitareya Brahmana]], the Andhras left [[North_India|North India]] from the banks of [[Yamuna|river Yamuna]] and migrated to [[South_India|South India]].
sentence_12: The [[Assaka|Assaka]] Mahajanapada (700–300 BCE) was an ancient kingdom located between the [[Godavari_River|Godavari]] and [[Krishna_River|Krishna Rivers]] in southeastern India accounts that people in the region are descended from the [[Viswamitra|Viswamitra]] are found in the [[Ramayana|Ramayana]], the [[Mahabharata|Mahabharata]] and the [[Puranas|Puranas]].
sentence_13: The region also derives its name from [[Satavahana_dynasty|Satavahanas]] who are also known as [[Satavahana_dynasty|Andhras]], the earliest [[Monarch|kings]] of Andhra Pradesh and India.
sentence_14: Early peoples supported local art culture by building temples and sculptures of the [[Stupa|Buddhist monuments]] in the state.
sentence_15: It was ruled by Satavahanas, [[Eastern_Chalukyas|Eastern Chalukyas]], [[Andhra_Ikshvaku|Andhra Ikshvakus]], [[Vijayanagara_Empire|Vijayanagara Empire]], [[Maurya_Empire|Mauryan Empire]], [[Medieval_Cholas|Cholas]], [[Pallava_dynasty|Pallavas]], [[Shalankayana|Salankayanas]], [[Vishnukundina_dynasty|Vishnukundinas]], [[Kakatiya_dynasty|Kakatiyas]] and [[Rashtrakuta_dynasty|Rashtrakutas]].
sentence_16: In the 3rd century BCE, Andhra was a vassal kingdom of [[Ashoka|Ashoka]] but after his death Andhra became powerful and extended its empire to the whole of Maratha country and beyond.
sentence_17: Andhra Pradesh comprises two major regions, namely Rayalaseema in the south-west and Coastal Andhra bordering the [[Bay_of_Bengal|Bay of Bengal]] in the east and north-east.
sentence_18: The state has a total of [[List_of_districts_of_Andhra_Pradesh|thirteen districts]], nine located in Coastal Andhra and four in Rayalaseema.
sentence_19: The state also has a [[Union_territory|union territory]], [[Yanam_district|Yanam]] - a district of Puducherry which lies to the south of [[Kakinada|Kakinada]] in the [[Godavari_River|Godavari]] delta on the eastern side of the state.
sentence_20: It is the only state with three capitals.
sentence_21: The largest city and commercial hub of the state, [[Visakhapatnam|Visakhapatnam]] being the [[Executive_(government)|executive]] capital while Amaravati and [[Kurnool|Kurnool]] serve as [[Legislative|legislative]] and [[Judicial|judicial]] capitals respectively.
sentence_22: The [[Economy_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Economy of Andhra Pradesh]] is the [[List_of_Indian_states_and_union_territories_by_GDP|seventh-largest state economy]] in India with [[Indian_rupee|₹]]9.33 trillion (US$130 billion) in gross domestic product and a higher than national average per capita GDP of ₹164,000 (US$2,300).
sentence_23: Andhra Pradesh [[List_of_Indian_states_and_territories_by_Human_Development_Index|ranks 27th]] among Indian states in [[Human_Development_Index|Human Development Index]] (HDI).
sentence_24: Andhra Pradesh has a jurisdiction over almost 15,000 square kilometres (5,800 sq mi) of territorial waters.
sentence_25: Andhra Pradesh hosted 121.8 million visitors in 2015, a 30% growth in tourist arrivals over the previous year, making it the [[Tourism_in_India#Statistics|third most-visited]] state in India.
sentence_26: The [[Venkateswara_Temple,_Tirumala|Tirumala Venkateswara Temple]] in [[Tirupati|Tirupati]] is one of the world's most visited religious sites, with 18.25 million visitors per year.
sentence_27: The region is also home to a variety of other [[Tourism_in_Andhra_Pradesh#Religious_and_pilgrimage_sites|pilgrimage centres]], such as the [[Pancharama_Kshetras|Pancharama Kshetras]], [[Mallikarjuna_Jyotirlinga|Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga]] and [[Kodandarama_Temple,_Vontimitta|Kodanda Rama Temple]].
sentence_28: The state's [[Tourism_in_Andhra_Pradesh#Nature_tourism|natural attractions]] include the [[Tourist_attractions_in_Visakhapatnam#Beaches|beaches]] of Visakhapatnam, [[Hill_station|hill stations]] such as the [[Araku_Valley|Araku Valley]] and [[Horsley_Hills|Horsley Hills]], and the delta of [[Konaseema|Konaseema]] in the [[Godavari_River|Godavari River]] delta.
sentence_29: Main article: History of Andhra Pradesh
sentence_30: A group of people named Andhras was mentioned in [[Sanskrit|Sanskrit]] texts such as [[Aitareya_Brahmana|Aitareya Brahmana]] (800–500 [[BCE|BCE]]).
sentence_31: According to Aitareya Brahmana of the [[Rig_Veda|Rig Veda]], the Andhras left north India from banks of [[River_Yamuna|River Yamuna]] and settled in south India.
sentence_32: The Satavahanas have been mentioned by the names Andhra, Andhrara-jateeya and [[Andhrabhrtya|Andhrabhrtya]] in the [[Puranas|Puranic literature]].
sentence_33: They did not refer themselves as Andhra in any of their coins or inscriptions; it is possible that they were termed as Andhras because of their ethnicity or because their territory included the Andhra region.
sentence_34: The [[Assaka|Assaka]] Mahajanapada, one of the sixteen Vedic Mahajanapadas, included Andhra, [[Maharashtra|Maharashtra]] and Telangana.
sentence_35: Archaeological evidence from places such as [[Amaravathi_(village),_Guntur_district|Amaravati]], [[Dharanikota|Dharanikota]], and [[Vaddamanu|Vaddamanu]] suggests that the Andhra region was part of the [[Mauryan_Empire|Mauryan Empire]].
sentence_36: Amaravati might have been a regional centre for the Mauryan rule.
sentence_37: After the death of Emperor [[Ashoka|Ashoka]], Mauryan rule weakened around 200 BCE and was replaced by several smaller [[Kingship_and_kingdom_of_God|kingdoms]] in the Andhra region.
sentence_38: The [[Satavahana_dynasty|Satavahana dynasty]] dominated the [[Deccan_Plateau|Deccan region]] from the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
sentence_39: The later Satavahanas made [[Dharanikota|Dharanikota]] and [[Amaravathi_village,_Guntur_district|Amaravathi]] their capital, which according to the Buddhists is the place where [[Nagarjuna|Nagarjuna]], the philosopher of [[Mahayana|Mahayana]] lived in the 2nd and 3rd centuries.
sentence_40: The [[Andhra_Ikshvaku|Andhra Ikshvakus]], with their capital at [[Vijayapuri_(South)|Vijayapuri]], succeeded the Satavahanas in the [[Krishna_River|Krishna River]] valley in the latter half of the 2nd century.
sentence_41: Pallavas, who were originally executive officers under the Satavahana kings, were not a recognised political power before the 2nd century CE and were swept away by the [[Western_Chalukya_Empire|Western Chalukyan]] invasion, led by Pulakesin II in the first quarter of the 7th century CE.
sentence_42: After the downfall of the Ikshvakus, the [[Vishnukundinas|Vishnukundinas]] were the first great dynasty in the 5th and 6th centuries, and held sway over the entire Andhra country, including [[Kalinga_(historical_region)|Kalinga]] and parts of [[Telangana|Telangana]].
sentence_43: They played an important role in the history of Deccan during the 5th and 6th century CE, with [[Eluru|Eluru]], Amaravathi and Puranisangam.
sentence_44: The [[Salankayanas|Salankayanas]] were an ancient dynasty that ruled the Andhra region between [[Godavari_River|Godavari]] and Krishna with their capital at Vengi (modern [[Pedavegi|Pedavegi]]) from 300 to 440 CE.
sentence_45: The [[Eastern_Chalukyas|Eastern Chalukyas]] of Vengi, whose dynasty lasted for around five hundred years from the 7th century until 1130 CE, eventually merged with the [[Chola_Empire|Chola Empire]].
sentence_46: They continued to rule under the protection of the [[Chola_Empire|Chola Empire]] until 1189 CE when the kingdom succumbed to the [[Hoysalas|Hoysalas]] and the [[Yadavas|Yadavas]].
sentence_47: The roots of the [[Telugu_language|Telugu language]] have been seen on inscriptions found near the [[Guntur|Guntur]] district and from others dating to the rule of Renati Cholas in the fifth century [[Common_Era|CE]].
sentence_48: [[Kakatiyas|Kakatiyas]] ruled Andhra Pradesh state for nearly two hundred years and constructed several forts.
sentence_49: They were succeeded by the [[Musunuri_Nayaks|Musunuri Nayaks]].
sentence_50: Musunuri Nayaks led a confederation of Nayakas to overthrow the rule of the [[Delhi|Delhi]] Sultanate in Telugu lands.
sentence_51: The [[Reddi_kingdom|Reddi kingdom]] (1325–1448 CE) was established by Prolaya Vema Reddi in the early 14th century, who ruled from present day Kondaveedu.
sentence_52: Prolaya Vema Reddi was part of the confederation of states that started a movement against the invading [[Turkic_peoples|Turkic]] Muslim armies of the [[Delhi_Sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]].
sentence_53: They constructed Kondaveedu Fort, which they ruled between 1328 and 1428, before it was taken over by the Gajpathis of Orissa, and later ravaged by the [[Muslim|Muslim]] rulers of the [[Bahmani_kingdom|Bahmani kingdom]] in 1458.
sentence_54: The [[Vijayanagara|Vijayanagara]] emperor [[Krishnadevaraya|Krishnadevaraya]] captured it in 1516.
sentence_55: The [[Golconda|Golconda]] [[Sultan|Sultans]] fought for the fort in 1531, 1536 and 1579, and Sultan [[Quli_Qutb_Shah|Quli Qutb Shah]] captured it in 1579, renaming it Murtuzanagar.
sentence_56: It was reconquered by Vijayanagara who overthrew sultanate rule across the entirety of modern-day Andhra Pradesh (excluding Telangana).
sentence_57: After this rebellion, the Bahmani sultans launched no further military campaigns outside their kingdoms, because the Maratha empire soon emerged as the strongest power in India.
sentence_58: Efforts are in progress to classify Kondaveedu Fort as a UNESCO [[World_Heritage_Site|World Heritage Site]].
sentence_59: The [[Vijayanagara_Empire|Vijayanagara]] Empire originated in the [[Deccan_Plateau|Deccan Plateau]] region in the early 14th century.
sentence_60: It was established in 1336 by [[Harihara_Raya_I|Harihara Raya I]] and his brother [[Bukka_Raya_I|Bukka Raya I]] of the Sangama Dynasty.
sentence_61: The empire's patronage enabled fine arts and literature to reach new heights in [[Kannada_language|Kannada]], [[Telugu_language|Telugu]], [[Tamil_language|Tamil]], and [[Sanskrit|Sanskrit]], while [[Carnatic_music|Carnatic music]] evolved into its current form.
sentence_62: During the Vijayanagara Empire, the [[Pemmasani_Nayaks|Pemmasani Nayaks]] controlled parts of Andhra Pradesh and had large mercenary armies that were the vanguard of the [[Vijayanagara_Empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] in the sixteenth century.
sentence_63: The [[Lepakshi|Lepakshi]] group of monuments are culturally and archaeologically significant as it is the location of shrines dedicated to [[Shiva|Shiva]], [[Vishnu|Vishnu]], and [[Veerabhadra_Temple,_Lepakshi|Veerabhadra]] which were built during the Vijayanagara Kings' period (1336–1646).
sentence_64: The temples are the location of mural paintings of the Vijayanagara kings, Dravidian art, and inscriptions.
sentence_65: Near the temple complex is a large granite [[Nandi_bull|Nandi bull]].
sentence_66: On a hillock known as Kurma Saila ('tortoise-shaped hill') are other temples to Papanatheswara, [[Raghunatha|Raghunatha]], [[Rama|Srirama]], and [[Durga|Durga]].
sentence_67: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has taken the initiative for including the "Lepakshi Group of Monuments" among the [[List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_India|UNESCO World Heritage sites in India]].
sentence_68: [[Harihara|Harihara]] and [[Bukka|Bukka]], who served as treasury officers of the [[Kakatiya_dynasty|Kakatiyas]] of Warangal, founded the [[Vijayanagara_Empire|Vijayanagara Empire]].
sentence_69: In 1347 [[Common_Era|CE]], an independent Muslim state, the [[Bahmani_Sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]], was established in [[South_India|south India]] by [[Ala-ud-Din_Bahman_Shah|Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah]] in a revolt against the Delhi Sultanate.
sentence_70: The [[Qutb_Shahi_dynasty|Qutb Shahi dynasty]] held sway over the Andhra country for about two hundred years from the early part of the sixteenth century to the end of the seventeenth century.
sentence_71: In the early nineteenth century, [[Northern_Circars|Northern Circars]] was ceded to the British East India Company and became part of the [[Madras_Presidency|Madras Presidency]].
sentence_72: Eventually, this region emerged as the Coastal Andhra region.
sentence_73: Later the [[Nizam|Nizam]] rulers of Hyderabad ceded five territories to the British that eventually became the Rayalaseema region.
sentence_74: The Nizams retained control of the interior provinces as the [[Princely_state|princely state]] of [[Hyderabad_State|Hyderabad]], acknowledging British rule in return for local autonomy.
sentence_75: However, [[Komaram_Bheem|Komaram Bheem]], a tribal leader, started his fight against the erstwhile [[Asaf_Jahi_Dynasty|Asaf Jahi Dynasty]] for the liberation of Hyderabad State.
sentence_76: Meanwhile, the [[French_colonial_empire|French]] occupied [[Yanam_(India)|Yanam]], in the Godavari delta, and (save for periods of British control) would hold it until 1954.
sentence_77: In 1947, Vizianagaram was the largest Hindu princely state in Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_78: [[Indian_independence_movement|India became independent]] from the United Kingdom in 1947.
sentence_79: The Nizam wanted to retain the independence of the Princely Hyderabad State from India, but the people of the region launched a movement to join the Indian Union.
sentence_80: The state of Hyderabad was integrated into the [[Dominion_of_India|Indian Union]] with [[Operation_Polo|Operation Polo]] in 1948.
sentence_81: See also: [[Andhra_State|Andhra State]], Vishalandhra Movement, and [[United_Andhra_Pradesh|United Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_82: In an effort to gain an independent state based on linguistic identity, and to protect the interests of the Telugu-speaking people of Madras State, [[Potti_Sreeramulu|Potti Sreeramulu]] fasted to death in 1952.
sentence_83: As Madras became a bone of contention, in 1949 a JVP committee report stated: "Andhra Province could be formed provided the Andhras give up their claim on the city of Madras (now Chennai)".
sentence_84: After Potti Sreeramulu's death, the Telugu-speaking area of [[Andhra_State|Andhra State]] was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953, with [[Kurnool|Kurnool]] as its capital city.
sentence_85: On the basis of the [[Gentlemen's_Agreement_of_1956|gentlemen's agreement]] of 1 November 1956, the [[States_Reorganisation_Act|States Reorganisation Act]] formed [[Combined_Andhra_Pradesh|combined Andhra Pradesh]] by merging Andhra State with the Telugu-speaking areas of the already existing [[Hyderabad_State|Hyderabad State]].
sentence_86: Hyderabad was made the capital of the new state.
sentence_87: The Marathi-speaking areas of Hyderabad State merged with [[Bombay_State|Bombay State]] and the Kannada-speaking areas were merged with [[Mysore_State|Mysore State]].
sentence_88: In February 2014, the [[Andhra_Pradesh_Reorganisation_Act,_2014|Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014]] bill was passed by the [[Parliament_of_India|Parliament of India]] for the formation of the [[Telangana|Telangana]] state comprising [[List_of_districts_in_Telangana|ten districts]].
sentence_89: [[Hyderabad|Hyderabad]] will remain as a joint capital for not exceeding ten years.
sentence_90: The new state of Telangana came into existence on 2 June 2014 after approval from the [[President_of_India|President of India]].
sentence_91: Number of petitions questioning the validity of Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is long pending for the verdict since April 2014 before the [[Supreme_court_of_India|supreme court]] constitutional bench.
sentence_92: Main articles: Geography of Andhra Pradesh and [[List_of_districts_of_Andhra_Pradesh|List of districts of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_93: The state has varied topography ranging from the hills of Eastern Ghats and [[Nallamala_Hills|Nallamala Hills]] to the shores of [[Bay_of_Bengal|Bay of Bengal]] that support varied ecosystems, the rich diversity of flora and fauna.
sentence_94: There are two main rivers namely, [[Krishna_River|Krishna]] and [[Godavari_river|Godavari]], that flow through the state.
sentence_95: The coast of the state extends along the [[Bay_of_Bengal|Bay of Bengal]] from [[Srikakulam_district|Srikakulam]] to [[Nellore_district|Nellore district]].
sentence_96: The plains to the east of Eastern Ghats form the Eastern coastal plains.
sentence_97: The coastal plains are for the most part of delta regions formed by the Godavari, Krishna, and [[Penner_River|Penner Rivers]].
sentence_98: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and individual sections have local names.
sentence_99: The Eastern Ghats are a major dividing line in the state's geography.
sentence_100: The Kadapa Basin formed by two arching branches of the Eastern Ghats is a mineral-rich area.
sentence_101: The Ghats become more pronounced towards the south and extreme north of the coast.
sentence_102: Most of the coastal plains are put to intense agricultural use.
sentence_103: The Rayalaseema region has semi-arid conditions.
sentence_104: Main article: [[Natural_vegetation_and_Wildlife_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Natural vegetation and Wildlife of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_105: The [[Andhra_Pradesh_Forest_Department|Andhra Pradesh Forest Department]] deals with protection, conservation and management of [[Forests|forests]].
sentence_106: The total forest cover of the state after the bifurcation is left with an area of 22,862 square kilometres (8,827 sq mi).
sentence_107: The forest in the state can be broadly divided into four major biotic provinces.
sentence_108: They are:
sentence_109: Eastern Ghats region is home to dense tropical forests, while the vegetation becomes sparse as the Ghats give way to the Deccan Plateau, where shrub vegetation is more common.
sentence_110: The vegetation found in the state is largely of dry deciduous types with a mixture of [[Teak|teak]], [[Terminalia_(plant)|Terminalia]], [[Dalbergia|Dalbergia]], [[Pterocarpus|Pterocarpus]], [[Anogeissus|Anogeissus]], etc.
sentence_111: The state has many [[Sanctuaries|sanctuaries]], [[National_parks|national parks]] and [[Zoo_Park|zoological parks]], such as [[Coringa_Wildlife_Sanctuary|Coringa]], [[Krishna_Wildlife_Sanctuary|Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary]], [[Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam_Tiger_Reserve|Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve]], [[Kambalakonda_Wildlife_Sanctuary|Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary]], [[Sri_Venkateswara_Zoological_Park|Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park]] and [[Indira_Gandhi_Zoological_Park|Indira Gandhi Zoological Park]].
sentence_112: [[Atapaka_Bird_Sanctuary|Atapaka Bird Sanctuary]], [[Nelapattu_Bird_Sanctuary|Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary]], [[Telineelapuram_and_Telukunchi_Bird_Sanctuaries|Telineelapuram and Telukunchi Bird Sanctuaries]] and [[Pulicat_Lake_Bird_Sanctuary|Pulicat Lake Bird Sanctuary]] attract many migratory birds.
sentence_113: The state possesses some rare and endemic plants like [[Cycas_beddomei|Cycas beddomei]], [[Pterocarpus_santalinus|Pterocarpus santalinus]], Terminalia pallida, Syzygium alternifolium, Shorea talura, Shorea tumburgia, [[Psilotum_nudum|Psilotum nudum]], etc.
sentence_114: The diversity of fauna includes tigers, panthers, hyenas, black bucks, cheetals, sambars, sea turtles and a number of birds and reptiles.
sentence_115: The estuaries of the Godavari and Krishna Rivers support rich mangrove forests with fishing cats and otters as keystone species.
sentence_116: The climate of Andhra Pradesh varies considerably, depending on the geographical region.
sentence_117: Summers last from March to June.
sentence_118: In the coastal plain, the summer temperatures are generally higher than the rest of the state, with temperature ranging between 20 and 41 °C (68 and 106 °F).
sentence_119: July to September is the season for tropical rains.
sentence_120: About one-third of the total rainfall is brought by the [[Northeast_monsoon|northeast monsoon]].
sentence_121: October and November see low-pressure systems and tropical cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal which, along with the northeast monsoon, bring rains to the southern and coastal regions of the state.
sentence_122: November, December, January, and February are the winter months in Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_123: Since the state has a long coastal belt the winters are not very cold.
sentence_124: The range of winter temperature is generally 12 to 30 °C (54 to 86 °F).
sentence_125: [[Lambasingi|Lambasingi]] in [[Visakhapatnam_district|Visakhapatnam district]] is also nicknamed as the "Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh" due to its relatively cool climate as compared to others and the temperature ranges from 0 to 10 °C (32 to 50 °F).
sentence_126: See also: [[Ethnic_groups_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Ethnic groups of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_127: As of 2011 [[Census_of_India|Census of India]], the residual state had a population of 49,386,799 with a population density of 308/km (800/sq mi).
sentence_128: According to the Polavaram ordinance bill 2014, 7 mandals of Khammam district in Telangana state merged with Andhra Pradesh to facilitate Polavaram project, due to which population of 247,515 added to Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_129: Thus the final population of Andhra Pradesh in the year 2014, as per census 2011 is 49,634,314, with a density of 304.5/km (789/sq mi).
sentence_130: The races Caucasoid, Mongoloid, Australoid or Veddoid are found throughout Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_131: The total population constitute, 70.4% of rural population with 34,776,389 inhabitants and 29.6% of urban population with 14,610,410 inhabitants.
sentence_132: Children in the age group of 0–6 years are 5,222,384, constituting 10.6% of the total population, among them 2,686,453 are boys and 2,535,931 are girls.
sentence_133: [[Visakhapatnam_district|Visakhapatnam district]] has the largest urban population of 47.5% and [[Srikakulam_district|Srikakulam district]] with 83.8%, has the largest rural population, among others districts in the state.
sentence_134: The overall population of the state comprises 17.1% of Scheduled Caste and 5.3% of Scheduled Tribe population.
sentence_135: There are 24,738,068 male and 24,648,731 female citizens—a [[Human_sex_ratio|sex ratio]] of 996 females per 1000 males, higher than the national average of 926 per 1000.
sentence_136: The literacy rate of the state stands at 67.41%.
sentence_137: However, post bifurcation from Telangana, the state is expected to reach 91.1% by 2021.
sentence_138: [[West_Godavari_district|West Godavari district]] has the highest literacy rate of 74.6% and [[Vizianagaram_district|Vizianagaram district]] has the least with 58.9%.
sentence_139: Andhra Pradesh ranks tenth of all Indian States in the Human Development Index scores with a score of 0.416.
sentence_140: The National Council of Applied Economic Research district analysis in 2001 reveals that Krishna, West Godavari and [[Chittoor_district|Chittoor]] are the three districts in rural AP with the highest Human Development Index scores in ascending order.
sentence_141: [[Telugu_language|Telugu]] is the official language of Andhra Pradesh, which is also the mother tongue of nearly 90% of the population.
sentence_142: The Minister of Tourism and Culture has declared Telugu a [[Classical_languages_of_India#Classical|Classical Language]].
sentence_143: Urdu is the largest minority language.
sentence_144: [[Tamil_Nadu|Tamil]], [[Kannada|Kannada]] and [[Odia_language|Odia]] are spoken in border-areas.
sentence_145: [[Lambadi|Lambadi]], [[Koya_language|Koya]], [[Sora_language|Savara]], [[Ollari_language|Gadaba]] and a number of other languages are spoken by the Scheduled Tribes of the state.
sentence_146: The majority of the people in Andhra Pradesh are Hindus while Muslims constitute a sizeable minority.
sentence_147: According to the 2011 census, the major religious groups in the state are Hindus (90.87%), Muslims (7.32%) and Christians (1.38%).
sentence_148: Buddhists, Sikhs, Jains and the people who declined to state their religion make up the remaining portion of population.
sentence_149: [[Venkateswara_Temple,_Tirumala|Venkateswara Temple]] at [[Tirupati|Tirupati]] is the world's second-richest temple and is visited by millions of devotees throughout the year.
sentence_150: Andhra Pradesh is home to Shankaracharya of Pushpagiri Peetham.
sentence_151: Other Hindu saints include [[Sadasiva_Brahmendra|Sadasiva Brahmendra]], Bhaktha Kannappa, Yogi Vemana, [[Sathya_Sai_Baba|Sathya Sai Baba]] and Pothuluru Veerabrahmendra.
sentence_152: Buddhism spread to Andhra Pradesh early in its history.
sentence_153: The Krishna River valley was "a site of extraordinary Buddhist activity for almost a thousand years."
sentence_154: The ancient Buddhist sites in the lower Krishna Valley, including Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda and Jaggayyapeta "can be traced to at least the third century BCE, if not earlier."
sentence_155: The region played a central role in the development of [[Mahayana_Buddhism|Mahayana Buddhism]], along with the Magadha-area in northeastern India.
sentence_156: [[A._K._Warder|A.
sentence_157: K. Warder]] holds that "the Mahāyāna originated in the south of India and almost certainly in the Andhra country."
sentence_158: According to Xing, "Several scholars have suggested that the Prajnaparamita probably developed among the Mahasamghikas in Southern India probably in the Andhra country, on the Krishna River."
sentence_159: The [[Prajñāpāramitā|Prajñāpāramitā]] Sutras belong to the earliest [[Mahayana_Sutras|Mahayana Sutras]].
sentence_160: Andhra Pradesh comprises three regions: Coastal Andhra, [[Uttarandhra|Uttarandhra]] and Rayalaseema.
sentence_161: Main article: [[List_of_districts_in_Andhra_Pradesh|List of districts in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_162: It has a total of 13 districts, six in Coastal Andhra Region, three in Uttarandhra and four in the Rayalaseema Region.
sentence_163: Main article: [[List_of_Revenue_Divisions_in_Andhra_Pradesh|List of Revenue Divisions in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_164: These 13 districts are further divided into 50 revenue divisions.
sentence_165: There are as many as 7 revenue divisions in East Godavari, and only 2 in Vizianagaram district.
sentence_166: Main article: [[List_of_mandals_in_Andhra_Pradesh|List of mandals in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_167: The 50 revenue divisions are in turn divided into 671 [[Mandals|mandals]].
sentence_168: Chittoor district has the most [[Tehsil|mandals]] with 66 and Vizianagaram has the least with 34.
sentence_169: There are a total of [[List_of_cities_in_Andhra_Pradesh|31 cities]] which include, [[List_of_municipal_corporations_in_India|16 municipal corporations]] and [[List_of_cities_in_Andhra_Pradesh|14 municipalities]].
sentence_170: There are two cities with [[List_of_cities_in_India_by_population|more than one million]] inhabitants, namely [[Visakhapatnam|Visakhapatnam]] and [[Vijayawada|Vijayawada]].
sentence_171: Main articles: [[Government_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Government of Andhra Pradesh]] and [[Politics_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Politics of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_172: When the state was first created, [[Tanguturi_Prakasam|Tanguturi Prakasam]] Pantulu, became the chief minister.
sentence_173: After the unification with Telangana, [[Neelam_Sanjiva_Reddy|Neelam Sanjiva Reddy]] became the first chief minister.
sentence_174: He later served as president of India.
sentence_175: The [[Indian_National_Congress|Indian National Congress]] (INC), the [[Praja_Socialist_Party|Praja Socialist Party]] and the Krishi Lok Party were the major parties in the 1950s.
sentence_176: Later the Communist Party of India (CPI) became the dominant opposition party.
sentence_177: In the 1967 state assembly elections, all socialist parties were eliminated and the CPI lost opposition party status.
sentence_178: The INC ruled the state from 1956 to 1982.
sentence_179: In 1983, the [[Telugu_Desam_Party|Telugu Desam Party]] (TDP) won the state elections and [[N._T._Rama_Rao|N.
sentence_180: T. Rama Rao]] became the chief minister of the state for the first time.
sentence_181: This broke the long-time single party monopoly enjoyed by the INC.
sentence_182: The 1989 elections ended the rule of Rao, with the INC returning to power with [[Marri_Chenna_Reddy|Marri Chenna Reddy]] at the helm.
sentence_183: He was replaced by Janardhan Reddy in 1990, who was replaced by [[Kotla_Vijaya_Bhaskara_Reddy|Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy]] in 1992.
sentence_184: In 1994, Andhra Pradesh gave a mandate to the Telugu Desam Party again, and Rao became the chief minister again.
sentence_185: Nara Chandrababu Naidu, Rao's son-in-law, came to power in 1995 with the backing of a majority of the [[MLAs|MLAs]].
sentence_186: The Telugu Desam Party won both the assembly and [[Lok_Sabha|Lok Sabha]] election in 1999 under the leadership of Chandrababu Naidu.
sentence_187: Thus Naidu held the record for the longest-serving chief minister (1995 to 2004).
sentence_188: In 2004, Congress returned to power with a new chief ministerial face, [[Y._S._Rajasekhara_Reddy|YS Rajashekara Reddy]], better known as YSR.
sentence_189: He also won the 2009 elections, but shortly afterward was killed in a helicopter crash in September of that year.
sentence_190: He was succeeded by two other Congressmen, the last resigning over the impending [[Telangana_movement|division]] of [[Telangana|Telangana]].
sentence_191: In the last elections held in the unified state in 2014, the TDP got a mandate in their favour in the residuary (new) state.
sentence_192: After Telangana became a separate state, Naidu, the chief of the TDP became chief minister on 8 June 2014, for the new state of Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_193: As of 2014, the Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh is the lower house of the state with 175 members and the [[Andhra_Pradesh_Legislative_Council|Legislative Council]] is the upper house with 58 members.
sentence_194: In the [[Parliament_of_India|Parliament of India]], Andhra Pradesh has 11 seats in the [[Rajya_Sabha|Rajya Sabha]], and 25 seats in the [[Lok_Sabha|Lok Sabha]].
sentence_195: There are a total of 175 [[List_of_Assembly_constituencies_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Assembly constituencies]] in the state.
sentence_196: [[East_Godavari_district|East Godavari district]] has the highest number of constituencies with 19 and [[Vizianagaram_district|Vizianagaram district]] has the least with 9 assembly seats.
sentence_197: Whereas, the legislative council of the state has 58 seats, which is one-third of total assembly seats.
sentence_198: In the 2019 elections, YSR's son [[Y._S._Jaganmohan_Reddy|Y.
sentence_199: S. Jaganmohan Reddy]] of the [[YSR_Congress_Party|YSR Congress Party]] (founded in 2011) became chief minister with a resounding mandate by winning 151 out of 175 seats.
sentence_200: Main article: [[Economy_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Economy of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_201: Andhra Pradesh was ranked eighth among other Indian states in terms of [[Gross_state_product|GSDP]] for the financial year 2014–2015.
sentence_202: The GSDP at current prices was ₹5,200.3 billion (US$73 billion) and at constant prices was ₹2,645.21 billion (US$37 billion).
sentence_203: The domestic product of agriculture sector accounts for ₹545.99 billion (US$7.7 billion) and industrial sector for ₹507.45 billion (US$7.1 billion).
sentence_204: The service sector of the state accounts more percentage of the GSDP with a total of ₹1,305.87 billion (US$18 billion).
sentence_205: In the 2010 list by [[Forbes|Forbes]] magazine, several people from Andhra Pradesh were among the top 100 richest Indians.
sentence_206: Andhra Pradesh's economy is mainly based on agriculture and livestock.
sentence_207: Four important rivers of India, the [[Godavari_River|Godavari]], [[Krishna_River|Krishna]], [[Penner_River|Penna]], and [[Tungabhadra_River|Thungabhadra]] flow through the state and provide irrigation.
sentence_208: 60 percent of the population is engaged in agriculture and related activities.
sentence_209: Rice is the major food crop and staple food of the state.
sentence_210: It is an exporter of many agricultural products and is also known as "Rice Bowl of India".
sentence_211: The state has three Agricultural Economic Zones in Chittoor district for mango pulp and vegetables, Krishna district for mangoes, Guntur district for chilies.
sentence_212: Besides rice, farmers also grow jowar, bajra, maize, minor millet, coarse grain, many varieties of pulses, oil seeds, [[Sugarcane|sugarcane]], cotton, [[Chili_pepper|chili pepper]], [[Mango|mango]] nuts and tobacco.
sentence_213: Crops used for vegetable oil production such as [[Sunflower|sunflower]] and peanuts are popular.
sentence_214: There are many multi-state irrigation projects under development, including [[Godavari_River_Basin_Irrigation_Projects|Godavari River Basin Irrigation Projects]] and [[Nagarjuna_Sagar_Dam|Nagarjuna Sagar Dam]].
sentence_215: Livestock and poultry is also another profitable business, which involves rearing cattle in enclosed areas for commercial purposes.
sentence_216: The state is also a largest producer of eggs in the country and hence, it is nicknamed as "Egg Bowl of Asia".
sentence_217: Fisheries contribute 10% of total fish and over 70% of the shrimp production of India.
sentence_218: The geographical location of the state allows marine fishing as well as inland fish production.
sentence_219: The most exported marine exports include [[Whiteleg_shrimp|Vannamei shrimp]] and are expected to cross billion in 2013–2014.
sentence_220: Andhra Pradesh is investing in building infrastructure in the state such as highways and making every service of the government digital.
sentence_221: [[National_Highway_16_(India)|National Highway 16 (India)]] passes through Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_222: The [[List_of_state_highways_in_Andhra_Pradesh|highways in the state]] are also being widened.
sentence_223: [[APSFL|APSFL]] is an initiative of the government of Andhra Pradesh to set up an optical fiber network throughout the thirteen districts of Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_224: This network provides internet connectivity, telephony and [[IPTV|IPTV]] with fiber to private and corporate users of Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_225: The state also has seaports such as [[Visakhapatnam_Port|Visakhapatnam Port]], [[Kakinada_Port|Kakinada Port]], [[Krishnapatnam_Port|Krishnapatnam Port]] for import and export and a shipyard for building ships at Visakhapatnam.
sentence_226: Major airports in the state are Visakhapatnam, [[Rajamahendravaram|Rajamahendravaram]], Vijayawada, with [[Visakhapatnam_Airport|Visakhapatnam]], Tirupati and [[Vijayawada_Airport|Vijayawada]] being international airports.
sentence_227: The industrial sector of the state includes some of the key sectors like [[Pharmaceutical_industry|pharmaceutica]]l, [[Automobile_industry|automobile]], [[Textile_industry_in_India|textiles]] etc. Sricity located in [[Chittoor_district|Chittoor district]] is an integrated business city which is home to firms including [[PepsiCo|PepsiCo]], [[Isuzu_Motors|Isuzu Motors]], [[Cadbury_India|Cadbury India]], [[Kellogg's|Kellogg's]], [[Colgate-Palmolive|Colgate-Palmolive]], [[Kobelco|Kobelco]] etc.
sentence_228: The [[PepsiCo|PepsiCo]] firm has its largest plant in India at Sri City.
sentence_229: The state is also emerging as destination for the automobile industry which already hosts companies including [[Ashok_Leyland|Ashok Leyland]] in Krishna district, Hero Motors in Chittoor district, [[Kia_Motors|Kia Motors]] in Anantapur district.
sentence_230: The state is also emerging in information technology and biotechnology.
sentence_231: The IT/ITES revenues of Visakhapatnam is at ₹14.45 billion (US$200 million) in 2012–2013.
sentence_232: The development of IT in Tier-II and Tier-III cities like Vijayawada, [[Kakinada|Kakinada]] and [[Tirupati,_Andhra_Pradesh|Tirupati]] is also improving.
sentence_233: In the fiscal year 2012–2013, Vijayawada's IT/ITeS revenues were ₹1,153 million (US$16 million).
sentence_234: Tirupati with ₹693 million (US$9.7 million) and Kakinada with ₹615 million (US$8.6 million) stand next.
sentence_235: For the benefit of state i.e., after separating Telangana from Andhra, people of Andhra protested for special status during January in 2017
sentence_236: Andhra Pradesh is one of the storehouses of mineral resources in India.
sentence_237: Andhra Pradesh with varied geological formations, contain rich and variety of industrial minerals and building stones.
sentence_238: Andhra Pradesh is listed at the top in the deposit and production of mica in India.
sentence_239: Minerals found in the state include limestone, reserves of oil and natural gas, manganese, asbestos, iron ore, ball clay, fire clay, gold diamonds, graphite, dolomite, quartz, tungsten, steatitic, feldspar, silica sand.
sentence_240: It has about one-third of India's [[Limestone|limestone]] reserves and is known for large exclusive deposits of barytes and galaxy granite in the international market.
sentence_241: Mining is identified as one of the growth engines for the overall development of industry and infrastructure.
sentence_242: The [[Tummalapalle_Uranium_mine|Tummalapalle Uranium mine]] in Andhra has confirmed 49,000 tonnes (48,000 long tons; 54,000 short tons) of ore and there are indications that it could hold reserves totaling three times its current size.
sentence_243: 700 million tonnes (690,000,000 long tons; 770,000,000 short tons) of metal grade Bauxite deposits in proximity to Visakhapatnam Port.
sentence_244: Reliance Industries Limited struck nine trillion cubic feet of gas reserves in the [[Krishna_Godavari_Basin|KG basin]], 150 km (93 mi) off the Andhra Pradesh coast near [[Kakinada|Kakinada]].
sentence_245: Discovery of a large quantity of natural gas in KG Basin is expected to provide rapid economic growth.
sentence_246: During 2016, nearly 3.8 trillion m (134 trillion cu ft) of [[Methane_clathrate|methane hydrate]] deposits were explored in KG basin whose extraction was adequate to impart [[Energy_security|energy security]] for many decades to India.
sentence_247: Main article: [[Power_sector_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Power sector of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_248: The state is a pioneer nationwide in solar power generation.
sentence_249: [[APGENCO|APGENCO]] is the power generating company owned by the state.
sentence_250: The state has become power surplus with excess power generation being exported to other states.
sentence_251: The state is abundantly endowed with solar power and high head [[Pumped_hydroelectric_energy_storage|PHES]] sites to convert the solar power available during the day time in to round the clock power supply.
sentence_252: PHES projects also has synergy with the lift irrigation projects in storing water available during the monsoon season and supplying to the uplands throughout the year.
sentence_253: Ultimate water and energy requirements of the state can be fully met by the combination of cheap solar power, PHES and irrigation projects economically harnessing renewable energy without much damage to the environment.
sentence_254: Thermal (natural gas and coal based) and [[Renewable_power|renewable power]] plants totaling to 21,000 MW were installed in the state by the year 2015.
sentence_255: Local power plants of 9,600 [[Megawatt|MW]] capacity only are supplying electricity in the state which includes Simhadri Super Thermal Power Plant (2000 MW) of [[NTPC_Limited|NTPC]], [[Vizag_Thermal_Power_Station|Vizag Thermal Power Station]] (1040 MW), Rayalaseema Thermal Power Station (1650 MW), [[Sri_Damodaram_Sanjeevaiah_Thermal_Power_Station|Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah Thermal Power Station]] (1600 MW), [[Vijayawada_Thermal_Power_Plant|Vijayawada Thermal Power Plant]] (1760 MW), etc. Hydel power plants have a capacity of 1671 MW.
sentence_256: Main article: Culture of Andhra Pradesh
sentence_257: Andhra Pradesh has rich culture and heritage.
sentence_258: [[Kuchipudi|Kuchipudi]], the cultural dance recognized as the official dance form of the state of Andhra Pradesh, originated in the village of [[Kuchipudi,_Krishna_district|Kuchipudi]] in Krishna district.
sentence_259: It entered the [[Guinness_World_Records|Guinness World Records]] for performing Mahabrinda Natyam with a total of 6,117 dancers in Vijayawada.
sentence_260: Andhra Pradesh has thirteen geographical indications in categories of agricultural [[Handicraft|handicrafts]], foodstuff and textiles as per Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.
sentence_261: It increased to fifteen with the addition of [[Banaganapalle_Mangoes|Banaganapalle Mangoes]] and [[Bandar_laddu|Bandar laddu]].
sentence_262: The other GI tagged goods are, [[Bobbili_Veena|Bobbili Veena]], [[Budithi_Bell_and_Brass_Craft|Budithi Bell and Brass Craft]], [[Dharmavaram_Handloom_Pattu_Sarees_and_Paavadas|Dharmavaram Handloom Pattu Sarees and Paavadas]], [[Guntur_Sannam|Guntur Sannam]], [[Kondapalli_Toys|Kondapalli Toys]], [[Machilipatnam_Kalamkari|Machilipatnam Kalamkari]], [[Mangalagiri_Sarees_and_Fabrics|Mangalagiri Sarees and Fabrics]], [[Srikalahasti_Kalamkari|Srikalahasti Kalamkari]], [[Tirupati_Laddu|Tirupati Laddu]], [[Uppada_Jamdani_Sari|Uppada Jamdani Sari]] and [[Venkatagiri_Sari|Venkatagiri Sari]].
sentence_263: Machilipatnam and Srikalahasti Kalamkari are the two unique textile art forms practised in India.
sentence_264: There are also other notable handicrafts present in the state, like the soft [[Limestone|limestone]] [[Cult_image|idol]] carvings of [[Durgi|Durgi]].
sentence_265: Etikoppaka in [[Visakhapatnam_district|Visakhapatnam district]] is notable for its [[Lac|lac]] industry, producing lacquered wooden.
sentence_266: The state has many museums, which features a varied collection of ancient sculptures, paintings, idols, weapons, cutlery, and inscriptions, and religious artifacts such as the [[Amaravati_Archaeological_Museum|Amaravati Archaeological Museum]], [[Visakha_Museum|Visakha Museum]] and Telugu Cultural Museum in Visakhapatnam displays the history of the pre-independence and the [[Victoria_Jubilee_Museum|Victoria Jubilee Museum]] in Vijayawada with a large collection of artifacts.
sentence_267: Main article: [[Telugu_literature|Telugu literature]]
sentence_268: Nannayya, Tikkana and Yerrapragada form the trinity who translated the [[Sanskrit|Sanskrit]] epic [[Mahabharata|Mahabharata]] into [[Telugu_language|Telugu language]].
sentence_269: Nannayya wrote the first treatise on Telugu grammar called Andhra Shabda Chintamani in Sanskrit, as there was no grammatical work in Telugu prior to that.
sentence_270: [[Pothana|Pothana]] is the poet who composed the classic Srimad Maha Bhagavatamu, a Telugu translation of Sri Bhagavatam.
sentence_271: Vemana is notable for his philosophical poems.
sentence_272: The [[Vijayanagara|Vijayanagara]] emperor [[Krishnadevaraya|Krishnadevaraya]] wrote [[Amuktamalyada|Amuktamalyada]].
sentence_273: Telugu literature after Kandukuri Veeresalingam is termed as Adhunika Telugu Sahityam (Modern Telugu literature).
sentence_274: He is known as Gadya Tikkana and was the author of Telugu [[Social_novel|social novel]], Satyavati Charitam.
sentence_275: [[Jnanpith_Award|Jnanpith Award]] holders from the state include Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
sentence_276: The Andhra Pradesh native and revolutionary poet [[Srirangam_Srinivasarao|Sri Sri]] brought new forms of expressionism into Telugu literature.
sentence_277: The print media in the state consists mainly of Telugu and English newspapers.
sentence_278: [[Sakshi_(newspaper)|Sakshi]], Andhra Jyothi, and Tel.J.D.Patrika Vaartha all these are Telugu newspapers.
sentence_279: English newspapers include [[Deccan_Chronicle|Deccan Chronicle]] and The Hans India.
sentence_280: Main articles: [[Music_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Music of Andhra Pradesh]] and [[Telugu_theatre|Telugu theatre]]
sentence_281: See also: [[Tholu_bommalata|Tholu bommalata]]
sentence_282: Many composers of [[Carnatic_music|Carnatic music]] like [[Annamacharya|Annamacharya]], Kshetrayya, and [[Bhadrachala_Ramadas|Bhadrachala Ramadas]] were of Telugu descent.
sentence_283: Modern Carnatic music composers and singers like [[Ghantasala_(singer)|Ghantasala]], Sujatha Puligella and [[M._Balamuralikrishna|M.
sentence_284: Balamuralikrishna]] are also of Telugu descent.
sentence_285: The Telugu film industry hosts many music composers and playback singers such as [[S._P._Balasubrahmanyam|S.
sentence_286: P. Balasubrahmanyam]], [[P._Susheela|P.
sentence_287: Susheela]], [[S._Janaki|S.
sentence_288: Janaki]] and [[P._B._Sreenivas|P.
sentence_289: B. Sreenivas]].
sentence_290: Folk songs are very important and popular in the many rural areas of the state.
sentence_291: Forms such as the [[Burra_katha|Burra katha]] and Poli are still performed today.
sentence_292: Harikathaa Kalakshepam (or Harikatha) involves the narration of a story, intermingled with various songs relating to the story.
sentence_293: Harikatha was originated in Andhra.
sentence_294: Burra katha is an oral storytelling technique with the topic be either a [[Hindu|Hindu]] mythological story or a contemporary social issue.
sentence_295: Rangasthalam is an Indian theatre in the [[Telugu_language|Telugu language]], based predominantly in Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_296: [[Gurazada_Apparao|Gurazada Apparao]] wrote the play [[Kanyasulkam|Kanyasulkam]] in 1892, often considered the greatest play in the Telugu language.
sentence_297: [[C._Pullaiah|C.
sentence_298: Pullaiah]] is cited as the father of Telugu theatre movement.
sentence_299: The Telugu film industry is largely based in Hyderabad and Visakhapatnam.
sentence_300: The Telugu film culture (also known as "[[Telugu_cinema|Tollywood]]") is the second-largest film industry in India next to the [[Bollywood|Bollywood]] film industry.
sentence_301: Film producer [[D._Ramanaidu|D.
sentence_302: Ramanaidu]] holds a [[Guinness_Record|Guinness Record]] for the most films produced by a person.
sentence_303: In the years 2005, 2006 and 2008, the Telugu film industry produced the largest number of films in India, exceeding the number of films produced in Bollywood.
sentence_304: The industry holds the Guinness World Record for the largest film production facility in the world.
sentence_305: Main article: Telugu cuisine
sentence_306: Telugu people's traditional sweet [[Pootharekulu|Pootharekulu]] originated from Atreyapuram village, Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_307: Main article: [[Tourism_in_Andhra_Pradesh|Tourism in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_308: The state has several beaches in its coastal districts such as [[Rushikonda|Rushikonda]], [[Mypadu|Mypadu]], Suryalanka etc.; caves such as, [[Borra_Caves|Borra Caves]], [[Indian_rock-cut_architecture|Indian rock-cut architecture]] depicting [[Undavalli_caves|Undavalli caves]] and the country's second longest caves- the [[Belum_Caves|Belum Caves]].
sentence_309: The valleys and hills include, [[Araku_Valley|Araku Valley]], [[Horsley_Hills|Horsley Hills]], [[Papi_Hills|Papi Hills]] etc. [[Arma_Konda|Arma Konda]] peak located in Visakhapatnam district is the highest peak in Eastern Ghats.
sentence_310: The state is home to various religious pilgrim destinations such as, [[Tirumala_Temple|Tirumala Temple]], [[Simhachalam_Temple|Simhachalam Temple]], [[Annavaram|Annavaram]], [[Mallikarjuna_Swamy|Srisailam temple]], [[Kanaka_Durga_Temple|Kanaka Durga Temple]], [[Amaralingeswara_Swamy|Amaravati]], [[Srikalahasti|Srikalahasti]], [[Shahi_jamia_masjid|Shahi jamia masjid]] in [[Adoni|Adoni]], Gunadala Church in [[Vijayawada|Vijayawada]], Buddhist centres at [[Amaravathi_village,_Guntur_district|Amaravati]], and [[Nagarjuna_Konda|Nagarjuna Konda]].
sentence_311: The state is well connected to other states through road and rail networks.
sentence_312: It is also connected to other countries by means of airways and seaports as well.
sentence_313: With a long seacoast along the [[Bay_of_Bengal|Bay of Bengal]], it also has many ports for sea trade.
sentence_314: The state has one of the largest railway junctions at Vijayawada and one of the largest seaports at Visakhapatnam.
sentence_315: The state has a total road network of 53,403 km (33,183 mi), of which 6,401 km (3,977 mi) of [[National_Highway_(India)|National highways]], 14,722 km (9,148 mi) of state highways and 32,280 km (20,060 mi) of district roads.
sentence_316: [[National_Highway_5_(India)(old_numbering)|NH 16]], with a highway network of around 1,000 km (620 mi) in the state, is a part of [[Golden_Quadrilateral_Project|Golden Quadrilateral Project]] undertaken by [[National_Highways_Development_Project|National Highways Development Project]].
sentence_317: It also forms part of [[Asian_Highway|AH 45]] which comes under the [[Asian_Highway_Network|Asian Highway Network]].
sentence_318: The state government owned Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) is the major public bus transport, which runs thousands of buses connecting different parts of the state.
sentence_319: [[Pandit_Nehru_Bus_Station|Pandit Nehru Bus Station]] (PNBS) in Vijayawada is one of the largest bus terminals in Asia.
sentence_320: From 30 January 2019, all the vehicles in the state are registered as [[List_of_RTO_districts_in_India|AP–39]], followed by an alphabet and four digits.
sentence_321: See also: [[South_Coast_Railway_zone|South Coast Railway zone]]
sentence_322: Andhra Pradesh has a total [[Broad_gauge|broad gauge]] railway route of 3,703.25 km (2,301.09 mi) and has no [[Metre_gauge_railway|metre gauge railway]].
sentence_323: The rail density of the state is 16.59 per 1,000 km (620 mi), compared to an all India average of 20.
sentence_324: The [[Howrah–Chennai_main_line|Howrah–Chennai main line]] which runs through the state is proposed to be upgraded into a high-speed rail corridor through the [[Diamond_Quadrilateral|Diamond Quadrilateral]] project of the Indian Railways.
sentence_325: The railway network spans two [[Zones_and_divisions_of_Indian_Railways|zones]], further subdivided into divisions – [[Vijayawada_railway_division|Vijayawada]], [[Guntur_railway_division|Guntur]] and [[Guntakal_railway_division|Guntakal railway divisions]] of South Central Railway zone, and Waltair railway division of East Coast Railway zone.
sentence_326: There is a demand for creating a unified zone for the state based out of Visakhapatnam.
sentence_327: There are three A1 and twenty three A-category railway stations in the state.
sentence_328: [[Visakhapatnam_railway_station|Visakhapatnam railway station]] has been declared the cleanest railway station in the country.
sentence_329: The railway station of [[Shimiliguda|Shimiliguda]] was the first highest [[Broad_gauge|broad gauge]] railway station in the country.
sentence_330: As on date the Railways lines in Andhra Pradesh are under the following Railway zones/Divisions
sentence_331: See also: [[List_of_airports_in_Andhra_Pradesh|List of airports in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_332: [[Visakhapatnam_Airport|Visakhapatnam Airport]], is the only airport in the state with operating international flights while [[Vijayawada_Airport|Vijayawada Airport]] at Gannavaram has launched an international flight to Singapore, recently.
sentence_333: The state has four other domestic airports, [[Rajahmundry_Airport|Rajahmundry Airport]], [[Cuddapah_Airport|Cuddapah Airport]], a privately owned, public use airport at [[Sri_Sathya_Sai_Airport|Puttaparthi]], and [[Tirupati_Airport|Tirupati Airport]] located in the city of [[Tirupati|Tirupati]].
sentence_334: There are also 16 small air strips located in the state.
sentence_335: See also: [[Ports_and_harbours_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Ports and harbours of Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_336: Andhra Pradesh has one of the country's largest port at [[Visakhapatnam_Port|Visakhapatnam]] in terms of cargo handling.
sentence_337: The other famous ports are [[Krishnapatnam_Port|Krishnapatnam Port]] ([[Nellore_district|Nellore]]), [[Gangavaram_Port|Gangavaram Port]] and [[Kakinada_Port|Kakinada Port]].
sentence_338: [[Gangavaram_Port|Gangavaram Port]] is a deep seaport which can accommodate ocean liners up to 200,000–250,000 [[Deadweight_tonnage|DWT]].
sentence_339: There are 14 notified non-major ports at Bheemunipatnam, S.Yanam, Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, and Vadarevu.
sentence_340: Main article: Education in Andhra Pradesh
sentence_341: Andhra Pradesh has an overall [[Literacy_rate|literacy rate]] of 67.41% as per the 2011 Indian census.
sentence_342: The primary and secondary school education is imparted by government, aided and private schools, managed and regulated by the School Education Department of the state.
sentence_343: There are urban, rural and residential schools.
sentence_344: As per the child info and school information report (2018–19), there were a total of 7,041,568 students, enrolled in 62,063 schools respectively.
sentence_345: The Directorate of Government Examinations of the state administers and conduct the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination.
sentence_346: More than 600,000 students have appeared for the 2019 SSC exam and recorded an overall pass percentage of 94.88% with a 100% pass percentage in 5,464 schools.
sentence_347: The mediums of instruction are primarily [[Telugu_language|Telugu]] and English with a very few opting for [[Urdu|Urdu]], [[Hindi|Hindi]], [[Kannada_language|Kannada]], [[Odia_language|Odia]] and [[Tamil_language|Tamil]].
sentence_348: Higher education in the state is administered by the Department of Higher Education.
sentence_349: The central universities are [[All_India_Institute_of_Medical_Sciences|All India Institute of Medical Sciences]], [[Indian_Institute_of_Management_Visakhapatnam|IIM Visakhapatnam]], [[Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Tirupati|IIT Tirupati]], NIT Tadepalligudem, [[Indian_Institute_of_Information_Technology_Design_and_Manufacturing,_Kurnool|IIITDM Kurnool]], [[Indian_Institute_of_Petroleum_and_Energy|Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy]], [[National_Institute_of_Design,_Vijayawada|NIDV]], Central University of Andhra Pradesh, [[Indian_Institute_of_Information_Technology,_Sri_City|IIIT Sri City]], [[IISER_Tirupati|IISER Tirupati]], Agriculture University, Guntur and IIFT Kakinada.
sentence_350: The [[Government_of_Andhra_Pradesh|Government of Andhra Pradesh]] established Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT) in 2008 to cater to the education needs of the rural youth of Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_351: As per the University Grants Commission, [[Gandhi_Institute_of_Technology_and_Management|GITAM]], [[K_L_University|K L University]] and Vignan University are the [[Deemed_Universities|Deemed Universities]] in the state.
sentence_352: There are 18 state universities in the districts providing higher education in horticulture, law, medical, technology, [[Vedic|Vedic]] and [[Veterinary|veterinary]].
sentence_353: [[Andhra_University|Andhra University]] is the oldest of the universities in the state, established in 1926.
sentence_354: Research institutes have been set up by the central state government.
sentence_355: Naval Science & Technological Laboratory (NSTL), National Institute of Oceanography, Visakhapatnam (NIO), [[School_of_Planning_and_Architecture,_Vijayawada|School of Planning and Architecture]] at Vijayawada is an autonomous research institute under Ministry of Human Resource Development of [[Government_of_India|Government of India]], [[National_Atmospheric_Research_Laboratory|National Atmospheric Research Laboratory]] carry out fundamental and applied research in atmospheric and space sciences, [[Indian_Institute_of_Science_Education_and_Research,_Tirupati|Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Tirupati]], Society for Applied Microwave Electronics Engineering and Research, Visakhapatnam Central Tobacco Research Institute, [[Rajahmundry|Rajahmundry]] under control of ICAR (Indian Council of Agriculture Research) conducts fundamental and applied research on tobacco for the benefit of the farming community, Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research (IIOPR) at Pedavegi near [[Eluru|Eluru]] in [[West_Godavari_district|West Godavari district]] serves as a centre for conducting and co-ordinating research on all aspects of oil palm conservation, improvement, production, protection, post-harvest technology and transfer of technology, CCRH Regional Research Institute at [[Gudivada|Gudivada]], Clinical Research Institute at [[Tirupati|Tirupati]] and National Institute of Oceanography at Visakhapatnam are some of them.
sentence_356: [[Satish_Dhawan_Space_Centre|Satish Dhawan Space Centre]], also known as Sriharikota Range (SHAR), at barrier island of [[Sriharikota|Sriharikota]] in [[Nellore_district|Nellore district]] of Andhra Pradesh is a satellite launching station operated by [[Indian_Space_Research_Organisation|Indian Space Research Organisation]].
sentence_357: It is India's primary orbital launch site.
sentence_358: India's lunar orbiter [[Chandrayaan-1|Chandrayaan-1]] was launched from the centre at 6:22 [[Ante_meridiem|AM]] [[Indian_Standard_Time|IST]] on 22 October 2008.
sentence_359: Main article: [[Sports_in_Andhra_Pradesh|Sports in Andhra Pradesh]]
sentence_360: The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh is the governing body which looks after the infrastructure development in [[Cricket|cricket]], [[Field_hockey|field hockey]], association football, Skating, [[Olympic_weightlifting|Olympic weightlifting]], [[Chess|chess]], water sports, [[Tennis|tennis]], [[Badminton|badminton]], [[Table_tennis|table tennis]], cycling, etc.
sentence_361: [[Cricket|Cricket]] is one of the most popular sports in the state.
sentence_362: The ACA-VDCA Stadium in [[Visakhapatnam|Visakhapatnam]] is the home to [[Andhra_Pradesh_cricket_team|Andhra Pradesh cricket team]].
sentence_363: The venue regularly hosts international as well as domestic matches.
sentence_364: Notable cricketers from Andhra Pradesh include former Indian captain [[Mohammad_Azharuddin|Mohammad Azharuddin]], [[Maharajkumar_of_Vizianagram|Maharajkumar of Vizianagram]], [[M._V._Narasimha_Rao|M.
sentence_365: V. Narasimha Rao]], [[M._S._K._Prasad|M.
sentence_366: S. K. Prasad]], [[V._V._S._Laxman|V.
sentence_367: V. S. Laxman]], [[Tirumalasetti_Suman|Tirumalasetti Suman]], [[Arshad_Ayub|Arshad Ayub]], [[Ambati_Rayudu|Ambati Rayudu]], [[Venkatapathy_Raju|Venkatapathy Raju]], [[Sravanthi_Naidu|Sravanthi Naidu]], [[Yalaka_Venugopal_Rao|Yalaka Venugopal Rao]] and [[Hanuma_Vihari|Hanuma Vihari]].
sentence_368: [[Humpy_Koneru|Humpy Koneru]], from [[Gudivada|Gudivada]] in Krishna district, is an Indian [[Chess|chess]] [[International_Grandmaster|Grandmaster]].
sentence_369: [[Karnam_Malleswari|Karnam Malleswari]], the first female Indian to win an [[Olympic_medal|Olympic medal]], hails from [[Srikakulam_district|Srikakulam district]] of Andhra Pradesh.
sentence_370: She won the bronze medal on 19 September 2000, in the 69 kg (152 lb) category with a lift of 240 kg (530 lb).
sentence_371: [[Krishnam_Raju_Gadiraju|Krishnam Raju Gadiraju]] of [[Bhimavaram|Bhimavaram]], Andhra Pradesh, is a four-time world record holder.
sentence_372: He is a speedsolver and [[Unicycle|Unicyclist]].
sentence_373: [[Pullela_Gopichand|Pullela Gopichand]] is a former Indian [[Badminton|badminton]] player.
sentence_374: He won the [[All_England_Open_Badminton_Championships|All England Open Badminton Championships]] in 2001, becoming the second Indian to win after [[Prakash_Padukone|Prakash Padukone]].
sentence_375: Cherukuri Lenin (1985 or 1986 – 24 October 2010) was an Indian archer and coach who won a silver medal at the Asian Grand Prix in Malaysia and was a national archery coach.
