title: AFC Ajax
sentence_0: For the women's team, see [[AFC_Ajax_Vrouwen|AFC Ajax Vrouwen]].
sentence_1: Amsterdamsche Football Club Ajax (Dutch pronunciation: [[Dutch|[ˈaːjɑks]]), also known as AFC Ajax, Ajax Amsterdam, or simply Ajax, is a Dutch professional [[Association_football|football]] [[Football_team|club]] based in [[Amsterdam|Amsterdam]], that plays in the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], the top tier in Dutch football.
sentence_2: Historically, Ajax (named after the [[Ajax_the_Great|legendary Greek hero]]) has been the most successful club in the [[Netherlands|Netherlands]], with 34 [[List_of_Dutch_football_champions|Eredivisie titles]] and 19 [[KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cups]].
sentence_3: It has continuously played in the Eredivisie, since the league's inception in 1956 and, along with [[Feyenoord|Feyenoord]] and [[PSV_Eindhoven|PSV Eindhoven]], it is one of the country's "[[Big_Three_(Netherlands)|big three]]" clubs that have dominated that competition.
sentence_4: Ajax has historically been one of the most successful clubs in the world.
sentence_5: According to the [[International_Federation_of_Football_History_&_Statistics|IFFHS]], Ajax were the seventh-most successful European club of the 20th century and The World's Club Team of the Year in 1992.
sentence_6: According to German magazine [[Kicker_(sports_magazine)|Kicker]], Ajax were the second-most successful European club of the 20th century.
sentence_7: The club is one of the five teams that has [[European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently|earned the right]] to keep the [[UEFA_Champions_League|European Cup]] and to wear a multiple-winner badge; they won consecutively in 1971–1973.
sentence_8: In 1972, they completed the [[Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles|continental treble]] by winning the [[1971–72_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], [[1971–72_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]], and the [[1971–72_European_Cup|European Cup]].
sentence_9: It also won the first organized [[UEFA_Super_Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] in 1972 against [[Rangers_FC|Glasgow Rangers]] (played in 1973).
sentence_10: Ajax's last international trophies were the [[1995_Intercontinental_Cup|1995 Intercontinental Cup]], [[1995_UEFA_Super_Cup|1995 UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[1994–95_UEFA_Champions_League|1995 Champions League]], where they defeated [[A.C._Milan|Milan]] in the [[1995_UEFA_Champions_League_Final|final]]; they lost the [[1995–96_UEFA_Champions_League|1996 Champions League]] [[1996_UEFA_Champions_League_Final|final]] on [[Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football)|penalties]] to [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]].
sentence_11: In 1995, Ajax was crowned as World Team of the Year by [[World_Soccer_(magazine)|World Soccer]] magazine.
sentence_12: Ajax is also one of four teams to win the [[Treble_(association_football)#Continental_Trebles|continental treble]] and the [[Intercontinental_Cup_(football)|Intercontinental Cup]] or [[FIFA_Club_World_Cup|Club World Cup]] in the same season/calendar year; This was achieved in the 1971–72 season.
sentence_13: Ajax are one of the five clubs to have won all three major UEFA club competitions.
sentence_14: They have also won the [[Intercontinental_Cup_(football)|Intercontinental Cup]] twice, the [[1991–92_UEFA_Cup|1991–92 UEFA Cup]], as well as the [[1961–62_Intertoto_Cup|Karl Rappan Cup]], a predecessor of the [[UEFA_Intertoto_Cup|UEFA Intertoto Cup]] in 1962.
sentence_15: Ajax plays at the [[Johan_Cruyff_Arena|Johan Cruyff Arena]], which opened as the Amsterdam ArenA in 1996 and was renamed in 2018.
sentence_16: They previously played at De Meer Stadion and the [[Olympic_Stadium_(Amsterdam)|Amsterdam Olympic Stadium]] (for international matches).
sentence_17: Main article: History of AFC Ajax
sentence_18: Ajax was founded in Amsterdam on 18 March 1900.
sentence_19: The club achieved promotion to the highest level of Dutch football in 1911 and had its first major success in 1917, winning the [[KNVB_Beker|KNVB Beker]], the Netherlands' national cup.
sentence_20: The [[1917–18_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|following season]], Ajax became [[List_of_Dutch_football_champions|national champion]] for the first time.
sentence_21: The club defended its title in [[1918–19_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1918–19]], becoming the only team to achieve an unbeaten season in the Netherlands Football League Championship.
sentence_22: Throughout the 1920s, Ajax was a strong regional power, winning the Eerste Klasse West division in 1921, 1927 and 1928, but could not maintain its success at national level.
sentence_23: This changed in the 1930s, with the club winning five national championships ([[1930–31_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1931]], [[1931–32_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1932]], [[1933–34_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1934]], [[1936–37_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1937]], [[1938–39_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1939]]), making it the most successful Dutch team of the decade.
sentence_24: Ajax won its second KNVB Cup in 1942–43, and an eighth Dutch title in [[1946–47_Netherlands_Football_League_Championship|1946–47]], the last season the club was managed by Englishman [[Jack_Reynolds_(footballer,_born_1881)|Jack Reynolds]], who, up to this point, had overseen all of its national championship successes as well as its 1917 KNVB Cup win.
sentence_25: In 1956, the [[1956–57_Eredivisie|first season]] of the Netherlands' new professional league, the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], was played with Ajax participating as a founding member.
sentence_26: The Amsterdam club became the first national champions under the new format and made its debut in the [[European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup|European Champion Clubs' Cup]] the [[1957–58_European_Cup|following year]], losing to Hungarian champions [[Vasas_SC|Vasas SC]] 6–2 on aggregate at the quarter-final stage.
sentence_27: The team were again Eredivisie champions in [[1959–60_Eredivisie|1960]] and won a third KNVB Cup in 1961.
sentence_28: In 1965, [[Rinus_Michels|Rinus Michels]], who had played for the club between 1946 and 1958, was appointed manager of Ajax, implementing his philosophy of [[Total_Football|Total Football]] which was to become synonymous with both Ajax and the [[Netherlands_national_football_team|Netherlands national team]].
sentence_29: A year earlier, [[Johan_Cruyff|Johan Cruyff]], who would go on to become the greatest Dutch footballer of all-time, made his debut.
sentence_30: Between them, Michels and Cruyff led Ajax through the most successful period in its history, winning seven Eredivisie titles, four KNVB Cups and three European Cups.
sentence_31: Ajax won the Dutch championship in [[1965–66_Eredivisie|1966]], [[1966–67_Eredivisie|1967]] and [[1967–68_Eredivisie|1968]], and reached the [[1969_European_Cup_Final|1969 European Cup final]], losing to [[A.C._Milan|Milan]].
sentence_32: During the 1966–67 season, Ajax scored a record 122 goals in an Eredivisie season and also won the KNVB Cup to achieve its first league and cup [[Double_(association_football)|double]].
sentence_33: In [[1969–70_Eredivisie|1969–70]], Ajax won a fourth Dutch league championship and second league and cup double in five seasons, winning 27 out of 34 league matches and scoring 100 goals.
sentence_34: The [[1970–71_Eredivisie|1970–71 season]] saw Ajax retain the [[1970–71_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]] and reach the 1971 European Cup final, where they defeated [[Panathinaikos_F.C.|Panathinaikos]] 2–0 with goals from [[Dick_van_Dijk|Dick van Dijk]] and [[Arie_Haan|Arie Haan]] to become continental champions for the first time, with Cruyff being named [[Ballon_d'Or_(1956–2009)|European Footballer of the Year]].
sentence_35: After this success, Michels departed to become manager of [[FC_Barcelona|Barcelona]] and was replaced by the Romanian Ștefan Kovács.
sentence_36: In Kovács' first season, Ajax completed a [[Treble_(association_football)|treble]] of the [[1971–72_European_Cup|European Cup]], the [[1971–72_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] and a third consecutive [[1971–72_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]].
sentence_37: The following season, the team beat Argentine club [[Club_Atlético_Independiente|Independiente]] to win the [[1972_Intercontinental_Cup|1972 Intercontinental Cup]] and retained their [[1972–73_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] and [[1972–73_European_Cup|European Cup]] titles, becoming the first club to win three consecutive European Cups since [[Real_Madrid_C.F.|Real Madrid]] in the 1950s.
sentence_38: In 1973, Michels' Barcelona broke the world transfer record to bring Cruyff to Catalonia.
sentence_39: Kovács also departed to become manager of the [[France_national_football_team|France national team]], signalling the end of this period of international success.
sentence_40: In [[1976–77_Eredivisie|1976–77]], Ajax won its first domestic championship in four seasons and recorded a double of the [[1977–78_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] and [[1977–78_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]] two years later.
sentence_41: The early 1980s saw the return of Johan Cruyff to the club, as well as the emergence of young players [[Marco_van_Basten|Marco van Basten]] and [[Frank_Rijkaard|Frank Rijkaard]].
sentence_42: The team won back-to-back Eredivisie titles in [[1981–82_Eredivisie|1982]] and [[1982–83_Eredivisie|1983]], with all three playing a significant role in the latter.
sentence_43: After Cruyff's sale to rivals [[Feyenoord|Feyenoord]] in 1983, Van Basten became Ajax's key player, top scoring in the Eredivisie for four seasons between [[1983–84_Eredivisie|1983–84]] and [[1986–87_Eredivisie|1986–87]].
sentence_44: In 1985, Cruyff returned to Ajax as manager and the team ended [[1985–86_Eredivisie|his first season in charge]] with 120 goals from 34 matches.
sentence_45: However, Ajax still finished as runner-up to [[PSV_Eindhoven|PSV]] by eight points.
sentence_46: The following season, Ajax again lost out on the [[1986–87_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] title to PSV, but won the [[1986–87_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]], its first continental trophy in 14 years.
sentence_47: After this, Cruyff left the club to become manager of Barcelona and Rijkaard and Van Basten were sold to [[Sporting_CP|Sporting CP]] and Milan respectively.
sentence_48: Despite these losses, Ajax reached a second consecutive Cup Winners' Cup final in [[1988_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final|1988]], where they lost to Belgian club [[KV_Mechelen|KV Mechelen]].
sentence_49: The [[1988–89_Eredivisie|1988–89]] season saw [[Dennis_Bergkamp|Dennis Bergkamp]], a young forward who had first appeared under Cruyff in 1986, establish himself as a regular goalscorer for Ajax.
sentence_50: Bergkamp helped Ajax to the [[1989–90_Eredivisie|1989–90 Eredivisie]] title and was the top scorer in the division in [[1990–91_Eredivisie|1990–91]], [[1991–92_Eredivisie|1991–92]] and [[1992–93_Eredivisie|1992–93]].
sentence_51: Under the management of [[Louis_van_Gaal|Louis van Gaal]], Ajax won the [[UEFA_Europa_League|UEFA Cup]] in [[1991–92_UEFA_Cup|1992]] to become the second club, after [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]], to have won all three [[List_of_UEFA_club_competition_winners|major European club competitions]].
sentence_52: After the sale of Bergkamp to [[Inter_Milan|Internazionale]] in 1993, Van Gaal re-signed the experienced Frank Rijkaard to complement his young Ajax team featuring academy graduates [[Frank_de_Boer|Frank]] and [[Ronald_de_Boer|Ronald de Boer]], [[Edwin_van_der_Sar|Edwin van der Sar]], [[Clarence_Seedorf|Clarence Seedorf]], [[Edgar_Davids|Edgar Davids]], [[Michael_Reiziger|Michael Reiziger]] and [[Winston_Bogarde|Winston Bogarde]], as well as mercurial foreign talents [[Finidi_George|Finidi George]], [[Nwankwo_Kanu|Nwankwo Kanu]] and [[Jari_Litmanen|Jari Litmanen]], and veteran captain [[Danny_Blind|Danny Blind]].
sentence_53: The team regained the Dutch championship in [[1993–94_Eredivisie|1993–94]], and won it again in [[1994–95_Eredivisie|1994–95]] and [[1995–96_Eredivisie|1995–96]] to become the first Ajax side to win three back-to-back championships since 1968.
sentence_54: The height of Van Gaal's success came in 1994–95, where Ajax became the first, and to date only, team to complete an entire Eredivisie season unbeaten.
sentence_55: The team also won its first European Cup since its glorious 1970s era, defeating Milan in the [[1995_UEFA_Champions_League_Final|1995 UEFA Champions League final]] 1–0, with the winning goal scored by 18-year-old [[Patrick_Kluivert|Patrick Kluivert]].
sentence_56: Ajax again reached [[1996_UEFA_Champions_League_Final|the final]] one year later, but were defeated on penalties by Juventus.
sentence_57: Ajax's return as a European force was short lived as Van Gaal and several members of the squad soon departed to some of the continent's biggest clubs.
sentence_58: The 2000s was a lean decade for the club with only two Eredivisie championships won.
sentence_59: However, Ajax's academy continued to produce star players such as [[Wesley_Sneijder|Wesley Sneijder]] and [[Rafael_van_der_Vaart|Rafael van der Vaart]].
sentence_60: In 2010, Frank de Boer was appointed manager of Ajax and led the club to its first league title in seven years, and record 30th title overall, in the [[2010–11_Eredivisie|2010–11 season]].
sentence_61: This was followed by back-to-back wins in [[2011–12_Eredivisie|2011–12]] and [[2012–13_Eredivisie|2012–13]] to match his three consecutive titles as a player in the 1990s.
sentence_62: In [[2013–14_Eredivisie|2013–14]], Ajax were again Eredivisie champions, winning four consecutive league titles for the first time in club history.
sentence_63: After finishing as runner-up to PSV in both [[2014–15_Eredivisie|2014–15]] and [[2015–16_Eredivisie|2015–16]], De Boer resigned as Ajax head coach in May 2016.
sentence_64: [[Peter_Bosz|Peter Bosz]] took over the club and led them to the [[2017_UEFA_Europa_League_Final|2017 UEFA Europa League final]], their first European final in 21 years.
sentence_65: They lost to [[Manchester_United_F.C.|Manchester United]] with a lineup that was the youngest ever in a European final, averaging an age of 22 years and 282 days.
sentence_66: For the third consecutive season, they finished runner-up in the [[2016–17_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], this time to Feyenoord.
sentence_67: The [[2018–19_AFC_Ajax_season|2018–19 season]] for Ajax involved a remarkable run in the [[2018–19_UEFA_Champions_League|UEFA Champions League]].
sentence_68: Due to their runner-up finish in the [[2017–18_Eredivisie|2017–18 Eredivisie]], Ajax entered the tournament in the second qualifying round.
sentence_69: After successive victories against [[SK_Sturm_Graz|Sturm Graz]], [[Standard_Liège|Standard Liège]] and [[FC_Dynamo_Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]], they qualified for the group stage.
sentence_70: Ajax was drawn in a group with German champions [[FC_Bayern_Munich|Bayern Munich]], Portuguese side [[S.L._Benfica|Benfica]] and Greek champions [[AEK_Athens_F.C.|AEK Athens]].
sentence_71: Ajax finished runner-up in this group, qualifying for the knockout stages, where they were drawn against three-time defending champions [[Real_Madrid_CF|Real Madrid]].
sentence_72: After losing 1–2 in the first leg, they defeated Real Madrid 4–1 in the away match, stunning the defending champions in their own stadium, the [[Santiago_Bernabéu_Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]], with an aggregate score of 5–3.
sentence_73: [[Dušan_Tadić|Dušan Tadić]] was awarded a perfect score of 10 by L'Équipe following the match.
sentence_74: Thus, Ajax progressed to quarter-finals and were drawn with Italian champions [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]].
sentence_75: In the first leg in the Johan Cruyff Arena, they drew 1–1.
sentence_76: In the second leg at the [[Juventus_Stadium|Juventus Stadium]], Ajax came from behind to win 2–1 and 3–2 on aggregate.
sentence_77: [[Matthijs_de_Ligt|Matthijs de Ligt]] scored the winning goal for Ajax to help the team advance to its first Champions League semi-final since [[1996–97_UEFA_Champions_League|1997]].
sentence_78: There, they would face English side [[Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].
sentence_79: In the first leg of the semi-final, Ajax beat Tottenham 1–0 away from home.
sentence_80: In the second leg, Ajax scored twice in the first half to generate a 3–0 lead on aggregate.
sentence_81: However, in the second half, [[Lucas_Moura|Lucas Moura]] scored three times, including in the 6th minute of added time, resulting in Ajax losing via the [[Away_goals_rule|away goals rule]].
sentence_82: Ajax were in first place on goal difference when the [[2019–20_Eredivisie|2019–20 Eredivisie]] was declared void, preventing them being Dutch champions for the 35th time, but still qualified for the [[2020–21_UEFA_Champions_League|2020–21 UEFA Champions League]].
sentence_83: See also: [[UEFA_coefficient|UEFA coefficient]]
sentence_84: Main articles: [[Ajax_Youth_Academy|Ajax Youth Academy]], [[Ajax_Hellas_Youth_Academy|Ajax Hellas Youth Academy]], and Ajax Coaching Academy
sentence_85: The club is also particularly famous for its renowned youth programme that has produced many Dutch talents over the years – [[Johan_Cruyff|Johan Cruyff]], [[Edwin_van_der_Sar|Edwin van der Sar]], [[Gerald_Vanenburg|Gerald Vanenburg]], [[Frank_Rijkaard|Frank Rijkaard]], [[Dennis_Bergkamp|Dennis Bergkamp]], [[Rafael_van_der_Vaart|Rafael van der Vaart]], [[Patrick_Kluivert|Patrick Kluivert]], [[Marco_van_Basten|Marco van Basten]], [[Wesley_Sneijder|Wesley Sneijder]], [[Maarten_Stekelenburg|Maarten Stekelenburg]], [[Nigel_de_Jong|Nigel de Jong]], [[Frenkie_de_Jong|Frenkie de Jong]], and [[Matthijs_de_Ligt|Matthijs de Ligt]] have come through the ranks and are just some of the talents who've played for Ajax.
sentence_86: Ajax also regularly supplies the Dutch national youth teams with local talent.
sentence_87: Due to mutual agreements with foreign clubs, the youth academy has also signed foreign players as teenagers before making first team debuts, such as Belgian defensive trio [[Jan_Vertonghen|Jan Vertonghen]], [[Toby_Alderweireld|Toby Alderweireld]] and [[Thomas_Vermaelen|Thomas Vermaelen]] along with winger [[Tom_De_Mul|Tom De Mul]], all of whom are full internationals, as well as Dutch international [[Vurnon_Anita|Vurnon Anita]] and [[Javier_Martina|Javier Martina]], representing [[Curaçao_national_football_team|Curaçao]].
sentence_88: Ajax has also expanded its talent searching programme to South Africa with [[Ajax_Cape_Town_FC|Ajax Cape Town]].
sentence_89: Ajax Cape Town was set up with the help of Rob Moore.
sentence_90: Ajax has also had a satellite club in the United States under the name [[Ajax_Orlando_Prospects|Ajax America]], until it filed for bankruptcy.
sentence_91: There are some youth players from Ajax Cape Town that have been drafted into the Eredivisie squad, such as South African internationals [[Steven_Pienaar|Steven Pienaar]], [[Thulani_Serero|Thulani Serero]] and Cameroonian international [[Eyong_Enoh|Eyong Enoh]].
sentence_92: In 1995, the year Ajax won the UEFA Champions League, the Netherlands national team was almost entirely composed of Ajax players, with Edwin van der Sar in goal; players such as Michael Reiziger, Frank de Boer and Danny Blind in defence; Ronald de Boer, Edgar Davids and Clarence Seedorf in midfield; and Patrick Kluivert and [[Marc_Overmars|Marc Overmars]] in attack.
sentence_93: In 2011, Ajax opened its first youth academies outside the Netherlands when the club partnered up with George Kazianis and All Star Consultancy in Greece to open the [[Ajax_Hellas_Youth_Academy|Ajax Hellas Youth Academy]].
sentence_94: The offices are based in [[Nea_Smyrni|Nea Smyrni]], [[Attica_(region)|Attica]], with the main training facility located on the island of [[Corfu|Corfu]], hosting a total of 15 football youth academies throughout Greece and Cyprus.
sentence_95: Eddie van Schaik heads the organization as coach and consultant, introducing the Ajax football philosophy at the various Greek football training camps.
sentence_96: In 2016, Ajax launched the ACA (Ajax Coaching Academy) with the intention of sharing knowledge, setting up a variety of camps and clinics for both players and coaches.
sentence_97: Main article: [[Stadiums_of_AFC_Ajax|Stadiums of AFC Ajax]]
sentence_98: Ajax's first stadium was built in 1911 out of wood and was called [[Het_Houten_Stadion|Het Houten Stadion]] ("The Wooden Stadium").
sentence_99: Ajax later played in the [[Olympic_Stadium_(Amsterdam)|Olympic Stadium]] built for the [[1928_Summer_Olympics|1928 Summer Olympics]] hosted in Amsterdam.
sentence_100: This stadium, designed by [[Jan_Wils|Jan Wils]], is known as the Olympic Stadium.
sentence_101: In 1934, Ajax moved to De Meer Stadion in east Amsterdam, designed by architect and Ajax-member [[Jordanus_Roodenburgh|Daan Roodenburgh]], who had also designed the club's first stadium.
sentence_102: It could accommodate 29,500 spectators and Ajax continued to play there until 1996.
sentence_103: For big European and national fixtures the club would often play at the Olympic Stadium, which could accommodate about twice the number of spectators.
sentence_104: In 1996, Ajax moved to a new home ground in the southeast of the city known as the Amsterdam Arena, since 2018 known as the [[Johan_Cruyff_Arena|Johan Cruyff Arena]].
sentence_105: This stadium was built by the Amsterdam city authority at a cost of $134 million.
sentence_106: The stadium is capable of holding approximately 54,990 spectators.
sentence_107: The average attendance in 2006–07 was 48,610, rising in the next season to 49,128.
sentence_108: The Arena has a retractable roof and set a trend for other modern stadiums built in Europe in the following years.
sentence_109: In the Netherlands, the Arena has earned a reputation for a terrible grass pitch caused by the removable roof that, even when open, takes away too much sunlight and fresh air.
sentence_110: During the 2008–09 season, ground staff introduced an artificial lighting system that has finally reduced this problem considerably.
sentence_111: The much-loved De Meer Stadion was torn down and the land was sold to the city council.
sentence_112: A residential neighbourhood now occupies the area.
sentence_113: The only thing left of the old stadium are the letters "AJAX", which nowadays is in place on the façade of the youth training grounds [[Sportpark_De_Toekomst|De Toekomst]], near the Johan Cruyff Arena.
sentence_114: In 1900, when the club was founded, the emblem of Ajax was just a picture of an Ajax player.
sentence_115: The crest was slightly altered following the club's promotion to the top division in 1911 to match the club's new outfits.
sentence_116: In 1928, the club logo was introduced with the head of the [[Greeks|Greek]] hero [[Ajax_the_Great|Ajax]].
sentence_117: The logo was once again changed in 1990 into an abstract version of the previous one.
sentence_118: The new logo still sports the portrait of Ajax, but drawn with just 11 lines, symbolizing the 11 players of a football team.
sentence_119: Ajax originally played in an all-black uniform with a red sash tied around the players' waists, but that uniform was soon replaced by a red/white striped shirt and black shorts.
sentence_120: Red, black and white are the three colours of the [[Flag_of_Amsterdam|flag of Amsterdam]].
sentence_121: When under manager Jack Kirwan, however, the club earned promotion to the top flight of Dutch football for the first time in 1911 (then the Eerste Klasse or 'First Class', later named the Eredivisie), Ajax were forced to change their colours because [[Sparta_Rotterdam|Sparta Rotterdam]] already had exactly the same outfit.
sentence_122: Special kits for away fixtures did not exist at the time and according to football association regulations the newcomers had to change their colours if two teams in the same league had identical uniforms.
sentence_123: Ajax opted for white shorts and white shirt with a broad, vertical red stripe over chest and back, which still is Ajax's outfit.
sentence_124: Main article: [[AFC_Ajax_N.V.|AFC Ajax N.V.]]
sentence_125: AFC Ajax are the only Dutch club with an [[Initial_public_offering|Initial public offering]] (IPO).
sentence_126: The club is registered as a Naamloze vennootschap (N.V.) listed on the stock exchange [[Euronext|Euronext]] Amsterdam, since 17 May 1998.
sentence_127: With a launch price of ƒ25,- (Guilders) the club managed to a bring their total revenue up to €54 million (converted) in their first year on the market.
sentence_128: After short-lived success, however, the rate dropped, at one point as low as €3.50.
sentence_129: Criticism was brought forth that the legal grid for a naamloze vennootschap would not be suitable for a Football club, and that the sports related ambitions would suffer from the new commercial interests of the now listed Ajax.
sentence_130: Shares of the company in the year 2008 were valued at approximately €5.90 per share.
sentence_131: In 2008, a Commission under guidance of honorary member Uri Coronel concluded that the [[Initial_public_offering|IPO]] was of no value to the club, and that measures should be taken to exit the stock exchange by purchasing back all public shares.
sentence_132: Ajax remain on the stock exchange.
sentence_133: Ajax's shirts have been [[Sponsor_(commercial)|sponsored]] by [[TDK|TDK]] from 1982 to 1991, and by [[ABN_AMRO|ABN AMRO]] from 1991 to 2008.
sentence_134: [[Aegon_N.V.|AEGON]] then replaced ABN AMRO as the new head sponsor for a period of seven years.
sentence_135: On 1 April 2007, Ajax wore a different sponsor for the match against [[Heracles_Almelo|Heracles Almelo]], Florius.
sentence_136: Florius is a banking programme launched by ABN AMRO who wanted it to be the shirt sponsor for one match.
sentence_137: The shirts have been manufactured by [[Le_Coq_Sportif|Le Coq Sportif]] (1973–1977), [[Puma_SE|Puma]] (1977–1979), Cor du Buy (1979-1980), [[Le_Coq_Sportif|Le Coq Sportif]] (1980–1984), [[Kappa_(company)|Kappa]] (1985–1989) and [[Umbro|Umbro]] (1989–2000) in the past, and by [[Adidas|Adidas]] since 2000 (until at least 2025).
sentence_138: At the conclusion of the [[2013–14_AFC_Ajax_season|2013–14 season]], Ajax won the Football shirt of the Year award for their black and rose colored away shirt by Adidas.
sentence_139: The annual award was presented by Subside Sports, which had previously given the award to [[Inter_Milan|Internazionale]], Juventus and the [[Belgium_national_football_team|Belgium national team]].
sentence_140: It was Ajax's first time winning the award.
sentence_141: On 7 November 2014, it was announced that Ajax had agreed to a four-and-a-half-year contract worth €8 million annually with Dutch cable operating company [[Ziggo|Ziggo]] as the new shirt sponsor for the club.
sentence_142: Having extended their contract with AEGON for half a season until December, the club featured Fonds Gehandicaptensport, a charitable fund for handicapped sports on its away shirts for a six-month period before transitioning to Ziggo in 2015.
sentence_143: Main article: [[Jong_Ajax|Jong Ajax]]
sentence_144: [[Jong_Ajax|Jong Ajax]] (formerly more commonly known as Ajax 2) is the reserve team of AFC Ajax.
sentence_145: The team is composed mostly of professional footballers, who are often recent graduates from the highest youth level (Ajax A1) serving their first professional contract as a reserve, or players who are otherwise unable to play in the first team.
sentence_146: Since 1992, Jong Ajax competed in the Beloften Eredivisie, competing against other reserve teams such as [[Jong_PSV|Jong PSV]], [[FC_Groningen|Jong FC Groningen]] or [[AZ_Alkmaar|Jong AZ]].
sentence_147: They have won the Beloften Eredivisie title a record eight times, as well as the KNVB Reserve Cup three times, making them the most successful reserve squad in the Netherlands.
sentence_148: By winning the Beloften Eredivisie title, Jong Ajax were able to qualify for the actual KNVB Cup, even advancing to the semi-finals on three occasions.
sentence_149: Their best result in the Dutch Cup was under manager [[Jan_Olde_Riekerink|Jan Olde Riekerink]] in 2001–02, when a semi-final loss to [[FC_Utrecht|Utrecht]] in a [[Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football)|Penalty shoot-out]] after extra time, which saw Utrecht advance, and thus preventing an Ajax–Jong Ajax Dutch Cup final.
sentence_150: The 2013–14 season marked the [[Eerste_Divisie|Jupiler League]] debut of the Ajax reserves' squad, Jong Ajax.
sentence_151: Previously playing in the Beloften Eredivisie (a separate league for reserve teams, not included in the Dutch professional or amateur league structure), players were allowed to move around freely between the reserve team and the first team during the season.
sentence_152: This is no longer the case as Jong Ajax now registers and fields a separate squad from that of Ajax first team for the Eerste Divisie, the second tier of professional football in the Netherlands.
sentence_153: Their home matches are played at Sportpark De Toekomst, except for the occasional match in the Johan Cruyff Arena.
sentence_154: Now regarded a semi-professional team in their own respect, the only period in which players are able to move between squads are during the transfer windows, unless the player has made less than 15 appearances for the first team, then he is still eligible to appear in both first team and second team matches during the season.
sentence_155: Furthermore, the team is not eligible for promotion to the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] or to participate in the KNVB Cup.
sentence_156: Jong Ajax were joined in the Eerste Divisie by Jong Twente and [[Jong_PSV|Jong PSV]], reserve teams who have also moved from the Beloften Eredivisie to the Eerste Divisie, in place of [[VV_Katwijk|VV Katwijk]], [[SC_Veendam|SC Veendam]] and [[AGOVV_Apeldoorn|AGOVV Apeldoorn]], increasing the total number of teams in the Jupiler League from 18 to 20.
sentence_157: Ajax reserve squad Jong Ajax left the Beloften Eredivisie in 2013, having held a 21-year tenure in the reserves league, having also won the league title a record eight times (1994, 1996, 1998, 2001, 2002, 2004, 2005, 2009).
sentence_158: Main article: [[AFC_Ajax_(amateurs)|AFC Ajax (amateurs)]]
sentence_159: [[AFC_Ajax_(amateurs)|AFC Ajax Amateurs]], better known as Ajax Zaterdag, is a Dutch amateur football club founded 18 March 1900.
sentence_160: It is the amateur team of the professional club AFC Ajax, who play their home matches at the [[Sportpark_De_Toekomst|Sportpark De Toekomst]] training grounds to a capacity of 5,000.
sentence_161: The team was promoted from the [[Eerste_Klasse|Eerste Klasse]] to the [[Hoofdklasse|Hoofdklasse]] ahead of the 2011–12 season, the league in which they are currently competing.
sentence_162: The team has won the [[Eerste_Klasse|Eerste Klasse]] title twice, as well as the *[[KNVB_District_Cup|KNVB District Cup West I]] on two occasions as well.
sentence_163: Furthermore, Ajax Zaterdag have also managed to qualify for the KNVB Cup on their own accord on three occasions, namely in 2004, 2005 and in 2008, even advancing to the second round before bowing out to [[SBV_Vitesse|Vitesse]] on 24 September 2008 during their last appearance in the cup tournament.
sentence_164: Main article: [[AFC_Ajax_(women)|AFC Ajax (women)]]
sentence_165: [[AFC_Ajax_(women)|AFC Ajax Vrouwen]] (English: AFC Ajax Women) are the women's team of AFC Ajax, competing in the [[Eredivisie_(women)|women's eredivisie]], the highest level of women's football in the Netherlands.
sentence_166: Founded on 18 May 2012, the women's team saw Ajax attracting many of the Netherlands top talents, with International players such as [[Anouk_Hoogendijk|Anouk Hoogendijk]], [[Daphne_Koster|Daphne Koster]] and [[Petra_Hogewoning|Petra Hogewoning]] joining the Amsterdam club in its maiden season in women's professional football.
sentence_167: The team won their first piece of silverware when the defeated [[FC_Eindhoven|PSV/FC Eindhoven]] 2–1 in the final of the [[KNVB_Women's_Cup|KNVB Women's Cup]].
sentence_168: Main article: [[Ajax_HVA|Ajax HVA]]
sentence_169: [[Ajax_HVA|Ajax HVA]] (1922–1972) was the [[Baseball|baseball]] team of AFC Ajax founded in 1922, and competed as founding members of the Honkbal Hoofdklasse, the top flight of professional baseball in the Netherlands.
sentence_170: Ajax won the national baseball title a total of four times (1924, 1928, 1942, 1948) before the club opted to no longer field a baseball team, and to focus solely on football in 1972.
sentence_171: Ajax spent a total of 50 years at the top flight of Baseball in the Netherlands from 1922 to 1972.
sentence_172: The dissolution of Ajax baseball club resulted in the players finding a new sponsor in a [[Mustard_(condiment)|mustard]] manufacturing company called Luycks, while merging with the Diemen Giants to become the Luycks Giants, thus replacing both former clubs.
sentence_173: Main article: [[AFC_Ajax_eSports|AFC Ajax eSports]]
sentence_174: In 2016, Ajax launched an eSports team, with Koen Weijland as the club's first signing, making their debut on the Global stage of [[Video_game|professional gaming]].
sentence_175: They have since signed the likes of Dani Hagebeuk, Lev Vinken, Joey Calabro and Bob van Uden, the latter spent his first season on loan to the eSports team of Japanese club Sagan Tosu.
sentence_176: Main article: [[List_of_AFC_Ajax_affiliated_clubs|List of AFC Ajax affiliated clubs]]
sentence_177: The following clubs are currently affiliated with AFC Ajax:
sentence_178: The following clubs were affiliated with AFC Ajax in the past:
sentence_179: As one of the traditional [[Big_Three_(Netherlands)|big three clubs]] in the Netherlands, Ajax have amassed a number of intense rivalries over the years.
sentence_180: Listed below are the most significant of the rivalries involving Ajax.
sentence_181: Main article: [[De_Klassieker|De Klassieker]]
sentence_182: [[Feyenoord|Feyenoord]] from [[Rotterdam|Rotterdam]] are Ajax's archrivals.
sentence_183: Every year both clubs play the [[De_Klassieker|De Klassieker]] ("The Classic"), a match between the teams from the two largest cities of the Netherlands.
sentence_184: During the 1970s, Ajax and Feyenoord were the only two clubs in the Netherlands who were able to clinch national titles, as well as achieve continental and even global success.
sentence_185: A meeting between the two clubs became the measure for who was truly the best club in the Netherlands.
sentence_186: The Klassieker is the most famous of all the rivalries in the Netherlands and the matches are always sold out.
sentence_187: The fixture is seen in the public eye as "the graceful and elegant football of Ajax, against the indomitable fighting spirit of Feyenoord"; the confidence of the capital city versus the blue collar mentality of [[Rotterdam|Rotterdam]].
sentence_188: Matches are known for their tension and violence, both on and off the pitch.
sentence_189: Over the years, several violent incidents have taken place involving rival supporters, leading to the current prohibition of away supporters in both stadiums.
sentence_190: The lowest point was reached on 23 March 1997, when supporters of both clubs met on a field near [[Beverwijk|Beverwijk]], where Ajax-supporter Carlo Picornie was fatally injured, the incident is commonly referred to as the "[[Battle_of_Beverwijk|Battle of Beverwijk]]".
sentence_191: Main article: [[AFC_Ajax–PSV_Eindhoven_rivalry|AFC Ajax–PSV Eindhoven rivalry]]
sentence_192: [[PSV_Eindhoven|PSV]] are also a rival of Ajax, but in terms of tension and rivalry, these matches are not as loaded as the duels with Feyenoord.
sentence_193: The rivalry has existed for some time with PSV and stems from various causes, such as the different interpretations of whether current national and international successes of both clubs correlates and the supposed opposition between the [[Randstad|Randstad]] and the province.
sentence_194: The matches between these two teams is commonly referred to as "De Topper" ("The Topper"), and involves the two most trophy-laden sides in Dutch football and is essentially a clash of two competing schools of thought in Dutch football.
sentence_195: Historically, PSV compete with a workmanlike ethic, preferring a more robust 4–3–1–2 or 4–2–3–1, typically shunning the frivolous 4–3–3 approach favoured in Amsterdam.
sentence_196: While [[Rinus_Michels|Rinus Michels]] and [[Johan_Cruyff|Johan Cruyff]] helped to innovate [[Total_Football|Total Football]] in the sixties and seventies, a different philosophy was honed in [[Eindhoven|Eindhoven]] by Kees Rijvers and [[Guus_Hiddink|Guus Hiddink]] in the late 1970s and '80s.
sentence_197: This in turn has created one of the more philosophical rivalries in football, an ideological battleground, which is gradually becoming as heated and intense as the matches Ajax and Feyenoord partake in.
sentence_198: Main article: [[Amsterdam_derby|Amsterdam derby]]
sentence_199: Aside from Feyenoord and PSV, Ajax have several other rivalries, although in most cases the sentiment is mostly felt by the opposition and is more directed towards Ajax, with one of them being [[FC_Utrecht|Utrecht]].
sentence_200: Although the rivalry is more felt on the Utrecht side then with Ajax, matchups between the two sides are often quite intense.
sentence_201: Both teams have fanatic supporters, and clashes off the pitch are more often the rule than the exception.
sentence_202: The same goes for [[ADO_Den_Haag|ADO Den Haag]], with both supporter groups often getting in conflicts, when ADO-Hooligans set fire to the supporters home of Ajax, and Ajax hooligans subsequently broke into the Supporters home of ADO tensions between the two clubs rose.
sentence_203: In 2006, supporters from both clubs were banned from attending away matches for five years due to frequent violent outbreaks and clashes.
sentence_204: Further teams who share a rivalry with Ajax include [[FC_Twente|Twente]], [[Vitesse_Arnhem|Vitesse Arnhem]], [[FC_Groningen|Groningen]] and AZ, although the latter is often regarded by Ajax supporters as the club's "little brother".
sentence_205: With AZ being from nearby [[Alkmaar|Alkmaar]] and therefore situated in the same province as Ajax, match-ups between the two sides are commonly known as the "De Noord-Hollandse Derby" ("[[North_Holland|North Holland]] Derby") and are often very competitive, intense and loaded fixtures.
sentence_206: Past rivalries include local [[Amsterdam_derby|Amsterdam derbies]] between Ajax and clubs such as [[Blauw-Wit_Amsterdam|Blauw-Wit]], [[AFC_DWS|DWS]] and [[De_Volewijckers|De Volewijckers]] (which later merged to become FC Amsterdam in 1972).
sentence_207: However, the tension between the local sides lessened as the division of the clubs through playing in different leagues over time became greater.
sentence_208: Years of not competing in the same league resulted in less frequent match-ups, until tensions finally settled between the Amsterdam clubs.
sentence_209: The last Amsterdam derby to take place in an official league match was when Ajax defeated FC Amsterdam 5–1 on 19 March 1978.
sentence_210: Main articles: [[A.F.C.A_(hooligans)|A.F.C.A (hooligans)]], [[F-side|F-side]], [[North_Up_Alliance|North Up Alliance]], [[South_Crew|South Crew]], and [[VAK410|VAK410]]
sentence_211: Ajax are known for having fanatic core supporter-groups, of which [[F-side|F-Side]] and [[VAK410|VAK410]] are the most famous.
sentence_212: F-Side were founded on 3 October 1976, and are situated right behind the goal in the Johan Cruyff Arena, on the southern end of the stadium in rows 125–129.
sentence_213: Their name is derived from the group's former location on the F-side of the old De Meer Stadion.
sentence_214: The F-side supporters are responsible for a big part of the atmosphere in the stadium, but are also known for rioting during and after matches.
sentence_215: If in any match Ajax should win the coin toss, the second half of the match Ajax always play towards the south-end of the stadium.
sentence_216: VAK410 (English: Row 410) were founded in 2001 and are situated in the Zuidhoek (South corner) of the stadium on the upper ring in rows 424–425.
sentence_217: The group was originally situated on the North-West side of the stadium in row 410, from where it derives its name, until relocating to their current place in the stands in 2008.
sentence_218: Members of VAK410 are known to perform various stunts, which include massive banners, to enhance the atmosphere in the stadium.
sentence_219: Neither F-Side or VAK410 have seats in their sections of the stadium, and both groups stand for the duration of the match.
sentence_220: Through the official Football Top 20 of Dutch sports research group SPORT+MARKT, it was revealed in 2010 that Ajax had approximately 7.1 million supporters throughout Europe.
sentence_221: This is significantly more than rivals Feyenoord and PSV (each 1.6 and 1.3 million, respectively), which puts Ajax as the club with the 15th-most supporters across Europe.
sentence_222: The study also revealed that approximately 39% of the Netherlands were Ajax supporters.
sentence_223: Not only does Ajax have many supporters, but several fans attend their matches in European competition, with an average attendance of 48,677 spectators for every international match Ajax played, putting the team at 12th place in Europe for highest attendance, ahead of high-profile clubs such as Milan and [[Chelsea_F.C.|Chelsea]].
sentence_224: It is noteworthy that not all stadiums share the capacity of the Johan Cruyff Arena.
sentence_225: Main articles: [[AFCA_Supportersclub|AFCA Supportersclub]], [[Ajax_Business_Associates|Ajax Business Associates]], and [[Supportersvereniging_Ajax|Supportersvereniging Ajax]]
sentence_226: The [[Supportersvereniging_Ajax|Supporters Club Ajax]] ([[Dutch_language|Dutch]]: Supportersvereniging Ajax) is officially the largest supporters club in the Netherlands with 94,000 members.
sentence_227: Founded on 7 May 1992, the supporters club organize big monthly events throughout the Netherlands, and particularly around the official Ajax Open Training Day, which attracts thousands of supporters each year.
sentence_228: Furthermore, the supporters group is responsible for the [[Ajax_Life|Ajax Life]] website, as well as the [[Fanzine|fanzine]] which is issued 20 times a year.
sentence_229: In 2006, the [[AFCA_Supportersclub|AFCA Supportersclub]] was introduced as the club's second official supporters' association, through the merger of the Onafhankelijke Fanclub Ajax (OFA) and the Ajax Supporters Delegatie (ASD).
sentence_230: The AFCA Supportersclub has a reported 42,000 members, as well as a former member on the Board of Administration of Ajax, in Ronald Pieloor.
sentence_231: The third official supporters club is the [[Ajax_Business_Associates|Ajax Business Associates]] (ABA).
sentence_232: Founded in 1991 the ABA is the Business club of Ajax.
sentence_233: Members occupy the skyboxes in the Stadium and can make use of the clubs' amenities and luxury suites including the ABA club and lounge.
sentence_234: The ABA is also responsible for hosting the annual Ajax Business Golf Trophy, an amateur golf tournament where several active and former Ajax players, as well as prominent people and members of the ABA, participate.
sentence_235: This graph displays the average attendance for home matches of Ajax from 1988 to 2018, whereby the difference in capacity of the De Meer Stadion and the Johan Cruyff Arena (est. 1996) is clearly visible.
sentence_236: Historically, Ajax was popularly seen as having "Jewish roots".
sentence_237: Although not an official Jewish club like the city's , Ajax has had a Jewish image since the 1930s when the home stadium was located next to a Jewish neighbourhood of [[Amsterdam-Oost|Amsterdam-Oost]] and opponents saw many supporters walking through the Nieuwmarkt/Waterloopleinbuurt (de Jodenhoek—the "Jews' corner") to get to the stadium.
sentence_238: The city of Amsterdam was historically referred to as a [[Mokum|Mokum]] city, Mokum (מקום) being the [[Yiddish_language|Yiddish]] word for "place" or "safe haven", and as [[Antisemitism|anti-Semitic]] chants and name calling developed and intensified at the old De Meer Stadion from frustrated supporters of opposing clubs, Ajax fans (few of whom are actually Jewish) responded by embracing Ajax's "Jewish" identity: calling themselves "super Jews", chanting "Jews, Jews" ("Joden, Joden") at games, and adopting Jewish symbols such as the [[Star_of_David|Star of David]] and the [[Flag_of_Israel|Israeli flag]].
sentence_239: This Jewish imagery eventually became a central part of Ajax fans' culture.
sentence_240: At one point ringtones of "[[Hava_Nagila|Hava Nagila]]", a [[Hebrew|Hebrew]] [[Folk_song|folk song]], could be downloaded from the club's official website.
sentence_241: Beginning in the 1980s, fans of Ajax's rivals escalated their [[Antisemitic|antisemitic]] rhetoric, chanting slogans like "[[Hamas|Hamas]], Hamas/Jews to the [[Gas_chamber|gas]]" ("Hamas, hamas, joden aan het gas"), hissing to imitate the flow of gas, giving [[Nazi_salute|Nazi salutes]], and other things.
sentence_242: The eventual result was that many (genuinely) Jewish Ajax fans stopped going to games.
sentence_243: In the 2000s, the club began trying to persuade fans to drop their Jewish image.
sentence_244: In 2013, a documentary titled [[Superjews|Superjews]] was released by [[Omroep_NTR|NTR]] and Viewpoint Productions which premiered at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

sentence_265: Main article: [[Club_van_100_(AFC_Ajax)|Club van 100 (AFC Ajax)]]
sentence_266: The Club van 100 is the official list of [[Association_football|Football]] players who have appeared in one hundred or more official matches for AFC Ajax.
sentence_267: The club currently has a total of over 150 members.
sentence_268: The record for league appearances is held by Mr. Ajax himself [[Sjaak_Swart|Sjaak Swart]], who appeared in 463 league matches for Ajax.
sentence_269: There is a beneficiary team called Lucky Ajax, which was initiated by Sjaak Swart.
sentence_270: Lucky Ajax participate in at least one match a year, usually in the name of charity, and commonly at football ceremonies to bid farewell to retiring players.
sentence_271: One of the prerequisites for playing on Lucky Ajax, which is invitational only, is that you are a member of the Club van 100, having made at least 100 official match appearances for Ajax in the first team of the club.
sentence_272: Lucky Ajax are a beneficiary team that was initiated by Sjaak Swart in the seventies, competing in at least one match a year, usually in the name of charity and/or to bid farewell to retiring former Ajax players.
sentence_273: The team is made up of various members of the [[Club_van_100_(AFC_Ajax)|Club van 100]] of Ajax who will come out of retirement for this match to face the Ajax squad that is current of that year.
sentence_274: Past participants have included [[Barry_Hulshoff|Barry Hulshoff]], [[Sonny_Silooy|Sonny Silooy]], [[Simon_Tahamata|Simon Tahamata]], [[Ronald_Koeman|Ronald Koeman]], [[Tscheu_La_Ling|Tscheu La Ling]], [[Gerrie_Mühren|Gerrie Mühren]], [[John_van_'t_Schip|John van 't Schip]], [[Brian_Roy|Brian Roy]], [[Stanley_Menzo|Stanley Menzo]], [[Peter_van_Vossen|Peter van Vossen]] and [[Fred_Grim|Fred Grim]].
sentence_275: The name Lucky Ajax is derived from the famous "Lucky Ajax" nickname from how people used to refer to the club when Ajax would either win a match by chance, by a decision of a referee, or by coincidence such as was said to be the case during the infamous [[De_Mistwedstrijd|Mistwedstrijd]] ("Fog Match").
sentence_276: Main article: list of retired numbers in association football
sentence_277: As of the [[2007–08_Eredivisie|2007–08 season]], no player could wear the number 14 shirt at Ajax after the club decided to retire the shirt out of respect for Johan Cruyff, "the legendary number fourteen".
sentence_278: Cruyff himself laughed off the tribute, saying the club had to let its best player play with number 14.
sentence_279: Spanish midfielder [[Roger_García_Junyent|Roger]] was the last player to wear the number.
sentence_280: [[Marvin_Zeegelaar|Marvin Zeegelaar]] wore the shirt number In preparation for the [[2011–12_Eredivisie|2011–12 season]] in one preseason match, while [[Aras_Özbiliz|Aras Özbiliz]] wore the number 14 shirt in one pre-season match ahead of the [[2011–12_Eredivisie|2011–12 season]] as well.
sentence_281: The club stated that this was, in fact, not done in error.

sentence_283: Main article: [[Amsterdam_Tournament|Amsterdam Tournament]]
sentence_284: Established in 1975 as the [[Amsterdam_Tournament|Amsterdam 700 Tournament]] to celebrate 700 years of history in the city.
sentence_285: The tournament was hosted annually each summer by Ajax until 1992, when the last edition of the original tournament was played.
sentence_286: It returned in 1999 with the backing of the International Event Partnership (IEP).
sentence_287: Four teams participated in the competition, played in a league format since 1986.
sentence_288: Since its return, the tournament used an unusual point scoring system.
sentence_289: As with most league competitions, three points were awarded for a win, one for a draw, and none for a loss.
sentence_290: An additional point, however, was awarded for each goal scored.
sentence_291: The system was designed to reward teams that adopted a more attacking style of play.
sentence_292: Each entrant played two matches, with the winner being the club that finished at the top of the table.
sentence_293: The original competition was held at De Meer Stadion, Ajax's home between 1934 and 1996.
sentence_294: The Amsterdam Arena (now Johan Cruyff Arena) played host to the event since its return until the last edition was played in 2009.
sentence_295: Ajax is the most successful team of the tournament, having won it a record ten times, while [[S.L._Benfica|Benfica]] from [[Portugal|Portugal]] were the last team to win the tournament, in 2009.
sentence_296: Main article: [[Copa_Amsterdam|Copa Amsterdam]]
sentence_297: Established in 2005, the [[Copa_Amsterdam|Copa Amsterdam]] is an international friendly football tournament for Under-19 youth teams, that is organized by Ajax and the [[Amsterdam_city_council|Amsterdam city council]], which takes place at the [[Olympic_Stadium_(Amsterdam)|Olympic Stadium]] as part of the annual Amsterdam Sports Weekend, a citywide sponsored initiative to promote 'sports and recreation' within the city of Amsterdam.
sentence_298: Each Summer the city of Amsterdam and Ajax invite U-19 teams from various top clubs from around the World to participate in the tournament.
sentence_299: Seven teams are invited and play in the competition every year.
sentence_300: Over the years, clubs such as [[FC_Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Juventus_F.C.|Juventus]], [[Chelsea_F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Real_Madrid_C.F.|Real Madrid]] have had their senior youth teams participate in the tournament.
sentence_301: [[Cruzeiro_Esporte_Clube|Cruzeiro]] from [[Brazil|Brazil]] are the most successful club in the history of the tournament, having won it three times in total.
sentence_302: Main article: [[Future_Cup|Future Cup]]
sentence_303: Established in 2010, the [[AEGON_Future_Cup|AEGON Future Cup]] is an international friendly tournament for Under-17 youth teams, which is organized by AFC Ajax and their main sponsor, the insurance company [[Aegon_N.V.|AEGON]].
sentence_304: The tournament is held each year at the Johan Cruyff Arena and at the [[Sportpark_De_Toekomst|Sportpark De Toekomst]], the team's training ground, which also inspired the name of the competition, since De Toekomst in Dutch means The Future.
sentence_305: Every year during the [[Easter|Easter]] weekend, six U-17 teams are invited to participate in the competition, while the seventh place for the contesters is reserved for the winners of the "Craques Mongeral AEGON Future Cup" in Brazil, the sister competition of the tournament in South America.
sentence_306: Youth teams from top clubs such as [[Manchester_United_F.C.|Manchester United]], [[FC_Bayern_Munich|Bayern Munich]], [[A.C._Milan|Milan]] and many more have participated in the competition over the years.
sentence_307: Ajax are the most successful club of the tournament, having won the trophy a total of five times.

sentence_0: Actinopterygii ([[English|/ˌæktɪnɒptəˈrɪdʒiaɪ/]]) ([[New_Latin|New Latin]], actino- ("having rays") + Ancient Greek πτέρυξ (ptérux, "wing, fins")), members of which are known as ray-finned fishes, is a [[Clade|clade]] (traditionally [[Class_(biology)|class]] or subclass) of the [[Osteichthyes|bony fishes]].
sentence_1: The ray-finned [[Fish|fishes]] are so called because their fins are webs of skin supported by bony or horny spines ("rays"), as opposed to the fleshy, lobed fins that characterize the class [[Sarcopterygii|Sarcopterygii]] (lobe-finned fish).
sentence_2: These actinopterygian fin rays attach directly to the proximal or basal skeletal elements, the radials, which represent the link or connection between these fins and the internal skeleton (e.g., pelvic and pectoral girdles).
sentence_3: Numerically, actinopterygians are the dominant class of [[Vertebrate|vertebrates]], comprising nearly 99% of the over 30,000 species of fish.
sentence_4: They are ubiquitous throughout [[Freshwater|freshwater]] and [[Ocean|marine]] environments from the deep sea to the highest mountain streams.
sentence_5: Extant species can range in size from [[Paedocypris|Paedocypris]], at 8 mm (0.3 in), to the massive [[Ocean_sunfish|ocean sunfish]], at 2,300 kg (5,070 lb), and the long-bodied [[Oarfish|oarfish]], at 11 m (36 ft).
sentence_6: The vast majority of Actinopterygii (~95%) are [[Teleost|teleosts]].
sentence_7: Ray-finned fishes occur in many variant forms.
sentence_8: The main features of a typical ray-finned fish are shown in the adjacent diagram.
sentence_9: The swim bladder is the more derived structure.
sentence_10: Ray-finned fishes have many different types of scales; but all [[Teleost|teleosts]], the most advanced actinopterygians, have leptoid scales.
sentence_11: The outer part of these scales fan out with bony ridges while the inner part is crossed with fibrous connective tissue.
sentence_12: Leptoid scales are thinner and more transparent than other types of scales, and lack the hardened enamel or dentine-like layers found in the scales of many other fish.
sentence_13: Unlike ganoid scales, which are found in non-teleost actinopterygians, new scales are added in concentric layers as the fish grows.
sentence_14: Ray-finned and lobe-finned fishes, including tetrapods, possessed lungs used for aerial respiration.
sentence_15: Only bichirs retain ventrally budding lungs.
sentence_16: Further information: [[Fish_fin|Fish fin]]
sentence_17: Ray-finned fish are very varied in size and shape, and in the number of their ray-fins and the manner in which they arrange them.
sentence_18: In nearly all ray-finned fish, the sexes are separate, and in most species the females spawn eggs that are fertilized externally, typically with the male inseminating the eggs after they are laid.
sentence_19: Development then proceeds with a free-swimming larval stage.
sentence_20: However other patterns of [[Ontogeny|ontogeny]] exist, with one of the commonest being [[Sequential_hermaphroditism|sequential hermaphroditism]].
sentence_21: In most cases this involves [[Protogyny|protogyny]], fish starting life as females and converting to males at some stage, triggered by some internal or external factor.
sentence_22: [[Protandry|Protandry]], where a fish converts from male to female, is much less common than protogyny.
sentence_23: Most families use [[External_fertilization|external]] rather than [[Internal_fertilization|internal fertilization]].
sentence_24: Of the [[Oviparity|oviparous]] teleosts, most (79%) do not provide parental care.
sentence_25: [[Viviparity|Viviparity]], [[Ovoviviparity|ovoviviparity]], or some form of parental care for eggs, whether by the male, the female, or both parents is seen in a significant fraction (21%) of the 422 teleost families; no care is likely the ancestral condition.
sentence_26: Viviparity is relatively rare and is found in about 6% of teleost species; male care is far more common than female care.
sentence_27: Male territoriality [[Exaptation|"preadapts"]] a species for evolving male parental care.
sentence_28: There are a few examples of fish that self-fertilise.
sentence_29: The [[Mangrove_rivulus|mangrove rivulus]] is an amphibious, simultaneous hermaphrodite, producing both eggs and spawn and having internal fertilisation.
sentence_30: This mode of reproduction may be related to the fish's habit of spending long periods out of water in the mangrove forests it inhabits.
sentence_31: Males are occasionally produced at temperatures below 19 °C (66 °F) and can fertilise eggs that are then spawned by the female.
sentence_32: This maintains genetic variability in a species that is otherwise highly inbred.
sentence_33: See also: [[Evolution_of_fish|Evolution of fish]]
sentence_34: The earliest known fossil actinopterygian is [[Andreolepis_hedei|Andreolepis hedei]], dating back 420 million years ([[Late_Silurian|Late Silurian]]).
sentence_35: Remains have been found in [[Russia|Russia]], [[Sweden|Sweden]], and [[Estonia|Estonia]].
sentence_36: Actinopterygia is divided into the subclasses [[Chondrostei|Chondrostei]] and [[Neopterygii|Neopterygii]].
sentence_37: The [[Neopterygii|Neopterygii]], in turn, is divided into the infraclasses [[Holostei|Holostei]] and [[Teleostei|Teleostei]].
sentence_38: During the [[Mesozoic|Mesozoic]] and [[Cenozoic|Cenozoic]] the teleosts in particular diversified widely, and as a result, 96% of all known fish species are teleosts.
sentence_39: The [[Cladogram|cladogram]] shows the major groups of actinopterygians and their relationship to the terrestrial vertebrates (tetrapods) that evolved from a related group of fish.
sentence_40: Approximate dates are from Near et al., 2012.
sentence_41: The polypterids (bichirs and reedfish) are the sister lineage of all other actinopterygians, the Acipenseriformes (sturgeons and paddlefishes) are the sister lineage of Neopterygii, and Holostei (bowfin and gars) are the sister lineage of teleosts.
sentence_42: The Elopomorpha (eels and tarpons) appear to be the most basal teleosts.

table.value: [[Chondrostei|Chondrostei]] (cartilage bone) is a subclass of primarily [[Cartilage|cartilaginous]] fish showing some ossification. Earlier definitions of Chondrostei are now known to be [[Paraphyly|paraphyletic]], meaning that this subclass does not contain all the descendants of their common ancestor. There were 52 species divided among two orders, the [[Acipenseriformes|Acipenseriformes]] ([[Sturgeon|sturgeons]] and [[Paddlefish|paddlefishes]]) and the [[Polypteriformes|Polypteriformes]] ([[Reedfish|reedfishes]] and [[Bichir|bichirs]]). Reedfish and birchirs are now separated from the Chondrostei into their own sister lineage, the [[Cladistia|Cladistia]]. It is thought that the chondrosteans evolved from bony fish but lost the bony hardening of their cartilaginous skeletons, resulting in a lightening of the frame. Elderly chondrosteans show beginnings of ossification of the skeleton, suggesting that this process is delayed rather than lost in these fish. This group had once been classified with the [[Shark|sharks]]: the similarities are obvious, as not only do the chondrosteans mostly lack bone, but the structure of the jaw is more akin to that of sharks than other bony fish, and both lack [[Scale_(zoology)|scales]] (excluding the Polypteriforms). Additional shared features include [[Spiracle_(vertebrates)|spiracles]] and, in sturgeons, a heterocercal tail (the [[Vertebra|vertebrae]] extend into the larger lobe of the [[Caudal_fin|caudal fin]]). However the fossil record suggests that these fish have more in common with the [[Teleostei|Teleostei]] than their external appearance might suggest.

[[Neopterygii|Neopterygii]] (new fins) is a subclass of ray-finned fish that appeared somewhere in the Late [[Permian|Permian]]. There were only few changes during its evolution from the earlier actinopterygians. Neopterygians are a very successful group of fishes because they can move more rapidly than their ancestors. Their scales and skeletons began to lighten during their evolution, and their jaws became more powerful and efficient. While [[Electroreception|electroreception]] and the [[Ampullae_of_Lorenzini|ampullae of Lorenzini]] is present in all other groups of fish, with the exception of [[Hagfish|hagfish]], neopterygians have lost this sense, though it later re-evolved within [[Gymnotiformes|Gymnotiformes]] and [[Catfish|catfishes]], who possess nonhomologous teleost ampullae.

sentence_2: Bulgaria ([[English|/bʌlˈɡɛəriə, bʊl-/]] (listen); Bulgarian: България, [[Romanization_of_Bulgarian|romanized]]: Balgariya), officially the Republic of Bulgaria (Bulgarian: Република България, romanized: Republika Balgariya, IPA: [[Bulgarian|[rɛˈpublikɐ bɐɫˈɡarijɐ]]), is a country in [[Southeast_Europe|Southeast Europe]].
sentence_3: It is bordered by [[Romania|Romania]] to the north, [[Serbia|Serbia]] and [[North_Macedonia|North Macedonia]] to the west, [[Greece|Greece]] and [[Turkey|Turkey]] to the south, and the [[Black_Sea|Black Sea]] to the east.
sentence_4: The capital and largest city is [[Sofia|Sofia]]; other major cities are [[Plovdiv|Plovdiv]], [[Varna|Varna]] and [[Burgas|Burgas]].
sentence_5: With a territory of 110,994 square kilometres (42,855 sq mi), Bulgaria is Europe's [[List_of_European_countries_by_area|sixteenth-largest country]].
sentence_6: One of the earliest societies in the lands of modern-day Bulgaria was the [[Neolithic|Neolithic]] [[Karanovo_culture|Karanovo]] and Varna cultures, which dates back to 6,500 BC and 4,400 BC respectively.
sentence_7: In the 6th to 3rd century BC the region was a battleground for ancient [[Thracians|Thracians]], [[Greek_colonisation|Greeks]], [[Persians|Persians]], [[Celts|Celts]], [[Ancient_Macedonians|Macedonians]] and [[Scythians|Scythians]]; stability came when the [[Roman_Empire|Roman Empire]] conquered the region in AD 45.
sentence_8: The [[Byzantine_Empire|Eastern Roman Empire]] lost some of these territories to the numerous [[Early_Slavs|early Slavs]].
sentence_9: In the 7th century those territories were invaded by Bulgars from Old Great Bulgaria.
sentence_10: From around AD 671, leaded by [[Asparuh_of_Bulgaria|Asparuh]], major part of the Bulgars settled in the [[Ongal|Ongal]] area, and in AD 680, already allied with the [[Seven_Slavic_tribes|local Slavs]], successfully attacked the Byzantines and founded the [[First_Bulgarian_Empire|First Bulgarian Empire]] in AD 681.
sentence_11: It dominated most of the [[Balkans|Balkans]] and significantly influenced [[Slavs|Slavic]] cultures by developing the [[Cyrillic_script|Cyrillic script]].
sentence_12: This state lasted until the early 11th century, when Byzantine emperor [[Basil_II|Basil II]] conquered and dismantled it.
sentence_13: A successful Bulgarian revolt in 1185 established a [[Second_Bulgarian_Empire|Second Bulgarian Empire]], which reached its apex under [[Ivan_Asen_II_of_Bulgaria|Ivan Asen II of Bulgaria]] (1218–1241).
sentence_14: After numerous exhausting wars and feudal strife, the empire disintegrated in 1396 and fell under [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman]] rule for nearly five centuries.
sentence_15: The [[Russo-Turkish_War_(1877–1878)|Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78]] resulted in the formation of the third and current Bulgarian state.
sentence_16: Many ethnic Bulgarians were left outside the new nation's borders, which stoked [[Irredentism|irredentist]] sentiments that led to several conflicts with its neighbours and alliances with Germany in both world wars.
sentence_17: In 1946 Bulgaria came under the Soviet-led [[Eastern_Bloc|Eastern Bloc]] and became a [[People's_Republic_of_Bulgaria|one-party socialist state]].
sentence_18: The ruling [[Bulgarian_Communist_Party|Communist Party]] gave up its monopoly on power after the [[Revolutions_of_1989|revolutions of 1989]] and allowed multiparty elections.
sentence_19: Bulgaria then transitioned into a [[Democracy|democracy]] and a market-based economy.
sentence_20: Since adopting a democratic constitution in 1991, Bulgaria has been a [[Unitary_state|unitary]] parliamentary republic composed of 28 provinces, with a high degree of political, administrative, and economic centralisation.
sentence_21: Bulgaria is a member of the [[European_Union|European Union]], [[NATO|NATO]], and the [[Council_of_Europe|Council of Europe]]; it is a founding state of the [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] (OSCE) and has taken a seat on the [[United_Nations_Security_Council|United Nations Security Council]] three times.
sentence_22: Its [[Market_economy|market economy]] is part of the [[European_Single_Market|European Single Market]] and mostly relies on services, followed by industry—especially machine building and mining—and agriculture.
sentence_23: Bulgaria is a [[Developing_country|developing country]] with an [[List_of_countries_by_GNI_(nominal)_per_capita#Upper-middle-income_group|upper-middle-income economy]], [[List_of_countries_by_Human_Development_Index#Countries|very high]] [[Human_Development_Index|Human Development Index]]; although it has the [[Economy_of_the_European_Union#Wealth|lowest GDP per capita]] and [[List_of_sovereign_states_in_Europe_by_Human_Development_Index|joint-lowest Human Development Index]] in the European Union.
sentence_24: [[Corruption_in_Bulgaria|Widespread corruption]] is a major socioeconomic issue; Bulgaria ranked as the most corrupt country in the European Union in 2018.
sentence_25: The country also faces a demographic crisis, with its population shrinking annually since the late 1980s; it currently numbers roughly seven million, down from a peak of nearly nine million in 1988.
sentence_26: The name Bulgaria is derived from the Bulgars, a tribe of [[Turkic_peoples|Turkic]] origin that founded the country.
sentence_27: Their name is not completely understood and is difficult to trace back earlier than the 4th century AD, but it is possibly derived from the [[Proto-Turkic_language|Proto-Turkic]] word bulģha ("to mix", "shake", "stir") and its derivative bulgak ("revolt", "disorder").
sentence_28: The meaning may be further extended to "rebel", "incite" or "produce a state of disorder", and so, in the derivative, the "disturbers".
sentence_29: Ethnic groups in [[Inner_Asia|Inner Asia]] with phonologically similar names were frequently described in similar terms: during the 4th century, the [[Jie_people|Buluoji]], a component of the "[[Five_Barbarians|Five Barbarian]]" groups in ancient China, were portrayed as both a "mixed race" and "troublemakers".
sentence_30: Main article: [[History_of_Bulgaria|History of Bulgaria]]
sentence_31: Further information: [[Neolithic_Europe|Neolithic Europe]], [[Odrysian_kingdom|Odrysian kingdom]], [[Thracians|Thracians]], [[Greek_colonisation|Greek colonisation]], and [[Slavs|Slavs]]
sentence_32: [[Neanderthal|Neanderthal]] remains dating to around 150,000 years ago, or the [[Middle_Paleolithic|Middle Paleolithic]], are some of the earliest traces of human activity in the lands of modern Bulgaria.
sentence_33: Remains from [[Homo_sapiens|Homo sapiens]] found there are dated c. 47,000 [[Years_BP|years BP]].
sentence_34: This result represents the earliest arrival of modern humans in Europe.
sentence_35: The [[Karanovo_culture|Karanovo culture]] arose circa 6,500 BC and was one of several [[Neolithic|Neolithic]] societies in the region that thrived on [[Agriculture|agriculture]].
sentence_36: The [[Copper_Age|Copper Age]] Varna culture (fifth millennium BC) is credited with inventing gold metallurgy.
sentence_37: The associated [[Varna_Necropolis|Varna Necropolis treasure]] contains the oldest golden jewellery in the world with an approximate age of over 6,000 years.
sentence_38: The treasure has been valuable for understanding social hierarchy and stratification in the earliest European societies.
sentence_39: The [[Thracians|Thracians]], one of the three primary ancestral groups of modern [[Bulgarians|Bulgarians]], appeared on the [[Balkans|Balkan Peninsula]] some time before the 12th century BC.
sentence_40: The Thracians excelled in [[Metallurgy|metallurgy]] and gave the [[Ancient_Greece|Greeks]] the [[Orpheus|Orphean]] and [[Dionysus|Dionysian]] cults, but remained tribal and stateless.
sentence_41: The Persian [[Achaemenid_Empire|Achaemenid Empire]] conquered most of present-day Bulgaria in the 6th century BC and retained control over the region until [[Second_Persian_invasion_of_Greece|479 BC]].
sentence_42: The invasion became a catalyst for Thracian unity, and the bulk of their tribes united under king [[Teres_I|Teres]] to form the [[Odrysian_kingdom|Odrysian kingdom]] in the 470s BC.
sentence_43: It was weakened and vassalized by Philip II of Macedon in 341 BC, attacked [[Tylis|by Celts]] in the 3rd century, and finally [[Thracia|became a province]] of the [[Roman_Empire|Roman Empire]] in AD 45.
sentence_44: By the end of the 1st century AD, Roman governance was established over the entire Balkan Peninsula and [[Christianity|Christianity]] began spreading in the region around the 4th century.
sentence_45: The [[Gothic_Bible|Gothic Bible]]—the first Germanic language book—was created by [[Goths|Gothic]] bishop [[Ulfilas|Ulfilas]] in what is today northern Bulgaria around 381.
sentence_46: The region came under [[Byzantine|Byzantine]] control after the [[Fall_of_the_Western_Roman_Empire|fall of Rome]] in 476.
sentence_47: The Byzantines were engaged in prolonged warfare against Persia and could not defend their Balkan territories from barbarian incursions.
sentence_48: This enabled the [[Early_Slavs|Slavs]] to enter the Balkan Peninsula as marauders, primarily through an area between the Danube River and the Balkan Mountains known as Moesia.
sentence_49: Gradually, the interior of the peninsula became a country of the [[Sclaveni|South Slavs]], who lived under a [[Democracy|democracy]].
sentence_50: The Slavs assimilated the partially [[Hellenistic_period#Balkans|Hellenized]], [[Thraco-Romans|Romanized]], and Gothicized Thracians in the rural areas.
sentence_51: Main article: [[First_Bulgarian_Empire|First Bulgarian Empire]]
sentence_52: Not long after the Slavic incursion, Moesia was once again invaded, this time by the Bulgars under [[Khan_(title)|Khan]] [[Asparuh_of_Bulgaria|Asparukh]].
sentence_53: Their horde was a remnant of Old Great Bulgaria, an extinct tribal confederacy situated north of the Black Sea in what is now Ukraine and southern Russia.
sentence_54: Asparukh attacked Byzantine territories in Moesia and conquered the Slavic tribes there in 680.
sentence_55: A peace treaty with the [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantine Empire]] was signed in 681, marking the foundation of the [[First_Bulgarian_Empire|First Bulgarian Empire]].
sentence_56: The minority Bulgars formed a close-knit ruling caste.
sentence_57: Succeeding rulers strengthened the Bulgarian state throughout the 8th and 9th centuries.
sentence_58: [[Krum_of_Bulgaria|Krum]] introduced a written code of law and checked a major Byzantine incursion at the [[Battle_of_Pliska|Battle of Pliska]], in which Byzantine emperor [[Nicephorus_I|Nicephorus I]] was killed.
sentence_59: [[Boris_I_of_Bulgaria|Boris I]] abolished paganism in favour of [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|Eastern Orthodox Christianity]] in 864.
sentence_60: The conversion was followed by a Byzantine recognition of the [[Bulgarian_Orthodox_Church|Bulgarian church]] and the adoption of the [[Cyrillic_script|Cyrillic alphabet]], developed in the capital, [[Preslav|Preslav]].
sentence_61: The common language, religion and script strengthened central authority and gradually fused the Slavs and Bulgars into a unified people speaking a single Slavic language.
sentence_62: A golden age began during the 34-year rule of [[Simeon_I_of_Bulgaria|Simeon the Great]], who oversaw the largest territorial expansion of the state.
sentence_63: After Simeon's death, Bulgaria was weakened by wars with [[Magyars|Magyars]] and [[Pechenegs|Pechenegs]] and the spread of the [[Bogomilism|Bogomil heresy]].
sentence_64: Preslav was seized by the Byzantine army in 971 after consecutive [[Kievan_Rus'|Rus']] and Byzantine invasions.
sentence_65: The empire briefly recovered from the attacks under [[Samuel_of_Bulgaria|Samuil]], but this ended when Byzantine emperor [[Basil_II|Basil II]] defeated the Bulgarian army at [[Battle_of_Kleidion|Klyuch]] in 1014.
sentence_66: Samuil died shortly after the battle, and by 1018 the Byzantines [[Byzantine_conquest_of_Bulgaria|had conquered the First Bulgarian Empire]].
sentence_67: After the conquest, Basil II prevented revolts by retaining the rule of local nobility, integrating them in Byzantine bureaucracy and aristocracy, and relieving their lands of the obligation to pay taxes in gold, allowing [[Tax_in_kind|tax in kind]] instead.
sentence_68: The [[Bulgarian_Orthodox_Church|Bulgarian Patriarchate]] was reduced to an [[Orthodox_Archbishopric_of_Ohrid_(ancient)|archbishopric]], but retained its [[Autocephaly|autocephalous status]] and its dioceses.
sentence_69: Main article: [[Second_Bulgarian_Empire|Second Bulgarian Empire]]
sentence_70: Byzantine domestic policies changed after Basil's death and a series of unsuccessful rebellions broke out, [[Bulgarian_uprising_against_the_Byzantine_Empire_(1040-1041)|the largest]] being led by [[Peter_Delyan|Peter Delyan]].
sentence_71: The empire's authority declined after a catastrophic military [[Battle_of_Manzikert|defeat at Manzikert]] against [[Seljuk_Empire|Seljuk]] invaders, and was further disturbed by the [[Crusades|Crusades]].
sentence_72: This prevented Byzantine attempts at [[Hellenisation|Hellenisation]] and created fertile ground for further revolt.
sentence_73: In 1185 [[Asen_dynasty|Asen dynasty]] nobles [[Ivan_Asen_I|Ivan Asen I]] and [[Peter_IV_of_Bulgaria|Peter IV]] organized a major uprising and succeeded in re-establishing the Bulgarian state.
sentence_74: Ivan Asen and Peter laid the foundations of the Second Bulgarian Empire with its capital at Tarnovo.
sentence_75: [[Kaloyan|Kaloyan]], the third of the Asen monarchs, extended his dominion to [[Belgrade|Belgrade]] and [[Ohrid|Ohrid]].
sentence_76: He acknowledged the spiritual supremacy of [[The_pope|the pope]] and received a royal crown from a [[Papal_legate|papal legate]].
sentence_77: The empire reached its zenith under [[Ivan_Asen_II|Ivan Asen II]] (1218–1241), when its borders expanded as far as the coast of [[Albania|Albania]], Serbia and [[Epirus|Epirus]], while commerce and culture flourished.
sentence_78: Ivan Asen's rule was also marked by a shift away from Rome in religious matters.
sentence_79: The Asen dynasty became extinct in 1257.
sentence_80: Internal conflicts and incessant Byzantine and Hungarian attacks followed, enabling the [[Golden_Horde|Mongols]] to [[Mongol_invasion_of_Bulgaria_and_Serbia|establish suzerainty]] over the weakened Bulgarian state.
sentence_81: In 1277, swineherd [[Ivaylo_of_Bulgaria|Ivaylo]] led a [[Uprising_of_Ivaylo|great peasant revolt]] that expelled the Mongols from Bulgaria and briefly made him emperor.
sentence_82: He was overthrown in 1280 by [[Boyars|the feudal landlords]], whose factional conflicts caused the Second Bulgarian Empire to disintegrate into small feudal dominions by the 14th century.
sentence_83: These fragmented [[Rump_state|rump states]]—two tsardoms at [[Tsardom_of_Vidin|Vidin]] and [[Second_Bulgarian_Empire#Ivan_Alexander_and_fall_of_Bulgaria|Tarnovo]] and the [[Despotate_of_Dobruja|Despotate of Dobrudzha]]—became easy prey for a new threat arriving from the Southeast: the Ottoman Turks.
sentence_84: Main article: [[Ottoman_Bulgaria|Ottoman Bulgaria]]
sentence_85: The Ottomans were employed as mercenaries by the Byzantines in the 1340s but later became invaders in their own right.
sentence_86: Sultan Murad I took [[Adrianople|Adrianople]] from the Byzantines in 1362; [[Sofia|Sofia]] fell in 1382, followed by [[Shumen|Shumen]] in 1388.
sentence_87: The Ottomans completed their conquest of Bulgarian lands in 1393 when Tarnovo was sacked after a three-month siege and the [[Battle_of_Nicopolis|Battle of Nicopolis]] which brought about the fall of the Vidin Tsardom in 1396.
sentence_88: [[Sozopol|Sozopol]] was the last Bulgarian settlement to fall, in 1453.
sentence_89: The Bulgarian nobility was subsequently eliminated and the peasantry was enserfed to Ottoman masters, while much of the educated clergy fled to other countries.
sentence_90: Bulgarians were subjected to heavy taxes (including [[Devshirme|devshirme]], or blood tax), their culture was suppressed, and they experienced partial [[Islamisation|Islamisation]].
sentence_91: Ottoman authorities established a religious administrative community called the [[Rum_Millet|Rum Millet]], which governed all Orthodox Christians regardless of their ethnicity.
sentence_92: Most of the local population then gradually lost its distinct national consciousness, identifying only by its faith.
sentence_93: The clergy remaining in some isolated monasteries kept their ethnic identity alive, enabling its survival in remote rural areas, and in the militant [[Roman_Catholicism_in_Bulgaria|Catholic community]] in the northwest of the country.
sentence_94: As Ottoman power began to wane, Habsburg Austria and Russia saw Bulgarian Christians as potential allies.
sentence_95: The Austrians first backed an [[First_Tarnovo_Uprising|uprising in Tarnovo in 1598]], then a second one in 1686, the Chiprovtsi Uprising in 1688 and finally Karposh's Rebellion in 1689.
sentence_96: The [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] also asserted itself as a protector of Christians in Ottoman lands with the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca in 1774.
sentence_97: The Western European [[Age_of_Enlightenment|Enlightenment]] in the 18th century influenced the initiation of a [[National_awakening_of_Bulgaria|national awakening of Bulgaria]].
sentence_98: It restored national consciousness and provided an ideological basis for the liberation struggle, resulting in the 1876 [[April_Uprising|April Uprising]].
sentence_99: Up to 30,000 Bulgarians were killed as Ottoman authorities put down the rebellion.
sentence_100: The massacres prompted the [[Great_Powers#History|Great Powers]] to take action.
sentence_101: They convened the [[Constantinople_Conference|Constantinople Conference]] in 1876, but their decisions were rejected by the Ottomans.
sentence_102: This allowed the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] to seek a military solution without risking confrontation with other Great Powers, as had happened in the [[Crimean_War|Crimean War]].
sentence_103: In 1877 [[Russo-Turkish_War,_1877–1878|Russia declared war]] on the Ottomans and defeated them with the help of [[Opalchentsi|Bulgarian rebels]], particularly during the crucial [[Battle_of_Shipka_Pass|Battle of Shipka Pass]] which secured Russian control over the main road to Constantinople.
sentence_104: Main articles: [[History_of_Bulgaria_(1878–1946)|History of Bulgaria (1878–1946)]], [[People's_Republic_of_Bulgaria|People's Republic of Bulgaria]], and [[History_of_Bulgaria_since_1989|History of Bulgaria since 1989]]
sentence_105: The Treaty of San Stefano was signed on 3 March 1878 by [[Russian_Empire|Russia]] and the [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]].
