title: Abdur Rahman Khan
sentence_0: For other people with the same given name, see [[Abdur_Rahman_(disambiguation)|Abdur Rahman (disambiguation)]].
sentence_1: Abdur Rahman Khan ([[Pashto_language|Pashto]]: عبدالرحمان خان‎) (between 1840 and 1844 – October 1, 1901) was [[List_of_monarchs_of_Afghanistan|Emir of Afghanistan]] from 1880 to 1901.
sentence_2: He is known for uniting the country after years of internal fighting and negotiation of the [[Durand_Line|Durand Line]] Agreement with [[British_Raj|British India]].
sentence_3: Abdur Rahman Khan was the first child and only son of [[Mohammad_Afzal_Khan|Mohammad Afzal Khan]], and grandson of [[Dost_Mohammad_Khan_(Emir_of_Afghanistan)|Dost Mohammad Khan]].
sentence_4: Abdur Rahman Khan re-established the writ of the [[Politics_of_Afghanistan|Afghan government]] after the disarray that followed the [[Second_Anglo-Afghan_War|second Anglo-Afghan war]].
sentence_5: He became known as The Iron Amir because his government was a military despotism resting upon a well-appointed army administered through officials absolutely subservient to an inflexible will and controlled by a widespread system of [[Espionage|espionage]]; and for his [[1888-1893_Uprisings_of_Hazaras|crushing of a number of rebellions]] by various tribes who were led by his relatives.
sentence_6: Before his death in [[Herat|Herat]], on June 9, 1863, Abdur Rahman's grandfather, [[Dost_Mohammad_Khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]], nominated his third son, [[Sher_Ali_Khan|Sher Ali Khan]], as his successor, passing over the two elder brothers, [[Mohammad_Afzal_Khan|Afzal Khan]] and [[Mohammad_Azam_Khan|Azam Khan]].
sentence_7: At first, the new Amir was quietly recognized.
sentence_8: But after a few months, Afzal Khan raised an [[Insurrection|insurrection]] in the north of the country, where he had been governing when his father died.
sentence_9: This began a fierce internecine conflict for power between Dost Mohammad's sons, which lasted for nearly five years.
sentence_10: The [[Musahiban|Musahiban]] are descendants of [[Dost_Mohammad_Khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]]'s older brother, [[Sultan_Mohammad_Khan|Sultan Mohammad Khan]].
sentence_11: Described by the American scholar and explorer [[Eugene_Schuyler|Eugene Schuyler]] as "a tall well-built man, with a large head, and a marked Afghan, almost [[Jewish_people|Jewish]], face", Abdur Rahman distinguished himself for his ability and energetic daring.
sentence_12: Although his father, Afzal Khan came to terms with the Amir Sher Ali, Abdur's behaviour in the northern province soon excited the Amir's suspicion and, when he was summoned to Kabul, fled across the [[Oxus|Oxus]] into [[Bukhara|Bukhara]].
sentence_13: Sher Ali threw Afzal Khan into prison, and a revolt followed in southern Afghanistan.
sentence_14: The Amir had scarcely suppressed it by winning a desperate battle when Abdur Rahman's reappearance in the north was a signal for a mutiny by troops stationed in those parts and a gathering of armed bands to his standard.
sentence_15: After some delay and desultory fighting, he and his uncle, Azam Khan, occupied Kabul in March 1866.
sentence_16: The Amir Sher Ali marched up against them from [[Kandahar|Kandahar]]; but in the battle that ensued at Sheikhabad on May 10, he was deserted by a large body of his troops, and after his signal defeat Abdur Rahman released his father, Afzal Khan, from prison in [[Ghazni|Ghazni]], and installed him upon the throne as Amir of Afghanistan.
sentence_17: Notwithstanding the new Amir's incapacity, and some jealousy between the real leaders, Abdur Rahman and his uncle, they again routed Sher Ali's forces, and occupied Kandahar in 1867.
sentence_18: When Afzal Khan died at the end of the year, Azam Khan became the new ruler, with Abdur Rahman installed as governor in the northern province.
sentence_19: But towards the end of 1868, Sher Ali's return and a general rising in his favour resulted in Abdur Rahman and Azam Khan's defeat at Tinah Khan on January 3, 1869.
sentence_20: Both sought refuge to the east in Central Asia, where Abdur Rahman placed himself under Russian protection at [[Samarkand|Samarkand]].
sentence_21: Azam died in Kabul in October 1869.

section_1.value: Exile and negotiated return to power

sentence_22: Abdur Rahman lived in exile in [[Tashkent|Tashkent]].
sentence_23: He was being told to cross the [[Oxus|Oxus]] and claim [[Throne|throne]] for Amir.
sentence_24: In March 1880, a report reached India that Abdur Rahman was in northern Afghanistan; and the Governor-General, [[Robert_Bulwer-Lytton,_1st_Earl_of_Lytton|Lord Lytton]], opened communications with him to the effect that the [[Her_Majesty's_Government|British government]] were prepared to withdraw their troops, and to recognize Abdur Rahman as Amir of Afghanistan, with the exception of Kandahar and some districts adjacent to it.
sentence_25: After some negotiations, and an interview with [[Lepel_Griffin|Lepel Griffin]], the diplomatic representative at Kabul of the Indian government.
sentence_26: Griffin described Abdur Rahman as a man of middle height, with an exceedingly intelligent face and frank and courteous manners, shrewd and able in conversation on the business in hand.
sentence_27: At the [[Durbar_(court)|durbar]] on July 22, 1880, Abdur Rahman was officially recognized as Amir, granted assistance in arms and money, and promised, in case of unprovoked foreign aggression, such further aid as might be necessary to repel it, provided that he align his foreign policy with the British.
sentence_28: The British evacuation of Afghanistan was settled on the terms proposed, and in 1881, the [[British_Army|British troops]] also handed over Kandahar to the new Amir.
sentence_29: However, [[Mohammad_Ayub_Khan_(Emir_of_Afghanistan)|Ayub Khan]], one of Sher Ali Khan's sons, marched upon that city from Herat, defeated Abdur Rahman's troops, and occupied the place in July 1880.
sentence_30: This serious reverse roused the Amir, who had not displayed much activity.
sentence_31: Instead, Ayub Khan was defeated in Kandahar by the British General Frederick Roberts on 1 September 1880.
sentence_32: Ayub Khan was forced to flee into Persia.
sentence_33: From that time Abdur Rahman was fairly seated firm on the throne at Kabul, thanks to the unwavering British protections in terms of giving large supplies of arms and money.
sentence_34: In the course of the next few years, Abdul Rahman consolidated his grip over all Afghanistan, suppressing [[Insurrection|insurrection]] by a relentless and brutal use of his [[Despotism|despotic]] authority.
sentence_35: The powerful [[Ghilzai|Ghilzai]] revolted against the severity of his measures several times.
sentence_36: In that same year, Ayub Khan made a fruitless inroad from Persia.
sentence_37: In 1885, at the moment when the Amir was in conference with the British viceroy, [[Frederick_Hamilton-Temple-Blackwood,_1st_Marquess_of_Dufferin_and_Ava|Lord Dufferin]], in India, the news came of a skirmish between Russian and Afghan troops at Panjdeh, over a disputed point in the demarcation of the northwestern frontier of Afghanistan.
sentence_38: Abdur Rahman's attitude at this critical juncture is a good example of his political sagacity.
sentence_39: To one who had been a man of war from his youth, who had won and lost many fights, the rout of a detachment and the forcible seizure of some debatable frontier lands was an untoward incident; but it was not a [[Principle_of_sufficient_reason|sufficient reason]] for calling upon the British, although they had guaranteed his territory's integrity, to vindicate his rights by hostilities which would certainly bring upon him a Russian invasion from the north, and would compel his British allies to throw an army into Afghanistan from the southeast.
sentence_40: He also published his [[Autobiography|autobiography]] in 1885, which served more as an advice guide for princes than anything else.
sentence_41: His interest lay in keeping powerful neighbours, whether friends or foes, outside his kingdom.
sentence_42: He knew this to be the only policy that would be supported by the Afghan nation; and although for some time a rupture with Russia seemed imminent, while the [[India_Office|Government of India]] made ready for that contingency, the Amir's reserved and circumspect tone in the consultations with him helped to turn the balance between peace and war, and substantially conduced towards a pacific solution.
sentence_43: Abdur Rahman left on those who met him in India the impression of a clear-headed man of action, with great self-reliance and hardihood, not without indications of the implacable severity that too often marked his administration.
sentence_44: His investment with the insignia of the highest grade of the [[Order_of_the_Star_of_India|Order of the Star of India]] appeared to give him much pleasure.
sentence_45: His adventurous life, his forcible character, the position of his state as a barrier between the Indian and the Russian empires, and the skill with which he held the balance in dealing with them, combined to make him a prominent figure in contemporary Asian politics and will mark his reign as an epoch in the history of Afghanistan.
sentence_46: The Amir received an annual [[Subsidy|subsidy]] from the British government of 1,850,000 [[Rupee|rupees]].
sentence_47: He was allowed to import munitions of war.
sentence_48: He succeeded in imposing an organized government upon the fiercest and most unruly population in [[Asia|Asia]]; he availed himself of [[Europe|European]] inventions for strengthening his armament, while he sternly set his face against all innovations which, like [[Railway|railways]] and [[Telegraphy|telegraphs]], might give Europeans a foothold within his country.
sentence_49: In 1893 he built himself a summer house called the [[Bagh-e_Bala_Palace|Bagh-e Bala Palace]].
sentence_50: The Amir found himself unable, by reason of [[Illness|ill-health]], to accept an invitation from [[Queen_Victoria|Queen Victoria]] to visit England; but his second son [[Nasrullah_Khan_(Afghanistan)|Nasrullah Khan]] went instead.
sentence_51: See also: [[Durand_Line|Durand Line]]
sentence_52: In 1893, Mortimer Durand was deputed to Kabul by the government of British India for this purpose of settling an exchange of territory required by the demarcation of the boundary between northeastern Afghanistan and the Russian possessions, and in order to discuss with Amir Abdur Rahman Khan other pending questions.
sentence_53: Abdur Rahman Khan showed his usual ability in diplomatic argument, his tenacity where his own views or claims were in debate, with a sure underlying insight into the real situation.
sentence_54: In the agreement that followed relations between the British Indian and Afghan governments, as previously arranged, were confirmed; and an understanding was reached upon the important and difficult subject of the border line of Afghanistan on the east, towards India.
sentence_55: A Royal Commission was set up to determine the boundary between Afghanistan and British Governed India was tasked to negotiate terms for agreeing to the [[Durand_Line|Durand Line]], between the two parties camped at Parachinar, now part of FATA Pakistan, which is near [[Khost|Khost]], Afghanistan.
sentence_56: From the British side the camp was attended by Mortimer Durand and [[Sahibzada_Abdul_Qayyum|Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum]], [[Political_officer_(British_Empire)|Political Agent]] Khyber.
sentence_57: Afghanistan was represented by Sahibzada Abdul Latif and the Governor Sardar Shireendil Khan representing Amir Abdur Rahman Khan.
sentence_58: In 1893, [[Mortimer_Durand|Mortimer Durand]] negotiated with Abdur Rahman Khan the Durand Line Treaty for the demarcation of the frontier between Afghanistan, the [[FATA|FATA]], [[Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa|North-West Frontier Province]] and Baluchistan Provinces of Pakistan the successor state of [[British_India|British India]].
sentence_59: In 1905, Amir [[Habibullah_Khan|Habibullah Khan]] signed a new agreement with the [[United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland|United Kingdom]] which confirmed the legality of Durand Line.
sentence_60: Similarly, the legality durand line was once again confirmed by King [[Amanullah_Khan|Amanullah Khan]] through the treaty of Rawalpindi in 1919.
sentence_61: Durand Line was once again recognised as international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan by [[Daoud_Khan|Sardar Mohammed Daoud Khan]] (former prime minister and later president of Afghanistan) during his visit to Pakistan in August 1976.
sentence_62: Abdur Rahman Khan's government was a military despotism resting upon a well-appointed army; it was administered through officials absolutely subservient to an inflexible will and controlled by a widespread system of [[Espionage|espionage]]; while the exercise of his personal authority was too often stained by acts of unnecessary cruelty.
sentence_63: He held open courts for the receipt of petitioners and the dispensation of justice; and in the disposal of business he was indefatigable.
sentence_64: In the 1880s, the "Iron Emir" decided to strategically displace some members of different ethnic groups in order to bring better security.
sentence_65: For example, he "uprooted troublesome Durrani and Ghilzai [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] tribes and [[Pashtun_colonization_of_northern_Afghanistan|transported them]] to [[Uzbeks|Uzbek]] and [[Tajiks|Tajik]] populated areas in the north, where they could spy on local Dari-speaking, non-Pashtun ethnic groups and act as a screen against further Russian encroachments on Afghan territory."
sentence_66: From the end of 1888, the Amir spent eighteen months in his northern provinces bordering upon the Oxus, where he was engaged in pacifying the country that had been disturbed by revolts, and in punishing with a heavy hand all who were known or suspected to have taken any part in rebellion.
sentence_67: In 1895–1896, Abdur Rahman directed the invasion of [[Kafiristan|Kafiristan]] and the conversion of its indigenous peoples to Islam.
sentence_68: The region was subsequently renamed [[Nuristan_Province|Nuristan]].
sentence_69: In 1896, he adopted the title of Zia-ul-Millat-Wa-ud Din ("Light of the nation and religion"), and his zeal for the cause of [[Islam|Islam]] induced him to publish [[Treatises|treatises]] on [[Jihad|jihad]].
sentence_70: Chitral, Yarkand and Ferghana became shelters for refugees in 1887 and 1883 from Badakhshan who fled from the campaigns of Abdul Rahman.
sentence_71: Main article: [[1888-1893_Uprisings_of_Hazaras|1888-1893 Uprisings of Hazaras]]
sentence_72: In the early 1890s some Hazara tribes revolted against Abdur Rahman.
sentence_73: In 1888, the Amir's cousin, Ishak Khan, rebelled against him in the north; and also the Ghilzais (Hotakis, Tokhis and Andaris) revolted against him in 1887; but these enterprises came to nothing.
sentence_74: As the Kabul Newsletters written by the British agents indicate, Abdur Rahman was an extremely ruthless man.
sentence_75: He has been called 'The Dracula Amir' by some writers.
sentence_76: According to [[Syed_Askar_Mousavi|Syed Askar Mousavi]], after the crushing of the Hazara Uprising "thousands of Hazara men, women, and children were sold as slaves in the markets of Kabul and [[Kandahar|Qandahar]], while numerous towers of Hazara heads were made from the defeated rebels as a warning to others who might challenge the rule of the Iron Amir."
sentence_77: Due to Amir's depredations, some Hazaras migrated to [[Quetta|Quetta]] in Balochistan, while smaller number moved to [[Mashhad|Mashhad]] in northeastern Iran.
sentence_78: The crackdown resulted in mass killing, enslavement and displacement of more than 65% of [[Hazara_people|Hazara]] community in Afghanistan.
sentence_79: This significant reduction in the [[Hazaras|Hazaras]]' population made them a minority in Afghanistan.
sentence_80: Abdur Rahman Khan's atrocious punishments were unusually genocidal compared to his punishing of previous Pashtun rebellions of [[Ghilzais|Ghilzais]] like (Hotakis, Tokhis and Andaris).
sentence_81: While these aforementioned tribes' revolts were crushed, but since they shared the same ethnicity with the Amir, they did not suffer mass enslavement, massacre and depopulation of their people and lands.
sentence_82: Abdur Rahman died on October 1, 1901 inside his summer palace, being succeeded by his son [[Habibullah_Khan|Habibullah Khan]].
sentence_83: Today, his descendants can be found in many places outside Afghanistan, such as in America, [[France|France]], [[Germany|Germany]], and even in Scandinavian countries such as [[Denmark|Denmark]].
sentence_84: His two eldest sons, Habibullah Khan and [[Nasrullah_Khan_(Afghanistan)|Nasrullah Khan]], were born at [[Samarkand|Samarkand]].
sentence_85: His youngest son, Mahomed Omar Jan, was born in 1889 of an Afghan mother, connected by descent with the [[Barakzai|Barakzai]] family.
sentence_86: Afghan society has mixed feelings about his rule.
sentence_87: Majority of [[Pashtuns|Pashtuns]] (his native ethnics) remember him as a ruler who initiated many programs for modernization and effectively prevented the country from being occupied by Russia with the "financial and advisory" support of [[British_Empire|British Empire]] during [[The_Great_Game|the Great Game]].
sentence_88: On the other hand, the vast majority of Afghan population, including [[Hazaras|Hazaras]] and [[Tajiks|Tajiks]], remember him as an extremely brutal tyrant domestically and a puppet ruler in that he was brought into power and supported by the British; and instead of fighting the British who were deciding Afghanistan's foreign policy for him, he declared war on other Afghan ethnics.

title: Atlanta
sentence_0: This article is about the city in the U.S. state of Georgia.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Atlanta_(disambiguation)|Atlanta (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: Not to be confused with Atalanta.
sentence_3: Atlanta ([[English|/ætˈlæntə/]]) is the [[Capital_city|capital]] and [[List_of_municipalities_in_Georgia_(U.S._state)|most populous city]] of the [[U.S._state|U.S.
sentence_4: state]] of [[Georgia_(U.S._state)|Georgia]].
sentence_5: With an estimated 2019 population of 506,811, it is also the [[List_of_United_States_cities_by_population|37th most populous city in the United States]].
sentence_6: The city serves as the cultural and economic center of the Atlanta metropolitan area, home to more than 6 million people and the [[List_of_metropolitan_statistical_areas|ninth-largest metropolitan area]] in the nation.
sentence_7: Atlanta is the [[County_seat|seat]] of [[Fulton_County,_Georgia|Fulton County]], the most populous county in Georgia.
sentence_8: Portions of the city extend eastward into neighboring [[DeKalb_County,_Georgia|DeKalb County]].
sentence_9: The city is situated among the foothills of the [[Appalachian_Mountains|Appalachian Mountains]] and has the highest elevation among major cities east of the [[Mississippi_River|Mississippi River]].
sentence_10: Atlanta was originally founded as the terminus of a major state-sponsored railroad.
sentence_11: With rapid expansion, however, it soon became the convergence point among multiple railroads, spurring its rapid growth.
sentence_12: The city's name derives from that of the [[Western_and_Atlantic_Railroad|Western and Atlantic Railroad]]'s local depot, signifying the town's growing reputation as a transportation hub.
sentence_13: During the [[American_Civil_War|American Civil War]], the city was almost entirely burned to the ground in [[General_William_T._Sherman|General William T. Sherman]]'s famous [[Sherman's_March_to_the_Sea|March to the Sea]].
sentence_14: However, the city rose from its ashes and quickly became a national center of commerce and the unofficial capital of the "[[New_South|New South]]".
sentence_15: During the 1950s and 1960s, Atlanta became a major organizing center of the [[Civil_rights_movement|civil rights movement]], with [[Martin_Luther_King_Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr.]], [[Ralph_David_Abernathy|Ralph David Abernathy]], and many other locals playing major roles in the movement's leadership.
sentence_16: During the modern era, Atlanta has attained international prominence as a major air transportation hub, with [[Hartsfield–Jackson_Atlanta_International_Airport|Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport]] being the [[World's_busiest_airport|world's busiest airport]] by passenger traffic since 1998.
sentence_17: It ranks in the top twenty among world cities and 10th in the nation with a [[Gross_domestic_product|gross domestic product]] (GDP) of $385 billion.
sentence_18: Atlanta's economy is considered diverse, with dominant sectors that include aerospace, transportation, logistics, professional and business services, media operations, medical services, and information technology.
sentence_19: Atlanta has topographic features that include rolling hills and [[Atlanta_tree_canopy|dense tree coverage]], earning it the nickname of "the city in a forest".
sentence_20: [[Gentrification_of_Atlanta|Gentrification of Atlanta's neighborhoods]], initially spurred by the [[1996_Summer_Olympics|1996 Summer Olympics]], has intensified in the 21st century with the growth of the [[Atlanta_Beltline|Atlanta Beltline]], altering the city's demographics, politics, aesthetics, and culture.
sentence_21: Main articles: [[History_of_Atlanta|History of Atlanta]] and [[Timeline_of_Atlanta|Timeline of Atlanta]]
sentence_22: For thousands of years prior to the arrival of European settlers in north Georgia, the indigenous [[Creek_(people)|Creek people]] and their ancestors inhabited the area.
sentence_23: [[Standing_Peachtree|Standing Peachtree]], a Creek village where [[Peachtree_Creek|Peachtree Creek]] flows into the [[Chattahoochee_River|Chattahoochee River]], was the closest Native American settlement to what is now Atlanta.
sentence_24: Through the early nineteenth century, European Americans systematically encroached on the Creek of northern Georgia, forcing them out of the area from 1802 to 1825.
sentence_25: The Creek were forced to leave the area in 1821, under [[Indian_Removal|Indian Removal]] by the federal government, and European American settlers arrived the following year.
sentence_26: In 1836, the [[Georgia_General_Assembly|Georgia General Assembly]] voted to build the Western and Atlantic Railroad in order to provide a link between the port of [[Savannah,_Georgia|Savannah]] and the [[Midwestern_United_States|Midwest]].
sentence_27: The initial route was to run southward from [[Chattanooga,_Tennessee|Chattanooga]] to a terminus east of the [[Chattahoochee_River|Chattahoochee River]], which would be linked to Savannah.
sentence_28: After engineers surveyed various possible locations for the terminus, the "zero milepost" was driven into the ground in what is now [[Five_Points_(Atlanta)|Five Points]].
sentence_29: A year later, the area around the milepost had developed into a settlement, first known as Terminus, and later Thrasherville, after a local merchant who built homes and a [[General_store|general store]] in the area.
sentence_30: By 1842, the town had six buildings and 30 residents and was renamed [[Marthasville,_Georgia|Marthasville]] to honor Governor [[Wilson_Lumpkin|Wilson Lumpkin's]] daughter Martha.
sentence_31: Later, [[J._Edgar_Thomson|J.
sentence_32: Edgar Thomson]], Chief Engineer of the [[Georgia_Railroad|Georgia Railroad]], suggested the town be renamed Atlanta.
sentence_33: The residents approved, and the town was incorporated as Atlanta on December 29, 1847.
sentence_34: By 1860, Atlanta's population had grown to 9,554.
sentence_35: During the [[American_Civil_War|American Civil War]], the nexus of multiple railroads in Atlanta made the city a strategic hub for the distribution of military supplies.
sentence_36: In 1864, the Union Army moved southward following the capture of Chattanooga and began its [[Atlanta_campaign|invasion of north Georgia]].
sentence_37: The region surrounding Atlanta was the location of several major army [[Battle|battles]], culminating with the [[Battle_of_Atlanta|Battle of Atlanta]] and a four-month-long siege of the city by the Union Army under the command of General [[William_Tecumseh_Sherman|William Tecumseh Sherman]].
sentence_38: On September 1, 1864, [[Confederate_States_of_America|Confederate]] General [[John_Bell_Hood|John Bell Hood]] decided to retreat from Atlanta, and he ordered the destruction of all public buildings and possible assets that could be of use to the Union Army.
sentence_39: On the next day, Mayor [[James_Calhoun_(politician,_born_1811)|James Calhoun]] surrendered Atlanta to the Union Army, and on September 7, Sherman ordered the city's civilian population to evacuate.
sentence_40: On November 11, 1864, Sherman prepared for the Union Army's [[Sherman's_March_to_the_Sea|March to the Sea]] by ordering the destruction of Atlanta's remaining military assets.
sentence_41: After the Civil War ended in 1865, Atlanta was gradually rebuilt.
sentence_42: The work attracted many new residents.
sentence_43: Due to the city's superior [[Rail_transportation|rail transportation]] network, the [[List_of_U.S._state_historical_capitals|state capital]] was moved from [[Milledgeville,_Georgia|Milledgeville]] to Atlanta in 1868.
sentence_44: In the 1880 Census, Atlanta had surpassed Savannah as Georgia's largest city.
sentence_45: Beginning in the 1880s, Henry W. Grady, the editor of the [[Atlanta_Constitution|Atlanta Constitution]] newspaper, promoted Atlanta to potential investors as a city of the "[[New_South|New South]]" that would be based upon a modern economy and less reliant on agriculture.
sentence_46: By 1885, the founding of the Georgia School of Technology (now [[History_of_Georgia_Tech|Georgia Tech]]) and the [[Atlanta_University_Center|Atlanta University Center]], a consortium of [[Historically_black_colleges|historically black colleges]] made up of units for men and women, had established Atlanta as a center for higher education.
sentence_47: In 1895, Atlanta hosted the [[Cotton_States_and_International_Exposition|Cotton States and International Exposition]], which attracted nearly 800,000 attendees and successfully promoted the New South's development to the world.
sentence_48: During the first decades of the 20th century, Atlanta enjoyed a period of unprecedented growth.
sentence_49: In three decades' time, Atlanta's population tripled as the city limits expanded to include nearby streetcar suburbs.
sentence_50: The city's skyline grew taller with the construction of the [[Equitable_Building_(Atlanta_1892)|Equitable]], [[Flatiron_Building_(Atlanta)|Flatiron]], [[J._Mack_Robinson_College_of_Business_Administration_Building|Empire]], and [[Candler_Building_(Atlanta)|Candler]] buildings.
sentence_51: [[Sweet_Auburn|Sweet Auburn]] emerged as a center of black commerce.
sentence_52: The period was also marked by strife and tragedy.
sentence_53: Increased racial tensions led to the [[Atlanta_Race_Riot|Atlanta Race Riot]] of 1906, when whites attacked blacks, leaving at least 27 people dead and over 70 injured, with extensive damage in black neighborhoods.
sentence_54: In 1913, [[Leo_Frank|Leo Frank]], a Jewish-American factory superintendent, was convicted of the murder of a 13-year-old girl in a highly publicized trial.
sentence_55: He was sentenced to death but the governor commuted his sentence to life.
sentence_56: An enraged and organized [[Lynching|lynch mob]] took him from jail in 1915 and hanged him in [[Marietta,_Georgia|Marietta]].
sentence_57: The Jewish community in Atlanta and across the country were horrified.
sentence_58: On May 21, 1917, the [[Great_Atlanta_Fire_of_1917|Great Atlanta Fire]] destroyed 1,938 buildings in what is now the [[Old_Fourth_Ward|Old Fourth Ward]], resulting in one fatality and the displacement of 10,000 people.
sentence_59: On December 15, 1939, Atlanta hosted the [[Premiere|premiere]] of [[Gone_with_the_Wind_(film)|Gone with the Wind]], the epic film based on the best-selling novel by Atlanta's [[Margaret_Mitchell|Margaret Mitchell]].
sentence_60: The gala event at [[Loew's_Grand_Theatre|Loew's Grand Theatre]] was attended by the film's legendary producer, David O. Selznick, and the film's stars [[Clark_Gable|Clark Gable]], [[Vivien_Leigh|Vivien Leigh]], and [[Olivia_de_Havilland|Olivia de Havilland]], but Oscar winner [[Hattie_McDaniel|Hattie McDaniel]], an African-American actress, was barred from the event due to racial segregation laws.
sentence_61: Atlanta played a vital role in the Allied effort during [[World_War_II|World War II]] due to the city's war-related manufacturing companies, railroad network and military bases.
sentence_62: The defense industries attracted thousands of new residents and generated revenues, resulting in rapid population and economic growth.
sentence_63: In the 1950s, the city's newly constructed highway system, supported by federal subsidies, allowed middle class Atlantans the ability to relocate to the suburbs.
sentence_64: As a result, the city began to make up an ever-smaller proportion of the metropolitan area's population.
sentence_65: African-American veterans returned from World War II seeking full rights in their country and began heightened activism.
sentence_66: In exchange for support by that portion of the black community that could vote, in 1948 the mayor ordered the hiring of the first eight African-American police officers in the city.
sentence_67: In the 1960s, Atlanta became a major organizing center of the [[Civil_rights_movement|civil rights movement]], with [[Martin_Luther_King_Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr.]], [[Ralph_David_Abernathy|Ralph David Abernathy]], and students from Atlanta's [[Historically_black_colleges_and_universities|historically black colleges and universities]] playing major roles in the movement's leadership.
sentence_68: While Atlanta in the postwar years had relatively minimal racial strife compared to other cities, blacks were limited by discrimination, segregation, and continued [[Disfranchisement_after_Reconstruction_era|disenfranchisement]] of most voters.
sentence_69: In 1961, the city attempted to thwart [[Blockbusting|blockbusting]] by realtors by erecting road barriers in Cascade Heights, countering the efforts of civic and business leaders to foster Atlanta as the "city too busy to hate".
sentence_70: Desegregation of the public sphere came in stages, with public transportation desegregated by 1959, the restaurant at [[Rich's_(department_store)|Rich's]] department store by 1961, movie theaters by 1963, and public schools by 1973 (nearly 20 years after the US Supreme Court ruled that segregated public schools were unconstitutional).
sentence_71: In 1960, whites comprised 61.7% of the city's population.
sentence_72: During the 1950s–70s, suburbanization and [[White_flight|white flight]] from urban areas led to a significant demographic shift.
sentence_73: By 1970, African Americans were the majority of the city's population and exercised their recently enforced voting rights and political influence by electing Atlanta's first black mayor, [[Maynard_Jackson|Maynard Jackson]], in 1973.
sentence_74: Under Mayor Jackson's tenure, Atlanta's airport was modernized, strengthening the city's role as a transportation center.
sentence_75: The opening of the [[Georgia_World_Congress_Center|Georgia World Congress Center]] in 1976 heralded Atlanta's rise as a convention city.
sentence_76: Construction of the city's [[Metropolitan_Atlanta_Rapid_Transit_Authority|subway system]] began in 1975, with rail service commencing in 1979.
sentence_77: Despite these improvements, Atlanta lost more than 100,000 residents between 1970 and 1990, over 20% of its population.
sentence_78: At the same time, it developed new office space after attracting numerous corporations, with an increasing portion of workers from northern areas.
sentence_79: Atlanta was selected as the site for the [[1996_Summer_Olympic_Games|1996 Summer Olympic Games]].
sentence_80: Following the [[Bids_for_the_1996_Summer_Olympics|announcement]], the city government undertook several major construction projects to improve Atlanta's parks, sporting venues, and transportation infrastructure; however, for the first time, none of the $1.7 billion cost of the games was governmentally funded.
sentence_81: While the games experienced transportation and accommodation problems and, despite extra security precautions, there was the [[Centennial_Olympic_Park_bombing|Centennial Olympic Park bombing]], the spectacle was a watershed event in Atlanta's history.
sentence_82: For the first time in Olympic history, every one of the record 197 national Olympic committees invited to compete sent athletes, sending more than 10,000 contestants participating in a record 271 events.
sentence_83: The related projects such as [[Atlanta's_Olympic_Legacy_Program|Atlanta's Olympic Legacy Program]] and civic effort initiated a fundamental transformation of the city in the following decade.
sentence_84: During the 2000s, Atlanta underwent a profound physical, [[Human_culture|cultural]], and [[Demographics|demographic]] transformation.
sentence_85: As some of the black middle and upper classes also began to move to the suburbs, a booming economy drew numerous new migrants from other areas of the country, who contributed to changes in the city's demographics.
sentence_86: African Americans made up a decreasing portion of the population, from a high of 67% in 1990 to 54% in 2010.
sentence_87: From 2000 to 2010, Atlanta gained 22,763 white residents, 5,142 Asian residents, and 3,095 Hispanic residents, while the city's black population decreased by 31,678.
sentence_88: Much of the city's demographic change during the decade was driven by young, college-educated professionals: from 2000 to 2009, the [[Intown_Atlanta|three-mile radius]] surrounding [[Downtown_Atlanta|Downtown Atlanta]] gained 9,722 residents aged 25 to 34 and holding at least a four-year degree, an increase of 61%.
sentence_89: This was similar to the tendency in other cities for young, college educated, single or married couples to live in downtown areas.
sentence_90: Between the mid-1990s and 2010, stimulated by funding from the [[HOPE_VI|HOPE VI]] program and under leadership of CEO Renee Lewis Glover (1994–2013), the [[Atlanta_Housing_Authority|Atlanta Housing Authority]] demolished nearly all of its public housing, a total of 17,000 units and about 10% of all housing units in the city.
sentence_91: After reserving 2,000 units mostly for elderly, the AHA allowed redevelopment of the sites for mixed-use and mixed-income, higher density developments, with 40% of the units to be reserved for affordable housing.
sentence_92: Two-fifths of previous public housing residents attained new housing in such units; the remainder received vouchers to be used at other units, including in suburbs.
sentence_93: At the same time, in an effort to change the culture of those receiving subsidized housing, the AHA imposed a requirement for such residents to work (or be enrolled in a genuine, limited-time training program).
sentence_94: It is virtually the only housing authority to have created this requirement.
sentence_95: To prevent problems, the AHA also gave authority to management of the mixed-income or voucher units to evict tenants who did not comply with the work requirement or who caused behavior problems.
sentence_96: In 2005, the city approved the $2.8 billion [[BeltLine|BeltLine]] project.
sentence_97: It was intended to convert a disused 22-mile freight railroad loop that surrounds the central city into an art-filled multi-use trail and light rail transit line, which would increase the city's park space by 40%.
sentence_98: The project stimulated retail and residential development along the loop, but has been criticised for its adverse effects on some Black communities.
sentence_99: Atlanta's cultural offerings expanded during the 2000s: the [[High_Museum_of_Art|High Museum of Art]] doubled in size; the [[Alliance_Theatre|Alliance Theatre]] won a [[Tony_Award|Tony Award]]; and art galleries were established on the once-industrial [[West_Midtown|Westside]].
sentence_100: The city of Atlanta was the subject of a [[2018_Atlanta_cyberattack|massive cyberattack]] which began in March 2018.
sentence_101: Main article: [[Geography_of_Atlanta|Geography of Atlanta]]
sentence_102: Atlanta encompasses 134.0 square miles (347.1 km), of which 133.2 square miles (344.9 km) is land and 0.85 square miles (2.2 km) is water.
sentence_103: The city is situated among the foothills of the [[Appalachian_Mountains|Appalachian Mountains]].
sentence_104: At 1,050 feet (320 m) above mean sea level, Atlanta has the highest elevation among major cities east of the [[Mississippi_River|Mississippi River]].
sentence_105: Atlanta straddles the [[Eastern_Continental_Divide|Eastern Continental Divide]].
sentence_106: Rainwater that falls on the south and east side of the divide flows into the Atlantic Ocean, while rainwater on the north and west side of the divide flows into the [[Gulf_of_Mexico|Gulf of Mexico]].
sentence_107: Atlanta developed on a ridge south of the [[Chattahoochee_River|Chattahoochee River]], which is part of the [[ACF_River_Basin|ACF River Basin]].
sentence_108: The river borders the far northwestern edge of the city, and much of its natural habitat has been preserved, in part by the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area.
sentence_109: Main articles: [[Architecture_of_Atlanta|Architecture of Atlanta]] and Neighborhoods of Atlanta
sentence_110: See also: [[List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Atlanta|List of tallest buildings in Atlanta]]
sentence_111: Most of Atlanta was burned during the Civil War, depleting the city of a large stock of its historic architecture.
sentence_112: Yet architecturally, the city had never been traditionally "southern" because Atlanta originated as a railroad town, rather than a southern seaport dominated by the planter class, such as [[Savannah,_Georgia|Savannah]] or [[Charleston,_South_Carolina|Charleston]].
sentence_113: Because of its later development, many of the city's landmarks share architectural characteristics with buildings in the Northeast or Midwest, as they were designed at a time of shared national architectural styles.
sentence_114: During the late twentieth century, Atlanta embraced the global trend of [[Modern_architecture|modern architecture]], especially for commercial and institutional structures.
sentence_115: Examples include the [[State_of_Georgia_Building|State of Georgia Building]] built in 1966, and the [[Georgia-Pacific_Tower|Georgia-Pacific Tower]] in 1982.
sentence_116: Many of the most notable examples from this period we designed by world renowned Atlanta architect [[John_C._Portman_Jr.|John Portman]].
sentence_117: Most of the buildings that define the downtown skyline were designed by Portman during this period, including the [[Westin_Peachtree_Plaza|Westin Peachtree Plaza]] and the [[Atlanta_Marriott_Marquis|Atlanta Marriott Marquis]].
sentence_118: In the latter half of the 1980s, Atlanta became one of the early homes of postmodern buildings that reintroduced classical elements to their designs.
sentence_119: Many of Atlanta's tallest skyscrapers were built in this period and style, displaying tapering spires or otherwise ornamented crowns, such as [[One_Atlantic_Center|One Atlantic Center]] (1987), [[191_Peachtree_Tower|191 Peachtree Tower]] (1991), and the Four Seasons Hotel Atlanta (1992).
sentence_120: Also completed during the era is the Portman-designed [[Bank_of_America_Plaza_(Atlanta)|Bank of America Plaza]] built in 1992.
sentence_121: At 1,023 feet (312 m), it is the tallest building in the city and the 14th-tallest in the United States.
sentence_122: The city's embrace of modern architecture has often translated into an ambivalent approach toward historic preservation, leading to the destruction of many notable architectural landmarks.
sentence_123: These include the [[Equitable_Building_(Atlanta_1892)|Equitable Building]] (1892–1971), [[Terminal_Station_(Atlanta)|Terminal Station]] (1905–1972), and the [[Atlanta-Fulton_Public_Library_System#The_Carnegie_Library|Carnegie Library]] (1902–1977).
sentence_124: In the mid-1970s, the [[Fox_Theatre_(Atlanta,_Georgia)|Fox Theatre]], now a cultural icon of the city, would have met the same fate if not for a grassroots effort to save it.
sentence_125: More recently, preservationists may have made some inroads.
sentence_126: For example, in 2016 activists convinced the Atlanta City Council not to demolish the Atlanta-Fulton Central Library, the last building designed by noted architect [[Marcel_Breuer|Marcel Breuer]].
sentence_127: Atlanta is divided into 242 officially defined neighborhoods.
sentence_128: The city contains three major high-rise districts, which form a north–south axis along [[Peachtree_Street|Peachtree]]: [[Downtown_Atlanta|Downtown]], [[Midtown_Atlanta|Midtown]], and [[Buckhead_(Atlanta)|Buckhead]].
sentence_129: Surrounding these high-density districts are leafy, low-density neighborhoods, most of which are dominated by single-family homes.
sentence_130: Downtown Atlanta contains the most office space in the metro area, much of it occupied by government entities.
sentence_131: Downtown is home to the city's sporting venues and many of its tourist attractions.
sentence_132: [[Midtown_Atlanta|Midtown Atlanta]] is the city's second-largest business district, containing the offices of many of the region's law firms.
sentence_133: Midtown is known for its art institutions, cultural attractions, institutions of higher education, and dense form.
sentence_134: [[Buckhead_(Atlanta)|Buckhead]], the city's uptown district, is eight miles (13 km) north of Downtown and the city's third-largest business district.
sentence_135: The district is marked by an urbanized core along [[Peachtree_Street|Peachtree Road]], surrounded by suburban single-family neighborhoods situated among woods and rolling hills.
sentence_136: Surrounding Atlanta's three high-rise districts are the city's low- and medium-density neighborhoods, where the craftsman bungalow single-family home is dominant.
sentence_137: The [[Eastside_(Atlanta)|eastside]] is marked by historic [[Streetcar_suburbs|streetcar suburbs]], built from the 1890s–1930s as havens for the upper middle class.
sentence_138: These neighborhoods, many of which contain their own villages encircled by shaded, architecturally distinct residential streets, include the [[Victorian_architecture|Victorian]] [[Inman_Park|Inman Park]], [[Bohemianism|Bohemian]] East Atlanta, and eclectic [[Old_Fourth_Ward|Old Fourth Ward]].
sentence_139: On the [[West_Midtown|westside]] and along the [[BeltLine|BeltLine]] on the [[Eastside,_Atlanta|eastside]], former warehouses and factories have been converted into housing, retail space, and art galleries, transforming the once-industrial areas such as [[West_Midtown|West Midtown]] into model neighborhoods for smart growth, historic rehabilitation, and infill construction.
sentence_140: In southwest Atlanta, neighborhoods closer to downtown originated as streetcar suburbs, including the historic [[West_End_(Atlanta)|West End]], while those farther from downtown retain a postwar suburban layout.
sentence_141: These include [[Collier_Heights|Collier Heights]] and Cascade Heights, home to much of the city's affluent African-American population.
sentence_142: Northwest Atlanta contains the areas of the city to west of Marietta Boulevard and to the north of Martin Luther King, Jr. Drive, including those neighborhoods remote to downtown, such as Riverside, Bolton and Whittier Mill.
sentence_143: The latter is one of Atlanta's designated Landmark Historical Neighborhoods.
sentence_144: Vine City, though technically Northwest, adjoins the city's Downtown area and has recently been the target of community outreach programs and economic development initiatives.
sentence_145: Gentrification of the city's neighborhoods is one of the more controversial and transformative forces shaping contemporary Atlanta.
sentence_146: The [[Gentrification_of_Atlanta|gentrification of Atlanta]] has its origins in the 1970s, after many of Atlanta's neighborhoods had declined and suffered the urban decay that affected other major American cities in the mid-20th century.
sentence_147: When neighborhood opposition successfully prevented two [[Interstate_485_(Georgia)|freeways]] from being built through the city's east side in 1975, the area became the starting point for Atlanta's [[Gentrification|gentrification]].
sentence_148: After Atlanta was awarded the Olympic games in 1990, gentrification expanded into other parts of the city, stimulated by infrastructure improvements undertaken in preparation for the games.
sentence_149: New development post-2000 has been aided by the [[Atlanta_Housing_Authority|Atlanta Housing Authority]]'s eradication of the city's public housing.
sentence_150: As noted above, it allowed development of these sites for mixed-income housing, requiring developers to reserve a considerable portion for affordable housing units.
sentence_151: It has also provided for other former residents to be given vouchers to gain housing in other areas.
sentence_152: Construction of the Beltline has stimulated new and related development along its path.
sentence_153: Under the [[Köppen_climate_classification|Köppen classification]], Atlanta has a humid subtropical climate (Cfa) with four distinct seasons and generous precipitation year-round, typical for the [[Upland_South|Upland South]]; the city is situated in [[Hardiness_zone|USDA Plant Hardiness Zone]] 8a, with the northern and western suburbs transitioning to 7b.
sentence_154: Summers are hot and humid, with temperatures somewhat moderated by the city's elevation.
sentence_155: Winters are cool but variable, occasionally susceptible to [[Winter_storm|snowstorms]] even if in small quantities on several occasions, unlike the central and southern portions of the state.
sentence_156: Warm air from the [[Gulf_of_Mexico|Gulf of Mexico]] can bring spring-like highs while strong Arctic air masses can push lows into the teens °F (−7 to −12 °C).
sentence_157: July averages 80.2 °F (26.8 °C), with high temperatures reaching 90 °F (32 °C) on an average of 44 days per year, though 100 °F (38 °C) readings are not seen most years.
sentence_158: January averages 43.5 °F (6.4 °C), with temperatures in the suburbs slightly cooler due largely to the [[Urban_heat_island|urban heat island]] effect.
sentence_159: Lows at or below freezing can be expected 40 nights annually, but the last occurrence of temperatures below 10 °F (−12 °C) is [[Early_2014_North_American_cold_wave|January 6, 2014]].
sentence_160: Extremes range from −9 °F (−23 °C) on [[Great_Blizzard_of_1899|February 13, 1899]] to 106 °F (41 °C) on [[Summer_2012_North_American_heat_wave|June 30, 2012]].
sentence_161: Average dewpoints in the summer range from 63.7 °F (17.6 °C) in June to 67.8 °F (19.9 °C) in July.
sentence_162: Typical of the southeastern U.S., Atlanta receives abundant rainfall that is evenly distributed throughout the year, though spring and early fall are markedly drier.
sentence_163: The average annual rainfall is 49.7 in (1,260 mm), while snowfall is typically light with a normal of 2.9 inches (7.4 cm) per winter.
sentence_164: The heaviest single snowfall occurred on January 23, 1940, with around 10 inches (25 cm) of snow.
sentence_165: However, [[Ice_storm|ice storms]] usually cause more problems than snowfall does, the most severe occurring on January 7, 1973.
sentence_166: Tornadoes are rare in the city itself, but the [[2008_Atlanta_tornado_outbreak|March 14, 2008]] [[Enhanced_Fujita_scale|EF2]] [[Tornado|tornado]] damaged prominent structures in downtown Atlanta.
sentence_167: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Atlanta|Demographics of Atlanta]]
sentence_168: See also: [[Religion_in_Atlanta|Religion in Atlanta]]
sentence_169: The [[2010_United_States_Census|2010 United States Census]] reported that Atlanta had a population of 420,003.
sentence_170: The [[Population_density|population density]] was 3,154 per [[Square_mile|square mile]] (1232/[[Square_kilometer|km]]).
sentence_171: The racial makeup and population of Atlanta was 54.0% Black or African American, 38.4% White, 3.1% Asian and 0.2% Native American.
sentence_172: Those from some other race made up 2.2% of the city's population, while those from two or more races made up 2.0%.
sentence_173: Hispanics of any race made up 5.2% of the city's population.
sentence_174: The median income for a household in the city was $45,171.
sentence_175: The per capita income for the city was $35,453.
sentence_176: 22.6% percent of the population was living below the [[Poverty_threshold|poverty line]].
sentence_177: In the 1920s, the black population began to grow in Southern cities like Atlanta, [[Birmingham,_Alabama|Birmingham]], [[Houston|Houston]], and [[Memphis,_Tennessee|Memphis]].
sentence_178: In the 2010 Census, Atlanta was recorded as the nation's fourth-largest majority-black city.
sentence_179: The [[New_Great_Migration|New Great Migration]] brought an insurgence of African Americans from [[California|California]] and the [[Northern_United_States|North]] to the Atlanta area.
sentence_180: It has long been known as a center of African-American political power, education, economic prosperity, and culture, often called a [[Black_mecca|black mecca]].
sentence_181: Some middle and upper class [[African_Americans_in_Atlanta|African-American residents of Atlanta]] followed an influx of whites to newer housing and public schools in the suburbs in the early 21st century.
sentence_182: From 2000 to 2010, the city's black population decreased by 31,678 people, shrinking from 61.4% of the city's population in 2000 to 54.0% in 2010, as the overall population expanded and migrants increased from other areas.
sentence_183: At the same time, the white population of Atlanta has increased.
sentence_184: Between 2000 and 2010, the proportion of whites in the city had notable growth.
sentence_185: In that decade, Atlanta's white population grew from 31% to 38% of the city's population, an absolute increase of 22,753 people, more than triple the increase that occurred between 1990 and 2000.
sentence_186: Early immigrants in the Atlanta area were mostly [[American_Jews|Jews]] and [[Greek_Americans|Greeks]].
sentence_187: Since 1970, the Hispanic immigrant population, especially Mexicans, has experienced the most rapid growth, particularly in Gwinnett, Cobb, and DeKalb counties.
sentence_188: Since 2010, the Atlanta area has seen very notable growth with immigrants from India, China, South Korea, and Jamaica.
sentence_189: Other notable countries immigrants come from are Vietnam, Eritrea, Nigeria, the Arabian gulf, Ukraine and Poland.
sentence_190: Within a few decades, and in keeping with national trends, immigrants from England, Ireland, and German-speaking central Europe were no longer the majority of Atlanta's foreign-born population.
sentence_191: The city's Italians included immigrants from northern Italy, many of whom had been in Atlanta since the 1890s; more recent arrivals from southern Italy; and Sephardic Jews from the Isle of Rhodes, which Italy had seized from [[Turkey|Turkey]] in 1912.
sentence_192: Of the total population five years and older, 83.3% spoke only English at home, while 8.8% spoke Spanish, 3.9% another Indo-European language, and 2.8% an Asian language.
sentence_193: 7.3% of Atlantans were born abroad (86th in the US).
sentence_194: Atlanta's dialect has traditionally been a variation of [[Southern_American_English|Southern American English]].
sentence_195: The [[Chattahoochee_River|Chattahoochee River]] long formed a border between the [[Southern_American_English#Dialects|Coastal Southern]] and [[Southern_American_English#Dialects|Southern Appalachian]] dialects.
sentence_196: Because of the development of corporate headquarters in the region, attracting migrants from other areas of the country, by 2003, [[Atlanta_(magazine)|Atlanta]] magazine concluded that Atlanta had become significantly "de-Southernized".
sentence_197: A Southern accent was considered a handicap in some circumstances.
sentence_198: In general, Southern accents are less prevalent among residents of the city and inner suburbs and among younger people; they are more common in the outer suburbs and among older people.
sentence_199: At the same time, some residents of the city speak in Southern variations of [[African-American_English|African-American English]].
sentence_200: [[Religion_in_Atlanta|Religion in Atlanta]], while historically centered on [[Protestant_Christianity|Protestant Christianity]], now encompasses many faiths, as a result of the city and metro area's increasingly international population.
sentence_201: Some 63% of residents identify as some type of Protestant, but in recent decades the [[Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Atlanta|Catholic Church]] has increased in numbers and influence because of new migrants to the region.
sentence_202: Metro Atlanta also has numerous ethnic or national Christian congregations, including Korean and Indian churches.
sentence_203: The larger non-Christian faiths are Judaism, [[Islam|Islam]], and [[Hinduism|Hinduism]].
sentence_204: Overall, there are over 1,000 places of worship within Atlanta.
sentence_205: Atlanta has one of the highest [[LGBT|lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT)]] populations per capita in the U.S.
sentence_206: According to a 2006 survey by the [[Williams_Institute_on_Sexual_Orientation_and_Gender_Identity_Law_and_Public_Policy|Williams Institute]], Atlanta ranked third among major American cities, behind [[San_Francisco|San Francisco]] and slightly behind [[Seattle|Seattle]], with 12.8% of the city's total population identifying as LGBT.
sentence_207: The [[Midtown_Atlanta|Midtown]] and [[Cheshire_Bridge_Road|Cheshire Bridge]] areas have historically been the epicenters of [[LGBT_culture|LGBT culture]] in Atlanta.
sentence_208: Atlanta formed a reputation for being a place of tolerance after former mayor [[Ivan_Allen_Jr.|Ivan Allen Jr.]] dubbed it "the city too busy to hate" in the 1960s.
sentence_209: Main article: [[Economy_of_Atlanta|Economy of Atlanta]]
sentence_210: With a GDP of $385 billion, the Atlanta metropolitan area's economy is the [[List_of_cities_by_GDP|tenth-largest in the country and among the top 20-largest in the world]].
sentence_211: Corporate operations play a major role in Atlanta's economy, as the city claims the nation's third-largest concentration of [[Fortune_500|Fortune 500]] companies.
sentence_212: It also hosts the global headquarters of corporations like [[The_Coca-Cola_Company|The Coca-Cola Company]], [[The_Home_Depot|The Home Depot]], [[Delta_Air_Lines|Delta Air Lines]], [[AT&T_Mobility|AT&T Mobility]], [[Chick-fil-A|Chick-fil-A]], and UPS.
sentence_213: Over 75% of [[Fortune_1000|Fortune 1000]] companies conduct business operations in the city's metro area, and the region hosts offices of over 1,250 multinational corporations.
sentence_214: Many corporations are drawn to the city by its educated workforce; as of 2014, 45% of adults aged 25 or older residing in the city have at least 4-year college degrees, compared to the national average of 28%.
sentence_215: Atlanta started as a railroad town, and [[Logistics|logistics]] has been a major component of the city's economy to this day.
sentence_216: Atlanta serves as an important rail junction and contains major classification yards for [[Norfolk_Southern|Norfolk Southern]] and [[CSX_Transportation|CSX]].
sentence_217: Since its construction in the 1950s, [[Hartsfield–Jackson_Atlanta_International_Airport|Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport]] has served as a key engine of the city's economic growth.
sentence_218: Delta Air Lines, the city's largest employer and the metro area's third-largest, operates the world's largest airline hub at Hartsfield-Jackson, and it has helped make it the [[World's_busiest_airport|world's busiest airport]], in terms of both passenger traffic and aircraft operations.
sentence_219: Partly due to the airport, Atlanta has been also a hub for diplomatic missions; as of 2017, the city contains [[List_of_diplomatic_missions_in_Atlanta|26 consulates general]], the seventh-highest concentration of diplomatic missions in the US.
sentence_220: Broadcasting is also an important aspect of Atlanta's economy.
sentence_221: In the 1980s, media mogul [[Ted_Turner|Ted Turner]] founded the [[Cable_News_Network|Cable News Network]] (CNN) and the Turner Broadcasting System (TBS) in the city.
sentence_222: Around the same time, [[Cox_Enterprises|Cox Enterprises]], now the nation's third-largest cable television service and the publisher of over a dozen American newspapers, moved its headquarters to the city.
sentence_223: [[The_Weather_Channel|The Weather Channel]] is also based just outside of the city in suburban Cobb County.
sentence_224: [[Information_technology|Information technology]] (IT) has become an increasingly important part of Atlanta's economic output, earning the city the nickname the "[[Silicon_peach|Silicon peach]]".
sentence_225: As of 2013, Atlanta contains the fourth-largest concentration of IT jobs in the US, numbering 85,000+.
sentence_226: The city is also ranked as the sixth fastest-growing for IT jobs, with an employment growth of 4.8% in 2012 and a three-year growth near 9%, or 16,000 jobs.
sentence_227: Companies are drawn to Atlanta's lower costs and educated workforce.
sentence_228: Recently, Atlanta has been the [[Economy_of_Atlanta#Film_and_television|center for film and television production]], largely because of the [[Georgia_Department_of_Economic_Development#Georgia_Entertainment_Industry_Investment_Act|Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act]], which awards qualified productions a transferable income tax credit of 20% of all in-state costs for film and television investments of $500,000 or more.
sentence_229: Some film and television production facilities based in Atlanta include Turner Studios, [[Pinewood_Studios|Pinewood Studios]] (Pinewood Atlanta), [[Tyler_Perry_Studios|Tyler Perry Studios]], [[Williams_Street|Williams Street]] Productions, and the EUE/Screen Gems soundstages.
sentence_230: Film and television production injected $9.5 billion into Georgia's economy in 2017, with Atlanta garnering most of the projects.
sentence_231: Atlanta has emerged as the all-time most popular destination for film production in the United States and one of the ten most popular destinations globally.
sentence_232: Compared to other American cities, Atlanta's economy in the past had been disproportionately affected by the [[2007–2012_global_financial_crisis|2008 financial crisis]] and the [[Great_Recession|subsequent recession]], with the city's economy earning a ranking of 68 among 100 American cities in a September 2014 report due to an elevated unemployment rate, declining real income levels, and a depressed housing market.
sentence_233: From 2010 to 2011, Atlanta saw a 0.9% contraction in employment and plateauing income growth at 0.4%.
sentence_234: Although unemployment had decreased to 7% by late 2014, this was still higher than the national unemployment rate of 5.8% Atlanta's housing market has also struggled, with home prices dropping by 2.1% in January 2012, reaching levels not seen since 1996.
sentence_235: Compared with a year earlier, the average home price in Atlanta plummeted to 17.3% in February 2012, thus becoming the largest annual drop in the history of the index for any American or global city.
sentence_236: The decline in home prices prompted some economists to deem Atlanta the worst housing market in the nation at the height of the depression.
sentence_237: Nevertheless, the city's real estate market has resurged since 2012, so much median home value and rent growth significantly outpaced the national average by 2018, thanks to a rapidly-growing regional economy.
sentence_238: Atlanta is noted for its lack of [[Southern_United_States|Southern]] culture.
sentence_239: This is due to a large population of migrants from other parts of the U.S., in addition to many recent [[Immigration_to_the_United_States|immigrants to the U.S.]] who have made the metropolitan area their home, establishing Atlanta as the cultural and economic hub of an increasingly multi-cultural metropolitan area.
sentence_240: Thus, although traditional Southern culture is part of Atlanta's cultural fabric, it is mostly a footnote to one of the nation's most cosmopolitan cities.
sentence_241: This unique cultural combination reveals itself in the arts district of Midtown, the quirky neighborhoods on the city's [[Eastside_(Atlanta)|eastside]], and the multi-ethnic enclaves found along [[Buford_Highway|Buford Highway]].
sentence_242: Main article: [[Arts_in_Atlanta|Arts in Atlanta]]
sentence_243: Atlanta is one of few United States cities with permanent, professional, and resident companies in all major performing arts disciplines: opera ([[Atlanta_Opera|Atlanta Opera]]), ballet ([[Atlanta_Ballet|Atlanta Ballet]]), orchestral music (Atlanta Symphony Orchestra), and theater (the [[Alliance_Theatre|Alliance Theatre]]).
sentence_244: Atlanta attracts many touring Broadway acts, concerts, shows, and exhibitions catering to a variety of interests.
sentence_245: Atlanta's performing arts district is concentrated in [[Midtown_Atlanta|Midtown Atlanta]] at the [[Woodruff_Arts_Center|Woodruff Arts Center]], which is home to the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra and the [[Alliance_Theatre|Alliance Theatre]].
sentence_246: The city frequently hosts touring Broadway acts, especially at The [[Fox_Theatre_(Atlanta,_Georgia)|Fox Theatre]], a historic landmark among the highest-grossing theaters of its size.
sentence_247: As a national center for the arts, Atlanta is home to significant art museums and institutions.
sentence_248: The renowned [[High_Museum_of_Art|High Museum of Art]] is arguably the South's leading art museum.
sentence_249: The [[Museum_of_Design_Atlanta|Museum of Design Atlanta]] (MODA) and the SCAD FASH Museum of Fashion + Film are the only such museums in the Southeast.
sentence_250: Contemporary art museums include the Atlanta Contemporary Art Center and the Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia.
sentence_251: Institutions of higher education contribute to Atlanta's art scene, with the Savannah College of Art and Design's Atlanta campus providing the city's arts community with a steady stream of curators, and Emory University's [[Michael_C._Carlos_Museum|Michael C. Carlos Museum]] containing the largest collection of ancient art in the Southeast.
sentence_252: In nearby [[Athens,_Georgia|Athens]] is the [[Georgia_Museum_of_Art|Georgia Museum of Art]] that is associated with the [[University_of_Georgia|University of Georgia]] and is both an academic museum and the official art museum of the state of Georgia.
sentence_253: Atlanta has become one of the USA's best cities for [[Street_art|street art]] in recent years.
sentence_254: It is home to [[Living_Walls|Living Walls]], an annual street art conference and the , an annual event series that merges public art, live music, design, action sports, and culture.
sentence_255: Examples of [[Street_art_in_Atlanta|street art in Atlanta]] can be found on the .
sentence_256: Main article: [[Music_of_Atlanta|Music of Atlanta]]
sentence_257: Atlanta has played a major or contributing role in the development of various genres of American music at different points in the city's history.
sentence_258: Beginning as early as the 1920s, Atlanta emerged as a center for [[Country_music|country music]], which was brought to the city by migrants from [[Appalachia|Appalachia]].
sentence_259: During the [[Counterculture_of_the_1960s|countercultural 1960s]], Atlanta hosted the [[Atlanta_International_Pop_Festival_(1969)|Atlanta International Pop Festival]], with the 1969 festival taking place more than a month before [[Woodstock|Woodstock]] and featuring many of the same bands.
sentence_260: The city was also a center for Southern rock during its 1970s heyday: the [[Allman_Brothers_Band|Allman Brothers Band]]'s hit instrumental "Hot 'Lanta" is an ode to the city, while [[Lynyrd_Skynyrd|Lynyrd Skynyrd]]'s famous live rendition of "[[Free_Bird|Free Bird]]" was recorded at the [[Fox_Theatre_(Atlanta,_Georgia)|Fox Theatre]] in 1976, with lead singer [[Ronnie_Van_Zant|Ronnie Van Zant]] directing the band to "play it pretty for Atlanta".
sentence_261: During the 1980s, Atlanta had an active [[Punk_rock|punk rock]] scene centered on two of the city's music venues, [[688_Club|688 Club]] and the Metroplex, and Atlanta famously played host to the [[Sex_Pistols|Sex Pistols]]' first U.S. show, which was performed at the Great Southeastern Music Hall.
sentence_262: The 1990s saw the city produce major mainstream acts across many different musical genres.
sentence_263: Country music artist [[Travis_Tritt|Travis Tritt]], and R&B sensations [[Xscape_(group)|Xscape]], [[TLC_(group)|TLC]], [[Usher_(musician)|Usher]] and [[Toni_Braxton|Toni Braxton]], were just some of the musicians who call Atlanta home.
sentence_264: The city also gave birth to [[Atlanta_hip_hop|Atlanta hip hop]], a subgenre that gained relevance and success with the introduction of the home-grown Atlantans known as [[Outkast|Outkast]], along with other [[Dungeon_Family|Dungeon Family]] artists such as [[Organized_Noize|Organized Noize]] and Goodie Mob; however, it was not until the 2000s that Atlanta moved "from the margins to becoming hip-hop's center of gravity with another sub-genre called [[Crunk|Crunk]], part of a larger shift in hip-hop innovation to the South and East".
sentence_265: Also in the 2000s, Atlanta was recognized by the Brooklyn-based [[Vice_(magazine)|Vice]] magazine for its [[Indie_rock|indie rock]] scene, which revolves around the various live music venues found on the city's alternative [[Eastside_(Atlanta)|eastside]].
sentence_266: To facilitate further local development, the state government provides qualified businesses and productions a 15% transferable income tax credit for in-state costs of music investments.
sentence_267: [[Trap_music|Trap music]] became popular in Atlanta, and has since become a hub for popular trap artists and producers due to the success of [[T.I.|T.I.
sentence_268: ]], [[Young_Jeezy|Young Jeezy]], [[21_Savage|21 Savage]], [[Gucci_Mane|Gucci Mane]], [[Future_(rapper)|Future]], [[Migos|Migos]], [[Lil_Yachty|Lil Yachty]], [[2_Chainz|2 Chainz]], [[Playboi_Carti|Playboi Carti]] and [[Young_Thug|Young Thug]].
sentence_269: As the national leader for motion picture and television production, and a top ten global leader, Atlanta plays a significant role in the entertainment industry.
sentence_270: Atlanta is considered a hub for filmmakers of [[Person_of_color|color]] and houses [[Tyler_Perry_Studios|Tyler Perry Studios]] (first African-American owned major studio) and Areu Bros. Studios (first Latino-American owned major studio).
sentence_271: Atlanta doubles for other parts of the world and fictional settlements in blockbuster productions, among them the newer titles from The Fast and the Furious franchise and [[Marvel_Studios|Marvel]] features such as [[Ant-Man_(film)|Ant-Man]] (2015), Captain America: Civil War (2016), [[Black_Panther_(film)|Black Panther]] and Avengers: Infinity War (both 2018).
sentence_272: On the other hand, [[Gone_with_the_Wind_(1939_film)|Gone With the Wind]] (1939), [[Smokey_and_the_Bandit|Smokey and the Bandit]] (1977), [[Sharky's_Machine_(film)|Sharkey's Machine]] (1981), [[The_Slugger's_Wife|The Slugger's Wife]] (1985), [[Driving_Miss_Daisy_(film)|Driving Miss Daisy]] (1989), [[ATL_(film)|ATL]] (2006), and [[Baby_Driver|Baby Driver]] (2017) are among several notable examples of films actually set in Atlanta.
sentence_273: The city also provides the backdrop for shows such as [[Ozark_(TV_series)|Ozark]], [[Watchmen_(TV_series)|Watchmen]], [[The_Walking_Dead_(TV_series)|The Walking Dead]], [[Stranger_Things|Stranger Things]], [[Love_is_Blind_(TV_series)|Love is Blind]], [[Star_(TV_series)|Star]], [[Dolly_Parton's_Heartstrings_(TV_series)|Dolly Parton's Heartstrings]], [[The_Outsider_(miniseries)|The Outsider]], [[The_Vampire_Diaries|The Vampire Diaries]] and [[Atlanta_(TV_series)|Atlanta]], in addition to a myriad of [[Animated_series|animated]] and [[Reality_television|reality television]] programming.
sentence_274: Main article: Festivals in Atlanta
sentence_275: Atlanta has more festivals than any city in the southeastern United States.
sentence_276: Some notable festivals in Atlanta include [[Shaky_Knees_Music_Festival|Shaky Knees Music Festival]], [[Dragon_Con|Dragon Con]], the [[Peachtree_Road_Race|Peachtree Road Race]], [[Music_Midtown|Music Midtown]], the [[Atlanta_Film_Festival|Atlanta Film Festival]], National Black Arts Festival, [[Honda_Battle_of_the_Bands|Honda Battle of the Bands]], [[Festival_Peachtree_Latino|Festival Peachtree Latino]], [[Atlanta_Pride|Atlanta Pride]], the neighborhood festivals in [[Inman_Park|Inman Park]], [[Atkins_Park|Atkins Park]], [[Virginia-Highland_Summerfest|Virginia-Highland (Summerfest)]], and the [[Little_Five_Points|Little Five Points]] Halloween festival.
sentence_277: Main articles: [[Tourism_in_Atlanta|Tourism in Atlanta]], List of museums in Atlanta, and [[Cuisine_of_Atlanta|Cuisine of Atlanta]]
sentence_278: As of 2010, Atlanta is the seventh-most visited city in the United States, with over 35 million visitors per year.
sentence_279: Although the most popular attraction among visitors to Atlanta is the [[Georgia_Aquarium|Georgia Aquarium]], the world's largest indoor aquarium, Atlanta's tourism industry is mostly driven by the city's history museums and outdoor attractions.
sentence_280: Atlanta contains a notable number of historical museums and sites, including the [[Martin_Luther_King_Jr._National_Historical_Park|Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park]], which includes the preserved childhood home of Dr. [[Martin_Luther_King_Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr.]], as well as his final resting place; the [[Atlanta_Cyclorama_&_Civil_War_Museum|Atlanta Cyclorama & Civil War Museum]], which houses a massive painting and [[Diorama|diorama]] in-the-round, with a rotating central audience platform, depicting the [[Battle_of_Atlanta|Battle of Atlanta]] in the Civil War; the [[World_of_Coca-Cola|World of Coca-Cola]], featuring the history of the world-famous soft drink brand and its well-known advertising; the [[College_Football_Hall_of_Fame|College Football Hall of Fame]], which honors college football and its athletes; the [[National_Center_for_Civil_and_Human_Rights|National Center for Civil and Human Rights]], which explores the civil rights movement and its connection to contemporary [[Human_rights_movement|human rights movements]] throughout the world; the [[Carter_Center|Carter Center]] and Presidential Library, housing U.S. President [[Jimmy_Carter|Jimmy Carter]]'s papers and other material relating to the Carter administration and the Carter family's life; and the Margaret Mitchell House and Museum, where Mitchell wrote the best-selling novel [[Gone_with_the_Wind_(novel)|Gone with the Wind]].
sentence_281: Atlanta contains several outdoor attractions.
sentence_282: The Atlanta Botanical Garden, adjacent to Piedmont Park, is home to the 600-foot-long (180 m) [[Atlanta_Botanical_Garden#Canopy_Walk|Kendeda Canopy Walk]], a [[Skyway|skywalk]] that allows visitors to tour one of the city's last remaining urban forests from 40 feet (12 m) above the ground.
sentence_283: The Canopy Walk is considered the only canopy-level pathway of its kind in the United States.
sentence_284: [[Zoo_Atlanta|Zoo Atlanta]], in [[Grant_Park_(Atlanta)|Grant Park]], accommodates over 1,300 animals representing more than 220 species.
sentence_285: Home to the nation's largest collections of gorillas and orangutans, the zoo is one of only four zoos in the U.S. to house [[Giant_panda|giant pandas]].
sentence_286: Festivals showcasing arts and crafts, film, and music, including the [[Atlanta_Dogwood_Festival|Atlanta Dogwood Festival]], the [[Atlanta_Film_Festival|Atlanta Film Festival]], and [[Music_Midtown|Music Midtown]], respectively, are also popular with tourists.
sentence_287: Tourists are drawn to the city's culinary scene, which comprises a mix of urban establishments garnering national attention, ethnic restaurants serving cuisine from every corner of the world, and traditional eateries specializing in Southern dining.
sentence_288: Since the turn of the 21st century, Atlanta has emerged as a sophisticated restaurant town.
sentence_289: Many restaurants opened in the city's [[Gentrification_of_Atlanta|gentrifying neighborhoods]] have received praise at the national level, including Bocado, Bacchanalia, and Miller Union in [[West_Midtown|West Midtown]], Empire State South in [[Midtown_Atlanta|Midtown]], and Two Urban Licks and [[Kevin_Rathbun|Rathbun's]] on the [[Eastside_(Atlanta)|east side]].
sentence_290: In 2011, The New York Times characterized Empire State South and Miller Union as reflecting "a new kind of sophisticated Southern sensibility centered on the farm but experienced in the city".
sentence_291: Visitors seeking to sample international Atlanta are directed to [[Buford_Highway|Buford Highway]], the city's international corridor, and suburban [[Gwinnett_County,_Georgia|Gwinnett County]].
sentence_292: There, the nearly-million [[Immigrants|immigrants]] that make Atlanta home have established various authentic ethnic restaurants representing virtually every nationality on the globe.
sentence_293: For traditional Southern fare, one of the city's most famous establishments is [[The_Varsity|The Varsity]], a long-lived fast food chain and the world's largest drive-in restaurant.
sentence_294: Mary Mac's Tea Room and [[Paschal's|Paschal's]] are more formal destinations for Southern food.
sentence_295: Main article: [[Sports_in_Atlanta|Sports in Atlanta]]
sentence_296: Sports are an important part of the culture of Atlanta.
sentence_297: The city is home to professional franchises for four major team sports: the [[Atlanta_Braves|Atlanta Braves]] of [[Major_League_Baseball|Major League Baseball]], the [[Atlanta_Hawks|Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National_Basketball_Association|National Basketball Association]], the [[Atlanta_Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National_Football_League|National Football League]], and [[Atlanta_United_FC|Atlanta United FC]] of [[Major_League_Soccer|Major League Soccer]].
sentence_298: In addition, many of the city's universities participate in collegiate sports.
sentence_299: The city also regularly hosts international, professional, and collegiate sporting events.
sentence_300: The Braves moved to Atlanta in 1966.
sentence_301: Originally established as the [[Boston|Boston]] Red Stockings in 1871, they are the oldest continually operating professional sports franchise in the United States.
sentence_302: The Braves won the [[World_Series|World Series]] in 1995, during an unprecedented run of 14 straight divisional championships from 1991 to 2005.
sentence_303: The team plays at [[Truist_Park|Truist Park]], having moved from [[Turner_Field|Turner Field]] for the 2017 season.
sentence_304: The new stadium is outside the city limits, located 10 miles (16 km) northwest of downtown in the Cumberland/Galleria area of Cobb county.
sentence_305: The [[Atlanta_Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] have played in Atlanta since their inception in 1966.
sentence_306: The team play their home games at [[Mercedes_Benz_Stadium|Mercedes Benz Stadium]], having moved from the [[Georgia_Dome|Georgia Dome]] in 2017.
sentence_307: The Falcons have won the division title six times (1980, 1998, 2004, 2010, 2012, 2016) and the NFC championship twice in 1998 and 2016.
sentence_308: However, they have been unsuccessful in both of their Super Bowl trips, losing to the [[Denver_Broncos|Denver Broncos]] in [[Super_Bowl_XXXIII|Super Bowl XXXIII]] in 1999 and to the [[New_England_Patriots|New England Patriots]] in [[Super_Bowl_LI|Super Bowl LI]] in 2017.
sentence_309: In 2019, Atlanta also briefly hosted an [[Alliance_of_American_Football|Alliance of American Football]] team, the [[Atlanta_Legends|Atlanta Legends]], but the league was suspended during its first season and the team folded.
sentence_310: The [[Atlanta_Hawks|Atlanta Hawks]] were founded in 1946 as the Tri-Cities Blackhawks, playing in [[Moline,_Illinois|Moline, Illinois]].
sentence_311: they moved to Atlanta in 1968 and play their games in [[State_Farm_Arena|State Farm Arena]].
sentence_312: The city is also home to a [[Women's_National_Basketball_Association|Women's National Basketball Association]] franchise, the [[Atlanta_Dream|Atlanta Dream]], who share the stadium with the Hawks.
sentence_313: Professional soccer has been played in some form in Atlanta since 1967.
sentence_314: Atlanta's first professional soccer team was the [[Atlanta_Chiefs|Atlanta Chiefs]] of the original [[North_American_Soccer_League_(1968–84)|North American Soccer League]] which won the 1968 NASL Championship and defeated English first division club [[Manchester_City_F.C.|Manchester City F.C.]] twice in international friendlies.
sentence_315: In 1998 the [[Atlanta_Silverbacks|Atlanta Silverbacks]] were formed, playing the new [[North_American_Soccer_League|North American Soccer League]].
sentence_316: They now play as an amateur club in the National Premier Soccer League.
sentence_317: In 2017, [[Atlanta_United_FC|Atlanta United FC]] began play as Atlanta's first premier-division professional soccer club since the Chiefs.
sentence_318: They won [[MLS_Cup_2018|MLS Cup 2018]], defeating the [[Portland_Timbers|Portland Timbers]] 2–0.
sentence_319: Fan reception has been very positive; the team has broken several single-game and season attendance records for both MLS and the [[U.S._Open_Cup|U.S.
sentence_320: Open Cup]].
sentence_321: The club is estimated by [[Forbes|Forbes]] to be the most valuable club in Major League Soccer.
sentence_322: In ice hockey, Atlanta has had two [[National_Hockey_League|National Hockey League]] franchises, both of which relocated after playing in Atlanta for fewer than 15 years.
sentence_323: The [[Atlanta_Flames|Atlanta Flames]] began play in 1972 before moving to [[Calgary_Flames|Calgary]] in 1980, and the [[Atlanta_Thrashers|Atlanta Thrashers]] began play in 1999 before moving to [[Winnipeg_Jets|Winnipeg]] in 2011.
sentence_324: The [[Atlanta_Gladiators|Atlanta Gladiators]] of the [[ECHL|ECHL]] Play in Duluth, a suburb northeast of the city.
sentence_325: Several other, less popular sports also have professional franchises in Atlanta.
sentence_326: The [[Georgia_Swarm|Georgia Swarm]] compete in the National Lacrosse League.
sentence_327: On September 21, 2018, [[Major_League_Rugby|Major League Rugby]] announced that Atlanta was one of the expansion teams joining the league for the 2020 season named [[Rugby_ATL|Rugby ATL]].
sentence_328: On August 2, 2018, it was announced that Atlanta would have its own [[Overwatch_League|Overwatch League]] team, [[Atlanta_Reign|Atlanta Reign]].
sentence_329: Atlanta has long been known as the "capital" of college football in America.
