title: Asteraceae
sentence_0: Asteraceae or Compositae (commonly referred to as the aster, daisy, composite, or sunflower family), is a very large and widespread [[Family_(biology)|family]] of [[Flowering_plant|flowering plants]] (Angiospermae).
sentence_1: The family includes over 32,000 currently accepted species, in over 1,900 genera ([[List_of_Asteraceae_genera|list]]) in 13 subfamilies.
sentence_2: In terms of numbers of species, the Asteraceae are rivaled only by the [[Orchidaceae|Orchidaceae]].
sentence_3: Which is the larger family is unclear, because of the uncertainty about how many [[Extant_taxon|extant]] species each family includes.
sentence_4: Nearly all Asteraceae bear their flowers in dense heads (capitula or pseudanthia) surrounded by [[Bract#Involucral_bracts|involucral bracts]].
sentence_5: When viewed from a distance, each [[Capitulum_(flower)|capitulum]] may appear to be a single flower.
sentence_6: Enlarged outer (peripheral) flowers in the capitula may resemble petals, and the involucral bracts may look like a calyx.
sentence_7: The alternative name of the family Asteraceae comes from the type genus [[Aster_(genus)|Aster]], from the Ancient Greek , meaning star, and refers to the star-like form of the inflorescence.
sentence_8: The original name Compositae is still valid under the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants.)
sentence_9: It refers to the "composite" nature of the capitula, which consist of a few or many individual flowers.
sentence_10: Most members of Asteraceae are [[Annual_plant|annual]] or perennial herbs, but a significant number are also shrubs, vines, or trees.
sentence_11: The family has a [[Cosmopolitan_distribution|cosmopolitan distribution]], with species ranging from to tropical regions, colonizing a wide variety of habitats.
sentence_12: The largest proportion of the species occur in the arid and semiarid regions of subtropical and lower temperate latitudes.
sentence_13: The Asteraceae may represent as much as 10% of [[Autochthon_(nature)|autochthonous]] flora in many regions of the world.
sentence_14: Asteraceae is an economically important family, providing products such as cooking oils, [[Leaf_vegetable|leaf vegetables]] like [[Lettuce|lettuce]], [[Sunflower_seed|sunflower seeds]], [[Artichoke|artichokes]], [[Sweetening_agent|sweetening agents]], coffee substitutes and herbal teas.
sentence_15: Several genera are of [[Horticulture|horticultural]] importance, including pot marigold ([[Calendula_officinalis|Calendula officinalis]]), [[Echinacea|Echinacea]] (coneflowers), various daisies, [[Erigeron|fleabane]], [[Chrysanthemum|chrysanthemums]], [[Dahlia|dahlias]], [[Zinnia|zinnias]], and [[Helenium|heleniums]].
sentence_16: Asteraceae are important in herbal medicine, including [[Grindelia|Grindelia]], [[Achillea_millefolium|yarrow]], and many others.
sentence_17: On the other hand, many Asteraceae are considered weeds in various circumstances.
sentence_18: Of these, many are [[Invasive_species|invasive species]] in particular regions, often having been introduced by human agency.
sentence_19: Examples include various [[Tumbleweed|tumbleweeds]], [[Bidens|Bidens]], [[Ambrosia_(plant)|ragweeds]], [[Thistle|thistles]], and [[Taraxacum_officinale|dandelion]].
sentence_20: Dandelion was introduced into North America by European settlers who used the young leaves as a salad green.
sentence_21: The study of this family is known as [[Synantherology|synantherology]].
sentence_22: The name Asteraceae (English: [[English|/ˌæstəˈreɪsi, -siˌaɪ, -siˌeɪ, -siˌiː/]]) comes to [[International_scientific_vocabulary|international scientific vocabulary]] from [[New_Latin|New Latin]], from [[Aster_(genus)|Aster]], the [[Type_genus|type genus]], + , a standardized [[Suffix|suffix]] for plant family names in modern taxonomy.
sentence_23: The genus name comes from the [[Classical_Latin|Classical Latin]] word , "star", which came from Ancient Greek ἀστήρ (astḗr), "star".
sentence_24: The earlier name, Compositae (now recognized as an alternative name) means "composite" and refers to the characteristic [[Inflorescence|inflorescence]], a special type of [[Pseudanthium|pseudanthium]] found in only a few other [[Angiosperm|angiosperm]] families.
sentence_25: The vernacular name daisy, widely applied to members of this family, is derived from the [[Old_English|Old English]] name of the daisy ([[Bellis_perennis|Bellis perennis]]): , meaning "day's eye".
sentence_26: This is because the petals open at dawn and close at dusk.
sentence_27: Asteraceae species have a [[Cosmopolitan_distribution|cosmopolitan distribution]], and are found everywhere except [[Antarctica|Antarctica]] and the extreme Arctic.
sentence_28: They are especially numerous in tropical and subtropical regions (notably [[Central_America|Central America]], eastern [[Brazil|Brazil]], the Mediterranean, [[The_Levant|the Levant]], [[Southern_Africa|southern Africa]], [[Central_Asia|central Asia]], and [[Southwestern_China|southwestern China]]).
sentence_29: See also: [[List_of_Asteraceae_genera|List of Asteraceae genera]]
sentence_30: Compositae, the original name for Asteraceae, were first described in 1792 by the German botanist [[Paul_Dietrich_Giseke|Paul Dietrich Giseke]].
sentence_31: Traditionally, two subfamilies were recognised: [[Asteroideae|Asteroideae]] (or Tubuliflorae) and [[Cichorioideae|Cichorioideae]] (or Liguliflorae).
sentence_32: The latter has been shown to be extensively [[Paraphyletic|paraphyletic]], and has now been divided into 12 subfamilies, but the former still stands.
sentence_33: The [[Phylogenetic_tree|phylogenetic tree]] presented below is based on Panero & Funk (2002) updated in 2014, and now also includes the monotypic Famatinanthoideae.
sentence_34: The diamond denotes a very poorly supported [[Cladistics|node]] (<50% bootstrap support), the dot a poorly supported node (<80%).
sentence_35: The four subfamilies [[Asteroideae|Asteroideae]], [[Cichorioideae|Cichorioideae]], [[Carduoideae|Carduoideae]] and [[Mutisioideae|Mutisioideae]] contain 99% of the species diversity of the whole family (approximately 70%, 14%, 11% and 3% respectively).
sentence_36: Because of the [[Morphology_(biology)|morphological]] complexity exhibited by this family, agreeing on generic circumscriptions has often been difficult for [[Taxonomist|taxonomists]].
sentence_37: As a result, several of these genera have required multiple revisions.
sentence_38: Members of the Asteraceae are mostly [[Herbaceous_plants|herbaceous plants]], but some shrubs, [[Vine|climbers]] and trees (such as [[Lachanodes_arborea|Lachanodes arborea]]) do exist.
sentence_39: They are generally easy to distinguish from other plants, mainly because of their characteristic [[Inflorescence|inflorescence]] and other shared characteristics.
sentence_40: However, determining genera and species of some groups such as [[Hieracium#Species|Hieracium]] is notoriously difficult (see "[[Damned_yellow_composite|damned yellow composite]]" for example).
sentence_41: Members of the Asteraceae generally produce taproots, but sometimes they possess fibrous root systems.
sentence_42: Stems are herbaceous aerial branched cylindrical with glandular hairs generally erect but can be prostrate to ascending.
sentence_43: Some species have underground stems in the form of [[Caudex|caudices]] or [[Rhizome|rhizomes]].
sentence_44: These can be fleshy or woody depending on the species.
sentence_45: The [[Leaf|leaves]] and the stems very often contain secretory canals with [[Resin|resin]] or [[Latex|latex]] (particularly common among the Cichorioideae).
sentence_46: The leaves can be [[Phyllotaxis|alternate]], [[Phyllotaxis|opposite]], or [[Phyllotaxis|whorled]].
sentence_47: They may be simple, but are often deeply [[Leaf#Morphology|lobed]] or otherwise [[Leaf#Morphology|incised]], often [[Leaf#Morphology|conduplicate]] or [[Leaf#Morphology|revolute]].
sentence_48: The margins can be entire or lobed or toothed.
sentence_49: In plants of the family Asteraceae, what appears to be a single flower is actually a cluster of much smaller flowers.
sentence_50: The overall appearance of the cluster, as a single flower, functions in attracting pollinators in the same way as the structure of an individual flower in some other plant families.
sentence_51: The older family name, Compositae, comes from the fact that what appears to be a single flower is actually a composite of smaller flowers.
sentence_52: The "petals" or "sunrays" in a sunflower head are actually individual strap-shaped flowers called ray flowers, and the "sun disk" is made of smaller circular shaped individual flowers called disc flowers.
sentence_53: The word "aster" means "star" in Greek, referring to the appearance of some family members, as a "star" surrounded by "rays".
sentence_54: The cluster of flowers that may appear to be a single flower, is called a head.
sentence_55: The entire head may move tracking the sun, like a "smart" solar panel, which maximizes reflectivity of the whole unit and can thereby attract more pollinators.
sentence_56: At the base of the head, and surrounding the flowers before opening, is a bundle of [[Sepal|sepal]]-like [[Bract|bracts]] or scales called [[Phyllaries|phyllaries]], which together form the involucre that protects the individual flowers in the head before opening.
sentence_57: The individual heads have the smaller individual flowers arranged on a round or dome-like structure called the receptacle.
sentence_58: The flowers mature first at the outside, moving toward the center, with the youngest in the middle.
sentence_59: The individual flowers in a head have 5 fused petals (rarely 4), but instead of sepals, have threadlike, hairy, or bristly structures called [[Pappus_(flower_structure)|pappus]], which surround the fruit and can stick to animal fur or be lifted by wind, aiding in seed dispersal.
sentence_60: The whitish fluffy head of a dandelion, commonly blown on by children, is made of the pappus, with tiny seeds attached at the ends, whereby the pappus provides a parachute like structure to help the seed be carried away in the wind.
sentence_61: A ray flower is a 3-tipped (3-lobed), strap-shaped, individual flower in the head of some members of the family Asteraceae.
sentence_62: Sometimes a ray flower is 2-tipped (2-lobed).
sentence_63: The [[Petal|corolla]] of the ray flower may have 2 tiny teeth opposite the 3-lobed strap, or tongue, indicating evolution by fusion from an originally 5-part corolla.
sentence_64: Sometimes, the 3:2 arrangement is reversed, with 2 tips on the tongue, and 0 or 3 tiny teeth opposite the tongue.
sentence_65: A ligulate flower is a 5-tipped, strap-shaped, individual flower in the heads of other members.
sentence_66: A ligule is the strap-shaped tongue of the [[Petal|corolla]] of either a ray flower or of a ligulate flower.
sentence_67: A disk flower (or disc flower) is a radially symmetric (i.e., with identical shaped petals arranged in circle around the center) individual flower in the head, which is ringed by ray flowers when both are present.
sentence_68: Sometimes ray flowers may be slightly off from radial symmetry, or weakly bilaterally symmetric, as in the case of desert pincushions [[Chaenactis_fremontii|Chaenactis fremontii]].
sentence_69: A radiate head has disc flowers surrounded by ray flowers.
sentence_70: A ligulate head has all ligulate flowers.
sentence_71: When a sunflower family flower head has only disc flowers that are sterile, male, or have both male and female parts, it is a discoid head.
sentence_72: Disciform heads have only disc flowers, but may have two kinds (male flowers and female flowers) in one head, or may have different heads of two kinds (all male, or all female).
sentence_73: Pistillate heads have all female flowers.
sentence_74: Staminate heads have all male flowers.
sentence_75: Sometimes, but rarely, the head contains only a single flower, or has a single flowered pistillate (female) head, and a multi-flowered male staminate (male) head.
sentence_76: The distinguishing characteristic of Asteraceae is their [[Inflorescence|inflorescence]], a type of specialised, composite flower head or [[Pseudanthium|pseudanthium]], technically called a calathium or [[Pseudanthium|capitulum]], that may look superficially like a single flower.
sentence_77: The capitulum is a contracted [[Raceme|raceme]] composed of numerous individual [[Sessility_(botany)|sessile]] [[Flower|flowers]], called florets, all sharing the same [[Receptacle_(botany)|receptacle]].
sentence_78: A set of [[Bract|bracts]] forms an [[Involucral_bract|involucre]] surrounding the base of the capitulum.
sentence_79: These are called "phyllaries", or "involucral bracts".
sentence_80: They may simulate the [[Sepal|sepals]] of the pseudanthium.
sentence_81: These are mostly herbaceous but can also be brightly coloured (e.g. [[Helichrysum|Helichrysum]]) or have a scarious (dry and membranous) texture.
sentence_82: The phyllaries can be free or fused, and arranged in one to many rows, overlapping like the tiles of a roof (imbricate) or not (this variation is important in identification of tribes and genera).
sentence_83: Each floret may be subtended by a bract, called a "palea" or "receptacular bract".
sentence_84: These bracts are often called "[[Chaff|chaff]]".
sentence_85: The presence or absence of these bracts, their distribution on the receptacle, and their size and shape are all important diagnostic characteristics for genera and tribes.
sentence_86: The florets have five [[Petal|petals]] fused at the base to form a [[Corolla_(flower)|corolla]] tube and they may be either [[Actinomorphic|actinomorphic]] or [[Zygomorphic|zygomorphic]].
sentence_87: Disc florets are usually actinomorphic, with five petal lips on the rim of the corolla tube.
sentence_88: The petal lips may be either very short, or long, in which case they form deeply lobed petals.
sentence_89: The latter is the only kind of floret in the Carduoideae, while the first kind is more widespread.
sentence_90: Ray florets are always highly zygomorphic and are characterised by the presence of a ligule, a strap-shaped structure on the edge of the corolla tube consisting of fused petals.
sentence_91: In the Asteroideae and other minor subfamilies these are usually borne only on florets at the circumference of the capitulum and have a 3+2 scheme – above the fused corolla tube, three very long fused [[Petal|petals]] form the ligule, with the other two petals being inconspicuously small.
sentence_92: The Cichorioideae has only ray florets, with a 5+0 scheme – all five petals form the ligule.
sentence_93: A 4+1 scheme is found in the Barnadesioideae.
sentence_94: The tip of the ligule is often divided into teeth, each one representing a petal.
sentence_95: Some marginal florets may have no petals at all (filiform floret).
sentence_96: The [[Calyx_(botany)|calyx]] of the florets may be absent, but when present is always modified into a [[Pappus_(flower_structure)|pappus]] of two or more teeth, scales or bristles and this is often involved in the dispersion of the seeds.
sentence_97: As with the bracts, the nature of the pappus is an important diagnostic feature.
sentence_98: There are usually five [[Stamen|stamens]].
sentence_99: The filaments are fused to the corolla, while the anthers are generally [[Connation|connate]] (syngenesious anthers), thus forming a sort of tube around the style (theca).
sentence_100: They commonly have basal and/or apical appendages.
sentence_101: Pollen is released inside the tube and is collected around the growing style, and then, as the style elongates, is pushed out of the tube (nüdelspritze).
sentence_102: The [[Pistil|pistil]] consists of two connate [[Carpel|carpels]].
sentence_103: The [[Carpel|style]] has two lobes.
sentence_104: Stigmatic tissue may be located in the interior surface or form two lateral lines.
sentence_105: The [[Ovary_(plants)|ovary]] is inferior and has only one [[Ovule|ovule]], with basal [[Placentation|placentation]].
sentence_106: In members of the Asteraceae the fruit is achene-like, and is called a cypsela (plural cypselae).
sentence_107: Although there are two fused [[Carpel|carpels]], there is only one locule, and only one [[Seed|seed]] per fruit is formed.
sentence_108: It may sometimes be winged or spiny because the [[Pappus_(flower_structure)|pappus]], which is derived from [[Calyx_(botany)|calyx]] tissue often remains on the fruit (for example in [[Dandelion|dandelion]]).
sentence_109: In some species, however, the pappus falls off (for example in [[Helianthus|Helianthus]]).
sentence_110: Cypsela [[Morphology_(biology)|morphology]] is often used to help determine plant relationships at the genus and species level.
sentence_111: The mature [[Seed|seeds]] usually have little [[Endosperm|endosperm]] or none.
sentence_112: The pollen of composites is typically echinolophate, a [[Morphology_(biology)|morphological]] term meaning "with elaborate systems of ridges and spines dispersed around and between the apertures."
sentence_113: In Asteraceae, the energy store is generally in the form of [[Inulin|inulin]] rather than starch.
sentence_114: They produce iso/[[Chlorogenic_acid|chlorogenic acid]], [[Sesquiterpene|sesquiterpene]] [[Lactones|lactones]], pentacyclic triterpene alcohols, various [[Alkaloid|alkaloids]], [[Acetylene|acetylenes]] (cyclic, aromatic, with vinyl end groups), [[Tannin|tannins]].
sentence_115: They have [[Terpene|terpenoid]] [[Essential_oil|essential oils]] which never contain [[Iridoid|iridoids]].
sentence_116: Asteraceae produce secondary metabolites, such as [[Flavonoid|flavonoids]] and [[Terpenoid|terpenoids]].
sentence_117: Some of these molecules can inhibit protozoan [[Parasites|parasites]] such as [[Plasmodium|Plasmodium]], [[Trypanosoma|Trypanosoma]], [[Leishmania|Leishmania]] and parasitic intestinal worms, and thus have potential in medicine.
sentence_118: The oldest known fossils of members of Asteraceae are pollen grains from the [[Late_Cretaceous|Late Cretaceous]] of [[Antarctica|Antarctica]], dated to ∼76–66 [[Mya_(unit)|Mya]] ([[Campanian|Campanian]] to [[Maastrichtian|Maastrichtian]]) and assigned to the extant genus [[Dasyphyllum|Dasyphyllum]].
sentence_119: Barreda, et al.
sentence_120: (2015) estimated that the [[Crown_group|crown group]] of Asteraceae evolved at least 85.9 Mya (Late Cretaceous, [[Santonian|Santonian]]) with a stem node age of 88–89 Mya (Late Cretaceous, [[Coniacian|Coniacian]]).
sentence_121: It is still unknown whether the precise cause of their great success was the development of the highly specialised capitulum, their ability to store energy as [[Fructan|fructans]] (mainly [[Inulin|inulin]]), which is an advantage in relatively dry zones, or some combination of these and possibly other factors.
sentence_122: Heterocarpy, or the ability to produce different fruit morphs, has evolved and is common in Asteraceae.
sentence_123: It allows seeds to be dispersed over varying distances and each are adapted to different environments, increasing chances of survival.
sentence_124: Asteraceans are especially common in open and dry environments.
sentence_125: Many members of Asteraceae are [[Pollination|pollinated]] by insects, which explains their value in attracting [[Beneficial_insects|beneficial insects]], but [[Pollination_syndrome|anemophily]] is also present (e.g. [[Ragweed|Ambrosia]], [[Artemisia_(genus)|Artemisia]]).
sentence_126: There are many [[Apomixis|apomictic]] species in the family.
sentence_127: Seeds are ordinarily dispersed intact with the fruiting body, the cypsela.
sentence_128: [[Seed_dispersal#Wind|Anemochory]] (wind dispersal) is common, assisted by a hairy pappus.
sentence_129: [[Seed_dispersal#By_animals|Epizoochory]] is another common method, in which the dispersal unit, a single cypsela (e.g. [[Bidens|Bidens]]) or entire capitulum (e.g. [[Arctium|Arctium]]) has hooks, spines or some structure to attach to the fur or plumage (or even clothes, as in the photo) of an animal just to fall off later far from its mother plant.
sentence_130: Commercially important plants in Asteraceae include the food crops [[Lactuca_sativa|Lactuca sativa]] (lettuce), [[Cichorium|Cichorium]] (chicory), [[Cynara_scolymus|Cynara scolymus]] (globe artichoke), [[Helianthus_annuus|Helianthus annuus]] ([[Sunflower|sunflower]]), [[Smallanthus_sonchifolius|Smallanthus sonchifolius]] (yacón), [[Carthamus_tinctorius|Carthamus tinctorius]] (safflower) and [[Helianthus_tuberosus|Helianthus tuberosus]] (Jerusalem artichoke).
sentence_131: Plants are used as herbs and in herbal teas and other beverages.
sentence_132: Chamomile, for example, comes from two different species: the annual [[Matricaria_chamomilla|Matricaria chamomilla]] (German chamomile) and the perennial [[Chamaemelum_nobile|Chamaemelum nobile]] (Roman chamomile).
sentence_133: [[Calendula|Calendula]] (known as pot marigold) is grown commercially for herbal teas and [[Potpourri|potpourri]].
sentence_134: [[Echinacea_purpurea|Echinacea]] is used as a medicinal tea.
sentence_135: The wormwood genus [[Artemisia_(genus)|Artemisia]] includes [[Absinthe|absinthe]] (A. absinthium) and [[Tarragon|tarragon]] (A. dracunculus).
sentence_136: Winter tarragon ([[Tagetes_lucida|Tagetes lucida]]), is commonly grown and used as a tarragon substitute in climates where tarragon will not survive.
sentence_137: Many members of the family are grown as ornamental plants for their flowers, and some are important ornamental crops for the cut flower industry.
sentence_138: Some examples are [[Chrysanthemum|Chrysanthemum]], [[Gerbera|Gerbera]], [[Calendula|Calendula]], [[Dendranthema|Dendranthema]], [[Argyranthemum|Argyranthemum]], [[Dahlia|Dahlia]], [[Tagetes|Tagetes]], [[Zinnia|Zinnia]], and many others.
sentence_139: Many species of this family possess medicinal properties and are used as traditional [[Parasite|antiparasitic]] medicine.
sentence_140: Members of the family are also commonly featured in medical and phytochemical journals because the [[Sesquiterpene|sesquiterpene]] [[Lactone|lactone]] compounds contained within them are an important cause of [[Allergic_contact_dermatitis|allergic contact dermatitis]].
sentence_141: Allergy to these compounds is the leading cause of allergic contact dermatitis in florists in the US.
sentence_142: Pollen from ragweed [[Ragweed|Ambrosia]] is among the main causes of so-called [[Hay_fever|hay fever]] in the United States.
sentence_143: Asteraceae are also used for some industrial purposes.
sentence_144: French Marigold ([[Tagetes_patula|Tagetes patula]]) is common in commercial poultry feeds and its oil is extracted for uses in cola and the cigarette industry.
sentence_145: Several members of the family are copious [[Nectar_(plant)|nectar]] producers and are useful for evaluating pollinator populations during their bloom.
sentence_146: [[Centaurea|Centaurea]] (knapweed), [[Helianthus_annuus|Helianthus annuus]] (domestic [[Sunflower|sunflower]]), and some species of [[Solidago|Solidago]] (goldenrod) are major "honey plants" for beekeepers.
sentence_147: Solidago produces relatively high protein pollen, which helps [[Honey_bee|honey bees]] over winter.
sentence_148: Some members of Asteraceae are economically important as weeds.
sentence_149: Notable in the United States are [[Senecio_jacobaea|Senecio jacobaea]] (ragwort), [[Senecio_vulgaris|Senecio vulgaris]] (groundsel), and [[Taraxacum|Taraxacum]] (dandelion).
sentence_150: The genera [[Chrysanthemum|Chrysanthemum]], [[Pulicaria|Pulicaria]], [[Tagetes|Tagetes]], and [[Tanacetum|Tanacetum]] contain species with useful insecticidal properties.
sentence_151: [[Parthenium_argentatum|Parthenium argentatum]] (guayule) is a source of [[Hypoallergenic|hypoallergenic]] [[Latex|latex]].

title: Canton of Aargau
sentence_0: The canton of Aargau (German: Kanton Aargau [[Standard_German|[ˈaːrɡaʊ]] (listen); sometimes Latinized as Argovia; see also [[List_of_European_regions_with_alternative_names#A|other names]]) is one of the more northerly [[Cantons_of_Switzerland|cantons of Switzerland]].
sentence_1: It is situated by the lower course of the [[Aare|Aare]] River, which is why the canton is called Aar-[[Gau_(country_subdivision)|gau]] (meaning "Aare province").
sentence_2: It is one of the most densely populated regions of Switzerland.
sentence_3: Further information: [[Early_history_of_Switzerland|Early history of Switzerland]]
sentence_4: The area of Aargau and the surrounding areas were controlled by the [[Helvetians|Helvetians]], a member of the [[Celts|Celts]], as far back as 200 BC.
sentence_5: It was eventually occupied by the [[Roman_Empire|Romans]] and then by the 6th century, the [[Franks|Franks]].
sentence_6: The Romans built a major settlement called [[Vindonissa|Vindonissa]], near the present location of [[Brugg|Brugg]].
sentence_7: See also: [[List_of_castles_and_fortresses_in_Switzerland#Aargau|List of castles and fortresses in Switzerland § Aargau]], and [[Medieval_Switzerland|Medieval Switzerland]]
sentence_8: The reconstructed Old High German name of Aargau is Argowe, first unambiguously attested (in the spelling Argue) in 795.
sentence_9: The term described a territory only loosely equivalent to that of the modern canton, including the region between Aare and [[Reuss_(river)|Reuss]] rivers, including [[Pilatus_(mountain)|Pilatus]] and [[Napf|Napf]], i.e. including parts of the modern cantons of Bern (Bernese Aargau, [[Emmental|Emmental]], parts of the [[Bernese_Oberland|Bernese Oberland]]), [[Canton_of_Solothurn|Solothurn]], [[Basel-Landschaft|Basel-Landschaft]], [[Canton_of_Lucerne|Lucerne]], [[Obwalden|Obwalden]] and [[Nidwalden|Nidwalden]], but not the parts of the modern canton east of the Reuss ([[Baden_District,_Aargau|Baden District]]), which were part of [[Zürichgau|Zürichgau]].
sentence_10: Within the [[Frankish_Empire|Frankish Empire]] (8th to 10th centuries), the area was a disputed border region between the duchies of [[Alamannia|Alamannia]] and [[Burgundy_(region)|Burgundy]].
sentence_11: A line of the von [[Wetterau|Wetterau]] ([[Conradines|Conradines]]) intermittently held the countship of Aargau from 750 until about 1030, when they lost it (having in the meantime taken the name von [[Tegerfelden|Tegerfelden]]).
sentence_12: This division became the ill-defined (and sparsely settled) outer border of the early [[Holy_Roman_Empire|Holy Roman Empire]] at its formation in the second half of the 10th century.
sentence_13: Most of the region came under the control of the ducal [[House_of_Zähringen|house of Zähringen]] and the comital houses of [[House_of_Habsburg|Habsburg]] and [[House_of_Kyburg|Kyburg]] by about 1200.
sentence_14: In the second half of the 13th century, the territory became divided between the territories claimed by the [[Reichsfrei|imperial cities]] of [[Bern|Bern]], [[Lucerne|Lucerne]] and [[Solothurn|Solothurn]] and the Swiss canton of [[Unterwalden|Unterwalden]].
sentence_15: The remaining portion, largely corresponding to the modern canton of Aargau, remained under the control of the Habsburgs until the "conquest of Aargau" by the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1415.
sentence_16: [[Habsburg_Castle|Habsburg Castle]] itself, the original seat of the House of Habsburg, was taken by Bern in April 1415.
sentence_17: The Habsburgs had founded a number of monasteries (with some structures enduring, e.g., in [[Wettingen_Abbey|Wettingen]] and [[Muri_Abbey|Muri]]), the closing of which by the government in 1841 was a contributing factor to the outbreak of the Swiss civil war – the "Sonderbund War" – in 1847.
sentence_18: When [[Frederick_IV,_Duke_of_Austria|Frederick IV of Habsburg]] sided with [[Antipope_John_XXIII|Antipope John XXIII]] at the Council of Constance, [[Holy_Roman_Emperor|Emperor]] [[Sigismund,_Holy_Roman_Emperor|Sigismund]] placed him under the [[Imperial_ban|Imperial ban]].
sentence_19: In July 1414, the Pope visited [[Bern|Bern]] and received assurances from them, that they would move against the Habsburgs.
sentence_20: A few months later the [[Swiss_Confederation|Swiss Confederation]] denounced the Treaty of 1412.
sentence_21: Shortly thereafter in 1415, [[Bern|Bern]] and the rest of the Swiss Confederation used the ban as a pretext to invade the Aargau.
sentence_22: The Confederation was able to quickly conquer the towns of Aarau, Lenzburg, Brugg and Zofingen along with most of the Habsburg castles.
sentence_23: [[Bern|Bern]] kept the southwest portion ([[Zofingen|Zofingen]], [[Aarburg|Aarburg]], [[Aarau|Aarau]], [[Lenzburg|Lenzburg]], and [[Brugg|Brugg]]), northward to the confluence of the [[Aare_(river)|Aare]] and [[Reuss_(river)|Reuss]].
sentence_24: The important city of [[Baden,_Switzerland|Baden]] was taken by a united Swiss army and governed by all 8 members of the Confederation.
sentence_25: Some districts, named the [[Freie_Ämter|Freie Ämter]] (free bailiwicks) – [[Mellingen|Mellingen]], [[Muri_District|Muri]], [[Villmergen|Villmergen]], and [[Bremgarten_(district)|Bremgarten]], with the [[County_of_Baden|countship of Baden]] – were governed as "subject lands" by all or some of the Confederates.
sentence_26: Shortly after the conquest of the Aargau by the Swiss, [[Frederick_IV,_Duke_of_Austria|Frederick]] humbled himself to the Pope.
sentence_27: The Pope reconciled with him and ordered all of the taken lands to be returned.
sentence_28: The Swiss refused and years later after no serious attempts at re-acquisition, the Duke officially relinquished rights to the Swiss.
sentence_29: Bern's portion of the Aargau came to be known as the Unteraargau, though can also be called the Berner or Bernese Aargau.
sentence_30: In 1514 Bern expanded north into the [[Canton_of_Jura|Jura]] and so came into possession of several strategically important mountain passes into the Austrian Fricktal.
sentence_31: This land was added to the Unteraargau and was directly ruled from Bern.
sentence_32: It was divided into seven rural bailiwicks and four administrative cities, Aarau, Zofingen, Lenzburg and Brugg.
sentence_33: While the Habsburgs were driven out, many of their minor nobles were allowed to keep their lands and offices, though over time they lost power to the Bernese government.
sentence_34: The bailiwick administration was based on a very small staff of officials, mostly made up of Bernese citizens, but with a few locals.
sentence_35: When Bern converted during the [[Protestant_Reformation|Protestant Reformation]] in 1528, the Unteraargau also converted.
sentence_36: At the beginning of the 16th century a number of [[Anabaptist|anabaptists]] migrated into the upper Wynen and Rueder valleys from [[Zürich|Zürich]].
sentence_37: Despite pressure from the Bernese authorities in the 16th and 17th centuries anabaptism never entirely disappeared from the Unteraargau.
sentence_38: Bern used the Aargau bailiwicks mostly as a source of grain for the rest of the city-state.
sentence_39: The administrative cities remained economically only of regional importance.
sentence_40: However, in the 17th and 18th centuries Bern encouraged industrial development in Unteraargau and by the late 18th century it was the most industrialized region in the city-state.
sentence_41: The high industrialization led to high population growth in the 18th century, for example between 1764 and 1798, the population grew by 35%, far more than in other parts of the canton.
sentence_42: In 1870 the proportion of farmers in Aarau, Lenzburg, Kulm, and Zofingen districts was 34–40%, while in the other districts it was 46–57%.
sentence_43: The rest of the [[Freie_Ämter|Freie Ämter]] were collectively administered as subject territories by the rest of the Confederation.
sentence_44: Muri Amt was assigned to Zürich, Lucerne, [[Canton_of_Schwyz|Schwyz]], [[Unterwalden|Unterwalden]], [[Canton_of_Zug|Zug]] and [[Canton_of_Glarus|Glarus]], while the Ämter of Meienberg, Richensee and [[Villmergen|Villmergen]] were first given to Lucerne alone.
sentence_45: The final boundary was set in 1425 by an arbitration tribunal and Lucerne had to give the three Ämter to be collectively ruled.
sentence_46: The four Ämter were then consolidated under a single Confederation [[Bailiff|bailiff]] into what was known in the 15th century as the Waggental Bailiwick (German: Vogtei im Waggental).
sentence_47: In the 16th century, it came to be known as the Vogtei der Freien Ämter.
sentence_48: While the Freien Ämter often had independent lower courts, they were forced to accept the Confederation's sovereignty.
sentence_49: Finally, in 1532, the canton of Uri became part of the collective administration of the Freien Ämter.
sentence_50: At the time of the Protestant Reformation, the majority of the Ämter converted to the new faith.
sentence_51: In 1529, a wave of [[Iconoclasm|iconoclasm]] swept through the area and wiped away much of the old religion.
sentence_52: After the defeat of Zürich in the second [[Battle_of_Kappel|Battle of Kappel]] in 1531, the victorious five Catholic cantons marched their troops into the Freie Ämter and reconverted them to Catholicism.
sentence_53: In the First War of Villmergen, in 1656, and the [[Toggenburg_War|Toggenburg War]] (or Second War of Villmergen), in 1712, the Freie Ämter became the staging ground for the warring Reformed and Catholic armies.
sentence_54: While the peace after the 1656 war did not change the status quo, the fourth Peace of Aarau in 1712 brought about a reorganization of power relations.
sentence_55: The victory gave Zürich the opportunity to force the Catholic cantons out of the government in the [[County_of_Baden|county of Baden]] and the adjacent area of the Freie Ämter.
sentence_56: The Freie Ämter were then divided in two by a line drawn from the gallows in [[Fahrwangen|Fahrwangen]] to the [[Oberlunkhofen|Oberlunkhofen]] church steeple.
sentence_57: The northern part, the so-called Unteren Freie Ämter (lower Freie Ämter), which included the districts of Boswil (in part) and Hermetschwil and the Niederamt, were ruled by Zürich, Bern and Glarus.
sentence_58: The southern part, the Oberen Freie Ämter (upper Freie Ämter), were ruled by the previous seven cantons but Bern was added to make an eighth.
sentence_59: During the [[Helvetic_Republic|Helvetic Republic]] (1798–1803), the county of Baden, the Freie Ämter and the area known as the Kelleramt were combined into the [[Canton_of_Baden|canton of Baden]].
sentence_60: The [[County_of_Baden|County of Baden]] was a shared [[Condominium_(international_law)|condominium]] of the entire Old Swiss Confederacy.
sentence_61: After the Confederacy conquest in 1415, they retained much of the Habsburg legal structure, which caused a number of problems.
sentence_62: The local nobility had the right to hold the low court in only about one fifth of the territory.
sentence_63: There were over 30 different nobles who had the right to hold courts scattered around the surrounding lands.
sentence_64: All these overlapping jurisdictions caused numerous conflicts, but gradually the Confederation was able to acquire these rights in the County.
sentence_65: The cities of Baden, [[Bremgarten,_Aargau|Bremgarten]] and [[Mellingen|Mellingen]] became the administrative centers and held the high courts.
sentence_66: Together with the courts, the three administrative centers had considerable local autonomy, but were ruled by a governor who was appointed by the Acht Orte every two years.
sentence_67: After the [[Swiss_Reformed_Church|Protestant]] victory at the [[Toggenburg_War|Second Battle of Villmergen]], the administration of the County changed slightly.
sentence_68: Instead of the Acht Orte appointing a bailiff together, Zürich and Bern each appointed the governor for 7 out of 16 years while [[Canton_of_Glarus|Glarus]] appointed him for the remaining two years.
sentence_69: The chaotic legal structure and fragmented land ownership combined with a tradition of dividing the land among all the heirs in an inheritance prevented any large scale reforms.
sentence_70: The governor tried in the 18th century to reform and standardize laws and ownership across the County, but with limited success.
sentence_71: With an ever-changing administration, the County lacked a coherent long-term economic policy or support for reforms.
sentence_72: By the end of the 18th century there were no factories or mills and only a few small [[Cottage_industry#Cottage_industry|cottage industries]] along the border with Zürich.
sentence_73: Road construction first became a priority after 1750, when Zürich and Bern began appointing a governor for seven years.
sentence_74: During the Protestant Reformation, some of the municipalities converted to the new faith.
sentence_75: However, starting in 1531, some of the old parishes were converted back to the old faith.
sentence_76: The governors were appointed from both Catholic and Protestant cantons and since they changed every two years, neither faith gained a majority in the County.
sentence_77: After the French invasion, on 19 March 1798, the governments of Zürich and Bern agreed to the creation of the short lived [[Canton_of_Baden|canton of Baden]] in the [[Helvetic_Republic|Helvetic Republic]].
sentence_78: With the [[Act_of_Mediation|Act of Mediation]] in 1803, the canton of Baden was dissolved.
sentence_79: Portions of the lands of the former County of Baden now became the District of Baden in the newly created canton of Aargau.
sentence_80: After World War II, this formerly agrarian region saw striking growth and became the district with the largest and densest population in the canton (110,000 in 1990, 715 persons per km).
sentence_81: The contemporary canton of Aargau was formed in 1803, a canton of the [[Swiss_Confederation_(Napoleonic)|Swiss Confederation]] as a result of the [[Act_of_Mediation|Act of Mediation]].
sentence_82: It was a combination of three short-lived cantons of the [[Helvetic_Republic|Helvetic Republic]]: Aargau (1798–1803), Baden (1798–1803) and Fricktal (1802–1803).
sentence_83: Its creation is therefore rooted in the [[Switzerland_in_the_Napoleonic_era|Napoleonic era]].
sentence_84: In the year 2003, the canton of Aargau celebrated its 200th anniversary.
sentence_85: French forces occupied the Aargau from 10 March to 18 April 1798; thereafter the Bernese portion became the canton of Aargau and the remainder formed the [[Canton_of_Baden|canton of Baden]].
sentence_86: Aborted plans to merge the two halves came in 1801 and 1802, and they were eventually united under the name Aargau, which was then admitted as a full member of the reconstituted Confederation following the Act of Mediation.
sentence_87: Some parts of the canton of Baden at this point were transferred to other cantons: the Amt of [[Hitzkirch|Hitzkirch]] to Lucerne, whilst [[Hüttikon|Hüttikon]], [[Oetwil_an_der_Limmat|Oetwil an der Limmat]], [[Dietikon|Dietikon]] and [[Schlieren,_Zürich|Schlieren]] went to Zürich.
sentence_88: In return, Lucerne's Amt of [[Merenschwand|Merenschwand]] was transferred to Aargau (district of Muri).
sentence_89: The Fricktal, ceded in 1802 by [[Austria|Austria]] via Napoleonic France to the Helvetic Republic, was briefly a separate canton of the Helvetic Republic (the [[Canton_of_Fricktal|canton of Fricktal]]) under a [[Statthalter|Statthalter]] ('Lieutenant'), but on 19 March 1803 (following the Act of Mediation) was incorporated into the canton of Aargau.
sentence_90: The former cantons of Baden and Fricktal can still be identified with the contemporary [[Districts_of_Switzerland#Aargau|districts]] – the [[Canton_of_Baden|canton of Baden]] is covered by the districts of Zurzach, Baden, Bremgarten, and Muri (albeit with the gains and losses of 1803 detailed above); the [[Canton_of_Fricktal|canton of Fricktal]] by the districts of Rheinfelden and Laufenburg (except for [[Hottwil|Hottwil]] which was transferred to that district in 2010).

sentence_92: In the 17th century, Aargau was the only federal condominium where Jews were tolerated.
sentence_93: In 1774, they were restricted to just two towns, [[Endingen,_Switzerland|Endingen]] and [[Lengnau,_Aargau|Lengnau]].
sentence_94: While the rural upper class pressed incessantly for the expulsion the Jews, the financial interests of the authorities prevented it.
sentence_95: They imposed special taxes on peddling and cattle trading, the primary Jewish professions.
sentence_96: The Protestant occupiers also enjoyed the discomfort of the local Catholics by the presence of the Jewish community.
sentence_97: The Jews were directly subordinate to the governor; from 1696, they were compelled to renew a letter of protection from him every 16 years.
sentence_98: During this period, Jews and Christians were not allowed to live under the same roof, neither were Jews allowed to own land or houses.
sentence_99: They were taxed at a much higher rate than others and, in 1712, the Lengnau community was "pillaged."
sentence_100: In 1760, they were further restricted regarding marriages and procreation.
sentence_101: An exorbitant tax was levied on marriage licenses; oftentimes, they were outright refused.
sentence_102: This remained the case until the 19th century.
sentence_103: In 1799, all special tolls were abolished, and, in 1802, the poll tax was removed.
sentence_104: On 5 May 1809, they were declared citizens and given broad rights regarding trade and farming.
sentence_105: They were still restricted to Endingen and Lengnau until 7 May 1846, when their right to move and reside freely within the canton of Aargau was granted.
sentence_106: On 24 September 1856, the [[Swiss_Federal_Council|Swiss Federal Council]] granted them full political rights within Aargau, as well as broad business rights; however the majority Christian population did not abide by these new liberal laws fully.
sentence_107: The time of 1860 saw the canton government voting to grant suffrage in all local rights and to give their communities autonomy.
sentence_108: Before the law was enacted, it was repealed due to vocal opposition led by the [[Ultramontanism|Ultramonte Party]].
sentence_109: Finally, the federal authorities in July 1863, granted all Jews full rights of citizens.
sentence_110: However, they did not receive all of the rights in Endingen and Lengnau until a resolution of the [[Grand_Council_of_Aargau|Grand Council]], on 15 May 1877, granted citizens' rights to the members of the Jewish communities of those places, giving them charters under the names of New Endingen and New Lengnau.
sentence_111: The Swiss Jewish Kulturverein was instrumental in this fight from its founding in 1862 until it was dissolved 20 years later.
sentence_112: During this period of diminished rights, they were not even allowed to bury their dead in Swiss soil and had to bury their dead on an island called [[Judenäule|Judenäule]] (Jews' Isle) on the [[Rhine|Rhine]] near [[Waldshut-Tiengen|Waldshut]].
sentence_113: Beginning in 1603, the deceased Jews of the [[Surbtal|Surbtal]] communities were buried on the river island which was leased by the Jewish community.
sentence_114: As the island was repeatedly flooded and devastated, in 1750 the [[Surbtal_Jews|Surbtal Jews]] asked the [[Tagsatzung|Tagsatzung]] to establish the [[Jüdischer_Friedhof_Endingen|Endingen cemetery]] in the vicinity of their communities.
sentence_115: The capital of the canton is [[Aarau|Aarau]], which is located on its western border, on the [[Aare_(river)|Aare]].
sentence_116: The canton borders [[Germany|Germany]] ([[Baden-Württemberg|Baden-Württemberg]]) to the north, the Rhine forming the border.
sentence_117: To the west lie the Swiss cantons of [[Basel-Landschaft|Basel-Landschaft]], [[Canton_of_Solothurn|Solothurn]] and [[Canton_of_Bern|Bern]]; the [[Canton_of_Lucerne|canton of Lucerne]] lies south, and [[Canton_of_Zürich|Zürich]] and [[Canton_of_Zug|Zug]] to the east.
sentence_118: Its total area is 1,404 square kilometers (542 sq mi).
sentence_119: It contains both large rivers, the [[Aare_(river)|Aare]] and the [[Reuss_(river)|Reuss]].
sentence_120: The canton of Aargau is one of the least mountainous Swiss cantons, forming part of a great table-land, to the north of the [[Swiss_Alps|Alps]] and the east of the Jura, above which rise low hills.
sentence_121: The surface of the country is diversified with undulating tracts and well-wooded hills, alternating with fertile valleys watered mainly by the Aare and its tributaries.
sentence_122: The valleys alternate with hills, many of which are wooded.
sentence_123: Slightly over one-third of the canton is wooded (518 square kilometers (200 sq mi)), while nearly half is used from farming (635.7 square kilometers (245.4 sq mi)).
sentence_124: 33.5 square kilometers (12.9 sq mi) or about 2.4% of the canton is considered unproductive, mostly lakes (notably [[Lake_Hallwil|Lake Hallwil]]) and streams.
sentence_125: With a population density of 450/km (1,200/sq mi), the canton has a relatively high amount of land used for human development, with 216.7 square kilometers (83.7 sq mi) or about 15% of the canton developed for housing or transportation.
sentence_126: It contains the hot sulphur springs of [[Baden,_Switzerland|Baden]] and [[Schinznach-Bad|Schinznach-Bad]], while at [[Rheinfelden_(Aargau)|Rheinfelden]] there are very extensive saline springs.
sentence_127: Just below [[Brugg|Brugg]] the [[Reuss_(river)|Reuss]] and the [[Limmat|Limmat]] join the Aar, while around Brugg are the ruined castle of [[Habsburg|Habsburg]], the old convent of [[Königsfelden_Abbey|Königsfelden]] (with fine painted medieval glass) and the remains of the [[Ancient_Rome|Roman]] settlement of Vindonissa ([[Windisch|Windisch]]).
sentence_128: [[Fahr_Monastery|Fahr Monastery]] forms a small [[Enclave_and_exclave|exclave]] of the canton, otherwise surrounded by the [[Canton_of_Zürich|canton of Zürich]], and since 2008 is part of the Aargau municipality of [[Würenlos|Würenlos]].
sentence_129: See also: [[Districts_of_Switzerland|Districts of Switzerland]]
sentence_130: Aargau is divided into 11 districts:
sentence_131: The most recent change in district boundaries occurred in 2010 when [[Hottwil|Hottwil]] transferred from Brugg to Laufenburg, following its merger with other municipalities, all of which were in Laufenburg.
sentence_132: Main articles: [[Municipalities_of_the_canton_of_Aargau|Municipalities of the canton of Aargau]] and [[Municipalities_of_Switzerland|Municipalities of Switzerland]]
sentence_133: There are (as of 2014) 213 municipalities in the canton of Aargau.
sentence_134: As with most Swiss cantons there has been a trend since the early 2000s for municipalities to merge, though mergers in Aargau have so far been less radical than in other cantons.
sentence_135: The blazon of the coat of arms is Per pale, dexter: sable, a fess wavy argent, charged with two cotises wavy azure; sinister: sky blue, three mullets of five argent.
sentence_136: The flag and arms of the canton of Aargau date to 1803 and are an original design by Samuel Ringier-Seelmatter; the current official design, specifying the stars as five-pointed, dates to 1930.
sentence_137: Aargau has a population (as of December 2019) of 685,845.
sentence_138: As of 2010, 21.5% of the population are resident foreign nationals.
sentence_139: Over the last 10 years (2000–2010) the population has changed at a rate of 11%.
sentence_140: Migration accounted for 8.7%, while births and deaths accounted for 2.8%.
sentence_141: Most of the population (as of 2000) speaks German (477,093 or 87.1%) as their first language, Italian is the second most common (17,847 or 3.3%) and [[Serbo-Croatian|Serbo-Croatian]] is the third (10,645 or 1.9%).
sentence_142: There are 4,151 people who speak French and 618 people who speak [[Romansh_language|Romansh]].
sentence_143: Of the population in the canton, 146,421 or about 26.7% were born in Aargau and lived there in 2000.
sentence_144: There were 140,768 or 25.7% who were born in the same canton, while 136,865 or 25.0% were born somewhere else in Switzerland, and 107,396 or 19.6% were born outside of Switzerland.
sentence_145: As of 2000, children and teenagers (0–19 years old) make up 24.3% of the population, while adults (20–64 years old) make up 62.3% and seniors (over 64 years old) make up 13.4%.
sentence_146: As of 2000, there were 227,656 people who were single and never married in the canton.
sentence_147: There were 264,939 married individuals, 27,603 widows or widowers and 27,295 individuals who are divorced.
sentence_148: As of 2000, there were 224,128 private households in the canton, and an average of 2.4 persons per household.
sentence_149: There were 69,062 households that consist of only one person and 16,254 households with five or more people.
sentence_150: As of 2009, the construction rate of new housing units was 6.5 new units per 1000 residents.
sentence_151: The vacancy rate for the canton, in 2010, was 1.54%.
sentence_152: The majority of the population is centered on one of three areas: the Aare Valley, the side branches of the Aare Valley, or along the [[Rhine_(river)|Rhine]].

sentence_154: In the 2011 [[2011_Swiss_federal_election|federal election]], the most popular party was the [[Swiss_People's_Party|SVP]] which received 34.7% of the vote.
sentence_155: The next three most popular parties were the [[Social_Democratic_Party_of_Switzerland|SP/PS]] (18.0%), the [[FDP.The_Liberals|FDP]] (11.5%) and the [[Christian_Democratic_People's_Party_of_Switzerland|CVP]] (10.6%).
sentence_156: The SVP received about the same percentage of the vote as they did in the [[2007_Swiss_federal_election|2007 Federal election]] (36.2% in 2007 vs 34.7% in 2011).
sentence_157: The SPS retained about the same popularity (17.9% in 2007), the FDP retained about the same popularity (13.6% in 2007) and the CVP retained about the same popularity (13.5% in 2007).

sentence_158: The Grand Council of the [[Cantons_of_Switzerland|canton]] of [[Aargau|Aargau]] is called [[Grand_Council_of_Aargau|Grosser Rat]].
sentence_159: It's the [[Legislature|legislature]] of the canton, has 140 seats, with members elected every four years.
sentence_160: From the 2000 census, 219,800 or 40.1% were [[Roman_Catholic|Roman Catholic]], while 189,606 or 34.6% belonged to the [[Swiss_Reformed_Church|Swiss Reformed Church]].
sentence_161: Of the rest of the population, there were 11,523 members of an [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|Orthodox]] church (or about 2.10% of the population), there were 3,418 individuals (or about 0.62% of the population) who belonged to the [[Christian_Catholic_Church_of_Switzerland|Christian Catholic Church]], and there were 29,580 individuals (or about 5.40% of the population) who belonged to another Christian church.
sentence_162: There were 342 individuals (or about 0.06% of the population) who were [[Jewish|Jewish]], and 30,072 (or about 5.49% of the population) who were [[Islam|Muslim]].
sentence_163: There were 1,463 individuals who were [[Buddhism|Buddhist]], 2,089 individuals who were [[Hinduism|Hindu]] and 495 individuals who belonged to another church.
sentence_164: 57,573 (or about 10.52% of the population) belonged to no church, are agnostic or [[Atheism|atheist]], and 15,875 individuals (or about 2.90% of the population) did not answer the question.
sentence_165: In Aargau about 212,069 or (38.7%) of the population have completed non-mandatory [[Education_in_Switzerland#Secondary|upper secondary education]], and 70,896 or (12.9%) have completed additional higher education (either [[List_of_universities_in_Switzerland|university]] or a [[Fachhochschule|Fachhochschule]]).
sentence_166: Of the 70,896 who completed tertiary schooling, 63.6% were Swiss men, 20.9% were Swiss women, 10.4% were non-Swiss men and 5.2% were non-Swiss women.
sentence_167: As of 2010, Aargau had an unemployment rate of 3.6%.
sentence_168: As of 2008, there were 11,436 people employed in the [[Primary_sector_of_the_economy|primary economic sector]] and about 3,927 businesses involved in this sector.
sentence_169: 95,844 people were employed in the secondary sector and there were 6,055 businesses in this sector.
sentence_170: 177,782 people were employed in the [[Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy|tertiary sector]], with 21,530 businesses in this sector.
sentence_171: In 2008 the total number of full-time equivalent jobs was 238,225.
sentence_172: The number of jobs in the primary sector was 7,167, of which 6,731 were in agriculture, 418 were in forestry or lumber production and 18 were in fishing or fisheries.
sentence_173: The number of jobs in the secondary sector was 90,274 of which 64,089 or (71.0%) were in manufacturing, 366 or (0.4%) were in mining and 21,705 (24.0%) were in construction.
sentence_174: The number of jobs in the tertiary sector was 140,784.
sentence_175: In the tertiary sector; 38,793 or 27.6% were in the sale or repair of motor vehicles, 13,624 or 9.7% were in the movement and storage of goods, 8,150 or 5.8% were in a hotel or restaurant, 5,164 or 3.7% were in the information industry, 5,946 or 4.2% were the insurance or financial industry, 14,831 or 10.5% were technical professionals or scientists, 10,951 or 7.8% were in education and 21,952 or 15.6% were in health care.
sentence_176: Of the working population, 19.5% used public transportation to get to work, and 55.3% used a private car.
sentence_177: Public transportation – bus and train – is provided by [[Busbetrieb_Aarau_AG|Busbetrieb Aarau AG]].
sentence_178: The farmland of the canton of Aargau is some of the most fertile in Switzerland.
sentence_179: Dairy farming, cereal and fruit farming are among the canton's main economic activities.
sentence_180: The canton is also industrially developed, particularly in the fields of [[Electrical_engineering|electrical engineering]], precision instruments, iron, steel, cement and [[Textiles|textiles]].
sentence_181: Three of Switzerland's five nuclear power plants are in the canton of Aargau (Beznau I + II and Leibstadt).
sentence_182: Additionally, the many rivers supply enough water for numerous hydroelectric power plants throughout the canton.
sentence_183: The canton of Aargau is often called "the energy canton".
sentence_184: A significant number of people commute into the financial center of the city of [[Zürich|Zürich]], which is just across the cantonal border.
sentence_185: As such the per capita cantonal income (in 2005) is 49,209 [[Swiss_Franc|CHF]].
sentence_186: Tourism is significant, particularly for the hot springs at [[Baden,_Switzerland|Baden]] and [[Schinznach-Bad|Schinznach-Bad]], the ancient castles, the landscape, and the many old museums in the canton.
sentence_187: Hillwalking is another tourist attraction but is of only limited significance.

title: AZ Alkmaar
sentence_0: This article is about the men's association football team.
sentence_1: For the now-dissolved women's team, see [[AZ_Alkmaar_(women)|AZ Alkmaar (women)]].
sentence_2: Alkmaar Zaanstreek ([[Dutch|[ˈɑlkmaːr ˈzaːnstreːk]]), better known as AZ Alkmaar or simply AZ (Dutch pronunciation: [[Dutch|[aːˈzɛt]]), is a Dutch professional [[Association_football|football]] club from [[Alkmaar|Alkmaar]] and the [[Zaan#The_Zaan_district|Zaanstreek]].
sentence_3: The club plays in the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], the highest professional football league in the Netherlands, and hosts home matches at the [[AFAS_Stadion|AFAS Stadion]].
sentence_4: AZ has won the Eredivisie twice, in [[1980–81_Eredivisie|1980–81]] and [[2008–09_Eredivisie|2008–09]].
sentence_5: In the same season as their first league title, they also reached the [[1981_UEFA_Cup_Final|UEFA Cup Final]], which they lost to [[Ipswich_Town_F.C.|Ipswich Town]].
sentence_6: In addition, the team has won the [[KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]] on four occasions and one [[Johan_Cruyff_Shield|Johan Cruyff Shield]].
sentence_7: AZ was founded on 10 May 1967 as AZ '67, the result of a merger of Alkmaar '54 and FC Zaanstreek.
sentence_8: Alkmaar '54 was founded as a professional team in April 1954 to play in the 10-team NBVB league, created because the [[KNVB|KNVB]] refused to organize a professional league (the KNVB took over in 1955).
sentence_9: Alkmaar '54, and by extension AZ, played the very first professional match in the Netherlands: on 14 August 1954, they won 3–0 at home against Venlo '54, with [[Klaas_Smit|Klaas Smit]] scoring the first (and third) goal.
sentence_10: After winning the Eerste Divisie in 1960–61, it played one year in the Eredivisie.
sentence_11: FC Zaanstreek had been playing since 1910 as the Kooger Football Club (KFC).
sentence_12: KFC had nearly become national champion in 1934 through a narrow loss to [[AFC_Ajax|Ajax]] in the finals.
sentence_13: The team became professional in 1955.
sentence_14: In 1964 the professional part of KFC was renamed FC Zaanstreek, while the amateurs played on as KFC.
sentence_15: Also in 1964, the brothers Cees and Klaas Molenaar, former players and trainers for KFC and owners of a growing appliance store chain, sought to create a powerful football team in Zaanstreek by merging the two local professional teams: KFC and Zaanlandsche Football Club.
sentence_16: After the ZFC leadership thwarted this attempt, the Molenaars successfully merged FC Zaanstreek with Alkmaar '54 in 1967.
sentence_17: FC Zaanstreek had finished 7th and Alkmaar '54 12th in [[1966–67_Eerste_Divisie|1966–67 Eerste Divisie]].
sentence_18: The team would be based in Alkmaar, though the second team originally trained and played in [[Koog_aan_de_Zaan|Koog aan de Zaan]].
sentence_19: Partially through the hiring of expensive foreign players, the new club soon acquired large debts.
sentence_20: In 1972, the Molenaar brothers bailed it out and invested heavily in the club, to the point that AZ '67 were successful in the late 1970s and early '80s, regularly playing European football from 1977 to 1982 while also winning three [[KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cups]] over that period.
sentence_21: After four close league campaigns, AZ finally became [[Eredivisie|Dutch champions]] in [[1980–81_Eredivisie|1981]], becoming the only team other than the "big three" of Ajax, [[Feyenoord|Feyenoord]] and [[PSV_Eindhoven|PSV]] to do so in a 44-year period spanning from 1965 to 2009 (when AZ once again won the league title).
sentence_22: They won the title with overwhelming power, winning 27 of 34 matches and only losing once while scoring a club record 101 goals and conceding just 30.
sentence_23: That same season, AZ reached the [[1981_UEFA_Cup_Final|final of the UEFA Cup]], losing 5–4 on aggregate to [[Ipswich_Town_F.C.|Ipswich Town]].
sentence_24: The next year, in the [[1981–82_European_Cup|European Cup]], they lost in the second round 3–2 on aggregate to [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool]].
sentence_25: Georg Keßler was AZ's manager over most of these years (1978–82), while star players included: [[Kees_Kist|Kees Kist]], the club's highest ever goalscorer with 212 goals and the first ever Dutchman to win the [[European_Golden_Shoe|European Golden Boot]] in 1979 when he scored 34 goals in a season; [[Jan_Peters_(footballer)|Jan Peters]], who played 120 matches for AZ during this period scoring 30 goals from midfield; and [[Hugo_Hovenkamp|Hugo Hovenkamp]], who played 239 matches in defence for AZ from 1975 to 1983, as well as receiving 31 caps for the [[Netherlands_national_football_team|Netherlands national team]] from 1977 to 1983 and playing each match in [[UEFA_Euro_1980|UEFA Euro 1980]] while an AZ player.
sentence_26: Additional stars included [[John_Metgod|John Metgod]], who spent six years at AZ playing 195 matches as a defender, scoring 26 goals including a goal against Ipswich Town in the final of the UEFA Cup.
sentence_27: Like Hovenkamp, Metgod was also included in the Dutch squad for Euro 1980.
sentence_28: Meanwhile, Danish forward [[Kristen_Nygaard_(footballer)|Kristen Nygaard]] spent ten years at AZ, scoring 104 goals in 363 matches between 1972 and 1982.
sentence_29: Co-owner Cees Molenaar died in 1979.
sentence_30: AZ's fortunes deteriorated after his brother, Klaas Molenaar, left the club in 1985.
sentence_31: After several mid-table finishes in previous seasons, AZ was relegated in 1988 from the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], ending the season on 28 points from 34 matches and falling to the [[Eerste_Divisie|Eerste Divisie]] due to the superior goal difference of [[Roda_JC|Roda JC]].
sentence_32: This relegation was significant since it occurred just seven years after the club's historic domestic double and marked the end of AZ's first period of success in Dutch football.
sentence_33: Following this, AZ spent much of the next decade in the second tier, struggling to find a return to the top flight.
sentence_34: The involvement of businessman Dirk Scheringa in the mid-1990s marked the revival of the club as AZ returned to the Eredivisie, winning the [[1997-98_Eerste_Divisie|1997-98 Eerste Divisie]] title.
sentence_35: The club achieved consecutive finishes around the middle positions in the league until ending up in third place in the [[2004-05_Eredivisie|2004-05 Eredivisie]] season, AZ's highest position for 23 years.
sentence_36: In the summer of 2006, the club moved to a new 17,000 capacity stadium, [[AZ_Stadion|AZ Stadion]].
sentence_37: Despite playing strongly for the majority of the 2006–07 season, AZ's season ended in disappointment.
sentence_38: First, entering the last matchday of the [[2006–07_Eredivisie|2006–07 Eredivisie]] season, AZ led PSV and Ajax on goal difference at the top of the league table, but ended up third after losing their last match against 16th placed team [[S.B.V._Excelsior|Excelsior]], AZ played with ten men for 80 minutes.
sentence_39: Additionally, AZ then lost the [[2006–07_KNVB_Cup#Final|KNVB Cup final]] to Ajax 8–7 after a penalty shoot-out, while also falling to Ajax over two play-off matches for participation in the [[2007–08_UEFA_Champions_League|Champions League]].
sentence_40: After the season, key players like [[Tim_de_Cler|Tim de Cler]], [[Danny_Koevermans|Danny Koevermans]] and [[Shota_Arveladze|Shota Arveladze]] left the team.
sentence_41: A remarkable run ended in the 2007–08 season: after AZ lost a group stage match against [[Everton_F.C.|Everton]] (3–2) in the [[2007–08_UEFA_Cup|UEFA Cup]], the club's unbeaten run of 32 home matches in European competitions – lasting from 1977 to 2007 – ended.
sentence_42: AZ had a poor season, suffering elimination in the first round of the KNVB Cup and the group stage of the UEFA Cup, as well as finishing the [[2007–08_Eredivisie|2007–08 Eredivisie]] in a disappointing 11th place.
sentence_43: Towards the latter stages of the season, in March 2008, AZ manager [[Louis_van_Gaal|Louis van Gaal]] had initially tendered his resignation, but after protests the players and directors, he rescinded his resignation.
sentence_44: The [[2008–09_Eredivisie|2008–09 season]] had an unpromising start after two opening defeats against [[NAC_Breda|NAC Breda]] and [[ADO_Den_Haag|ADO Den Haag]].
sentence_45: However, starting with a 1–0 victory over defending league champions PSV, AZ did not lose a match in its next 28 matches, including a run of 11-straight matches where AZ did not concede an opposition goal.
sentence_46: Three weeks before the end of the season, AZ became Eredivisie champions, edging nearest title rivals [[FC_Twente|Twente]] and Ajax comfortably.
sentence_47: This was a historic achievement for the club as this was the first title-winning season for 28 years, and it also meant a return to the [[UEFA_Champions_League|UEFA Champions League]].
sentence_48: Being league champions, AZ qualified for the [[2009–10_UEFA_Champions_League|Champions League]] for only the second time.
sentence_49: It was drawn into a group alongside [[Arsenal_FC|Arsenal FC]], [[Standard_Liège|Standard Liège]] and [[Olympiacos|Olympiacos]] but only took four points from six matches and finished bottom of their group.
sentence_50: For the 2009–10 season, [[Ronald_Koeman|Ronald Koeman]] succeeded Louis van Gaal, who had departed to manage [[FC_Bayern_Munich|Bayern Munich]] after leading AZ to the championship.
sentence_51: Koeman was officially hired on 17 May 2009, but on 5 December, AZ announced he was no longer in charge of the club after losing 7 of his first 16 matches.
sentence_52: Former [[Rangers_F.C.|Rangers]] and [[FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] manager [[Dick_Advocaat|Dick Advocaat]] took over for the remainder of the season.
sentence_53: Under Advocaat, AZ achieved solid results and secured European football for the next season.
sentence_54: For the 2010–11 season, AZ appointed [[Gertjan_Verbeek|Gertjan Verbeek]] as its new manager.
sentence_55: They finished the [[2010–11_Eredivisie|2010–11 Eredivisie]] in fourth place, thus securing [[2011–12_UEFA_Europa_League|Europa League football]] for the next season, while in the [[2010–11_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]], AZ reached the last eight, where they were beaten by rivals Ajax by a 1–0 scoreline.
sentence_56: AZ also finished third in their [[2010–11_UEFA_Europa_League|Europa League]] group, thus failing to qualifying for the competition's knockout round.
sentence_57: In the 2011–12 season, AZ finished fourth in the [[2011–12_Eredivisie|Eredivisie]], though performed significantly better in cup competitions, reaching the semi-finals in the [[2011–12_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]] (losing to [[Heracles_Almelo|Heracles]] after extra time) and the quarter-finals in the Europa League.
sentence_58: In the latter, the club ultimately lost to Valencia after having defeated [[Udinese_Calcio|Udinese]], [[R.S.C._Anderlecht|Anderlecht]], [[Malmö_FF|Malmö FF]], [[FK_Austria_Wien|Austria Wien]], [[FC_Metalist_Kharkiv|Metalist Kharkiv]], [[Aalesunds_FK|Aalesund]] and [[FK_Baumit_Jablonec|Baumit Jablonec]] to reach that stage.
sentence_59: On 21 December 2011, during the quarter-finals of the [[2011–12_KNVB_Cup|2011–12 KNVB Cup]], a 19-year-old Ajax fan invaded the [[Amsterdam_Arena|Amsterdam Arena]] pitch in the 36th minute with Ajax winning 1–0, attacking AZ goalkeeper [[Esteban_Alvarado|Esteban Alvarado]].
sentence_60: The fan slipped and Alvarado kicked the fan twice, prompting the referee to issue the goalkeeper a red card.
sentence_61: Following this, AZ manager Gertjan Verbeek ordered his players to leave the pitch for the dressing room in protest.
sentence_62: The match was later played on 19 January 2012, with Alvarado's red card rescinded; AZ won 3–2.
sentence_63: The 2012–13 season started in the [[2012–13_UEFA_Europa_League_qualifying_phase_and_play-off_round|Europa League]] with a qualifying play-off round against [[Guus_Hiddink|Guus Hiddink]]'s [[FC_Anzhi_Makhachkala|Anzhi Makhachkala]].
sentence_64: AZ was hammered 6–0 on aggregate.
sentence_65: Disappointingly, AZ finished tenth in the [[2012–13_Eredivisie|2012–13 Eredivisie]], although the club won the [[2012–13_KNVB_Cup|2012–13 KNVB Cup]] after defeating PSV 2–1 in the [[2012–13_KNVB_Cup#Final|final]].
sentence_66: As cup winners, AZ automatically qualified for the [[2013–14_UEFA_Europa_League|2013–14 Europa League]].
sentence_67: In September 2013, just one day after emphatically beating PSV, at the time the [[2013–14_Eredivisie|league leaders]], Verbeek was dismissed as first team manager by the club due to "a lack of chemistry" between management and players.
sentence_68: He was replaced by Dick Advocaat for the remainder of the season until a permanent replacement could be found.
sentence_69: Advocaat took AZ to the semi-finals of the [[2013–14_KNVB_Cup|KNVB Cup]], the quarter-finals of the [[2013–14_UEFA_Europa_League|Europa League]] and eighth in the league, ultimately losing to [[FC_Groningen|Groningen]] in the Europa League play-off final round (their 58th match of the season, a club record).
sentence_70: The [[2014–15_Eredivisie|2014–15 season]] began with a new manager, former [[SC_Heerenveen|Heerenveen]] manager and Ajax great [[Marco_van_Basten|Marco van Basten]].
sentence_71: However, after just three matches into the season, Van Basten resigned as manager to become assistant manager under [[Alex_Pastoor|Alex Pastoor]], citing heavy stress as the main reason.
sentence_72: Pastoor was the interim manager during two matches under Van Basten's absence and received the official title on 16 September, but contract negotiations failed and he left the club just two days later.
sentence_73: A week later, John van den Brom was appointed manager.
sentence_74: Under Van den Brom, AZ quickly rose up to the sub-top, eventually finished the season in third place, surpassing Feyenoord on the final season's matchday and qualifying for the [[2015–16_UEFA_Europa_League|2015–16 Europa League]].
sentence_75: The [[2015–16_Eredivisie|2015–16 Eredivisie]] started with AZ selling most of its first-team players from the previous season during the summer transfer period.
sentence_76: As a response, AZ bought players from other Dutch clubs, notably [[Vincent_Janssen|Vincent Janssen]] from [[Almere_City_FC|Almere City]], [[Alireza_Jahanbakhsh|Alireza Jahanbakhsh]] from [[N.E.C._(football_club)|NEC]] and [[Ben_Rienstra|Ben Rienstra]] from [[PEC_Zwolle|PEC Zwolle]].
sentence_77: In December, it was announced free agent [[Ron_Vlaar|Ron Vlaar]] signed a contract until the end of the season after training with the club for a few weeks prior.
sentence_78: Vlaar quickly became team captain and helped lift AZ from tenth place to a fourth-place finish in the league.
sentence_79: Along this rise, new signing Vincent Janssen scored 27 goals for the club, earning him the Eredivisie top goalscorer title.
sentence_80: In the [[2015–16_KNVB_Cup|2015–16 KNVB Cup]], AZ made it to the semi-finals, losing 3–1 to Feyenoord.
sentence_81: AZ won the first two qualification rounds to qualify for the 2015–16 Europa League group stage, but finished last in their group.
sentence_82: At the start of the [[2016–17_Eredivisie|2016–17 Eredivisie]], AZ sold last season's performer Vincent Janssen to [[Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and long-time midfielder [[Markus_Henriksen|Markus Henriksen]] to [[Hull_City_A.F.C.|Hull City]].
sentence_83: In the [[2016–17_UEFA_Europa_League|2016–17 Europa League]], AZ finished second in Group D, surviving the group stage for the third time in five seasons.

sentence_90: Participating in the [[Eerste_Divisie|Eerste Divisie]], the reserve squad of AZ trains and plays their home games in [[Zaanstad|Zaanstad]].
sentence_91: See also: [[AFAS_Stadion|AFAS Stadion]]
sentence_92: AZ play its home matches at the [[AFAS_Stadion|AFAS Stadion]], located in the southern part of the city of Alkmaar.
sentence_93: The stadium, which is directly owned by the club, was opened in 2006 and replaced the old [[Alkmaarderhout|Alkmaarderhout]] venue as the [[DSB_Bank|DSB Stadion]].
sentence_94: The stadium currently has a capacity of 17,023.
sentence_95: During its design stages, the name Victorie Stadion was frequently used, referring to the [[Eighty_Years'_War|Dutch War of Independence]], the phrase "[[Siege_of_Alkmaar|In Alkmaar begint de victorie]]" (Victory begins in Alkmaar) in particular.
sentence_96: Until now, this name has not been officially in use, the board instead opting for sponsorship deals because of financial motives.
sentence_97: However, to this day, the name maintains a good share of support among the fans.
sentence_98: To further increase revenue, AZ's board of directors decided to expand the capacity of the new stadium to at least 30,000 somewhere in the future.
sentence_99: The extension will be realised by constructing a second tier to three of the four stands.
sentence_100: The main stand with all technical areas, VIP and sponsor and media facilities will remain in place.
sentence_101: These plans, however, were put on hold after the DSB bankruptcy and there are no current plans to increase the capacity.
sentence_102: In October 2009, sponsor [[DSB_Bank|DSB Bank]] was declared bankrupt.
sentence_103: The stadium name temporarily changed from DSB Stadion to AZ Stadion, as it was considered undesirable that the stadium was linked with a non-existent bank.
sentence_104: In February 2010, a new main sponsor was found in construction works service provider BUKO, based in [[Beverwijk|Beverwijk]].
sentence_105: A year later, in the 2010–11 season, AFAS Software took over as official stadium sponsor.
sentence_106: The current external name of the ground is the AFAS Stadion.
sentence_107: On 10 August 2019, the roof of the stadium partially collapsed.
sentence_108: No people were injured during the incident.
sentence_109: As the result AZ spent the rest of the year playing home matches at the [[Cars_Jeans_Stadion|Cars Jeans Stadion]] in [[The_Hague|The Hague]] whilst the damaged roof was being removed, before returning to the stadium on 15 December 2019, beating Ajax 1–0 in their first match back.
sentence_110: As of 27 August 2020, a new roof is under construction.
