sentence_153: In the 16th and 17th century, non-Dutch immigrants to Amsterdam were mostly [[Huguenot|Huguenots]], [[Flemish_people|Flemings]], [[Sephardi_Jews|Sephardi Jews]] and [[Westphalia|Westphalians]].
sentence_154: Huguenots came after the [[Edict_of_Fontainebleau|Edict of Fontainebleau]] in 1685, while the Flemish Protestants came during the [[Eighty_Years'_War|Eighty Years' War]].
sentence_155: The Westphalians came to Amsterdam mostly for economic reasons – their influx continued through the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentence_156: Before the Second World War, 10% of the city population was [[History_of_the_Jews_in_Amsterdam|Jewish]].
sentence_157: Just twenty percent of them survived the [[The_Holocaust|Shoah]].
sentence_158: The first mass immigration in the 20th century was by people from Indonesia, who came to Amsterdam after the independence of the [[Dutch_East_Indies|Dutch East Indies]] in the 1940s and 1950s.
sentence_159: In the 1960s [[Foreign_worker|guest workers]] from Turkey, Morocco, Italy, and Spain emigrated to Amsterdam.
sentence_160: After the independence of Suriname in 1975, a large wave of Surinamese settled in Amsterdam, mostly in the [[Bijlmermeer|Bijlmer]] area.
sentence_161: Other immigrants, including refugees [[Right_of_asylum|asylum seekers]] and [[Illegal_immigration|illegal immigrants]], came from Europe, [[Americas|America]], Asia, and Africa.
sentence_162: In the 1970s and 1980s, many 'old' Amsterdammers moved to 'new' cities like [[Almere|Almere]] and [[Purmerend|Purmerend]], prompted by the third [[Land-use_planning|planological]] bill of the Dutch government.
sentence_163: This bill promoted suburbanisation and arranged for new developments in so-called "groeikernen", literally cores of growth.
sentence_164: Young professionals and artists moved into neighbourhoods de Pijp and the Jordaan abandoned by these Amsterdammers.
sentence_165: The non-Western immigrants settled mostly in the [[Public_housing|social housing]] projects in Amsterdam-West and the Bijlmer.
sentence_166: Today, people of non-Western origin make up approximately one-third of the population of Amsterdam, and more than 50% of the city' s children.
sentence_167: Ethnic Dutch (as [[Dutch_people#Ethnic_identity|defined]] by the Dutch census) now make up a minority of the total population, although by far the largest one.
sentence_168: Only one in three inhabitants under 15 is an autochtoon, or a person who has two parents of Dutch origin.
sentence_169: Segregation along ethnic lines is clearly visible, with people of non-Western origin, considered a separate group by [[Statistics_Netherlands|Statistics Netherlands]], concentrating in specific neighbourhoods especially in [[Amsterdam_Nieuw-West|Nieuw-West]], [[Zeeburg|Zeeburg]], [[Bijlmermeer|Bijlmer]] and in certain areas of [[Amsterdam-Noord|Amsterdam-Noord]].
sentence_170: In 2000, Christians formed the largest religious group in the city (18% of the population).
sentence_171: The next largest religion was Islam (12%), most of whose followers were [[Sunni|Sunni]].
sentence_172: In 2015, [[Christians|Christians]] formed the largest religious group in the city (24% of the population).
sentence_173: The next largest religion was Islam (11.1%), most of whose followers were [[Sunni|Sunni]].
sentence_174: In 1578, the largely Roman Catholic city of Amsterdam joined the revolt against Spanish rule, late in comparison to other major northern Dutch cities.
sentence_175: Roman Catholic priests were driven out of the city.
sentence_176: Following the Dutch takeover, all churches were converted to Protestant worship.
sentence_177: [[Calvinism|Calvinism]] was declared the main religion, and although Catholicism was not forbidden and priests allowed to serve, the [[Hierarchy_of_the_Catholic_Church|Catholic hierarchy]] was prohibited.
sentence_178: This led to the establishment of schuilkerken, covert religious buildings that were hidden in pre-existing buildings.
sentence_179: Catholics, some Jewish and dissenting Protestants worshiped in such buildings.
sentence_180: A large influx of foreigners of many religions came to 17th-century Amsterdam, in particular [[Sephardi_Jews|Sefardic Jews]] from Spain and Portugal, [[Huguenot|Huguenots]] from France, [[Lutheranism|Lutherans]], Mennonites, and Protestants from across the Netherlands.
sentence_181: This led to the establishment of many non-Dutch-speaking churches.
sentence_182: In 1603, the Jewish received permission to practice their religion.
sentence_183: In 1639, the first synagogue was consecrated.
sentence_184: The Jews came to call the town [[Jerusalem_of_the_West|Jerusalem of the West]].
sentence_185: As they became established in the city, other [[Christian_denomination|Christian denominations]] used converted Catholic chapels to conduct their own services.
sentence_186: The oldest English-language church congregation in the world outside the United Kingdom is found at the [[Begijnhof,_Amsterdam|Begijnhof]].
sentence_187: Regular services there are still offered in English under the auspices of the [[Church_of_Scotland|Church of Scotland]].
sentence_188: Being Calvinists, the Huguenots soon integrated into the [[Dutch_Reformed_Church|Dutch Reformed Church]], though often retaining their own congregations.
sentence_189: Some, commonly referred by the moniker 'Walloon', are recognisable today as they offer occasional services in French.
sentence_190: In the second half of the 17th century, Amsterdam experienced an influx of Ashkenazim, Jews from [[Central_Europe|Central and Eastern Europe]].
sentence_191: Jews often fled the [[Pogrom|pogroms]] in those areas.
sentence_192: The first Ashkenazis who arrived in Amsterdam were [[Refugee|refugees]] from the [[Khmelnytsky_Uprising|Khmelnytsky Uprising]] in Ukraine and the [[Thirty_Years'_War|Thirty Years' War]], which devastated much of Central Europe.
sentence_193: They not only founded their own synagogues, but had a strong influence on the 'Amsterdam dialect' adding a large [[Yiddish_language|Yiddish]] local vocabulary.
sentence_194: Despite an absence of an official Jewish [[Ghetto|ghetto]], most Jews preferred to live in the eastern part of the old medieval heart of the city.
sentence_195: The main street of this Jewish neighbourhood was the Jodenbreestraat.
sentence_196: The neighbourhood comprised the Waterlooplein and the Nieuwmarkt.
sentence_197: Buildings in this neighbourhood fell into disrepair after the Second World War, and a large section of the neighbourhood was demolished during the construction of the subway.
sentence_198: This led to riots, and as a result the original plans for large-scale reconstruction were abandoned.
sentence_199: The neighbourhood was rebuilt with smaller-scale residence buildings on the basis of its original layout.
sentence_200: Catholic churches in Amsterdam have been constructed since the restoration of the episcopal hierarchy in 1853.
sentence_201: One of the principal architects behind the city's Catholic churches, Cuypers, was also responsible for the Amsterdam Central station and the [[Rijksmuseum|Rijksmuseum]].
sentence_202: In 1924, the [[Catholic_Church|Roman Catholic Church]] of the Netherlands hosted the [[Eucharistic_Congress|International Eucharistic Congress]] in Amsterdam, and numerous Catholic [[Prelate|prelates]] visited the city, where festivities were held in churches and stadiums.
sentence_203: Catholic processions on the public streets, however, were still forbidden under law at the time.
sentence_204: Only in the 20th century was Amsterdam's relation to Catholicism normalised, but despite its far larger population size, the episcopal see of the city was placed in the provincial town of [[Haarlem|Haarlem]].
sentence_205: Historically, Amsterdam has been predominantly Christian, in 1900 Christians formed the largest religious group in the city (70% of the population), [[Dutch_Reformed_Church|Dutch Reformed Church]] formed 45% of the city population, while Roman catholic formed 25% of the city population.
sentence_206: In recent times, religious demographics in Amsterdam have been changed by immigration from former colonies.
sentence_207: [[Hinduism|Hinduism]] has been introduced from the Hindu diaspora from Suriname and several distinct branches of Islam have been brought from various parts of the world.
sentence_208: Islam is now the largest non-Christian religion in Amsterdam.
sentence_209: The large community of Ghanaian immigrants have established African churches, often in parking garages in the [[Bijlmermeer|Bijlmer]] area.
sentence_210: Amsterdam experienced an influx of religions and cultures after the Second World War.
sentence_211: With 180 different nationalities, Amsterdam is home to one of the widest varieties of nationalities of any city in the world.
sentence_212: The proportion of the population of immigrant origin in the city proper is about 50% and 88% of the population are Dutch citizens.
sentence_213: Amsterdam has been one of the municipalities in the Netherlands which provided immigrants with extensive and free [[Dutch_language|Dutch-language]] courses, which have benefited many immigrants.
sentence_214: See also: [[List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Amsterdam|List of tallest buildings in Amsterdam]]
sentence_215: Amsterdam fans out south from the [[Amsterdam_Centraal_station|Amsterdam Centraal station]] and [[Damrak|Damrak]], the main street off the station.
sentence_216: The oldest area of the town is known as [[De_Wallen|De Wallen]] (English: "The Quays").
sentence_217: It lies to the east of Damrak and contains the city's famous red-light district.
sentence_218: To the south of De Wallen is the old Jewish quarter of Waterlooplein.
sentence_219: The medieval and colonial age [[Canals_of_Amsterdam|canals of Amsterdam]], known as grachten, embraces the heart of the city where homes have interesting gables.
sentence_220: Beyond the Grachtengordel are the former working-class areas of Jordaan and de Pijp.
sentence_221: The [[Museumplein|Museumplein]] with the city's major museums, the [[Vondelpark|Vondelpark]], a 19th-century park named after the Dutch writer [[Joost_van_den_Vondel|Joost van den Vondel]], and the [[Plantage_(Amsterdam)|Plantage]] neighbourhood, with the [[Natura_Artis_Magistra|zoo]], are also located outside the Grachtengordel.
sentence_222: Several parts of the city and the surrounding urban area are [[Polder|polders]].
sentence_223: This can be recognised by the suffix -meer which means lake, as in [[Aalsmeer|Aalsmeer]], [[Bijlmermeer|Bijlmermeer]], [[Haarlemmermeer|Haarlemmermeer]], and [[Watergraafsmeer|Watergraafsmeer]].
sentence_224: Main article: [[Canals_of_Amsterdam|Canals of Amsterdam]]
sentence_225: The Amsterdam canal system is the result of conscious [[Urban_planning|city planning]].
sentence_226: In the early 17th century, when immigration was at a peak, a comprehensive plan was developed that was based on four concentric half-circles of canals with their ends emerging at the [[IJ_(Amsterdam)|IJ]] bay.
sentence_227: Known as the [[Grachtengordel_(Amsterdam)|Grachtengordel]], three of the canals were mostly for residential development: the Herengracht (where "Heren" refers to Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam (ruling lords of Amsterdam), and [[Gracht|gracht]] means canal, so that the name can be roughly translated as "Canal of the Lords"), Keizersgracht (Emperor's Canal), and Prinsengracht (Prince's Canal).
sentence_228: The fourth and outermost canal is the Singelgracht, which is often not mentioned on maps because it is a collective name for all canals in the outer ring.
sentence_229: The Singelgracht should not be confused with the oldest and innermost canal, the [[Singel|Singel]].
sentence_230: The canals served for defence, [[Water_resource_management|water management]] and transport.
sentence_231: The defences took the form of a moat and [[Earthworks_(engineering)|earthen dikes]], with gates at transit points, but otherwise no masonry superstructures.
sentence_232: The original plans have been lost, so historians, such as Ed Taverne, need to speculate on the original intentions: it is thought that the considerations of the layout were purely practical and defensive rather than ornamental.
sentence_233: Construction started in 1613 and proceeded from west to east, across the breadth of the layout, like a gigantic windshield wiper as the historian Geert Mak calls it – and not from the centre outwards, as a popular myth has it.
sentence_234: The canal construction in the southern sector was completed by 1656.
sentence_235: Subsequently, the construction of residential buildings proceeded slowly.
sentence_236: The eastern part of the concentric canal plan, covering the area between the Amstel river and the IJ bay, has never been implemented.
sentence_237: In the following centuries, the land was used for parks, senior citizens' homes, theatres, other public facilities, and waterways without much planning.
sentence_238: Over the years, several canals have been filled in, becoming streets or squares, such as the [[Nieuwezijds_Voorburgwal|Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal]] and the [[Spui_(Amsterdam)|Spui]].
sentence_239: Main article: [[Expansion_of_Amsterdam_since_the_19th_century|Expansion of Amsterdam since the 19th century]]
sentence_240: After the development of Amsterdam's canals in the 17th century, the city did not grow beyond its borders for two centuries.
sentence_241: During the 19th century, Samuel Sarphati devised a plan based on the grandeur of Paris and London at that time.
sentence_242: The plan envisaged the construction of new houses, public buildings and streets just outside the [[Grachtengordel_(Amsterdam)|Grachtengordel]].
sentence_243: The main aim of the plan, however, was to improve public health.
sentence_244: Although the plan did not expand the city, it did produce some of the largest public buildings to date, like the Paleis voor Volksvlijt.
sentence_245: Following Sarphati, civil engineers Jacobus van Niftrik and Jan Kalff designed an entire ring of 19th-century neighbourhoods surrounding the city's centre, with the city preserving the ownership of all land outside the 17th-century limit, thus firmly controlling development.
sentence_246: Most of these neighbourhoods became home to the working class.
sentence_247: In response to overcrowding, two plans were designed at the beginning of the 20th century which were very different from anything Amsterdam had ever seen before: Plan Zuid, designed by the architect [[Hendrik_Petrus_Berlage|Berlage]], and West.
sentence_248: These plans involved the development of new neighbourhoods consisting of housing blocks for all social classes.
sentence_249: After the Second World War, large new neighbourhoods were built in the western, southeastern, and northern parts of the city.
sentence_250: These new neighbourhoods were built to relieve the city's shortage of living space and give people affordable houses with modern conveniences.
sentence_251: The neighbourhoods consisted mainly of large housing blocks situated among green spaces, connected to wide roads, making the neighbourhoods easily accessible by [[Car|motor car]].
sentence_252: The western suburbs which were built in that period are collectively called the Westelijke Tuinsteden.
sentence_253: The area to the southeast of the city built during the same period is known as the Bijlmer.
sentence_254: Amsterdam has a rich [[History_of_architecture|architectural history]].
sentence_255: The oldest building in Amsterdam is the [[Oude_Kerk,_Amsterdam|Oude Kerk]] (English: Old Church), at the heart of the Wallen, consecrated in 1306.
sentence_256: The oldest wooden building is Het Houten Huys at the [[Begijnhof,_Amsterdam|Begijnhof]].
sentence_257: It was constructed around 1425 and is one of only two existing wooden buildings.
sentence_258: It is also one of the few examples of [[Gothic_architecture|Gothic architecture]] in Amsterdam.
sentence_259: The oldest stone building of the Netherlands, The Moriaan is built in [['s-Hertogenbosch|'s-Hertogenbosch]].
sentence_260: In the 16th century, wooden buildings were razed and replaced with brick ones.
sentence_261: During this period, many buildings were constructed in the [[Architectural_style|architectural style]] of the [[The_Renaissance|Renaissance]].
sentence_262: Buildings of this period are very recognisable with their [[Crow-stepped_gable|stepped gable]] façades, which is the common Dutch Renaissance style.
sentence_263: Amsterdam quickly developed its own [[Renaissance_architecture|Renaissance architecture]].
sentence_264: These buildings were built according to the principles of the architect [[Hendrick_de_Keyser|Hendrick de Keyser]].
sentence_265: One of the most striking buildings designed by Hendrick de Keyser is the [[Westerkerk|Westerkerk]].
sentence_266: In the 17th century [[Baroque_architecture|baroque architecture]] became very popular, as it was elsewhere in Europe.
sentence_267: This roughly coincided with Amsterdam's [[Dutch_Golden_Age|Golden Age]].
sentence_268: The leading architects of this style in Amsterdam were [[Jacob_van_Campen|Jacob van Campen]], [[Philips_Vingboons|Philips Vingboons]] and [[Daniël_Stalpaert|Daniel Stalpaert]].
sentence_269: Philip Vingboons designed splendid merchants' houses throughout the city.
sentence_270: A famous building in [[Baroque|baroque style]] in Amsterdam is the [[Royal_Palace_of_Amsterdam|Royal Palace]] on Dam Square.
sentence_271: Throughout the 18th century, Amsterdam was heavily influenced by [[Culture_of_France|French culture]].
sentence_272: This is reflected in the architecture of that period.
sentence_273: Around 1815, architects broke with the baroque style and started building in different neo-styles.
sentence_274: Most Gothic style buildings date from that era and are therefore said to be built in a [[Gothic_Revival_architecture|neo-gothic]] style.
sentence_275: At the end of the 19th century, the [[Art_Nouveau|Jugendstil]] or [[Art_Nouveau|Art Nouveau]] style became popular and many new buildings were constructed in this architectural style.
sentence_276: Since Amsterdam expanded rapidly during this period, new buildings adjacent to the city centre were also built in this style.
sentence_277: The houses in the vicinity of the [[Museumplein|Museum Square]] in Amsterdam Oud-Zuid are an example of Jugendstil.
sentence_278: The last style that was popular in Amsterdam before the [[Modern_history|modern era]] was [[Art_Deco|Art Deco]].
sentence_279: Amsterdam had its own version of the style, which was called the Amsterdamse School.
sentence_280: Whole districts were built this style, such as the Rivierenbuurt.
sentence_281: A notable feature of the façades of buildings designed in Amsterdamse School is that they are highly decorated and ornate, with oddly shaped windows and doors.
sentence_282: The old city centre is the focal point of all the architectural styles before the end of the 19th century.
sentence_283: Jugendstil and Georgian are mostly found outside the city's centre in the neighbourhoods built in the early 20th century, although there are also some striking examples of these styles in the city centre.
sentence_284: Most historic buildings in the city centre and nearby are houses, such as the famous merchants' houses lining the canals.
sentence_285: Main articles: [[List_of_parks_in_Amsterdam|List of parks in Amsterdam]] and [[List_of_squares_in_Amsterdam|List of squares in Amsterdam]]
sentence_286: Amsterdam has many parks, open spaces, and squares throughout the city.
sentence_287: The [[Vondelpark|Vondelpark]], the largest park in the city, is located in the [[Amsterdam_Oud-Zuid|Oud-Zuid]] neighbourhood and is named after the 17th-century Amsterdam author [[Joost_van_den_Vondel|Joost van den Vondel]].
sentence_288: Yearly, the park has around 10 million visitors.
sentence_289: In the park is an open-air theatre, a playground and several [[Horeca|horeca]] facilities.
sentence_290: In the [[Amsterdam-Zuid|Zuid]] borough, is the Beatrixpark, named after [[Beatrix_of_the_Netherlands|Queen Beatrix]].
sentence_291: Between Amsterdam and [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]] is the [[Amsterdamse_Bos|Amsterdamse Bos]] ("Amsterdam Forest"), the largest recreational area in Amsterdam.
sentence_292: Annually, almost 4.5 million people visit the park, which has a size of 1.000 hectares and is approximately three times the size of [[Central_Park|Central Park]].
sentence_293: The Amstelpark in the [[Amsterdam-Zuid|Zuid]] borough houses the Rieker windmill, which dates to 1636.
sentence_294: Other parks include the [[Sarphatipark|Sarphatipark]] in the [[De_Pijp|De Pijp]] neighbourhood, the [[Oosterpark_(Amsterdam)|Oosterpark]] in the [[Amsterdam-Oost|Oost]] borough and the [[Westerpark_(park)|Westerpark]] in the [[Westerpark_(neighbourhood)|Westerpark]] neighbourhood.
sentence_295: The city has three beaches: Nemo Beach, Citybeach "Het stenen hoofd" (Silodam) and Blijburg, all located in the Centrum borough.
sentence_296: The city has many open squares (plein in Dutch).
sentence_297: The namesake of the city as the site of the original dam, Dam Square, is the main city square and has the [[Royal_Palace_of_Amsterdam|Royal Palace]] and [[National_Monument_(Amsterdam)|National Monument]].
sentence_298: [[Museumplein|Museumplein]] hosts various museums, including the [[Rijksmuseum|Rijksmuseum]], [[Van_Gogh_Museum|Van Gogh Museum]], and [[Stedelijk_Museum_Amsterdam|Stedelijk Museum]].
sentence_299: Other squares include [[Rembrandtplein|Rembrandtplein]], Muntplein, Nieuwmarkt, [[Leidseplein|Leidseplein]], [[Spui_(Amsterdam)|Spui]], and Waterlooplein.
sentence_300: Also, near to Amsterdam is the [[Nekkeveld_estate|Nekkeveld estate]] conservation project.
sentence_301: Amsterdam is the financial and business capital of the Netherlands.
sentence_302: According to the 2007 European Cities Monitor (ECM) – an annual location survey of Europe's leading companies carried out by global real estate consultant [[Cushman_&_Wakefield|Cushman & Wakefield]] – Amsterdam is one of the top European cities in which to locate an [[International_business|international business]], ranking fifth in the survey.
sentence_303: with the survey determining [[London|London]], [[Paris|Paris]], [[Frankfurt|Frankfurt]] and [[Barcelona|Barcelona]] as the four European cities surpassing Amsterdam in this regard.
sentence_304: A substantial number of large corporations and banks' headquarters are located in the Amsterdam area, including: [[AkzoNobel|AkzoNobel]], [[Heineken_International|Heineken International]], [[ING_Group|ING Group]], [[ABN_AMRO|ABN AMRO]], [[TomTom|TomTom]], [[Delta_Lloyd_Group|Delta Lloyd Group]], [[Booking.com|Booking.com]] and [[Philips|Philips]].
sentence_305: Although many small offices remain along the [[Canals_of_Amsterdam|historic canals]], centrally based companies have increasingly relocated outside [[Amsterdam-Centrum|Amsterdam's city centre]].
sentence_306: Consequently, the Zuidas (English: South Axis) has become the new financial and legal hub of Amsterdam, with the country's five largest law firms and several subsidiaries of large consulting firms, such as [[Boston_Consulting_Group|Boston Consulting Group]] and [[Accenture|Accenture]], as well as the [[World_Trade_Center_(Amsterdam)|World Trade Centre (Amsterdam)]] located in the Zuidas district.
sentence_307: In addition to the Zuidas, there are three smaller financial districts in Amsterdam:

list.value: around Amsterdam Sloterdijk railway station. Where one can find the offices of several newspapers, such as De Telegraaf. as well as those of [[Deloitte|Deloitte]], the Gemeentelijk Vervoerbedrijf (municipal public transport company), and the [[Tax_and_Customs_Administration|Dutch tax offices]] (Belastingdienst);
around the [[Johan_Cruyff_Arena|Johan Cruyff Arena]] in [[Amsterdam_Zuidoost|Amsterdam Zuidoost]];

around the [[Amsterdam_Amstel_railway_station|Amstel railway station]] in the [[Amsterdam-Oost|Amsterdam-Oost]] district to the east of the historical city. Amsterdam's [[List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures_in_the_world|tallest building]], the [[Rembrandt_Tower|Rembrandt Tower]], is situated here. As are the headquarters of [[Philips|Philips]], the Dutch multinational conglomerate.

sentence_308: The adjoining municipality of [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]] is the location of [[KPMG|KPMG International's]] global headquarters.
sentence_309: Other non-Dutch companies have chosen to settle in communities surrounding Amsterdam since they allow [[Freehold_(law)|freehold]] property ownership, whereas Amsterdam retains [[Ground_rent|ground rent]].
sentence_310: The [[Port_of_Amsterdam|Port of Amsterdam]] is the fourth-largest port in Europe, the 38th largest port in the world and the second-largest port in the Netherlands by metric tons of cargo.
sentence_311: In 2014 the Port of Amsterdam had a cargo throughput of 97,4 million tons of cargo, which was mostly [[Bulk_cargo|bulk cargo]].
sentence_312: Amsterdam has the biggest cruise port in the Netherlands with more than 150 cruise ships every year.
sentence_313: In 2019 the new lock in IJmuiden will open; the port will then be able to grow to 125 million tonnes in capacity.
sentence_314: The [[Amsterdam_Stock_Exchange|Amsterdam Stock Exchange]] (AEX), now part of [[Euronext|Euronext]], is the world's oldest stock exchange and is one of Europe's largest bourses.
sentence_315: It is near Dam Square in the city centre.
sentence_316: Together with [[Eindhoven|Eindhoven]] ([[BrabantStad#Brainport|Brainport]]) and [[Rotterdam|Rotterdam]] ([[Port_of_Rotterdam|Seaport]]), Amsterdam (Airport) forms the foundation of the Dutch economy.
sentence_317: Main article: [[List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Amsterdam|List of tourist attractions in Amsterdam]]
sentence_318: Amsterdam is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Europe, receiving more than 5.34 million international visitors annually, this is excluding the 16 million day-trippers visiting the city every year.
sentence_319: The number of visitors has been growing steadily over the past decade.
sentence_320: This can be attributed to an increasing number of European visitors.
sentence_321: Two-thirds of the hotels are located in the city's centre.
sentence_322: Hotels with 4 or 5 stars contribute 42% of the total beds available and 41% of the overnight stays in Amsterdam.
sentence_323: The room occupation rate was 85% in 2017, up from 78% in 2006.
sentence_324: The majority of tourists (74%) originate from Europe.
sentence_325: The largest group of non-European visitors come from the United States, accounting for 14% of the total.
sentence_326: Certain years have a theme in Amsterdam to attract extra tourists.
sentence_327: For example, the year 2006 was designated "Rembrandt 400", to celebrate the 400th birthday of [[Rembrandt|Rembrandt van Rijn]].
sentence_328: Some hotels offer special arrangements or activities during these years.
sentence_329: The average number of guests per year staying at the four campsites around the city range from 12,000 to 65,000.
sentence_330: Main article: [[De_Wallen|De Wallen]]
sentence_331: De Wallen, also known as Walletjes or Rosse Buurt, is a designated area for [[Prostitution_in_the_Netherlands|legalised prostitution]] and is Amsterdam's largest and best-known [[Red-light_district|red-light district]].
sentence_332: This neighbourhood has become a famous attraction for tourists.
sentence_333: It consists of a network of canals, streets, and alleys containing several hundred small, one-room apartments rented by [[Sex_worker|sex workers]] who offer their services from behind a window or glass door, typically illuminated with red lights.
sentence_334: In recent years, the city government has been closing and repurposing the famous red-light district windows in an effort to clean up the area and reduce the amount of party and sex tourism.
sentence_335: Shops in Amsterdam range from large high-end department stores such as [[De_Bijenkorf|De Bijenkorf]] founded in 1870 to small speciality shops.
sentence_336: Amsterdam's high-end shops are found in the streets [[P.C._Hooftstraat|P.C.
sentence_337: Hooftstraat]] and Cornelis Schuytstraat, which are located in the vicinity of the [[Vondelpark|Vondelpark]].
sentence_338: One of Amsterdam's busiest high streets is the narrow, medieval Kalverstraat in the heart of the city.
sentence_339: Other shopping areas include the Negen Straatjes and Haarlemmerdijk and Haarlemmerstraat.
sentence_340: Negen Straatjes are nine narrow streets within the Grachtengordel, the concentric canal system of Amsterdam.
sentence_341: The Negen Straatjes differ from other shopping districts with the presence of a large diversity of privately owned shops.
sentence_342: The Haarlemmerstraat and Haarlemmerdijk were voted best shopping street in the Netherlands in 2011.
sentence_343: These streets have as the Negen Straatjes a large diversity of privately owned shops.
sentence_344: However, as the Negen Straatjes are dominated by fashion stores, the Haarlemmerstraat and Haarlemmerdijk offer a wide variety of stores, just to name some specialities: candy and other food-related stores, lingerie, sneakers, wedding clothing, interior shops, books, Italian deli's, racing and mountain bikes, skatewear, etc.
sentence_345: The city also features a large number of open-air markets such as the [[Albert_Cuyp_Market|Albert Cuyp Market]], Westerstraat-markt, Ten Katemarkt, and Dappermarkt.
sentence_346: Some of these markets are held daily, like the Albert Cuypmarkt and the Dappermarkt.
sentence_347: Others, like the Westerstraatmarkt, are held every week.
sentence_348: Several fashion brands and designers are based in Amsterdam.
sentence_349: Fashion designers include [[Iris_van_Herpen|Iris van Herpen]], Mart Visser, [[Viktor_&_Rolf|Viktor & Rolf]], Marlies Dekkers and [[Frans_Molenaar|Frans Molenaar]].
sentence_350: Fashion models like Yfke Sturm, [[Doutzen_Kroes|Doutzen Kroes]] and Kim Noorda started their careers in Amsterdam.
sentence_351: Amsterdam has its garment centre in the World Fashion Center.
sentence_352: Fashion photographers [[Inez_and_Vinoodh|Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin]] were born in Amsterdam.
sentence_353: Amsterdam is home of the [[Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] football club [[AFC_Ajax|AFC Ajax]].
sentence_354: The stadium [[Johan_Cruyff_Arena|Johan Cruyff Arena]] is the home of Ajax.
sentence_355: It is located in the [[Amsterdam_Zuidoost|south-east]] of the city next to the new Amsterdam Bijlmer ArenA railway station.
sentence_356: Before moving to their current location in 1996, Ajax played their regular matches in the now demolished De Meer Stadion in the eastern part of the city or in the [[Olympic_Stadium_(Amsterdam)|Olympic Stadium]].
sentence_357: In 1928, Amsterdam hosted the [[1928_Summer_Olympics|Summer Olympics]].
sentence_358: The [[Olympic_Stadium_(Amsterdam)|Olympic Stadium]] built for the occasion has been completely restored and is now used for cultural and sporting events, such as the [[Amsterdam_Marathon|Amsterdam Marathon]].
sentence_359: In 1920, Amsterdam assisted in hosting some of the [[Sailing_at_the_1920_Summer_Olympics|sailing]] events for the [[1920_Summer_Olympics|Summer Olympics]] held in neighbouring [[Antwerp|Antwerp]], Belgium by hosting events at [[IJ_(Amsterdam)|Buiten IJ]].
sentence_360: The city holds the [[Dam_tot_Damloop|Dam to Dam Run]], a 16-kilometre (10 mi) race from Amsterdam to [[Zaandam|Zaandam]], as well as the [[Amsterdam_Marathon|Amsterdam Marathon]].
sentence_361: The ice hockey team [[Amstel_Tijgers|Amstel Tijgers]] play in the [[Jaap_Eden|Jaap Eden]] ice rink.
sentence_362: The team competes in the Dutch ice hockey premier league.
sentence_363: [[Long_track_speed_skating|Speed skating]] championships have been held on the 400-metre lane of this ice rink.
sentence_364: Amsterdam holds two [[American_football|American football]] franchises: the [[Amsterdam_Crusaders|Amsterdam Crusaders]] and the Amsterdam Panthers.
sentence_365: The [[Amsterdam_Pirates|Amsterdam Pirates]] baseball team competes in the Dutch Major League.
sentence_366: There are three [[Field_hockey|field hockey]] teams: Amsterdam, Pinoké and Hurley, who play their matches around the [[Wagener_Stadium|Wagener Stadium]] in the nearby city of [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]].
sentence_367: The basketball team [[MyGuide_Amsterdam|MyGuide Amsterdam]] competes in the Dutch premier division and play their games in the Sporthallen Zuid.
sentence_368: There is one rugby club in Amsterdam, which also hosts sports training classes such as RTC (Rugby Talenten Centrum or Rugby Talent Centre) and the National Rugby stadium.
sentence_369: Since 1999, the city of Amsterdam honours the best sportsmen and women at the [[Amsterdam_Sportsman_of_the_year|Amsterdam Sports Awards]].
sentence_370: Boxer [[Raymond_Joval|Raymond Joval]] and field hockey midfielder Carole Thate were the first to receive the awards, in 1999.
sentence_371: Amsterdam hosted the World Gymnaestrada in 1991 and will do so again in 2023.
sentence_372: Main article: [[Government_of_Amsterdam|Government of Amsterdam]]
sentence_373: The city of Amsterdam is a municipality under the Dutch Municipalities Act.
sentence_374: It is governed by a directly elected [[Municipal_council_(Netherlands)|municipal council]], a municipal executive board and a mayor.
sentence_375: Since 1981, the municipality of Amsterdam has gradually been divided into semi-autonomous [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|boroughs]], called stadsdelen or 'districts'.
sentence_376: Over time, a total of 15 boroughs were created.
sentence_377: In May 2010, under a major reform, the number of [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|Amsterdam boroughs]] was reduced to eight: [[Amsterdam-Centrum|Amsterdam-Centrum]] covering the city centre including the [[Canals_of_Amsterdam|canal belt]], [[Amsterdam-Noord|Amsterdam-Noord]] consisting of the neighbourhoods north of the [[IJ_(Amsterdam)|IJ lake]], [[Amsterdam-Oost|Amsterdam-Oost]] in the east, [[Amsterdam-Zuid|Amsterdam-Zuid]] in the south, [[Amsterdam-West|Amsterdam-West]] in the west, [[Amsterdam_Nieuw-West|Amsterdam Nieuw-West]] in the far west, [[Amsterdam_Zuidoost|Amsterdam Zuidoost]] in the southeast, and [[Westpoort_(Amsterdam)|Westpoort]] covering the [[Port_of_Amsterdam|Port of Amsterdam]] area.
sentence_378: Main articles: [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|Boroughs of Amsterdam]] and [[Municipal_council_(Netherlands)|Municipal council (Netherlands)]]
sentence_379: As with all Dutch municipalities, Amsterdam is governed by a directly elected [[Municipal_council_(Netherlands)|municipal council]], a municipal executive board and a government appointed mayor (burgemeester).
sentence_380: The mayor is a member of the municipal executive board, but also has individual responsibilities in maintaining public order.
sentence_381: On 27 June 2018, [[Femke_Halsema|Femke Halsema]] (former member of [[House_of_Representatives_(Netherlands)|House of Representatives]] for [[GroenLinks|GroenLinks]] from 1998 to 2011) was appointed as the first woman to be [[List_of_mayors_of_Amsterdam|Mayor of Amsterdam]] by the [[King's_Commissioner|King's Commissioner]] of [[North_Holland|North Holland]] for a six-year term after being nominated by the Amsterdam [[Municipal_council_(Netherlands)|municipal council]] and began serving a six-year term on 12 July 2018.
sentence_382: She replaces [[Eberhard_van_der_Laan|Eberhard van der Laan]] ([[Labour_Party_(Netherlands)|Labour Party]]) who was the Mayor of Amsterdam from 2010 until his death in October 2017.
sentence_383: After the 2014 municipal council elections, a governing majority of [[Democrats_66|D66]], [[People's_Party_for_Freedom_and_Democracy|VVD]] and [[Socialist_Party_(Netherlands)|SP]] was formed – the first coalition without the [[Labour_Party_(Netherlands)|Labour Party]] since [[World_War_II|World War II]].
sentence_384: Next to the Mayor, the municipal executive board consists of eight wethouders ('alderpersons') appointed by the [[Municipal_council_(Netherlands)|municipal council]]: four [[Democrats_66|D66]] alderpersons, two [[People's_Party_for_Freedom_and_Democracy|VVD]] alderpersons and two [[Socialist_Party_(Netherlands)|SP]] alderpersons.
sentence_385: On 18 September 2017, it was announced by [[Eberhard_van_der_Laan|Eberhard van der Laan]] in an open letter to Amsterdam citizens that [[Kajsa_Ollongren|Kajsa Ollongren]] would take up his office as acting Mayor of Amsterdam with immediate effect due to ill health.
sentence_386: Ollongren was succeeded as acting Mayor by Eric van der Burg on 26 October 2017 and by [[Jozias_van_Aartsen|Jozias van Aartsen]] on 4 December 2017.
sentence_387: Unlike most other Dutch municipalities, Amsterdam is subdivided into eight [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|boroughs]], called stadsdelen or 'districts', a system that was implemented gradually in the 1980s to improve local governance.
sentence_388: The [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|boroughs]] are responsible for many activities that had previously been run by the central city.
sentence_389: In 2010, the number of [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|Amsterdam boroughs]] reached fifteen.
sentence_390: Fourteen of those had their own district council (deelraad), elected by a popular vote.
sentence_391: The fifteenth, [[Westpoort|Westpoort]], covers the harbour of Amsterdam and had very few residents.
sentence_392: Therefore, it was governed by the central municipal council.
sentence_393: Under the borough system, municipal decisions are made at borough level, except for those affairs pertaining to the whole city such as major infrastructure projects, which are the jurisdiction of the central municipal authorities.
sentence_394: In 2010, the [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|borough]] system was restructured, in which many smaller boroughs merged into larger boroughs.
sentence_395: In 2014, under a reform of the Dutch Municipalities Act, the [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|Amsterdam boroughs]] lost much of their autonomous status, as their district councils were abolished.
sentence_396: The municipal council of Amsterdam voted to maintain the borough system by replacing the district councils with smaller, but still directly elected district committees (bestuurscommissies).
sentence_397: Under a municipal ordinance, the new district committees were granted responsibilities through delegation of regulatory and executive powers by the central municipal council.
sentence_398: "Amsterdam" is usually understood to refer to the municipality of Amsterdam.
sentence_399: Colloquially, some areas within the municipality, such as the town of [[Durgerdam|Durgerdam]], may not be considered part of Amsterdam.
sentence_400: [[Statistics_Netherlands|Statistics Netherlands]] uses three other definitions of Amsterdam: metropolitan agglomeration Amsterdam (Grootstedelijke Agglomeratie Amsterdam, not to be confused with Grootstedelijk Gebied Amsterdam, a synonym of Groot Amsterdam), Greater Amsterdam (Groot Amsterdam, a [[COROP|COROP]] region) and the urban region Amsterdam (Stadsgewest Amsterdam).
sentence_401: The Amsterdam Department for Research and Statistics uses a fourth conurbation, namely the Stadsregio Amsterdam ('City Region of Amsterdam').
sentence_402: The city region is similar to Greater Amsterdam but includes the municipalities of [[Zaanstad|Zaanstad]] and [[Wormerland|Wormerland]].
sentence_403: It excludes [[Graft-De_Rijp|Graft-De Rijp]].
sentence_404: The smallest of these areas is the municipality of Amsterdam with a population of 802,938 in 2013.
sentence_405: The conurbation had a population of 1,096,042 in 2013.
sentence_406: It includes the municipalities of Zaanstad, Wormerland, Oostzaan, Diemen and Amstelveen only, as well as the municipality of Amsterdam.
sentence_407: Greater Amsterdam includes 15 municipalities, and had a population of 1,293,208 in 2013.
sentence_408: Though much larger in area, the population of this area is only slightly larger, because the definition excludes the relatively populous municipality of [[Zaanstad|Zaanstad]].
sentence_409: The largest area by population, the [[Amsterdam_Metropolitan_Area|Amsterdam Metropolitan Area]] (Dutch: Metropoolregio Amsterdam), has a population of 2,33 million.
sentence_410: It includes for instance Zaanstad, Wormerland, Muiden, Abcoude, Haarlem, Almere and Lelystad but excludes Graft-De Rijp.
sentence_411: Amsterdam is part of the conglomerate metropolitan area [[Randstad|Randstad]], with a total population of 6,659,300 inhabitants.
sentence_412: Of these various metropolitan area configurations, only the Stadsregio Amsterdam (City Region of Amsterdam) has a formal governmental status.
sentence_413: Its responsibilities include regional spatial planning and the metropolitan public transport concessions.
sentence_414: Main article: [[Capital_of_the_Netherlands|Capital of the Netherlands]]
sentence_415: Under the Dutch Constitution, Amsterdam is the [[Capital_of_the_Netherlands|capital of the Netherlands]].
sentence_416: Since the 1983 constitutional revision, the constitution mentions "Amsterdam" and "capital" in chapter 2, article 32: The king's confirmation by oath and his coronation take place in "the capital Amsterdam" ("de hoofdstad Amsterdam").
sentence_417: Previous versions of the constitution only mentioned "the city of Amsterdam" ("de stad Amsterdam").
sentence_418: For a royal investiture, therefore, the [[States_General_of_the_Netherlands|States General of the Netherlands]] (the Dutch Parliament) meets for a ceremonial joint session in Amsterdam.
sentence_419: The ceremony traditionally takes place at the [[Nieuwe_Kerk_(Amsterdam)|Nieuwe Kerk]] on Dam Square, immediately after the former monarch has signed the act of abdication at the nearby [[Royal_Palace_of_Amsterdam|Royal Palace of Amsterdam]].
sentence_420: Normally, however, the Parliament sits in [[The_Hague|The Hague]], the city which has historically been the seat of the Dutch government, the [[Monarchy_of_the_Netherlands|Dutch monarchy]], and the [[Supreme_Court_of_the_Netherlands|Dutch supreme court]].
sentence_421: Foreign embassies are also located in The Hague.
sentence_422: Main articles: [[Coat_of_arms_of_Amsterdam|Coat of arms of Amsterdam]] and [[Flag_of_Amsterdam|Flag of Amsterdam]]
sentence_423: The coat of arms of Amsterdam is composed of several historical elements.
sentence_424: First and centre are three [[Saltire|St Andrew's crosses]], aligned in a vertical band on the city's shield (although Amsterdam's [[Patron_saint|patron saint]] was [[Saint_Nicholas|Saint Nicholas]]).
sentence_425: These St Andrew's crosses can also be found on the city shields of neighbours [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]] and [[Ouder-Amstel|Ouder-Amstel]].
sentence_426: This part of the coat of arms is the basis of the [[Flag_of_Amsterdam|flag of Amsterdam]], flown by the city government, but also as [[Civil_ensign|civil ensign]] for ships registered in Amsterdam.
sentence_427: Second is the [[Imperial_Crown_of_Austria|Imperial Crown of Austria]].
sentence_428: In 1489, out of gratitude for services and loans, [[Maximilian_I,_Holy_Roman_Emperor|Maximilian I]] awarded Amsterdam the right to adorn its coat of arms with the [[King_of_the_Romans|king's]] crown.
sentence_429: Then, in 1508, this was replaced with Maximilian's [[Imperial_crown|imperial crown]] when he was crowned [[Holy_Roman_Emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]].
sentence_430: In the early years of the 17th century, Maximilian's crown in Amsterdam's coat of arms was again replaced, this time with the crown of Emperor Rudolph II, a crown that became the Imperial [[Austrian_Crown_Jewels|Crown of Austria]].
sentence_431: The lions date from the late 16th century, when city and province became part of the [[Dutch_Republic|Republic of the Seven United Netherlands]].
sentence_432: Last came the city's official motto: Heldhaftig, Vastberaden, Barmhartig ("Heroic, Determined, Merciful"), bestowed on the city in 1947 by [[Wilhelmina_of_the_Netherlands|Queen Wilhelmina]], in recognition of the city's bravery during the Second World War.
sentence_433: Main article: [[Transport_in_Amsterdam|Transport in Amsterdam]]
sentence_434: Main articles: [[Amsterdam_Metro|Amsterdam Metro]] and [[Trams_in_Amsterdam|Trams in Amsterdam]]
sentence_435: Currently, there are sixteen [[Trams_in_Amsterdam|tram routes]] and five [[Amsterdam_Metro|metro routes]].
sentence_436: All are operated by municipal public transport operator Gemeentelijk Vervoerbedrijf (GVB), which also runs the city bus network.
sentence_437: Four fare-free GVB ferries carry pedestrians and cyclists across the [[IJ_(Amsterdam)|IJ lake]] to the [[Boroughs_of_Amsterdam|borough]] of [[Amsterdam-Noord|Amsterdam-Noord]], and two fare-charging ferries run east and west along the harbour.
sentence_438: There are also privately operated water taxis, a water bus, a boat sharing operation, electric rental boats and canal cruises, that transport people along Amsterdam's waterways.
sentence_439: Regional buses, and some suburban buses, are operated by [[Connexxion|Connexxion]] and [[Egged_(company)|EBS]].
sentence_440: International coach services are provided by [[Eurolines|Eurolines]] from [[Amsterdam_Amstel_railway_station|Amsterdam Amstel railway station]], [[IDBUS|IDBUS]] from Amsterdam Sloterdijk railway station, and [[Megabus_(Europe)|Megabus]] from the Zuiderzeeweg in the east of the city.
sentence_441: In order to facilitate easier transport to the centre of Amsterdam, the city has various P+R Locations where people can park their car at an affordable price and transfer to one of the numerous public transport lines.
sentence_442: Amsterdam was intended in 1932 to be the hub, a kind of Kilometre Zero, of the [[List_of_motorways_in_the_Netherlands|highway system of the Netherlands]], with freeways numbered One to Eight planned to originate from the city.
sentence_443: The outbreak of the Second World War and shifting priorities led to the current situation, where only roads [[A1_motorway_(Netherlands)|A1]], [[A2_motorway_(Netherlands)|A2]], and [[A4_motorway_(Netherlands)|A4]] originate from Amsterdam according to the original plan.
sentence_444: The A3 to [[Rotterdam|Rotterdam]] was cancelled in 1970 in order to conserve the Groene Hart.
sentence_445: Road [[A8_motorway_(Netherlands)|A8]], leading north to [[Zaandam|Zaandam]] and the [[A10_motorway_(Netherlands)|A10]] [[Beltway|Ringroad]] were opened between 1968 and 1974.
sentence_446: Besides the A1, A2, A4 and A8, several freeways, such as the [[A7_motorway_(Netherlands)|A7]] and [[A6_motorway_(Netherlands)|A6]], carry traffic mainly bound for Amsterdam.
sentence_447: The [[A10_motorway_(Netherlands)|A10 ringroad]] surrounding the city connects Amsterdam with the Dutch [[List_of_motorways_in_the_Netherlands|national network of freeways]].
sentence_448: [[Interchange_(road)|Interchanges]] on the A10 allow cars to enter the city by transferring to one of the 18 city roads, numbered S101 through to S118.
sentence_449: These city roads are regional roads without grade separation, and sometimes without a central reservation.
sentence_450: Most are accessible by cyclists.
sentence_451: The S100 Centrumring is a smaller ringroad circumnavigating the city's centre.
sentence_452: In the city centre, driving a car is discouraged.
sentence_453: Parking fees are expensive, and many streets are closed to cars or are [[One-way_traffic|one-way]].
sentence_454: The local government sponsors carsharing and [[Carpool|carpooling]] initiatives such as Autodelen and Meerijden.nu.
sentence_455: The local government has also started removing parking spaces in the city, with the goal of removing 10,000 spaces (roughly 1,500 per year) by 2025
sentence_456: Amsterdam is served by ten [[Railway_stations_in_the_Netherlands#A|stations]] of the [[Nederlandse_Spoorwegen|Nederlandse Spoorwegen]] (Dutch Railways).
sentence_457: Five are intercity stops: [[Sloterdijk_(Amsterdam)|Sloterdijk]], [[Amsterdam_Zuid_railway_station|Zuid]], [[Amsterdam_Amstel_railway_station|Amstel]], Bijlmer ArenA and [[Amsterdam_Centraal_railway_station|Amsterdam Centraal]].
sentence_458: The stations for local services are: [[Amsterdam_Lelylaan_railway_station|Lelylaan]], RAI, [[Amsterdam_Holendrecht_railway_station|Holendrecht]], Muiderpoort and [[Amsterdam_Science_Park_railway_station|Science Park]].
sentence_459: [[Amsterdam_Centraal_railway_station|Amsterdam Centraal]] is also an international railway station.
sentence_460: From the station there are regular services to destinations such as Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Czechia, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Russia, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.
sentence_461: Among these trains are international trains of the [[Nederlandse_Spoorwegen|Nederlandse Spoorwegen]] (Amsterdam-Berlin), the [[Eurostar|Eurostar]] (Amsterdam-Brussels-London), [[Thalys|Thalys]] (Amsterdam-Brussels-Paris/Lille), and [[Intercity-Express|Intercity-Express]] (Amsterdam–Cologne–Frankfurt).
sentence_462: [[Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]] is less than 20 minutes by train from [[Amsterdam_Centraal_station|Amsterdam Centraal station]] and is served by domestic and international intercity trains, such as [[Thalys|Thalys]], [[Eurostar|Eurostar]] and Intercity Brussel.
sentence_463: Schiphol is the largest airport in the Netherlands, the third-largest in Europe, and the 14th-largest in the world in terms of passengers.
sentence_464: It handles over 68 million passengers per year and is the home base of four airlines, [[KLM|KLM]], [[Transavia|Transavia]], [[Martinair|Martinair]] and [[Arkefly|Arkefly]].
sentence_465: As of 2014, Schiphol was the fifth busiest airport in the world measured by international passenger numbers.
sentence_466: This airport is 4 meters below sea level.
sentence_467: Although Schiphol is internationally known as Amsterdam Schiphol Airport it actually lies in the neighbouring municipality of Haarlemmermeer, southwest of the city.
sentence_468: Main article: [[Cycling_in_Amsterdam|Cycling in Amsterdam]]
sentence_469: Amsterdam is one of the most bicycle-friendly large cities in the world and is a centre of [[Bicycle_culture|bicycle culture]] with good facilities for cyclists such as bike paths and [[Bicycle_stand|bike racks]], and several guarded bike storage garages (fietsenstalling) which can be used.
sentence_470: According to the most recent figures published by Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS), in 2015 the 442.693 households (850.000 residents) in Amsterdam together owned 847.000 bicycles – 1.91 bicycle per household.
sentence_471: Previously, wildly different figures were arrived at using a [[Wisdom_of_the_crowd|Wisdom of the crowd]] approach.
sentence_472: Theft is widespread—in 2011, about 83,000 bicycles were stolen in Amsterdam.
sentence_473: Bicycles are used by all socio-economic groups because of their convenience, Amsterdam's small size, the 400 kilometres (249 miles) of bike paths, the flat terrain, and the inconvenience of driving an automobile.
sentence_474: Amsterdam has two universities: the [[University_of_Amsterdam|University of Amsterdam]] (Universiteit van Amsterdam, UvA), and the [[Vrije_Universiteit_Amsterdam|Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] (VU).
sentence_475: Other institutions for higher education include an [[Art_school|art school]] – [[Gerrit_Rietveld_Academie|Gerrit Rietveld Academie]], a university of applied sciences – the [[Hogeschool_van_Amsterdam|Hogeschool van Amsterdam]], and the [[Amsterdamse_Hogeschool_voor_de_Kunsten|Amsterdamse Hogeschool voor de Kunsten]].
sentence_476: Amsterdam's [[International_Institute_of_Social_History|International Institute of Social History]] is one of the world's largest documentary and research institutions concerning [[Social_history|social history]], and especially the [[Labor_history_(discipline)|history of the labour movement]].
sentence_477: Amsterdam's [[Hortus_Botanicus_(Amsterdam)|Hortus Botanicus]], founded in the early 17th century, is one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world, with many old and rare specimens, among them the [[Coffee|coffee plant]] that served as the parent for the entire coffee culture in Central and South America.
sentence_478: There are over 200 primary schools in Amsterdam.
sentence_479: Some of these primary schools base their teachings on particular pedagogic theories like the various [[Maria_Montessori|Montessori]] schools.
sentence_480: The biggest Montessori high school in Amsterdam is the [[Montessori_Lyceum_Amsterdam|Montessori Lyceum Amsterdam]].
sentence_481: Many schools, however, are based on religion.
sentence_482: This used to be primarily Roman Catholicism and various Protestant denominations, but with the influx of Muslim immigrants, there has been a rise in the number of Islamic schools.
sentence_483: Jewish schools can be found in the southern suburbs of Amsterdam.
sentence_484: Amsterdam is noted for having five independent grammar schools (Dutch: gymnasia), the Vossius Gymnasium, [[Barlaeus_Gymnasium|Barlaeus Gymnasium]], St. [[Ignatius_Gymnasium|Ignatius Gymnasium]], [[Het_4e_Gymnasium|Het 4e Gymnasium]] and the Cygnus Gymnasium where a classical curriculum including [[Latin|Latin]] and classical Greek is taught.
sentence_485: Though believed until recently by many to be an anachronistic and elitist concept that would soon die out, the gymnasia have recently experienced a revival, leading to the formation of a fourth and fifth grammar school in which the three aforementioned schools participate.
sentence_486: Most secondary schools in Amsterdam offer a variety of different levels of education in the same school.
sentence_487: The city also has various colleges ranging from art and design to politics and economics which are mostly also available for students coming from other countries.
sentence_488: Schools for foreign nationals in Amsterdam include the [[Amsterdam_International_Community_School|Amsterdam International Community School]], [[British_School_of_Amsterdam|British School of Amsterdam]], Albert Einstein International School Amsterdam, [[Lycée_Vincent_van_Gogh_La_Haye-Amsterdam|Lycée Vincent van Gogh La Haye-Amsterdam]] primary campus (French school), [[International_School_of_Amsterdam|International School of Amsterdam]], and the [[Japanese_School_of_Amsterdam|Japanese School of Amsterdam]].
sentence_489: Main article: [[List_of_people_from_Amsterdam|List of people from Amsterdam]]
sentence_490: Amsterdam is a prominent centre for national and international media.
sentence_491: Some locally based newspapers include [[Het_Parool|Het Parool]], a national daily paper; De Telegraaf, the largest Dutch daily newspaper; the daily newspapers [[Trouw|Trouw]], [[De_Volkskrant|de Volkskrant]] and [[NRC_Handelsblad|NRC Handelsblad]]; [[De_Groene_Amsterdammer|De Groene Amsterdammer]], a weekly newspaper; the free newspapers [[Metro_(Dutch_newspaper)|Metro]] and The Holland Times (printed in English).
sentence_492: Amsterdam is home to the second-largest Dutch commercial TV group SBS Broadcasting Group, consisting of TV-stations [[SBS_6|SBS 6]], [[Net_5|Net 5]] and [[Veronica_(TV_channel)|Veronica]].
sentence_493: However, Amsterdam is not considered 'the media city of the Netherlands'.
sentence_494: The town of [[Hilversum|Hilversum]], 30 kilometres (19 miles) south-east of Amsterdam, has been crowned with this unofficial title.
sentence_495: Hilversum is the principal centre for radio and television broadcasting in the Netherlands.
sentence_496: [[Radio_Netherlands_Worldwide|Radio Netherlands]], heard worldwide via shortwave radio since the 1920s, is also based there.
sentence_497: Hilversum is home to an extensive complex of audio and television studios belonging to the national broadcast production company NOS, as well as to the studios and offices of all the Dutch public broadcasting organisations and many commercial TV production companies.
sentence_498: In 2012, the music video of Far East Movement, 'Live My Life', was filmed in various parts of Amsterdam.
sentence_499: Also, several movies were filmed in Amsterdam, such as [[James_Bond|James Bond]]'s [[Diamonds_Are_Forever_(film)|Diamonds Are Forever]], [[Ocean's_Twelve|Ocean's Twelve]], [[Girl_with_a_Pearl_Earring_(film)|Girl with a Pearl Earring]] and [[The_Hitman's_Bodyguard|The Hitman's Bodyguard]].
sentence_500: Amsterdam is also featured in [[John_Green_(author)|John Green]]'s book [[The_Fault_in_Our_Stars|The Fault in Our Stars]], which has been made into [[The_Fault_in_Our_Stars_(film)|a film]] as well that partly takes place in Amsterdam.
sentence_501: The housing market is heavily regulated.
sentence_502: The increased influx of migrants, especially since the Syrian Civil War (2011–present), has been burdensome, economically and culturally, but the government deals with citizen and migrant cases for housing equally.
sentence_503: According to the Netherlands' Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, "60% of housing stock is controlled by housing corporations.
sentence_504: No different treatment for migrant groups".
sentence_505: From the late 1960s onwards many buildings in Amsterdam have been [[Squatting|squatted]] both for housing and for using as social centres.
sentence_506: A number of these squats have legalised and become well known, such as [[OCCII|OCCII]], [[OT301|OT301]], [[Paradiso_(Amsterdam)|Paradiso]] and [[Vrankrijk|Vrankrijk]].

title: British Columbia
sentence_0: British Columbia (BC) is the westernmost [[Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada|province in Canada]], between the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]] and the [[Rocky_Mountains|Rocky Mountains]].
sentence_1: With an estimated population of 5.1 million as of 2020, it is Canada's [[Population_of_Canada_by_province_and_territory|third-most populous province]].
sentence_2: The capital of British Columbia is [[Victoria,_British_Columbia|Victoria]], the [[List_of_census_metropolitan_areas_and_agglomerations_in_Canada|fifteenth-largest metropolitan region]] in Canada, named for [[Queen_Victoria|Queen Victoria]], who ruled during the creation of the original colonies.
sentence_3: The largest city is [[Vancouver|Vancouver]], the third-largest [[Metropolitan_area|metropolitan area]] in Canada, the largest in [[Western_Canada|Western Canada]], and the second-largest in the [[Pacific_Northwest|Pacific Northwest]].
sentence_4: In October 2013, British Columbia had an estimated population of 4,606,371 (about 2.5 million of whom were in [[Greater_Vancouver|Greater Vancouver]]).
sentence_5: The province is currently governed by the British Columbia New Democratic Party, led by [[John_Horgan|John Horgan]] with a majority government.
sentence_6: The first [[British_people|British]] settlement in the area was [[Fort_Victoria_(British_Columbia)|Fort Victoria]], established in 1843, which gave rise to the [[Victoria,_British_Columbia|City of Victoria]], at first the capital of the separate Colony of Vancouver Island.
sentence_7: Subsequently, on the mainland, the [[Colony_of_British_Columbia_(1858–1866)|Colony of British Columbia (1858–1866)]] was founded by [[Richard_Clement_Moody|Richard Clement Moody]] and the [[Royal_Engineers,_Columbia_Detachment|Royal Engineers, Columbia Detachment]], in response to the [[Fraser_Canyon_Gold_Rush|Fraser Canyon Gold Rush]].
sentence_8: Moody was Chief Commissioner of Lands and Works for the Colony and the first [[Lieutenant_Governor_of_British_Columbia|Lieutenant Governor of British Columbia]]: he was hand-picked by the [[Colonial_Office|Colonial Office]] in [[London|London]] to transform British Columbia into the [[British_Empire|British Empire]]'s "bulwark in the farthest west", and "to found a second England on the shores of the Pacific".
sentence_9: Moody selected the site for and founded the original capital of British Columbia, [[New_Westminster|New Westminster]], established the [[Cariboo_Road|Cariboo Road]] and [[Stanley_Park|Stanley Park]], and designed the first version of the [[Coat_of_arms_of_British_Columbia|coat of arms of British Columbia]].
sentence_10: [[Port_Moody|Port Moody]] is named after him.
sentence_11: In 1866, [[Vancouver_Island|Vancouver Island]] became part of the colony of British Columbia, and Victoria became the united colony's capital.
sentence_12: In 1871, British Columbia became the sixth province of Canada.
sentence_13: Its [[Latin|Latin]] motto is Splendor sine occasu ("Splendour without Diminishment").
sentence_14: British Columbia evolved from British possessions that were established in what is now British Columbia by 1871.
sentence_15: [[First_Nations|First Nations]], the original inhabitants of the land, have a history of at least 10,000 years in the area.
sentence_16: Today there are few treaties, and the question of Aboriginal Title, long ignored, has become a legal and political question of frequent debate as a result of recent court actions.
sentence_17: Notably, the Tsilhqot'in Nation has established Aboriginal title to a portion of their territory, as a result of the 2014 [[Supreme_Court_of_Canada|Supreme Court of Canada]] decision in [[Tsilhqot'in_Nation_v_British_Columbia|Tsilhqot'in Nation v British Columbia]].
sentence_18: The province's name was chosen by [[Queen_Victoria|Queen Victoria]], when the [[Colony_of_British_Columbia_(1858–1866)|Colony of British Columbia (1858–1866)]], i.e., "the Mainland", became a British colony in 1858.
sentence_19: It refers to the [[Columbia_District|Columbia District]], the British name for the territory drained by the [[Columbia_River|Columbia River]], in southeastern British Columbia, which was the namesake of the pre-Oregon Treaty [[Columbia_Department|Columbia Department]] of the [[Hudson's_Bay_Company|Hudson's Bay Company]].
sentence_20: Queen Victoria chose British Columbia to distinguish what was the British sector of the Columbia District from the United States ("American Columbia" or "Southern Columbia"), which became the [[Oregon_Territory|Oregon Territory]] on August 8, 1848, as a result of the treaty.
sentence_21: Ultimately, the Columbia in the name British Columbia is derived from the name of the [[Columbia_Rediviva|Columbia Rediviva]], an American ship which lent its name to the [[Columbia_River|Columbia River]] and later the wider region; the Columbia in the name Columbia Rediviva came from [[Columbia_(name)|the name Columbia for the New World or parts thereof]], a reference to [[Christopher_Columbus|Christopher Columbus]].
sentence_22: Main article: Geography of British Columbia
sentence_23: British Columbia is bordered to the west by the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]] and the American state of [[Alaska|Alaska]], to the north by [[Yukon|Yukon]] and the [[Northwest_Territories|Northwest Territories]], to the east by the province of [[Alberta|Alberta]], and to the south by the American states of [[Washington_(state)|Washington]], [[Idaho|Idaho]], and [[Montana|Montana]].
sentence_24: The [[Canada–United_States_border|southern border of British Columbia]] was established by the 1846 Oregon Treaty, although its history is tied with lands as far south as [[California|California]].
sentence_25: British Columbia's land area is 944,735 square kilometres (364,800 sq mi).
sentence_26: British Columbia's rugged coastline stretches for more than 27,000 kilometres (17,000 mi), and includes deep, mountainous fjords and about 6,000 islands, most of which are uninhabited.
sentence_27: It is the only province in Canada that borders the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]].
sentence_28: British Columbia's capital is [[Victoria,_British_Columbia|Victoria]], located at the southeastern tip of [[Vancouver_Island|Vancouver Island]].
sentence_29: Only a narrow strip of Vancouver Island, from [[Campbell_River,_British_Columbia|Campbell River]] to Victoria, is significantly populated.
sentence_30: Much of the western part of Vancouver Island and the rest of the coast is covered by [[Temperate_rainforest|temperate rainforest]].
sentence_31: The province's most populous city is Vancouver, which is at the confluence of the [[Fraser_River|Fraser River]] and [[Georgia_Strait|Georgia Strait]], in the mainland's southwest corner (an area often called the [[Lower_Mainland|Lower Mainland]]).
sentence_32: By land area, [[Abbotsford,_British_Columbia|Abbotsford]] is the largest city.
sentence_33: [[Vanderhoof,_British_Columbia|Vanderhoof]] is near the geographic centre of the province.
sentence_34: The [[Coast_Mountains|Coast Mountains]] and the Inside Passage's many [[Fjord|inlets]] provide some of British Columbia's renowned and spectacular scenery, which forms the backdrop and context for a growing outdoor adventure and [[Ecotourism|ecotourism]] industry.
sentence_35: 75% of the province is mountainous (more than 1,000 metres (3,300 ft) above sea level); 60% is forested; and only about 5% is arable.
sentence_36: The province's mainland away from the coastal regions is somewhat moderated by the Pacific Ocean.
sentence_37: Terrain ranges from dry inland forests and [[Semi-arid_climate|semi-arid]] valleys, to the range and canyon districts of the Central and Southern Interior, to boreal forest and subarctic prairie in the Northern Interior.
sentence_38: High mountain regions both north and south have [[Montane_ecosystems#Subalpine_zone|subalpine flora]] and [[Subalpine_climate|subalpine climate]].
sentence_39: The [[Okanagan_Valley_(wine_region)|Okanagan wine area]], extending from Vernon to [[Osoyoos,_British_Columbia|Osoyoos]] at the United States border, is one of several wine and cider-producing regions in Canada.
sentence_40: Other wine regions in British Columbia include the [[Cowichan_Valley|Cowichan Valley]] on Vancouver Island and the [[Fraser_Valley|Fraser Valley]].
sentence_41: The Southern Interior cities of [[Kamloops|Kamloops]] and Penticton have some of the warmest and longest summer climates in Canada (while higher elevations are cold and snowy), although their temperatures are often exceeded north of the [[Fraser_Canyon|Fraser Canyon]], close to the confluence of the Fraser and [[Thompson_River|Thompson]] rivers, where the terrain is rugged and covered with desert-type flora.
sentence_42: Semi-desert grassland is found in large areas of the [[Interior_Plateau|Interior Plateau]], with land uses ranging from ranching at lower altitudes to forestry at higher ones.
sentence_43: The northern, mostly mountainous, two-thirds of the province is largely unpopulated and undeveloped, except for the area east of the Rockies, where the [[Peace_River_Country|Peace River Country]] contains BC's portion of the [[Canadian_Prairies|Canadian Prairies]], centred at the city of [[Dawson_Creek,_British_Columbia|Dawson Creek]].
sentence_44: British Columbia is considered part of the [[Pacific_Northwest|Pacific Northwest]] and the [[Cascadia_(bioregion)|Cascadia bioregion]], along with the [[U.S._state|American states]] of [[Alaska|Alaska]], [[Idaho|Idaho]], (western) [[Montana|Montana]], [[Oregon|Oregon]], [[Washington_(state)|Washington]], and (northern) [[Northern_California|California]].
sentence_45: Because of the many mountain ranges and rugged coastline, British Columbia's climate varies dramatically across the province.
sentence_46: Coastal southern British Columbia has a mild, rainy oceanic climate, influenced by the [[North_Pacific_Current|North Pacific Current]], which has its origins in the [[Kuroshio_Current|Kuroshio Current]].
sentence_47: [[Henderson_Lake_(British_Columbia)|Henderson Lake]] on [[Vancouver_Island|Vancouver Island]] receives an average of 6,903 mm (271.8 in) of rain annually, and some parts of the area are even classified as warm-summer [[Mediterranean_climate|Mediterranean]], the northernmost occurrence in the world.
sentence_48: In [[Victoria,_British_Columbia|Victoria]], the annual average temperature is 11.2 °C (52.2 °F), the warmest in Canada.
sentence_49: Due to the blocking presence of successive mountain ranges, the climate of some of the interior valleys of the province is semi-arid with certain locations receiving less than 250 millimetres (9.8 in) in annual precipitation.
sentence_50: The annual mean temperature in the most populated areas of the province is up to 12 °C (54 °F), the mildest anywhere in Canada.
sentence_51: The valleys of the Southern Interior have short winters with only brief bouts of cold or infrequent heavy snow, while those in the Cariboo, in the [[British_Columbia_Interior#Central_Interior|Central Interior]], are colder because of increased altitude and latitude, but without the intensity or duration experienced at similar latitudes elsewhere in Canada.
sentence_52: For example, the average daily low in [[Prince_George,_British_Columbia|Prince George]] (roughly in the middle of the province) in January is −12 °C (10 °F).
sentence_53: Small towns in the southern interior with high elevation such as [[Princeton,_British_Columbia|Princeton]] are typically colder and snowier than cities in the valleys.
sentence_54: Heavy snowfall occurs in all elevated mountainous terrain providing bases for skiers in both south and central British Columbia.
sentence_55: Annual snowfall on highway mountain passes in the southern interior rival some of the snowiest cities in Canada, and freezing rain and fog are sometimes present on such roads as well.
sentence_56: This can result in hazardous driving conditions, as people are usually travelling between warmer areas such as Vancouver or [[Kamloops,_British_Columbia|Kamloops]], and may be unaware that the conditions may be slippery and cold.
sentence_57: Winters are generally severe in the Northern Interior, but even there, milder air can penetrate far inland.
sentence_58: The coldest temperature in British Columbia was recorded in [[Smith_River,_British_Columbia|Smith River]], where it dropped to −58.9 °C (−74.0 °F) on January 31, 1947, one of the coldest readings recorded anywhere in North America.
sentence_59: Atlin in the province's far northwest, along with the adjoining Southern Lakes region of [[Yukon|Yukon]], get midwinter thaws caused by the [[Chinook_(wind)|Chinook]] effect, which is also common (and much warmer) in more southerly parts of the Interior.
sentence_60: During winter on the coast, rainfall, sometimes relentless heavy rain, dominates because of consistent barrages of cyclonic low-pressure systems from the North Pacific.
sentence_61: Average snowfall on the coast during a normal winter is between 25 and 50 centimetres (9.8 and 19.7 in), but on occasion (and not every winter) heavy snowfalls with more than 20 centimetres (7.9 in) and well below freezing temperatures arrive when modified arctic air reaches coastal areas, typically for short periods, and can take temperatures below −10 °C (14 °F), even at sea level.
sentence_62: Arctic outflow winds can occasionally result in wind chill temperatures at or even below −17.8 °C (0.0 °F)..
sentence_63: While winters are very wet, coastal areas are generally milder and dry during summer under the influence of stable anti-cyclonic high pressure.
sentence_64: Southern Interior valleys are hot in summer; for example, in [[Osoyoos,_British_Columbia|Osoyoos]], the July maximum temperature averages 31.7 °C (89.1 °F), making it the hottest month of any location in Canada; this hot weather sometimes spreads towards the coast or to the far north of the province.
sentence_65: Temperatures often exceed 40 °C (104 °F) in the lower elevations of valleys in the Interior during mid-summer, with the record high of 44.4 °C (111.9 °F) being held in Lytton on July 16, 1941.
sentence_66: The extended summer dryness often creates conditions that spark forest fires, from dry-lightning or man-made causes.
sentence_67: Many areas of the province are often covered by a blanket of heavy cloud and low fog during the winter months, in contrast to abundant summer sunshine.
sentence_68: Annual sunshine hours vary from 2200 near Cranbrook and Victoria to less than 1300 in [[Prince_Rupert,_British_Columbia|Prince Rupert]], on the [[British_Columbia_Coast#North_Coast|North Coast]] just south of [[Southeast_Alaska|Southeast Alaska]].
sentence_69: The exception to British Columbia's wet and cloudy winters is during the [[El_Niño|El Niño]] phase.
sentence_70: During El Niño events, the jet stream is much farther south across North America, making the province's winters milder and drier than normal.
sentence_71: Winters are much wetter and cooler during the opposite phase, [[La_Niña|La Niña]].
