sentence_2: Asia ([[English|/ˈeɪʒə, ˈeɪʃə/]] (listen)) is Earth's largest and most populous [[Continent|continent]], located primarily in the [[Eastern_Hemisphere|Eastern]] and Northern [[Hemisphere_of_the_Earth|Hemispheres]].
sentence_3: It shares the continental [[Landmass|landmass]] of [[Eurasia|Eurasia]] with the continent of [[Europe|Europe]] and the continental landmass of [[Afro-Eurasia|Afro-Eurasia]] with both Europe and [[Africa|Africa]].
sentence_4: Asia covers an area of 44,579,000 square kilometres (17,212,000 sq mi), about 30% of Earth's total land area and 8.7% of the Earth's total surface area.
sentence_5: The continent, which has long been home to the majority of the human population, was the site of many of the [[First_civilization|first civilizations]].
sentence_6: Asia is notable for not only its overall large size and population, but also dense and large settlements, as well as vast barely populated regions.
sentence_7: Its 4.5 billion people (as of June 2019) constitute roughly 60% of the world's population.
sentence_8: In general terms, Asia is bounded on the east by the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]], on the south by the [[Indian_Ocean|Indian Ocean]], and on the north by the [[Arctic_Ocean|Arctic Ocean]].
sentence_9: The border of Asia with Europe is a historical and [[Cultural_construct|cultural construct]], as there is no clear physical and geographical separation between them.
sentence_10: It is somewhat arbitrary and has moved since its first conception in [[Classical_antiquity|classical antiquity]].
sentence_11: The division of Eurasia into two continents reflects [[East–West_dichotomy|East–West]] cultural, linguistic, and ethnic differences, some of which vary on a spectrum rather than with a sharp dividing line.
sentence_12: The most commonly accepted boundaries place Asia to the east of the [[Suez_Canal|Suez Canal]] separating it from Africa; and to the east of the [[Turkish_Straits|Turkish Straits]], the [[Ural_Mountains|Ural Mountains]] and [[Ural_River|Ural River]], and to the south of the Caucasus Mountains and the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian]] and [[Black_Sea|Black Seas]], separating it from Europe.
sentence_13: [[China|China]] and [[India|India]] alternated in being the [[List_of_regions_by_past_GDP_(PPP)|largest economies in the world]] from 1 to 1800 CE.
sentence_14: China was a major economic power and attracted many to the east, and for many the legendary wealth and prosperity of the ancient culture of India personified Asia, attracting European commerce, exploration and colonialism.
sentence_15: The accidental discovery of a trans-Atlantic route from Europe to America by Columbus while in search for a route to India demonstrates this deep fascination.
sentence_16: The [[Silk_Road|Silk Road]] became the main east–west trading route in the Asian hinterlands while the [[Strait_of_Malacca|Straits of Malacca]] stood as a major sea route.
sentence_17: Asia has exhibited economic dynamism (particularly East Asia) as well as robust population growth during the 20th century, but overall population growth has since fallen.
sentence_18: Asia was the birthplace of most of the world's mainstream religions including [[Hinduism|Hinduism]], [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]], Judaism, [[Jainism|Jainism]], [[Buddhism|Buddhism]], [[Confucianism|Confucianism]], [[Taoism|Taoism]], [[Christianity|Christianity]], [[Islam|Islam]], [[Sikhism|Sikhism]], as well as many other religions.
sentence_19: Given its size and diversity, the concept of Asia—a [[Toponymy|name]] dating back to [[Classical_antiquity|classical antiquity]]—may actually have more to do with [[Human_geography|human geography]] than [[Physical_geography|physical geography]].
sentence_20: Asia varies greatly across and within [[Regions_of_Asia|its regions]] with regard to ethnic groups, cultures, environments, economics, historical ties and government systems.
sentence_21: It also has a mix of many different climates ranging from the equatorial south via the hot desert in the Middle East, temperate areas in the east and the continental centre to vast subarctic and polar areas in [[Siberia|Siberia]].
sentence_22: Further information on Asian borders: [[Geography_of_Asia#Boundary|Geography of Asia § Boundary]], [[Boundaries_between_continents|Boundaries between continents]], [[List_of_transcontinental_countries#Asia_and_Europe|List of transcontinental countries § Asia and Europe]], and Copenhagen criteria
sentence_23: The boundary between Asia and Africa is the [[Red_Sea|Red Sea]], the [[Gulf_of_Suez|Gulf of Suez]], and the [[Suez_Canal|Suez Canal]].
sentence_24: This makes Egypt a transcontinental country, with the [[Sinai_peninsula|Sinai peninsula]] in Asia and the remainder of the country in Africa.
sentence_25: The threefold division of the Old World into Europe, Asia and Africa has been in use since the 6th century BC, due to [[Greek_geographers|Greek geographers]] such as [[Anaximander|Anaximander]] and [[Hecataeus_of_Miletus|Hecataeus]].
sentence_26: Anaximander placed the boundary between Asia and Europe along the [[Phasis_River|Phasis River]] (the modern Rioni river) in [[Georgia_(country)|Georgia]] of Caucasus (from its mouth by [[Poti|Poti]] on the [[Black_Sea|Black Sea]] coast, through the Surami Pass and along the [[Kura_(Caspian_Sea)|Kura River]] to the Caspian Sea), a convention still followed by [[Herodotus|Herodotus]] in the 5th century BC.
sentence_27: During the [[Hellenistic_period|Hellenistic period]], this convention was revised, and the boundary between Europe and Asia was now considered to be the [[Don_River_(Russia)|Tanais]] (the modern Don River).
sentence_28: This is the convention used by Roman era authors such as [[Posidonius|Posidonius]], [[Strabo|Strabo]] and [[Ptolemy|Ptolemy]].
sentence_29: The border between Asia and Europe was historically defined by European academics.
sentence_30: The [[Don_River_(Russia)|Don River]] became unsatisfactory to northern Europeans when Peter the Great, king of the [[Tsardom_of_Russia|Tsardom of Russia]], defeating rival claims of [[Sweden|Sweden]] and the [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]] to the eastern lands, and armed resistance by the tribes of [[Siberia|Siberia]], synthesized a new [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] extending to the [[Ural_Mountains|Ural Mountains]] and beyond, founded in 1721.
sentence_31: The major geographical theorist of the empire was a former Swedish prisoner-of-war, taken at the [[Battle_of_Poltava|Battle of Poltava]] in 1709 and assigned to [[Tobolsk|Tobolsk]], where he associated with Peter's Siberian official, [[Vasily_Tatishchev|Vasily Tatishchev]], and was allowed freedom to conduct geographical and anthropological studies in preparation for a future book.
sentence_32: In Sweden, five years after Peter's death, in 1730 [[Philip_Johan_von_Strahlenberg|Philip Johan von Strahlenberg]] published a new atlas proposing the Ural Mountains as the border of Asia.
sentence_33: Tatishchev announced that he had proposed the idea to von Strahlenberg.
sentence_34: The latter had suggested the [[Emba_River|Emba River]] as the lower boundary.
sentence_35: Over the next century various proposals were made until the [[Ural_River|Ural River]] prevailed in the mid-19th century.
sentence_36: The border had been moved perforce from the Black Sea to the Caspian Sea into which the Ural River projects.
sentence_37: The border between the Black Sea and the Caspian is usually placed along the crest of the Caucasus Mountains, although it is sometimes placed further north.
sentence_38: The border between Asia and the region of [[Oceania|Oceania]] is usually placed somewhere in the [[Malay_Archipelago|Malay Archipelago]].
sentence_39: The [[Maluku_Islands|Maluku Islands]] in Indonesia are often considered to lie on the border of southeast Asia, with [[New_Guinea|New Guinea]], to the east of the islands, being wholly part of Oceania.
sentence_40: The terms Southeast Asia and Oceania, devised in the 19th century, have had several vastly different geographic meanings since their inception.
sentence_41: The chief factor in determining which islands of the Malay Archipelago are Asian has been the location of the colonial possessions of the various empires there (not all European).
sentence_42: Lewis and Wigen assert, "The narrowing of 'Southeast Asia' to its present boundaries was thus a gradual process."
sentence_43: Geographical Asia is a cultural artifact of European conceptions of the world, beginning with the [[Ancient_Greece|Ancient Greeks]], being imposed onto other cultures, an imprecise concept causing endemic contention about what it means.
sentence_44: Asia does not exactly correspond to the cultural borders of its various types of constituents.
sentence_45: From the time of [[Herodotus|Herodotus]] a minority of geographers have rejected the three-continent system (Europe, Africa, Asia) on the grounds that there is no substantial physical separation between them.
sentence_46: For example, Sir [[Barry_Cunliffe|Barry Cunliffe]], the emeritus professor of European archeology at Oxford, argues that Europe has been geographically and culturally merely "the western excrescence of the continent of Asia".
sentence_47: Geographically, Asia is the major eastern constituent of the continent of [[Eurasia|Eurasia]] with Europe being a northwestern [[Peninsula|peninsula]] of the landmass.
sentence_48: Asia, Europe and Africa make up a single continuous landmass—[[Afro-Eurasia|Afro-Eurasia]] (except for the Suez Canal)—and share a common [[Continental_shelf|continental shelf]].
sentence_49: Almost all of Europe and the better part of Asia sit atop the Eurasian Plate, adjoined on the south by the [[Arabian_Plate|Arabian]] and [[Indian_Plate|Indian Plate]] and with the easternmost part of Siberia (east of the [[Chersky_Range|Chersky Range]]) on the [[North_American_Plate|North American Plate]].
sentence_50: The idea of a place called "Asia" was originally a concept of [[Greek_civilization|Greek civilization]], though this might not correspond to the entire continent currently known by that name.
sentence_51: The English word comes from Latin literature, where it has the same form, "Asia".
sentence_52: Whether "Asia" in other languages comes from Latin of the [[Roman_Empire|Roman Empire]] is much less certain, and the ultimate source of the Latin word is uncertain, though several theories have been published.
sentence_53: One of the first classical writers to use Asia as a name of the whole continent was [[Pliny_the_Elder|Pliny]].
sentence_54: This [[Metonymy|metonymical]] change in meaning is common and can be observed in some other geographical names, such as [[Scandinavia|Scandinavia]] (from [[Scania|Scania]]).
sentence_55: Before Greek poetry, the [[Aegean_Sea|Aegean Sea]] area was in a [[Greek_Dark_Age|Greek Dark Age]], at the beginning of which syllabic writing was lost and alphabetic writing had not begun.
sentence_56: Prior to then in the [[Bronze_Age|Bronze Age]] the records of the [[Assyrian_Empire|Assyrian Empire]], the [[Hittite_Empire|Hittite Empire]] and the various [[Mycenaean_Greece|Mycenaean]] states of Greece mention a region undoubtedly Asia, certainly in Anatolia, including if not identical to Lydia.
sentence_57: These records are administrative and do not include poetry.
sentence_58: The Mycenaean states were destroyed about 1200 BCE by unknown agents although one school of thought assigns the [[Dorian_invasion|Dorian invasion]] to this time.
sentence_59: The burning of the palaces baked clay diurnal administrative records written in a Greek syllabic script called [[Linear_B|Linear B]], deciphered by a number of interested parties, most notably by a young World War II cryptographer, [[Michael_Ventris|Michael Ventris]], subsequently assisted by the scholar, [[John_Chadwick|John Chadwick]].
sentence_60: A major cache discovered by [[Carl_Blegen|Carl Blegen]] at the site of ancient [[Pylos|Pylos]] included hundreds of male and female names formed by different methods.
sentence_61: Some of these are of women held in servitude (as study of the society implied by the content reveals).
sentence_62: They were used in trades, such as cloth-making, and usually came with children.
sentence_63: The epithet lawiaiai, "captives", associated with some of them identifies their origin.
sentence_64: Some are ethnic names.
sentence_65: One in particular, aswiai, identifies "women of Asia".
sentence_66: Perhaps they were captured in Asia, but some others, Milatiai, appear to have been of [[Miletus|Miletus]], a Greek colony, which would not have been raided for slaves by Greeks.
sentence_67: Chadwick suggests that the names record the locations where these foreign women were purchased.
sentence_68: The name is also in the singular, Aswia, which refers both to the name of a country and to a female from there.
sentence_69: There is a masculine form, aswios.
sentence_70: This Aswia appears to have been a remnant of a region known to the Hittites as Assuwa, centered on Lydia, or "Roman Asia".
sentence_71: This name, Assuwa, has been suggested as the origin for the name of the continent "Asia".
sentence_72: The [[Assuwa_league|Assuwa league]] was a confederation of states in western Anatolia, defeated by the [[Hittites|Hittites]] under [[Tudhaliya_I|Tudhaliya I]] around 1400 BCE.
sentence_73: Alternatively, the etymology of the term may be from the [[Akkadian_language|Akkadian]] word (w)aṣû(m), which means 'to go outside' or 'to ascend', referring to the direction of the sun at sunrise in the Middle East and also likely connected with the Phoenician word asa meaning 'east'.
sentence_74: This may be contrasted to a similar etymology proposed for Europe, as being from Akkadian erēbu(m) 'to enter' or 'set' (of the sun).
sentence_75: [[T.R._Reid|T.R.
sentence_76: Reid]] supports this alternative etymology, noting that the ancient Greek name must have derived from asu, meaning 'east' in [[Assyria|Assyrian]] (ereb for Europe meaning 'west').
sentence_77: The ideas of Occidental (form [[Latin|Latin]] occidens 'setting') and Oriental (from Latin oriens for 'rising') are also European invention, synonymous with Western and Eastern.
sentence_78: Reid further emphasizes that it explains the Western point of view of placing all the peoples and cultures of Asia into a single classification, almost as if there were a need for setting the distinction between Western and [[Eastern_world|Eastern civilizations]] on the [[Eurasia|Eurasian]] continent.
sentence_79: Kazuo Ogura and [[Tenshin_Okakura|Tenshin Okakura]] are two outspoken Japanese figures on the subject.
sentence_80: Latin Asia and Greek Ἀσία appear to be the same word.
sentence_81: Roman authors translated Ἀσία as Asia.
sentence_82: The Romans named a province [[Asia_(Roman_province)|Asia]], located in western Anatolia (in modern-day Turkey).
sentence_83: There was an Asia Minor and an Asia Major located in modern-day [[Iraq|Iraq]].
sentence_84: As the earliest evidence of the name is Greek, it is likely circumstantially that Asia came from Ἀσία, but ancient transitions, due to the lack of literary contexts, are difficult to catch in the act.
sentence_85: The most likely vehicles were the ancient geographers and historians, such as [[Herodotus|Herodotus]], who were all Greek.
sentence_86: Ancient Greek certainly evidences early and rich uses of the name.
sentence_87: The first continental use of Asia is attributed to Herodotus (about 440 BCE), not because he innovated it, but because his Histories are the earliest surviving prose to describe it in any detail.
sentence_88: He defines it carefully, mentioning the previous geographers whom he had read, but whose works are now missing.
sentence_89: By it he means [[Anatolia|Anatolia]] and the [[Achaemenid_Empire|Persian Empire]], in contrast to [[Greece|Greece]] and [[Egypt|Egypt]].
sentence_90: Herodotus comments that he is puzzled as to why three women's names were "given to a tract which is in reality one" ([[Europa_(mythology)|Europa]], [[Asia_(mythology)|Asia]], and [[Libya_(mythology)|Libya]], referring to Africa), stating that most Greeks assumed that Asia was named after the wife of [[Prometheus|Prometheus]] (i.e. [[Hesione|Hesione]]), but that the Lydians say it was named after Asies, son of Cotys, who passed the name on to a tribe at Sardis.
sentence_91: In [[Greek_mythology|Greek mythology]], "Asia" (Ἀσία) or "Asie" (Ἀσίη) was the name of a "[[Nymph|Nymph]] or [[Titan_(mythology)|Titan]] goddess of Lydia".
sentence_92: In ancient Greek religion, places were under the care of female divinities, parallel to guardian angels.
sentence_93: The poets detailed their doings and generations in allegoric language salted with entertaining stories, which subsequently playwrights transformed into classical Greek drama and became "Greek mythology".
sentence_94: For example, [[Hesiod|Hesiod]] mentions the daughters of [[Tethys_(mythology)|Tethys]] and [[Oceanus|Ocean]], among whom are a "holy company", "who with the Lord [[Apollo|Apollo]] and the Rivers have youths in their keeping".
sentence_95: Many of these are geographic: Doris, Rhodea, Europa, Asia.
sentence_96: Hesiod explains:
sentence_97: The [[Iliad|Iliad]] (attributed by the ancient Greeks to [[Homer|Homer]]) mentions two Phrygians (the tribe that replaced the [[Luvians|Luvians]] in Lydia) in the [[Trojan_War|Trojan War]] named [[Asius_(mythology)|Asios]] (an adjective meaning "Asian"); and also a marsh or lowland containing a marsh in Lydia as ασιος.
sentence_98: According to many Muslims, the term came from [[Ancient_Egypt|Ancient Egypt]]'s Queen [[Asiya|Asiya]], the adoptive mother of [[Moses|Moses]].
sentence_99: Main article: [[History_of_Asia|History of Asia]]
sentence_100: The history of Asia can be seen as the distinct histories of several peripheral coastal regions: East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, linked by the interior mass of the Central Asian steppes.
sentence_101: The coastal periphery was home to some of the world's earliest known civilizations, each of them developing around fertile river valleys.
sentence_102: The civilizations in Mesopotamia, the [[Indus_Valley|Indus Valley]] and the [[Yellow_River|Yellow River]] shared many similarities.
sentence_103: These civilizations may well have exchanged technologies and ideas such as [[Mathematics|mathematics]] and the [[Wheel|wheel]].
sentence_104: Other innovations, such as writing, seem to have been developed individually in each area.
sentence_105: Cities, states and empires developed in these lowlands.
sentence_106: The central steppe region had long been inhabited by horse-mounted nomads who could reach all areas of Asia from the steppes.
sentence_107: The earliest postulated expansion out of the steppe is that of the [[Proto-Indo-Europeans|Indo-Europeans]], who spread their languages into the Middle East, South Asia, and the borders of China, where the [[Tocharians|Tocharians]] resided.
sentence_108: The northernmost part of Asia, including much of [[Siberia|Siberia]], was largely inaccessible to the steppe nomads, owing to the dense forests, climate and [[Tundra|tundra]].
sentence_109: These areas remained very sparsely populated.
sentence_110: The center and the peripheries were mostly kept separated by mountains and deserts.
sentence_111: The [[Caucasus|Caucasus]] and [[Himalaya|Himalaya]] mountains and the [[Karakum_Desert|Karakum]] and Gobi deserts formed barriers that the steppe horsemen could cross only with difficulty.
sentence_112: While the urban city dwellers were more advanced technologically and socially, in many cases they could do little in a military aspect to defend against the mounted hordes of the steppe.
sentence_113: However, the lowlands did not have enough open grasslands to support a large horsebound force; for this and other reasons, the [[Nomad|nomads]] who conquered states in China, India, and the Middle East often found themselves adapting to the local, more affluent societies.
sentence_114: The Islamic [[Caliphate|Caliphate]]'s defeats of the Byzantine and Persian empires led to West Asia and southern parts of Central Asia and western parts of South Asia under its control during [[Early_Muslim_conquests|its conquests]] of the 7th century.
sentence_115: The [[Mongol_Empire|Mongol Empire]] conquered a large part of Asia in the 13th century, an area extending from China to Europe.
sentence_116: Before the Mongol invasion, [[Song_dynasty|Song dynasty]] reportedly had approximately 120 million citizens; the 1300 census which followed the invasion reported roughly 60 million people.
sentence_117: The [[Black_Death|Black Death]], one of the most devastating [[Pandemic|pandemics]] in human history, is thought to have originated in the arid plains of central Asia, where it then travelled along the [[Silk_Road|Silk Road]].
sentence_118: The [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] began to expand into Asia from the 17th century, and would eventually take control of all of Siberia and most of Central Asia by the end of the 19th century.
sentence_119: The [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]] controlled Anatolia, most of the Middle East, North Africa and the Balkans from the mid 16th century onwards.
sentence_120: In the 17th century, the [[Manchu_people|Manchu]] conquered China and established the [[Qing_dynasty|Qing dynasty]].
sentence_121: The Islamic [[Mughal_Empire|Mughal Empire]] and the Hindu Maratha Empire controlled much of India in the 16th and 18th centuries respectively.
sentence_122: The [[Empire_of_Japan|Empire of Japan]] controlled most of East Asia and much of Southeast Asia, New Guinea and the Pacific islands until the end of [[World_War_II|World War II]].
sentence_123: Main articles: [[Geography_of_Asia|Geography of Asia]] and [[Climate_of_Asia|Climate of Asia]]
sentence_124: See also: :Category:Biota of Asia
sentence_125: Asia is the largest continent on Earth.
sentence_126: It covers 9% of the Earth's total surface area (or 30% of its land area), and has the longest coastline, at 62,800 kilometres (39,022 mi).
sentence_127: Asia is generally defined as comprising the eastern four-fifths of [[Eurasia|Eurasia]].
sentence_128: It is located to the east of the [[Suez_Canal|Suez Canal]] and the [[Ural_Mountains|Ural Mountains]], and south of the Caucasus Mountains (or the [[Kuma–Manych_Depression|Kuma–Manych Depression]]) and the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian]] and [[Black_Sea|Black Seas]].
sentence_129: It is bounded on the east by the Pacific Ocean, on the south by the Indian Ocean and on the north by the Arctic Ocean.
sentence_130: Asia is subdivided into 49 countries, five of them ([[Georgia_(country)|Georgia]], [[Azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]], [[Russia|Russia]], [[Kazakhstan|Kazakhstan]] and [[Turkey|Turkey]]) are transcontinental countries lying partly in Europe.
sentence_131: Geographically, Russia is partly in Asia, but is considered a [[List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_in_Europe|European nation]], both [[Russian_culture|culturally]] and politically.
sentence_132: Asia has extremely diverse climates and geographic features.
sentence_133: Climates range from arctic and subarctic in Siberia to tropical in southern India and Southeast Asia.
sentence_134: It is moist across southeast sections, and dry across much of the interior.
sentence_135: Some of the largest daily temperature ranges on Earth occur in western sections of Asia.
sentence_136: The monsoon circulation dominates across southern and eastern sections, due to the presence of the Himalayas forcing the formation of a thermal low which draws in moisture during the summer.
sentence_137: Southwestern sections of the continent are hot.
sentence_138: Siberia is one of the coldest places in the Northern Hemisphere, and can act as a source of arctic air masses for North America.
sentence_139: The most active place on Earth for tropical cyclone activity lies northeast of the Philippines and south of Japan.
sentence_140: The Gobi Desert is in [[Mongolia|Mongolia]] and the [[Arabian_Desert|Arabian Desert]] stretches across much of the Middle East.
sentence_141: The [[Yangtze_River|Yangtze River]] in China is the longest river in the continent.
sentence_142: The [[Himalayas|Himalayas]] between Nepal and China is the tallest mountain range in the world.
sentence_143: Tropical rainforests stretch across much of southern Asia and coniferous and deciduous forests lie farther north.
sentence_144: There are various approaches to the regional division of Asia.
sentence_145: The following subdivision into regions is used, among others, by the UN statistics agency UNSD.
sentence_146: This division of Asia into regions by the United Nations is done solely for statistical reasons and does not imply any assumption about political or other affiliations of countries and territories.
sentence_147: A survey carried out in 2010 by global risk analysis farm Maplecroft identified 16 countries that are extremely vulnerable to climate change.
sentence_148: Each nation's vulnerability was calculated using 42 socio, economic and environmental indicators, which identified the likely climate change impacts during the next 30 years.
sentence_149: The Asian countries of [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], India, [[Vietnam|Vietnam]], Thailand, Pakistan and [[Sri_Lanka|Sri Lanka]] were among the 16 countries facing extreme risk from climate change.
sentence_150: Some shifts are already occurring.
sentence_151: For example, in tropical parts of India with a [[Semi-arid_climate|semi-arid climate]], the temperature increased by 0.4 °C between 1901 and 2003.
sentence_152: A 2013 study by the [[International_Crops_Research_Institute_for_the_Semi-Arid_Tropics|International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics]] (ICRISAT) aimed to find science-based, pro-poor approaches and techniques that would enable Asia's agricultural systems to cope with climate change, while benefitting poor and vulnerable farmers.
sentence_153: The study's recommendations ranged from improving the use of climate information in local planning and strengthening weather-based agro-advisory services, to stimulating diversification of rural household incomes and providing incentives to farmers to adopt natural resource conservation measures to enhance forest cover, replenish groundwater and use [[Renewable_energy|renewable energy]].
sentence_154: Main articles: [[Economy_of_Asia|Economy of Asia]], [[List_of_Asian_countries_by_GDP|List of Asian countries by GDP]], [[List_of_countries_in_Asia-Pacific_by_GDP_(nominal)|List of countries in Asia-Pacific by GDP (nominal)]], and [[List_of_Asian_and_Pacific_countries_by_GDP_(PPP)|List of Asian and Pacific countries by GDP (PPP)]]
sentence_155: Asia has the largest continental economy by both [[GDP|GDP]] [[List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)|Nominal]] and [[Purchasing_power_parity|PPP]] in the world, and is the fastest growing economic region.
sentence_156: As of 2018, the largest economies in Asia are China, Japan, India, South Korea, Indonesia and Turkey based on GDP in both nominal and PPP.
sentence_157: Based on Global Office Locations 2011, Asia dominated the office locations with 4 of the top 5 being in Asia: [[Hong_Kong|Hong Kong]], [[Singapore|Singapore]], [[Tokyo|Tokyo]] and [[Seoul|Seoul]].
sentence_158: Around 68 percent of international firms have office in Hong Kong.
sentence_159: In the late 1990s and early 2000s, the economies of China and India have been growing rapidly, both with an average annual growth rate of more than 8%.
sentence_160: Other recent very-high-growth nations in Asia include [[Israel|Israel]], [[Malaysia|Malaysia]], [[Indonesia|Indonesia]], [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], [[Thailand|Thailand]], [[Vietnam|Vietnam]], and the [[Philippines|Philippines]], and mineral-rich nations such as [[Kazakhstan|Kazakhstan]], [[Turkmenistan|Turkmenistan]], [[Iran|Iran]], [[Brunei|Brunei]], the [[United_Arab_Emirates|United Arab Emirates]], [[Qatar|Qatar]], [[Kuwait|Kuwait]], [[Saudi_Arabia|Saudi Arabia]], [[Bahrain|Bahrain]] and [[Oman|Oman]].
sentence_161: According to [[Economic_historian|economic historian]] Angus Maddison in his book The World Economy: A Millennial Perspective, India had the world's largest economy during 0 BCE and 1000 BCE.
sentence_162: China was the [[Economic_history_of_China|largest and most advanced economy]] on earth for much of recorded history.
sentence_163: For several decades in the late twentieth century Japan was the largest economy in Asia and second-largest of any single nation in the world, after surpassing the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]] (measured in net material product) in 1990 and Germany in 1968.
sentence_164: (NB: A number of supernational economies are larger, such as the [[European_Union|European Union]] (EU), the [[North_American_Free_Trade_Agreement|North American Free Trade Agreement]] (NAFTA) or [[APEC|APEC]]).
sentence_165: This ended in 2010 when China overtook Japan to become the world's second largest economy.
sentence_166: In the late 1980s and early 1990s, Japan's GDP was almost as large (current exchange rate method) as that of the rest of Asia combined.
sentence_167: In 1995, Japan's economy nearly equaled that of the US as the largest economy in the world for a day, after the Japanese currency reached a record high of 79 [[Japanese_yen|yen]]/US$.
sentence_168: Economic growth in Asia since World War II to the 1990s had been concentrated in Japan as well as the four regions of South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore located in the [[Pacific_Rim|Pacific Rim]], known as the [[Four_Asian_Tigers|Asian tigers]], which have now all received developed country status, having the highest [[GDP_per_capita|GDP per capita]] in Asia.
sentence_169: It is forecasted that India will overtake Japan in terms of nominal GDP by 2025.
sentence_170: By 2027, according to [[Goldman_Sachs|Goldman Sachs]], China will have the largest economy in the world.
sentence_171: Several trade blocs exist, with the most developed being the [[Association_of_Southeast_Asian_Nations|Association of Southeast Asian Nations]].
sentence_172: Asia is the largest continent in the world by a considerable margin, and it is rich in natural resources, such as petroleum, forests, fish, water, rice, copper and silver.
sentence_173: Manufacturing in Asia has traditionally been strongest in East and Southeast Asia, particularly in China, [[Taiwan|Taiwan]], South Korea, Japan, India, the Philippines, and Singapore.
sentence_174: Japan and South Korea continue to dominate in the area of [[Multinational_corporation|multinational corporations]], but increasingly the PRC and India are making significant inroads.
sentence_175: Many companies from Europe, North America, South Korea and Japan have operations in Asia's developing countries to take advantage of its abundant supply of cheap labour and relatively developed infrastructure.
sentence_176: According to [[Citigroup|Citigroup]] 9 of 11 [[3G_(countries)|Global Growth Generators]] countries came from Asia driven by population and income growth.
sentence_177: They are [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], China, India, Indonesia, [[Iraq|Iraq]], Mongolia, Philippines, [[Sri_Lanka|Sri Lanka]] and Vietnam.
sentence_178: Asia has three main financial centers: Hong Kong, Tokyo and Singapore.
sentence_179: [[Call_center|Call centers]] and [[Business_process_outsourcing|business process outsourcing]] (BPOs) are becoming major employers in India and the Philippines due to the availability of a large pool of highly skilled, English-speaking workers.
sentence_180: The increased use of outsourcing has assisted the rise of India and the China as financial centers.
sentence_181: Due to its large and extremely competitive information technology industry, India has become a major hub for outsourcing.
sentence_182: In 2010, Asia had 3.3 million millionaires (people with net worth over US$1 million excluding their homes), slightly below North America with 3.4 million millionaires.
sentence_183: Last year Asia had toppled Europe.
sentence_184: Citigroup in The Wealth Report 2012 stated that Asian centa-millionaire overtook North America's wealth for the first time as the world's "economic center of gravity" continued moving east.
sentence_185: At the end of 2011, there were 18,000 Asian people mainly in Southeast Asia, China and Japan who have at least $100 million in disposable assets, while North America with 17,000 people and Western Europe with 14,000 people.
sentence_186: With growing Regional Tourism with domination of Chinese visitors, [[MasterCard|MasterCard]] has released Global Destination Cities Index 2013 with 10 of 20 are dominated by Asia and Pacific Region Cities and also for the first time a city of a country from Asia (Bangkok) set in the top-ranked with 15.98 international visitors.
sentence_187: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Asia|Demographics of Asia]]
sentence_188: East Asia had by far the strongest overall [[Human_Development_Index|Human Development Index]] (HDI) improvement of any region in the world, nearly doubling average HDI attainment over the past 40 years, according to the report's analysis of health, education and income data.
sentence_189: China, the second highest achiever in the world in terms of HDI improvement since 1970, is the only country on the "Top 10 Movers" list due to income rather than health or education achievements.
sentence_190: Its per capita income increased a stunning 21-fold over the last four decades, also lifting hundreds of millions out of income poverty.
sentence_191: Yet it was not among the region's top performers in improving school enrollment and life expectancy.
sentence_192: [[Nepal|Nepal]], a South Asian country, emerges as one of the world's fastest movers since 1970 mainly due to health and education achievements.
sentence_193: Its present [[Life_expectancy|life expectancy]] is 25 years longer than in the 1970s.
sentence_194: More than four of every five children of school age in Nepal now attend primary school, compared to just one in five 40 years ago.
sentence_195: Hong Kong ranked highest among the countries grouped on the HDI (number 7 in the world, which is in the "very high human development" category), followed by Singapore (9), Japan (19) and South Korea (22).
sentence_196: [[Afghanistan|Afghanistan]] (155) ranked lowest amongst Asian countries out of the 169 countries assessed.
sentence_197: Main article: Languages of Asia
sentence_198: Asia is home to several [[Language_family|language families]] and many [[Language_isolate|language isolates]].
sentence_199: Most Asian countries have more than one language that is natively spoken.
sentence_200: For instance, according to [[Ethnologue|Ethnologue]], more than 600 languages are spoken in Indonesia, more than 800 languages spoken in India, and more than 100 are spoken in the Philippines.
sentence_201: China has many languages and dialects in different provinces.
sentence_202: See also: [[Eastern_philosophy|Eastern philosophy]], [[Religion_in_Asia|Religion in Asia]], and [[List_of_Asian_mythologies|List of Asian mythologies]]
sentence_203: Many of the world's [[Major_religious_groups|major religions]] have their origins in Asia, including the five most practiced in the world (excluding [[Irreligion|irreligion]]), which are Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Chinese folk religion (classified as Confucianism and Taoism), and Buddhism respectively.
sentence_204: Asian mythology is complex and diverse.
sentence_205: The story of the [[Flood_myth|Great Flood]] for example, as presented to Jews in the [[Hebrew_Bible|Hebrew Bible]] in the narrative of [[Noah|Noah]]—and later to Christians in the [[Old_Testament|Old Testament]], and to [[Islam|Muslims]] in the [[Quran|Quran]]—is earliest found in Mesopotamian mythology, in the [[Enûma_Eliš|Enûma Eliš]] and [[Epic_of_Gilgamesh|Epic of Gilgamesh]].
sentence_206: [[Hindu_mythology|Hindu mythology]] similarly tells about an [[Avatar|avatar]] of [[Vishnu|Vishnu]] in the form of a [[Matsya|fish]] who warned [[Sraddhadeva_Manu|Manu]] of a terrible flood.
sentence_207: Ancient [[Chinese_mythology|Chinese mythology]] also tells of a [[Great_Flood_(China)|Great Flood]] spanning generations, one that required the combined efforts of emperors and divinities to control.
sentence_208: The [[Abrahamic_religions|Abrahamic religions]] including Judaism, [[Christianity|Christianity]], [[Islam|Islam]] and [[Bahá'í_Faith|Bahá'í Faith]] originated in West Asia.
sentence_209: Judaism, the oldest of the Abrahamic faiths, is practiced primarily in [[Israel|Israel]], the indigenous homeland and historical birthplace of the [[Jews|Hebrew nation]]: which today consists both of those [[Jews|Jews]] who remained in [[Mizrahi_Jews|the Middle East]] and those who returned from [[Jewish_diaspora|diaspora]] in Europe, [[American_Jews|North America]], and other regions; though various diaspora communities persist worldwide.
sentence_210: Jews are the predominant ethnic group in [[Israel|Israel]] (75.6%) numbering at about 6.1 million, although the levels of adherence to Jewish religion vary.
sentence_211: Outside of Israel there are small ancient Jewish communities in [[Turkey|Turkey]] (17,400), [[Azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] (9,100), Iran (8,756), India (5,000) and [[Uzbekistan|Uzbekistan]] (4,000), among many other places.
sentence_212: In total, there are 14.4–17.5 million (2016, est.) Jews alive in the world today, making them one of the smallest Asian minorities, at roughly 0.3 to 0.4 percent of the total population of the continent.
sentence_213: [[Christianity|Christianity]] is a widespread religion in Asia with more than 286 million adherents according to [[Pew_Research_Center|Pew Research Center]] in 2010, and nearly 364 million according to [[Encyclopædia_Britannica|Britannica]] Book of the Year 2014.
sentence_214: Constituting around 12.6% of the total population of Asia.
sentence_215: In the Philippines and [[East_Timor|East Timor]], Roman Catholicism is the predominant religion; it was introduced by the Spaniards and the Portuguese, respectively.
sentence_216: In [[Armenia|Armenia]], Georgia and Asian Russia, [[Eastern_Orthodoxy|Eastern Orthodoxy]] is the predominant religion.
sentence_217: In the Middle East, such as in the [[Levant|Levant]], [[Syriac_Christianity|Syriac Christianity]] ([[Church_of_the_East|Church of the East]]) and [[Oriental_Orthodoxy|Oriental Orthodoxy]] are prevalent minority denominations, which are both [[Eastern_Christian|Eastern Christian]] sects mainly adhered to [[Assyrian_people|Assyrian people]] or Syriac Christians.
sentence_218: [[Saint_Thomas_Christians|Saint Thomas Christians]] in India trace their origins to the evangelistic activity of [[Thomas_the_Apostle|Thomas the Apostle]] in the 1st century.
sentence_219: [[Islam|Islam]], which originated in the [[Hejaz|Hejaz]] located in modern-day Saudi Arabia, is the second largest and most widely-spread religion in Asia with at least 1 billion Muslims constituting around 23.8% of the total population of Asia.
sentence_220: With 12.7% of the world Muslim population, the country currently with the largest Muslim population in the world is Indonesia, followed by Pakistan (11.5%), India (10%), [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], Iran and [[Turkey|Turkey]].
sentence_221: [[Mecca|Mecca]], [[Medina|Medina]] and [[Holiest_sites_in_Islam#Jerusalem|Jerusalem]] are the three holiest cities for Islam in all the world.
sentence_222: The [[Hajj|Hajj]] and [[Umrah|Umrah]] attract large numbers of Muslim devotees from all over the world to Mecca and Medina.
sentence_223: Iran is the largest [[Shi'a|Shi'a]] country.
sentence_224: The [[Bahá'í_Faith|Bahá'í Faith]] originated in Asia, in Iran (Persia), and spread from there to the Ottoman Empire, Central Asia, India, and Burma during the lifetime of Bahá'u'lláh.
sentence_225: Since the middle of the 20th century, growth has particularly occurred in other Asian countries, because Bahá'í activities in many Muslim countries has been [[Persecution_of_Bahá'ís|severely suppressed]] by authorities.
sentence_226: [[Lotus_Temple|Lotus Temple]] is a big Bahá'í Temple in India.
sentence_227: Almost all Asian religions have philosophical character and Asian philosophical traditions cover a large spectrum of philosophical thoughts and writings.
sentence_228: [[Indian_philosophy|Indian philosophy]] includes [[Hindu_philosophy|Hindu philosophy]] and [[Buddhist_philosophy|Buddhist philosophy]].
sentence_229: They include elements of nonmaterial pursuits, whereas another school of thought from India, [[Cārvāka|Cārvāka]], preached the enjoyment of the material world.
sentence_230: The religions of [[Hinduism|Hinduism]], [[Buddhism|Buddhism]], [[Jainism|Jainism]] and [[Sikhism|Sikhism]] originated in India, South Asia.
sentence_231: In East Asia, particularly in China and Japan, [[Confucianism|Confucianism]], [[Taoism|Taoism]] and [[Zen|Zen Buddhism]] took shape.
sentence_232: As of 2012, Hinduism has around 1.1 billion adherents.
sentence_233: The faith represents around 25% of Asia's population and is the largest religion in Asia.
sentence_234: However, it is mostly concentrated in South Asia.
sentence_235: Over 80% of the populations of both India and Nepal adhere to Hinduism, alongside significant communities in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and [[Bali|Bali]], Indonesia.
sentence_236: Many overseas Indians in countries such as Burma, Singapore and Malaysia also adhere to Hinduism.
sentence_237: Buddhism has a great following in mainland Southeast Asia and East Asia.
sentence_238: Buddhism is the religion of the majority of the populations of [[Cambodia|Cambodia]] (96%), [[Thailand|Thailand]] (95%), [[Burma|Burma]] (80–89%), Japan (36–96%), [[Bhutan|Bhutan]] (75–84%), [[Sri_Lanka|Sri Lanka]] (70%), [[Laos|Laos]] (60–67%) and [[Mongolia|Mongolia]] (53–93%).
sentence_239: Large Buddhist populations also exist in Singapore (33–51%), [[Taiwan|Taiwan]] (35–93%), South Korea (23–50%), [[Malaysia|Malaysia]] (19–21%), [[Nepal|Nepal]] (9–11%), [[Vietnam|Vietnam]] (10–75%), China (20–50%), [[North_Korea|North Korea]] (2–14%), and small communities in India and [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]].
sentence_240: In many Chinese communities, Mahayana Buddhism is easily syncretized with Taoism, thus exact religious statistics is difficult to obtain and may be understated or overstated.
sentence_241: The Communist-governed countries of China, Vietnam and North Korea are officially atheist, thus the number of Buddhists and other religious adherents may be under-reported.
sentence_242: [[Jainism|Jainism]] is found mainly in India and in oversea Indian communities such as the United States and Malaysia.
sentence_243: [[Sikhism|Sikhism]] is found in Northern India and amongst overseas Indian communities in other parts of Asia, especially Southeast Asia.
sentence_244: [[Confucianism|Confucianism]] is found predominantly in Mainland China, South Korea, Taiwan and in overseas Chinese populations.
sentence_245: [[Taoism|Taoism]] is found mainly in Mainland China, Taiwan, Malaysia and Singapore.
sentence_246: Taoism is easily syncretized with [[Mahayana_Buddhism|Mahayana Buddhism]] for many Chinese, thus exact religious statistics is difficult to obtain and may be understated or overstated.

list.value: The Dissolution of the Soviet Union

sentence_248: Main article: Culture of Asia
sentence_249: The [[Polymath|polymath]] [[Rabindranath_Tagore|Rabindranath Tagore]], a Bengali poet, dramatist, and writer from [[Santiniketan|Santiniketan]], now in [[West_Bengal|West Bengal]], India, became in 1913 the first Asian [[Nobel_Prize|Nobel laureate]].
sentence_250: He won his [[Nobel_Prize_in_Literature|Nobel Prize in Literature]] for notable impact his prose works and poetic thought had on English, French, and other national literatures of Europe and the Americas.
sentence_251: He is also the writer of the national anthems of [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]] and India.
sentence_252: Other Asian writers who won Nobel Prize for literature include Yasunari Kawabata (Japan, 1968), [[Kenzaburō_Ōe|Kenzaburō Ōe]] (Japan, 1994), [[Gao_Xingjian|Gao Xingjian]] (China, 2000), [[Orhan_Pamuk|Orhan Pamuk]] (Turkey, 2006), and [[Mo_Yan|Mo Yan]] (China, 2012).
sentence_253: Some may consider the American writer, [[Pearl_S._Buck|Pearl S. Buck]], an honorary Asian Nobel laureate, having spent considerable time in China as the daughter of missionaries, and based many of her novels, namely [[The_Good_Earth|The Good Earth]] (1931) and [[The_Mother_(1934_novel)|The Mother]] (1933), as well as the biographies of her parents of their time in China, [[The_Exile_(1936_book)|The Exile]] and [[Fighting_Angel|Fighting Angel]], all of which earned her the Literature prize in 1938.
sentence_254: Also, [[Mother_Teresa|Mother Teresa]] of India and [[Shirin_Ebadi|Shirin Ebadi]] of Iran were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for their significant and pioneering efforts for democracy and human rights, especially for the rights of women and children.
sentence_255: Ebadi is the first Iranian and the first Muslim woman to receive the prize.
sentence_256: Another Nobel Peace Prize winner is [[Aung_San_Suu_Kyi|Aung San Suu Kyi]] from [[Myanmar|Burma]] for her peaceful and non-violent struggle under a military dictatorship in Burma.
sentence_257: She is a nonviolent pro-democracy activist and leader of the National League for Democracy in Burma (Myanmar) and a noted prisoner of conscience.
sentence_258: She is a [[Buddhist|Buddhist]] and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991.
sentence_259: Chinese dissident [[Liu_Xiaobo|Liu Xiaobo]] was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "his long and non-violent struggle for fundamental human rights in China" on 8 October 2010.
sentence_260: He is the first Chinese citizen to be awarded a Nobel Prize of any kind while residing in China.
sentence_261: In 2014, [[Kailash_Satyarthi|Kailash Satyarthi]] from India and [[Malala_Yousafzai|Malala Yousafzai]] from Pakistan were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize "for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education".
sentence_262: Sir [[C.V._Raman|C.V.
sentence_263: Raman]] is the first Asian to get a Nobel prize in Sciences.
sentence_264: He won the [[Nobel_Prize_in_Physics|Nobel Prize in Physics]] "for his work on the scattering of light and for the discovery of the [[Raman_scattering|effect named after him]]".
sentence_265: Japan has won the most Nobel Prizes of any Asian nation with 24 followed by India which has won 13.
sentence_266: Amartya Sen, (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist who was awarded the 1998 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his contributions to welfare economics and [[Social_choice_theory|social choice theory]], and for his interest in the problems of society's poorest members.
sentence_267: Other Asian Nobel Prize winners include [[Subrahmanyan_Chandrasekhar|Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]], [[Abdus_Salam|Abdus Salam]], [[Malala_Yousafzai|Malala Yousafzai]], [[Robert_Aumann|Robert Aumann]], [[Menachem_Begin|Menachem Begin]], [[Aaron_Ciechanover|Aaron Ciechanover]], [[Avram_Hershko|Avram Hershko]], [[Daniel_Kahneman|Daniel Kahneman]], [[Shimon_Peres|Shimon Peres]], [[Yitzhak_Rabin|Yitzhak Rabin]], [[Ada_Yonath|Ada Yonath]], [[Yasser_Arafat|Yasser Arafat]], [[José_Ramos-Horta|José Ramos-Horta]] and Bishop [[Carlos_Filipe_Ximenes_Belo|Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo]] of [[Timor_Leste|Timor Leste]], [[Kim_Dae-jung|Kim Dae-jung]], and 13 Japanese scientists.
sentence_268: Most of the said awardees are from Japan and [[Israel|Israel]] except for Chandrasekhar and Raman (India), Abdus Salam and Malala yousafzai, (Pakistan), Arafat (Palestinian Territories), Kim (South Korea), and Horta and Belo (Timor Leste).
sentence_269: In 2006, Dr. Muhammad Yunus of [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]] was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for the establishment of [[Grameen_Bank|Grameen Bank]], a community development bank that lends money to poor people, especially women in Bangladesh.
sentence_270: Dr. Yunus received his PhD in economics from Vanderbilt University, United States.
sentence_271: He is internationally known for the concept of micro credit which allows poor and destitute people with little or no collateral to borrow money.
sentence_272: The borrowers typically pay back money within the specified period and the incidence of default is very low.
sentence_273: The Dalai Lama has received approximately eighty-four awards over his spiritual and political career.
sentence_274: On 22 June 2006, he became one of only four people ever to be recognized with Honorary Citizenship by the Governor General of Canada.
sentence_275: On 28 May 2005, he received the Christmas Humphreys Award from the Buddhist Society in the United Kingdom.
sentence_276: Most notable was the Nobel Peace Prize, presented in [[Oslo|Oslo]], [[Norway|Norway]] on 10 December 1989.

title: American Revolutionary War
sentence_0: This article is about military actions primarily.
sentence_1: For origins and aftermath, see [[American_Revolution|American Revolution]].
sentence_2: The American Revolutionary War (1775–1783), also known as the American War of Independence or the Revolutionary War, was initiated by delegates from the [[Thirteen_Colonies|thirteen American colonies]] in [[Continental_Congress|Congress]] against [[Kingdom_of_Great_Britain|Great Britain]] over their objection to Parliament's taxation policies and [[No_taxation_without_representation|lack of colonial representation]].
sentence_3: From their founding in the 1600s, the colonies were largely left to govern themselves.
sentence_4: The cost of victory in the 1754 to 1763 [[French_and_Indian_War|French and Indian War]] and 1756 to 1763 [[Seven_Years'_War|Seven Years' War]] left the British government deeply in debt; attempts to have the [[The_Thirteen_Colonies|colonies]] pay for their own defense were vigorously resisted.
sentence_5: The [[Stamp_Act_1765|Stamp Act]] and [[Townshend_Acts|Townshend Acts]] provoked colonial opposition and unrest, leading to the 1770 [[Boston_massacre|Boston massacre]] and 1773 [[Boston_Tea_Party|Boston Tea Party]].
sentence_6: When Parliament imposed the [[Intolerable_Acts|Intolerable Acts]] upon [[Province_of_Massachusetts_Bay|Massachusetts]], twelve colonies sent delegates to the [[First_Continental_Congress|First Continental Congress]] to draft a [[Petition_to_the_King|Petition to the King]] and organize a boycott of British goods.
sentence_7: Fighting broke out on 19 April 1775: the British garrison at Boston was harassed by Massachusetts militia at [[Battles_of_Lexington_and_Concord|Lexington and Concord]] after destroying colonial Assembly powder stores.
sentence_8: In June the [[Second_Continental_Congress|Second Continental Congress]] appointed [[George_Washington|George Washington]] to create a [[Continental_Army|Continental Army]] and oversee the [[Siege_of_Boston|capture of Boston]].
sentence_9: The [[Patriot_(American_Revolution)|Patriots]] sent their [[Olive_Branch_Petition|Olive Branch Petition]] to the King and Parliament, both of whom rebuffed it.
sentence_10: In response they invaded [[Invasion_of_Quebec_(1775)|British Quebec]] but were repulsed.
sentence_11: In July 1776, Congress unanimously passed the [[United_States_Declaration_of_Independence|Declaration of Independence]].
sentence_12: Hopes of a quick settlement were supported by [[Rockingham_Whigs|American sympathizers within Parliament]] who opposed [[Frederick_North,_Lord_North|Lord North]]'s "coercion policy" in the colonies.
sentence_13: However, the new British commander-in-chief, General [[William_Howe,_5th_Viscount_Howe|Sir William Howe]], launched a [[New_York_and_New_Jersey_campaign|counter-offensive]] and captured New York City.
sentence_14: Washington retaliated with harassing fire at the [[Battle_of_Trenton|Battle of Trenton]] and [[Battle_of_Princeton|Battle of Princeton]].
sentence_15: Howe's 1777–1778 [[Philadelphia_campaign|Philadelphia campaign]] captured the city, but the British lost the [[Battles_of_Saratoga|Battles of Saratoga]] in October 1777.
sentence_16: At [[Valley_Forge|Valley Forge]] during the winter of 1777–1778, Prussian emigrant General [[Friedrich_Wilhelm_von_Steuben|Friedrich Wilhelm von Steuben]] trained the [[Continental_Army|Continental Army]] with a system of progressive training.
sentence_17: French Foreign Minister [[Charles_Gravier,_comte_de_Vergennes|Vergennes]] saw the war as a way to create an America economically and militarily dependent on France, not Britain.
sentence_18: Although talks on a formal alliance began in late 1776, they proceeded slowly until Patriot victory at [[Battles_of_Saratoga|Saratoga]] in October 1777.
sentence_19: Fears Congress might come to an early settlement with Britain resulted in France and the United States signing two treaties in February 1778.
sentence_20: The first was a [[Treaty_of_Amity_and_Commerce_(United_States–France)|commercial treaty]], the second a [[Treaty_of_Alliance_(1778)|Treaty of Alliance]]; in return for a French guarantee of American independence, Congress agreed to join the war against Britain and defend the French West Indies.
sentence_21: Although Spain refused to join the Franco-American alliance, in the 1779 [[Treaty_of_Aranjuez_(1779)|Treaty of Aranjuez]] they agreed to support France in its [[Anglo-French_War_(1778–1783)|global war with Britain]], hoping to regain losses incurred in 1713.
sentence_22: In other fronts in North America, Governor of Spanish Louisiana Bernardo Gálvez routed British forces from [[Louisiana_(New_Spain)|Louisiana]].
sentence_23: The Spanish, along with [[Privateer#United_States|American privateers]] supplied the 1779 American conquest of [[Illinois_campaign|Western Quebec]] ([[Northwest_Territory#British_control|later the US Northwest Territory]]).
sentence_24: Gálvez then expelled British forces from Mobile during the Battle of Fort Charlotte and the Siege of Pensacola, cutting off British military aid to their American Indian allies in the interior southeast.
sentence_25: Howe's replacement, General [[Henry_Clinton_(British_Army_officer,_born_1730)|Sir Henry Clinton]], then mounted a 1778 "[[Southern_theater_of_the_American_Revolutionary_War#British_campaign_in_the_South|Southern strategy]]" from Charleston.
sentence_26: After [[Capture_of_Savannah|capturing Savannah]], defeats at the [[Battle_of_Kings_Mountain|Battle of Kings Mountain]] and the [[Battle_of_Cowpens|Battle of Cowpens]] forced [[Charles_Cornwallis,_1st_Marquess_Cornwallis|Cornwallis]] to retreat to [[Siege_of_Yorktown_(1781)|Yorktown]], where his army was besieged by an allied French and American force.
sentence_27: An attempt to resupply the garrison was repulsed by the French navy at the [[Battle_of_the_Chesapeake|Battle of the Chesapeake]], and Cornwallis surrendered in October 1781.
sentence_28: Although their war with France and Spain continued for another two years, Yorktown ended the British will to continue the war in North America.
sentence_29: The [[North_Ministry|North Ministry]] was replaced by [[Charles_Watson-Wentworth,_2nd_Marquess_of_Rockingham|Lord Rockingham]], who accepted office on the basis [[George_III|George III]] agreed to American independence.
sentence_30: Preliminary articles were signed in November 1782, and in April 1783 Congress accepted British terms; these included independence, evacuation of British troops, cession of territory up to the [[Mississippi_River|Mississippi River]] and navigation to the sea, as well as fishing rights in Newfoundland.
sentence_31: On September 3, 1783, the [[Treaty_of_Paris_(1783)|Treaty of Paris]] was signed between Great Britain and the United States, then ratified the following spring.
sentence_32: Main article: [[American_Revolution|American Revolution]]
sentence_33: See also: [[Colonial_History_of_the_United_States|Colonial History of the United States]] and [[Thirteen_Colonies|Thirteen Colonies]]
sentence_34: The [[French_and_Indian_War|French and Indian War]] and the wider conflict known as the [[Seven_Years'_War|Seven Years' War]] ended with the [[Peace_of_Paris_(1763)|1763 Peace of Paris]], which expelled France from [[New_France|North America]].
sentence_35: At the same time, the British rescinded provisions of colonial charters claiming to extend from the [[Atlantic|Atlantic]] to the [[Pacific|Pacific]]; the [[Mississippi_River|Mississippi River]] became the dividing line between British and Spanish possessions in the Americas, with free navigation on it "to the open sea".
sentence_36: More American territory changed hands in 1763 than any settlement before or after, destabilising existing alliances and trade networks, and leading to conflict between settlers and American Indians.
sentence_37: The [[Proclamation_Line_of_1763|Proclamation Line of 1763]] was intended to refocus colonial expansion north into Nova Scotia or south into Florida, while separating American Indians and colonials by restricting settlement in the west.
sentence_38: Both sides agreed with the principle but disagreed on where to set the border; keeping the peace required garrisons of regular troops along the frontier, and led to disputes with the [[Colonial_government_in_the_Thirteen_Colonies|colonial legislatures]] over who should bear the expense.
sentence_39: Although directly administered by the Crown, acting through a local Governor, the colonies were largely governed by native-born property owners.
sentence_40: While external affairs were managed by [[London|London]], colonial [[Militia_(United_States)|militia]] were funded locally but with the ending of the French threat in 1763, the legislatures expected less taxation, not more.
sentence_41: At the same time, the huge costs of the Seven Years' War meant Parliament expected the colonies to fund their own defense.
sentence_42: The outcome was a series of disputes as to how these expenses should be paid.
sentence_43: The 1763 to 1765 [[Grenville_ministry|Grenville ministry]] began by instructing the Royal Navy to clamp down on smuggled goods and enforce customs duties levied in American ports.
sentence_44: The most important was the 1733 [[Molasses_Act|Molasses Act]]; routinely ignored prior to 1763, it had a significant economic impact since 85% of New England rum exports were manufactured from imported molasses.
sentence_45: These measures were followed by the [[Sugar_Act|Sugar Act]] and [[Stamp_Act|Stamp Act]], which imposed additional taxes on the colonies to pay for defending the western frontier.
sentence_46: In July 1765, the [[Whigs_(British_political_party)|Whigs]] formed the [[First_Rockingham_ministry|First Rockingham ministry]], which repealed the Stamp Act and reduced tax on foreign molasses to help the New England economy, but re-asserted Parliamentary authority in the [[Declaratory_Act|Declaratory Act]].
sentence_47: However, this did little to end the discontent; in 1768, a riot started in Boston when the authorities seized the sloop [[HMS_Liberty_(1768)|Liberty]] on suspicion of smuggling.
sentence_48: Tensions escalated further in March 1770 when British troops fired on rock-throwing civilians, killing five in what became known as the [[Boston_massacre|Boston massacre]].
sentence_49: The Massacre coincided with the partial repeal of the [[Townshend_Acts|Townshend Acts]] by the Tory-based [[North_Ministry|North Ministry]], which came to power in January 1770 and remained in office until 1781.
sentence_50: North insisted on retaining duty on tea to enshrine Parliament's right to tax the colonies; the amount was minor, but ignored the fact it was that very principle Americans objected to.
sentence_51: Tensions escalated following the destruction of a customs vessel in the June 1772 [[Gaspee_Affair|Gaspee Affair]], then came to a head in 1773.
sentence_52: A [[Crisis_of_1772|banking crisis]] led to the near collapse of the [[East_India_Company|East India Company]], which dominated the British economy; to support it, Parliament passed the Tea Act, giving it a trading monopoly for North America.
sentence_53: Since most American tea was smuggled by the Dutch, the Act was opposed by those who managed the illegal trade, while being seen as yet another attempt to impose the principle of taxation by Parliament.

sentence_55: While aimed specifically at Massachusetts, many in America and within the Whig opposition considered them a threat to liberty in general; it led to increased sympathy for the Patriot cause locally, as well as in Parliament and the London press.
sentence_56: Over the course of the 18th century, the [[Colonial_government_in_the_Thirteen_Colonies#Assembly|elected lower houses]] in the colonial legislatures gradually wrested power from their Royal Governors.

sentence_60: However, after some debate, on September 17, 1774, Congress endorsed the Massachusetts [[Suffolk_Resolves|Suffolk Resolves]] and on October 20 passed the [[Continental_Association|Continental Association]]; based on a draft prepared by the First Virginia Convention in August, this instituted [[Economic_sanctions|economic sanctions]] against Britain.
sentence_61: While denying its authority over internal American affairs, a faction led by [[James_Duane|James Duane]] and future Loyalist [[Joseph_Galloway|Joseph Galloway]] insisted Congress recognise Parliament's right to regulate colonial trade.
sentence_62: Expecting concessions by the North administration, Congress authorized the extralegal committees and conventions of the colonial legislatures to enforce the boycott; this succeeded in reducing British imports by 97% from 1774 to 1775.
sentence_63: However, on February 9 Parliament declared Massachusetts to be in a state of rebellion and instituted a blockade of the colony.
sentence_64: In July, the [[Restraining_Acts_1775|Restraining Acts]] limited colonial trade with the British West Indies and Britain and barred New England ships from the [[History_of_Newfoundland_and_Labrador#Fishing|Newfoundland cod fisheries]].
sentence_65: The increase in tension led to a scramble for control of militia stores, which each Assembly was legally obliged to maintain for defense.

sentence_67: Main articles: [[Olive_Branch_Petition|Olive Branch Petition]] and [[United_States_Declaration_of_Independence|United States Declaration of Independence]]

sentence_70: Although constitutionally correct, since George could not oppose his own government, it disappointed those Americans who hoped he would mediate in the dispute, while the hostility of his language annoyed even [[Loyalists_fighting_in_the_American_Revolution|Loyalist]] members of Congress.

sentence_220: Main articles: France in the American Revolutionary War, [[Spain_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War|Spain in the American Revolutionary War]], and [[Carlisle_Peace_Commission|Carlisle Peace Commission]]

sentence_224: Vergennes persuaded [[Louis_XVI|Louis XVI]] to secretly fund a [[Roderigue_Hortalez_and_Company|government front company]] to purchase munitions, carried in neutral Dutch ships and imported through [[Sint_Eustatius|Sint Eustatius]] in the Carribean.
sentence_225: Despite general backing for a trade agreement with France, many Americans opposed a military treaty, fearing to "exchange one tyranny for another"; this changed when they appeared to be losing the war in early 1776.

sentence_229: [[Silas_Deane|Silas Deane]] was sent to Paris to begin negotiations with Vergennes, whose key objectives were replacing Britain as the United States' primary commercial and military partner, while securing the French West Indies from American expansion.

sentence_233: On February 6 1778, France and the United States signed the [[Treaty_of_Amity_and_Commerce_(United_States–France)|Treaty of Amity and Commerce]] regulating trade between the two countries, followed by a defensive military alliance against Britain, the [[Treaty_of_Alliance_(1778)|Treaty of Alliance]].
sentence_234: In return for French guarantees of American independence, Congress undertook to defend their interests in the West Indies, while both sides agreed not to make a separate peace; conflict over these provisions would lead to the 1798 to 1800 [[Quasi-War|Quasi-War]].
sentence_235: [[Charles_III_of_Spain|Charles III of Spain]] was invited to join on the same terms but refused, largely due to concerns over the impact of the Revolution on Spanish colonies in the Americas.
sentence_236: Spain had complained on multiple occasions about encroachment by American settlers into [[Louisiana_(New_Spain)|Louisiana]], a problem that could only get worse once the United States replaced Britain.
sentence_237: Although Spain ultimately made important contributions to American success, in the [[Treaty_of_Aranjuez_(1779)|Treaty of Aranjuez (1779)]], Charles agreed only to support [[Anglo-French_War_(1778–1783)|France's war with Britain]] outside America, in return for help in recovering [[Gibraltar|Gibraltar]], [[Menorca|Menorca]] and the [[Spanish_Florida|Floridas]].
sentence_238: The terms were confidential since several conflicted with American aims; for example, the French claimed exclusive control of the Newfoundland cod fisheries, a non-negotiable for colonies like Massachusetts.
sentence_239: One less well-known impact of this agreement was the abiding American distrust of 'foreign entanglements'; the US would not sign another treaty until the [[NATO|NATO]] agreement in 1949.

sentence_241: To encourage French participation in the struggle for independence, the US representative in Paris, [[Silas_Deane|Silas Deane]] promised promotion and command positions to any French officer who joined the Continental Army.
sentence_242: Although many proved incompetent, one outstanding exception was [[Gilbert_du_Motier,_Marquis_de_Lafayette|Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette]], whom Congress appointed a major General.
sentence_243: In addition to his military ability, Lafayette showed considerable political skill in building support for Washington among his officers and within Congress, liaising with French army and naval commanders, and promoting the Patriot cause in France.
sentence_244: When the war started, Britain tried to borrow the Dutch-based [[Scots_Brigade|Scots Brigade]] for service in America, but pro-Patriot sentiment led the [[States_General_of_the_Netherlands|States General]] to refuse.
sentence_245: Although the Republic was no longer a major power, prior to 1774 they still dominated the European carrying trade, and Dutch merchants benefitted from neutrality by shipping French-supplied munitions to the Patriots.
sentence_246: This ended when Britain [[Fourth_Anglo-Dutch_War|declared war]] in December 1780, a conflict that proved disastrous to the Dutch economy.
sentence_247: The Dutch were also excluded from the [[First_League_of_Armed_Neutrality|First League of Armed Neutrality]], formed by Russia, Sweden and Denmark in March 1780 to protect neutral shipping from being stopped and searched for contraband by Britain and France.
sentence_248: The British government failed to take into account the strength of the American merchant marine and support from European countries, which allowed the colonies to import munitions and continue trading with relative impunity.

sentence_258: The resulting [[Battle_of_Rhode_Island|Battle of Rhode Island]] was indecisive; badly damaged by a storm, the French withdrew to avoid putting their ships at risk.

sentence_262: In July, a large American naval operation, the [[Penobscot_Expedition|Penobscot Expedition]], attempted to retake Maine (Massachusetts), but was defeated.
sentence_263: The high frequency of [[Northern_theater_of_the_American_Revolutionary_War#Raiding_in_the_valleys,_1778|Iroquois raids]] compelled Washington to mount the punitive [[Sullivan_Expedition|Sullivan Expedition]] that destroyed a large number of Iroquois settlements, which failed to stop the raids.
sentence_264: During the winter of 1779–1780, the Continental Army suffered greater hardships than at Valley Forge.
sentence_265: Morale was poor, public support fell away in the long war, the [[Continental_dollar|Continental dollar]] was virtually worthless, the army was plagued with supply problems, desertion was common, and mutinies occurred in the [[Pennsylvania_Line_Mutiny|Pennsylvania Line]] and [[Pompton_Mutiny|New Jersey Line]] regiments over the conditions in early 1780.
sentence_266: In June 1780, Clinton sent 6,000 men under [[Wilhelm_von_Knyphausen|Wilhelm von Knyphausen]] to retake New Jersey, but they were halted by local militia at the Battle of Connecticut Farms; although the Americans withdrew, Knyphausen felt he was not strong enough to engage Washington's main force and retreated.
sentence_267: A second attempt two weeks later ended in a British defeat at the [[Battle_of_Springfield_(1780)|Battle of Springfield]], effectively ending their ambitions in New Jersey.
sentence_268: In July, Washington appointed [[Benedict_Arnold|Benedict Arnold]] commander of [[West_Point|West Point]]; his attempt to betray the fort to the British failed due to incompetent planning, and the plot was revealed when his British contact [[John_André|John André]] was captured and later executed.
sentence_269: Arnold escaped to New York and switched sides, an action justified in a pamphlet addressed "[[To_the_Inhabitants_of_America|To the Inhabitants of America]]"; the Patriots condemned his betrayal, while he found himself almost as unpopular with the British.
sentence_270: The war to the west of the [[Appalachian_Mountains|Appalachians]] was largely confined to skirmishing and raids.
sentence_271: In February 1778, an expedition of militia to destroy British military supplies in settlements along the [[Cuyahoga_River|Cuyahoga River]] was halted by adverse weather.

sentence_273: Virginia militia, [[Canadien|Canadien]] settlers, and Indian allies commanded by Colonel [[George_Rogers_Clark|George Rogers Clark]] captured [[Kaskaskia,_Illinois|Kaskaskia]] on July 4 then secured [[Vincennes,_Indiana|Vincennes]], though Vincennes was recaptured by Quebec Governor [[Henry_Hamilton_(colonial_administrator)|Henry Hamilton]].

sentence_284: French soldier [[Augustin_de_La_Balme|Augustin de La Balme]] led Canadien militiamen in an attempt to capture Detroit, but they dispersed when [[Miami_tribe|Miami Indians]] led by [[Little_Turtle|Little Turtle]] attacked the encamped settlers on November 5.

sentence_286: Main article: Southern theater of the American Revolutionary War
sentence_287: The "Southern Strategy" was developed by Lord Germain, based on input from London-based Loyalists like Joseph Galloway.
sentence_288: They argued it made no sense to fight the Patriots in the north where they were strongest, while the New England economy was reliant on trade with Britain, regardless of who governed it.
sentence_289: On the other hand, duties on tobacco made the South far more profitable for Britain, while local support meant securing it required small numbers of regular troops.
sentence_290: Victory would leave a truncated United States facing British possessions in the south, Canada to the north and Ohio on their western border; with the Atlantic seaboard controlled by the Royal Navy, Congress would be forced to agree terms.
sentence_291: However, assumptions about the level of Loyalist support proved wildly optimistic.
sentence_292: Germain accordingly ordered [[Augustine_Prévost|Augustine Prévost]], British commander in [[East_Florida|East Florida]], to advance into [[Georgia_in_the_American_Revolution#Return_of_the_British_Army|Georgia]] in December 1778.
sentence_293: [[Archibald_Campbell_(British_Army_officer,_born_1739)|Lieutenant-Colonel Archibald Campbell]], an experienced officer taken prisoner earlier in the war before being exchanged for Ethan Allen, [[Capture_of_Savannah|captured Savannah]] on December 29 1778.
sentence_294: He recruited a Loyalist militia of nearly 1,100, many of whom allegedly joined only after Campbell threatened to confiscate their property.

sentence_296: In June, Prévost launched an abortive assault on Charleston, before retreating to Savannah, an operation notorious for widespread looting by British troops that enraged both Loyalists and Patriots.
sentence_297: In October, a joint French and American operation under Admiral [[Charles_Henri_Hector_d'Estaing|d'Estaing]] and General [[Benjamin_Lincoln|Benjamin Lincoln]] failed to [[Siege_of_Savannah|recapture Savannah]].
sentence_298: Prévost was replaced by [[Charles_Cornwallis,_1st_Marquess_Cornwallis|Lord Cornwallis]], who assumed responsibility for Germain's strategy; he soon realised estimates of Loyalist support were considerably over-stated, and he needed far larger numbers of regular forces.
sentence_299: Reinforced by Clinton, his troops [[Siege_of_Charleston|captured Charleston]] in May 1780, inflicting the most serious Patriot defeat of the war; over 5,000 prisoners were taken and the Continental Army in the south effectively destroyed.
sentence_300: On May 29, Loyalist regular [[Banastre_Tarleton|Banastre Tarleton]] defeated an American force of 400 at the [[Battle_of_Waxhaws|Battle of Waxhaws]]; over 120 were killed, many allegedly after surrendering.

sentence_303: The Southern strategy depended on local support, but this was undermined by a series of coercive measures.

sentence_306: In July, Congress appointed General [[Horatio_Gates|Horatio Gates]] commander in the south; he was defeated at the [[Battle_of_Camden|Battle of Camden]] on August 16, leaving Cornwallis free to enter North Carolina.

sentence_311: The Patriots now held the initiative in the south, with the exception of a raid on Richmond led by Benedict Arnold in January 1781.
sentence_312: Greene led Cornwallis on a series of counter marches around North Carolina; by early March, the British were exhausted and short of supplies and Greene felt strong enough to fight the [[Battle_of_Guilford_Court_House|Battle of Guilford Court House]] on March 15.

sentence_314: The Patriots now controlled most of the Carolinas and Georgia outside the coastal areas; after a minor reversal at the [[Battle_of_Hobkirk's_Hill|Battle of Hobkirk's Hill]], they recaptured [[Siege_of_Fort_Watson|Fort Watson]] and [[Siege_of_Fort_Motte|Fort Motte]] on April 15.
sentence_315: On June 6, Brigadier General [[Andrew_Pickens_(congressman)|Andrew Pickens]] captured [[Siege_of_Augusta|Augusta]], leaving the British in Georgia confined to Charleston and Savannah.

sentence_317: Despite halting Greene's advance at the [[Battle_of_Eutaw_Springs|Battle of Eutaw Springs]] on September 8, Cornwallis withdrew to Charleston with little to show for his campaign.

sentence_320: This provided an alternative transportation route for the Continental Army, bypassing the British blockade of the Atlantic Coast.
sentence_321: The trade was organized by [[Oliver_Pollock|Oliver Pollock]], a successful merchant in Havana and New Orleans who was appointed US "commercial agent".
sentence_322: It also helped support the American [[Western_theater_of_the_American_Revolutionary_War|campaign in the west]]; in the 1778 [[Illinois_campaign|Illinois campaign]], militia under General [[George_Rogers_Clark|George Rogers Clark]] cleared the British from what was then part of [[Province_of_Quebec_(1763–1791)|Quebec]], creating [[Illinois_County,_Virginia|Illinois County, Virginia]].
sentence_323: Despite official neutrality, Gálvez initiated offensive operations against British outposts.
sentence_324: First, he cleared British garrisons in [[History_of_Baton_Rouge,_Louisiana#1763–1779:_British_period|Baton Rouge]], [[History_of_Louisiana#Spanish_interregnum_(1763–1803)|Louisiana]], [[Fort_Bute|Fort Bute]], and [[History_of_Natchez,_Mississippi#Colonial_history_(1716–1783)|Natchez]], [[History_of_Mississippi#Eurpean_colonial_period|Mississippi]], and captured five forts.
sentence_325: In doing so, Gálvez opened navigation on the Mississippi River north to the American settlement in Pittsburg.

sentence_342: An attempted breakout over the York River at [[Gloucester_County,_Virginia#Gloucester_County_formation_and_divisions|Gloucester Point]] failed due to bad weather.

sentence_346: Despite criticism from his junior officers, Cornwallis retained the confidence of his peers and later held a series of senior government positions; Clinton ultimately took most of the blame and spent the rest of his life in obscurity.
sentence_347: In the American Revolutionary War, the national strategies for victory and the commander operational choices for success were different for the two sides.
sentence_348: The [[Continental_Congress|Continental Congress]] had to field an army to outlast the will of the British Crown and its Parliament while maintaining its republican governance among constituent states.
sentence_349: In London, the British government had a track record of successfully subduing a rebelling countryside in both Scotland and Ireland by enlisting local landowners to administer county government of the realm, and admitted local [[House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom#19th_century|Members of Parliament]] for the [[History_of_Scotland#Union_with_England|Scots]] after 1704.
sentence_350: To win the "American war", the British Ministry would have needed to defeat the Continental Army early in the war and force the dissolution of Congress to allow the King's men to retake local colonial administration.
sentence_351: The revolt for and against colonial independence between British subjects in the [[Thirteen_Colonies|Thirteen Colonies]] of North America can be seen as three kinds of ongoing and interrelated warfare.
sentence_352: First, there was an economic war between a European state and its territory that was settled for its own economic strength, and Great Britain against France and Spain over the balance of power in North America.
sentence_353: By 1775, British American colonies supplied raw materials for British ships and one-third of its sailors and they purchased British-manufactured goods that maintained its industrial growth.
sentence_354: Newly enforced and expanded mercantile regulation restricted previous international Caribbean trade and colonial [[Laissez-faire|laissez-faire]] smuggling.
sentence_355: Second, there was a political civil war: a British constitutional war.
sentence_356: Across 1000 miles of Atlantic coastline, settled as much as 300 miles into the continental frontier, thirteen British colonies proclaimed themselves to be independent states from Parliament and united in a Congress of their delegates to declare their independence as "one people" in a political revolution from monarchy to republic.
sentence_357: This initiated a political struggle for British recognition assisted by the Whigs in Parliament, a military struggle assisted by state militias and the creation of [[George_Washington|George Washington]]'s national Continental Army, and an economic struggle for international free trade that threatened European systems of [[Mercantilism|mercantilism]].
sentence_358: It also began thirteen civil wars in every state, as there were in every colony and county, a mix of Patriots (Whigs) and Loyalists (Tories) who went to war among their neighbors.
sentence_359: These divided variously in each state along both ethnic and religious lines.
sentence_360: Every faction and element had veterans from the conflict between Britain and France fifteen years before, and there were officers and sergeants on every side that were practiced in the arts of both Indian frontier warfare and European infantry line formations of musketry.
