sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Albania_(disambiguation)|Albania (disambiguation)]].

table.value:

sentence_2: Albania ([[English|/ælˈbeɪniə, ɔːl-/]] (listen) a(w)l-BAY-nee-ə; [[Albanian_language|Albanian]]: Shqipëri or Shqipëria; [[Gheg_Albanian_language|Gheg Albanian]]: Shqipni or Shqipnia also Shqypni or Shqypnia), officially the Republic of Albania ([[Albanian_language|Albanian]]: Republika e Shqipërisë, pronounced [[Albanian|[ɾɛpuˈblika ɛ ʃcipəˈɾiːsə]]), is a country in Southeast Europe on the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic]] and [[Ionian_Sea|Ionian Sea]] within the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]].
sentence_3: It shares [[Land_border|land borders]] with [[Montenegro|Montenegro]] to the northwest, [[Kosovo|Kosovo]] to the northeast, [[North_Macedonia|North Macedonia]] to the east, [[Greece|Greece]] to the south and [[Maritime_border|maritime borders]] with Greece, Montenegro and Italy to the west.
sentence_4: [[Geography_of_Albania|Geographically]], Albania displays varied climatic, geological, hydrological, and morphological conditions, defined in an area of 28,748 km (11,100 sq mi).
sentence_5: It possesses significant diversity with the landscape ranging from the snow-capped mountains in the [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]] as well as the [[Korab|Korab]], [[Central_Mountain_Range,_Albania#Skanderbeg_Mountains|Skanderbeg]], Pindus and [[Ceraunian_Mountains|Ceraunian Mountains]] to the hot and sunny coasts of the [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Albanian Adriatic]] and [[Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast|Ionian Sea]] along the Mediterranean Sea.
sentence_6: [[History_of_Albania|Historically]], Albania has been inhabited by numerous civilisations such as the [[Illyrians|Illyrians]], [[Thracians|Thracians]], Ancient Greeks, [[Roman_Empire|Romans]], [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantines]], [[Venetian_Empire|Venetians]] and [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottomans]].
sentence_7: The [[Albanians|Albanians]] established the autonomous [[Principality_of_Arbër|Principality of Arbër]] in the 12th century.
sentence_8: The [[Kingdom_of_Albania_(medieval)|Kingdom of Albania]] and [[Principality_of_Albania_(medieval)|Principality of Albania]] formed between the 13th and 14th centuries.
sentence_9: Prior to the Ottoman conquest of Albania in the 15th century, the [[Skanderbeg#Rebellion_against_the_Ottomans|Albanian resistance]] to Ottoman expansion into Europe led by [[Gjergj_Kastrioti_Skanderbeg|Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg]] won them acclaim over most of Europe.
sentence_10: Between the 18th and 19th centuries, cultural developments, widely attributed to Albanians having gathered both spiritual and intellectual strength, conclusively led to the [[Albanian_Renaissance|Albanian Renaissance]].
sentence_11: After the defeat of the Ottomans in the [[Balkan_Wars|Balkan Wars]], the modern [[Nation_state|nation state]] of Albania [[Declaration_of_independence_of_Albania|declared independence]] in 1912.
sentence_12: In the 20th century, the [[Kingdom_of_Albania_(1928–39)|Kingdom of Albania]] was invaded by [[Kingdom_of_Italy|Italy]] which formed [[Albanian_Kingdom_(1939–43)|Greater Albania]] before becoming a [[Albanian_Kingdom_(1943–44)|protectorate]] of [[Nazi_Germany|Nazi Germany]].
sentence_13: [[Enver_Hoxha|Enver Hoxha]] formed [[People's_Socialist_Republic_of_Albania|Communist Albania]] after the [[Second_World_War|Second World War]] and launched the Albanians on a path of oppression and decades of isolation.
sentence_14: The [[Revolutions_of_1989|Revolutions of 1991]] concluded the fall of communism in Albania and eventually the establishment of the current Republic of Albania.
sentence_15: [[Politics_of_Albania|Politically]], Albania is a [[Unitary_state|unitary]] [[Parliamentary_system|parliamentary]] [[Constitutional_republic|constitutional republic]] and [[Developing_country|developing country]] with an upper-middle income [[Economy_of_Albania|economy]] dominated by the service sector, followed by manufacturing.
sentence_16: It went through a process of transition following the end of communism in 1990, from [[Centralized_planning|centralized planning]] to a [[Market-based_economy|market-based economy]].
sentence_17: Albania provides [[Universal_health_care|universal health care]] and free primary and secondary [[Education_in_Albania|education]] to its citizens.
sentence_18: Albania is a member of the United Nations, [[World_Bank|World Bank]], [[UNESCO|UNESCO]], [[NATO|NATO]], [[World_Trade_Organization|WTO]], [[Council_of_Europe|COE]], [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|OSCE]], and [[Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation|OIC]].
sentence_19: It is an [[Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union|official candidate]] for membership in the [[European_Union|European Union]].
sentence_20: It is one of the founding members of the Energy Community, including the Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation and [[Union_for_the_Mediterranean|Union for the Mediterranean]].
sentence_21: Main article: [[Names_of_the_Albanians_and_Albania|Etymology of Albania]]
sentence_22: The term Albania is the medieval Latin name of the country.
sentence_23: It may be derived from the [[Illyrian_tribe|Illyrian tribe]] of [[Albani_(Illyrian_tribe)|Albani]] ([[Albanian_language|Albanian]]: Albanët) recorded by [[Ptolemy|Ptolemy]], the geographer and astronomer from [[Alexandria|Alexandria]], who drafted a map in 150 AD which shows the city of [[Albanopolis|Albanopolis]] located northeast of [[Durrës|Durrës]].
sentence_24: The term may have a continuation in the name of a medieval settlement called [[Principality_of_Arbanon|Albanon]] or Arbanon, although it is not certain that this was the same place.
sentence_25: In his history written in the 10th century, the [[Byzantine|Byzantine]] historian [[Michael_Attaliates|Michael Attaliates]] was the first to refer to [[Albanoi|Albanoi]] as having taken part in a revolt against Constantinople in 1043 and to the Arbanitai as subjects of the Duke of [[Dyrrachium|Dyrrachium]].
sentence_26: During the [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]], the [[Albanians|Albanians]] called their country Arbëri or Arbëni and referred to themselves as [[Arbëreshë_people|Arbëreshë]] or Arbëneshë.
sentence_27: Nowadays, Albanians call their country Shqipëri or Shqipëria.
sentence_28: The words Shqipëri and Shqiptar are attested from 14th century onward, but it was only at the end of 17th and beginning of the early 18th centuries that the placename Shqipëria and the ethnic demonym Shqiptarë gradually replaced Arbëria and Arbëreshë amongst [[Albanian_language|Albanian]] speakers.
sentence_29: The two terms are popularly interpreted as "Land of the Eagles" and "Children of the Eagles".
sentence_30: Main article: [[History_of_Albania|History of Albania]]
sentence_31: See also: [[Timeline_of_Albanian_history|Timeline of Albanian history]]
sentence_32: Main article: [[Prehistoric_Albania|Prehistory of Albania]]
sentence_33: The first attested traces of [[Neanderthal|neanderthal]] presence in the territory of Albania dates back to the [[Middle_Paleolithic|middle]] and [[Upper_Paleolithic|upper Paleolithic]] period and were discovered in [[Xarrë|Xarrë]] and at [[Mount_Dajt|Mount Dajt]] in the adjacent region of [[Tirana|Tirana]].
sentence_34: Archaeological sites from this period include the [[Kamenica_Tumulus|Kamenica Tumulus]], [[Konispol|Konispol]] Cave and [[Pellumbas_Cave|Pellumbas Cave]].
sentence_35: The discovered objects in a cave near Xarrë include [[Flint|flint]] and [[Jasper|jasper]] objects along with fossilised animal bones, while those discoveries at Mount Dajt comprise bone and stone tools similar to those of the [[Aurignacian_culture|Aurignacian culture]].
sentence_36: They also demonstrate notable similarities with objects of the equivalent period found at Crvena Stijena in [[Montenegro|Montenegro]] and northwestern [[Greece|Greece]].
sentence_37: Multiple artefacts from the [[Iron_Age|Iron]] and [[Bronze_Age|Bronze Ages]] near [[Tumulus|tumulus]] burials have been unearthed in central and southern Albania, which has similar affinity with the sites in southwestern [[Macedonia_(region)|Macedonia]] and [[Lefkada|Lefkada]].
sentence_38: Archaeologists have come to the conclusion that these regions were inhabited from the middle of the third millennium BC by [[Indo-European_migrations|Indo-European people]] who spoke a [[Proto-Greek_language|Proto-Greek language]].
sentence_39: Hence, a part of this historical population later moved to [[Mycenae|Mycenae]] around 1600 BC and properly established the [[Mycenaean_Greece|Mycenaean civilisation]].
sentence_40: Main article: [[History_of_Albania#Antiquity|Antiquity in Albania]]
sentence_41: In ancient times, the incorporated territory of Albania was historically inhabited by [[Indo-European_people|Indo-European peoples]], among them numerous [[Illyrians|Illyrian]] [[Illyrian_tribe|tribes]], Ancient Greeks and [[Thracians|Thracians]].
sentence_42: In view of the Illyrian tribes, there is no evidence that these tribes used any collective nomenclature for themselves, while it is regarded to be unlikely that they used a common [[Endonym|endonym]].
sentence_43: The endonym Illyrians seems to be the name applied to a specific Illyrian tribe, which was the first to come in liaison with the Ancient Greeks resulting the endonym Illyrians to be applied pars pro toto to all people of similar language and customs.
sentence_44: The territory referred to as [[Illyria|Illyria]] corresponded roughly to the area east of the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic Sea]] in the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]] extending in the south to the mouth of the [[Vjosë|Vjosë]].
sentence_45: The first account of the Illyrian groups comes from [[Periplus_of_the_Euxine_Sea|Periplus of the Euxine Sea]], an ancient Greek text written in the middle of the 4th century BC.
sentence_46: The west was inhabited by the Thracian tribe of the [[Bryges|Bryges]] while the south was inhabited by the Ancient Greek-speaking tribe of the [[Chaonians|Chaonians]], whose capital was at [[Phoenice|Phoenice]].
sentence_47: Other colonies such as [[Apollonia_(Illyria)|Apollonia]], [[Epidamnos|Epidamnos]] and [[Amantia|Amantia]], were established by Ancient Greek city-states on the coast by the 7th century BC.
sentence_48: The Illyrian [[Ardiaei|Ardiaei]] tribe, centered in Montenegro, ruled over most of the territory of Albania.
sentence_49: Their [[Ardiaean_Kingdom|Ardiaean Kingdom]] reached its greatest extent under [[Agron_of_Illyria|King Agron]], the son of [[Pleuratus_II|Pleuratus II]].
sentence_50: Agron extended his rule over other neighboring tribes as well.
sentence_51: Following Agron's death in 230 BC, his wife, [[Teuta|Teuta]], inherited the Ardiaean kingdom.
sentence_52: Teuta's forces extended their operations further southward to the Ionian Sea.
sentence_53: In 229 BC, Rome declared war on the kingdom for extensively plundering Roman ships.
sentence_54: The war ended in Illyrian defeat in 227 BC.
sentence_55: Teuta was eventually succeeded by [[Gentius|Gentius]] in 181 BC.
sentence_56: Gentius clashed with the Romans in 168 BC, initiating the [[Third_Illyrian_War|Third Illyrian War]].
sentence_57: The conflict resulted in Roman conquest of the region by 167 BC.
sentence_58: The Romans split the region into three administrative divisions.
sentence_59: Main article: Albania in the Middle Ages
sentence_60: The [[Roman_Empire|Roman Empire]] was split in 395 upon the death of [[Theodosius_I|Theodosius I]] into an [[Eastern_Roman_Empire|Eastern]] and [[Western_Roman_Empire|Western Roman Empire]] in part because of the increasing pressure from threats during the [[Barbarian_Invasions|Barbarian Invasions]].
sentence_61: From the 6th century into the 7th century, the [[South_Slavs|Slavs]] crossed the [[Danube|Danube]] and largely absorbed the indigenous Ancient Greeks, Illyrians and Thracians in the [[Balkans|Balkans]]; thus, the Illyrians were mentioned for the last time in historical records in the 7th century.
sentence_62: In the 11th century, the [[Great_Schism_of_1054|Great Schism]] formalised the break of communion between the [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|Eastern Orthodox]] and [[Western_Catholic_Church|Western Catholic Church]] that is reflected in Albania through the emergence of a Catholic north and Orthodox south.
sentence_63: The Albanian people inhabited the west of [[Lake_Ochrida|Lake Ochrida]] and the upper valley of [[Shkumbin|River Shkumbin]] and established the [[Principality_of_Arbanon|Principality of Arbanon]] in 1190 under the leadership of [[Progon_of_Kruja|Progon of Kruja]].
sentence_64: The realm was succeeded by his sons [[Gjin_Progoni|Gjin]] and Dhimitri.
sentence_65: Upon the death of Dhimiter, the territory came under the rule of the Albanian-Greek [[Gregory_Kamonas|Gregory Kamonas]] and subsequently under the [[Golem_of_Kruja|Golem of Kruja]].
sentence_66: In the 13th century, the principality was dissolved.
sentence_67: Arbanon is considered to be the first sketch of an Albanian state, that retained a semi-autonomous status as the western extremity of the [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantine Empire]], under the Byzantine [[Doukas|Doukai]] of [[Despotate_of_Epirus|Epirus]] or [[Laskaris|Laskarids]] of [[Empire_of_Nicaea|Nicaea]].
sentence_68: Towards the end of the 12th and beginning of the 13th centuries, [[Kingdom_of_Serbia_(medieval)|Serbs]] and [[Venetian_Empire|Venetians]] started to take possession over the territory.
sentence_69: The ethnogenesis of the Albanians is uncertain; however the first undisputed mention of Albanians dates back in historical records from 1079 or 1080 in a work by [[Michael_Attaliates|Michael Attaliates]], who referred to the [[Albanoi|Albanoi]] as having taken part in a revolt against Constantinople.
sentence_70: At this point the Albanians were fully Christianized.
sentence_71: Few years after the dissolution of Arbanon, [[Charles_I_of_Naples|Charles of Anjou]] concluded an agreement with the Albanian rulers, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties.
sentence_72: In 1272, he established the [[Kingdom_of_Albania_(medieval)|Kingdom of Albania]] and conquered regions back from the [[Despotate_of_Epirus|Despotate of Epirus]].
sentence_73: The kingdom claimed all of central Albania territory from [[Dyrrhachium|Dyrrhachium]] along the Adriatic Sea coast down to [[Butrint|Butrint]].
sentence_74: A catholic political structure was a basis for the papal plans of spreading [[Catholicism|Catholicism]] in the Balkan Peninsula.
sentence_75: This plan found also the support of [[Helen_of_Anjou|Helen of Anjou]], a cousin of Charles of Anjou.
sentence_76: Around 30 Catholic churches and monasteries were built during her rule mainly in northern Albania.
sentence_77: Internal power struggles within the Byzantine Empire in the 14th century enabled Serbs' most powerful medieval ruler, [[Stefan_Dusan|Stefan Dusan]], to establish a [[Serbian_Empire|short-lived empire]] that included all of Albania except Durrës.
sentence_78: In 1367, various Albanian rulers established the [[Despotate_of_Arta|Despotate of Arta]].
sentence_79: During that time, several [[Albanian_principalities|Albanian principalities]] were created, notably the [[Balsha|Balsha]], [[Thopia_family|Thopia]], [[Kastrioti_Principality|Kastrioti]], [[Muzaka_family|Muzaka]] and [[Arianiti_family|Arianiti]].
sentence_80: In the first half of the 15th century, the [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]] invaded most of Albania, and the [[League_of_Lezhë|League of Lezhë]] was held under [[Skanderbeg|Skanderbeg]] as a ruler, who became the national hero of the Albanian medieval history.
sentence_81: Main article: Albania under the Ottoman Empire
sentence_82: See also: [[Skanderbeg#Rebellion_against_the_Ottomans|Albanian rebellion against the Ottoman Empire]]
sentence_83: Further information: [[League_of_Lezhë|League of Lezhë]]
sentence_84: With the [[Fall_of_Constantinople|fall of Constantinople]], the Ottoman Empire continued an extended period of conquest and expansion with its borders going deep into [[Ottoman_conquest_of_the_Balkans|Southeast Europe]].
sentence_85: They reached the [[Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast|Albanian Ionian Sea Coast]] in 1385 and erected their garrisons across [[Southern_Albania|Southern Albania]] in 1415 and then occupied most of Albania in 1431.
sentence_86: Thousands of Albanians consequently fled to Western Europe, particularly to Calabria, Naples, Ragusa and [[Kingdom_of_Sicily|Sicily]], whereby others sought protection at the often inaccessible [[Geography_of_Albania|Mountains of Albania]].
sentence_87: The Albanians, as Christians, were considered as an [[Rayah|inferior class]] of people, and as such they were subjected to heavy [[Jizya|taxes]] among others by the [[Devshirme|Devshirme]] system that allowed the [[Sultan|Sultan]] to collect a requisite percentage of Christian adolescents from their families to compose the [[Janissary|Janissary]].
sentence_88: The Ottoman conquest was also accompanied with the gradual process of [[Islamisation|Islamisation]] and the rapid construction of mosques which consequently modified the religious picture of Albania.
sentence_89: A prosperous and longstanding revolution erupted after the formation of the [[League_of_Lezhë|Assembly of Lezhë]] until the [[Siege_of_Shkodra|Siege of Shkodër]] under the leadership of [[Gjergj_Kastrioti_Skanderbeg|Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg]], multiple times defeating major Ottoman armies led by [[Sultan|Sultans]] Murad II and Mehmed II.
sentence_90: Skanderbeg managed to gather several of the Albanian principals, amongst them the [[Arianiti_family|Arianitis]], [[Dukagjini_family|Dukagjinis]], [[Zaharia_family|Zaharias]] and [[Thopia_family|Thopias]], and establish a centralised authority over most of the non-conquered territories, becoming the [[Skanderbeg|Lord of Albania]].
sentence_91: Skanderbeg consistently pursued the goal relentlessly but rather unsuccessfully to constitute a European coalition against the Ottomans.
sentence_92: He thwarted every attempt by the Ottomans to regain Albania, which they envisioned as a springboard for the invasion of Italy and Western Europe.
sentence_93: His unequal fight against them won the esteem of Europe also among others financial and military aid from the [[Papacy|Papacy]] and Naples, [[Republic_of_Venice|Venice]] and Ragusa.
sentence_94: When the Ottomans were gaining a firm foothold in the region, Albanian towns were organised into four principal [[Sanjaks|sanjaks]].
sentence_95: The government fostered trade by settling a sizeable Jewish colony of refugees fleeing persecution in Spain.
sentence_96: The city of [[Vlorë|Vlorë]] saw passing through its ports imported merchandise from Europe such as velvets, cotton goods, mohairs, carpets, spices and leather from [[Bursa|Bursa]] and Constantinople.
sentence_97: Some citizens of Vlorë even had business associates throughout Europe.
sentence_98: The phenomenon of Islamisation among the Albanians became primarily widespread from the 17th century and continued into the 18th century.
sentence_99: Islam offered them equal opportunities and advancement within the Ottoman Empire.
sentence_100: However, motives for conversion were, according to some scholars, diverse depending on the context though the lack of source material does not help when investigating such issues.
sentence_101: Because of increasing suppression of Catholicism, mostly catholic Albanians converted in the 17th century, while orthodox Albanians followed suit mainly in the following century.
sentence_102: Since the Albanians were seen as strategically important, they made up a significant proportion of the [[Ottoman_military|Ottoman military]] and bureaucracy.
sentence_103: A couple of Muslim Albanians attained important political and military positions who culturally contributed to the broader Muslim world.
sentence_104: Enjoying this privileged position, they held various high administrative positions with over two dozen Albanian [[Grand_Viziers|Grand Viziers]] among others members of the prominent [[Köprülü_family|Köprülü family]], [[Zagan_Pasha|Zagan Pasha]], [[Muhammad_Ali_of_Egypt|Muhammad Ali of Egypt]] and [[Ali_Pasha_of_Tepelena|Ali Pasha of Tepelena]] however, two sultans such as [[Bayezid_II|Bayezid II]] and [[Mehmed_III|Mehmed III]] had both mothers of Albanian origin.
sentence_105: Main article: [[Albanian_Renaissance|Albanian Renaissance]]
sentence_106: See also: [[League_of_Prizren|League of Prizren]]
sentence_107: The [[Albanian_Renaissance|Albanian Renaissance]] was a period with its roots in the late 18th century and continuing into the 19th century, during which the Albanian people gathered spiritual and intellectual strength for an independent cultural and political life within an [[Independent_Albania|independent nation]].
sentence_108: Modern [[Albanian_culture|Albanian culture]] flourished too, especially [[Albanian_literature|Albanian literature]] and [[Albanian_art|arts]], and was frequently linked to the influences of the [[Romanticism|Romanticism]] and [[Age_of_Enlightenment|Enlightenment]] principles.
sentence_109: Prior to the rise of nationalism, Albania was under the rule of the Ottoman Empire for almost five centuries, and Ottoman authorities suppressed any expression of national unity or conscience by the Albanian people.
sentence_110: Through literature, Albanians started to make a conscious effort to awaken feelings of pride and unity among their people that would call to mind the rich history and hopes for a more decent future.
sentence_111: The victory of Russia over the Ottoman Empire following the [[Russian-Ottoman_War|Russian-Ottoman Wars]] resulted the execution of the Treaty of San Stefano which overlooked to assign Albanian-populated lands to the Slavic and Greek neighbours.
sentence_112: However, the [[United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland|United Kingdom]] and [[Austro-Hungarian_Empire|Austro-Hungarian Empire]] consequently blocked the arrangement and caused the [[Treaty_of_Berlin_(1878)|Treaty of Berlin]].
sentence_113: From this point, Albanians started to organise themselves with the goal to protect and unite the Albanian-populated lands into a unitary nation, leading to the formation of the [[League_of_Prizren|League of Prizren]].
sentence_114: The league had initially the assistance of the Ottoman authorities whose position was based on the religious solidarity of Muslim people and landlords connected with the [[Ottoman_Porte|Ottoman administration]].
sentence_115: They favoured and protected the Muslim solidarity and called for defense of Muslim lands simultaneously constituting the reason for titling the league [[League_of_Prizren#Formation|Committee of the Real Muslims]].
sentence_116: Approximately 300 Muslims participated in the assembly composed by delegates from Bosnia, the [[Sanjakbey|administrator]] of the [[Sanjak_of_Prizren|Sanjak of Prizren]] as representatives of the central authorities and no delegates from Vilayet of Scutari.
sentence_117: Signed by only 47 Muslim deputies, the league issued the [[Kararname_(League_of_Prizren)|Kararname]] that contained a proclamation that the people from northern Albania, [[Epirus|Epirus]] and [[Bosnia_and_Herzegovina|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] are willing to defend the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire by all possible means against the troops of Bulgaria, [[Kingdom_of_Serbia|Serbia]] and [[Kingdom_of_Montenegro|Montenegro]].
sentence_118: Ottomans authorities cancelled their assistance when the league, under [[Abdyl_Frashëri|Abdyl Frashëri]], became focused on working toward Albanian autonomy and requested merging four [[Ottoman_vilayet|vilayets]], including Kosovo, Shkodër, [[Monastir_Vilayet|Monastir]] and [[Janina_Vilayet|Ioannina]], into an unified vilayet, the [[Albanian_Vilayet|Albanian Vilayet]].
sentence_119: The league used military force to prevent the annexing areas of [[Plav_Municipality|Plav]] and [[Gusinje|Gusinje]] assigned to Montenegro.
sentence_120: After several successful battles with Montenegrin troops, such as the [[Battle_of_Novšiće|Battle of Novšiće]], the league was forced to retreat from their contested regions.
sentence_121: The league was later defeated by the Ottoman army sent by the sultan.
sentence_122: Main article: [[Independent_Albania|Independent Albania]]
sentence_123: See also: [[Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence|Albanian Declaration of Independence]]
sentence_124: Albania [[Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence|declared independence]] from the Ottoman Empire on 28 November 1912, accompanied with the establishment of the [[Senate_of_Albania|Senate]] and [[Provisional_Government_of_Albania|Government]] by the [[Assembly_of_Vlorë|Assembly of Vlorë]] on 4 December 1912.
sentence_125: Its sovereignty was recognised by the [[London_Conference_of_1912–1913|Conference of London]].
sentence_126: On 29 July 1913, the [[Treaty_of_London_(1913)|Treaty of London]] delineated the borders of the country and its neighbors, leaving many Albanians outside Albania, predominantly [[Partition_(politics)|partitioned]] between [[Kingdom_of_Montenegro|Montenegro]], [[Kingdom_of_Serbia|Serbia]] and [[Kingdom_of_Greece|Greece]].
sentence_127: Headquartered in Vlorë, the [[International_Commission_of_Control|International Commission of Control]] was established on 15 October 1913 to take care of the administration of newly established Albania, until its own political institutions were in order.
sentence_128: The [[International_Gendarmerie|International Gendarmerie]] was established as the first law enforcement agency of the Principality of Albania.
sentence_129: In November, the first gendarmerie members arrived in the country.
sentence_130: Prince of Albania [[Wilhelm_of_Wied|Wilhelm of Wied]] (Princ Vilhelm Vidi) was selected as the first prince of the principality.
sentence_131: On 7 March, he arrived in the provisional capital of [[Durrës|Durrës]] and started to organise his government, appointing Turhan Pasha Përmeti to form the first Albanian cabinet.
sentence_132: In November 1913, the Albanian pro-Ottoman forces had offered the throne of Albania to the Ottoman war Minister of Albanian origin, [[Ahmed_Izzet_Pasha|Ahmed Izzet Pasha]].
sentence_133: The pro-Ottoman peasants believed that the new regime was a tool of the six Christian [[Great_Power|Great Powers]] and local landowners, that owned half of the arable land.
sentence_134: In February 1914, the [[Autonomous_Republic_of_Northern_Epirus|Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus]] was proclaimed in [[Gjirokastër|Gjirokastër]] by the local [[Greeks_in_Albania|Greek population]] against incorporation to Albania.
sentence_135: This initiative was short lived, and in 1921 the southern provinces were incorporated into the Albanian Principality.
sentence_136: Meanwhile, the [[Peasant_Revolt_in_Albania|revolt of Albanian peasants]] against the new Albanian regime erupted under the leadership of the group of Muslim clerics gathered around [[Essad_Pasha_Toptani|Essad Pasha Toptani]], who proclaimed himself the savior of Albania and Islam.
sentence_137: In order to gain support of the [[Mirdita|Mirdita]] Catholic volunteers from the northern part of Albania, Prince [[Wilhelm_of_Wied|Wied]] appointed their leader, [[Prênk_Bibë_Doda|Prênk Bibë Doda]], to be the foreign minister of the Principality of Albania.
sentence_138: In May and June 1914, the International Gendarmerie was joined by [[Isa_Boletini|Isa Boletini]] and his men, mostly from [[Kosovo|Kosovo]], and northern [[Mirdita|Mirdita]] Catholics, were defeated by the rebels who captured most of Central Albania by the end of August 1914.
sentence_139: The regime of Prince Wied collapsed, and he left the country on 3 September 1914.
sentence_140: Main article: First Republic of Albania
sentence_141: See also: [[World_War_II_in_Albania|World War II in Albania]]
sentence_142: Further information: [[The_Holocaust_in_Albania|The Holocaust in Albania]] and [[List_of_Albanian_Righteous_Among_the_Nations|Albanian Righteous Among the Nations]]
sentence_143: Following the end of the government of [[Fan_Noli|Fan Noli]], the parliament adopted a new constitution and proclaimed the country as a parliamentary republic in which King [[Zog_I_of_Albania|Zog I of Albania]] (Ahmet Muhtar Zogu) served as the head of state for a seven-year term.
sentence_144: Immediately after, [[Tirana|Tirana]] was endorsed officially as the country's permanent capital.
sentence_145: The politics of Zogu was authoritarian and conservative with the primary aim of the maintenance of stability and order.
sentence_146: He was forced to adopt a policy of cooperation with Italy where a pact had been signed between both countries, whereby Italy gained a monopoly on shipping and trade concessions.
sentence_147: Italians exercised control over nearly every Albanian official through money and patronage.
sentence_148: In 1928, the country was eventually replaced by [[Kingdom_of_Albania_(1928–1939)|another monarchy]] with a strong support by the [[Italian_Fascism|fascist regime]] of Italy however, both maintained close relations until the [[Italian_invasion_of_Albania|Italian invasion]] of the country.
sentence_149: Zogu remained a conservative but initiated reforms and placed great emphasis on the development of infrastructure.
sentence_150: In an attempt at social modernisation, the custom of adding one's region to one's name was dropped.
sentence_151: He also made donations of land to international organisations for the building of schools and hospitals.
sentence_152: The armed forces were trained and supervised by instructors from Italy, and as a counterweight, he kept British officers in the Gendarmerie despite strong Italian pressure to remove them.
sentence_153: After being militarily occupied by Italy from 1939 until 1943, the [[Albanian_Kingdom_(1939–43)|Kingdom of Albania]] was a [[Protectorate|protectorate]] and a dependency of the [[Kingdom_of_Italy|Kingdom of Italy]] governed by [[Victor_Emmanuel_III_of_Italy|Victor Emmanuel III]] and his government.
sentence_154: In October 1940, Albania served as a staging ground for an unsuccessful Italian [[Greco-Italian_War|invasion of Greece]].
sentence_155: A counterattack resulted in a sizeable portion of southern Albania coming under Greek military control until April 1941 when Greece capitulated during the [[Battle_of_Greece|German invasion]].
sentence_156: In April 1941, territories of [[Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] with substantial Albanian population were annexed to Albania inclusively western Macedonia, a strip of eastern Montenegro, the town of [[Tutin,_Serbia|Tutin]] in central Serbia and most of Kosovo.
sentence_157: Germans started to occupy the country in September 1943 and subsequently announced that they would recognise the independence of a neutral Albania and set about organising a new government, military and law enforcement.
sentence_158: [[Balli_Kombëtar|Balli Kombëtar]], which had fought against Italy, formed a neutral government and side by side with the Germans fought against the communist-led [[National_Liberation_Movement_(Albania)|National Liberation Movement]] of Albania.
sentence_159: During the last years of the war, the country fell into a civil war-like state between the communists and nationalists.
sentence_160: The communists defeated the last anti-communist forces in the south in 1944.
sentence_161: Before the end of November, the main German troops had withdrawn from Tirana, and the communists took control by attacking it.
sentence_162: The partisans entirely liberated the country from German occupation on 29 November 1944.
sentence_163: A provisional government, which the communists had formed at Berat in October, administered Albania with [[Enver_Hoxha|Enver Hoxha]] as the head of government.
sentence_164: By the end of the [[Second_World_War|Second World War]], the main military and political force of the nation, the Communist party sent forces to northern Albania against the nationalists to eliminate its rivals.
sentence_165: They faced open resistance in [[Nikaj-MÃ«rtur|Nikaj-MÃ«rtur]], [[Dukagjin_highlands|Dukagjin]] and [[Kelmendi_(tribe)|Kelmend]] led by [[Prek_Cali|Prek Cali]].
sentence_166: On 15 January 1945, a clash took place between partisans of the first Brigade and nationalist forces at the Tamara Bridge, resulting in the defeat of the nationalist forces.
sentence_167: About 150 [[Kelmendi_(tribe)|Kelmendi]] people were killed or tortured.
sentence_168: This event was the starting point of many other issues which took place during [[Enver_Hoxha|Enver Hoxha]]'s dictatorship.
sentence_169: [[Class_conflict|Class struggle]] was strictly applied, human freedom and human rights were denied.
sentence_170: The Kelmend region was almost isolated by both the border and by a lack of roads for another 20 years, the institution of [[Agricultural_cooperative|agricultural cooperatives]] brought about economic decline.
sentence_171: Many Kelmendi people fled, and some were executed trying to cross the border.
sentence_172: Main article: [[Communism_in_Albania|Communism in Albania]]
sentence_173: Further information: [[Bunkers_in_Albania|Bunkers in Albania]]
sentence_174: In the aftermath of World War II and the defeat of [[Nazi_Germany|Nazi Germany]], the country became initially a satellite state of the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]], and Enver Hoxha emerged as the leader of the newly established [[People's_Socialist_Republic_of_Albania|People's Republic of Albania]].
sentence_175: Soviet-Albanian relations [[Soviet–Albanian_split|began to deteriorate]] after Stalin's death in 1953.
sentence_176: At this point, the country started to develop foreign relations with other communist countries, among others with the [[People's_Republic_of_China|People's Republic of China]].
sentence_177: During this period, the country experienced an increasing industrialisation and urbanisation, a rapid collectivisation and economic growth which led to a higher standard of living.
sentence_178: The government called for the development of infrastructure and most notably the introduction of a [[Hekurudha_Shqiptare|railway system]] that completely revamped transportation.
sentence_179: The new land reform laws were passed granting ownership of the land to the workers and peasants who tilled it.
sentence_180: Agriculture became [[Worker_cooperative|cooperative]], and production increased significantly, leading to the country becoming agriculturally self-sufficient.
sentence_181: In the field of education, illiteracy was eliminated among the country's adult population.
sentence_182: The government also oversaw the emancipation of women and the expansion of healthcare and education throughout the country.
sentence_183: The average annual increase in the country's national income was 29% and 56% higher than the world and European average, respectively.
sentence_184: The nation incurred large debts initially with Yugoslavia until 1948, then the Soviet Union until 1961 and China from the middle of the 1950s.
sentence_185: The constitution of the communist regime did not allow taxes on individuals, instead, taxes were imposed on cooperatives and other organisations, with much the same effect.
sentence_186: Today a secular state without any [[Official_religion|official religion]], [[Freedom_of_religion_in_Albania|religious freedoms]] and practices were severely curtailed during the communist era with all forms of worship being outlawed.
sentence_187: In 1945, the Agrarian Reform Law meant that large swaths of property owned by religious groups were nationalised, mostly the [[Waqfs|waqfs]] along with the estates of mosques, tekkes, monasteries and dioceses.
sentence_188: Many believers, along with the [[Ulema|ulema]] and many priests, were arrested and executed.
sentence_189: In 1949, a new Decree on Religious Communities required that all their activities be sanctioned by the state alone.
sentence_190: After hundreds of mosques and dozens of Islamic libraries containing priceless manuscripts were destroyed, Hoxha proclaimed Albania the world's first [[State_atheism|atheist state]] in 1967.
sentence_191: The churches had not been spared either and many were converted into cultural centres for young people.
sentence_192: A 1967 law banned all fascist, religious, and antisocialist activity and propaganda.
sentence_193: Preaching religion carried a three to ten-year prison sentence.
sentence_194: Nonetheless, many Albanians continued to practice their beliefs secretly.
sentence_195: The anti-religious policy of Hoxha attained its most fundamental legal and political expression a decade later: "The state recognizes no religion", states the 1976 constitution, "and supports and carries out atheistic propaganda in order to implant a scientific materialistic world outlook in people".
sentence_196: Main article: Fall of communism in Albania
sentence_197: Further information: Pyramid schemes and [[Albanian_civil_war_of_1997|civil war of 1997]]
sentence_198: After forty years of communism and [[Isolationism|isolation]] as well as the [[Revolutions_of_1989|revolutions of 1989]], people, most notably students, became politically active and campaigned against the government that led to the transformation of the existing order.
sentence_199: Following the popular support in the first multi-party elections of [[Albanian_parliamentary_election,_1991|1991]], the communists retained a stronghold in the [[Parliament_of_Albania|parliament]] until the victory in the [[Albanian_parliamentary_election,_1992|general elections]] of 1992 led by the [[Democratic_Party_of_Albania|Democratic Party]].
sentence_200: Considerable economic and financial resources were devoted to pyramid schemes that were widely supported by the government.
sentence_201: The schemes swept up somewhere between one sixth and one third of the population of the country.
sentence_202: Despite the warnings of the [[International_Monetary_Fund|International Monetary Fund]], [[Sali_Berisha|Sali Berisha]] defended the schemes as large investment firms, leading more people to redirect their remittances and sell their homes and cattle for cash to deposit in the schemes.
sentence_203: The schemes began to collapse in late 1996, leading many of the investors to join initially peaceful protests against the government, requesting their money back.
sentence_204: The protests turned violent in February 1997 as government forces responded with fire.
sentence_205: In March, the Police and Republican Guard deserted, leaving their armouries open.
sentence_206: These were promptly emptied by militias and criminal gangs.
sentence_207: The resulting [[Albanian_Civil_War|civil war]] caused a wave of evacuations of foreign nationals and refugees.
sentence_208: The crisis led both Aleksandër Meksi and [[Sali_Berisha|Sali Berisha]] to resign from office in the wake of the general election.
sentence_209: In April 1997, [[Operation_Alba|Operation Alba]], a UN peacekeeping force led by Italy, entered the country with two goals exclusively to assist with the evacuation of expatriates and to secure the ground for international organisations.
sentence_210: The main international organisation that was involved was the [[Western_European_Union|Western European Union]]'s [[Albanian_civil_war_of_1997#International_intervention|multinational]] [[Albanian_Police|Albanian Police]] element, which worked with the government to restructure the [[Judicial_system_of_Albania|judicial system]] and simultaneously the Albanian police.
sentence_211: See also: [[Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union|Accession of Albania to the EU]] and [[Albania–NATO_relations|NATO]]
sentence_212: Further information: [[2019_Albania_earthquake|2019 Albania earthquake]] and [[COVID-19_pandemic_in_Albania|COVID-19 pandemic in Albania]]
sentence_213: Following the disintegration of the [[Communist_Albania|communist system]], Albania plunged itself through an active process of Westernisation and increased workload in the process of its accession to the [[European_Union|European Union]] (EU) and [[North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organisation|North Atlantic Treaty Organisation]] (NATO).
sentence_214: In 2009, the country, along with [[Croatia|Croatia]], gained [[Albania–NATO_relations|active membership]] for accession to the NATO simultaneously becoming among the first countries in Southeast Europe to enter the partnership for peace programme.
sentence_215: Out side of it, it also [[Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union|applied]] to join the European Union on 28 April 2009 however, it received, upon its application, an [[Future_enlargement_of_the_European_Union|official candidate status]] on 24 June 2014.
sentence_216: Following its application, the EU twice rejected the country's accession to its EU membership.
sentence_217: Between 2013 and 2017, [[Edi_Rama|Edi Rama]] of the [[Socialist_Party_of_Albania|Socialist Party]] won both the [[Albanian_parliamentary_election,_2013|2013]] and [[Albanian_parliamentary_election,_2017|2017 parliamentary elections]].
sentence_218: As a [[Prime_Minister_of_Albania|Prime Minister]], he implemented numerous reforms focused on [[Modernism|modernising]] the [[Economy_of_Albania|economy]], as well as democratising the state institutions, including the country's [[Judiciary_of_Albania|judiciary]] and [[Law_enforcement_in_Albania|law enforcement]].
sentence_219: Unemployment has been steadily reduced while having the 4th lowest [[List_of_countries_by_unemployment_rate|unemployment rate]] in the Balkans.
sentence_220: Rama has also placed [[Gender_equality|gender equality]] at the center of its agenda, since 2017 almost 50% of the ministers are female, making it the largest number of women serving in the country's history.
sentence_221: On 26 November 2019, a 6.4 [[Moment_magnitude_scale|magnitude]] [[Earthquake|earthquake]] ravaged Albania with the [[Epicenter|epicenter]] positioned 16 km (10 mi) southwest of the town of [[Mamurras|Mamurras]].
sentence_222: The tremor was felt in [[Tirana|Tirana]] and in places as far away as [[Taranto|Taranto]], Italy, and [[Belgrade|Belgrade]], Serbia, thus, the most affected areas were the coastal city of [[Durrës|Durrës]] and [[Kodër-Thumanë|Kodër-Thumanë]].
sentence_223: Response to the earthquake included substantial humanitarian aid, designed to help the Albanian people, from the [[Albanian_diaspora|Albanian diaspora]] and several countries [[2019_Albania_earthquake#International_assistance|around the world]].
sentence_224: On 9 March 2020, the [[COVID-19_pandemic_in_Albania|coronavirus disease 2019]] (COVID-19) was confirmed to have spread to Albania.
sentence_225: From March to June, the government declared a state of emergency, as a measure to limit the rapid spread of the pandemic in the country.
sentence_226: On 28 July 2020, the country reported its 5 thousandth case, at this time, there had been nearly 150 reported deaths.
sentence_227: Main article: [[Geography_of_Albania|Geography of Albania]]
sentence_228: Albania is defined in an area of 28,748 km (11,100 sq mi) and is located on the [[Balkan_Peninsula|Balkan Peninsula]] in [[Southern_Europe|South]] and [[Southeast_Europe|Southeast Europe]].
sentence_229: Its shoreline faces the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic Sea]] to the northwest and the [[Ionian_Sea|Ionian Sea]] to the southwest along the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]].
sentence_230: Albania lies between latitudes [[42nd_parallel_north|42°]] and [[39th_parallel_north|39° N]], and longitudes [[21st_meridian_east|21°]] and [[19th_meridian_east|19° E]].
sentence_231: Its northernmost point is Vërmosh at 42° 35' 34" northern latitude; the southernmost is [[Konispol|Konispol]] at 39° 40' 0" northern latitude; the westernmost point is [[Sazan_Island|Sazan]] at 19° 16' 50" eastern longitude; and the easternmost point is [[Vërnik|Vërnik]] at 21° 1' 26" eastern longitude.
sentence_232: The highest point is [[Mount_Korab|Mount Korab]] at 2,764 m (9,068.24 ft) [[Metres_above_the_Adriatic|above the Adriatic]]; the lowest point is the Mediterranean Sea at 0 m (0.00 ft).
sentence_233: The distance from the east to west is 148 km (92 mi) and from the north to south about 340 km (211 mi).
sentence_234: For a small country, much of Albania rises into mountains and hills that run in different directions across the length and breadth of its territory.
sentence_235: The most extensive mountain ranges are the [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]] in the north, the [[Korab|Korab Mountains]] in the east, the Pindus Mountains in the southeast, the [[Ceraunian_Mountains|Ceraunian Mountains]] in the southwest and the Skanderbeg Mountains in the centre.
sentence_236: Perhaps the most remarkable feature of the country is the presence of numerous important lakes.
sentence_237: The [[Lake_of_Shkodër|Lake of Shkodër]] is the largest lake in [[List_of_largest_lakes_of_Europe|Southern Europe]] and located in northwest.
sentence_238: In the [[Albanian_Ohrid_Lake_Coast|southeast]] rises the [[Lake_of_Ohrid|Lake of Ohrid]] that is one of the oldest continuously existing lakes in the world.
sentence_239: Farther south extends the [[Prespa_Lake|Large]] and [[Small_Prespa_Lake|Small Lake of Prespa]], which are among the highest positioned lakes in the Balkans.
sentence_240: Rivers rise mostly in the east of Albania and discharge into the Adriatic Sea but as well as into the Ionian Sea to a lesser extent.
sentence_241: The longest river in the country, measured from its mouth to its source, is the [[Drin_River|Drin]] that starts at the confluence of its two headwaters, the [[Black_Drin|Black]] and White Drin.
sentence_242: Of particular concern is the [[Vjosë|Vjosë]], which represents one of the last intact large river systems in Europe.
sentence_243: Main article: [[Climate_of_Albania|Climate of Albania]]
sentence_244: The [[Climate_of_Albania|climate]] in the country is extremely variable and diverse owing to the differences in latitude, longitude and altitude.
sentence_245: Albania experiences predominantly a [[Mediterranean_climate|mediterranean]] and continental climate, with four distinct seasons.
sentence_246: Defined by the [[Köppen_climate_classification|Köppen classification]], it accommodates five major climatic types ranging from mediterranean and subtropical in the western half to [[Oceanic_climate|oceanic]], [[Humid_continental_climate|continental]] and [[Subarctic_climate|subarctic]] in the eastern half of Albania.
sentence_247: The warmest areas of the country are immediately placed along the [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Adriatic]] and [[Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast|Ionian Sea Coasts]].
sentence_248: On the contrary, the coldest areas are positioned within the [[Northern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|northern]] and [[Central_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|eastern highlands]].
sentence_249: The mean monthly temperature ranges between −1 [[Celsius|°C]] (30 [[Fahrenheit|°F]]) in winter to 21.8 °C (71.2 °F) in summer.
sentence_250: The highest temperature of 43.9 °C (111.0 °F) was recorded in [[Kuçovë|Kuçovë]] on 18 July 1973.
sentence_251: The lowest temperature of −29 °C (−20 °F) was registered in the village of Shtyllë, [[Librazhd|Librazhd]] on 9 January 2017.
sentence_252: Rainfall naturally varies from season to season and from year to year.
sentence_253: The country receives most of the [[Precipitation_(meteorology)|precipitation]] in winter months and less in summer months.
sentence_254: The average precipitation is about 1,485 millimetres (58.5 inches).
sentence_255: The mean annual precipitation ranges between 600 millimetres (24 inches) and 3,000 millimetres (120 inches) depending on geographical location.
sentence_256: The [[Northern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|northwestern]] and [[Southern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|southeastern highlands]] receive the intenser amount of precipitation, whilst the [[Northern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|northeastern]] and [[Southern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)|southwestern highlands]] as well as the [[Western_Lowlands|Western Lowlands]] the more limited amount.
sentence_257: The [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]] in the far north of the country are considered to be among the most humid regions of Europe, receiving at least 3,100 mm (122.0 in) of rain annually.
sentence_258: An expedition from the [[University_of_Colorado|University of Colorado]] discovered four [[Glacier|glaciers]] within these mountains at a relatively low altitude of 2,000 metres (6,600 ft), which is almost virtually for such a southerly latitude.
sentence_259: Snowfall occurs frequently in winter in the highlands of the country, particularly on the mountains in the north and east, including the [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]] and [[Korab|Korab]] Mountains.
sentence_260: Snow also falls on the coastal areas in the southwest almost every winter such as in the [[Ceraunian_Mountains|Ceraunian Mountains]], where it can lie even beyond March.
sentence_261: Main article: [[Biodiversity_of_Albania|Biodiversity of Albania]]
sentence_262: See also: [[List_of_ecoregions_in_Albania|Ecoregions in Albania]]
sentence_263: A [[Biodiversity_hotspot|biodiversity hotspot]], Albania possesses an exceptionally rich and contrasting [[Biodiversity|biodiversity]] on account of its geographical location at the centre of the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]] and the great diversity in its [[Climatic|climatic]], geological and hydrological conditions.
sentence_264: Because of remoteness, the mountains and hills of Albania are endowed with forests, trees and grasses that are essential to the lives for a wide variety of animals, among others for two of the most [[Endangered_species|endangered species]] of the country, the [[Balkan_lynx|lynx]] and [[Brown_bear|brown bear]], as well as the [[Wildcat|wildcat]], [[Gray_wolf|gray wolf]], [[Red_fox|red fox]], [[Golden_jackal|golden jackal]], [[Egyptian_vulture|egyptian vulture]] and [[Golden_eagle|golden eagle]], the latter constituting the national animal of the country.
sentence_265: The estuaries, wetlands and lakes are extraordinarily important for the [[Greater_flamingo|greater flamingo]], pygmy cormorant and the extremely rare and perhaps the most iconic bird of the country, the [[Dalmatian_pelican|dalmatian pelican]].
sentence_266: Of particular importance are the [[Mediterranean_monk_seal|mediterranean monk seal]], [[Loggerhead_sea_turtle|loggerhead sea turtle]] and [[Green_sea_turtle|green sea turtle]] that use to nest on the country's coastal waters and shores.
sentence_267: In terms of [[Phytogeography|phytogeography]], Albania is part of the Boreal Kingdom and stretches specifically within the [[Illyria|Illyrian]] province of the Circumboreal and Mediterranean Region.
sentence_268: Its territory can be subdivided into four terrestrial [[Ecoregion|ecoregions]] of the [[Palearctic_realm|Palearctic realm]] namely within the [[Illyrian_deciduous_forests|Illyrian deciduous forests]], [[Balkan_mixed_forests|Balkan mixed forests]], [[Pindus_Mountains_mixed_forests|Pindus Mountains mixed forests]] and [[Dinaric_Mountains_mixed_forests|Dinaric Mountains mixed forests]].
sentence_269: Approximately 3,500 different species of plants can be found in Albania which refers principally to a [[Mediterranean|Mediterranean]] and [[Eurasia|Eurasian]] character.
sentence_270: The country maintains a vibrant tradition of herbal and [[Medicinal_Purposes|medicinal practices]].
sentence_271: At the minimum 300 plants growing locally are used in the preparation of herbs and medicines.
sentence_272: The trees within the forests are primarily made up of [[Fir|fir]], [[Oak|oak]], [[Beech|beech]] and [[Pine|pine]].
sentence_273: In the 2010 [[Environmental_Performance_Index|Environmental Performance Index]], Albania was ranked 23rd out of 163 countries in the world.
sentence_274: In 2012, the country advanced from 23rd to 15th, whereas it had the highest ranking in [[Southern_Europe|South]] and Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
sentence_275: The country was the 24th greenest country in the world according to the 2005 [[Environmental_Sustainability_Index|Environmental Sustainability Index]].
sentence_276: Nevertheless, for 2016, the country was ranked the 13th best performing country on the [[Happy_Planet_Index|Happy Planet Index]] by the United Nations.
sentence_277: Main article: [[Protected_areas_of_Albania|Protected areas of Albania]]
sentence_278: See also: [[National_parks_of_Albania|National parks of Albania]]
sentence_279: The [[Protected_areas_of_Albania|protected areas of Albania]] are the system through the [[Albanian_government|Albanian government]] protects, maintains and displays some of the country's most impressive and treasured [[Natural_environment|environments]].
sentence_280: There are 15 [[National_park|national parks]], 4 [[Ramsar_site|ramsar sites]], 1 [[Biosphere_reserve|biosphere reserve]] and 786 other types of conservation reserves across Albania all of them depicting a huge variety of natural sceneries ranging from imposing mountains to picturesque [[Coast|coasts]].
sentence_281: Albania has fifteen officially designated [[National_parks_of_Albania|national parks]] scattered across its territory.
sentence_282: Encircled by numerous [[Two-thousander|two-thousanders]], [[Valbonë_Valley_National_Park|Valbonë Valley National Park]] and [[Theth_National_Park|Theth National Park]] cover a combined territory of 106.3 square kilometres (41.0 sq mi) within the rugged [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]] in northern Albania.
sentence_283: [[Shebenik-Jabllanicë_National_Park|Shebenik-Jabllanicë National Park]] and [[Prespa_National_Park_(Albania)|Prespa National Park]] protect the spectacular mountainous scenery of eastern Albania as well as the country's sections of the [[Prespa_Lake|Great]] and [[Small_Prespa_Lake|Small Lakes of Prespa]].
sentence_284: [[Divjakë-Karavasta_National_Park|Divjakë-Karavasta National Park]] extends along the central [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast]] and possesses one of the largest lagoons in the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]], the [[Lagoon_of_Karavasta|Lagoon of Karavasta]].
sentence_285: The [[Ceraunian_Mountains|Ceraunian Mountains]] in southern Albania, rising immediately along the [[Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast|Albanian Ionian Sea Coast]], characterises the topographical picture of [[Llogara_National_Park|Llogara National Park]] and continue on the [[Karaburun_Peninsula_(Albania)|Peninsula of Karaburun]] within the [[Karaburun-Sazan_Marine_Park|Karaburun-Sazan Marine Park]].
sentence_286: Further south sprawls the [[Butrint_National_Park|Butrint National Park]] on a peninsula that is surrounded by the [[Lake_Butrint|Lake of Butrint]] and Channel of Vivari on the eastern half of the [[Straits_of_Corfu|Straits of Corfu]].
sentence_287: [[Dajti_National_Park|Dajti National Park]] is equipped with a cable car and trails to some spectacular scenery is a popular retreat in the capital, Tirana.
sentence_288: Main article: [[Politics_of_Albania|Politics of Albania]]
sentence_289: See also: [[Government_of_Albania|Government of Albania]]
sentence_290: Albania is a parliamentary [[Constitutional_republic|constitutional republic]] and [[Sovereign_state|sovereign state]] whose [[Politics_of_Albania|politics]] operate under a framework laid out in the [[Constitution_of_Albania|constitution]] wherein the [[President_of_Albania|president]] functions as the head of state and the [[Prime_Minister_of_Albania|prime minister]] as the head of government.
sentence_291: The sovereignty is vested in the [[Albanian_people|Albanian people]] and exercised by the Albanian people through their representatives or directly.
sentence_292: The [[Government_of_Albania|government]] is based on the separation and balancing of powers among the [[Legislative|legislative]], [[Judiciary|judiciary]] and executive.
sentence_293: The [[Legislative_power|legislative power]] is held by the [[Parliament_of_Albania|parliament]] and is elected every four years by a system of [[Party-list_proportional_representation|party-list proportional representation]] by the Albanian people on the basis of free, equal, universal and periodic [[Suffrage|suffrage]] by secret ballot.
sentence_294: The [[Civil_law_(legal_system)|civil law]], codified and based on the Napoleonic Code, is divided between courts with regular civil and criminal jurisdiction and administrative courts.
sentence_295: The [[Judicial_power|judicial power]] is vested in the [[Supreme_Court_of_Albania|supreme court]], [[Constitutional_Court_of_Albania|constitutional court]], [[Appeals_courts_of_Albania|appeal court]] and [[Administrative_Courts_in_Albania|administrative court]].
sentence_296: [[Law_enforcement|Law enforcement]] in the country is primarily the responsibility of the [[Albanian_Police|Albanian Police]], the main and largest state law enforcement agency.
sentence_297: It carries out nearly all general police duties including criminal investigation, patrol activity, traffic policing and border control.
sentence_298: The executive power is exercised by the president and prime minister whereby the power of the president is very limited.
sentence_299: The president is the [[Commander-in-chief|commander-in-chief]] of the [[Albanian_Armed_Forces|military]] and the representative of the unity of the Albanian people.
sentence_300: The tenure of the president depends on the [[Confidence_and_supply|confidence]] of the parliament and is elected for a five-year term by the parliament by a majority of three-fifths of all its members.
sentence_301: The prime minister, appointed by the president and approved by the parliament, is authorized to constitute the [[Cabinet_of_Albania|cabinet]].
sentence_302: The cabinet is composed primarily of the prime minister inclusively its deputies and ministers.
sentence_303: Main article: [[Foreign_relations_of_Albania|Foreign relations of Albania]]
sentence_304: In the time since the end of communism and [[Isolationism|isolationism]], Albania has extended its responsibilities and position in continental and international affairs, developing and establishing friendly [[Foreign_relations_of_Albania|relations]] with other countries around the world.
sentence_305: The country's foreign policy priorities are its [[Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union|accession]] into the [[European_Union|European Union]] (EU), the [[International_recognition_of_Kosovo|international recognition of Kosovo]] and the expulsion of Cham Albanians, as well as helping and protecting the rights of the [[Albanians|Albanians]] in [[Albanians_in_Kosovo|Kosovo]], [[Albanians_in_Montenegro|Montenegro]], North Macedonia, [[Albanians_in_greece|Greece]], [[Albanians_in_south_Serbia|Serbia]], [[Arbëreshë_people|Italy]] and the [[Albanian_diaspora|Diaspora]].
sentence_306: Albania's [[Albania-NATO_relations|admission]] into the [[NATO|North Atlantic Treaty Organisation]] (NATO) was considered by Albanian politicians as a significant ambition for the country's foreign policy.
sentence_307: The country has been extensively engaged with the NATO and has maintained its position as a stability factor and a strong ally of the [[United_States|United States]] and the European Union (EU) in the region of the [[Balkans|Balkans]].
sentence_308: Albania maintains strong [[Albanian_American_relations|ties]] with the United States ever after it supported the Albania's independence and democracy.
sentence_309: Nowadays, both countries have signed a number of agreements and [[Treaties|treaties]].
sentence_310: In 2007, Albania welcomed [[George_W._Bush|George W. Bush]] who became the first President of the United States ever to visit the country.
sentence_311: Albania and [[Kosovo|Kosovo]] are culturally, socially and economically very closely rooted due to the Albanian majority population in Kosovo.
sentence_312: In 1998, the country contributed in supporting allied efforts to end the [[Kosovo_War|humanitarian tragedy in Kosovo]] and secure the peace after the [[NATO_bombing_of_Yugoslavia|NATO bombing of Yugoslavia]].
sentence_313: Albania has been an active member of the United Nations since 1955.
sentence_314: They country took on membership for the [[United_Nations_Economic_and_Social_Council|United Nations Economic and Social Council]] from 2005 to 2007 as well as in 2012.
sentence_315: It served as vice president of the [[United_Nations_Economic_and_Social_Council|ECOSOC]] in 2006 and 2013.
sentence_316: In 2014, it also joined the [[United_Nations_Human_Rights_Council|United Nations Human Rights Council]] from 2015 to 2017 and was elected vice president in 2015.
sentence_317: Albania is a full member of numerous international organisations inclusively the [[Council_of_Europe|Council of Europe]], International Organisation for Migration, [[World_Health_Organization|World Health Organization]], [[Union_for_the_Mediterranean|Union for the Mediterranean]], [[Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation|Organisation of Islamic Cooperation]], [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]], [[International_Monetary_Fund|International Monetary Fund]], [[World_Trade_Organization|World Trade Organization]] and [[La_Francophonie|La Francophonie]].
sentence_318: Main article: [[Armed_Forces_of_Albania|Armed Forces of Albania]]
sentence_319: The [[Albanian_Armed_Forces|Albanian Armed Forces]] consist of [[Albanian_Land_Force|Land]], [[Albanian_Air_Force|Air]] and [[Albanian_Naval_Force|Naval Forces]] and constitute the military and paramilitary forces of the country.
sentence_320: They are led by a [[Commander-in-chief|commander-in-chief]] under the supervision of the [[Ministry_of_Defence_(Albania)|Ministry of Defence]] and by the [[President_of_Albania|President]] as the supreme commander during wartime however, in times of peace its powers are executed through the [[Prime_Minister_of_Albania|Prime Minister]] and the [[Ministry_of_Defence_(Albania)|Defence Minister]].
sentence_321: The chief purpose of the armed forces of Albania is the defence of the independence, the sovereignty and the territorial integrity of the country, as well as the participation in humanitarian, combat, non-combat and peace support operations.
sentence_322: Military service is voluntary since 2010 with the age of 19 being the legal minimum age for the duty.
sentence_323: Albania has committed to increase the participations in multinational operations.
sentence_324: Since the fall of communism, the country has participated in six international missions but participated in only one United Nations mission in [[UNOMIG|Georgia]] sending of 3 military observers.
sentence_325: Since February 2008, Albania has participated officially in NATO's Operation Active Endeavor in the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]].
sentence_326: It was invited to join NATO on 3 April 2008, and it became a full member on 2 April 2009.
sentence_327: Albania reduced the number of active troops from 65,000 in 1988 to 14,500 in 2009.
sentence_328: The military now consists mainly of a small fleet of aircraft and sea vessels.
sentence_329: In the 1990s, the country scrapped enormous amounts of obsolete hardware from China, such as tanks and SAM systems.
sentence_330: Increasing the military budget was one of the most important conditions for [[NATO|NATO]] integration.
sentence_331: Military spending has generally been low.
sentence_332: As of 1996 military spending was an estimated 1.5% of the country's GDP, only to peak in 2009 at 2% and fall again to 1.5%.
sentence_333: Main article: [[Counties_of_Albania|Counties of Albania]]
sentence_334: See also: [[Municipalities_of_Albania|Municipalities of Albania]]
sentence_335: Albania is defined within a territorial area of 28,748 km (11,100 sq mi) in the [[Balkan_Peninsula|Balkan Peninsula]].
sentence_336: The country is divided into three regions, the [[Northern_Albania|Northern]], [[Central_Albania|Central]] and [[Southern_Albania|Southern Region]], which consist of a number of [[Counties_of_Albania|counties]] (qarqe) and [[Municipalities_of_Albania|municipalities]] (bashkia).
sentence_337: The highest level of [[Subdivisions_of_Albania|administrative divisions]] are the twelve constituent counties.
sentence_338: Each county has the same status but vary in their areas, [[List_of_counties_of_Albania_by_population|populations]] and contributions to the economy.
sentence_339: Nonetheless, they are further subdivided into 61 municipalities with each of them being responsible for geographical, economic, social and cultural purposes inside the counties.
sentence_340: The counties were created on 31 July 2000 to replace the 36 former districts.
sentence_341: The [[Government_of_Albania|government]] introduced the new administrative divisions to be implemented in 2015, whereby municipalities were reduced to 61, while the rurals were abolished.
sentence_342: The defunct municipalities are known as neighborhoods or villages.
sentence_343: There are overall 2980 villages or communities in the entire country, formerly known as localities.
sentence_344: The municipalities are the first level of local governance, responsible for local needs and [[Law_enforcement_in_Albania|law enforcement]].
sentence_345: The largest county in Albania, by population, is [[Tirana_County|Tirana County]] with over 800,000 people.
sentence_346: The smallest county, by population, is [[Gjirokastër_County|Gjirokastër County]] with over 70,000 people.
sentence_347: The largest in the county, by area, is [[Korçë_County|Korçë County]] encompassing 3,711 square kilometres (1,433 sq mi) of the southeast of Albania.
sentence_348: The smallest county, by area, is [[Durrës_County|Durrës County]] with an area of 766 square kilometres (296 sq mi) in the west of Albania.
sentence_349: Main article: [[Economy_of_Albania|Economy of Albania]]
sentence_350: The transition from a socialist [[Planned_economy|planned economy]] to a capitalist [[Mixed_economy|mixed economy]] in Albania has been largely successful.
sentence_351: The country has a [[Developing_country|developing]] mixed economy classified by the [[World_Bank|World Bank]] as an [[List_of_countries_by_GNI_(nominal,_Atlas_method)_per_capita#Upper-middle-income_group|upper-middle income economy]].
sentence_352: In 2016, it had the 4th lowest [[List_of_countries_by_unemployment_rate|unemployment rate]] in the [[Balkans|Balkans]] with an estimated value of 14.7%.
sentence_353: Its largest trading partners are Italy, Greece, China, Spain, Kosovo and the United States.
sentence_354: The [[Albanian_lek|lek]] (ALL) is the country's currency and is [[Fixed_exchange_rate|pegged]] at approximately 132,51 lek per euro.
sentence_355: The cities of [[Tirana|Tirana]] and [[Durrës|Durrës]] constitute the economic and financial heart of Albania due to their high population, modern infrastructure and strategic geographical location.
sentence_356: The country's most important infrastructure facilities take course through both of the cities, connecting the north to the south as well as the west to the east.
sentence_357: Among the largest [[List_of_companies_of_Albania|companies]] are the petroleum [[Taçi_Oil|Taçi Oil]], [[Albpetrol|Albpetrol]], [[ARMO_oil_refiner|ARMO]] and Kastrati, the mineral AlbChrome, the cement [[Antea_Cement|Antea]], the investment [[Samir_Mane|BALFIN Group]] and the technology [[Albtelecom|Albtelecom]], [[Vodafone_Albania|Vodafone]], [[Telekom_Albania|Telekom Albania]] and others.
sentence_358: In 2012, Albania's [[GDP_per_capita|GDP per capita]] stood at 30% of the [[European_Union|European Union]] average, while [[GDP_(PPP)_per_capita|GDP (PPP) per capita]] was 35%.
sentence_359: Albania were one of three countries in Europe to record an economic growth in the first quarter of 2010 after the [[Global_financial_crisis|global financial crisis]].
sentence_360: The [[International_Monetary_Fund|International Monetary Fund]] predicted 2.6% growth for Albania in 2010 and 3.2% in 2011.
sentence_361: According to the [[Forbes|Forbes]] as of December 2016, the [[Gross_Domestic_Product_(GDP)|Gross Domestic Product (GDP)]] was growing at 2.8%.
sentence_362: The country had a [[Trade_balance|trade balance]] of −9.7% and [[Unemployment_rate|unemployment rate]] of 14.7%.
sentence_363: The [[Foreign_direct_investment|Foreign direct investment]] has increased significantly in recent years as the government has embarked on an ambitious program to improve the business climate through fiscal and legislative reforms.
sentence_364: The economy is expected to expand in the near term, driven by a recovery in consumption and robust investments.
sentence_365: Growth is projected to be 3.2% in 2016, 3.5% in 2017, and 3.8% in 2018.
sentence_366: Main article: [[Agriculture_in_Albania|Agriculture in Albania]]
sentence_367: Agriculture in the country is based on small to medium-sized family-owned dispersed units.
sentence_368: It remains a significant sector of the [[Economy_of_Albania|economy of Albania]].
sentence_369: It employs 41% of the population, and about 24.31% of the land is used for agricultural purposes.
sentence_370: One of the earliest farming sites in Europe has been found in the southeast of the country.
sentence_371: As part of the pre-accession process of Albania to the [[European_Union|European Union]], farmers are being aided through IPA funds to improve Albanian agriculture standards.
sentence_372: Albania produces significant amounts of fruits (apples, [[Olive|olives]], grapes, oranges, lemons, [[Apricot|apricots]], [[Peach|peaches]], [[Cherry|cherries]], [[Figs|figs]], [[Prunus_cerasus|sour cherries]], [[Plum|plums]], and [[Strawberry|strawberries]]), [[Vegetable_oil|vegetables]] (potatoes, tomatoes, maize, onions, and wheat), [[Sugar_beet|sugar beets]], tobacco, meat, [[Honey|honey]], [[Dairy_product|dairy products]], traditional medicine and [[Essential_oil|aromatic plants]].
sentence_373: Further, the country is a worldwide significant producer of [[Salvia|salvia]], [[Rosemary|rosemary]] and yellow gentian.
sentence_374: The country's proximity to the [[Ionian_Sea|Ionian Sea]] and the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic Sea]] give the underdeveloped fishing industry great potential.
sentence_375: The [[World_Bank|World Bank]] and [[European_Community|European Community]] economists report that, Albania's fishing industry has good potential to generate export earnings because prices in the nearby Greek and Italian markets are many times higher than those in the Albanian market.
sentence_376: The fish available off the coasts of the country are [[Carp|carp]], trout, [[Sea_bream|sea bream]], [[Mussel|mussels]] and [[Crustacean|crustaceans]].
sentence_377: Albania has one of Europe's longest histories of [[Viticulture|viticulture]].
sentence_378: The today's region was one of the few places where vine was naturally grown during the ice age.
sentence_379: The oldest found seeds in the region are 4,000 to 6,000 years old.
sentence_380: In 2009, the nation produced an estimated 17,500 tonnes of wine.
sentence_381: During the communist era, the production area expanded to some 20,000 hectares (49,000 acres).
sentence_382: See also: :Category:Mines in Albania
sentence_383: The secondary sector of Albania have undergone many changes and diversification, since the collapse of the communist regime in the country.
sentence_384: It is very diversified, from [[Electronics_industry|electronics]], [[Manufacturing_industries|manufacturing]], [[Textile_industry|textiles]], to food, [[Cement_industry|cement]], [[Mining_industry|mining]], and [[Energy_industry|energy]].
sentence_385: The [[Antea_Cement|Antea Cement]] plant in [[Fushë-Krujë|Fushë-Krujë]] is considered as one of the largest industrial greenfield investments in the country.
sentence_386: Albanian oil and gas is represents of the most promising albeit strictly regulated sectors of its economy.
sentence_387: Albania has the [[List_of_countries_by_proven_oil_reserves|second largest oil deposits]] in the [[Balkan_peninsula|Balkan peninsula]] after [[Romania|Romania]], and the largest [[Patos-Marinza_Oil_Field|oil reserves]] in Europe.
sentence_388: The [[Albpetrol|Albpetrol]] company is owned by the Albanian state and monitors the state petroleum agreements in the country.
sentence_389: The textile industry has seen an extensive expansion by approaching companies from the [[European_Union|European Union]] (EU) in Albania.
sentence_390: According to the [[Institute_of_Statistics_(Albania)|Institute of Statistics (INSTAT)]] as of 2016, the textile production marked an annual growth of 5.3% and an annual turnover of around 1.5 billion euros.
sentence_391: Albania is a significant minerals producer and is ranked among the world's leading [[Chromium|chromium]] producers and exporters.
sentence_392: The nation is also a notable producer of copper, [[Nickel|nickel]] and coal.
sentence_393: The [[Batra_mine|Batra mine]], [[Bulqizë_mine|Bulqizë mine]], and [[Thekna_mine|Thekna mine]] are among the most recognised Albanian mines that are still in operation.
sentence_394: See also: [[Banking_in_Albania|Banking]], [[Telecommunications_in_Albania|Telecommunications]], and [[Tourism_in_Albania|Tourism in Albania]]
sentence_395: The [[Tertiary_sector|tertiary sector]] represents the fastest growing sector of the country's economy.
sentence_396: 36% of the population work in the service sector which contributes to 65% of the country's GDP.
sentence_397: Ever since the end of the 20th century, the banking industry is a major component of the tertiary sector and remains in good conditions overall due to [[Privatization|privatization]] and the commendable [[Monetary_policy|monetary policy]].
sentence_398: Previously one of the most [[Isolationism|isolated]] and controlled countries in the world, [[Telecommunication_industry|telecommunication industry]] represents nowadays another major contributor to the sector.
sentence_399: It developed largely through privatisation and subsequent investment by both domestic and foreign investors.
sentence_400: [[Eagle_Mobile|Eagle]], [[Vodafone_Albania|Vodafone]] and [[Telekom_Albania|Telekom Albania]] are the leading telecommunications service providers in the country.
sentence_401: Tourism is recognised as an industry of national importance and has been steadily increasing since the beginnings of the 21st century.
sentence_402: It directly accounted for 8.4% of GDP in 2016 though including indirect contributions pushes the proportion to 26%.
sentence_403: In the same year, the country received approximately 4.74 million visitors mostly from across Europe and the United States as well.
sentence_404: The increase of foreign visitors has been dramatic.
sentence_405: Albania had only 500,000 visitors in 2005, while in 2012 had an estimated 4.2 million, an increase of 740 percent in only 7 years.
sentence_406: In 2015, tourism in summer increased by 25 percent in contrast the previous year according to the country's tourism agency.
sentence_407: In 2011, [[Lonely_Planet|Lonely Planet]] named as a top travel destination, while [[The_New_York_Times|The New York Times]] placed Albania as number 4 global touristic destination in 2014.
sentence_408: The bulk of the tourist industry is concentrated along the [[Adriatic|Adriatic]] and [[Ionian_Sea|Ionian Sea]] in the west of the country.
sentence_409: However, the [[Albanian_Riviera|Albanian Riviera]] in the southwest has the most scenic and pristine beaches, and is often called the pearl of the Albanian coast.
sentence_410: Its coastline has a considerable length of 446 kilometres (277 miles).
sentence_411: The coast has a particular character because it is rich in varieties of virgin beaches, capes, coves, covered bays, lagoons, small gravel beaches, sea caves and many landforms.
sentence_412: Some parts of this seaside are very clean ecologically, which represent in this prospective unexplored areas, which are very rare within the [[Mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
sentence_413: Other attractions include the mountainous areas such as the [[Albanian_Alps|Albanian Alps]], [[Ceraunian_Mountains|Ceraunian Mountains]] and [[Korab|Korab]] Mountains but also the historical cities of [[Berat|Berat]], [[Durrës|Durrës]], [[Gjirokastër|Gjirokastër]], [[Sarandë|Sarandë]], [[Shkodër|Shkodër]] and [[Korçë|Korçë]].
sentence_414: Main article: [[Transport_in_Albania|Transport in Albania]]
sentence_415: Transportation in Albania is managed within the functions of the [[Ministry_of_Infrastructure_and_Energy_(Albania)|Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy]] and entities such as the [[Albanian_Road_Authority|Albanian Road Authority]] (ARRSH), responsible for the construction and maintenance of the [[Highways_in_Albania|highways]] and [[Motorways_in_Albania|motorways]] in Albania, as well as the [[Civil_Aviation_Authority_(Albania)|Albanian Aviation Authority]] (AAC), with the responsibility of coordinating civil aviation and airports in the country.
sentence_416: The [[Tirana_International_Airport_Nënë_Tereza|international airport]] of [[Tirana|Tirana]] is the premier air gateway to the country, and is also the principal hub for Albania's national [[Flag_carrier|flag carrier]] airline, [[Air_Albania|Air Albania]].
sentence_417: The airport carried more than 3.3 million passengers in 2019 with connections to many destinations in other countries around [[Europe|Europe]], [[Africa|Africa]] and [[Asia|Asia]].
sentence_418: The country plans to progressively increase the number of airports especially in the south with possible locations in [[Sarandë|Sarandë]], [[Gjirokastër|Gjirokastër]] and [[Vlorë_International_Airport|Vlorë]].
sentence_419: The [[Highways_in_Albania|highways]] and [[Motorways_in_Albania|motorways in Albania]] are properly maintained and often still under construction and renovation.
sentence_420: The [[A1_motorway_(Albania)|Autostrada 1]] (A1) represents an integral transportation corridor in Albania and the longest motorway of the country.
sentence_421: It will prospectively link [[Durrës|Durrës]] on the Adriatic Sea across [[Pristina|Pristina]] in Kosovo with the Pan-European Corridor X in Serbia.
sentence_422: The [[A2_motorway_(Albania)|Autostrada 2]] (A2) is part of the Adriatic–Ionian Corridor as well as the [[Pan-European_Corridor_VIII|Pan-European Corridor VIII]] and connects [[Fier|Fier]] with [[Vlorë|Vlorë]].
sentence_423: The [[A3_motorway_(Albania)|Autostrada 3]] (A3) is currently under construction and will connect, after its completion, [[Tirana|Tirana]] and [[Elbasan|Elbasan]] with the Pan-European Corridor VIII.
sentence_424: When all three corridors are completed, Albania will have an estimated 759 kilometres (472 mi) of highway linking it with all of its neighboring countries.
sentence_425: [[Port_of_Durrës|Durrës]] is the busiest and largest [[Seaport|seaport]] in the country, followed by [[Port_of_Vlorë|Vlorë]], [[Port_of_Shëngjin|Shëngjin]] and [[Port_of_Sarandë|Sarandë]].
sentence_426: As of 2014, it is as one of the largest passenger ports on the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic Sea]] with annual passenger volume of approximately 1.5 million.
sentence_427: The principal ports serve a system of ferries connecting Albania with numerous islands and coastal cities in Croatia, Greece and Italy.
sentence_428: The rail network is administered by the national railway company [[Hekurudha_Shqiptare|Hekurudha Shqiptare]] which was extensively promoted by the dictator [[Enver_Hoxha|Enver Hoxha]].
sentence_429: There has been a considerable increase in private car ownership and bus usage while rail use decreased since the end of communism.
sentence_430: However, a new railway line from Tirana and its airport to Durrës is currently planned.
