sentence_431: The specific location of this railway, connecting the most populated urban areas in Albania, merely makes it an important economic development project.
sentence_432: Main article: [[Education_in_Albania|Education in Albania]]
sentence_433: In the country, education is secular, free, [[Compulsory_education|compulsory]] and based on three levels of education segmented in primary, secondary and tertiary education.
sentence_434: The academic year is apportioned into two semesters beginning in September or October, and ending in June or July.
sentence_435: [[Albanian_language|Albanian]] serves as the primary language of instruction in all academic institutions across the country.
sentence_436: The study of a first [[Foreign_language|foreign language]] is mandatory and taught most often at elementary and bilingual schools.
sentence_437: The languages taught in schools are English, Italian, French and German.
sentence_438: The country has a [[School_life_expectancy|school life expectancy]] of 16 years and a [[Literacy_rate|literacy rate]] of 98.7%, with 99.2% for males and 98.3% for females.
sentence_439: Compulsory primary education is divided into two levels, elementary and secondary school, from grade one to five and six to nine, respectively.
sentence_440: Pupils are required to attend school from the age of six until they turn 16.
sentence_441: Upon successful completion of primary education, all pupils are entitled to attend high schools with specialising in any particular field including arts, [[Sport|sports]], [[Language|languages]], sciences or technology.
sentence_442: The country's tertiary education, an optional stage of formal learning following secondary education, has undergone a thorough reformation and restructuring in compliance with the principles of the [[Bologna_Process|Bologna Process]].
sentence_443: There is a significant number of private and public [[Institutions_of_higher_education|institutions of higher education]] well dispersed in the major cities of Albania.
sentence_444: Studies in tertiary education are organized at three successive levels which include the bachelor, [[Master's_degree|master]] and [[Doctorate_Degree|doctorate]].
sentence_445: Main article: [[Health_in_Albania|Health in Albania]]
sentence_446: The [[Constitution_of_Albania|constitution of Albania]] guarantees equal, free and [[Universal_health_care|universal health care]] for all its citizens.
sentence_447: The health care system of the country is currently organised in three levels, among others [[Primary_healthcare|primary]], [[Secondary_care|secondary]] and [[Tertiary_healthcare|tertiary healthcare]], and is in a process of modernisation and development.
sentence_448: The [[Life_expectancy|life expectancy]] at birth in Albania is at 77.8 years and ranks [[List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy|37th]] in the world outperforming several [[Developed_countries|developed countries]].
sentence_449: The average [[Life_expectancy#Healthy_life_expectancy|healthy life expectancy]] is at 68.8 years and ranks as well 37th in the world.
sentence_450: The country's [[Infant_mortality_rate|infant mortality rate]] is estimated at 12 per 1,000 live births in 2015.
sentence_451: In 2000, the country had the 55th best healthcare performance in the world, as defined by the [[World_Health_Organization|World Health Organization]].
sentence_452: [[Cardiovascular_disease|Cardiovascular disease]] remain the principal cause of death in the country accounting 52% of total deaths.
sentence_453: Accidents, injuries, [[Malignant_disease|malignant]] and [[Respiratory_disease|respiratory diseases]] are other primary causes of death.
sentence_454: [[Neuropsychiatric_disorders|Neuropsychiatric disease]] has also increased due to recent demographic, social and economic changes in the country.
sentence_455: In 2009, the country had a fruit and vegetable supply of 886 grams per capita per day, the fifth highest supply in Europe.
sentence_456: In comparison to other developed and developing countries, Albania has a relatively low rate of [[Obesity|obesity]] probably thanks to the health benefits of the [[Mediterranean_diet|Mediterranean diet]].
sentence_457: According to [[List_of_countries_by_Body_Mass_Index_(BMI)#WHO_Data_on_Prevalence_of_Obesity_(BMI_above_30)_(2014)|World Health Organization data from 2016]], 21.7% of adults in the country are clinically [[Overweight|overweight]], with a [[Body_mass_index|Body mass index]] (BMI) score of 25 or more.
sentence_458: Main article: [[Renewable_energy_in_Albania|Renewable energy in Albania]]
sentence_459: See also: [[List_of_power_stations_in_Albania|Power stations]] and [[List_of_oil_and_gas_fields_in_Albania|Oil fields in Albania]]
sentence_460: Due to its geographical location and natural resources, Albania has a wide variety of [[Energy_resource|energy resources]] ranging from gas, oil and coal, to [[Wind_energy|wind]], [[Solar_energy|solar]] and water as well as other [[Renewable_energy|renewable]] sources.
sentence_461: Currently, the electricity generation sector of Albania is dependent on [[Hydroelectricity|hydroelectricity]] simultaneously ranking fifth in the world in percentage terms.
sentence_462: The [[Drin_(river)|Drin]], located in the north, hosts four [[Hydroelectric_power_station|hydroelectric power stations]], including [[Fierza_Hydroelectric_Power_Station|Fierza]], [[Koman_Hydroelectric_Power_Station|Koman]], [[Skavica_Hydro_Power_Plant|Skavica]] and [[Vau_i_Dejës_Hydroelectric_Power_Station|Vau i Dejës]].
sentence_463: Two other power stations, such as the [[Banjë_Hydro_Power_Plant|Banjë]] and [[Moglicë_Hydro_Power_Plant|Moglicë]], are located along the [[Devoll_(river)|Devoll]] in the south.
sentence_464: Albania has considerably large deposits of oil.
sentence_465: It has the 10th largest oil reserves in Europe and the 58th in the world.
sentence_466: The country's main petroleum deposits are located around the [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast]] and [[Myzeqe|Myzeqe]] Plain within the [[Western_Lowlands|Western Lowlands]], where the country's largest reserve is located.
sentence_467: Although, [[Patos-Marinza_Oil_Field|Patos-Marinza]], also located within the area, is the largest onshore oil field in Europe.
sentence_468: After the completion of the [[Trans_Adriatic_Pipeline|Trans Adriatic Pipeline]] (TAP), Albania will be significantly connected to the planned [[Southern_Gas_Corridor|Southern Gas Corridor]], that will transport [[Natural_gas|natural gas]] from the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] through Albania to Europe.
sentence_469: Withal the TAP runs for 215 kilometres (134 miles) across Albania's territory before entering the [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast]] approximately 17 kilometres (11 miles) northwest of [[Fier|Fier]].
sentence_470: In 2009, the company Enel announced plans to build an 800 MW [[Coal_Fired_Power_Plant|coal-fired power plant]] in the country, to diversify electricity sources.
sentence_471: The [[Water_resources|water resources]] of Albania are particularly abundant in all the regions of the country and comprise [[Lakes_of_Albania|lakes]], [[Rivers_of_Albania|rivers]], springs and groundwater aquifers.
sentence_472: The country's available average quantity of [[Fresh_water|fresh water]] is estimated at 1,297 cubic metres (45,803 cubic feet) per inhabitant per year, which is one of the highest rates in Europe.
sentence_473: According to the data presented by the [[Joint_Monitoring_Programme_for_Water_Supply_and_Sanitation|Joint Monitoring Program for Water Supply and Sanitation]] (JMP) in 2015, about 93% of the country's total population had access to [[Improved_sanitation|improved sanitation]].
sentence_474: Main articles: [[Science_and_technology_in_Albania|Technology]] and [[Telecommunications_in_Albania|Telecommunications in Albania]]
sentence_475: After the fall of communism in 1991, human resources in sciences and technology in Albania have drastically decreased.
sentence_476: As of various reports, during 1991 to 2005 approximately 50% of the professors and scientists of the universities and science institutions in the country have left Albania.
sentence_477: In 2009, the [[Government_of_Albania|government]] approved the National Strategy for Science, Technology and Innovation in Albania covering the period 2009 to 2015.
sentence_478: It aims to triple public spending on research and development to 0.6% of GDP and augment the share of [[Gross_domestic_expenditure_on_R&D|GDE]] from foreign sources, including the framework programmes for research of the [[European_Union|European Union]], to the point where it covers 40% of research spending, among others.
sentence_479: Telecommunication represents one of the fastest growing and dynamic sectors in Albania.
sentence_480: [[Vodafone_Albania|Vodafone Albania]], [[Telekom_Albania|Telekom Albania]] and [[Albtelecom|Albtelecom]] are the three large providers of mobile and [[Internet|internet]] in Albania.
sentence_481: As of the [[Electronic_and_Postal_Communications_Authority_(Albania)|Electronic and Postal Communications Authority]] (AKEP) in 2018, the country had approximately 2.7 million active mobile users with almost 1.8 million active broadband subscribers.
sentence_482: Vodafone Albania alone served more than 931,000 mobile users, Telekom Albania had about 605,000 users and Albtelecom had more than 272,000 users.
sentence_483: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Albania|Demography of Albania]]
sentence_484: See also: [[Albanian_people|Albanian people]] and [[Origin_of_the_Albanians|Origin of the Albanians]]
sentence_485: As defined by the [[Institute_of_Statistics_(Albania)|Institute of Statistics]] (INSTAT), the [[Demographics_of_Albania|population]] of Albania was estimated in 2020 at 2,845,955.
sentence_486: The country's [[Total_fertility_rate|total fertility rate]] of 1.51 children born per woman is one of the [[List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_by_fertility_rate|lowest in the world]].
sentence_487: Its [[List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_by_population_density|population density]] stands at 259 inhabitants per square kilometre.
sentence_488: The overall [[List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy|life expectancy]] at birth is 78.5 years; 75.8 years for males and 81.4 years for females.
sentence_489: The country is the [[Balkans#Demographics|8th most populous country]] in the [[Balkans|Balkans]] and ranks as the [[List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population|137th most populous country]] in the world.
sentence_490: Nonetheless, the country's population rose steadily from 2,5 million in 1979 until 1989, when it peaked at 3.1 million.
sentence_491: It is forecasted that the population will continue shrinking for the next decade at least, depending on the actual [[Birth_rate|birth rate]] and the level of net migration.
sentence_492: The explanation for the recent population decrease is the fall of communism in Albania in the late twentieth century.
sentence_493: That period was marked by economic [[Mass_migration|mass emigration]] from Albania to [[Greece|Greece]], Italy and the United States.
sentence_494: Four decades of total [[Communism_in_Albania|isolation]] from the world, combined with its disastrous economic, social and political situation, had caused this exodus.
sentence_495: The [[Human_migration|external migration]] was prohibited outright during the communist era, while [[Human_migration|internal migration]] was quite limited, hence this was a new phenomenon.
sentence_496: At least, 900,000 people left Albania during this period, with about 600,000 of them settling in Greece.
sentence_497: The migration affected the country's internal population distribution.
sentence_498: It decreased particularly in the north and south, while it increased in the center within the cities of [[Tirana|Tirana]] and [[Durrës|Durrës]].
sentence_499: About 53.4% of the country's [[Demographics_of_Albania|population]] lives in cities.
sentence_500: The three largest counties by population account for half of the total population.
sentence_501: Almost 30% of the total population is found in [[Tirana_County|Tirana County]] followed by [[Fier_County|Fier County]] with 11% and [[Durrës_County|Durrës County]] with 10%.
sentence_502: Over 1 million people are concentrated in [[Tirana|Tirana]] and [[Durrës|Durrës]], making it the largest urban area in Albania.
sentence_503: [[Tirana|Tirana]] is one of largest cities in the [[Balkan_Peninsula|Balkan Peninsula]] and ranks seventh with a population about 800,000.
sentence_504: The second largest city in the country by population is [[Durrës|Durrës]], with a population of 201,110, followed by [[Vlorë|Vlorë]] with a population of 141,513.

sentence_505: Main article: [[Minorities_of_Albania|Minorities of Albania]]
sentence_506: Issues of ethnicity are a delicate topic and subject to debate.
sentence_507: Contrary to official statistics that show an over 97 per cent Albanian majority in the country, minority groups (such as [[Greeks_in_Albania|Greeks]], [[Macedonians_in_Albania|Macedonians]], [[Montenegrins_of_Albania|Montenegrins]], [[Roma_in_Albania|Roma]] and [[Aromanians_in_Albania|Aromanians]]) have frequently disputed the official numbers, asserting a higher percentage of the country's population.
sentence_508: According to the disputed 2011 census, ethnic affiliation was as follows: [[Albanians|Albanians]] 2,312,356 (82.6% of the total), [[Greeks_in_Albania|Greeks]] 24,243 (0.9%), [[Macedonians_of_Albania|Macedonians]] 5,512 (0.2%), [[Montenegrins_of_Albania|Montenegrins]] 366 (0.01%), [[Aromanians|Aromanians]] 8,266 (0.30%), [[Romani_people|Romani]] 8,301 (0.3%), Balkan Egyptians 3,368 (0.1%), other ethnicities 2,644 (0.1%), no declared ethnicity 390,938 (14.0%), and not relevant 44,144 (1.6%).
sentence_509: On the quality of the specific data the Advisory Committee on the [[Framework_Convention_for_the_Protection_of_National_Minorities|Framework Convention for the Protection of National Minorities]] stated that "the results of the census should be viewed with the utmost caution and calls on the authorities not to rely exclusively on the data on nationality collected during the census in determining its policy on the protection of national minorities.
sentence_511: Albania recognises nine national or cultural minorities: [[Aromanians|Aromanian]], [[Greeks|Greek]], [[Macedonians_(ethnic_group)|Macedonian]], [[Montenegrins|Montenegrin]], [[Serbs|Serb]], [[Romani_people|Roma]], [[Egyptians_(Balkans)|Egyptian]], Bosnian and [[Bulgarians|Bulgarian]] peoples.
sentence_512: Other Albanian minorities are the [[Gorani_people|Gorani people]] and Jews.
sentence_513: Regarding the Greeks, "it is difficult to know how many Greeks there are in Albania".
sentence_514: The estimates vary between 60,000 and 300,000 ethnic Greeks in Albania.
sentence_515: According to Ian Jeffries, most of Western sources put the number at around 200,000.
sentence_516: The 300,000 mark is supported by Greek government as well.
sentence_517: The [[CIA_World_Factbook|CIA World Factbook]] estimates the Greek minority to constitute 0.9% of the total population.
sentence_518: The US State Department estimates that Greeks make up 1.17%, and other minorities 0.23%, of the population.
sentence_519: The latter questions the validity of the census data about the Greek minority, due to the fact that measurements have been affected by boycott.
sentence_520: Macedonians and some Greek minority groups have sharply criticised Article 20 of the Census law, according to which a $1,000 fine will be imposed on anyone who will declare an ethnicity other than what is stated on his or her birth certificate.
sentence_521: This is claimed to be an attempt to intimidate minorities into declaring Albanian ethnicity; according to them the Albanian government has stated that it will jail anyone who does not participate in the census or refuse to declare his or her ethnicity.
sentence_522: Genc Pollo, the minister in charge has declared that: "Albanian citizens will be able to freely express their ethnic and religious affiliation and mother tongue.
sentence_523: However, they are not forced to answer these sensitive questions".
sentence_524: The amendments criticized do not include jailing or forced declaration of ethnicity or religion; only a fine is envisioned which can be overthrown by court.
sentence_525: Greek representatives form part of the Albanian parliament and the government has invited Albanian Greeks to register, as the only way to improve their status.
sentence_526: On the other hand, nationalists, various organisations and political parties in Albania have expressed their concern that the census might artificially increase the numbers of the Greek minority, which might be then exploited by Greece to threaten Albania's territorial integrity.
sentence_529: The [[Official_language|official language]] of the country is [[Albanian_language|Albanian]] which is spoken by the vast majority of the country's population.
sentence_530: Its standard spoken and written form is revised and merged from the two main dialects, [[Gheg|Gheg]] and [[Tosk_Albanian|Tosk]], though it is notably based more on the Tosk dialect.
sentence_531: The [[Shkumbin|Shkumbin]] river is the rough dividing line between the two dialects.
sentence_532: Also a [[Greeks_in_Albania#Language|dialect of Greek]] that preserves features now lost in standard modern Greek is spoken in areas inhabited by the [[Greek_minority_in_Albania|Greek minority]].
sentence_533: Other languages spoken by ethnic minorities in Albania include Aromanian, [[Serbian_language|Serbian]], [[Macedonian_language|Macedonian]], [[Bosnian_language|Bosnian]], Bulgarian, [[Gora_dialect|Gorani]], and [[Romani_language|Roma]].
sentence_534: Macedonian is official in the Pustec Municipality in East Albania.
sentence_535: According to the 2011 population census, 2,765,610 or 98.767% of the population declared [[Albanian_language|Albanian]] as their mother tongue (mother tongue is defined as the first or main language spoken at home during childhood).
sentence_536: In recent years, the shrinking number of pupils in schools dedicated to the Greek minority has caused problems for teachers.
sentence_537: The Greek language is spoken by an important percentage in the southern part of the country, due to cultural and economic links with adjacent Greece.
sentence_538: In a 2017 study carried out by Instat, the Albanian government statistical agency, 39.9% of the 25–64 years old is able to use at least one foreign language, with English first at 40.0%, followed by Italian with 27.8% and Greek with 22.9%.
sentence_539: Among young people aged 25 or less, English, German and Turkish have seen rising interest after 2000.
sentence_540: Italian and French have had a stable interest, while Greek has lost much of its previous interest.
sentence_541: The trends are linked with cultural and economic factors.
sentence_542: [[Greek_language|Greek]] is the second most-spoken language in the country, with 0.5 to 3% of the population speaking it as first language, and with two-thirds of mainly Albanian families having at least one member that speaks Greek, most having learned it in the post communist era (1992–present) due to private schools or migration to Greece.
sentence_543: Outside of the small designated "minority area" in the south the teaching of Greek was banned during the communist era.
sentence_544: As of 2003 Greek was offered at over 100 private tutoring centers all over Albania and at a private school in Tirana, the first of its kind outside Greece.
sentence_545: Young people have shown a growing interest in German language in recent years.
sentence_546: Some of them go to Germany for studying or various experiences.
sentence_547: Albania and Germany have agreements for cooperating in helping young people of the two countries know both cultures better.
sentence_548: Due to a sharp rise in economic relations with Turkey, interest in learning Turkish, in particular among young people, has been growing on a yearly basis.
sentence_549: Young people, attracted by economic importance of Turkish investments and common values between the two nations, gain from cultural and academic collaboration of universities.
sentence_551: Albania is a secular and religiously diverse country with no [[Official_religion|official religion]] and thus, [[Freedom_of_religion|freedom of religion]], [[Freedom_of_belief|belief]] and [[Freedom_of_conscience|conscience]] are guaranteed under the country's [[Constitution_of_Albania|constitution]].
sentence_552: Culturally, religious tolerance is one of the most considerable values of the tradition of the [[Albanians|Albanians]].
sentence_553: It is widely accepted that they generally value a peaceful coexistence among the believers of different religious communities in the country.
sentence_554: [[Pope_Francis|Pope Francis]] hailed Albania during his [[Official_visit|official visit]] in [[Tirana|Tirana]] as model of religious harmony, due to the long tradition of religious coexistence and tolerance.
sentence_555: During [[Classical_antiquity|classical times]], there are thought to have been about seventy Christian families in [[Durrës|Durrës]], as early as the time of the [[Apostle|Apostles]].
sentence_556: The [[Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Tiranë-Durrës|Archbishopric of Durrës]] was purportedly founded by [[Paul_the_Apostle|Paul the Apostle]], while preaching in [[Illyria|Illyria]] and [[Ancient_epirus|Epirus]].
sentence_557: Meanwhile, in [[Middle_Ages|medieval times]], the [[Albanian_people|Albanian people]] first appeared within historical records from the [[Byzantine|Byzantines]].
sentence_558: At this point, they were mostly Christianised.
sentence_559: [[Islam|Islam]] arrived for the first time in the late 9th century to the region, when [[Arabs|Arabs]] raided parts of the eastern banks of the [[Adriatic_Sea|Adriatic Sea]].
sentence_560: It later emerged as the majority religion, during centuries of [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman rule]], though a significant Christian minority remained.
sentence_561: During [[Modern_history|modern times]], the Albanian republican, monarchic and later communist regimes followed a systematic policy of separating religion from official functions and cultural life.
sentence_562: The country has never had an [[Official_religion|official religion]] either as a republic or as a kingdom.
sentence_563: In the 20th century, the clergy of all faiths was weakened under the monarchy and ultimately eradicated during the 1950s and 1960s, under the state policy of obliterating all organised religion from the territories of Albania.
sentence_564: The [[Communism_in_Albania|communist regime]] persecuted and suppressed religious observance and institutions and entirely [[Anti-religious|banned religion]].
sentence_565: The country was then officially declared to be the world's first [[Atheist_state|atheist state]].
sentence_566: Religious freedom has returned, however, since the end of communism.
sentence_567: Islam survived communist era persecution and reemerged in the modern era as a practised religion in Albania.
sentence_568: Some smaller Christian sects in Albania include [[Evangelicalism|Evangelicals]] and several [[Protestant|Protestant]] communities including [[Seventh-day_Adventist_Church|Seventh-day Adventist Church]], [[The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints|Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] and [[Jehovah's_Witnesses|Jehovah's Witnesses]].
sentence_569: The first recorded Protestant of Albania was Said Toptani, who travelled around Europe and returned to [[Tirana|Tirana]] in 1853, where he preached [[Protestantism|Protestantism]].
sentence_570: Due to that, he was arrested and imprisoned by the Ottoman authorities in 1864.
sentence_571: The first [[Evangelical_Protestants|evangelical Protestants]] appeared in the 19th century and the Evangelical Alliance was founded in 1892.
sentence_572: Nowadays, it has 160 member congregations from different Protestant denominations.
sentence_573: Following mass emigration to Israel after the fall of communism, there are only 200 Albanian [[Judaism_in_Albania|Jews]] left in the country.
sentence_574: As of the [[2011_Census_of_Albania|2011 census]], there were 1,587,608 (56.7%) [[Islam|Sunni Muslims]], 280,921 (10.03%) [[Roman_Catholicism|Roman Catholics]], 188,992 (6.75%) [[Eastern_Orthodoxy|Eastern Orthodox]], 58,628 (2.09%) [[Bektashi_Order|Bektashi Muslims]], 3,797 (0.14%) [[Evangelicalism|Evangelists]], 1,919 (0.07%) other [[Christians|Christians]], 602 (0.02%) of other religions and 153,630 (5.49%) believers without denomination.
sentence_575: 69,995 people (2.5%) were [[Atheism|irreligious]] while 386,024 (13.79%) did not declare their religion.
sentence_576: The country is ranked among the least religious countries in the world.
sentence_577: Religion plays an important role in the lives of only 39% of its population.
sentence_578: In another report, 56% considered themselves religious, 30% considered themselves non-religious, while 9% defined themselves as convinced atheists.
sentence_579: 80% believed in God and 40% believed in life after death.
sentence_580: However, 40% believed in hell, while 42% believed in heaven.
sentence_581: The preliminary results of the 2011 census seemed to give widely different results, with 70% of respondents refusing to declare belief in any of the listed faiths.
sentence_582: The Albanian Orthodox Church officially refused to recognize the results, claiming that 24% of the total population adhered to its faith.
sentence_583: Some Muslim Community officials expressed unhappiness with the data claiming that many Muslims were not counted and that the number of adherents numbered some 70% of the Albanian population.
sentence_584: The Albanian Catholic Bishops Conference also cast doubts on the census, complaining that many of its believers were not contacted.
sentence_585: The [[Islam_in_Albania|Muslim Albanians]] are spread throughout the country.
sentence_586: [[Orthodoxy_in_Albania|Orthodox]] and [[Bektashi|Bektashis]] are mostly found in the south, whereas [[Catholicism_in_Albania|Catholics]] mainly live in the north.
sentence_587: In 2008, there were 694 [[Catholic|Catholic]] churches and 425 [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|orthodox]] churches, 568 mosques and 70 [[Bektashi_Order|bektashi]] [[Khanqah|tekkes]] in the country.
sentence_591: The [[Albanian_art|artistic history]] of Albania has been particularly influenced by a multitude of ancient and medieval [[Civilisation|people]], traditions and religions.
sentence_592: It covers a broad spectrum with mediums and disciplines that include painting, [[Pottery|pottery]], sculpture, [[Ceramic|ceramics]] and architecture all of them exemplifying a great variety in style and shape, in different regions and period.
sentence_593: The rise of the [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantine]] and [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman Empire]] in the [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]] was accompanied by a corresponding growth in [[Christian_art|Christian]] and [[Islamic_art|Islamic art]] in the lands of Albania which are apparent in examples of architecture and mosaics throughout the country.
sentence_594: Centuries later, the [[Albanian_Renaissance|Albanian Renaissance]] proved crucial to the emancipation of the modern Albanian culture and saw unprecedented developments in all fields of literature and art whereas artists sought to return to the ideals of [[Impressionism|Impressionism]] and [[Romanticism_(art)|Romanticism]].
sentence_595: However, [[Onufri|Onufri]], [[Kolë_Idromeno|Kolë Idromeno]], [[David_Selenica|David Selenica]], [[Kostandin_Shpataraku|Kostandin Shpataraku]] and the [[Zografi_Brothers|Zografi Brothers]] are the most eminent representatives of Albanian art.
sentence_596: The [[Architecture_of_Albania|architecture of Albania]] reflects the legacy of various civilisations tracing back to the [[Classical_antiquity|classical antiquity]].
sentence_597: Major cities in Albania have evolved from within the castle to include dwellings, religious and commercial structures, with constant redesigning of town squares and evolution of building techniques.
sentence_598: Nowadays, the cities and towns reflect a whole spectrum of various [[Architectural_style|architectural styles]].
sentence_599: In the 20th century, many historical as well as sacred buildings bearing the ancient influence were demolished during the [[Communism_in_Albania|communist era]].
sentence_600: [[Ancient_architecture|Ancient architecture]] is found throughout Albania and most visible in [[Byllis|Byllis]], [[Amantia|Amantia]], [[Phoenice|Phoenice]], [[Apollonia_(Illyria)|Apollonia]], [[Butrint|Butrint]], [[Antigonia_(Chaonia)|Antigonia]], [[Rozafa_Castle|Shkodër]] and [[Durrës_Amphitheatre|Durrës]].
sentence_601: Considering the long period of rule of the [[Byzantine_Empire|Byzantine Empire]], they introduced castles, citadels, churches and monasteries with spectacular wealth of visible [[Mural|murals]] and [[Fresco|frescos]].
sentence_602: Perhaps the best known examples can be found in the southern Albanian cities and surroundings of [[Korçë|Korçë]], [[Berat|Berat]], [[Voskopojë|Voskopojë]] and [[Gjirokastër|Gjirokastër]].
sentence_603: Involving the introduction of [[Ottoman_architecture|Ottoman architecture]] there was a development of mosques and other Islamic buildings, particularly seen in Berat and Gjirokastër.
sentence_604: A productive period of [[Historicism_(art)|Historicism]], [[Art_Nouveau|Art Nouveau]] and [[Neoclassicism|Neoclassicism]] merged into the 19th century, best exemplified in [[Korçë|Korçë]].
sentence_605: The 20th century brought new architectural styles such as the modern [[Italianate_architecture|Italian style]], which is present in [[Tirana|Tirana]] such as the [[Skanderbeg_Square|Skanderbeg Square]] and Ministries.
sentence_606: It is also present in Shkodër, [[Vlorë|Vlorë]], [[Sarandë|Sarandë]] and [[Durrës|Durrës]].
sentence_607: Moreover, other towns received their present-day Albania-unique appearance through various cultural or economic influences.
sentence_608: [[Socialist_classicism|Socialist classicism]] arrived during the [[Peoples_Republic_of_Albania|communist era]] in Albania after the [[Second_World_War|Second World War]].
sentence_609: At this period many socialist-styled complexes, wide roads and factories were constructed, while town squares were redesigned and numerous of historic and important buildings demolished.
sentence_610: Notable examples of that style include the [[Mother_Teresa_Square_(Tirana)|Mother Teresa Square]], [[Pyramid_of_Tirana|Pyramid of Tirana]], [[Palace_of_Congresses|Palace of Congresses]] and so on.
sentence_611: Three Albanian archaeological sites are included in the list of [[UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site|UNESCO World Heritage Sites]].
sentence_612: These include the ancient remains of Butrint, the medieval [[Historic_Centres_of_Berat_and_Gjirokastër|Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër]], and [[Ohrid_Lake|Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region]] site shared with [[North_Macedonia|North Macedonia]] since 2019.
sentence_613: Furthermore, the royal [[Royal_Tombs_of_Selca_e_Poshtme|Illyrian tombs]], the remains of [[Apollonia_(Illyria)|Apollonia]], the ancient [[Durrës_Amphitheatre|Amphitheatre]] of Durrës and the [[Fortress_of_Bashtovë|Fortress of Bashtovë]] has been included on the tentative list of Albania.
sentence_615: Throughout the centuries, [[Albanian_cuisine|Albanian cuisine]] has been widely influenced by [[Albanian_culture|Albanian culture]], [[Geography_of_Albania|geography]] and [[History_of_Albania|history]], and as such, different parts of the country enjoy specific [[Regional_cuisine|regional cuisines]].
sentence_616: Cooking traditions especially vary between the north and the south, owing to differing topography and [[Climate|climate]] that essentially contribute to the excellent growth conditions for a wide array of herbs, fruits, and vegetables.
sentence_617: Albanians produce and use many varieties of fruits such as [[Lemon_(fruit)|lemons]], oranges, [[Figs_(fruit)|figs]], and most notably, [[Olive_(fruit)|olives]], which are perhaps the most important element of Albanian cooking.
sentence_618: Spices and other herbs such as [[Basil_(herb)|basil]], [[Lavender|lavender]], [[Spearmint|mint]], [[Oregano|oregano]], [[Rosemary|rosemary]], and [[Thyme|thyme]] are widely used, as are vegetables such as garlic, onions, [[Bell_pepper|peppers]], potatoes, tomatoes, as well as [[Legume|legumes]] of all types.
sentence_619: With a coastline along the [[Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast|Adriatic]] and [[Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast|Ionian]] in the [[Mediterranean_Sea|Mediterranean Sea]], fish, [[Crustacean|crustaceans]], and seafood are a popular and an integral part of the Albanian diet.
sentence_620: Otherwise, [[Lamb_(food)|lamb]] is the traditional meat for different holidays and [[Religious_festival|religious festivals]] for both [[Christianity_in_Albania|Christians]] and [[Islam_in_Albania|Muslims]], although poultry, beef, and pork are also in plentiful supply.
sentence_621: [[Tavë_kosi|Tavë kosi]] ("[[Soured_milk|soured milk]] [[Casserole|casserole]]") is the [[National_dish|national dish]] of Albania, consisting of lamb and rice baked under a thick, tart veil of [[Yogurt|yogurt]].
sentence_622: Fërgesë is another national dish, made up of peppers, tomatoes, and [[Cottage_cheese|cottage cheese]].
sentence_623: Pite is also popular, a baked pastry with a filling of a mixture of [[Spinach|spinach]] and gjizë (curd) or mish (ground meat).
sentence_624: Petulla, a traditional fried dough, is also a popular speciality, and is served with [[Powdered_sugar|powdered sugar]] or [[Feta_cheese|feta cheese]] and different sorts of [[Fruit_preserves|fruit jams]].
sentence_625: [[Flia|Flia]] consists of multiple crêpe-like layers brushed with cream and served with sour cream.
sentence_626: [[Krofne|Krofne]], similar to [[Berliner_(doughnut)|Berliner doughnuts]], are filled with jam, or chocolate and often eaten during cold winter months.
sentence_627: Coffee is an integral part of the Albanian lifestyle.
sentence_628: The country has more coffee houses per capita than any other country in the world.
sentence_629: Tea is also enjoyed both at home or outside at cafés, bars, or restaurants.
sentence_630: Çaj Mali ([[Sideritis|Sideritis]] tea) is enormously beloved, and a part of the daily routine for most Albanians.
sentence_631: It is cultivated across Southern Albania and noted for its medicinal properties.
sentence_632: Black tea with a slice of lemon and sugar, milk, or honey is also popular.
sentence_633: [[Albanian_wine|Albanian wine]] is also common throughout the country, and has been cultivated for thousands of years.
sentence_634: Albania has a long and ancient history of wine production, and belongs to the [[Old_World_wine|Old World of wine producing countries]].
sentence_635: Its wine is characterized by its sweet taste and traditionally indigenous varieties.
sentence_638: The [[Freedom_of_press|freedom of press]] and [[Freedom_of_speech|speech]], and the right to free expression is guaranteed in the [[Constitution_of_Albania|constitution of Albania]].
sentence_639: Albania was ranked 84th on the [[Press_Freedom_Index|Press Freedom Index]] of 2020 compiled by the [[Reporters_Without_Borders|Reporters Without Borders]], with its score steadily declining since 2003.
sentence_640: Nevertheless in the 2020 report of [[Freedom_in_the_World|Freedom in the World]], the [[Freedom_House|Freedom House]] classified the freedoms of press and speech in Albania as partly free from political interference and manipulation.
sentence_641: Radio Televizioni Shqiptar (RTSH) is the [[National_broadcaster|national broadcaster]] corporation of Albania operating numerous television and radio stations in the country.
sentence_642: The three major private broadcaster corporations are [[Top_Channel|Top Channel]], [[TV_Klan|Televizioni Klan]] and [[Vizion_Plus|Vizion Plus]] whose content are distributed throughout Albania and beyond its territory in [[Kosovo|Kosovo]] and other [[Albanian_language|Albanian-speaking]] territories.
sentence_643: Albanian cinema has its roots in the 20th century and developed after the country's [[Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence|declaration of independence]].
sentence_644: The first [[Movie_theater|movie theater]] exclusively devoted to showing motion pictures was built in 1912 in [[Shkodër|Shkodër]] by an Austrian distribution company with strong efforts by Albanian painter [[Kolë_Idromeno|Kolë Idromeno]].
sentence_645: The opening of other movie theaters followed by 1920 in Shkodër, [[Berat|Berat]], Tirana and [[Vlorë|Vlorë]].
sentence_646: During the [[Peoples_Republic_of_Albania|Peoples Republic of Albania]], Albanian cinema developed rapidly with the inauguration of the [[Kinostudio_Shqipëria_e_Re|Kinostudio Shqipëria e Re]] in Tirana.
sentence_647: In 1953, the Albanian-Soviet [[Epic_film|epic film]], the [[The_Great_Warrior_Skanderbeg|Great Warrior Skanderbeg]], was released chronicling the life and fight of the medieval Albanian hero [[Gjergj_Kastriot_Skanderbeg|Skanderbeg]].
sentence_648: It went on to win the international prize at the [[1954_Cannes_Film_Festival|1954 Cannes Film Festival]].
sentence_649: In 2003, the [[Tirana_International_Film_Festival|Tirana International Film Festival]] was established, the largest film festival in the country.
sentence_650: [[Durrës|Durrës]] is host to the [[Durrës_International_Film_Festival|Durrës International Film Festival]], the second largest film festival, taking place at the [[Durrës_Amphitheatre|Durrës Amphitheatre]].
sentence_652: Albanian folk music is a prominent part of the national identity, and continues to play a major part in overall [[Music_of_Albania|Albanian music]].
sentence_653: Folk music can be divided into two stylistic groups, mainly the northern [[Gheg_Albanian|Gheg]] varieties, and southern [[Labëria|Lab]] and [[Tosk_Albanian|Tosk]] varieties.
sentence_654: Northern and southern traditions are contrasted by a rugged tone from the north, and the more relaxed southern form of music.
sentence_655: Many songs concern events from [[History_of_Albania|Albanian history]] and [[Culture_of_Albania|culture]], including traditional themes of honour, hospitality, treachery, and revenge.
sentence_656: The first compilation of Albanian folk music was made by two [[Himara|Himariot]] musicians, Neço Muka and Koço Çakali, in Paris, during their work with Albanian soprano [[Tefta_Tashko-Koço|Tefta Tashko-Koço]].
sentence_657: Several [[Phonograph_record|gramophone]] compilations were recorded at the time by the three artists, which eventually led to the recognition of [[Albanian_iso-polyphony|Albanian iso-polyphony]] as a [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] [[UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists|Intangible Cultural Heritage]].
sentence_658: Contemporary artists [[Rita_Ora|Rita Ora]], [[Bebe_Rexha|Bebe Rexha]], [[Era_Istrefi|Era Istrefi]], [[Dua_Lipa|Dua Lipa]], [[Ava_Max|Ava Max]], [[Bleona|Bleona]], [[Elvana_Gjata|Elvana Gjata]], [[Ermonela_Jaho|Ermonela Jaho]], and Inva Mula have achieved international recognition for their music, while soprano [[Ermonela_Jaho|Ermonela Jaho]] has been described by some as the "world's most acclaimed soprano".
sentence_659: Albanian opera singer [[Saimir_Pirgu|Saimir Pirgu]] was nominated for the 2017 [[Grammy_Award|Grammy Award]].
sentence_661: Every cultural and geographical region of Albania has its own specific variety of costume that vary in style, material, color, shape, detail, and form.
sentence_662: Presently, [[National_costume_of_Albania|national costumes]] are most often worn during special events and celebrations, mostly at ethnic festivals, religious holidays, weddings, and by performing dance groups.
sentence_663: Some elderly people continue to wear traditional clothing in their daily lives.
sentence_664: Clothing was traditionally made mainly from local materials such as leather, wool, linen, hemp fibre, and silk; Albanian textiles are still embroidered in elaborate ancient patterns.
sentence_665: See also: [[Albania_at_the_Olympics|Albania at the Olympics]] and [[Albania_at_the_Mediterranean_Games|Albania at the Mediterranean Games]]
sentence_666: Albania participated at the [[1972_Summer_Olympics|Olympic Games in 1972]] for the first time.
sentence_667: The country made their Winter Olympic Games debut in [[Winter_Olympics_2006|2006]].
sentence_668: Albania missed the next four games, two of them due to the 1980 and 1984 boycotts, but returned for the 1992 games in [[1992_Olympic_Winter_Games|Barcelona]].
sentence_669: Since then, Albania have participated in all games.
sentence_670: Albania normally competes in events that include swimming, athletics, weightlifting, shooting and wrestling.
sentence_671: The country have been represented by the [[National_Olympic_Committee_of_Albania|National Olympic Committee of Albania]] since 1972.
sentence_672: The nation has participated at the [[Mediterranean_Games|Mediterranean Games]] since the games of [[1987_Mediterranean_Games|1987]] in Syria.
sentence_673: The Albanian athletes have won a total of 43 (8 gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze) medals from [[1987_Mediterranean_Games|1987]] to [[2013_Mediterranean_Games|2013]].
sentence_674: Popular sports in Albania include [[Football_in_Albania|Football]], weightlifting, [[Albania_national_basketball_team|basketball]], volleyball, tennis, swimming, [[Rugby_union|rugby union]] and gymnastics.
sentence_675: Football is by far the most popular sport in Albania.
sentence_676: It is governed by the [[Football_Association_of_Albania|Football Association of Albania]] ([[Albanian_language|Albanian]]: Federata Shqiptare e Futbollit, F.SH.F.), which was created in 1930 and has membership in [[FIFA|FIFA]] and [[UEFA|UEFA]].
sentence_677: Football arrived in Albania early in the 20th century when the inhabitants of the northern city of [[Shkodër|Shkodër]] were surprised to see a strange game being played by students at a Christian mission.
sentence_678: The [[Albania_national_football_team|Albania national football team]], ranking 51st in the [[FIFA_World_Rankings|World]] in 2017 (highest 22nd on 22 August 2015) have won the [[1946_Balkan_Cup|1946 Balkan Cup]] and the [[Rothmans_International_Tournament_2000|Malta Rothmans International Tournament 2000]], but had never participated in any major [[UEFA|UEFA]] or [[FIFA|FIFA]] tournament, until [[UEFA_Euro_2016|UEFA Euro 2016]], Albania's first ever appearance at the continental tournament and at a major men's football tournament.
sentence_679: Albania scored their first ever goal in a major tournament and secured their first ever win in European Championship when they beat [[Romania_national_football_team|Romania]] by 1–0 in a [[UEFA_Euro_2016|UEFA Euro 2016]] match on 19 June 2016.
sentence_680: The most successful football clubs in the country are [[KF_Skënderbeu_Korçë|Skënderbeu]], [[KF_Tirana|KF Tirana]], [[FK_Dinamo_Tirana|Dinamo Tirana]], [[FK_Partizani_Tirana|Partizani]] and [[KF_Vllaznia_Shkodër|Vllaznia]].
sentence_681: Weightlifting is one of the most successful individual sport for the Albanians, with the national team winning medals at the European Weightlifting Championships and the rest international competitions.
sentence_682: Albanian weightlifters have won a total of 16 medals at the European Championships with 1 of them being gold, 7 silver and 8 bronze.
sentence_683: In the [[World_Weightlifting_Championships|World Weightlifting Championships]], the Albanian weightlifting team has won in [[1972_World_Weightlifting_Championships|1972]] a gold in [[2002_World_Weightlifting_Championships|2002]] a silver and in [[2011_World_Weightlifting_Championships|2011]] a bronze medal.
sentence_684: Main articles: [[Albanian_diaspora|Albanian diaspora]] and Albanian communities
sentence_685: Historically, the Albanian people have established several communities in many regions throughout Southern Europe.
sentence_686: The [[Albanian_diaspora|Albanian diaspora]] has been formed since the late [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]], when they emigrated to places such as Italy, especially in [[Sicily|Sicily]] and Calabria, and [[Greece|Greece]] to escape either various socio-political difficulties or the [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman conquest]] of Albania.
sentence_687: Following the fall of communism, large numbers of Albanians have migrated to countries such as Australia, Canada, France, Germany, [[Greece|Greece]], Italy, [[Scandinavia|Scandinavia]], [[Switzerland|Switzerland]], United Kingdom and the United States.
sentence_688: Albanian minorities are present in the neighbouring territories such as the west of [[North_Macedonia|North Macedonia]], the east of [[Montenegro|Montenegro]], [[Kosovo|Kosovo]] in its entirety and southern [[Serbia|Serbia]].
sentence_689: In [[Kosovo|Kosovo]], Albanians make up the largest ethnic group in the country.
sentence_690: Altogether, the number of ethnic Albanian living abroad its territory is estimated to be higher than the total population inside the territory of Albania.

title: Athena

sentence_2: "Athene", "Athina", and "Pallas Athena" redirect here.
sentence_3: For other uses, see [[Athene_(disambiguation)|Athene (disambiguation)]], [[Athina_(disambiguation)|Athina (disambiguation)]], and [[Pallas_Athena_(disambiguation)|Pallas Athena (disambiguation)]].
