sentence_556: It also hosted the [[Walker_Cup|Walker Cup]] in 1983.
sentence_557: Liverpool once contained four greyhound tracks, [[Seaforth_Greyhound_Stadium|Seaforth Greyhound Stadium]] (1933–1965), [[Breck_Park_Stadium|Breck Park Stadium]] (1927–1948), [[Stanley_Greyhound_Stadium_(Liverpool)|Stanley Greyhound Stadium]] (1927–1961) and [[White_City_Stadium_(Liverpool)|White City Stadium]] (1932–1973).
sentence_558: Breck Park also hosted boxing bouts and both Stanley and Seaforth hosted [[Motorcycle_speedway|Motorcycle speedway]].
sentence_559: [[Wavertree_Sports_Park|Wavertree Sports Park]] is home to the Liverpool Harriers athletics club, which has produced such athletes as [[Curtis_Robb|Curtis Robb]], Allyn Condon (the only British athlete to compete at both the Summer and Winter Olympics), and [[Katarina_Johnson-Thompson|Katarina Johnson-Thompson]]; Great Britain was represented by Johnson-Thompson at the [[2012_London_Olympics|2012 London Olympics]] in the women's heptathlon, and she would go on to win the gold medal at the [[2019_World_Championships_in_Athletics|2019 World Championships]], giving Liverpool its first gold medal and breaking the [[List_of_British_records_in_athletics|British record]] in the process.
sentence_560: In August 2012, Liverpool gymnast [[Beth_Tweddle|Beth Tweddle]] won an Olympic bronze medal in [[London_2012|London 2012]] in the uneven bars at her third [[Olympic_Games|Olympic Games]], thus becoming the most decorated British gymnast in history.
sentence_561: Park Road Gymnastics Centre provides training to a high level.
sentence_562: Liverpool has produced several swimmers who have represented their nation at major championships such as the [[Olympic_Games|Olympic Games]].
sentence_563: The most notable of which is [[Stephen_Parry_(swimmer)|Steve Parry]] who claimed a bronze medal at the [[2004_Athens_Olympics|2004 Athens Olympics]] in the 200m butterfly.
sentence_564: Others include Herbert Nickel Haresnape, [[Margaret_Kelly_(swimmer)|Margaret Kelly]], Shellagh Ratcliffe and Austin Rawlinson.
sentence_565: There is a purpose-built aquatics centre at [[Wavertree_Sports_Park|Wavertree Sports Park]], which opened in 2008.
sentence_566: The City of Liverpool Swimming Club has been National Speedo League Champions 8 out of the last 11 years.
sentence_567: The city is the hub of the [[Liverpool_and_District_Cricket_Competition|Liverpool and District Cricket Competition]], an [[England_and_Wales_Cricket_Board|ECB]] [[ECB_Premier_Leagues|Premier League]].
sentence_568: [[Sefton_Park_Cricket_Club|Sefton Park]] and [[Liverpool_Cricket_Club|Liverpool]] are the league's founder members based in the city with Wavertree, Alder and Old Xaverians clubs having joined the league more recently.
sentence_569: Liverpool plays host [[Lancashire_County_Cricket_Club|Lancashire County Cricket Club]] as an outground most seasons, including six of eight home [[County_Championship|County Championship]] games during Lancashire's 2011 title winning campaign whilst [[Old_Trafford_Cricket_Ground|Old Trafford]] was refurbished.
sentence_570: Since 2014 [[Liverpool_Cricket_Club|Liverpool Cricket Club]] has played host to the annual [[Tradition-ICAP_Liverpool_International|Tradition-ICAP Liverpool International]] tennis tournament, which has seen tennis stars such as [[Novak_Djokovic|Novak Djokovic]], [[David_Ferrer|David Ferrer]], [[Mardy_Fish|Mardy Fish]], Laura Robson and [[Caroline_Wozniacki|Caroline Wozniacki]].
sentence_571: Previously this had been held at [[Calderstones_Park|Calderstones Park]], situated in [[Allerton,_Merseyside|Allerton]] in the south of the city.
sentence_572: Liverpool Tennis Development Programme at Wavertree Tennis Centre is one of the largest in the UK.
sentence_573: Professional basketball came to the city in 2007 with the entry of Everton Tigers, now known as [[Mersey_Tigers|Mersey Tigers]], into the elite [[British_Basketball_League|British Basketball League]].
sentence_574: The club was originally associated with Everton F.C., and was part of the Toxteth Tigers youth development programme, which reached over 1,500 young people every year.
sentence_575: The Tigers began to play in Britain's top league for the [[2007–08_British_Basketball_League_season|2007–08 season]], playing at the Greenbank Sports Academy before moving into the newly completed [[Echo_Arena_Liverpool|Echo Arena]] during that season.
sentence_576: After the 2009–10 season, Everton F.C. withdrew funding from the Tigers, who then changed their name to Mersey Tigers.
sentence_577: Their closest professional rivals are the [[Cheshire_Jets|Cheshire Jets]], based 18 miles (29 km) away in [[Chester|Chester]].
sentence_578: Liverpool is one of three cities which still host the traditional sport of [[British_baseball|British baseball]] and it hosts the annual England-Wales international match every two years, alternating with [[Cardiff|Cardiff]] and [[Newport,_Wales|Newport]].
sentence_579: Liverpool Trojans are the oldest existing baseball club in the UK.
sentence_580: The [[2014_Tour_of_Britain|2014 Tour of Britain]] cycle race began in Liverpool on 7 September, utilising a city centre circuit to complete 130 km (80.8 mi) of racing.
sentence_581: The Tour of Britain took nine stages and finished in London on 14 September.
sentence_582: A 2016 study of UK fitness centres found that, of the top 20 UK urban areas, Liverpool had the highest number of leisure and sports centres per capita, with 4.3 centres per 100,000 of the city population.
sentence_583: Liverpool is home to the [[Premier_League|Premier League]] football clubs [[Everton_F.C.|Everton]] and [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool F.C.]] [[Liverpool_F.C.|Liverpool]] has played at [[Anfield|Anfield]] since 1892, when the club was formed to occupy the stadium following [[Everton_F.C.|Everton's]] departure due to a dispute with their landlord.
sentence_584: Liverpool are still playing there 125 years later, although the ground has been completely rebuilt since the 1970s.
sentence_585: The Spion Kop (rebuilt as an all-seater stand in 1994–95) was the most famous part of the ground, gaining cult status across the world due to the songs and celebrations of the many fans who packed onto its terraces.
sentence_586: Anfield is classified as a 4 Star [[UEFA_Elite_Stadium|UEFA Elite Stadium]] with capacity for 54,000 spectators in comfort and is a distinctive landmark in an area filled with smaller and older buildings.
sentence_587: Liverpool club also has a multimillion-pound youth training facility called The Academy.
sentence_588: After leaving Anfield in 1892, Everton moved to [[Goodison_Park|Goodison Park]] on the opposite side of [[Stanley_Park,_Liverpool|Stanley Park]].
sentence_589: Goodison Park was the first major football stadium built in England.
sentence_590: [[Molineux_Stadium|Molineux]] (Wolves' ground) had been opened three years earlier but was still relatively undeveloped.
sentence_591: St. James's Park, Newcastle, opened in 1892, was little more than a field.
sentence_592: Only Scotland had more advanced grounds.
sentence_593: Rangers opened [[Ibrox_Stadium|Ibrox]] in 1887, while [[Celtic_Park|Celtic Park]] was officially inaugurated at the same time as Goodison Park.
sentence_594: Everton performed a miraculous transformation at Mere Green, spending up to £3000 on laying out the ground and erecting stands on three sides.
sentence_595: For £552 Mr Barton prepared the land at 4½d a square yard.
sentence_596: Kelly Brothers of Walton built two uncovered stands each for 4,000 people, and a covered stand seating 3,000, at a total cost of £1,460.
sentence_597: Outside, hoardings cost a further £150, gates and sheds cost £132 10s and 12 turnstiles added another £7 15s to the bill.
sentence_598: The ground was immediately renamed Goodison Park and proudly opened on 24 August 1892, by Lord Kinnaird and Frederick Wall of the FA.
sentence_599: But instead of a match, the 12,000 crowds saw a short athletics meeting followed by a selection of music and a fireworks display.
sentence_600: Everton's first game there was on 2 September 1892 when they beat Bolton 4–2.
sentence_601: It now has the capacity for just under 40,000 spectators all-seated, but the last expansion took place in 1994 when a new goal-end stand gave the stadium an all-seater capacity.
sentence_602: The Main Stand dates back to the 1970s, while the other two stands are refurbished pre-Second World War structures.
sentence_603: Everton is currently looking to relocate.
sentence_604: The club have had previously raised the subject before in 1996, and in 2003 were forced to scrap plans for a 55,000-seat stadium at [[King's_Dock,_Port_of_Liverpool|King's Dock]] due to financial reasons and also [[The_Kirkby_Project|Destination Kirkby]] to move just beyond Liverpool's council boundary in [[Kirkby|Kirkby]].
sentence_605: The latest plan is currently being drawn up to move to nearby [[Bramley-Moore_Dock_Stadium|Bramley-Moore Dock]] on Liverpool's waterfront.
sentence_606: [[Made_in_Liverpool|Made in Liverpool]] is a local television station serving Liverpool City Region and surrounding areas.
sentence_607: The station is owned and operated by Made Television Ltd and forms part of a group of eight local TV stations.
sentence_608: It broadcasts from studios and offices in Liverpool.
sentence_609: The [[ITV_(TV_network)|ITV]] region which covers Liverpool is [[ITV_Granada|ITV Granada]].
sentence_610: In 2006, the Television company opened a new newsroom in the Royal Liver Building.
sentence_611: Granada's regional news broadcasts were produced at the [[Royal_Albert_Dock,_Liverpool|Albert Dock]] News Centre during the 1980s and 1990s.
sentence_612: The [[BBC|BBC]] also opened a new newsroom on Hanover Street in 2006.
sentence_613: ITV's daily magazine programme [[This_Morning_(TV_series)|This Morning]] was broadcast from studios at [[Royal_Albert_Dock,_Liverpool|Albert Dock]] until 1996, when production was moved to London.
sentence_615: was also produced in Liverpool until it was cancelled in 2002.
sentence_616: Liverpool is the home of the TV production company [[Lime_Pictures|Lime Pictures]], formerly Mersey Television, which produced the now-defunct soap operas [[Brookside|Brookside]] and [[Grange_Hill|Grange Hill]].
sentence_617: It also produces the soap opera [[Hollyoaks|Hollyoaks]], which was formerly filmed in [[Chester|Chester]] and began on [[Channel_4|Channel 4]] in 1995.
sentence_618: All three series were/are largely filmed in the [[Childwall|Childwall]] area of Liverpool.
sentence_619: The city has one daily newspaper: the [[Liverpool_Echo|Echo]], published by the Trinity Mirror group.
sentence_620: The Liverpool Daily Post was also published until 2013.
sentence_621: The UK's first online only weekly newspaper called [[Southport_Reporter|Southport Reporter]] (Southport and [[Mersey_Reporter|Mersey Reporter]]), is also one of the many other news outlets that cover the city.
sentence_622: Radio stations include [[BBC_Radio_Merseyside|BBC Radio Merseyside]], [[Capital_Liverpool|Capital Liverpool]], [[Radio_City_(Liverpool)|Radio City]], Greatest Hits Liverpool and [[Radio_City_Talk|Radio City Talk]].
sentence_623: The last three are located in [[Radio_City_Tower|Radio City Tower]] which, along with the two cathedrals, dominates the city's skyline.
sentence_624: The independent media organisation [[Indymedia|Indymedia]] also covers Liverpool, while [[Nerve_(magazine)|Nerve magazine]] publishes articles and reviews of cultural events.
sentence_625: Liverpool has also featured in films; see [[List_of_films_set_in_Liverpool|List of films set in Liverpool]] for some of them.
sentence_626: In films the city has "doubled" for London, Paris, New York, Chicago, Moscow, Dublin, Venice and Berlin.

list.value: "Lyrpole, alias Lyverpoole, a pavid towne, hath but a chapel ... The king hath a castelet there, and the [[Earl_of_Derby|Earl of Darbe]] hath a stone howse there. Irisch merchants cum much thither, as to a good haven ... At Lyrpole is smaul custom payed, that causith marchantes to resorte thither. Good marchandis at Lyrpole, and much Irish yarrn that [[Manchester|Manchester]] men do buy there ..." – [[John_Leland_(antiquary)|John Leland]], Itinerary, c. 1536–1539

"Liverpoole is one of the wonders of Britain ... In a word, there is no town in England, London excepted, that can equal [it] for the fineness of the streets, and the beauty of the buildings." – [[Daniel_Defoe|Daniel Defoe]], [[A_tour_thro'_the_Whole_Island_of_Great_Britain|A tour thro' the Whole Island of Great Britain]], 1721–1726
"[O]ne of the neatest, best towns I have seen in England." – [[John_Wesley|John Wesley]]. Journal, 1755

"I have not come here to be insulted by a set of wretches, every brick in whose infernal town is cemented with an African's blood." – George Frederick Cooke (1756–1812), an actor responding to being hissed at when he came onstage drunk during a visit to Liverpool

"That immense City which stands like another [[Venice|Venice]] upon the water ... where there are riches overflowing and every thing which can delight a man who wishes to see the prosperity of a great community and a great empire ... This quondam village, now fit to be the proud capital of any empire in the world, has started up like an enchanted palace even in the memory of living men." – [[Thomas_Erskine,_1st_Baron_Erskine|Thomas Erskine, 1st Baron Erskine]], 1791
"I have heard of the greatness of Liverpool, but the reality far surpasses my expectation." – [[Albert,_Prince_Consort|Prince Albert]], speech, 1846
"Liverpool ... has become a wonder of the world. It is the New York of Europe, a world city rather than merely British provincial." – [[Illustrated_London_News|Illustrated London News]], 15 May 1886

"The dream represented my situation at the time. I can still see the grayish-yellow raincoats, glistening with the wetness of the rain. Everything was extremely unpleasant, black and opaque – just as I felt then. But I had a vision of unearthly beauty, and that is why I was able to live at all. Liverpool is the "pool of life." The "liver," according to an old view, is the seat of life, that which makes to live." – [[C._G._Jung|C. G. Jung]], Memories, Dreams, Reflections, 1928

"The centre is imposing, dignified and darkish, like a city in a rather gloomy Victorian novel ... We had now arrived in the heart of the big city, and as usual it was almost a heart of darkness. But it looked like a big city, there was no denying that. Here, emphatically, was the English seaport second only to London. The very weight of stone emphasised that fact. And even if the sun never seems to properly rise over it, I like a big city to proclaim itself a big city at once..." – J. B. Priestley, English Journey, 1934

"If Liverpool can get into top gear again, there is no limit to the city's potential. The scale and resilience of the buildings and people is amazing – it is a world city, far more so than London and Manchester. It doesn't feel like anywhere else in Lancashire: comparisons always end up overseas – [[Dublin|Dublin]], or [[Boston|Boston]], or [[Hamburg|Hamburg]]. The city is tremendous, and so, right up to the [[First_World_War|First World War]], were the abilities of the architects who built over it. The centre is humane and convenient to walk around in, but never loses its scale. And, in spite of [[Liverpool_Blitz|the bombings]] and the carelessness, it is still full of superb buildings. Fifty years ago it must have outdone anything in England." – [[Ian_Nairn|Ian Nairn]], Britain's Changing Towns, 1967

title: KLM
sentence_0: This article is about the Amsterdam-based airline.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[KLM_(disambiguation)|KLM (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, legally [[Koninklijk|Koninklijke]] Luchtvaart Maatschappij N.V.
sentence_3: (literal translation: Royal Aviation Company, Inc.), is the [[Flag_carrier|flag carrier]] airline of the [[Netherlands|Netherlands]].
sentence_4: KLM is headquartered in [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]], with its hub at nearby [[Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]].
sentence_5: It is part of the [[Air_France–KLM|Air France–KLM]] group and a member of the SkyTeam airline alliance.
sentence_6: Founded in 1919, KLM is the oldest airline in the world still operating under its original name and had 35,488 employees and a fleet of 119 (excluding subsidiaries) as of 2015.
sentence_7: KLM operates scheduled passenger and cargo services to [[List_of_KLM_destinations|145 destinations]].
sentence_8: In 1919, a young aviator lieutenant named [[Albert_Plesman|Albert Plesman]] sponsored the ELTA aviation exhibition in [[Amsterdam|Amsterdam]].
sentence_9: The exhibition was a great success; after it closed, several Dutch commercial interests intended to establish a Dutch airline, which Plesman was nominated to head.
sentence_10: In September 1919, [[Wilhelmina_of_the_Netherlands|Queen Wilhelmina]] awarded the yet-to-be-founded KLM its "Royal" ("[[Koninklijk|Koninklijke]]") predicate.
sentence_11: On 7 October 1919, eight Dutch businessmen, including [[Frits_Fentener_van_Vlissingen_(1882)|Frits Fentener van Vlissingen]], founded KLM as one of the first commercial airline companies.
sentence_12: Plesman became its first administrator and director.
sentence_13: The first KLM flight took place on 17 May 1920.
sentence_14: KLM's first pilot, Jerry Shaw, flew from [[Croydon_Airport|Croydon Airport]], London, to Amsterdam.
sentence_15: The flight was flown using a leased [[Aircraft_Transport_and_Travel|Aircraft Transport and Travel]] [[Airco_DH.16|De Haviland DH-16]], registration G-EALU, which was carrying two British journalists and some newspapers.
sentence_16: In 1920, KLM carried 440 passengers and 22 tons of freight.
sentence_17: In April 1921, after a winter hiatus, KLM resumed its services using its pilots, and [[Fokker_F.II|Fokker F.II]] and [[Fokker_F.III|Fokker F.III]] aircraft.
sentence_18: In 1921, KLM started scheduled services.
sentence_19: KLM's first intercontinental flight took off on 1 October 1924.
sentence_20: The final destination was [[Halim_Perdanakusuma_International_Airport|Jakarta]] (then called '[[Batavia,_Dutch_East_Indies|Batavia]]'), [[Java|Java]], in the [[Dutch_East_Indies|Dutch East Indies]]; the flight used a [[Fokker_F.VII|Fokker F.VII]] with registration H-NACC and was piloted by Van der Hoop.
sentence_21: In September 1929, regular scheduled services between Amsterdam and Batavia commenced.
sentence_22: Until the outbreak of the [[Second_World_War|Second World War]] in 1939, this was the world's longest-distance scheduled service by airplane.
sentence_23: By 1926, it was offering flights to Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Brussels, Paris, London, Bremen, Copenhagen, and Malmö, using primarily Fokker F.II and Fokker F.III aircraft.
sentence_24: In 1930, KLM carried 15,143 passengers.
sentence_25: The [[Douglas_DC-2|Douglas DC-2]] was introduced on the Batavia service in 1934.
sentence_26: The first experimental transatlantic KLM flight was between Amsterdam and [[Curaçao|Curaçao]] in December 1934 using the [[Fokker_F.XVIII|Fokker F.XVIII]] "Snip".
sentence_27: The first of the airline's [[Douglas_DC-3|Douglas DC-3]] aircraft were delivered in 1936; these replaced the DC-2s on the service via Batavia to [[Sydney_Airport|Sydney]].
sentence_28: KLM was the first airline to serve [[Manchester_Airport|Manchester's new Ringway airport]], starting June 1938.
sentence_29: KLM was the only civilian airline to receive the [[Douglas_DC-5|Douglas DC-5]]; the airline used two of them in the West Indies and sold two to the East Indies government, and is thus the only airline to have operated all Douglas 'DC' models other than the DC-1.
sentence_30: Further information: [[1942_KNILM_Douglas_DC-3_shootdown|1942 KNILM Douglas DC-3 shootdown]]
sentence_31: When Germany invaded the Netherlands on 10 May 1940, several KLM aircraft—mostly DC-3s and a few DC-2s—were en route to or from the Far East, or were operating services in Europe.
sentence_32: Five [[Douglas_DC-3|DC-3s]] and one [[Douglas_DC-2|DC-2]] were taken to Britain.
sentence_33: During the war, these aircraft and crew members flew scheduled passenger flights between Bristol and Lisbon under [[British_Overseas_Airways_Corporation|BOAC]] registration.
sentence_34: The Douglas DC-3 PH-ALI "Ibis", then registered as G-AGBB, was attacked by the [[Luftwaffe|Luftwaffe]] on 15 November 1942, 19 April 1943, and finally on 1 June 1943 as [[BOAC_Flight_777|BOAC Flight 777]], killing all passengers and crew.
sentence_35: Some KLM aircraft and their crews ended up in the Australia-Dutch East Indies region, where they helped transport refugees from Japanese aggression in that area.
sentence_36: Although operations paused in Europe, KLM continued to fly and expand in the Caribbean.
sentence_37: Also during the Second World War a KLM [[1942_KNILM_Douglas_DC-3_shootdown|flight]] carrying eight passengers, four crew and a 2020 value of $15 million in diamonds was shot down by Japanese fighters returning from the [[Attack_on_Broome|Attack on Broome]] approximately 1,000 miles north of [[Perth|Perth]] in [[Western_Australia|Western Australia]].
sentence_38: The pilot managed to dive to evade the fighters and crash land on the beach but three passengers and one crewman were killed.
sentence_39: After six days and suffering other attacks by strafing Japanese pilots they were rescued.
sentence_40: The diamonds may have been heisted by a survivor or civilian happening upon the wreck soon after.
sentence_41: After the end of the Second World War in August 1945, KLM immediately started to rebuild its network.
sentence_42: Since the Dutch East Indies were in a state of revolt, Plesman's priority was to re-establish KLM's route to Batavia.
sentence_43: This service was reinstated by the end of 1945.
sentence_44: Domestic and European flights resumed in September 1945, initially with a fleet of Douglas [[Douglas_DC-3|DC-3s]] and [[Douglas_DC-4|Douglas DC-4s]].
sentence_45: On 21 May 1946, KLM was the first continental European airline to start scheduled transatlantic flights between Amsterdam and [[New_York_City|New York City]] using Douglas DC-4 aircraft.
sentence_46: By 1948, KLM had reconstructed its network and services to Africa, North and South America, and the [[Caribbean|Caribbean]] resumed.
sentence_47: Long-range, pressurized [[Lockheed_Constellation|Lockheed Constellations]] and [[Douglas_DC-6|Douglas DC-6s]] joined KLM's fleet in the late 1940s; the [[Convair_240|Convair 240]] short-range pressurized twin-engined airliner began European flights for the company in late 1948.
sentence_48: During the immediate post-war period, the Dutch government expressed interest in gaining a majority stake in KLM, thus partially nationalizing it.
sentence_49: Plesman wanted KLM to remain a private company under private control; he allowed the Dutch government to acquire a minority stake in the airline.
sentence_50: In 1950, KLM carried 356,069 passengers.
sentence_51: The expansion of the network continued in the 1950s with the addition of several destinations in western North America.
sentence_52: KLM's fleet expanded with the addition of new versions of the Lockheed Constellation and [[Lockheed_L-188_Electra|Lockheed Electra]], of which KLM was the first European airline to fly.
sentence_53: On 31 December 1953, the founder and president of KLM, Albert Plesman, died at the age of 64.
sentence_54: He was succeeded as president by Fons Aler.
sentence_55: After Plesman's death, the company and other airlines entered a difficult economic period.
sentence_56: The conversion to jet aircraft placed a further financial burden on KLM.
sentence_57: The Netherlands government increased its ownership of the company to two-thirds, thus partly nationalizing it.
sentence_58: The board of directors remained under the control of private shareholders.
sentence_59: On 25 July 1957, the airline introduced its flight simulator for the [[Douglas_DC-7|Douglas DC-7]]C – the last KLM aircraft with piston engines – which opened the transpolar route from Amsterdam via [[Anchorage|Anchorage]] to [[Tokyo|Tokyo]] on 1 November 1958.
sentence_60: Each crew flying the transpolar route over the Arctic was equipped with a winter survival kit, including a 7.62 mm selective-fire [[AR-10|AR-10]] carbine for use against polar bears, in the event the plane was forced down onto the polar ice.
sentence_61: The four-engine turboprop [[Vickers_Viscount|Vickers Viscount]] 800 was introduced on European routes in 1957.
sentence_62: Beginning in September 1959, KLM introduced the four-engine turboprop [[Lockheed_L-188_Electra|Lockheed L-188 Electra]] onto some of its European and Middle Eastern routes.
sentence_63: In March 1960, the airline introduced the first [[Douglas_DC-8|Douglas DC-8]] jet into its fleet.
sentence_64: In 1961, KLM reported its first year of losses.
sentence_65: In 1961, the airline's president Fons Aler was succeeded by [[Ernst_van_der_Beugel|Ernst van der Beugel]].
sentence_66: This change of leadership, however, did not lead to a reversal of KLM's financial difficulties.
sentence_67: Van der Beugel resigned as president in 1963 due to health reasons.
sentence_68: Horatius Albarda was appointed to succeed Ernst van der Beugel as president of KLM in 1963.
sentence_69: Alberda initiated a reorganization of the company, which led to the reduction of staff and air services.
sentence_70: In 1965, Alberda died in an air crash and was succeeded as president by Dr. Gerrit van der Wal.
sentence_71: Van der Wal forged an agreement with the Dutch government that KLM would be once again run as a private company.
sentence_72: By 1966, the stake of the Dutch government in KLM was reduced to a minority stake of 49.5%.
sentence_73: In 1966, KLM introduced the [[Douglas_DC-9|Douglas DC-9]] on European and Middle East routes.
sentence_74: The new terminal buildings at [[Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]] opened in April 1967, and in 1968 the stretched [[Douglas_DC-8-63|Douglas DC-8-63]] ("Super DC-8") entered service.
sentence_75: With 244 seats, it was the largest airliner at the time.
sentence_76: KLM was the first airline to put the higher-gross-weight [[Boeing_747|Boeing 747-200]]B, powered by [[Pratt_&_Whitney_JT9D|Pratt & Whitney JT9D]] engines, into service in February 1971; this began the airline's use of [[Widebody|widebody]] jets.
sentence_77: In March 1971, KLM opened its current headquarters in [[Amstelveen|Amstelveen]].
sentence_78: In 1972, it purchased the first of several [[McDonnell_Douglas_DC-10|McDonnell Douglas DC-10]] aircraft—McDonnell Douglas's response to [[Boeing|Boeing]]'s 747.
sentence_79: In 1973, Sergio Orlandini was appointed to succeed Gerrit van der Wal as president of KLM.
sentence_80: At the time, KLM, as well as other airlines, had to deal with overcapacity.
sentence_81: Orlandini proposed to convert KLM 747s to "combis" that could carry a combination of passengers and freight in a mixed configuration on the main deck of the aircraft.
sentence_82: In November 1975, the first of these seven [[Boeing_747-200|Boeing 747-200]]B Combi aircraft were added to the KLM fleet.
sentence_83: The airline previously operated DC-8 passenger and freight combi aircraft as well and currently operates [[Boeing_747-400|Boeing 747-400]] combi aircraft.
sentence_84: The [[1973_oil_crisis|1973 oil crisis]], which caused difficult economic conditions, led KLM to seek government assistance in arranging debt refinancing.
sentence_85: The airline issued additional shares of stock to the government in return for its money.
sentence_86: In the late 1970s, the government's stake had again increased to a majority of 78%, effectively re-nationalizing it.
sentence_87: The company management remained under the control of private stakeholders.
sentence_88: In 1980, KLM carried 9,715,069 passengers.
sentence_89: In 1983, it reached an agreement with Boeing to convert ten of its Boeing 747-200 aircraft (Three 747-200Bs and Seven 747-200Ms) into Boeing 747-300s with the stretched-upper-deck modification.
sentence_90: The work started in 1984 at the Boeing factory in [[Everett,_Washington|Everett, Washington]], and finished in 1986.
sentence_91: The converted aircraft were called Boeing 747-200SUD or 747-300, which the airline operated in addition to three newly built Boeing 747-300s manufactured from the ground up.
sentence_92: In 1983, KLM took delivery of the first of ten [[Airbus_A310|Airbus A310]] passenger jets.
sentence_93: Sergio Orlandini retired in 1987 and was succeeded as president of KLM by Jan de Soet.
sentence_94: In 1986, the Dutch government's shareholding in KLM was reduced to 54.8 percent.
sentence_95: It was expected that this share would be further reduced during the decade.
sentence_96: The [[Boeing_747-400|Boeing 747-400]] was introduced into KLM's fleet in June 1989.
sentence_97: With the liberalization of the European market, KLM started developing its hub at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol by feeding its network with traffic from affiliated airlines.
sentence_98: As part of its development of a worldwide network, KLM acquired a 20% stake in [[Northwest_Airlines|Northwest Airlines]] in July 1989.
sentence_99: In 1990, KLM carried 16,000,000 passengers.
sentence_100: KLM president Jan de Soet retired at the end of 1990 and was succeeded in 1991 by Pieter Bouw.
sentence_101: In December 1991, KLM was the first European airline to introduce a frequent flyer loyalty program, which was called Flying Dutchman.
sentence_102: In January 1993, the United States Department of Transportation granted KLM and Northwest Airlines anti-trust immunity, which allowed them to intensify their partnership.
sentence_103: As of September 1993, the airlines operated their flights between the United States and Europe as part of a joint venture.
sentence_104: In March 1994, KLM and Northwest Airlines introduced World Business Class on intercontinental routes.
sentence_105: KLM's stake in Northwest Airlines was increased to 25% in 1994.
sentence_106: KLM introduced the [[Boeing_767|Boeing 767-300ER]] in July 1995.
sentence_107: In January 1996, KLM acquired a 26% share in [[Kenya_Airways|Kenya Airways]], the flag-carrier airline of Kenya.
sentence_108: In 1997, Pieter Bouw resigned as president of KLM and was succeeded by [[L._M._van_Wijk|Leo van Wijk]].
sentence_109: In August 1998, KLM repurchased all regular shares from the Dutch government to make KLM a private company.
sentence_110: On 1 November 1999, KLM founded AirCares, a communication and fundraising platform supporting worthy causes and focusing on underprivileged children.
sentence_111: KLM renewed its intercontinental fleets by replacing the Boeing 767s, Boeing 747-300s, and eventually, the [[McDonnell_Douglas_MD-11|McDonnell Douglas MD-11s]] with [[Boeing_777|Boeing 777-200ERs]] and [[Airbus_A330|Airbus A330-200s]].
sentence_112: Some 747s were withdrawn from service first.
sentence_113: The MD-11s remained in service until October 2014.
sentence_114: The first Boeing 777 was received on 25 October 2003, while the first Airbus A330-200 was introduced on 25 August 2005.
sentence_115: On 30 September 2003, [[Air_France|Air France]] and KLM agreed to a merger plan in which Air France and KLM would become subsidiaries of a holding company called [[Air_France–KLM|Air France–KLM]].
sentence_116: Both airlines would retain their own brands; both [[Charles_de_Gaulle_Airport|Charles de Gaulle Airport]] and [[Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]] would become key hubs.
sentence_117: In February 2004, the [[European_Commission|European Commission]] and [[United_States_Department_of_Justice|United States Department of Justice]] approved the proposed merger of the airlines.
sentence_118: In April 2004, an exchange offer in which KLM shareholders exchanged their KLM shares for Air France shares took place.
sentence_119: Since 5 May 2004, Air France–KLM has been listed on the [[Euronext|Euronext]] exchanges in Paris, Amsterdam and New York.
sentence_120: In September 2004, the merger was completed by creation of the Air France–KLM holding company.
sentence_121: The merger resulted in the world's largest airline group and should have led to an estimated annual cost-saving of between €400 million and €500 million.
sentence_122: It did not appear that KLM's longstanding joint venture with Northwest Airlines—which merged with [[Delta_Air_Lines|Delta Air Lines]] in 2008—was affected by the merger with Air France.
sentence_123: KLM and Northwest joined the SkyTeam alliance in September 2004.
sentence_124: Also in 2004, senior management came under fire for providing itself with controversial bonuses after the merger with Air France, while 4,500 jobs were lost at KLM.
sentence_125: After external pressure, management gave up on these bonuses.
sentence_126: In March 2007, KLM started to use the [[Amadeus_CRS|Amadeus]] reservation system, along with partner Kenya Airways.
sentence_127: After 10 years as president of the airline, Leo van Wijk resigned from his position and was succeeded by [[Peter_Hartman|Peter Hartman]].
sentence_128: Beginning in September 2010, KLM integrated the passenger division of [[Martinair|Martinair]] into KLM, transferring all personnel and routes.
sentence_129: By November 2011, Martinair consisted of only the cargo and maintenance division.
sentence_130: In March 2011, KLM and [[InselAir|InselAir]] reached an agreement for mutual cooperation on InselAir destinations, thus expanding its passenger services.
sentence_131: Beginning 27 March 2011, KLM passengers could fly to all InselAir destinations through InselAir's hubs in [[Curaçao|Curaçao]] and [[Sint_Maarten|Sint Maarten]].
sentence_132: This cooperation was extended to a codeshare agreement in 2012.
sentence_133: In early 2018, the cooperation with Inselair was terminated, including any interlining agreements, after Inselair found itself in financial difficulties which forced the airline to sell off part of its fleet and cancel some of its routes.
sentence_134: On 20 February 2013, KLM announced that Peter Hartman would resign as president and CEO of KLM on 1 July 2013.
sentence_135: He was succeeded by [[Camiel_Eurlings|Camiel Eurlings]].
sentence_136: Hartman remained employed by the company until he retired on 1 January 2014.
sentence_137: On 15 October 2014, KLM announced that Eurlings, in joint consultation with the supervisory board, had decided to immediately resign as president and CEO.
sentence_138: As of this date, he was succeeded by [[Pieter_Elbers|Pieter Elbers]].
sentence_139: KLM received the award for "Best Airline Staff Service" in Europe at the World Airline Awards 2013.
sentence_140: This award represents the rating for an airline's performance across both airport staff and cabin staff combined.
sentence_141: It is the second consecutive year that KLM won this award; in 2012 it was awarded with this title as well.
sentence_142: On 19 June 2012, KLM made the first transatlantic flight fueled partly by sustainable biofuels to [[Rio_de_Janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]].
sentence_143: This was the longest distance any aircraft had flown on biofuels.
sentence_144: In 2019, KLM celebrated its centennial, as it was founded in 1919.
sentence_145: Since it is the oldest airline still operating under its original name, it was the first airline to achieve this feat.

sentence_147: As of October 2015, KLM's corporate leader is its president and chief executive officer (CEO) Pieter Elbers, who replaced Camiel Eurlings suddenly on 15 October 2014.
sentence_148: The president and CEO is part of the larger Executive Committee, which manages KLM and consists of the statutory managing directors and executive vice-presidents of KLM's business units that are represented in the Executive Committee.
sentence_149: The supervision and management of KLM are structured in accordance with the two-tier model; the Board of Managing Directors is supervised by a separate and independent [[Supervisory_Board|Supervisory Board]].
sentence_150: The Supervisory Board also supervises the general performance of KLM.
sentence_151: The Board of Managing Directors is formed by the four Managing Directors, including the CEO.
sentence_152: Nine Supervisory Directors compose the Supervisory Board.
sentence_153: KLM's head office is located in Amstelveen, on a 6.5-hectare (16-acre) site near [[Schiphol_Airport|Schiphol Airport]].
sentence_154: The airline's current headquarters was built between 1968 and 1970.
sentence_155: Before the opening of the new headquarters, the airline's head office was on the property of Schiphol Airport in [[Haarlemmermeer|Haarlemmermeer]].

sentence_158: KLM also worked closely with [[ALM_Antillean_Airlines|ALM Antillean Airlines]] in the Caribbean in order to provide air service for the Dutch controlled islands in the region with KLM aircraft such as the [[Douglas_DC-8|Douglas DC-8]] and [[McDonnell_Douglas_DC-9-30|McDonnell Douglas DC-9-30]] being operated by KLM flight crews on behalf of ALM.
sentence_159: KLM Asia (Chinese: 荷蘭亞洲航空公司; [[Pinyin|pinyin]]: Hélán Yàzhōu Hángkōng Gōngsī) is a wholly KLM-owned subsidiary registered in Taiwan.
sentence_160: The airline was established in 1995 to operate flights to [[Taipei|Taipei]] without compromising the traffic rights held by KLM for destinations in the People's Republic of China.
sentence_161: The livery of KLM Asia uses the same color scheme and livery of the original KLM but the only notable difference is that it lacks Dutch national symbols, such as the flag of the Netherlands and KLM's stylised [[Monarchy_of_the_Netherlands|Dutch Crown]] logo.
sentence_162: Instead, it features a special KLM Asia logo.
sentence_163: This division of the airline's fleet consists, as of March 2020, of seven [[Boeing_777-200ER|Boeing 777-200ER]] and two [[Boeing_777-300ER|Boeing 777-300ER]] aircraft.
sentence_164: KLM Asia initially operated the Amsterdam-[[Suvarnabhumi_Airport|Bangkok]]-[[Taiwan_Taoyuan_International_Airport|Taipei]] route with a B747-400 Combi or a B747-400 non-combi aircraft.
sentence_165: Since March 2012, it has operated the revised Amsterdam-Taipei-[[Ninoy_Aquino_International_Airport|Manila]] route with Boeing 777-200ER/-300ER aircraft.
sentence_166: Some aircraft are already painted in the revised KLM Asia livery of 2014.
sentence_167: KLM Asia aircraft are also occasionally used to service other destinations in the wider KLM network.
sentence_168: Dirk Roosenburg designed the KLM logo at its establishment in 1919; he intertwined the letter K, L, and M, and gave them wings and a [[Crown_of_the_Netherlands|crown]].
sentence_169: The crown was depicted to denote KLM's royal status, which was granted at KLM's establishment.
sentence_170: The logo became known as the "vinklogo" in reference to the [[Common_chaffinch|common chaffinch]].
sentence_171: The KLM logo was largely redesigned in 1961 by [[F.H.K._Henrion|F.H.K.
sentence_172: Henrion]].
sentence_173: The crown, redesigned using a line, four blue circles and a cross, was retained.
sentence_174: In 1991, the logo was further revised by Chris Ludlow of Henrion, Ludlow & Schmidt.
sentence_175: In addition to its main logo, KLM displays its alliance status in its branding, including "Worldwide Reliability" with Northwest Airlines (1993–2002) and the SkyTeam alliance (2004–present).
sentence_176: KLM has utilized several major liveries since its founding, with numerous variations on each.
sentence_177: Initially, many aircraft featured a bare-metal fuselage with a stripe above the windows bearing the phrase "The Flying Dutchman".
sentence_178: The rudder was divided into three segments and painted to match the Dutch flag.
sentence_179: Later aircraft types sometimes bore a white upper fuselage, and additional detail striping and titling.
sentence_180: In the mid-1950s, the livery was changed to feature a split cheatline in two shades of blue on a white upper fuselage and angled blue stripes on the vertical stabilizer.
sentence_181: The tail stripes were later enlarged and made horizontal, and the then-new crown logo was placed in a white circle.
sentence_182: The final major variation of this livery saw the vertical stabilizer painted completely white with the crown logo in the center.
sentence_183: All versions of this livery had small "KLM Royal Dutch Airlines" titles, first in red, and later in blue.
sentence_184: Since 1971, the KLM livery has primarily featured a bright blue fuselage, with variations on the striping and details.
sentence_185: Originally a wide, dark blue cheatline covered the windows and was separated from the light grey lower fuselage by a thin white stripe.
sentence_186: The KLM logo was placed centrally on the white tail and the front of the fuselage.
sentence_187: In December 2002, KLM introduced an updated livery in which the white strip was removed and the dark-blue cheatline was significantly narrowed.
sentence_188: The bright blue colour was retained and now covers most of the fuselage.
sentence_189: The KLM logo was placed more centrally on the fuselage while its position on the tail and the tail design remained the same.
sentence_190: In 2014, KLM modified its livery with a swooping cheatline that wraps around the entire forward fuselage.
sentence_191: The livery was first introduced on [[Embraer_190|Embraer 190s]].
sentence_192: In April 2010, KLM introduced new uniforms for its female cabin attendants, ground attendants and pilots at KLM and KLM Cityhopper.
sentence_193: The new uniform was designed by Dutch couturier Mart Visser.
sentence_194: It retains the KLM blue colour that was introduced in 1971 and adds a touch of orange—the national colour of the Netherlands.
sentence_195: KLM has used several slogans for marketing throughout its operational history:

list.value: "The businessman travels, sends, and receives by KLM" (translated from Dutch) (1920s)

sentence_196: KLM has an extensive presence on [[Social_media|social media]] platforms and also runs a blog.
sentence_197: Customers can make inquiries through these channels.
sentence_198: The airline also uses these networks to inform customers of KLM news, marketing campaigns and promotions.
sentence_199: The airline's use of social media platforms to reach customers peaked when the Icelandic volcano [[Eyjafjallajökull|Eyjafjallajökull]] erupted in April 2010, causing widespread disruption to air traffic.
sentence_200: Customers used the social networks to contact the airline, which used them to provide information about the situation.
sentence_201: Following the increased use of social media, KLM created a centralized, public social media website named the Social Media Hub in October 2010.
sentence_202: KLM has developed several services based on these social platforms, including:

list.value: Meet & Seat; this service allows passengers to find information about people who will be on the same KLM flight by connecting their Facebook or LinkedIn profiles to the flight. Meet & Seat facilitates contact with fellow travelers who have the same background or interests. By launching Meet & Seat, KLM became the first airline to integrate social networking into its regular flight process.
Trip Planner; this platform uses Facebook to organize a trip with Facebook friends.

Twitterbots; KLM operates several [[Twitterbot|Twitterbots]], including one to request the current status of a flight and one to request the lowest KLM fares to a destination on a specified date or month.

sentence_203: In June 2013, KLM launched its own 3D strategy game "Aviation Empire" for [[IOS|iOS]] and [[Android_(operating_system)|Android]] platforms.
sentence_204: The game allows users to experience airline management.
sentence_205: Players manage KLM from its establishment until the present; they can by investing in a fleet, build a network with international destinations and develop airports.
sentence_206: The game combines the digital world with the real world by enabling the unlocking of airports by [[GPS|GPS]] check-ins.
sentence_207: KLM started KLM AirCares, a program that aids underprivileged children in developing countries to which KLM flies, in 1999.
sentence_208: The airline collects money and airmiles from passengers.
sentence_209: In 2012, new applications for support from the program were suspended because it needed an overhaul.
sentence_210: Main article: [[List_of_KLM_destinations|List of KLM destinations]]
sentence_211: KLM and its partners serve 133 destinations in 70 countries on five continents from their hub at [[Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]].
sentence_212: Codeshare agreements bring the total amount of destinations available via KLM to 826.
