sentence_215: KLM's first of 8 Boeing 787-10 aircraft was delivered on 28 June 2019; it featured 100th anniversary markings.
sentence_216: On 19 June 2013, KLM had ordered 7 [[Airbus_A350_XWB|Airbus A350-900s]].
sentence_217: In June 2019, Air France–KLM announced that KLM will not take up any of the group's ordered A350s, because of fleet rationalization purposes.
sentence_218: CEO Ben Smith has announced at Air France's Investor Day (5 November 2019) in Paris that "in the near future" KLM will only use the 777 and 787 as their long-haul fleet, retiring their 13 A330's.
sentence_219: This move will make KLM an all-Boeing airline.
sentence_220: KLM has several aircraft painted in special liveries; they include:

list.value: PH-BVA, a Boeing 777-300ER, features an orange forward fuselage that fades into the standard blue to commemorate the Netherlands national team's participation in the [[2016_Summer_Olympics|2016 Summer Olympics]] in [[Rio_de_Janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]].

PH-KZU, a Fokker F70, has been applied with a special livery featuring [[Anthony_Fokker|Anthony Fokker]], the founder of [[Fokker|Fokker]], commemorating the airline's long-standing history with Fokker aircraft and the phase-out of the [[Fokker_70|Fokker 70]] aircraft in October 2017.
Several aircraft bear the silver SkyTeam alliance livery, including PH-BVD (a 777-300ER), PH-BXO (a 737-900), and PH-EZX (a KLM Cityhopper ERJ-190).
PH-BKA, a Boeing 787-10, features the standard KLM livery with a 100 wrapped around its lettering on the plane, this is because of the 100 years of being an established airline.

sentence_221: KLM has three cabin classes for international long-haul routes; World Business Class, Economy Comfort and Economy.
sentence_222: Personal screens with audio-video on-demand, satellite telephone, SMS, and e-mail services are available in all cabins on all long-haul aircraft.
sentence_223: European short-haul and medium-haul flights have Economy seats in the rear cabin, and Economy Comfort and Europe Business in the forward cabin.
sentence_224: World Business Class is KLM's long-haul business class product.
sentence_225: Seats in the older World Business Class are 20 inches (51 cm) wide and have a 60-inch (150 cm) [[Seat_pitch|pitch]].
sentence_226: Seats can be reclined into a 170-degree angled flat bed with a length of 75 inches (190 cm).
sentence_227: Seats are equipped with a 10.4-inch (26 cm) personal entertainment system with audio and video on demand in the armrest, privacy canopy, massage function and laptop power ports.
sentence_228: World Business Class seating is in a 2–2–2 abreast arrangement on all Airbus A330s.
sentence_229: In March 2013, KLM introduced a new World Business Class seat to the long-haul fleet.
sentence_230: Dutch designer Hella Jongerius designed the new cabin.
sentence_231: The diamond-type seat is manufactured by [[E_Aerospace|B/E Aerospace]] and is currently installed on all Airbus A330s and Boeing 777s.
sentence_232: The seats were also refurbished on former KLM Boeing 747-400s between 2013 and 2014.
sentence_233: The new seats are fully flat and offer 17-inch (43 cm)-high definition personal entertainment systems.
sentence_234: When fully flat, the bed is about 2 metres (6.6 ft) long.
sentence_235: The cabin features a [[Cradle-to-cradle|cradle-to-cradle]] carpet made from old uniforms woven in an intricate pattern, which is combined with new pillows and curtains with a similar design.
sentence_236: A completely new design of Business Class seat was introduced with the launch of KLM's Boeing 787; this aircraft's business class seats are based on the Zodiac Cirrus platform used by Air France.
sentence_237: The new seats lie fully flat, with a 1-2-1 layout so every passenger has direct aisle access, a large side-storage area and 16-inch (41 cm) HD video screen.
sentence_238: Dutch design group [[Viktor_&_Rolf|Viktor & Rolf]] has designed and provides amenity kits to World Business Class passengers.
sentence_239: A new design will be introduced each year and the color of the kits will change every six months.
sentence_240: The kit contains socks, eye mask, toothbrush, toothpaste, earplugs and Viktor & Rolf lip balm.
sentence_241: Europe Business Class is KLM's and KLM Cityhopper's short-haul business-class.
sentence_242: Europe Business Class seats are 17-inch (43 cm) wide and have an average pitch of 33 inches (84 cm).
sentence_243: Middle seats in rows of three are blocked to increase passengers' personal space.
sentence_244: Europe Business Class seats feature extra legroom and recline further than regular Economy Class seats.
sentence_245: In-seat power is available on all [[Boeing_737_Next_Generation|Boeing 737]] aircraft.
sentence_246: Europe Business Class has no personal entertainment.
sentence_247: Seating is arranged 3–3 abreast with the middle seat blocked on the Boeing 737 aircraft, and a 2–2 abreast arrangement on the Embraer 190 aircraft.
sentence_248: Economy Comfort is the premium economy class offered on all KLM and KLM Cityhopper flights.
sentence_249: Economy Comfort seats on long-haul flights have 4 inches (10 cm) more pitch than Economy Class, a 35–36-inch (89–91 cm) pitch and recline up to 7 inches (18 cm); double the recline of Economy.
sentence_250: Economy Comfort seats on short-haul flights have 3.5 inches (8.9 cm) more pitch, totaling 33.5–34.5-inch (85–88 cm), and can recline up to 5 inches (13 cm) (40%) further.
sentence_251: Except for the increased pitch and recline, seating and service in Economy Comfort is the same as in Economy Class.
sentence_252: Economy Comfort is located in a separate cabin before the Economy Class; passengers can exit the aircraft before Economy passengers.
sentence_253: Economy Comfort seats can be reserved by Economy Class passengers.
sentence_254: The service is free for passengers with a full-fare ticket, for Flying Blue Platinum members and Delta Air Lines SkyMiles Platinum or Diamond members.
sentence_255: Discounts apply for Flying Blue Silver or Gold members, SkyTeam Elite Plus members and Delta SkyMiles members.
sentence_256: The Economy Class seats on long-haul flights have a 31-to-32-inch (79–81 cm) pitch and are 17.5 inches (44 cm) wide.
sentence_257: All seats are equipped with adjustable winged headrests, a 9-inch (23 cm) PTV with AVOD, and a personal handset satellite telephone that can be used with a credit card.
sentence_258: Economy Class seats in Airbus A330-300 aircraft are also equipped with in-seat power.
sentence_259: The Economy Class seats on short-haul flights have a 30-to-31-inch (76–79 cm) pitch and are 17 inches (43 cm) wide.
sentence_260: The Economy Class seats on short-haul flights do not feature any personal entertainment.
sentence_261: The long-haul Economy Class seating is in a 3–4–3 abreast arrangement on the Boeing 747-400, Boeing 777-300ER aircraft and on Boeing 777-200ER aircraft, a 3-3-3 abreast arrangement on the Boeing 787-9 aircraft, and a 2–4–2 abreast arrangement on the Airbus A330 aircraft.
sentence_262: The short-haul Economy Class seating is in a 3–3 abreast arrangement on the Boeing 737 aircraft and a 2–2 abreast arrangement on the Embraer 175 and 190 aircraft, and the seats on these aircraft are 17 inches (43 cm) wide.
sentence_263: The [[Tenerife_airport_disaster|Tenerife disaster]], which occurred on 27 March 1977, remains the accident with the highest number of airliner passenger fatalities, as well as the most recent fatal and notable incident involving a KLM aircraft.
sentence_264: 583 people died when a KLM [[Boeing_747-200B|Boeing 747-200B]] attempted to take off without clearance, and collided with a taxiing [[Pan_American_World_Airways|Pan Am]] [[Boeing_747-100|Boeing 747-100]] at Los Rodeos Airport on the [[Canary_Island|Canary Island]] of [[Tenerife|Tenerife]], [[Spain|Spain]].
sentence_265: No one on the KLM 747 survived (14 crew, 234 passengers were killed) while 61 of the 396 passengers and crew on the Pan Am aircraft survived.
sentence_266: Pilot error from the KLM aircraft was the primary cause.
sentence_267: Owing to a communication misunderstanding, the KLM captain thought he had clearance for takeoff.
sentence_268: Another cause was dense fog, meaning the KLM flight crew was unable to see the Pan Am aircraft on the runway until immediately prior to the collision.
sentence_269: The accident had a lasting influence on the industry, particularly in the area of communication.
sentence_270: An increased emphasis was placed on using standardized phraseology in air traffic control (ATC) communication by both controllers and pilots alike, thereby reducing the chance for misunderstandings.
sentence_271: As part of these changes, the word "takeoff" was removed from general usage, and is only spoken by ATC when clearing an aircraft to take off.
sentence_272: Main article: [[List_of_KLM_accidents_and_incidents|List of KLM accidents and incidents]]

title: Los Angeles
sentence_0: This article is about the U.S. city.
sentence_1: For the county, see [[Los_Angeles_County|Los Angeles County]].
sentence_2: For other uses, see [[Los_Angeles_(disambiguation)|Los Angeles (disambiguation)]] and [[City_of_Los_Angeles_(disambiguation)|City of Los Angeles (disambiguation)]].
sentence_3: "LA" redirects here.
sentence_4: For other uses, see [[LA_(disambiguation)|LA (disambiguation)]].
sentence_5: Los Angeles ([[English|/lɔːs ˈændʒələs/]] (listen); Spanish: Los Ángeles; Spanish for 'The Angels'), officially the City of Los Angeles and often known by its initials L.A., is the [[List_of_cities_and_towns_in_California|largest city]] in [[California|California]].
sentence_6: With an estimated population of nearly four million people, it is the [[List_of_U.S._cities_by_population|second most populous city]] in the [[United_States|United States]] (after [[New_York_City|New York City]]) and the [[List_of_North_American_cities_by_population|third most populous city]] in [[North_America|North America]] (after [[Mexico_City|Mexico City]] and New York City).
sentence_7: Los Angeles is known for its [[Mediterranean_climate|Mediterranean climate]], ethnic diversity, [[Cinema_of_the_United_States|Hollywood entertainment industry]], and its sprawling metropolis.
sentence_8: Los Angeles lies in [[Los_Angeles_Basin|a basin]] in [[Southern_California|Southern California]], adjacent to the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]], with [[San_Gabriel_Mountains|mountains]] as high as 10,000 feet (3,000 m), and [[High_Desert_(California)|deserts]].
sentence_9: The city, which covers about 469 square miles (1,210 km), is the [[County_seat|seat]] of [[Los_Angeles_County|Los Angeles County]], the most populous [[County_(United_States)|county]] in the United States.
sentence_10: The [[Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area|Los Angeles metropolitan area]] (MSA) is home to 13.1 million people, making it the [[List_of_Metropolitan_Statistical_Areas|second-largest metropolitan area]] in the nation after [[New_York_metropolitan_area|New York]].
sentence_11: [[Greater_Los_Angeles|Greater Los Angeles]] includes metro Los Angeles as well as the [[Inland_Empire|Inland Empire]] and Ventura County.
sentence_12: It is the second most populous U.S. [[Combined_statistical_area|combined statistical area]], also after New York, with a 2015 estimate of 18.7 million people.
sentence_13: Home to the [[Chumash_people|Chumash]] and [[Tongva|Tongva]], the area that became Los Angeles was claimed by [[Juan_Rodríguez_Cabrillo|Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo]] for [[Spanish_Empire|Spain]] in 1542.
sentence_14: The city was founded on September 4, 1781, under Spanish governor [[Felipe_de_Neve|Felipe de Neve]], on the village of [[Yaanga|Yaanga]].
sentence_15: It became a part of [[First_Mexican_Empire|Mexico]] in 1821 following the [[Mexican_War_of_Independence|Mexican War of Independence]].
sentence_16: In 1848, at the end of the [[Mexican–American_War|Mexican–American War]], Los Angeles and the rest of California were purchased as part of the [[Treaty_of_Guadalupe_Hidalgo|Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo]], and thus became part of the United States.
sentence_17: Los Angeles was incorporated as a municipality on April 4, 1850, five months before California achieved [[U.S._state|statehood]].
sentence_18: The discovery of oil in the 1890s brought rapid growth to the city.
sentence_19: The city was further expanded with the completion of the [[Los_Angeles_Aqueduct|Los Angeles Aqueduct]] in 1913, which delivers water from [[Eastern_California|Eastern California]].
sentence_20: Los Angeles has a diverse economy and hosts businesses in a broad range of professional and cultural fields.
sentence_21: It also has the [[Port_of_Los_Angeles|busiest container port]] in the Americas.
sentence_22: The Los Angeles metropolitan area also has a [[Gross_metropolitan_product|gross metropolitan product]] of $1.0 trillion (as of 2017), making it the [[List_of_cities_by_GDP|third-largest city by GDP]] in the world, after the [[Greater_Tokyo_Area|Tokyo]] and [[New_York_metropolitan_area|New York City]] metropolitan areas.
sentence_23: Los Angeles hosted the [[1932_Summer_Olympics|1932]] and [[1984_Summer_Olympics|1984 Summer Olympics]] and will host the [[2028_Summer_Olympics|2028 Summer Olympics]].
sentence_24: Main article: [[History_of_Los_Angeles|History of Los Angeles]]
sentence_25: See also: [[Timeline_of_Los_Angeles|Timeline of Los Angeles]] and [[Los_Angeles_in_the_1920s|Los Angeles in the 1920s]]
sentence_26: The Los Angeles coastal area was settled by the [[Tongva_people|Tongva]] (Gabrieleños) and [[Chumash_people|Chumash]] [[Indigenous_peoples_of_California|tribes]].
sentence_27: Los Angeles would eventually be founded on the village of iyáangẚ or [[Yaanga|Yaanga]] (written "Yang-na" by the Spanish), meaning "[[Toxicodendron_diversilobum|poison oak]] place."
sentence_28: Maritime explorer [[Juan_Rodríguez_Cabrillo|Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo]] claimed the area of southern [[California|California]] for the [[Spanish_Empire|Spanish Empire]] in 1542 while on an official military exploring expedition moving north along the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific]] coast from earlier colonizing bases of [[New_Spain|New Spain]] in [[Central_America|Central]] and South America.
sentence_29: Gaspar de Portolà and [[Franciscan|Franciscan]] missionary Juan Crespí, reached the present site of Los Angeles on August 2, 1769.
sentence_30: In 1771, Franciscan friar Junípero Serra directed the building of the [[Mission_San_Gabriel_Arcángel|Mission San Gabriel Arcángel]], the first mission in the area.
sentence_31: On September 4, 1781, a group of forty-four settlers known as "[[Los_Angeles_Pobladores|Los Pobladores]]" founded the pueblo they called [[El_Pueblo_de_Nuestra_Señora_la_Reina_de_los_Ángeles|El Pueblo de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles]], 'The Town of Our Lady the Queen of the Angels'.
sentence_32: The present-day city has the largest [[Archdiocese_of_Los_Angeles|Roman Catholic archdiocese]] in the United States.
sentence_33: Two-thirds of the Mexican or ([[New_Spain|New Spain]]) settlers were [[Mestizo|mestizo]] or [[Mulatto|mulatto]], a mixture of African, indigenous and European ancestry.
sentence_34: The settlement remained a small ranch town for decades, but by 1820, the population had increased to about 650 residents.
sentence_35: Today, the pueblo is commemorated in the historic district of [[El_Pueblo_de_Los_Ángeles_Historical_Monument|Los Angeles Pueblo Plaza]] and [[Olvera_Street|Olvera Street]], the oldest part of Los Angeles.
sentence_36: [[New_Spain|New Spain]] achieved its independence from the Spanish Empire in 1821, and the pueblo continued as a part of [[Mexico|Mexico]].
sentence_37: During Mexican rule, Governor [[Pío_Pico|Pío Pico]] made Los Angeles [[Alta_California|Alta California]]'s regional capital.
sentence_38: Mexican rule ended during the [[Mexican–American_War|Mexican–American War]]: Americans took control from the [[Californios|Californios]] after a series of battles, culminating with the signing of the [[Treaty_of_Cahuenga|Treaty of Cahuenga]] on January 13, 1847.
sentence_39: [[History_of_Los_Angeles#Railroads|Railroads arrived]] with the completion of the transcontinental [[Southern_Pacific_Railroad|Southern Pacific]] line from [[New_Orleans|New Orleans]] to Los Angeles in 1876 and the [[Atchison,_Topeka_and_Santa_Fe_Railway|Santa Fe Railroad]] in 1885.
sentence_40: [[Petroleum|Petroleum]] was discovered in the city and surrounding area in 1892, and by 1923, the discoveries had helped California become the country's largest oil producer, accounting for about one-quarter of the world's petroleum output.
sentence_41: By 1900, the population had grown to more than 102,000, putting pressure on the city's [[Water_supply|water supply]].
sentence_42: The completion of the [[Los_Angeles_Aqueduct|Los Angeles Aqueduct]] in 1913, under the supervision of [[William_Mulholland|William Mulholland]], ensured the continued growth of the city.
sentence_43: Because of clauses in the city's charter that prevented the City of Los Angeles from selling or providing water from the aqueduct to any area outside its borders, many adjacent cities and communities felt compelled to annex themselves into Los Angeles.
sentence_44: Los Angeles created the first municipal [[Zoning|zoning]] ordinance in the United States.
sentence_45: On September 14, 1908, the [[Los_Angeles_City_Council,_1889–1909|Los Angeles City Council]] promulgated residential and industrial land use zones.
sentence_46: The new ordinance established three residential zones of a single type, where industrial uses were prohibited.
sentence_47: The proscriptions included barns, lumber yards, and any industrial land use employing machine-powered equipment.
sentence_48: These laws were enforced against industrial properties after-the-fact.
sentence_49: These prohibitions were in addition to existing activities that were already regulated as nuisances.
sentence_50: These included explosives warehousing, gas works, oil-drilling, slaughterhouses, and [[Tannery|tanneries]].
sentence_51: Los Angeles City Council also designated seven industrial zones within the city.
sentence_52: However, between 1908 and 1915, Los Angeles City Council created various exceptions to the broad proscriptions that applied to these three residential zones, and as a consequence, some industrial uses emerged within them.
sentence_53: There are two differences from the 1908 Residence District Ordinance and later zoning laws in the United States.
sentence_54: First, the 1908 laws did not establish a comprehensive zoning map as the [[Zoning_in_the_United_States#Origins_and_history|1916 New York City Zoning Ordinance]] did.
sentence_55: Second, the residential zones did not distinguish types of housing; it treated apartments, hotels, and detached-single-family housing equally.
sentence_56: In 1910, [[Hollywood|Hollywood]] merged into Los Angeles, with 10 movie companies already operating in the city at the time.
sentence_57: By 1921, more than 80 percent of the world's film industry was concentrated in LA.
sentence_58: The money generated by the industry kept the city insulated from much of the economic loss suffered by the rest of the country during the [[Great_Depression_in_the_United_States|Great Depression]].
sentence_59: By 1930, the population surpassed one million.
sentence_60: In 1932, the city hosted the [[1932_Summer_Olympics|Summer Olympics]].
sentence_61: During [[United_States_home_front_during_World_War_II|World War II]], Los Angeles was a major center of wartime manufacturing, such as shipbuilding and aircraft.
sentence_62: [[California_Shipbuilding_Corporation|Calship]] built hundreds of [[Liberty_Ship|Liberty Ships]] and [[Victory_Ship|Victory Ships]] on Terminal Island, and the Los Angeles area was the headquarters of six of the country's major aircraft manufacturers ([[Douglas_Aircraft_Company|Douglas Aircraft Company]], [[Hughes_Aircraft_Company|Hughes Aircraft]], [[Lockheed_Corporation|Lockheed]], [[North_American_Aviation|North American Aviation]], [[Northrop_Corporation|Northrop Corporation]], and [[Vultee_Aircraft|Vultee]]).
sentence_63: During the war, more aircraft were produced in one year than in all the pre-war years since the Wright brothers flew the first airplane in 1903, combined.
sentence_64: Manufacturing in Los Angeles skyrocketed, and as [[William_S._Knudsen|William S. Knudsen]], of the National Defense Advisory Commission put it, "We won because we smothered the enemy in an avalanche of production, the like of which he had never seen, nor dreamed possible."
sentence_65: In the 1930s–1940s, Los Angeles county was the national leader in agriculture.
sentence_66: Following the end of [[World_War_II|World War II]], Los Angeles grew more rapidly than ever, [[Urban_sprawl|sprawling]] into the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]].
sentence_67: The expansion of the [[Interstate_Highway_System|Interstate Highway System]] during the 1950s and 1960s helped propel suburban growth and signaled the demise of the city's [[Pacific_Electric|electrified rail system]], once the world's largest.
sentence_68: Previous to the 1950s, Los Angeles' name had multiple pronunciations, but the soft "G" pronunciation is universal today.
sentence_69: Some early movies or video shows it pronounced with a hard "G" ([[English|/lɔːs ˈænɡələs/]]).
sentence_70: Sam Yorty was one of the last public figures who still used the hard "G" pronunciation.
sentence_71: Racial tensions led to the [[Watts_riots|Watts riots]] in 1965, resulting in 34 deaths and over 1,000 injuries.
sentence_72: In 1969, California became the birthplace of the [[Internet|Internet]], as the first [[ARPANET|ARPANET]] transmission was sent from the [[University_of_California,_Los_Angeles|University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) to the [[Stanford_Research_Institute|Stanford Research Institute]] in [[Menlo_Park,_California|Menlo Park]].
sentence_73: In 1973, [[Tom_Bradley_(American_politician)|Tom Bradley]] was elected as the city's first [[African_American|African American]] mayor, serving for five terms until retiring in 1993.
sentence_74: Other events in the city during the 1970s included the [[Symbionese_Liberation_Army|Symbionese Liberation Army]]'s [[South_Los_Angeles|South Central]] standoff in 1974 and the [[Hillside_Stranglers|Hillside Stranglers]] [[Murder|murder]] cases in 1977–1978.
sentence_75: In 1984, the city hosted the Summer Olympic Games [[1984_Summer_Olympics|for the second time]].
sentence_76: Despite being boycotted by 14 Communist countries, the 1984 Olympics became more financially successful than any previous, and the second Olympics to turn a profit until then–the other, according to an analysis of contemporary newspaper reports, being the 1932 Summer Olympics, also held in Los Angeles.
sentence_77: Racial tensions erupted on April 29, 1992, with the acquittal by a [[Simi_Valley|Simi Valley]] jury of four [[Los_Angeles_Police_Department|Los Angeles Police Department]] (LAPD) officers captured on videotape beating [[Rodney_King|Rodney King]], culminating in [[Los_Angeles_riots_of_1992|large-scale riots]].
sentence_78: In 1994, the 6.7 [[Northridge_earthquake|Northridge earthquake]] shook the city, causing $12.5 billion in damage and 72 deaths.
sentence_79: The century ended with the [[Rampart_scandal|Rampart scandal]], one of the most extensive documented cases of police misconduct in American history.
sentence_80: In 2002, Mayor James Hahn led the campaign against secession, resulting in voters defeating efforts by the San Fernando Valley and Hollywood to secede from the city.
sentence_81: Los Angeles will host the [[2028_Summer_Olympics|2028 Summer Olympics]] and [[Paralympic_Games|Paralympic Games]], making Los Angeles the third city to host the Olympics three times.
sentence_82: See also: [[Los_Angeles_Basin|Los Angeles Basin]]; [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]]; [[Greater_Los_Angeles_Area|Greater Los Angeles Area]]; and [[Los_Angeles_County,_California|Los Angeles County, California]]
sentence_83: The city of Los Angeles covers a total area of 502.7 square miles (1,302 km), comprising 468.7 square miles (1,214 km) of land and 34.0 square miles (88 km) of water.
sentence_84: The city extends for 44 miles (71 km) north-south and for 29 miles (47 km) east-west.
sentence_85: The perimeter of the city is 342 miles (550 km).
sentence_86: Los Angeles is both flat and hilly.
sentence_87: The highest point in the city proper is [[Mount_Lukens|Mount Lukens]] at 5,074 ft (1,547 m), located at the northeastern end of the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]].
sentence_88: The eastern end of the Santa Monica Mountains stretches from [[Downtown_Los_Angeles|Downtown]] to the [[Pacific_Ocean|Pacific Ocean]] and separates the Los Angeles Basin from the San Fernando Valley.
sentence_89: Other hilly parts of Los Angeles include the [[Mt._Washington,_Los_Angeles|Mt.
sentence_90: Washington]] area north of Downtown, eastern parts such as [[Boyle_Heights|Boyle Heights]], the [[Crenshaw,_Los_Angeles|Crenshaw district]] around the [[Baldwin_Hills,_Los_Angeles|Baldwin Hills]], and the [[San_Pedro,_Los_Angeles|San Pedro]] district.
sentence_91: Surrounding the city are much higher mountains.
sentence_92: Immediately to the north lie the [[San_Gabriel_Mountains|San Gabriel Mountains]], which is a popular recreation area for Angelenos.
sentence_93: Its high point is [[Mount_San_Antonio|Mount San Antonio]], locally known as Mount Baldy, which reaches 10,064 feet (3,068 m).
sentence_94: Further afield, the highest point in the Greater Los Angeles area is [[San_Gorgonio_Mountain|San Gorgonio Mountain]], with a height of 11,503 feet (3,506 m).
sentence_95: The [[Los_Angeles_River|Los Angeles River]], which is largely seasonal, is the primary drainage channel.
sentence_96: It was straightened and lined in 51 miles (82 km) of concrete by the [[United_States_Army_Corps_of_Engineers|Army Corps of Engineers]] to act as a flood control channel.
sentence_97: The river begins in the [[Canoga_Park,_Los_Angeles|Canoga Park]] district of the city, flows east from the San Fernando Valley along the north edge of the Santa Monica Mountains, and turns south through the city center, flowing to its mouth in the Port of [[Long_Beach,_California|Long Beach]] at the Pacific Ocean.
sentence_98: The smaller [[Ballona_Creek|Ballona Creek]] flows into the [[Santa_Monica_Bay|Santa Monica Bay]] at [[Playa_del_Rey,_Los_Angeles|Playa del Rey]].
sentence_99: Los Angeles is rich in native plant species partly because of its diversity of habitats, including beaches, [[Wetland|wetlands]], and mountains.
sentence_100: The most prevalent plant communities are [[Coastal_sage_scrub|coastal sage scrub]], [[Chaparral|chaparral]] shrubland, and riparian woodland.
sentence_101: Native plants include: the [[California_poppy|California poppy]], [[Matilija_poppy|matilija poppy]], [[Heteromeles|toyon]], [[Ceanothus|Ceanothus]], [[Chamise|Chamise]], [[Coast_Live_Oak|Coast Live Oak]], [[Platanus_racemosa|sycamore]], [[Willow|willow]] and Giant Wildrye.
sentence_102: Many of these native species, such as the [[Helianthus_nuttallii|Los Angeles sunflower]], have become so rare as to be considered endangered.
sentence_103: Although it is not native to the area, the official tree of Los Angeles is the Coral Tree ([[Erythrina_caffra|Erythrina caffra]]) and the official flower of Los Angeles is the Bird of Paradise ([[Strelitzia_reginae|Strelitzia reginae]]).
sentence_104: [[Washingtonia_robusta|Mexican Fan Palms]], [[Phoenix_canariensis|Canary Island Palms]], [[Syagrus_romanzoffiana|Queen Palms]], [[Date_Palm|Date Palms]], and [[Washingtonia_filifera|California Fan Palms]] are common in the Los Angeles area, although only the last is native.
sentence_105: Los Angeles is subject to earthquakes because of its location on the [[Ring_of_Fire|Pacific Ring of Fire]].
sentence_106: The geologic instability has produced numerous [[Fault_(geology)|faults]], which cause approximately 10,000 [[Earthquake|earthquakes]] annually in Southern California, though most of them are too small to be felt.
sentence_107: The [[Strike-slip_fault|strike-slip]] [[San_Andreas_Fault|San Andreas Fault]] system, which sits at the boundary between the [[Pacific_Plate|Pacific Plate]] and the [[North_American_Plate|North American Plate]], passes through the Los Angeles metropolitan area.
sentence_108: The segment of the fault passing through Southern California experiences a major earthquake roughly every 110 to 140 years, and seismologists have warned about the next "big one", as the last major earthquake was the [[1857_Fort_Tejon_earthquake|1857 Fort Tejon earthquake]].
sentence_109: The Los Angeles basin and metropolitan area are also at risk from [[Blind_thrust_earthquake|blind thrust earthquakes]].
sentence_110: Major earthquakes that have hit the Los Angeles area include the [[1933_Long_Beach_earthquake|1933 Long Beach]], [[1971_San_Fernando_earthquake|1971 San Fernando]], [[1987_Whittier_Narrows_earthquake|1987 Whittier Narrows]], and the [[1994_Northridge_earthquake|1994 Northridge]] events.
sentence_111: All but a few are of low intensity and are not felt.
sentence_112: The USGS has released the [[California_earthquake_forecast|UCERF California earthquake forecast]], which models earthquake occurrence in California.
sentence_113: Parts of the city are also vulnerable to [[Tsunami|tsunamis]]; harbor areas were damaged by waves from [[1946_Aleutian_Islands_earthquake|Aleutian Islands earthquake]] in 1946, [[1960_Valdivia_earthquake|Valdivia earthquake]] in 1960, [[1964_Alaska_earthquake|Alaska earthquake]] in 1964, [[2010_Chile_earthquake|Chile earthquake]] in 2010 and [[2011_Tōhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami|Japan earthquake]] in 2011.
sentence_114: Main article: [[List_of_districts_and_neighborhoods_of_Los_Angeles|List of districts and neighborhoods of Los Angeles]]
sentence_115: The city is divided into many different districts and neighborhoods, some of which were incorporated cities that merged with Los Angeles.
sentence_116: These neighborhoods were developed piecemeal, and are well-defined enough that the city has signage marking nearly all of them.
sentence_117: The city's street patterns generally follow a [[Grid_plan|grid plan]], with uniform block lengths and occasional roads that cut across blocks.
sentence_118: However, this is complicated by rugged terrain, which has necessitated having different grids for each of the valleys that Los Angeles covers.
sentence_119: Major streets are designed to move large volumes of traffic through many parts of the city, many of which are extremely long; Sepulveda Boulevard is 43 miles (69 km) long, while [[Foothill_Boulevard_(Southern_California)|Foothill Boulevard]] is over 60 miles (97 km) long, reaching as far east as San Bernardino.
sentence_120: Drivers in Los Angeles suffer from one of the worst rush hour periods in the world, according to an annual traffic index by navigation system maker, [[TomTom|TomTom]].
sentence_121: LA drivers spend an additional 92 hours in traffic each year.
sentence_122: During the peak rush hour there is 80% congestion, according to the index.
sentence_123: Los Angeles is often characterized by the presence of [[Low-rise|low-rise]] buildings.
sentence_124: Outside of a few centers such as [[Downtown_Los_Angeles|Downtown]], Warner Center, [[Century_City|Century City]], [[Koreatown,_Los_Angeles|Koreatown]], Miracle Mile, [[Hollywood|Hollywood]], and [[Westwood,_Los_Angeles|Westwood]], skyscrapers and high-rise buildings are not common.
sentence_125: The few skyscrapers built outside of those areas often stand out above the rest of the surrounding landscape.
sentence_126: Most construction is done in separate units, rather than [[Curtain_wall_(architecture)|wall-to-wall]].
sentence_127: That being said, Downtown Los Angeles itself has many buildings over 30 stories, with fourteen over 50 stories, and two over 70 stories, the tallest of which is the [[Wilshire_Grand_Center|Wilshire Grand Center]].
sentence_128: Also, Los Angeles is increasingly becoming a city of apartments rather than single family dwellings, especially in the dense inner city and [[Westside_(Los_Angeles_County)|Westside]] neighborhoods.
sentence_129: See also: [[List_of_sites_of_interest_in_the_Los_Angeles_area|List of sites of interest in the Los Angeles area]] and [[National_Register_of_Historic_Places_listings_in_Los_Angeles,_California|National Register of Historic Places listings in Los Angeles, California]]
sentence_130: Important landmarks in Los Angeles include the [[Hollywood_Sign|Hollywood Sign]], [[Walt_Disney_Concert_Hall|Walt Disney Concert Hall]], Capitol Records Building, the [[Cathedral_of_Our_Lady_of_the_Angels|Cathedral of Our Lady of the Angels]], [[Angels_Flight|Angels Flight]], [[Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre|Grauman's Chinese Theatre]], [[Dolby_Theatre|Dolby Theatre]], [[Griffith_Observatory|Griffith Observatory]], [[Getty_Center|Getty Center]], [[Getty_Villa|Getty Villa]], [[Stahl_House|Stahl House]], the [[Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum|Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum]], [[L.A._Live|L.A.
sentence_131: Live]], the [[Los_Angeles_County_Museum_of_Art|Los Angeles County Museum of Art]], the [[Venice_Canal_Historic_District|Venice Canal Historic District]] and boardwalk, [[Theme_Building|Theme Building]], [[Bradbury_Building|Bradbury Building]], [[U.S._Bank_Tower|U.S.
sentence_132: Bank Tower]], [[Wilshire_Grand_Center|Wilshire Grand Center]], Hollywood Boulevard, [[Los_Angeles_City_Hall|Los Angeles City Hall]], [[Hollywood_Bowl|Hollywood Bowl]], Battleship [[USS_Iowa_(BB-61)|USS Iowa]], [[Watts_Towers|Watts Towers]], [[Staples_Center|Staples Center]], Dodger Stadium, and [[Olvera_Street|Olvera Street]].
sentence_133: Main article: [[Climate_of_Los_Angeles|Climate of Los Angeles]]
sentence_134: Los Angeles has a [[Mediterranean_climate|Mediterranean climate]] ([[Köppen_climate_classification|Köppen]] Csb on the coast and most of downtown, Csa near the metropolitan region to the west), and receives just enough annual precipitation to avoid [[Semi-arid_climate|semi-arid climate]] (BSh),.
sentence_135: Daytime temperatures are generally temperate all year round.
sentence_136: In winter, they average around 68 °F (20 °C) giving it a [[Tropical|tropical]] feel although it is a few degrees too cool to be a true tropical climate on average due to cool night temperatures.
sentence_137: Los Angeles has plenty of sunshine throughout the year, with an average of only 35 days with measurable precipitation annually.
sentence_138: Temperatures in the coastal basin exceed 90 °F (32 °C) on a dozen or so days in the year, from one day a month in April, May, June and November to three days a month in July, August, October and to five days in September.
sentence_139: Temperatures in the San Fernando and San Gabriel Valleys are considerably warmer.
sentence_140: Temperatures are subject to substantial daily swings; in inland areas the difference between the average daily low and the average daily high is over 30 °F (17 °C).
sentence_141: The average annual temperature of the sea is 63 °F (17 °C), from 58 °F (14 °C) in January to 68 °F (20 °C) in August.
sentence_142: Hours of sunshine total more than 3,000 per year, from an average of 7 hours of sunshine per day in December to an average of 12 in July.
sentence_143: The Los Angeles area is also subject to phenomena typical of a microclimate, causing extreme variations in temperature in close physical proximity to each other.
sentence_144: For example, the average July maximum temperature at the [[Santa_Monica_Pier|Santa Monica Pier]] is 70 °F (21 °C) whereas it is 95 °F (35 °C) in Canoga Park, 15 miles (24 km) away.
sentence_145: The city, like much of the southern California coast, is subject to a late spring/early summer weather phenomenon called "[[June_Gloom|June Gloom]]".
sentence_146: This involves overcast or foggy skies in the morning that yield to sun by early afternoon.
sentence_147: Downtown Los Angeles averages 14.93 in (379 mm) of precipitation annually, mainly occurring between November and March, generally in the form of moderate rain showers, but sometimes as heavy rainfall during winter storms.
sentence_148: Rainfall is usually higher in the hills and coastal slopes of the mountains because of [[Orographic|orographic]] uplift.
sentence_149: Summer days are usually rainless.
sentence_150: Rarely, an incursion of moist air from the south or east can bring brief thunderstorms in late summer, especially to the mountains.
sentence_151: The coast gets slightly less rainfall, while the inland and mountain areas get considerably more.
sentence_152: Years of average rainfall are rare.
sentence_153: The usual pattern is year to year variability, with a short string of dry years of 5–10 in (130–250 mm) rainfall, followed by one or two wet years with more than 20 in (510 mm).
sentence_154: Wet years are usually associated with warm water [[El_Niño|El Niño]] conditions in the Pacific, dry years with cooler water [[La_Niña|La Niña]] episodes.
sentence_155: A series of rainy days can bring floods to the lowlands and mudslides to the hills, especially after [[Wildfire|wildfires]] have denuded the slopes.
sentence_156: Both freezing temperatures and snowfall are extremely rare in the city basin and along the coast, with the last occurrence of a 32 °F (0 °C) reading at the downtown station being January 29, 1979; freezing temperatures occur nearly every year in valley locations while the mountains within city limits typically receive snowfall every winter.
sentence_157: The greatest snowfall recorded in downtown Los Angeles was 2.0 inches (5 cm) on January 15, 1932.
sentence_158: While the most recent snowfall occurred in February 2019, the first snowfall since 1962.
sentence_159: At the official downtown station, the highest recorded temperature is 113 °F (45 °C) on September 27, 2010, while the lowest is 28 °F (−2 °C), on January 4, 1949.
sentence_160: Within the City of Los Angeles, the highest temperature ever officially recorded is 121 °F (49 °C), on September 6, 2020, at the weather station at [[Los_Angeles_Pierce_College|Pierce College]] in the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]] neighborhood of [[Woodland_Hills,_Los_Angeles|Woodland Hills]].
sentence_161: During autumn and winter, [[Santa_Ana_winds|Santa Ana winds]] sometimes bring much warmer and drier conditions to Los Angeles, and raise wildfire risk.

sentence_162: Further information: [[Pollution_in_California#Los_Angeles_Air_Pollution|Pollution in California § Los Angeles Air Pollution]]
sentence_163: A Gabrielino settlement in the area was called iyáangẚ (written Yang-na by the Spanish), which has been translated as "poison oak place".
sentence_164: Yang-na has also been translated as "the valley of smoke".
sentence_165: Owing to geography, heavy reliance on automobiles, and the Los Angeles/Long Beach port complex, Los Angeles suffers from [[Air_pollution|air pollution]] in the form of [[Smog|smog]].
sentence_166: The [[Los_Angeles_Basin|Los Angeles Basin]] and the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]] are susceptible to [[Inversion_(meteorology)|atmospheric inversion]], which holds in the exhausts from road vehicles, airplanes, locomotives, shipping, manufacturing, and other sources.
sentence_167: The percentage of small particle pollution (the kind that penetrates into the lungs) coming from vehicles in the city can get as high as 55 percent.
sentence_168: The smog season lasts from approximately May to October.
sentence_169: While other large cities rely on rain to clear smog, Los Angeles gets only 15 inches (380 mm) of rain each year: pollution accumulates over many consecutive days.
sentence_170: Issues of air quality in Los Angeles and other major cities led to the passage of early national environmental legislation, including the [[United_States_Clean_Air_Act|Clean Air Act]].
sentence_171: When the act was passed, California was unable to create a [[State_Implementation_Plan|State Implementation Plan]] that would enable it to meet the new air quality standards, largely because of the level of pollution in Los Angeles generated by older vehicles.
sentence_172: More recently, the state of California has led the nation in working to limit pollution by mandating low-emission vehicles.
sentence_173: Smog is expected to continue to drop in the coming years because of aggressive steps to reduce it, which include [[Electric_car|electric]] and [[Hybrid_electric_vehicle|hybrid]] cars, improvements in mass transit, and other measures.
sentence_174: The number of Stage 1 smog alerts in Los Angeles has declined from over 100 per year in the 1970s to almost zero in the new millennium.
sentence_175: Despite improvement, the 2006 and 2007 annual reports of the American Lung Association ranked the city as the most polluted in the country with short-term particle pollution and year-round particle pollution.
sentence_176: In 2008, the city was ranked the second most polluted and again had the highest year-round particulate pollution.
sentence_177: The city met its goal of providing 20 percent of the city's power from renewable sources in 2010.
sentence_178: The American Lung Association's 2013 survey ranks the metro area as having the nation's worst smog, and fourth in both short-term and year-round pollution amounts.
sentence_179: Los Angeles is also home to the nation's largest urban oil field.
sentence_180: There are more than 700 active oil wells within 1,500 feet of homes, churches, schools and hospitals in the city, a situation about which the [[United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency|EPA]] has voiced serious concerns.
sentence_181: Main articles: Demographics of Los Angeles and [[African-American_neighborhoods_in_Los_Angeles|African-American neighborhoods in Los Angeles]]
sentence_182: The [[2010_United_States_Census|2010 United States Census]] reported Los Angeles had a population of 3,792,621.
sentence_183: The population density was 8,092.3 people per square mile (2,913.0/km).
sentence_184: The age distribution was 874,525 people (23.1%) under 18, 434,478 people (11.5%) from 18 to 24, 1,209,367 people (31.9%) from 25 to 44, 877,555 people (23.1%) from 45 to 64, and 396,696 people (10.5%) who were 65 or older.
sentence_185: The median age was 34.1 years.
sentence_186: For every 100 females, there were 99.2 males.
sentence_187: For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 97.6 males.
sentence_188: There were 1,413,995 housing units—up from 1,298,350 during 2005–2009—at an average density of 2,812.8 households per square mile (1,086.0/km), of which 503,863 (38.2%) were owner-occupied, and 814,305 (61.8%) were occupied by renters.
sentence_189: The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.1%; the rental vacancy rate was 6.1%.
sentence_190: 1,535,444 people (40.5% of the population) lived in owner-occupied housing units and 2,172,576 people (57.3%) lived in rental housing units.
sentence_191: According to the 2010 United States Census, Los Angeles had a median household income of $49,497, with 22.0% of the population living below the federal poverty line.
sentence_192: According to the 2010 Census, the racial makeup of Los Angeles included: 1,888,158 [[White_American|Whites]] (49.8%), 365,118 [[African_American|African Americans]] (9.6%), 28,215 [[Native_Americans_in_the_United_States|Native Americans]] (0.7%), 426,959 [[Asian_American|Asians]] (11.3%), 5,577 [[Pacific_Islander_American|Pacific Islanders]] (0.1%), 902,959 from [[Race_and_ethnicity_in_the_United_States_Census#Race|other races]] (23.8%), and 175,635 (4.6%) from [[Multiracial_American|two or more races]].
sentence_193: [[Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans|Hispanics or Latinos]] of any race were 1,838,822 persons (48.5%).
sentence_194: Los Angeles is home to people from more than 140 countries speaking 224 different identified languages.
sentence_195: [[Ethnic_enclave|Ethnic enclaves]] like [[Chinatown,_Los_Angeles|Chinatown]], Historic Filipinotown, [[Koreatown,_Los_Angeles|Koreatown]], [[Little_Armenia,_Los_Angeles|Little Armenia]], [[Little_Ethiopia,_Los_Angeles|Little Ethiopia]], [[Tehrangeles|Tehrangeles]], [[Little_Tokyo,_Los_Angeles|Little Tokyo]], [[Little_Bangladesh|Little Bangladesh]], and Thai Town provide examples of the polyglot character of Los Angeles.
sentence_196: [[Non-Hispanic_whites|Non-Hispanic whites]] were 28.7% of the population in 2010, compared to 86.3% in 1940.
sentence_197: The majority of the Non-Hispanic white population is living in areas along the Pacific coast as well as in neighborhoods near and on the Santa Monica Mountains from the [[Pacific_Palisades,_Los_Angeles|Pacific Palisades]] to [[Los_Feliz,_Los_Angeles|Los Feliz]].
sentence_198: [[Mexican_American|Mexican]] ancestry make up the largest ethnic group of Hispanics at 31.9% of the city's population, followed by those of [[Salvadoran_American|Salvadoran]] (6.0%) and [[Guatemalan_American|Guatemalan]] (3.6%) heritage.
sentence_199: The Hispanic population has a long established Mexican-American and Central American community and is spread well-nigh throughout the entire city of Los Angeles and its metropolitan area.
sentence_200: It is most heavily concentrated in regions around Downtown as [[East_Los_Angeles_(region)|East Los Angeles]], Northeast Los Angeles and [[Westlake,_Los_Angeles|Westlake]].
sentence_201: Furthermore, a vast majority of residents in neighborhoods in eastern [[South_Los_Angeles|South Los Angeles]] towards [[Downey,_California|Downey]] are of Hispanic origin.
sentence_202: The largest Asian ethnic groups are [[Filipino_American|Filipinos]] (3.2%) and [[Korean_American|Koreans]] (2.9%), which have their own established ethnic enclaves—[[Koreatown,_Los_Angeles|Koreatown]] in the Wilshire Center and Historic Filipinotown.
sentence_203: [[Chinese_American|Chinese]] people, which make up 1.8% of Los Angeles's population, reside mostly outside of Los Angeles city limits and rather in the [[San_Gabriel_Valley|San Gabriel Valley]] of eastern Los Angeles County, but make a sizable presence in the city, notably in [[Chinatown,_Los_Angeles|Chinatown]].
sentence_204: Chinatown and Thaitown are also home to many [[Thai_American|Thais]] and [[Cambodian_American|Cambodians]], which make up 0.3% and 0.1% of Los Angeles's population, respectively.
sentence_205: The [[Japanese_American|Japanese]] comprise 0.9% of LA's population, and have an established [[Little_Tokyo,_Los_Angeles|Little Tokyo]] in the city's downtown, and another significant community of Japanese Americans is in the [[Sawtelle,_Los_Angeles|Sawtelle]] district of West Los Angeles.
sentence_206: [[Vietnamese_American|Vietnamese]] make up 0.5% of Los Angeles's population.
sentence_207: [[Indian_American|Indians]] make up 0.9% of the city's population.
sentence_208: The [[Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area|Los Angeles metropolitan area]] is home to a large population of [[Armenian_American|Armenians]], [[Assyrian_Americans|Assyrians]], and [[Iranian_Americans|Iranians]], many of whom live in enclaves like [[Little_Armenia,_Los_Angeles|Little Armenia]] and [[Tehrangeles|Tehrangeles]].
sentence_209: [[African_Americans|African Americans]] have been the predominant ethnic group in [[South_Los_Angeles|South Los Angeles]], which has emerged as the largest African American community in the western United States since the 1960s.
sentence_210: The neighborhoods of South Los Angeles with highest concentration of African Americans include [[Crenshaw,_Los_Angeles|Crenshaw]], [[Baldwin_Hills,_Los_Angeles|Baldwin Hills]], Leimert Park, [[Hyde_Park,_Los_Angeles|Hyde Park]], [[Gramercy_Park,_Los_Angeles|Gramercy Park]], [[Manchester_Square,_Los_Angeles|Manchester Square]] and [[Watts,_Los_Angeles|Watts]].
sentence_211: Apart from South Los Angeles, neighborhoods in the [[Central_Los_Angeles|Central]] region of Los Angeles, as [[Mid-City,_Los_Angeles|Mid-City]] and [[Mid-Wilshire,_Los_Angeles|Mid-Wilshire]] have a moderate concentration of African Americans as well.
sentence_212: According to a 2014 study by the [[Pew_Research_Center|Pew Research Center]], [[Christianity|Christianity]] is the most prevalently practiced religion in Los Angeles (65%).
sentence_213: The [[Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Los_Angeles|Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Los Angeles]] is the largest archdiocese in the country.
sentence_214: [[Roger_Mahony|Cardinal Roger Mahony]], as the archbishop, oversaw construction of the [[Cathedral_of_Our_Lady_of_the_Angels|Cathedral of Our Lady of the Angels]], which opened in September 2002 in Downtown Los Angeles.
sentence_215: In 2011, the once common, but ultimately lapsed, custom of conducting a procession and mass in honor of Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles, in commemoration of the founding of the City of Los Angeles in 1781, was revived by the [[Queen_of_Angels_Foundation|Queen of Angels Foundation]] and its founder Mark Albert, with the support of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles as well as several civic leaders.
sentence_216: The recently revived custom is a continuation of the original processions and masses that commenced on the first anniversary of the founding of Los Angeles in 1782 and continued for nearly a century thereafter.
sentence_217: With 621,000 [[American_Jews|Jews]] in the metropolitan area, the region has the second-largest population of Jews in the United States.
sentence_218: Many of Los Angeles's Jews now live on the [[Westside_(Los_Angeles_County)|Westside]] and in the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]], though [[Boyle_Heights,_Los_Angeles,_California|Boyle Heights]] once had a large Jewish population prior to World War II due to restrictive housing covenants.
sentence_219: Major Orthodox Jewish neighborhoods include [[Hancock_Park,_Los_Angeles|Hancock Park]], [[Pico-Robertson|Pico-Robertson]], and [[Valley_Village,_Los_Angeles|Valley Village]], while Jewish Israelis are well represented in the [[Encino,_Los_Angeles|Encino]] and [[Tarzana,_Los_Angeles|Tarzana]] neighborhoods, and [[Persian_Jews|Persian Jews]] in [[Beverly_Hills,_California|Beverly Hills]].
sentence_220: Many varieties of Judaism are represented in the greater Los Angeles area, including [[Reform_Judaism|Reform]], [[Conservative_Judaism|Conservative]], [[Orthodox_Judaism|Orthodox]], and [[Reconstructionist_Judaism|Reconstructionist]].
sentence_221: The [[Breed_Street_Shul|Breed Street Shul]] in [[East_Los_Angeles,_California|East Los Angeles]], built in 1923, was the largest synagogue west of Chicago in its early decades; it is no longer in daily use as a synagogue and is being converted to a museum and community center.
sentence_222: The [[Kabbalah_Centre|Kabbalah Centre]] also has a presence in the city.
sentence_223: The [[International_Church_of_the_Foursquare_Gospel|International Church of the Foursquare Gospel]] was founded in Los Angeles by [[Aimee_Semple_McPherson|Aimee Semple McPherson]] in 1923 and remains headquartered there to this day.
sentence_224: For many years, the church convened at [[Angelus_Temple|Angelus Temple]], which, when built, was one of the largest churches in the country.
sentence_225: Los Angeles has had a rich and influential Protestant tradition.
sentence_226: The first Protestant service in Los Angeles was a Methodist meeting held in a private home in 1850 and the oldest Protestant church still operating, [[First_Congregational_Church_of_Los_Angeles|First Congregational Church]], was founded in 1867.
sentence_227: In the early 1900s the [[Bible_Institute_Of_Los_Angeles|Bible Institute Of Los Angeles]] published the founding documents of the [[Christian_Fundamentalist|Christian Fundamentalist]] movement and the [[Azusa_Street_Revival|Azusa Street Revival]] launched [[Pentecostalism|Pentecostalism]].
sentence_228: The [[Metropolitan_Community_Church|Metropolitan Community Church]] also had its origins in the Los Angeles area.
sentence_229: Important churches in the city include [[First_Presbyterian_Church_of_Hollywood|First Presbyterian Church of Hollywood]], Bel Air Presbyterian Church, [[First_African_Methodist_Episcopal_Church_of_Los_Angeles|First African Methodist Episcopal Church of Los Angeles]], [[West_Angeles_Church_of_God_in_Christ|West Angeles Church of God in Christ]], [[Second_Baptist_Church_(Los_Angeles,_California)|Second Baptist Church]], [[Crenshaw_Christian_Center|Crenshaw Christian Center]], [[McCarty_Memorial_Christian_Church|McCarty Memorial Christian Church]], and First Congregational Church.
sentence_230: The [[Los_Angeles_California_Temple|Los Angeles California Temple]], the second-largest [[Temple_(Latter_Day_Saints)|temple]] operated by [[The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints|The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]], is on [[California_State_Route_2|Santa Monica Boulevard]] in the [[Westwood,_Los_Angeles|Westwood neighborhood]] of Los Angeles.
sentence_231: Dedicated in 1956, it was the first [[Temple_(LDS_Church)|temple]] of [[The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints|The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] built in California and it was the largest in the world when completed.
sentence_232: The Hollywood region of Los Angeles also has several significant headquarters, churches, and the Celebrity Center of [[Scientology|Scientology]].
sentence_233: Because of Los Angeles's large multi-ethnic population, a wide variety of faiths are practiced, including [[Buddhism|Buddhism]], [[Hinduism|Hinduism]], [[Islam|Islam]], [[Zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]], [[Sikhism|Sikhism]], [[Bahá'í_Faith|Bahá'í]], various [[Eastern_Orthodox_Church|Eastern Orthodox churches]], [[Sufism|Sufism]], [[Shinto|Shintoism]], [[Taoism|Taoism]], [[Confucianism|Confucianism]], [[Chinese_folk_religion|Chinese folk religion]] and countless others.
sentence_234: Immigrants from Asia for example, have formed a number of significant [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] congregations making the city home to the greatest variety of Buddhists in the world.
sentence_235: The first Buddhist joss house was founded in the city in 1875.
sentence_236: [[Atheism|Atheism]] and other [[Secular|secular]] beliefs are also common, as the city is the largest in the Western U.S. [[Unchurched_Belt|Unchurched Belt]].
sentence_237: See also: Los Angeles Chamber of Commerce and [[Los_Angeles_County,_California#Economy|Los Angeles County, California § Economy]]
sentence_238: The economy of Los Angeles is driven by international trade, entertainment (television, motion pictures, video games, music recording, and production), aerospace, technology, petroleum, fashion, apparel, and tourism.
sentence_239: Other significant industries include finance, telecommunications, law, healthcare, and transportation.
sentence_240: In the 2017 [[Global_Financial_Centres_Index|Global Financial Centres Index]], Los Angeles was ranked as having the 19th most competitive financial center in the world, and sixth most competitive in United States (after [[Economy_of_New_York_City#Finance|New York City]], [[San_Francisco#Economy|San Francisco]], [[Economy_of_Chicago#Finance|Chicago]], [[Boston#Economy|Boston]], and [[Washington,_D.C.#Economy|Washington, D.C.]]).
sentence_241: One of the five [[Major_film_studio|major film studios]], [[Paramount_Pictures|Paramount Pictures]], is within the city limits, its location being part of the so-called "[[Studio_zone|Thirty-Mile Zone]]" of entertainment headquarters in Southern California.
sentence_242: Los Angeles is the largest manufacturing center in the United States.
sentence_243: The contiguous [[Port_of_Los_Angeles|ports of Los Angeles]] and [[Port_of_Long_Beach|Long Beach]] together comprise the busiest port in the United States by some measures and the fifth-busiest port in the world, vital to trade within the [[Pacific_Rim|Pacific Rim]].
sentence_244: The [[Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area|Los Angeles metropolitan area]] has a [[Gross_metropolitan_product|gross metropolitan product]] of $1.0 trillion (as of 2017), making it the third-largest economic metropolitan area in the world, after [[Greater_Tokyo_Area|Tokyo]] and [[New_York_metropolitan_area|New York]].
sentence_245: Los Angeles has been classified an "[[Global_city|alpha world city]]" according to a 2012 study by a group at [[Loughborough_University|Loughborough University]].
sentence_246: The Department of Cannabis Regulation enforces cannabis legislation after the legalization of the sale and distribution of [[Cannabis_(drug)|cannabis]] in 2016.
sentence_247: As of October 2019, more than 300 existing cannabis businesses (both retailers and their suppliers) have been granted approval to operate in what is considered the nation's largest market.
sentence_248: As of 2018, Los Angeles is home to three Fortune 500 companies: [[AECOM|AECOM]], [[CBRE_Group|CBRE Group]], and [[Reliance_Steel_&_Aluminum_Co.|Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co]].

sentence_249: Main article: Culture of Los Angeles
sentence_250: Los Angeles is often billed as the "Creative Capital of the World", because one in every six of its residents works in a creative industry and there are more artists, writers, filmmakers, actors, dancers and musicians living and working in Los Angeles than any other city at any other time in history.
sentence_251: The city's [[Hollywood,_Los_Angeles|Hollywood neighborhood]] has become recognized as the center of the [[Film_industry|motion picture industry]] and the Los Angeles area is also associated as being the center of the [[Television_industry|television industry]].
sentence_252: The city is home to the major film studios as well as major record labels.
sentence_253: Los Angeles plays host to the annual [[Academy_Awards|Academy Awards]], the [[Primetime_Emmy_Awards|Primetime Emmy Awards]], the [[Grammy_Awards|Grammy Awards]] as well as many other entertainment industry awards shows.
sentence_254: Los Angeles is the site of the [[USC_School_of_Cinematic_Arts|USC School of Cinematic Arts]], the oldest [[Film_school|film school]] in the United States.
sentence_255: The performing arts play a major role in Los Angeles's cultural identity.
sentence_256: According to the USC Stevens Institute for Innovation, "there are more than 1,100 annual theatrical productions and 21 openings every week."
sentence_257: The [[Los_Angeles_Music_Center|Los Angeles Music Center]] is "one of the three largest performing arts centers in the nation", with more than 1.3 million visitors per year.
sentence_258: The [[Walt_Disney_Concert_Hall|Walt Disney Concert Hall]], centerpiece of the Music Center, is home to the prestigious [[Los_Angeles_Philharmonic|Los Angeles Philharmonic]].
sentence_259: Notable organizations such as [[Center_Theatre_Group|Center Theatre Group]], the Los Angeles Master Chorale, and the Los Angeles Opera are also resident companies of the Music Center.
sentence_260: Talent is locally cultivated at premier institutions such as the Colburn School and the [[USC_Thornton_School_of_Music|USC Thornton School of Music]].
sentence_261: See also: [[List_of_museums_in_California#Los_Angeles|Los Angeles City Museums]]
sentence_262: There are 841 museums and art galleries in [[Los_Angeles_County,_California|Los Angeles County]], more museums per capita than any other city in the U.S.
sentence_263: Some of the notable museums are the [[Los_Angeles_County_Museum_of_Art|Los Angeles County Museum of Art]] (the largest art museum in the Western United States), the [[Getty_Center|Getty Center]] (part of the [[J._Paul_Getty_Trust|J.
sentence_264: Paul Getty Trust]], the world's wealthiest art institution), the [[Petersen_Automotive_Museum|Petersen Automotive Museum]], the [[Huntington_Library|Huntington Library]], the [[Natural_History_Museum_of_Los_Angeles_County|Natural History Museum]], the [[Battleship_Iowa|Battleship Iowa]], and the [[Museum_of_Contemporary_Art,_Los_Angeles|Museum of Contemporary Art]].
sentence_265: A significant number of art galleries are on [[Gallery_Row|Gallery Row]], and tens of thousands attend the monthly Downtown Art Walk there.
sentence_266: See also: [[Sports_in_Los_Angeles|Sports in Los Angeles]] and [[History_of_the_National_Football_League_in_Los_Angeles|History of the National Football League in Los Angeles]]
sentence_267: The city of Los Angeles and its metropolitan area are the home of eleven top level professional sports teams, several of which play in neighboring communities but use Los Angeles in their name.
sentence_268: These teams include the [[Los_Angeles_Dodgers|Los Angeles Dodgers]] and [[Los_Angeles_Angels|Los Angeles Angels]] of [[Major_League_Baseball|Major League Baseball]] (MLB), the [[Los_Angeles_Rams|Los Angeles Rams]] and [[Los_Angeles_Chargers|Los Angeles Chargers]] of the [[National_Football_League|National Football League]] (NFL), the [[Los_Angeles_Lakers|Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Los_Angeles_Clippers|Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National_Basketball_Association|National Basketball Association]] (NBA), the [[Los_Angeles_Kings|Los Angeles Kings]] and [[Anaheim_Ducks|Anaheim Ducks]] of the [[National_Hockey_League|National Hockey League]] (NHL), the [[Los_Angeles_Galaxy|Los Angeles Galaxy]] and [[Los_Angeles_Football_Club|Los Angeles Football Club]] of [[Major_League_Soccer|Major League Soccer]] (MLS), and the [[Los_Angeles_Sparks|Los Angeles Sparks]] of the [[Women's_National_Basketball_Association|Women's National Basketball Association]] (WNBA).
sentence_269: Other notable sports teams include the [[UCLA_Bruins|UCLA Bruins]] and the [[USC_Trojans|USC Trojans]] in the [[National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association|National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA), both of which are Division I teams in the [[Pac-12_Conference|Pac-12 Conference]].
sentence_270: Los Angeles is the second-largest city in the United States but hosted no NFL team between 1995 and 2015.
sentence_271: At one time, the Los Angeles area hosted two NFL teams: the [[Los_Angeles_Rams|Rams]] and the [[Las_Vegas_Raiders|Raiders]].
sentence_272: Both left the city in 1995, with the Rams moving to [[St._Louis|St.
sentence_273: Louis]], and the Raiders moving back to their original home of [[Oakland,_California|Oakland]].
sentence_274: After 21 seasons in St. Louis, on January 12, 2016, the NFL announced the Rams would be moving back to Los Angeles for the [[2016_NFL_season|2016 NFL season]] with its home games played at the [[Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum|Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum]] for four seasons.
sentence_275: Prior to 1995, the Rams played their home games in the Coliseum from 1946 to 1979 which made them the first professional sports team to play in Los Angeles, and then moved to [[Anaheim_Stadium|Anaheim Stadium]] from 1980 until 1994.
sentence_276: The [[History_of_the_San_Diego_Chargers|San Diego Chargers]] announced on January 12, 2017 that they would also relocate back to Los Angeles (the first since its inaugural season in 1960) and become the [[Los_Angeles_Chargers|Los Angeles Chargers]] beginning in the [[2017_NFL_season|2017 NFL season]] and played at [[Dignity_Health_Sports_Park|Dignity Health Sports Park]] in [[Carson,_California|Carson, California]] for three seasons.
sentence_277: The Rams and the Chargers would soon moved to the newly-built [[SoFi_Stadium|SoFi Stadium]], located in nearby [[Inglewood,_California|Inglewood]] during the 2020 season.
sentence_278: Los Angeles boasts a number of sports venues, including Dodger Stadium, the [[Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum|Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum]], [[Banc_of_California_Stadium|Banc of California Stadium]] and the [[Staples_Center|Staples Center]].
sentence_279: [[The_Forum_(Inglewood,_California)|The Forum]], [[SoFi_Stadium|SoFi Stadium]], [[Dignity_Health_Sports_Park|Dignity Health Sports Park]], the [[Rose_Bowl_(stadium)|Rose Bowl]], [[Angel_Stadium|Angel Stadium]] and [[Honda_Center|Honda Center]] are also in adjacent cities and cities in Los Angeles's metropolitan area.
sentence_280: Los Angeles has twice hosted the [[Summer_Olympic_Games|Summer Olympic Games]]: in [[1932_Summer_Olympics|1932]] and in [[1984_Summer_Olympics|1984]], and will host the games for a third time in [[2028_Summer_Olympics|2028]].
sentence_281: Los Angeles will be the third city after London ([[1908_Summer_Olympics|1908]], [[1948_Summer_Olympics|1948]] and [[2012_Summer_Olympics|2012]]) and Paris ([[1900_Summer_Olympics|1900]], [[1924_Summer_Olympics|1924]] and [[2024_Summer_Olympics|2024]]) to host the Olympic Games three times.
sentence_282: When the tenth Olympic Games were hosted in 1932, the former 10th Street was renamed Olympic Blvd.
sentence_283: Los Angeles also hosted the [[Deaflympics|Deaflympics]] in 1985 and [[Special_Olympics_World_Games|Special Olympics World Summer Games]] in [[2015_Special_Olympics_World_Summer_Games|2015]].
sentence_284: 7 [[NFL|NFL]] [[Super_Bowl|Super Bowls]] were also held in the city and its surrounding areas- 2 at the Memorial Coliseum ([[Super_Bowl_I|the first Super Bowl, I]] and [[Super_Bowl_VII|VII]]) and 5 at the Rose Bowl in suburban [[Pasadena,_California|Pasadena]] ([[Super_Bowl_XI|XI]], [[Super_Bowl_XIV|XIV]], [[Super_Bowl_XVII|XVII]], [[Super_Bowl_XXI|XXI]], and [[Super_Bowl_XXVII|XXVII]]), 10 miles north of downtown Los Angeles.
sentence_285: [[Super_Bowl_LVI|Super Bowl LVI]] will be held at [[SoFi_Stadium|SoFi Stadium]] in [[Inglewood,_California|Inglewood]] in 2022.
sentence_286: The Rose Bowl is also host to an annual and highly prestigious [[NCAA|NCAA]] [[College_football|college football]] game called the [[Rose_Bowl_game|Rose Bowl]], which happens every New Year's Day.
sentence_287: Los Angeles also hosted 8 [[FIFA_World_Cup|FIFA World Cup]] soccer games at the [[Rose_Bowl_(stadium)|Rose Bowl]] in [[1994_FIFA_World_Cup|1994]], including the [[1994_FIFA_World_Cup_Final|final]], where [[Brazil_national_football_team|Brazil]] won.
sentence_288: The Rose Bowl also hosted 4 matches in the [[1999_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup|1999 FIFA Women's World Cup]], including the [[1999_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup_Final|final]], where the [[United_States_women's_national_soccer_team|United States]] won against [[China_women's_national_football_team|China]] on penalty kicks.
sentence_289: This was the game where [[Brandi_Chastain|Brandi Chastain]] took her shirt off after she scored the tournament-winning penalty kick, creating an iconic image.
sentence_290: Los Angeles is one of six North American cities to have won championships in all five of its major leagues (MLB, NFL, NHL, NBA and MLS), having completed the feat with the Kings' [[2012_Stanley_Cup_Finals|2012 Stanley Cup title]].
sentence_291: Main article: [[Government_of_Los_Angeles|Government of Los Angeles]]
sentence_292: See also: [[Government_of_Los_Angeles_County|Government of Los Angeles County]]
sentence_293: Los Angeles is a [[Charter_city|charter city]] as opposed to a general law city.
sentence_294: The current charter was adopted on June 8, 1999, and has been amended many times.
sentence_295: The elected government consists of the [[Los_Angeles_City_Council|Los Angeles City Council]] and the [[Mayor_of_Los_Angeles|mayor of Los Angeles]], which operate under a [[Mayor–council_government|mayor–council government]], as well as the [[Los_Angeles_City_Attorney|city attorney]] (not to be confused with the [[Los_Angeles_County_District_Attorney|district attorney]], a county office) and [[Los_Angeles_City_Controller|controller]].
sentence_296: The mayor is [[Eric_Garcetti|Eric Garcetti]].
sentence_297: There are [[Los_Angeles_City_Council|15 city council districts]].
sentence_298: The city has many departments and appointed officers, including the [[Los_Angeles_Police_Department|Los Angeles Police Department]] (LAPD), the [[Los_Angeles_Board_of_Police_Commissioners|Los Angeles Board of Police Commissioners]], the [[Los_Angeles_Fire_Department|Los Angeles Fire Department]] (LAFD), the [[Housing_Authority_of_the_City_of_Los_Angeles|Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles]] (HACLA), the [[Los_Angeles_Department_of_Transportation|Los Angeles Department of Transportation]] (LADOT), and the Los Angeles Public Library (LAPL).
sentence_299: The charter of the City of Los Angeles ratified by voters in 1999 created a system of advisory neighborhood councils that would represent the diversity of stakeholders, defined as those who live, work or own property in the neighborhood.
sentence_300: The neighborhood councils are relatively autonomous and spontaneous in that they identify their own boundaries, establish their own bylaws, and elect their own officers.
sentence_301: There are about 90 neighborhood councils.
sentence_302: Residents of Los Angeles elect [[Los_Angeles_County_Board_of_Supervisors|supervisors]] for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th supervisorial districts.
sentence_303: In the [[California_State_Assembly|California State Assembly]], Los Angeles is split between fourteen districts.
sentence_304: In the [[California_State_Senate|California State Senate]], the city is split between eight districts.
sentence_305: In the [[United_States_House_of_Representatives|United States House of Representatives]], it is split among ten congressional districts.
sentence_306: See also: Crime in Los Angeles and List of criminal gangs in Los Angeles
sentence_307: In 1992, the city of Los Angeles recorded 1,092 murders.
sentence_308: Los Angeles experienced a significant decline in crime in the 1990s and late 2000s and reached a 50-year low in 2009 with 314 homicides.
sentence_309: This is a rate of 7.85 per 100,000 population—a major decrease from 1980 when a homicide rate of 34.2 per 100,000 was reported.
sentence_310: This included 15 officer-involved shootings.
sentence_311: One shooting led to the death of a [[LAPD_Metropolitan_Division#S.W.A.T._("D"_Platoon)|SWAT]] team member, Randal Simmons, the first in LAPD's history.
sentence_312: Los Angeles in the year of 2013 totaled 251 murders, a decrease of 16 percent from the previous year.
sentence_313: Police speculate the drop resulted from a number of factors, including young people spending more time online.
sentence_314: In 2015, it was revealed that the LAPD had been under-reporting crime for eight years, making the crime rate in the city appear much lower than it really is.
sentence_315: The [[Los_Angeles_crime_family|Dragna crime family]] and the [[Cohen_crime_family|Cohen crime family]] dominated organized crime in the city during the [[Prohibition_in_the_United_States|Prohibition era]] and reached its peak during the 1940s and 1950s with the [[Battle_of_Sunset_Strip|battle of Sunset Strip]] as part of the [[American_Mafia|American Mafia]], but has gradually declined since then with the rise of various black and [[Hispanic|Hispanic]] gangs in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
sentence_316: According to the [[Los_Angeles_Police_Department|Los Angeles Police Department]], the city is home to 45,000 gang members, organized into 450 gangs.
sentence_317: Among them are the [[Crips|Crips]] and [[Bloods|Bloods]], which are both African American street gangs that originated in the [[South_Los_Angeles|South Los Angeles]] region.
sentence_318: Latino street gangs such as the [[Sureños|Sureños]], a Mexican American street gang, and [[Mara_Salvatrucha|Mara Salvatrucha]], which has mainly members of [[Salvadoran_American|Salvadoran]] descent, all originated in Los Angeles.
sentence_319: This has led to the city being referred to as the "Gang Capital of America".
sentence_320: There are three public universities within the city limits: [[California_State_University,_Los_Angeles|California State University, Los Angeles]] (CSULA), [[California_State_University,_Northridge|California State University, Northridge]] (CSUN) and [[University_of_California,_Los_Angeles|University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA).
sentence_321: Private colleges in the city include:
sentence_322: The community college system consists of nine campuses governed by the trustees of the Los Angeles Community College District:
sentence_323: There are numerous additional colleges and universities outside the city limits in the Greater Los Angeles area, including the [[Claremont_Colleges|Claremont Colleges]] consortium, which includes the most selective liberal arts colleges in the U.S., and the [[California_Institute_of_Technology|California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech), one of the top STEM-focused research institutions in the world.
sentence_324: See also: [[Los_Angeles_County,_California#Colleges_and_universities|Los Angeles County, California § Colleges and universities]]; and [[List_of_high_schools_in_Los_Angeles_County,_California|List of high schools in Los Angeles County, California]]
sentence_325: [[Los_Angeles_Unified_School_District|Los Angeles Unified School District]] serves almost all of the city of Los Angeles, as well as several surrounding communities, with a student population around 800,000.
sentence_326: After [[California_Proposition_13_(1978)|Proposition 13]] was approved in 1978, urban school districts had considerable trouble with funding.
sentence_327: LAUSD has become known for its underfunded, overcrowded and poorly maintained campuses, although its 162 [[Magnet_school|Magnet schools]] help compete with local private schools.
sentence_328: Several small sections of Los Angeles are in the [[Las_Virgenes_Unified_School_District|Las Virgenes Unified School District]].
sentence_329: The Los Angeles County Office of Education operates the [[Los_Angeles_County_High_School_for_the_Arts|Los Angeles County High School for the Arts]].
sentence_330: The Los Angeles Public Library system operates 72 public libraries in the city.
sentence_331: Enclaves of unincorporated areas are served by branches of the [[County_of_Los_Angeles_Public_Library|County of Los Angeles Public Library]], many of which are within walking distance to residents.
sentence_332: Main article: Media in Los Angeles
sentence_333: See also: [[List_of_television_shows_set_in_Los_Angeles|List of television shows set in Los Angeles]] and [[List_of_films_set_in_Los_Angeles|List of films set in Los Angeles]]
sentence_334: The Los Angeles metro area is the second-largest broadcast [[Designated_market_area|designated market area]] in the U.S. (after [[Media_in_New_York_City|New York]]) with 5,431,140 homes (4.956% of the U.S.), which is served by a wide variety of local [[Media_in_Los_Angeles#AM|AM]] and [[Media_in_Los_Angeles#FM|FM]] radio and [[Media_in_Los_Angeles#Television_stations|television]] stations.
sentence_335: Los Angeles and New York City are the only two media markets to have seven [[VHF|VHF]] allocations assigned to them.
sentence_336: As part of the region's aforementioned creative industry, the Big Four major broadcast television networks, ABC, [[CBS|CBS]], [[Fox_Broadcasting_Company|FOX]], and [[NBC|NBC]], all have production facilities and offices throughout various areas of Los Angeles.
sentence_337: All four major broadcast television networks, plus major Spanish-language networks [[Telemundo|Telemundo]] and [[Univision|Univision]], also own and operate stations that both serve the Los Angeles market and serve as each network's West Coast flagship station: ABC's KABC-TV (Channel 7), CBS's KCBS-TV (Channel 2), Fox's [[KTTV|KTTV]]-TV (Channel 11), NBC's [[KNBC|KNBC]]-TV (Channel 4), MyNetworkTV's [[KCOP|KCOP]]-TV (Channel 13), Telemundo's KVEA-TV (Channel 52), and Univision's [[KMEX-DT|KMEX-TV]] (Channel 34).
sentence_338: The region also has three PBS stations, as well as [[KCET|KCET]] (Channel 28), the nation's largest independent public television station.
sentence_339: KTBN (Channel 40) is the flagship station of the religious [[Trinity_Broadcasting_Network|Trinity Broadcasting Network]], based out of [[Santa_Ana,_California|Santa Ana]].
sentence_340: A variety of independent television stations, such as KCAL-TV (Channel 9) and [[KTLA|KTLA]]-TV (Channel 5), also operate in the area.
sentence_341: The major daily English-language newspaper in the area is the [[Los_Angeles_Times|Los Angeles Times]].
sentence_342: [[La_Opinión|La Opinión]] is the city's major daily Spanish-language paper.
sentence_343: [[The_Korea_Times_(Los_Angeles)|The Korea Times]] is the city's major daily [[Korean_language|Korean language]] paper while [[The_World_Journal|The World Journal]] is the city and county's major Chinese newspaper.
sentence_344: The [[Los_Angeles_Sentinel|Los Angeles Sentinel]] is the city's major [[African-American|African-American]] weekly paper, boasting the largest African-American readership in the [[Western_United_States|Western United States]].
sentence_345: [[Investor's_Business_Daily|Investor's Business Daily]] is distributed from its LA corporate offices, which are headquartered in Playa del Rey.
sentence_346: There are also a number of smaller regional newspapers, alternative weeklies and magazines, including the [[Freedom_Communications|Los Angeles Register]], Los Angeles Community News, (which focuses on coverage of the greater Los Angeles area), [[Los_Angeles_Daily_News|Los Angeles Daily News]] (which focuses coverage on the [[San_Fernando_Valley|San Fernando Valley]]), [[LA_Weekly|LA Weekly]], [[L.A._Record|L.A.
sentence_347: Record]] (which focuses coverage on the music scene in the [[Greater_Los_Angeles_Area|Greater Los Angeles Area]]), Los Angeles Magazine, the [[Los_Angeles_Business_Journal|Los Angeles Business Journal]], the Los Angeles Daily Journal (legal industry paper), [[The_Hollywood_Reporter|The Hollywood Reporter]], [[Variety_(magazine)|Variety]] (both entertainment industry papers), and [[Los_Angeles_Downtown_News|Los Angeles Downtown News]].
sentence_348: In addition to the major papers, numerous local periodicals serve immigrant communities in their native languages, including Armenian, English, Korean, Persian, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Hebrew, and Arabic.
sentence_349: Many cities adjacent to Los Angeles also have their own daily newspapers whose coverage and availability overlaps into certain Los Angeles neighborhoods.
sentence_350: Examples include The Daily Breeze (serving the [[South_Bay,_Los_Angeles|South Bay]]), and The [[Long_Beach_Press-Telegram|Long Beach Press-Telegram]].
sentence_351: Los Angeles arts, culture and nightlife news is also covered by a number of local and national online guides like Time Out Los Angeles, [[Thrillist|Thrillist]], Kristin's List, DailyCandy, Diversity News Magazine, LAist, and Flavorpill.
sentence_352: Main article: [[Transportation_in_Los_Angeles|Transportation in Los Angeles]]
sentence_353: Main article: Southern California freeways
sentence_354: The city and the rest of the [[Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area|Los Angeles metropolitan area]] are served by an extensive network of freeways and highways.
sentence_355: The Texas Transportation Institute, which publishes an annual Urban Mobility Report, ranked Los Angeles road traffic as the most congested in the United States in 2005 as measured by annual delay per traveler.
sentence_356: The average traveler in Los Angeles experienced 72 hours of traffic delay per year according to the study.
sentence_357: Los Angeles was followed by [[San_Francisco|San Francisco]]/[[Oakland|Oakland]], [[Washington,_D.C.|Washington, D.C.]] and [[Atlanta|Atlanta]], (each with 60 hours of delay).
sentence_358: Despite the congestion in the city, the mean travel time for commuters in Los Angeles is shorter than other major cities, including [[New_York_City|New York City]], [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia]] and [[Chicago|Chicago]].
sentence_359: Los Angeles's mean travel time for work commutes in 2006 was 29.2 minutes, similar to those of San Francisco and Washington, D.C.
