sentence_1: Kazakhstan, officially the Republic of Kazakhstan, is a transcontinental country mainly located in [[Central_Asia|Central Asia]] with a smaller portion west of the [[Ural_(river)|Ural River]] in [[Eastern_Europe|Eastern Europe]].
sentence_2: It covers a land area of 2,724,900 square kilometres (1,052,100 sq mi), and shares land borders with [[Russia|Russia]] in the north, [[China|China]] in the east, and [[Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyzstan]], [[Uzbekistan|Uzbekistan]], and [[Turkmenistan|Turkmenistan]] in the south while also adjoining a large part of the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] in the southwest.
sentence_3: Kazakhstan does not border [[Mongolia|Mongolia]], although they are only 37 kilometers apart.
sentence_4: Kazakhstan is the world's largest [[Landlocked_country|landlocked country]], and the [[List_of_countries_and_outlying_territories_by_land_area|eighth-largest country]] in the world.
sentence_5: It has a population of 18.3 million residents, and has [[List_of_countries_by_population_density|one of the lowest population densities]] in the world, at fewer than 6 people per square kilometre (15 people per sq mi).
sentence_6: Since 1997, the capital is [[Nur-Sultan|Nur-Sultan]], formerly known as Astana.
sentence_7: It was moved from [[Almaty|Almaty]], the country's largest city.
sentence_8: The territory of Kazakhstan has historically been inhabited by nomadic groups and empires.
sentence_9: In antiquity, the nomadic [[Scythians|Scythians]] inhabited the land and the Persian [[Achaemenid_Empire|Achaemenid Empire]] expanded towards the southern territory of the modern country.
sentence_10: [[Turkic_people|Turkic]] [[Nomads|nomads]], who trace their ancestry to many [[List_of_Turkic_dynasties_and_countries|Turkic states]] such as the [[First_Turkic_Khaganate|First]] and [[Second_Turkic_Khaganate|Second Turkic Khaganates]], have inhabited the country throughout its history.
sentence_11: In the 13th century, the territory was subjugated by the [[Mongol_Empire|Mongol Empire]] under [[Genghis_Khan|Genghis Khan]].
sentence_12: By the 16th century, the [[Kazakhs|Kazakh]] emerged as a distinct group, divided into three jüz.
sentence_13: The [[Russians|Russians]] began advancing into the [[Kazakh_steppe|Kazakh steppe]] in the 18th century, and by the mid-19th century, they nominally ruled all of Kazakhstan as part of the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]].
sentence_14: Following the 1917 [[Russian_Revolution|Russian Revolution]], and subsequent [[Russian_Civil_War|civil war]], the territory of Kazakhstan was reorganised several times.
sentence_15: In 1936, it was made the [[Kazakh_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic]], part of the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]].
sentence_16: Kazakhstan was the last of the [[Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union|Soviet republics]] to declare independence during the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.
sentence_17: The first [[President_of_Kazakhstan|president of Kazakhstan]] was characterised as an authoritarian, and [[Nursultan_Nazarbayev#Presidency|his government]] was accused of numerous human rights violations, including suppression of dissent and censorship of the media.
sentence_18: [[Human_Rights_Watch|Human Rights Watch]] says that "Kazakhstan heavily restricts freedom of assembly, speech, and religion."
sentence_19: Other human rights organisations regularly describe Kazakhstan's human rights situation as poor.
sentence_20: Kazakhstan is the most dominant nation of Central Asia economically, generating 60% of the region's GDP, primarily through its oil and gas industry.
sentence_21: It also has vast mineral resources, and is officially a democratic, secular, unitary, constitutional republic with a diverse cultural heritage.
sentence_22: Kazakhstan is a member of the United Nations (UN), [[World_Trade_Organization|WTO]], [[Commonwealth_of_Independent_States|CIS]], the [[Shanghai_Cooperation_Organization|Shanghai Cooperation Organization]] (SCO), the [[Eurasian_Economic_Union|Eurasian Economic Union]], [[Collective_Security_Treaty_Organisation|CSTO]], [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|OSCE]], [[Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation|OIC]], [[Turkic_Council|CCTS]], and [[International_Organization_of_Turkic_Culture|TURKSOY]].
sentence_23: The name "Kazakh" comes from the [[Old_Turkic_language|ancient Turkic]] word qaz, "to wander", reflecting the Kazakhs' [[Eurasian_nomads|nomadic]] culture.
sentence_24: The term "Cossack" is of the same origin.
sentence_25: The [[Persian_language|Persian]] suffix [[-stan|-stan]] means "land" or "place of", so Kazakhstan can be literally translated as "land of the wanderers".
sentence_26: Though the term traditionally referred to only [[Kazakhs|ethnic Kazakhs]], including those living in China, Russia, Turkey, Uzbekistan and other neighbouring countries, the term Kazakh is increasingly being used to refer to any inhabitant of Kazakhstan, including non-Kazakhs.
sentence_27: Main articles: [[Geography_of_Kazakhstan|Geography of Kazakhstan]] and List of cities in Kazakhstan
sentence_28: As it extends across both sides of the [[Ural_River|Ural River]], considered the dividing line with the European continent, Kazakhstan is one of only two [[Landlocked_country|landlocked countries]] in the world that has territory in two continents (the other is [[Azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]]).
sentence_29: With an area of 2,700,000 square kilometres (1,000,000 sq mi) – equivalent in size to Western Europe – Kazakhstan is the ninth-largest country and largest landlocked country in the world.
sentence_30: While it was part of the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]], Kazakhstan lost some of its territory to China's [[Xinjiang|Xinjiang]] province, and some to Uzbekistan's [[Karakalpakstan|Karakalpakstan]] autonomous republic during Soviet years.
sentence_31: It shares borders of 6,846 kilometres (4,254 mi) with Russia, 2,203 kilometres (1,369 mi) with [[Uzbekistan|Uzbekistan]], 1,533 kilometres (953 mi) with China, 1,051 kilometres (653 mi) with [[Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyzstan]], and 379 kilometres (235 mi) with [[Turkmenistan|Turkmenistan]].
sentence_32: Major cities include [[Nur-Sultan|Nur-Sultan]], [[Almaty|Almaty]], [[Karagandy|Karagandy]], [[Shymkent|Shymkent]], [[Atyrau|Atyrau]], and [[Oskemen|Oskemen]].
sentence_33: It lies between latitudes [[40th_parallel_north|40°]] and [[56th_parallel_north|56° N]], and longitudes [[46th_meridian_east|46°]] and 88° E.
sentence_34: While located primarily in Asia, a small portion of Kazakhstan is also located west of the [[Urals|Urals]] in Eastern Europe.
sentence_35: Kazakhstan's terrain extends west to east from the [[Caspian_Sea|Caspian Sea]] to the [[Altay_Mountains|Altay Mountains]] and north to south from the plains of [[Siberia|Western Siberia]] to the oases and deserts of Central Asia.
sentence_36: The [[Kazakh_Steppe|Kazakh Steppe]] (plain), with an area of around 804,500 square kilometres (310,600 sq mi), occupies one-third of the country and is the world's largest dry steppe region.
sentence_37: The steppe is characterised by large areas of [[Grassland|grasslands]] and sandy regions.
sentence_38: Major seas, lakes and rivers include [[Lake_Balkhash|Lake Balkhash]], [[Lake_Zaysan|Lake Zaysan]], the [[Charyn_Canyon|Charyn River and gorge]], the [[Ili_River|Ili]], [[Irtysh_River|Irtysh]], [[Ishim_River|Ishim]], [[Ural_River|Ural]] and [[Syr_Darya|Syr Darya]] rivers, and the [[Aral_Sea|Aral Sea]] until it largely dried up in one of the world's worst environmental disasters.
sentence_39: The [[Charyn_Canyon|Charyn Canyon]] is 80 kilometres (50 mi) long, cutting through a red [[Sandstone|sandstone]] plateau and stretching along the Charyn River gorge in northern [[Tian_Shan|Tian Shan]] ("Heavenly Mountains", 200 km (124 mi) east of Almaty) at .
sentence_40: The steep canyon slopes, columns and arches rise to heights of between 150 and 300 metres (490 and 980 feet).
sentence_41: The inaccessibility of the canyon provided a safe haven for a rare [[Ash_tree|ash tree]], Fraxinus sogdiana, which survived the [[Ice_Age|Ice Age]] there and has now also grown in some other areas.
sentence_42: [[Bigach_crater|Bigach crater]], at , is a Pliocene or [[Miocene|Miocene]] [[Asteroid|asteroid]] [[Impact_crater|impact crater]], 8 km (5 mi) in diameter and estimated to be 5±3 million years old.
sentence_43: See also: [[Energy_policy_of_Kazakhstan|Energy policy of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_44: Kazakhstan has an abundant supply of accessible mineral and fossil fuel resources.
sentence_45: Development of petroleum, natural gas, and mineral extractions has attracted most of the over $40 billion in foreign investment in Kazakhstan since 1993 and accounts for some 57% of the nation's industrial output (or approximately 13% of gross domestic product).
sentence_46: According to some estimates, Kazakhstan has the second largest [[Uranium|uranium]], [[Chromium|chromium]], lead, and [[Zinc|zinc]] reserves; the third largest [[Manganese|manganese]] reserves; the fifth largest copper reserves; and ranks in the top ten for coal, iron, and gold.
sentence_47: It is also an exporter of diamonds.
sentence_48: Perhaps most significant for economic development, Kazakhstan also currently has the 11th largest proven reserves of both petroleum and natural gas.
sentence_49: In total, there are 160 deposits with over 2.7 billion tonnes (2.7 billion long tons) of petroleum.
sentence_50: Oil explorations have shown that the deposits on the [[Caspian_sea|Caspian shore]] are only a small part of a much larger deposit.
sentence_51: It is said that 3.5 billion tonnes (3.4 billion long tons) of oil and 2.5 billion cubic metres (88 billion cubic feet) of gas could be found in that area.
sentence_52: Overall the estimate of Kazakhstan's oil deposits is 6.1 billion tonnes (6.0 billion long tons).
sentence_53: However, there are only three [[Oil_refinery|refineries]] within the country, situated in [[Atirau|Atyrau]], [[Pavlodar|Pavlodar]], and [[Shymkent|Shymkent]].
sentence_54: These are not capable of processing the total crude output, so much of it is exported to Russia.
sentence_55: According to the US [[Energy_Information_Administration|Energy Information Administration]] Kazakhstan was producing approximately 1,540,000 barrels (245,000 m) of oil per day in 2009.
sentence_56: Kazakhstan also possesses large deposits of phosphorite.
sentence_57: One of the largest known being the Karatau basin with 650 million tonnes of P2O5 and Chilisai deposit of located in north western Kazakhstan, with a resource of 500–800 million tonnes of 9% ore.
sentence_58: On 17 October 2013, the [[Extractive_Industries_Transparency_Initiative|Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative]] (EITI) accepted Kazakhstan as "EITI Compliant", meaning that the country has a basic and functional process to ensure the regular disclosure of natural resource revenues.
sentence_59: Kazakhstan has an "extreme" continental climate, with warm summers and very cold winters.
sentence_60: Indeed, Nursultan is the second coldest capital city in the world after [[Ulaanbaatar|Ulaanbaatar]].
sentence_61: [[Precipitation_(meteorology)|Precipitation]] varies between arid and semi-arid conditions, the winter being particularly dry.

sentence_62: Main article: [[Wildlife_of_Kazakhstan|Wildlife of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_63: There are ten [[List_of_protected_areas_of_Kazakhstan|nature reserves]] and ten [[List_of_national_parks_of_Kazakhstan|national parks]] in Kazakhstan that provide safe haven for many rare and endangered plants and animals.
sentence_64: Common plants are [[Astragalus|Astragalus]], [[Gagea|Gagea]], [[Allium|Allium]], [[Carex|Carex]] and [[Oxytropis|Oxytropis]]; endangered plant species include native wild apple ([[Malus_sieversii|Malus sieversii]]), wild grape ([[Vitis_vinifera|Vitis vinifera]]) and several wild [[Tulip|tulip]] species (e.g. [[Tulipa_greigii|Tulipa greigii]]) and rare onion species [[Allium_karataviense|Allium karataviense]], also [[Iris_willmottiana|Iris willmottiana]] and [[Tulipa_kaufmanniana|Tulipa kaufmanniana]].
sentence_65: Common mammals include the [[Wolf|wolf]], [[Red_fox|red fox]], corsac fox, [[Moose|moose]], [[Argali|argali]] (the largest species of sheep), [[Eurasian_lynx|Eurasian lynx]], [[Pallas's_cat|Pallas's cat]], and [[Snow_leopards|snow leopards]], several of which are protected.
sentence_66: Kazakhstan's Red Book of Protected Species lists 125 vertebrates including many birds and mammals, and 404 plants including fungi, algae and lichen.
sentence_67: Main articles: Government of Kazakhstan and Politics of Kazakhstan
sentence_68: Kazakhstan is a democratic, secular, constitutional [[Unitary_republic|unitary republic]]; [[Nursultan_Nazarbayev|Nursultan Nazarbayev]] led the country from 1991 to 2019.
sentence_69: He was succeeded by [[Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev|Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]].
sentence_70: The president may veto legislation that has been passed by the [[Parliament_of_Kazakhstan|parliament]] and is also the [[Commander_in_chief|commander in chief]] of the [[Armed_Forces_of_the_Republic_of_Kazakhstan|armed forces]].
sentence_71: The prime minister chairs the cabinet of ministers and serves as Kazakhstan's head of government.
sentence_72: There are three deputy prime ministers and sixteen ministers in the cabinet.
sentence_73: Kazakhstan has a bicameral parliament composed of the Majilis (the [[Lower_house|lower house]]) and [[Senate_of_Kazakhstan|senate]] (the upper house).
sentence_74: Single-mandate districts popularly elect 107 seats in the Majilis; there also are ten members elected by party-list vote.
sentence_75: The senate has 48 members.
sentence_76: Two senators are selected by each of the elected assemblies ([[Mäslihat|mäslihats]]) of Kazakhstan's sixteen principal [[Administrative_divisions_of_Kazakhstan|administrative divisions]] (fourteen regions plus the cities of Nur-Sultan, Almaty, and Shymkent).
sentence_77: The president appoints the remaining fifteen senators.
sentence_78: Majilis deputies and the government both have the right of legislative initiative, though the government proposes most legislation considered by the parliament.
sentence_79: Reforms have begun to be implemented after the election of Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in June 2019.
sentence_80: Tokayev supports a culture of opposition, public assembly, and loosening rules on forming political parties.
sentence_81: In June 2019, on the initiative of the President of Kazakhstan, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev the National Council of Public Trust have been established as a platform in which wider society can discuss different views and strengthen the national conversation regarding government policies and reforms.
sentence_82: In July 2019, the President of Kazakhstan announced a concept of a 'listening state' that quickly and efficiently responds to all constructive requests of the country's citizens.
sentence_83: A law will be passed to allow representatives from other parties to hold Chair positions on some Parliamentary committees, to foster alternative views and opinions.
sentence_84: The minimum membership threshold needed to register a political party will be reduced from 40,000 to 20,000 members.
sentence_85: Special places for peaceful rallies in central areas will be allocated and a new draft law outlining the rights and obligations of organisers, participants and observers will be passed.
sentence_86: In an effort to increase public safety, President Tokayev has strengthened the penalties for those who commit crimes against individuals.
sentence_87: [[Elections_in_Kazakhstan|Elections to the Majilis]] in September 2004, yielded a lower house dominated by the pro-government [[Nur-Otan|Otan Party]], headed by President Nazarbayev.
sentence_88: Two other parties considered sympathetic to the president, including the agrarian-industrial bloc AIST and the Asar Party, founded by President Nazarbayev's daughter, won most of the remaining seats.
sentence_89: The opposition parties which were officially registered and competed in the elections won a single seat.
sentence_90: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe was monitoring the election, which it said fell short of international standards.
sentence_91: On 4 December 2005, Nursultan Nazarbayev was re-elected in an apparent landslide victory.
sentence_92: The electoral commission announced that he had won over 90% of the vote.
sentence_93: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) concluded the election did not meet international standards despite some improvements in the administration of the election.
sentence_94: On 17 August 2007, elections to the lower house of parliament were held and a coalition led by the ruling [[Nur-Otan|Nur-Otan]] party, which included the Asar Party, the Civil Party of Kazakhstan, and the Agrarian Party, won every seat with 88% of the vote.
sentence_95: None of the opposition parties has reached the benchmark 7% level of the seats.
sentence_96: Opposition parties made accusations of serious irregularities in the election.
sentence_97: In 2010, president Nazarbayev rejected a call from supporters to hold a referendum to keep him in office until 2020.
sentence_98: He insisted on presidential elections for a five-year term.
sentence_99: In a vote held on 3 April 2011, president Nazarbayev received 95.54% of the vote with 89.9% of registered voters participating.
sentence_100: In March 2011, Nazarbayev outlined the progress made toward democracy by Kazakhstan.
sentence_101: As of 2010, Kazakhstan was reported on the [[Democracy_Index|Democracy Index]] by [[The_Economist|The Economist]] as an [[Authoritarian_regime|authoritarian regime]].
sentence_102: On 26 April 2015, the fifth presidential election was held in Kazakhstan.
sentence_103: Nursultan Nazarbayev was re-elected with 97.7% of votes.
sentence_104: On 19 March 2019, Nazarbayev announced his resignation from the presidency.
sentence_105: Kazakhstan's senate speaker [[Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev|Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] became acting president after Nursultan Nazarbayev's resignation.
sentence_106: Later, Tokayev won the [[2019_Kazakh_presidential_election|2019 presidential election]] that was held on 9 June.
sentence_107: Main articles: [[Regions_of_Kazakhstan|Regions of Kazakhstan]] and [[Districts_of_Kazakhstan|Districts of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_108: Kazakhstan is divided into fourteen [[Regions_of_Kazakhstan|regions]] ([[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]]: облыстар, oblystar; Russian: области, oblasti).
sentence_109: The regions are subdivided into 177 [[Districts_of_Kazakhstan|districts]] ([[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]]: аудандар, aýdandar; Russian: районы, rayony).
sentence_110: The districts are further subdivided into rural districts at the lowest level of administration, which include all rural settlements and villages without an associated municipal government.
sentence_111: The cities of [[Almaty|Almaty]] and [[Nur-Sultan|Nur-Sultan]] have status "state importance" and do not belong to any region.
sentence_112: The city of Baikonur has a special status because it is being leased until 2050 to Russia for the [[Baikonur_cosmodrome|Baikonur cosmodrome]].
sentence_113: In June 2018 the city of [[Shymkent|Shymkent]] became a "city of republican significance".
sentence_114: Each region is headed by an [[Akim|äkim]] (regional governor) appointed by the president.
sentence_115: District äkimi are appointed by regional akims.
sentence_116: Kazakhstan's government relocated its capital from Almaty, established under the Soviet Union, to Astana on 10 December 1997.
sentence_117: Municipalities exist at each level of administrative division in Kazakhstan.
sentence_118: Cities of republican, regional, and district significance are designated as urban inhabited localities; all others are designated rural.
sentence_119: At the highest level are the cities of Almaty and Nur-Sultan, which are classified as cities of republican significance on the administrative level equal to that of a region.
sentence_120: At the intermediate level are cities of regional significance on the administrative level equal to that of a district.
sentence_121: Cities of these two levels may be divided into city districts.
sentence_122: At the lowest level are cities of district significance, and over two-thousand villages and rural settlements (aul) on the administrative level equal to that of rural districts.
sentence_123: Main article: [[Foreign_relations_of_Kazakhstan|Foreign relations of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_124: Kazakhstan is a member of the [[Commonwealth_of_Independent_States|Commonwealth of Independent States]], the [[Economic_Cooperation_Organization|Economic Cooperation Organization]] and the [[Shanghai_Cooperation_Organization|Shanghai Cooperation Organization]].
sentence_125: The nations of Kazakhstan, Russia, [[Belarus|Belarus]], Kyrgyzstan and [[Tajikistan|Tajikistan]] established the [[Eurasian_Economic_Community|Eurasian Economic Community]] in 2000, to revive earlier efforts to harmonise trade tariffs and to create a free trade zone under a customs union.
sentence_126: On 1 December 2007, it was announced that Kazakhstan had been chosen to chair the [[Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] for the year 2010.
sentence_127: Kazakhstan was elected a member of the [[UN_Human_Rights_Council|UN Human Rights Council]] for the first time on 12 November 2012.
sentence_128: Kazakhstan is also a member of the United Nations, [[Organization_for_Security_and_Cooperation_in_Europe|Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe]], [[Euro-Atlantic_Partnership_Council|Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council]], [[Turkic_Council|Turkic Council]], and [[Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation|Organisation of Islamic Cooperation]] (OIC).
sentence_129: It is an active participant in the [[North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization|North Atlantic Treaty Organisation]] [[Partnership_for_Peace|Partnership for Peace]] program.
sentence_130: In 1999, Kazakhstan had applied for observer status at the Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly.
sentence_131: The official response of the Assembly was that because Kazakhstan is partially located in Europe, it could apply for full membership, but that it would not be granted any status whatsoever at the council until its democracy and human rights records improved.
sentence_132: Since independence in 1991, Kazakhstan has pursued what is known as the "multivector foreign policy" ([[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]]: көпвекторлы сыртқы саясат), seeking equally good relations with its two large neighbours, Russia and China, as well as with the United States and the rest of the Western world.
sentence_133: Russia currently leases approximately 6,000 square kilometres (2,317 sq mi) of territory enclosing the [[Baikonur_Cosmodrome|Baikonur Cosmodrome]] space launch site in south central Kazakhstan, where the first man was launched into space as well as Soviet space shuttle [[Buran_(spacecraft)|Buran]] and the well-known space station [[Mir|Mir]].
sentence_134: On 11 April 2010, presidents Nazarbayev and [[Barack_Obama|Obama]] met at the Nuclear Security Summit in Washington, D.C., and discussed strengthening the strategic partnership between the United States and Kazakhstan.
sentence_135: They pledged to intensify bilateral co-operation to promote nuclear safety and non-proliferation, regional stability in Central Asia, economic prosperity, and universal values.

sentence_356: The government of Kazakhstan has set prices for energy produced from renewable sources.
sentence_357: The price of 1 kilowatt-hour for energy produced by wind power plants was set at 22.68 tenge ($0.12).
sentence_358: The price for 1 kilowatt-hour produced by small hydro-power plants is 16.71 tenge ($0.09), and from biogas plants 32.23 tenge ($0.18).
sentence_359: Kazakhstan has attracted $330 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) from more than 120 countries since its independence.
sentence_360: According to the US State Department, Kazakhstan is widely considered to have the best investment climate in the region.
sentence_361: In 2002 the country became the first sovereign in the former Soviet Union to receive an investment-grade credit rating from an international credit rating agency.
sentence_362: Foreign direct investment (FDI) plays a more significant role in the national economy than in most other former Soviet republics.
sentence_363: President Nazarbayev signed into law tax concessions to promote foreign direct investment which include a ten-year exemption from corporation tax, an eight-year exemption from property tax, and a ten-year freeze on most other taxes.
sentence_364: Other incentives include a refund on capital investments of up to 30 percent once a production facility is in operation.
sentence_365: Sir [[Suma_Chakrabarti|Suma Chakrabarti]], the president of the [[European_Bank_of_Reconstruction_and_Development|European Bank of Reconstruction and Development]] (EBRD), cochaired the Kazakhstan Foreign Investors' Council with President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
sentence_366: In May 2014, the EBRD and government of Kazakhstan created the Partnership for Re-Energizing the Reform Process in Kazakhstan to work with international financial institutions to channel US$2.7 billion provided by the Kazakh government into important sectors of Kazakhstan's economy.
sentence_367: The partnership will boost investment and drive forward reforms in the country.
sentence_368: As of May 2014, Kazakhstan attracted $190 billion in gross foreign investments since its independence in 1991 and it leads the CIS countries in terms of FDI attracted per capita.
sentence_369: One of the factors that attract foreign direct investments is country's political stability.
sentence_370: According to the World Bank's report, Kazakhstan is among the top 40% of countries in the world that are considered the most politically stable and free of violence.
sentence_371: Kazakhstan also received high ratings in a survey conducted by [[Ernst_&_Young|Ernst & Young]] in 2014.
sentence_372: According to EY's 2014 Kazakhstan Attractiveness Survey, "Investor confidence in Kazakhstan's potential is also at an all-time high with 47.3% of respondents expecting Kazakhstan to become increasingly attractive over the next three years."
sentence_373: The high level of economic, political and social stability and Kazakhstan's competitive corporate tax rate were the primary reasons mentioned for its attractiveness.
sentence_374: The OECD 2017 Investment Policy Review noted that "great strides" have been made to open up opportunities to foreign investors and improving policy to attract FDI.
sentence_375: The banking industry of the Republic of Kazakhstan experienced a pronounced boom and bust cycle over 2000s decade.
sentence_376: After several years of rapid expansion in the mid-2000s, the banking industry collapsed in 2008.
sentence_377: Several large banking groups, including BTA Bank J.S.C.
sentence_378: and Alliance Bank, defaulted soon after.
sentence_379: Since then, the industry has shrunk and been restructured, with system-wide loans dropping to 39% of GDP in 2011 from 59% in 2007.
sentence_380: Although the Russian and Kazakhstani banking systems share several common features, there are also some fundamental differences.
sentence_381: Banks in Kazakhstan have experienced a lengthy period of political stability and economic growth.
sentence_382: Together with a rational approach to banking and finance policy, this has helped push Kazakhstan's banking system to a higher level of development.
sentence_383: Banking technology and personnel qualifications alike are stronger in Kazakhstan than in Russia.
sentence_384: On the negative side, past stability in Kazakhstan arose from the concentration of virtually all political power in the hands of a single individual – the key factor in any assessment of system or country risk.
sentence_385: The potential is there for serious disturbances if and when authority passes into new hands.
sentence_386: In October 2014, Kazakhstan introduced its first overseas dollar bonds in 14 years.
sentence_387: Kazakhstan issued $2.5 billion of 10- and 30-year bonds on 5 October 2014, in what was the nation's first dollar-denominated overseas sale since 2000.
sentence_388: Kazakhstan sold $1.5 billion of 10-year dollar bonds to yield 1.5 percentage points above midswaps and $1 billion of 30-year debt at two percentage points over midswaps.
sentence_389: The country drew bids for $11 billion.
sentence_390: The housing market of Kazakhstan has grown since 2010.
sentence_391: In 2013, the total housing area in Kazakhstan amounted to 336.1 million square metres (3,618 million square feet).
sentence_392: The housing stock rose over the year to 32.7 million [[Square_(unit)|squares]], which is nearly an 11% increase.
sentence_393: Between 2012 and 2013, the living area per Kazakh citizen rose from 19.6 to 20.9 square metres (211 to 225 square feet).
sentence_394: The urban areas concentrate 62.5 percent of the country's housing stock.
sentence_395: The UN's recommended standard for housing stands at 30 square metres (320 square feet) per person.
sentence_396: Kazakhstan will be able to reach the UN standards by 2019 or 2020, if in the medium term the housing growth rate remains within 7 percent.
sentence_397: On 11 November 2014, President of Kazakhstan [[Nursultan_Nazarbayev|Nursultan Nazarbayev]] delivered an unexpected state-of-the-nation address in Nur-Sultan at an extended session of the Political Council of the Nur Otan party, introducing a "Nurly Jol" (Bright Path), a new economic policy that implies massive state investment in infrastructure over the next several years.
sentence_398: The "Nurly Zhol" policy is accepted as preventive measures needed to help steer the economy towards sustainable growth in the context of the modern global economic and geopolitical challenges, such as the 25%-reduction in the oil price, reciprocal sanctions between the West and Russia over Ukraine, etc.
sentence_399: The policy embraces all aspects of economic growth, including finances, industry and social welfare, but especially emphasises investments into the development of infrastructure and construction works.
sentence_400: Given recent decreases in revenues from the export of raw materials, funds will be used from Kazakhstan's National Fund.
sentence_401: In the 2020 Doing Business Report by the World Bank, Kazakhstan ranked 25th globally and as the number one best country globally for protecting minority investors' rights.
sentence_402: Kazakhstan achieved its goal of entering the top 50 most competitive countries in 2013, and has maintained its position in the 2014–2015 World Economic Forum [[Global_Competitiveness_Report|Global Competitiveness Report]] that was published at the beginning of September 2014.
sentence_403: Kazakhstan is ahead of other states in the [[Commonwealth_of_Independent_States|CIS]] in almost all of the report's pillars of competitiveness, including institutions, infrastructure, macroeconomic environment, higher education and training, goods market efficiency, labour market development, financial market development, technological readiness, market size, business sophistication and innovation, lagging behind only in the category of health and primary education.
sentence_404: The Global Competitiveness Index gives a score from 1 to 7 in each of these pillars, and Kazakhstan earned an overall score of 4.4.
sentence_405: In 2005, the [[World_Bank|World Bank]] listed Kazakhstan as a corruption hotspot, on a par with [[Angola|Angola]], [[Bolivia|Bolivia]], [[Kenya|Kenya]], [[Libya|Libya]] and [[Pakistan|Pakistan]].
sentence_406: In 2012, Kazakhstan ranked low in an index of the least corrupt countries and the [[World_Economic_Forum|World Economic Forum]] listed corruption as the biggest problem in doing business in the country.
sentence_407: A 2017 OECD report on Kazakhstan indicated that Kazakhstan has reformed laws with regard to the civil service, judiciary, instruments to prevent corruption, [[Access_to_information|access to information]], and prosecuting corruption.
sentence_408: Kazakhstan has implemented anticorruption reforms that have been recognized by organizations like Transparency International.
sentence_409: In 2011 Switzerland confiscated US$48 million in Kazakhstani assets from Swiss bank accounts, as a result of a bribery investigation in the United States.
sentence_410: US officials believed the funds represented bribes paid by American officials to Kazakhstani officials in exchange for oil or prospecting rights in Kazakhstan.
sentence_411: Proceedings eventually involved US$84 million in the US and another US$60 million in Switzerland
sentence_412: The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Kazakh Anti-Corruption Agency signed a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty in February 2015.
sentence_413: Main article: Science and technology in Kazakhstan
sentence_414: Research remains largely concentrated in Kazakhstan's largest city and former capital, Almaty, home to 52% of research personnel.
sentence_415: Public research is largely confined to institutes, with universities making only a token contribution.
sentence_416: Research institutes receive their funding from national research councils under the umbrella of the Ministry of Education and Science.
sentence_417: Their output, however, tends to be disconnected from market needs.
sentence_418: In the business sector, few industrial enterprises conduct research themselves.
sentence_419: One of the most ambitious targets of the State Programme for Accelerated Industrial and Innovative Development adopted in 2010 is to raise the country's level of expenditure on research and development to 1% of GDP by 2015.
sentence_420: By 2013, this ratio stood at 0.18% of GDP.
sentence_421: It will be difficult to reach the target as long as economic growth remains strong.
sentence_422: Since 2005, the economy has grown faster (by 6% in 2013) than gross domestic expenditure on research and development, which only progressed from PPP$598 million to PPP$714 million between 2005 and 2013.
sentence_423: Innovation expenditure more than doubled in Kazakhstan between 2010 and 2011, representing KZT 235 billion (circa US$1.6 billion), or around 1.1% of GDP.
sentence_424: Some 11% of the total was spent on research and development.
sentence_425: This compares with about 40–70% of innovation expenditure in developed countries.
sentence_426: This augmentation was due to a sharp rise in product design and the introduction of new services and production methods over this period, to the detriment of the acquisition of machinery and equipment, which has traditionally made up the bulk of Kazakhstan's innovation expenditure.
sentence_427: Training costs represented just 2% of innovation expenditure, a much lower share than in developed countries.
sentence_428: In December 2012, President [[Nursultan_Nazarbayev|Nursultan Nazarbayev]] announced the Kazakhstan 2050 Strategy with the slogan "Strong Business, Strong State."
sentence_429: This pragmatic strategy proposes sweeping socio-economic and political reforms to hoist Kazakhstan among the top 30 economies by 2050.
sentence_430: In this document, Kazakhstan gives itself 15 years to evolve into a knowledge economy.
sentence_431: New sectors are to be created during each five-year plan.
sentence_432: The first of these, covering the years 2010–2014, focused on developing industrial capacity in car manufacturing, aircraft engineering and the production of locomotives, passenger and cargo railroad cars.
sentence_433: During the second five-year plan to 2019, the goal is to develop export markets for these products.
sentence_434: To enable Kazakhstan to enter the world market of geological exploration, the country intends to increase the efficiency of traditional extractive sectors such as oil and gas.
sentence_435: It also intends to develop rare earth metals, given their importance for electronics, laser technology, communication and medical equipment.
sentence_436: The second five-year plan coincides with the development of the Business 2020 roadmap for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which makes provision for the allocation of grants to SMEs in the regions and for microcredit.
sentence_437: The government and the National Chamber of Entrepreneurs also plan to develop an effective mechanism to help start-ups.
sentence_438: During subsequent five-year plans to 2050, new industries will be established in fields such as mobile, multi-media, nano- and space technologies, robotics, genetic engineering and alternative energy.
sentence_439: Food processing enterprises will be developed with an eye to turning the country into a major regional exporter of beef, dairy and other agricultural products.
sentence_440: Low-return, water-intensive crop varieties will be replaced with vegetable, oil and fodder products.
sentence_441: As part of the shift to a "green economy" by 2030, 15% of acreage will be cultivated with water-saving technologies.
sentence_442: Experimental agrarian and innovational clusters will be established and drought-resistant [[Genetically_modified_crops|genetically modified crops]] developed.
sentence_443: The Kazakhstan 2050 Strategy fixes a target of devoting 3% of GDP to research and development by 2050 to allow for the development of new high-tech sectors.
sentence_444: The Digital Kazakhstan program was launched in 2018 to boost the country's economic growth through the implementation of digital technologies.
sentence_445: Kazakhstan's digitization efforts generated 800 billion tenge (US$1.97 billion) in two years.
sentence_446: The program helped create 120,000 jobs and attracted 32.8 billion tenge (US$80.7 million) of investment into the country.
sentence_447: 82% of all public services became automated as part of the Digital Kazakhstan program.
sentence_448: Main article: [[Demographics_of_Kazakhstan|Demographics of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_449: See also: [[Kazakhs|Kazakhs]], [[Turkic_peoples|Turkic peoples]], and [[Eurasian_nomads|Eurasian nomads]]
sentence_450: The [[US_Census_Bureau|US Census Bureau]] International Database lists the population of Kazakhstan as 18.9 million (May 2019), while United Nations sources such as the 2019 revision of the World Population Prospects give an estimate of 18,319,618.
sentence_451: Official estimates put the population of Kazakhstan at 18.711 million as of May 2020.
sentence_452: In 2013, Kazakhstan's population rose to 17,280,000 with a 1.7% growth rate over the past year according to the Kazakhstan Statistics Agency.
sentence_453: The 2009 population estimate is 6.8% higher than the population reported in the last census from January 1999.
sentence_454: The decline in population that began after 1989 has been arrested and possibly reversed.
sentence_455: Men and women make up 48.3% and 51.7% of the population, respectively.
sentence_456: Main article: [[Ethnic_demography_of_Kazakhstan|Ethnic demography of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_457: As of 2018, ethnic [[Kazakhs|Kazakhs]] are 67.5% of the population and ethnic [[Russians_in_Kazakhstan|Russians in Kazakhstan]] are 19.8%.
sentence_458: Other groups include [[Tatars|Tatars]] (1.3%), [[Ukrainians|Ukrainians]] (2.1%), [[Uzbeks|Uzbeks]] (2.8%), [[Belarusians|Belarusians]], [[Uyghur_people|Uyghurs]] (1.4%), [[Azerbaijanis|Azerbaijanis]], [[Dungans|Dungans]], [[Kalmyks|Kalmyks]], [[Chuvashes|Chuvashes]], [[Poles_in_the_former_Soviet_Union|Poles]], and [[Lithuanians|Lithuanians]].
sentence_459: Some minorities such as [[Ukrainians|Ukrainians]], [[Koreans|Koreans]], [[Volga_Germans|Volga Germans]] (1.1%), [[Chechens|Chechens]], [[Meskhetian_Turks|Meskhetian Turks]], and Russian political opponents of the regime, had been [[Population_transfer_in_the_Soviet_Union|deported to Kazakhstan]] in the 1930s and 1940s by Stalin.
sentence_460: Some of the largest Soviet [[Labour_camp|labour camps]] ([[Gulag|Gulag]]) existed in the country.
sentence_461: Significant Russian immigration was also connected with the [[Virgin_Lands_Campaign|Virgin Lands Campaign]] and Soviet space program during the [[Nikita_Khrushchev|Khrushchev]] era.
sentence_462: In 1989, ethnic Russians were 37.8% of the population and Kazakhs held a majority in only 7 of the 20 regions of the country.
sentence_463: Before 1991 there were about 1 million [[Germans_of_Kazakhstan|Germans in Kazakhstan]], mostly descendants of the [[Volga_Germans|Volga Germans]] deported to Kazakhstan during World War II.
sentence_464: After the break-up of the Soviet Union, most of them emigrated to Germany.
sentence_465: Most members of the smaller [[Pontian_Greek|Pontian Greek]] minority have emigrated to Greece.
sentence_466: In the late 1930s thousands of [[Koreans|Koreans]] in the Soviet Union were [[Deportation_of_Koreans_in_the_Soviet_Union|deported to Central Asia]].
sentence_467: These people are now known as [[Koryo-saram|Koryo-saram]].
sentence_468: The 1990s were marked by the emigration of many of the country's [[Russians|Russians]] and [[Volga_Germans|Volga Germans]], a process that began in the 1970s.
sentence_469: This has made indigenous Kazakhs the largest ethnic group.
sentence_470: Additional factors in the increase in the Kazakhstani population are higher birthrates and immigration of ethnic Kazakhs from China, [[Mongolia|Mongolia]], and Russia.
sentence_471: Main article: [[Languages_of_Kazakhstan|Languages of Kazakhstan]]
sentence_472: Kazakhstan is officially a bilingual country.
sentence_473: [[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]], (part of the Kipchak family of [[Turkic_languages|Turkic languages]]) spoken natively by 64.4% of the population, has the status of "state" language, whereas Russian, which is spoken by most Kazakhs, is declared an "official" language, and is used routinely in business, government, and inter-ethnic communication, although Kazakh is slowly replacing it.
sentence_474: The government announced in January 2015 that the [[Latin_alphabet|Latin alphabet]] will replace [[Cyrillic|Cyrillic]] as the writing system for the Kazakh language by 2025.
sentence_475: Other minority languages spoken in Kazakhstan include [[Uzbek_language|Uzbek]], Ukrainian, [[Uyghur_language|Uyghur]], [[Kyrgyz_language|Kyrgyz]], and Tatar.
sentence_476: English, as well as Turkish, have gained popularity among younger people since the collapse of the Soviet Union.
sentence_477: Education across Kazakhstan is conducted in either Kazakh, Russian, or both.
sentence_478: In Nazarbayev's resignation speech of 2019, he projected that the people of Kazakhstan in the future will speak three languages (Kazakh, Russian and English).
sentence_479: Main article: [[Religion_in_Kazakhstan|Religion in Kazakhstan]]
sentence_480: According to the 2009 Census, 70% of the population is [[Islam_in_Kazakhstan|Muslim]], 26% [[Christianity_in_Kazakhstan|Christian]], 0.2% [[Buddhism|Buddhist]], 0.1% other religions (mostly Jewish), and 3% [[Irreligion|irreligious]], while 0.5% chose not to answer.
sentence_481: According to its Constitution, Kazakhstan is a secular state.
sentence_482: Religious freedoms are guaranteed by Article 39 of Kazakhstan's Constitution.
sentence_483: Article 39 states: "Human rights and freedoms shall not be restricted in any way."
sentence_484: Article 14 prohibits "discrimination on religious basis" and Article 19 ensures that everyone has the "right to determine and indicate or not to indicate his/her ethnic, party and religious affiliation."
sentence_485: The Constitutional Council recently affirmed these rights by ruling that a proposed law limiting the rights of certain individuals to practice their religion was declared unconstitutional.
sentence_486: [[Islam|Islam]] is the largest religion in Kazakhstan, followed by [[Orthodox_Church|Orthodox Christianity]].
sentence_487: After decades of [[Religion_in_the_Soviet_Union|religious suppression by the Soviet Union]], the coming of independence witnessed a surge in expression of ethnic identity, partly through religion.
sentence_488: The free practice of [[Religion|religious beliefs]] and the establishment of full freedom of religion led to an increase of religious activity.
sentence_489: Hundreds of mosques, churches, and other religious structures were built in the span of a few years, with the number of religious associations rising from 670 in 1990 to 4,170 today.
sentence_490: Some figures show that [[Non-denominational_Muslims|non-denominational Muslims]] form the majority, while others indicate that most Muslims in the country are [[Sunni_Islam|Sunnis]] following the [[Hanafi|Hanafi]] school.
sentence_491: These include ethnic [[Kazakhs|Kazakhs]], who constitute about 60% of the population, as well as ethnic [[Uzbeks|Uzbeks]], [[Uighurs|Uighurs]], and [[Tatars|Tatars]].
sentence_492: Less than 1% are part of the Sunni [[Shafi`i|Shafi`i]] school (primarily [[Chechens|Chechens]]).
sentence_493: There are also some [[Ahmadiyya|Ahmadi]] Muslims.
sentence_494: There are a total of 2,300 mosques, all of them are affiliated with the "Spiritual Association of Muslims of Kazakhstan", headed by a supreme [[Mufti|mufti]].
sentence_495: Unaffiliated mosques are forcefully closed.
sentence_496: [[Eid_al-Adha|Eid al-Adha]] is recognised as a national holiday.
sentence_497: One quarter of the population is Russian Orthodox, including ethnic Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians.
sentence_498: Other Christian groups include [[Roman_Catholic_Church|Roman Catholics]], [[Greek_Catholics|Greek Catholics]], and [[Protestants|Protestants]].
sentence_499: There are a total of 258 Orthodox churches, 93 Catholic churches (9 [[Greek_Catholic|Greek Catholic]]), and over 500 Protestant churches and prayer houses.
sentence_500: The Russian Orthodox Christmas is recognised as a national holiday in Kazakhstan.
sentence_501: Other religious groups include Judaism, the [[Bahá'í_Faith|Bahá'í Faith]], [[Hinduism|Hinduism]], [[Buddhism|Buddhism]], and [[The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints|The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]].
sentence_502: According to the 2009 Census data, there are very few Christians outside the Slavic and Germanic ethnic groups.
sentence_503: Main article: Education in Kazakhstan
sentence_504: Education is universal and mandatory through to the [[Secondary_education|secondary level]] and the [[List_of_countries_by_literacy_rate|adult literacy rate]] is 99.5%.
sentence_505: On average, these statistics are equal to both women and men in Kazakhstan.
sentence_506: Education consists of three main phases: primary education (forms 1–4), basic general education (forms 5–9) and senior level education (forms 10–11 or 12) divided into continued general education and vocational education.
sentence_507: Vocational Education usually lasts three or four years.
sentence_508: (Primary education is preceded by one year of pre-school education.)
sentence_509: These levels can be followed in one institution or in different ones (e.g., primary school, then secondary school).
sentence_510: Recently, several secondary schools, specialised schools, magnet schools, [[Gymnasium_(school)|gymnasiums]], [[Lyceum#Lyceums_in_today's_education|lyceums]] and linguistic and technical gymnasiums have been founded.
sentence_511: Secondary professional education is offered in special professional or technical schools, lyceums or colleges and vocational schools.
sentence_512: At present, there are [[List_of_universities_in_Kazakhstan|universities]], academies and institutes, [[College_or_university_school_of_music|conservatories]], higher schools and higher colleges.
sentence_513: There are three main levels: basic higher education that provides the fundamentals of the chosen field of study and leads to the award of the Bachelor's degree; specialised higher education after which students are awarded the Specialist's Diploma; and scientific-pedagogical higher education which leads to the master's degree.
sentence_514: Postgraduate education leads to the [[Kandidat_Nauk|Kandidat Nauk]] ("Candidate of Sciences") and the Doctor of Sciences (PhD).
sentence_515: With the adoption of the Laws on Education and on Higher Education, a private sector has been established and several private institutions have been licensed.
sentence_516: Over 2,500 students in Kazakhstan have applied for student loans totalling about $9 million.
sentence_517: The largest number of student loans come from Almaty, Nur-Sultan and Kyzylorda.
sentence_518: The training and skills development programs in Kazakhstan are also supported by international organisations.
sentence_519: For example, on 30 March 2015, the World Banks' Group of Executive Directors approved a $100 million loan for the Skills and Job project in Kazakhstan.
sentence_520: The project aims to provide relevant training to unemployed, unproductively self-employed, and current employees in need of training.
sentence_521: Main articles: [[Culture_of_Kazakhstan|Culture of Kazakhstan]], [[Kazakh_clothing|Kazakh clothing]], and [[Kazakh_wedding_ceremony|Kazakh wedding ceremony]]
sentence_522: Before the Russian colonisation, the Kazakhs had a highly developed culture based on their nomadic pastoral economy.
sentence_523: [[Islam|Islam]] was introduced into the region with the arrival of the [[Arabs|Arabs]] in the 8th century.
sentence_524: It initially took hold in the southern parts of [[Turkestan|Turkestan]] and spread northward.
sentence_525: The [[Samanids|Samanids]] helped the religion take root through zealous missionary work.
sentence_526: The [[Golden_Horde|Golden Horde]] further propagated Islam amongst the tribes in the region during the 14th century.
sentence_527: Kazakhstan is home to a large number of prominent contributors to literature, science and philosophy: [[Abay_Qunanbayuli|Abay Qunanbayuli]], Mukhtar Auezov, Gabit Musirepov, [[Kanysh_Satpayev|Kanysh Satpayev]], [[Mukhtar_Shakhanov|Mukhtar Shakhanov]], [[Saken_Seyfullin|Saken Seyfullin]], [[Jambyl_Jabayev|Jambyl Jabayev]], among many others.
sentence_528: Tourism is a rapidly growing industry in Kazakhstan and it is joining the international tourism networking.
sentence_529: In 2010, Kazakhstan joined The Region Initiative (TRI) which is a Tri-regional Umbrella of Tourism related organisations.
sentence_530: TRI is functioning as a link between three regions: South Asia, Central Asia, and Eastern Europe.
sentence_531: Armenia, Bangladesh, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Russia, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Turkey, and Ukraine are now partners, and Kazakhstan is linked with other South Asian, Eastern European, and Central Asian countries in the tourism market.
sentence_533: Kazakh literature is defined as "the body of literature, both [[Oral_literature|oral]] and written, produced in the [[Kazakh_language|Kazakh language]] by the [[Kazakh_people|Kazakh people]] of Central Asia".
sentence_534: Kazakh literature expands from the current territory of Kazakhstan, also including the era of [[Kazakh_Soviet_Socialist_Republic|Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic]], Kazakh recognised territory under the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] and the Kazakh Khanate.
sentence_535: There is some overlap with several complementary themes, including the literature of Turkic tribes that inhabited Kazakhstan over the course of the history and literature written by ethnic Kazakhs.
sentence_536: According to Chinese written sources of 6th–8th centuries CE, Turkic tribes of Kazakhstan had oral poetry tradition.
sentence_537: These came from earlier periods, and were primarily transmitted by [[Bard|bards]]: professional storytellers and musical performers.
sentence_538: Traces of this tradition are shown on Orkhon script stone carvings dated 5th–7th centuries CE that describe rule of Kultegin and Bilge, two early Turkic rulers ("kagans").
sentence_539: Amongst the Kazakhs, the bard was a primarily, though not exclusively, male profession.
sentence_540: Since at least the 17th century, Kazakh bards could be divided in two main categories: the zhıraws (zhiraus, žyraus), who passed on the works of others, usually not creating and adding their own original work; and the [[Aqyn|aqyns]] (akyns), who improvised or created their own poems, stories or songs.
sentence_541: There were several types of works, such as didactic termes, [[Elegiac|elegiac]] tolgaws, and [[Epic_(genre)|epic]] zhırs.
sentence_542: Although the origins of such tales are often unknown, most of them were associated with bards of the recent or more distant past, who supposedly created them or passed them on, by the time most Kazakh poetry and prose was first written down in the second half of the 19th century.
sentence_543: There are clear stylistic differences between works first created in the 19th century, and works dating from earlier periods but not documented before the 19th century, such as those attributed to such 16th- and 17th-century bards as Er Shoban and Dosmombet Zhıraw (also known as Dospambet Žyrau; he appeared to have been literate, and reportedly visited Constantinople), and even to such 15th-century bards as Shalkiz and Asan Qayghı.
sentence_544: Other notable bards include Kaztugan Žyrau, Žiembet Žyrau, Axtamberdy Žyrau, and Buxar Žyrau Kalkamanuly, who was an advisor to [[Ablai_Khan|Ablai Khan]], and whose works have been preserved by Mäšhür Žüsip Köpeev.
sentence_545: Er Targhın and [[Alpamysh|Alpamıs]] are two of the most famous examples of Kazakh literature to be recorded in the 19th century.
sentence_546: The [[Book_of_Dede_Korkut|Book of Dede Korkut]] and Oguz Name (a story of ancient Turkic king [[Oghuz_Khan|Oghuz Khan]]) are the most well-known Turkic heroic legends.
sentence_547: Initially created around 9th century CE, they were passed on through generations in oral form.
sentence_548: The legendary tales were recorded by Turkish authors in 14–16th centuries C.E.
sentence_549: The preeminent role in the development of modern literary Kazakh belongs to [[Abai_Qunanbaiuly|Abai Qunanbaiuly]] ([[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]]: Абай Құнанбайұлы, sometimes russified to Abay Kunanbayev, Абай Кунанбаев) (1845–1904), whose writings did much to preserve Kazakh folk culture.
sentence_550: Abai's major work is The Book of Words ([[Kazakh_language|Kazakh]]: қара сөздері, Qara sözderi), a philosophical treatise and collection of poems where he criticises Russian colonial policies and encourages other Kazakhs to embrace education and literacy.
sentence_551: The literary magazines [[Ay_Qap|Ay Qap]] (published between 1911 and 1915 in Arabic script) and Qazaq (published between 1913 and 1918) played an important role in the development of the intellectual and political life among early 20th-century Kazakhs.
sentence_553: The modern state of Kazakhstan is home to the Kazakh State Kurmangazy Orchestra of Folk Instruments, the Kazakh State Philharmonic Orchestra, the Kazakh National Opera and the Kazakh State Chamber Orchestra.
sentence_554: The folk instrument orchestra was named after Kurmangazy Sagyrbayuly, a famous composer and dombra player from the 19th century.
sentence_555: The Musical-Dramatic Training College, founded in 1931, was the first institute of higher education for music.
sentence_556: Two years later, the Orchestra of Kazakh Folk Musical Instruments was formed .
sentence_557: The Foundation Asyl Mura is archivating and publishing historical recordings of great samples of Kazakh music both traditional and classical.
sentence_558: The leading conservatoire is in Almaty, the Qurmanghazy Conservatoire.
sentence_559: It currently competes with the national conservatoire in Nur-Sultan, Kazakhstan's capital.
sentence_560: When referring to traditional Kazakh music, authentic folklore must be separated from "folklorism".
sentence_561: The latter denotes music executed by academically trained performers who aim at preserving the traditional music for coming generations.
sentence_562: As far as can be reconstructed, the music of Kazakhstan from the period before a strong Russian influence consists of instrumental music and vocal music.
sentence_563: Instrumental music, with the pieces ("Küy") being performed by soloists.
sentence_564: Text is often seen in the background (or "program") for the music, as a lot of Küy titles refer to stories.
sentence_565: Vocal music, either as part of a ceremony such as a wedding (mainly performed by women), or as part of a feast.
sentence_566: Here we might divide into subgenres: epic singing, containing not only historical facts, but as well the tribe's genealogy, love songs, didactic verses; and as a special form the composition of two or more singers in public (Aitys), of dialogue character and usually unexpectedly frankly in content.
sentence_567: The Russian influence on the music life in Kazakhstan can be seen in two spheres: first, the introduction of musical academic institutions such as concert houses with opera stages, conservatories, where the European music was performed and taught, and second, by trying to incorporate Kazakh traditional music into these academic structures.
sentence_568: Controlled first by the [[Russian_Empire|Russian Empire]] and then the [[Soviet_Union|Soviet Union]], Kazakhstan's folk and classical traditions became connected with ethnic Russian music and Western European music.
sentence_569: Prior to the 20th century, Kazakh folk music was collected and studied by ethnographic research teams including composers, music critics and [[Musicology|musicologists]].
sentence_570: In the first part of the 19th century, Kazakh music was transcribed in linear [[Musical_notation|notation]].
sentence_571: Some composers of this era set Kazakh folk songs to Russian-style [[European_classical_music|European classical music]].
sentence_572: The Kazakhs themselves, however, did not write their own music in notation until 1931.
sentence_573: Later, as part of the Soviet Union, Kazakh folk culture was encouraged in a sanitised manner designed to avoid political and social unrest.
sentence_574: The result was a bland derivative of real Kazakh folk music.
sentence_575: In 1920, [[Aleksandr_Zatayevich|Aleksandr Zatayevich]], a Russian official, created major works of art music with melodies and other elements of Kazakh folk music.
sentence_576: Beginning in 1928 and accelerating in the 1930s, he also adapted traditional Kazakh instruments for use in Russian-style ensembles, such as by increasing the number of frets and [[Strings_(music)|strings]].
sentence_577: Soon, these styles of modern orchestral playing became the only way for musicians to officially play; Kazakh folk was turned into patriotic, professional and socialist endeavours .
sentence_578: The current situation could be described as the effort to rediscover the traditional music as it had been practised before the heavy influence of European musical styles.
sentence_579: Although the quality of the performances and the striving for authenticity cannot be ignored, it is for methodological reasons important to remember that the contemporary musicians performing among traditional folk music are all well trained professionals (Rauchan Orazbaeva, Ramazan Stamgazi).
sentence_580: Another very challenging aspect arises from the young composers generation, and the rock and jazz musicians, as they aim to incorporate their traditional heritage into the music they learned from the western cultures, thus forming a new stage of "ethnic contemporary classics", respectively ethnic rock or jazz music that sounds distinctly Kazakh.
sentence_581: For the classical sector outstanding: Aqtoty Raimkulova, [[Turan_ensemble|Turan ensemble]]; for jazz: "Magic of Nomads"; for rock: Roksonaki, [[Urker|Urker]], [[Ulytau|Ulytau]], Alda span.
sentence_583: In the national cuisine, livestock meat can be cooked in a variety of ways and is usually served with a wide assortment of traditional bread products.
sentence_584: Refreshments often include black tea and traditional milk-derived drinks such as ayran, [[Shubat|shubat]] and [[Kymyz|kymyz]].
sentence_585: A traditional Kazakh dinner involves a multitude of appetisers on the table, followed by a soup and one or two main courses such as [[Pilaf|pilaf]] and [[Beshbarmak|beshbarmak]].
sentence_586: They also drink their national beverage, which consists of fermented mare's milk.
sentence_588: Kazakhstan consistently performs in Olympic competitions.
sentence_590: This has brought some attention to the Central Asian nation and increased world awareness of its athletes.
sentence_591: [[Dmitry_Karpov|Dmitry Karpov]] and [[Olga_Rypakova|Olga Rypakova]] are among the most notable Kazakhstani athletics.
sentence_592: [[Dmitry_Karpov|Dmitry Karpov]] is a distinguished decathlete, taking bronze in both the [[2004_Summer_Olympics|2004 Summer Olympics]], and the [[2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics|2003]] and [[2007_World_Athletics_Championships|2007 World Athletics Championships]].
sentence_593: [[Olga_Rypakova|Olga Rypakova]] is an athlete, specialised in [[Triple_jump|triple jump]] (women's), taking silver in the [[2011_World_Championships_in_Athletics|2011 World Championships in Athletics]] and Gold in the [[2012_Summer_Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]].
sentence_594: Kazakhstan's city of [[Almaty|Almaty]] submitted twice bid for the [[Winter_Olympics|Winter Olympics]]: in [[Almaty_bid_for_the_2014_Winter_Olympics|2014]] and again for the [[2022_Winter_Olympics|2022 Winter Olympics]].
sentence_595: [[Nur-Sultan|Nur-Sultan]] and [[Almaty|Almaty]] hosted the [[2011_Asian_Winter_Games|2011 Asian Winter Games]].
sentence_596: Popular sports in Kazakhstan include football, basketball, ice hockey, bandy, and boxing.
sentence_597: [[Association_football|Football]] is the most popular sport in Kazakhstan.
sentence_598: The [[Football_Federation_of_Kazakhstan|Football Federation of Kazakhstan]] is the sport's national governing body.
sentence_599: The FFK organises the [[Kazakhstan_national_football_team|men's]], [[Kazakhstan_women's_national_football_team|women's]], and [[Futsal|futsal]] national teams.
sentence_600: Kazakhstan's most famous basketball player was [[Alzhan_Zharmukhamedov|Alzhan Zharmukhamedov]], who played for [[PBC_CSKA_Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] and the [[Soviet_Union's_national_basketball_team|Soviet Union's national basketball team]] in the 1960s and 1970s.
sentence_601: Throughout his career, he won multiple titles and medals at some of the world's most prestigious basketball competitions, including the [[Basketball_at_the_Summer_Olympics|Summer Olympics]], the Basketball World Cup, the [[EuroBasket|EuroBasket]] (the European Basketball Championship), and the [[EuroLeague|EuroLeague]].
sentence_602: In 1971 he earned the title [[Unified_Sports_Classification_System_of_the_USSR|Master of Sports of the USSR, International Class]] and a year later he was awarded the [[Order_of_the_Badge_of_Honor|Order of the Badge of Honor]].
sentence_603: [[Kazakhstan's_national_basketball_team|Kazakhstan's national basketball team]] was established in 1992, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
sentence_604: Since its foundation, it has been competitive at the continental level.
sentence_605: Its greatest accomplishment was at the [[Basketball_at_the_2002_Asian_Games_–_Men|2002 Asian Games]], where it defeated the [[Philippines_men's_national_basketball_team|Philippines]] in its last game to win the bronze medal.
sentence_606: At the official [[Asian_Basketball_Championship|Asian Basketball Championship]], now called FIBA Asia Cup, the Kazakhs' best finish was 4th place in 2007.
sentence_607: The [[Kazakhstan_national_bandy_team|Kazakhstan national bandy team]] is among the best in the world, and has many times won the bronze medal at the [[Bandy_World_Championship|Bandy World Championship]], including the [[2012_Bandy_World_Championship|2012 edition]] when Kazakhstan hosted the tournament on home ice.
sentence_608: In the [[2011_Bandy_World_Championship|2011 tournament]], they were an extra-time in the semi-final from reaching the final for the first time.
sentence_609: In 2012, they were even closer when they took it to a penalty shootout.
sentence_610: The team won the first [[Bandy_at_the_2011_Asian_Winter_Games|bandy tournament at the Asian Winter Games]].
sentence_611: During the Soviet time, Dynamo Alma-Ata won the [[List_of_Russian_bandy_champions|Soviet Union national championships]] in 1977 and 1990 and the [[European_Cup_(bandy)|European Cup]] in 1978.
sentence_612: Bandy is developed in 10 of the country's 17 administrative divisions (8 of the 14 regions and 2 of the 3 cities which are situated inside of but are not part of regions).
sentence_613: [[Akzhaiyk|Akzhaiyk]] from [[Oral,_Kazakhstan|Oral]], however, is the only professional club.
sentence_614: The [[Kazakhstan_men's_national_ice_hockey_team|Kazakh national ice hockey team]] have competed in [[Ice_hockey|ice hockey]] in the 1998 and [[2006_Winter_Olympics|2006 Winter Olympics]], as well as in the [[2006_Men's_World_Ice_Hockey_Championships|2006 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships]].
sentence_615: The [[Kazakhstan_Hockey_Championship|Kazakhstan Hockey Championship]] is held since 1992.
sentence_616: [[Barys_Astana|Barys Astana]] is the main domestic Kazakhstani ice hockey professional team, and having played in the Kazakhstani national league until the 2008–09 season, when they were transferred to play in the [[Kontinental_Hockey_League|Kontinental Hockey League]].
sentence_617: Meanwhile, the [[Kazzinc-Torpedo|Kazzinc-Torpedo]] and play in the [[Supreme_Hockey_League|Supreme Hockey League]] since 1996 and the [[Saryarka_Karagandy|Saryarka Karagandy]] since 2012.
sentence_618: Top Kazakhstani ice hockey players include [[Nik_Antropov|Nik Antropov]], Ivan Kulshov and [[Evgeni_Nabokov|Evgeni Nabokov]].
sentence_619: [[Kazakhstan_national_amateur_boxing_athletes|Kazakh boxers]] are generally well known in the world.
sentence_620: In the last three Olympic Games, their performance was assessed as one of the best and they had more medals than any country in the world, except [[Cuba|Cuba]] and Russia (in all three games).
sentence_621: In 1996 and 2004, three Kazakhstani boxers (Vassiliy Jirov in 1996, [[Bakhtiyar_Artayev|Bakhtiyar Artayev]] in 2004 and [[Serik_Sapiyev|Serik Sapiyev]] in 2012) were recognised as the best boxers for their techniques with the [[Val_Barker_Trophy|Val Barker Trophy]], awarded to the best boxer of the tournament.
sentence_622: In [[Boxing|boxing]], Kazakhstan performed well in the [[2000_Summer_Olympics|2000 Summer Olympics]] in Sydney.
sentence_623: Two boxers, [[Bekzat_Sattarkhanov|Bekzat Sattarkhanov]] and [[Yermakhan_Ibraimov|Yermakhan Ibraimov]], earned gold medals.
sentence_624: Another two boxers, [[Bulat_Zhumadilov|Bulat Zhumadilov]] and [[Mukhtarkhan_Dildabekov|Mukhtarkhan Dildabekov]], earned [[Silver_medal|silver medals]].
sentence_625: Oleg Maskaev, born in [[Taraz|Zhambyl]], representing Russia, was the [[World_Boxing_Council|WBC]] Heavyweight Champion after knocking out [[Hasim_Rahman|Hasim Rahman]] on 12 August 2006.
sentence_626: The reigning [[World_Boxing_Association|WBA]], WBC, IBF and [[International_Boxing_Organisation|IBO]] [[List_of_middleweight_boxing_champions|middleweight champion]] is Kazakh boxer [[Gennady_Golovkin|Gennady Golovkin]].
sentence_627: [[Natascha_Ragosina|Natascha Ragosina]], representing Russia, but from [[Karaganda|Karaganda]] held seven versions of the women's super middleweight title, and two heavyweight titles during her boxing career.
sentence_628: She holds the record as the longest-reigning WBA female super middleweight champion, and the longest-reigning WBC female super middleweight champion.
sentence_630: Kazakhstan's film industry is run through the state-owned [[Kazakhfilm|Kazakhfilm]] studios based in Almaty.
sentence_631: The studio has produced award-winning movies such as [[Myn_Bala|Myn Bala]], [[Harmony_Lessons|Harmony Lessons]], and Shal.
sentence_632: Kazakhstan is host of the [[International_Astana_Action_Film_Festival|International Astana Action Film Festival]] and the [[Eurasia_International_Film_Festival|Eurasia International Film Festival]] held annually.
sentence_633: Hollywood director [[Timur_Bekmambetov|Timur Bekmambetov]] is from Kazakhstan and has become active in bridging Hollywood to the Kazakhstan film industry.
sentence_634: Kazakhstan journalist Artur Platonov won Best Script for his documentary "Sold Souls" about Kazakhstan's contribution to the struggle against terrorism at the 2013 Cannes Corporate Media and TV Awards.
sentence_635: Serik Aprymov's Little Brother (Bauyr) won at the Central and Eastern Europe Film Festival [[GoEast|goEast]] from the German Federal Foreign Office.
sentence_637: Kazakhstan is ranked 161 out of 180 countries on the [[World_Press_Freedom_Index|World Press Freedom Index]], compiled by [[Reporters_Without_Borders|Reporters Without Borders]].
sentence_638: A mid-March 2002 court order, with the government as a plaintiff, stated that [[Respublika_(Kazakh_newspaper)|Respublika]] were to stop printing for three months.
sentence_639: The order was evaded by printing under other titles, such as Not That Respublika.
sentence_640: In early 2014, a court also issued a cease publication order to the small-circulation Assandi-Times newspaper, saying it was a part of the Respublika group.
sentence_641: Human Rights Watch said: "this absurd case displays the lengths to which Kazakh authorities are willing to go to bully critical media into silence."
sentence_642: With support from the US Department of State's Bureau for Democracy, Human Rights and Labor (DRL), the American Bar Association Rule of Law Initiative opened a media support centre in Almaty to bolster free expression and journalistic rights in Kazakhstan.
sentence_643: Kazakhstan has three cultural and natural heritages on the [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] World Heritage list: the [[Mausoleum_of_Khoja_Ahmed_Yasawi|Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yassaui]], Petroglyphs within the Archaeological Landscape of [[Tamgaly|Tamgaly]], and the [[Korgalzhyn|Korgalzhyn]] and Nauryzumsky reserves.

title: Korean language
