sentence_1: The Lebanese Armed Forces ([LAF] [[Arabic_language|Arabic]]: القوات المسلحة اللبنانية | Al-Quwwāt al-Musallaḥa al-Lubnāniyya) or Forces Armées Libanaises (FAL) in [[French_language|French]], also known as the Lebanese Army ([[Arabic_language|Arabic]]: الجيش اللبناني or "Armée libanaise" in French), is the military of the [[Lebanon|Lebanese Republic]].
sentence_2: It consists of three branches, the army, the [[Lebanese_Air_Force|air force]], and the [[Lebanese_Navy|navy]].
sentence_3: The motto of the Lebanese Armed Forces is "Honor, Sacrifice, Loyalty" (Arabic: "شرف · تضحية · وفاء" - Sharaf.Tadhia.Wafa).
sentence_4: The Lebanese Armed Forces symbol consists of a [[Cedrus_libani|Lebanon cedar]] tree surrounded by two [[Bay_Laurel|laurel]] leaves, positioned above the symbols of the three branches: the ground forces represented by the two bayonets, the navy represented by an anchor, and the air force represented by two wings.
sentence_5: The Lebanese Armed Forces' primary missions include defending Lebanon and its citizens against external aggression, maintaining internal stability and security, confronting threats against the country's vital interests, engaging in social development activities and undertaking relief operations in coordination with public and [[Humanitarian|humanitarian]] institutions.
sentence_6: The armed forces consist of 72,000 active personnel with the ground force consisting of approximately 65,000 troops, the air force 2,000 personnel and 5,000 in the naval force.
sentence_7: The remaining personnel are commanders, advisors, engineers and members of the special forces.
sentence_8: All three branches are operated and coordinated by the LAF Commander; a position customarily held by a Maronite Catholic Christian, from the ministry of defence which is located in [[Yarze|Yarzeh]], east of Lebanon's capital, [[Beirut|Beirut]].
sentence_9: The current commander in chief of the Lebanese Armed Forces is General [[Joseph_Aoun_(military_officer)|Joseph Aoun]].
sentence_10: Currently, the LAF is ranked sixth in the world in terms of growth, with the number of military personnel doubling over the period between 1985 and 2000.
sentence_11: The country has six military colleges and schools.
sentence_12: Lebanese officers are sent to other countries such as the United States, Russia or other parts of Europe to receive additional training.
sentence_13: The equipment of the LAF is outdated due to lack of funds, political bickering and until the 2000s, the presence of foreign forces.
sentence_14: The Lebanese government is working with its partners to improve the armed forces' capabilities.
sentence_15: After the conclusion of the [[Lebanese_Civil_War|Lebanese Civil War]], the LAF decided to repair as much of its equipment as it could, while being aided by modest donations from other states.
sentence_16: The United States remains a key partner for Lebanon in this improvement process.
sentence_17: About 85% of the LAF's equipment is US-made, with the remaining being UK, French, and Soviet-made.
sentence_18: The [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] Army finds its local precedent in the mercenaries and irregulars that were recruited by the native dynasties that ruled Lebanon semi-autonomously during the late [[Mamluk|Mamluk]] & early [[Ottoman_Empire|Ottoman]] periods, most famously [[Ma'n_dynasty|Maan]] (c. 1490 - 1697) of [[Chouf|Chouf]], (c. 1483 - 1865) of [[Bekaa|Bekaa]] and [[Shihabs|Shihabs]] (c. 1697 - 1842) of [[Hasbaya|Hasbaya]].
sentence_19: The realm of these dynasties sometimes extended as far as [[Cilicia|Cilicia]] in [[Turkey|Turkey]] and [[Arish|Arish]] in [[Egypt|Egypt]] as under [[Fakhr_al-Din_II|Fakhr al-Din II]], and as far as [[Palmyra|Palmyra]] and [[Homs|Homs]] in 1568 under and his son.
sentence_20: These dynasties formed the defensive barrier of Lebanon since the late 15th century until Ottoman departure.
sentence_21: The first major victory came on October 31, 1622 against the Ottoman Empire Army under the lead of the [[List_of_rulers_of_Damascus|Pasha of Damascus]] in the Battle of Majdel Anjar.
sentence_22: Outnumbered (5,000 Lebanese soldiers against 12,000 Ottomans), Fakher el-Din was nevertheless victorious and was able to capture the Pasha of Damascus himself and take over Syria, Galilee and parts of Transjordan.
sentence_23: Another famous battle is [[Battle_of_Lake_Huleh_(1771)|Battle of Lake Huleh]], in September 2, 1771, in which a 10,000-strong Ottoman army was virtually destroyed by a coalition of forces of [[Nassif_al-Nassar|Nassif al-Nassar]] and [[Zahir_al-Umar|Zahir al-Umar]], with an outnumbered 3,000-strong cavalry army.
sentence_24: During the period of the [[Autonomous_entity|semi-autonomous province]] ([[Mutasarrifates|Mutasarrifia]]) period of [[Mount_Lebanon|Mount Lebanon]] between 1861 and 1914, no Turkish troops were allowed to station within its boundary.
sentence_25: Lebanon established its own army made up of volunteer militias; "the free independent bearing of these mountaineers was in striking contrast to that of the underpaid, underfed and poorly clothed conscripts of the regular [Turkish] army".
sentence_26: The beginnings of the modern Lebanese Army arose during 1916, when the French government established the "Legion of the Orient", which included Lebanese soldiers.
sentence_27: After a post [[World_War_I|World War I]] [[League_of_Nations|League of Nations]] mandate was established over Lebanon in April 1920, France formed the [[Army_of_the_Levant|Army of the Levant]], which was later reorganized into the "Troupes Spéciales du Levant" (Special Troops of the Levant).
sentence_28: These troops were composed of Lebanese and Syrian enlisted personnel, but were commanded predominantly by French officers; however, the percentage of Lebanese and Syrian officers in the force gradually increased in size to approximately 90% of the total number by 1945.
sentence_29: Later in 1926, the Lebanese First Sharp Shooters Unit was created out of the Special Troops of the Levant; it is considered to be a direct precursor to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF).
sentence_30: During [[World_War_II|World War II]], Lebanese troops fought in Lebanon with the [[Vichy_France|Vichy French]] forces against Free French and [[United_Kingdom|British]] forces.
sentence_31: After the Vichy forces in the Middle East surrendered in July 1941, volunteers from the Troupes Spéciales du Levant enlisted in the Free French forces and participated in combat in [[Italy|Italy]], [[North_Africa|North Africa]], and southern France.
sentence_32: In 1943, prior to the declaration of Lebanese independence, all the military units were combined in one brigade, the Fifth Brigade, under the command of General Fouad Chehab.
sentence_33: On the day Lebanon declared independence, the Lebanese Third Sharp Shooters Regiment was placed at the disposal of the Lebanese government in order to maintain security.
sentence_34: In June of the same year, the French reconstituted units of the Troupes Spéciales du Levant, which were then attached to the British forces in the Middle East.
sentence_35: The majority of the Lebanese Armed Forces remained a part of the [[French_Army|French Army]] in Lebanon.
sentence_36: After gaining independence in 1943, the Lebanese government formed an official delegation in 1944 to negotiate with the French the terms related to handing over the LAF.
sentence_37: After nearly three weeks of talks, the joint French-British Command decreed that responsibility for armed units under French control were to be handed over to the Independent Government of Lebanon.
sentence_38: These units were part of the Troupes Spéciales du Levant and totaled about 3,000 men.
sentence_39: On August 1, 1945 at 00:00 hours, the LAF was placed under full authority of the Lebanese National Government; this day is commemorated annually as Lebanese Army Day.
sentence_40: After establishing authority over the LAF in 1945, the Lebanese government intentionally kept its armed forces small and weak due to the country's unique internal politics.
sentence_41: [[Christianity|Christian]] politicians feared that [[Islam|Muslims]] might use the armed forces as a vehicle for seizing power in a military [[Coup_d'état|coup]].
sentence_42: They also appeared unwilling to incur the cost of maintaining a large well equipped army.
sentence_43: Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, Lebanon never spent more than 4% of its [[Gross_National_Product|GNP]] on the military budget.
sentence_44: Many Christian Lebanese also feared that a large army would inevitably force Lebanon into the [[Arab–Israeli_conflict|Arab–Israeli conflict]].
sentence_45: However, Muslim politicians were also worried that a strong army could be used against Muslim interests because it would be commanded by Christians.
sentence_46: At the same time they tended to feel that the military should be strong enough to play a part in the Arab-Israeli struggle.
sentence_47: In addition to the two major conflicting views, prominent Lebanese politicians of the myriad of religious denominations in Lebanon have also tended to be feudal warlords commanding their own private militias and feared that a strong army would endanger their personal power.
sentence_48: In 1948, the Lebanese Third Sharp Shooters Regiment fought [[Israel_Defense_Forces|Israeli Forces]] occupying the Lebanese village of [[Al-Malkiyya|Malkieh]] in the northern [[Galilee|Galilee]] and captured it, and that by the orders of Lebanese defense minister then, [[Emir_Majid_Arslan_II|Emir Majid Arslan II]].
sentence_49: This was the first major combat operation for the Lebanese Armed Forces under the Independent Lebanese Government.
sentence_50: The LAF Command is headquartered at Yarzeh.
sentence_51: The organizational structure of the LAF Command includes:
sentence_52: The Lebanese Ground Forces, القوات البريّة, literally "Ground Forces", are by far the largest of the three branches of the military.
sentence_53: The [[4th_Infantry_Brigade_(Lebanon)|Fourth Brigade]] was previously active but was disbanded in 1984.
sentence_54: The Lebanese Army Ground Forces consist of:
sentence_55: Main article: List of equipment of the Lebanese Armed Forces
sentence_56: See also: [[List_of_Lebanese_Armed_Forces_retired_equipment|List of Lebanese Armed Forces retired equipment]]
sentence_57: The Lebanese Army still uses equipment mostly received through donations or friendly prices.
sentence_58: Its work horse is the [[M113_armored_personnel_carrier|M113]] which is commonly used by every regiment and brigade.
sentence_59: A collection of Western and [[Soviet_Union|Soviet]] made weaponry and equipment exists ranging from rifles to [[Tank|tanks]].
sentence_60: However, the Lebanese Army is trying to re-arm and modernize itself through new aid and purchases from different countries such as the [[United_States|United States]], [[Belgium|Belgium]], [[Russia|Russia]], and [[Netherlands|The Netherlands]].
sentence_61: A list of awaiting-for-delivery armaments is constantly growing and includes [[M60_Patton|M60 Patton]] tanks, [[M198_Howitzer|M198 Howitzers]], etc. A recent Russian promise to supply Lebanon with [[T-90|T-90]] tanks has been in discussion since the Lebanese Defense Minister's last visit to Russia on December 16, 2008.
sentence_62: Throughout history the Lebanese Army employed different weapons and equipment which, at the time, were considered state of the art.
sentence_63: Most of these arms have either been phased out of service or sold to other countries.
sentence_64: Among the major equipment that is not currently active are AMX-13, [[Alvis_Saladin|Saladin]], [[Panhard_M3|Panhard M3]], and [[T17_(armored_car)|Staghound]] vehicles.
sentence_65: Main article: [[Lebanese_Air_Force|Lebanese Air Force]]
sentence_66: The Lebanese Air Force, القوات الجوية اللبنانية, are the aviation branch of the Lebanese Armed Forces.
sentence_67: It currently has a number of helicopters including the Bell [[UH-1_Iroquois|UH-1H]] Huey, [[Aérospatiale_SA_330_Puma|Aérospatiale SA 330 Puma]], [[Aérospatiale_Gazelle|Gazelle]], [[Cessna_Caravan|Cessna Caravan]], [[Hawker_Hunter|Hawker Hunters]], and various others.
sentence_68: The air force is currently in the process of restoring its jet capabilities and considering the purchase of a small number of fighters or jet trainers.
sentence_69: Main article: [[Lebanese_Navy|Lebanese Navy]]
sentence_70: The [[Lebanese_Navy|Lebanese Navy]], officially the Lebanese Naval Forces, القوات البحرية اللبنانية, is responsible for protecting [[Lebanon|Lebanon]]'s territorial waters, [[Port|ports]], and fighting illegal smuggling of goods.
sentence_71: At the head of the naval hierarchy is the Navy Command, then it branches off into the quarter-general of the Navy, the Department of Naval Equipment Stores, the Naval School, [[Beirut|Beirut]] Naval Base and the Jounieh Naval Base.
sentence_72: The navy, which currently lacks a suitable amount of equipment, has approximately 50 vessels of various sizes and roles; however, it is trying to modernize itself and increase its size.
sentence_73: Main article: Lebanese Special Operations Command
sentence_74: The Lebanese Special Forces are the elite of the Lebanese Army.
sentence_75: Those who enroll are subjected to rigorous training regimes and must be in peak physical and mental condition prior to their ascension to such a highly desired position.
sentence_76: Each branch of the Armed Forces maintains its own form of Special Forces or Commandos.
sentence_77: These include:

list.value: Panthers (part of the [[Internal_Security_Force|Internal Security Force]], i.e. police)

sentence_78: To ensure the effectiveness of such an elite force, many Commandos are sent overseas to nations such as the US, UK and France to receive extra training in specialized areas that the Lebanese Armed Forces are unable to provide, due to a lack of resources.
sentence_79: While training in Lebanon, each Commando is instructed in the art of urban and guerrilla warfare.
sentence_80: So rigorous is their domestic training regime that each commando is subjected to a training timetable consisting of 20 hours per day for 3 months, which is divided into different stages.
sentence_81: Each stage consists of a specialized form of warfare and its associated tactics.
sentence_82: Such tactics include: sabotage, sniping, extraction and covert operations.
sentence_83: The Lebanese Special Forces are also well known for killing and eating snakes with their bare hands at graduation ceremonies.
sentence_84: In 2008, the Lebanese Armed Forces started establishing the Lebanese Special Operations Command in order to group the LAF's elite units.
sentence_85: These special operations forces will include the Airborne Regiment, the Rangers Regiment, the Navy Commandos Regiment, and the Counter-Sabotage Regiment of the Military Intelligence.
sentence_86: The initial size of the force will be less than two brigades, around 5,000 troops, but the plan is to enlarge it up to three brigades.
sentence_87: The Lebanese Armed Forces has six official military colleges and schools that serve a wide variety of functions from officer training to overseeing national youth conscription programs.
sentence_88: The recent emphasis on the First Flag Service Center is designed to help overcome the diverse nature of the population.
sentence_89: The schools and colleges are:
sentence_90: The Staff and Command College, Military Academy, and Mountain Skiing Fighting School are training centers for Lebanese soldiers designed to upgrade the quality of their skills while the High Center for Military Sport is designed to keep them in peak physical shape (it also organizes sports groups and teams for international competition as well).
sentence_91: The Training Institute is designed to help soldiers specialize in certain aspects of the military, such as artillery and defense.
sentence_92: The military ranks are as follows:
sentence_93: Lebanon previously had mandatory military service for men only.
sentence_94: All men were required to do 1 year of military service through age 18+.
sentence_95: Training was only done whenever they had free time or time off school including summer vacations and holidays.
sentence_96: There were also training done alongside high school.
sentence_97: On May 4, 2005, a new conscription system was adopted, making for a six-month service, and pledging to end conscription within two years.
sentence_98: As of February 10, 2007 mandatory military service no longer exists in Lebanon thus making it a conscription-free all-volunteer force.
sentence_99: Training of new conscripts takes place in the First Flag Service Center (FFSC).
sentence_100: After a week of enlisting, they submit to two training courses, the common military training basic course and the specific course.
sentence_101: All these courses are organized in details according to a program determining hours of training taking into consideration the conscript rank.
sentence_102: The first course consists of 240 hours equivalent to 9 weeks and the training program is composed of:
sentence_103: The second course consists of 84 hours equivalent to three weeks.
sentence_104: The infantry course is composed of:

list.value: Infantry weapons, which are available in the Lebanese army and its tactics.

sentence_105: Main article: [[Lebanese_Civil_War|Lebanese Civil War]]
sentence_106: As the civil war escalated, Lebanese militias grew stronger and soon surpassed the regular army.
sentence_107: This rapidly undermined the authority of the central government.
sentence_108: The government's ability to maintain order was also handicapped by the nature of the Lebanese Army.
sentence_109: One of the smallest in the Middle East, it was composed based on a fixed ratio of religions.
sentence_110: As members defected to sectarian militias, the army would eventually prove unable to contain the militant groups, rein in the [[PLO|PLO]] or monitor foreign infiltration.
sentence_111: Since the government was Christian-dominated, especially the officers' ranks, trust among Muslims for central institutions, including the army, was low.
sentence_112: The disintegration of the Lebanese Army was eventually initiated by Muslim [[Deserter|deserters]] declaring that they would no longer take orders from the Maronite generals.
sentence_113: Main article: [[Dinnieh_fighting|Dinnieh fighting]]
sentence_114: During December 1999–January 2000 an Islamic group launched a failed uprising against the Lebanese authorities in the Dinnieh district.
sentence_115: In a period of 8 days of fighting in the snow-blanketed mountains east of the northern port of Tripoli, 14 soldiers and 25 rebels were killed.
sentence_116: Main article: [[2006_Lebanon_War|2006 Lebanon War]]
sentence_117: In the 2006 Lebanon War the LAF did not engage in a direct conflict with the [[Israel_Defense_Forces|Israeli Army]], despite its threat of retaliation if the IDF pushed too far northward into Lebanon.
sentence_118: However, Israel did bomb several Lebanese military bases.
sentence_119: While providing aid to civilians, Lebanese troops helped to uphold order in city streets, directed refugees to safer areas, and assisted with overlooking damage done by Israeli attacks.
sentence_120: On several occasions, Lebanese troops fired anti-air weapons at Israeli aircraft, but no damage was documented.
sentence_121: Overall, 49 Lebanese soldiers were killed.
sentence_122: After the 2006 Lebanon War the LAF deployed south of the [[Litani_River|Litani River]] for the first time since 1968 to enforce [[United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1701|Security Council Resolution 1701]].
sentence_123: The LAF says it will not, and cannot, disarm [[Hezbollah|Hezbollah]] by force.
sentence_124: On August 3, 2010, the Lebanese army [[2010_Israel–Lebanon_border_clash|fired at Israeli soldiers]] whom crane lifted a soldier across the border, to remove a tree off the fence; Israeli troops returned fire.
sentence_125: 3 LAF soldiers, one Israeli officer and 1 Lebanese journalist were killed in the incident (After Israeli Artillery & aircraft bombing).
sentence_126: According to UN reports, the border fence in the area is actually inside Israel's international border.
sentence_127: The UNIFIL force stationed in the south described the shootout as a "serious incident".
sentence_128: Main article: [[2007_Lebanon_conflict|2007 Lebanon conflict]]
sentence_129: The 2007 Lebanon conflict began when fighting broke out between [[Fatah_al-Islam|Fatah al-Islam]], an Islamic terrorist organization, and the Lebanese Armed Forces on May 20, 2007 in [[Nahr_al-Bared|Nahr al-Bared]], a Palestinian refugee camp near [[Tripoli,_Lebanon|Tripoli]].
sentence_130: It has been the most severe internal fighting since Lebanon's 1975–90 civil war.
sentence_131: The primary theater of conflict was the Siege of Nahr el-Bared.
sentence_132: There was heavy use of the Lebanese artillery in that area to eliminate snipers posted around the cities.
sentence_133: The conflict finally ended on September 2, 2007 with the Lebanese Army taking control of the camp after more than three months of heavy fights and a death toll of 155 Commandos and Infantrymen.
sentence_134: The LAF Engineering Corps achieved what was seen as a feat of ingenuity during the conflict where they converted a number of UH-1 helicopters into [[Helicopter_bombing|bombers]], arming them with 250 kg and 400 kg conventional bombs from old Hunter and Mirage III fighter jets.
sentence_135: Some helicopters were also fitted with French Matra rocket pods.
sentence_136: This was, according to observers, a decisive step that considerably shortened the conflict.
sentence_137: Main article: [[2008_fighting_in_Lebanon|2008 fighting in Lebanon]]
sentence_138: During the week-long clashes that occurred at the beginning of May 2008 in Beirut and other regions of the country, the army was unable to prevent rival Lebanese groups from fighting each other.
sentence_139: This was because the army, along with the government, had thought it would have been better if rival groups would eventually end the violence and sort out the dispute between them, alone, other than involving the national army which may have led to great divisions between the soldiers, just like in the civil war.
sentence_140: It would have also caused an out cry to the soldiers that could have died, leading to even greater divisions and blame to the political forces.
sentence_141: However, whenever ceasefire was brought into action in a specific area or district in Beirut or else where in the country, the LAF would straight away enforce peace.
sentence_142: On May 13, the national army had announced that if the clashes would not end as soon as possible, it would have to intervene and use force if necessary to stop them.

section_19.value: 2011–2017 Syrian Civil War spillover in Lebanon

sentence_143: Main article: [[Syrian_civil_war_spillover_in_Lebanon|Syrian civil war spillover in Lebanon]]
sentence_144: Since the outbreak of conflict in Syria, the Lebanese Army has been deployed to prevent Sunni-Shiite clashes from taking place in the city of Tripoli, as well as in other hot zones such as Arsal and downtown Beirut.
sentence_145: Islamic State and Al-Nusra Front terrorist groups have bases on Lebanon's mountainous eastern border with Syria from where they operate against the Lebanese army and Hezbollah.
sentence_146: Lebanon's military is coming under immense strain from the Syrian conflict spilling across the border.
sentence_147: On June 23, 2013, intense clashes in Sidon took place between followers of Salafist Sunni preacher Ahmad Al-Assir and Lebanese troops.
sentence_148: Following these clashes, the Lebanese Army was sent in to capture Sheikh Assir's headquarters at Abra and apprehend him.
sentence_149: Lebanese Army units fought against pro-Assir militants for two days in a battle that led to the deaths of at least 16 Lebanese soldiers, and the wounding of at least 50 men.
sentence_150: Although the LAF managed to secure his complex, Assir was able to escape and was only captured on August 16, 2015 while trying to flee the country on a false passport.
sentence_151: On the August 2, 2014, following the arrest of an [[Al-Nusra_Front|Al-Nusra Front]] Commander Abu Ahmad Jumaa; Terrorists from Al-Nusra and [[Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant|ISIS]] launched an [[Battle_of_Arsal|assault]] on the Lebanese Armed Forces in the town of [[Arsal|Arsal]] and seized control of the town.
sentence_152: By August 7, a fragile truce was established as ISIS and Al Nusra forces also retreated from the town and redeployed along the border with Syria.
sentence_153: Their hideouts there were subsequently bombed by the [[Syrian_Air_Force|Syrian Air Force]].
sentence_154: Two days later, the Lebanese Army entered Arsal in full force and re-established control over checkpoints that the militants had previously seized.

title: Leather
sentence_0: For other uses, see [[Leather_(disambiguation)|Leather (disambiguation)]].
sentence_1: "Cordwain" redirects here.
sentence_2: For the occupation, see [[Cordwainer|Cordwainer]].
sentence_3: "Deerskin" redirects here.
sentence_4: For the novel by Robin McKinley, see [[Deerskin_(novel)|Deerskin (novel)]].
sentence_5: For the 2019 film, see [[Deerskin_(film)|Deerskin (film)]].
sentence_6: Leather is a durable and flexible material created by [[Tanning_(leather)|tanning]] animal [[Rawhide_(textile)|rawhide]] and skins.
sentence_7: The most common raw material is [[Cattle|cattle]] hide.
sentence_8: It can be produced at manufacturing scales ranging from [[Artisan|artisan]] to modern [[Industry_(manufacturing)|industrial scale]].
sentence_9: Leather is used to make a variety of articles, including footwear, automobile seats, clothing, bags, book bindings, fashion accessories, and furniture.
sentence_10: It is produced in a wide variety of types and styles and decorated by a wide range of techniques.
sentence_11: The earliest record of leather artifacts dates back to 2200 BCE.
sentence_12: Leather usage has come under criticism in the 20th and 21st centuries by animal-rights groups.
sentence_13: These groups claim that buying or wearing leather is unethical because producing leather requires animals to be killed.
sentence_14: Main article: [[Leather_production_processes|Leather production processes]]
sentence_15: The leather manufacturing process is divided into three fundamental subprocesses: preparatory stages, tanning, and crusting.
sentence_16: A further subprocess, finishing, can be added into the leather process sequence, but not all leathers receive finishing.
sentence_17: The preparatory stages are when the hide is prepared for tanning.
sentence_18: Preparatory stages may include soaking, hair removal, [[Liming_(leather_processing)|liming]], [[Deliming|deliming]], bating, [[Bleaching|bleaching]], and [[Pickling|pickling]].
sentence_19: [[Tanning_(leather)|Tanning]] is a process that stabilizes the [[Protein|proteins]], particularly [[Collagen|collagen]], of the raw hide to increase the thermal, chemical and microbiological stability of the hides and skins, making it suitable for a wide variety of end applications.
sentence_20: The principal difference between raw and tanned hides is that raw hides dry out to form a hard, inflexible material that, when rewetted, will putrefy, while tanned material dries to a flexible form that does not become putrid when rewetted.
sentence_21: Many tanning methods and materials exist.
sentence_22: The typical process sees tanners load the hides into a drum and immerse them in a tank that contains the tanning "liquor."
sentence_23: The hides soak while the drum slowly rotates about its axis, and the tanning liquor slowly penetrates through the full thickness of the hide.
sentence_24: Once the process achieves even penetration, workers slowly raise the liquor's pH in a process called basification, which fixes the tanning material to the leather.
sentence_25: The more tanning material fixed, the higher the leather's hydrothermal stability and [[Shrinkage_(fabric)|shrinkage]] temperature resistance.
sentence_26: Crusting is a process that thins and lubricates leather.
sentence_27: It often includes a coloring operation.
sentence_28: Chemicals added during crusting must be fixed in place.
sentence_29: Crusting culminates with a drying and softening operation, and may include splitting, shaving, [[Dyeing|dyeing]], [[Whitening_(leather_processing)|whitening]] or other methods.
sentence_30: For some leathers, tanners apply a surface coating, called "finishing".
sentence_31: Finishing operations can include oiling, brushing, buffing, coating, polishing, embossing, [[Glaze_(painting_technique)|glazing]], or [[Tumble_finishing|tumbling]], among others.
sentence_32: Leather can be oiled to improve its water resistance.
sentence_33: This [[Currying_(leather)|currying]] process after tanning supplements the natural oils remaining in the leather itself, which can be washed out through repeated exposure to water.
sentence_34: Frequent oiling of leather, with [[Mink_oil|mink oil]], neatsfoot oil, or a similar material keeps it supple and improves its lifespan dramatically.
sentence_35: Tanning processes largely differ in which chemicals are used in the tanning liquor.
sentence_36: Some common types include:

list.value: Vegetable-tanned leather is tanned using [[Tannin|tannins]] extracted from [[Vegetable_matter|vegetable matter]], such as tree [[Tanbark|bark]] prepared in [[Bark_mill|bark mills]]. It is the oldest known method. It is supple and light brown in color, with the exact shade depending on the mix of materials and the color of the skin. The [[Tan_(color)|color tan]] derives its name from the appearance of undyed vegetable-tanned leather. Vegetable-tanned leather is not stable in water; it tends to discolor, and if left to soak and then dry, it shrinks and becomes harder, a feature of vegetable-tanned leather that is exploited in traditional shoemaking. In hot water, it shrinks drastically and partly congeals, becoming rigid and eventually brittle. [[Boiled_leather|Boiled leather]] is an example of this, where the leather has been hardened by being immersed in hot water, or in boiled [[Wax|wax]] or similar substances. Historically, it was occasionally used as [[Armor|armor]] after hardening, and it has also been used for [[Book_binding|book binding]].

Chrome-tanned leather is tanned using [[Chromium_(III)_sulfate|chromium sulfate]] and other [[Chromium|chromium]] [[Salt_(chemistry)|salts]]. It is also known as "wet blue" for the pale blue color of the undyed leather. The chrome tanning method usually takes approximately one day to complete, making it best suited for large-scale industrial use. This is the most common method in modern use. It is more supple and pliable than vegetable-tanned leather and does not discolor or lose shape as drastically in water as vegetable-tanned. However, there are environmental concerns with this tanning method, as chromium is a heavy metal. The method was developed in the latter half of the 19th century as tanneries wanted to find ways to speed up the process and to make leather more waterproof.

Aldehyde-tanned leather is tanned using [[Glutaraldehyde|glutaraldehyde]] or [[Oxazolidine|oxazolidine]] compounds. It is referred to as "wet white" due to its pale cream color. It is the main type of "chrome-free" leather, often seen in shoes for infants and automobiles. [[Formaldehyde|Formaldehyde]] has been used for tanning in the past; it is being phased out due to danger to workers and sensitivity of many people to formaldehyde.

[[Chamois_leather|Chamois leather]] is a form of aldehyde tanning that produces a porous and highly water-absorbent leather. Chamois leather is made using marine oils (traditionally cod oil) that oxidize to produce the aldehydes that tan the leather.

Brain tanned leathers are made by a labor-intensive process that uses emulsified oils, often those of animal brains such as deer, cattle, and buffalo. They are known for their exceptional softness and washability.

Alum leather is transformed using [[Aluminium|aluminium]] salts mixed with a variety of binders and [[Protein|protein]] sources, such as flour and egg yolk. Alum leather is not actually tanned; rather the process is called "tawing", and the resulting material reverts to rawhide if soaked in water long enough to remove the alum salts.

sentence_37: In general, leather is produced in the following grades:

list.value: Top-grain leather includes the outer layer of the hide, known as the grain, which features finer, more densely packed fibers, resulting in strength and durability. Depending on thickness, it may also contain some of the more fibrous under layer, known as the corium. Types of top-grain leather include:

Full-grain leather contains the entire grain layer, without any removal of the surface. Rather than wearing out, it develops a [[Patina|patina]] during its useful lifetime. It is usually considered the highest quality leather. Furniture and footwear are often made from full-grain leather. Full-grain leather is typically finished with a soluble [[Aniline_leather|aniline]] dye. [[Russia_leather|Russia leather]] is a form of full-grain leather.

Corrected grain leather has the surface subjected to finishing treatments to create a more uniform appearance. This usually involves buffing or sanding away flaws in the grain, then dyeing and embossing the surface.
[[Nubuck|Nubuck]] is top-grain leather that has been sanded or buffed on the grain side to give a slight nap of short protein fibers, producing a velvet-like surface.

Split leather is created from the corium left once the top-grain has been separated from the hide, known as the drop split. In thicker hides, the drop split can be further split into a middle split and a flesh split.

[[Bicast_leather|Bicast leather]] is split leather that has a polyurethane or vinyl layer applied to the surface and embossed to give it the appearance of a grain. It is slightly stiffer than top-grain leather but has a more consistent texture.

[[Patent_leather|Patent leather]] is leather that has been given a high-gloss finish by the addition of a coating. Dating to the late 1700s, it became widely popular after inventor [[Seth_Boyden|Seth Boyden]] developed the first mass-production process, using a linseed-oil-based lacquer, in 1818. Modern versions are usually a form of bicast leather.
[[Suede|Suede]] is made from the underside of a split to create a soft, napped finish. It is often made from younger or smaller animals, as the skins of adults often result in a coarse, shaggy nap.

[[Bonded_leather|Bonded leather]], also called reconstituted leather, is a material that uses leather scraps that are shredded and bonded together with polyurethane or [[Latex|latex]] onto a fiber mesh. The amount of leather fibers in the mix varies from 10% to 90%, affecting the properties of the product.

sentence_38: Today, most leather is made of [[Cattle|cattle]] hides, which constitute about 65% of all leather produced.
sentence_39: Other animals that are used include sheep (about 13%), goats (about 11%), and pigs (about 10%).
sentence_40: Obtaining accurate figures from around the world is difficult, especially for areas where the skin may be eaten.
sentence_41: Other animals mentioned below only constitute a fraction of a percent of total leather production.
sentence_42: Horse hides are used to make particularly durable leathers.
sentence_43: [[Shell_cordovan|Shell cordovan]] is a horse leather made not from the outer skin but from an under layer, found only in equine species, called the shell.
sentence_44: It is prized for its mirror-like finish and anti-creasing properties.
sentence_45: Lamb and deerskin are used for soft leather in more expensive apparel.
sentence_46: Deerskin is widely used in work gloves and indoor shoes.
sentence_47: Reptilian skins, such as [[Alligator_leather|alligator]], crocodile, and [[Snakeskin|snake]], are noted for their distinct patterns that reflect the scales of their species.
sentence_48: This has led to hunting and farming of these species in part for their skins.
sentence_49: [[Kangaroo_leather|Kangaroo leather]] is used to make items that must be strong and flexible.
sentence_50: It is the material most commonly used in [[Bullwhip|bullwhips]].
sentence_51: Some [[Motorcycle|motorcyclists]] favor kangaroo leather for [[Motorcycle_safety_clothing#Leathers|motorcycle leathers]] because of its light weight and abrasion resistance.
sentence_52: Kangaroo leather is also used for falconry jesses, soccer footwear, and boxing speed bags.
sentence_53: Although originally raised for their feathers in the 19th century, [[Ostrich|ostriches]] are now more popular for both meat and leather.
sentence_54: [[Ostrich_leather|Ostrich leather]] has a characteristic "goose bump" look because of the large follicles where the feathers grew.
sentence_55: Different processes produce different finishes for many applications, including upholstery, footwear, automotive products, accessories, and clothing.
sentence_56: In [[Thailand|Thailand]], [[Stingray|stingray]] leather is used in wallets and belts.
sentence_57: Stingray leather is tough and durable.
sentence_58: The leather is often dyed black and covered with tiny round bumps in the natural pattern of the back ridge of an animal.
sentence_59: These bumps are then usually dyed white to highlight the decoration.
sentence_60: Stingray rawhide is also used as grips on Chinese swords, Scottish basket hilted swords, and Japanese [[Katana|katanas]].
sentence_61: Stingray leather is also used for high abrasion areas in motorcycle racing leathers (especially in gloves, where its high abrasion resistance helps prevent wear through in the event of an accident).
sentence_62: For a given thickness, fish leather is typically much stronger due to its criss-crossed fibers.
sentence_63: Leather produces some environmental impact, most notably due to:

list.value: The carbon footprint of cattle rearing

Use of chemicals in the tanning process (e.g., [[Chromium|chromium]], [[Phthalate|phthalate esters]], [[Nonoxynols|nonyl phenol ethoxylate soaps]], [[Pentachlorophenol|pentachlorophenol]] and [[Solvent|solvents]])
Air pollution due to the transformation process ([[Hydrogen_sulfide|hydrogen sulfide]] is formed during mixing with acids and [[Ammonia|ammonia]] liberated during deliming, solvent vapors)

sentence_64: One estimate of the [[Carbon_footprint|carbon footprint]] of leather goods is 0.51 kg of CO2 equivalent per £1 of output at 2010 retail prices, or 0.71 kg CO2eq per £1 of output at 2010 industry prices.
sentence_65: One ton of hide or skin generally produces 20 to 80 m of waste water, including chromium levels of 100–400 mg/l, sulfide levels of 200–800 mg/l, high levels of fat and other solid wastes, and notable pathogen contamination.
sentence_66: Producers often add pesticides to protect hides during transport.
sentence_67: With solid wastes representing up to 70% of the wet weight of the original hides, the tanning process represents a considerable strain on water treatment installations.
sentence_68: Leather [[Biodegrade|biodegrades]] slowly—taking 25 to 40 years to [[Decompose|decompose]].
sentence_69: However, vinyl and petrochemical-derived materials take 500 or more years to decompose.
sentence_70: Tanning is especially polluting in countries where environmental regulations are lax, such as in India, the world's third-largest producer and exporter of leather.
sentence_71: To give an example of an efficient pollution prevention system, chromium loads per produced tonne are generally abated from 8 kg to 1.5 kg.
sentence_72: [[Volatile_organic_compounds|VOC]] emissions are typically reduced from 30 kg/t to 2 kg/t in a properly managed facility.
sentence_73: A review of the total pollution load decrease achievable according to the [[United_Nations_Industrial_Development_Organization|United Nations Industrial Development Organization]] posts precise data on the abatement achievable through industrially proven low-waste advanced methods, while noting, "even though the chrome pollution load can be decreased by 94% on introducing advanced technologies, the minimum residual load 0.15 kg/t raw hide can still cause difficulties when using landfills and composting sludge from wastewater treatment on account of the regulations currently in force in some countries."
sentence_74: In [[Kanpur|Kanpur]], the self-proclaimed "Leather City of World"—with 10,000 tanneries as of 2011 and a city of three million on the banks of the [[Ganges|Ganges]]—pollution levels were so high, that despite an industry crisis, the pollution control board decided to shut down 49 high-polluting tanneries out of 404 in July 2009.
sentence_75: In 2003 for instance, the main tanneries' effluent disposal unit was dumping 22 tonnes of chromium-laden solid waste per day in the open.
sentence_76: In the Hazaribagh neighborhood of Dhaka in [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], chemicals from tanneries end up in Dhaka's main river.
sentence_77: Besides the environmental damage, the health of both local factory workers and the end consumer is also negatively affected.
sentence_78: After approximately 15 years of ignoring high court rulings, the government shut down more than 100 tanneries the weekend of 8 April 2017 in the neighborhood.
sentence_79: The higher cost associated with the treatment of effluents than to untreated effluent discharging leads to illegal dumping to save on costs.
sentence_80: For instance, in [[Croatia|Croatia]] in 2001, proper pollution abatement cost US$70–100 per ton of raw hides processed against $43/t for irresponsible behavior.
sentence_81: In November 2009, one of Uganda's main leather making companies was caught directly dumping waste water into a wetland adjacent to [[Lake_Victoria|Lake Victoria]].
sentence_82: [[Enzyme|Enzymes]] like [[Protease|proteases]], [[Lipase|lipases]], and [[Amylase|amylases]] have an important role in the soaking, dehairing, degreasing, and bating operations of leather manufacturing.
sentence_83: Proteases are the most commonly used enzymes in leather production.
sentence_84: The enzyme must not damage or dissolve [[Collagen|collagen]] or [[Keratin|keratin]], but should hydrolyze [[Casein|casein]], [[Elastin|elastin]], albumin, [[Globulin|globulin]]-like proteins, and nonstructural proteins that are not essential for leather making.
sentence_85: This process is called bating.
sentence_86: Lipases are used in the degreasing operation to hydrolyze fat particles embedded in the skin.
sentence_87: Amylases are used to soften skin, to bring out the grain, and to impart strength and flexibility to the skin.
sentence_88: These enzymes are rarely used.
sentence_89: The natural fibers of leather break down with the passage of time.
sentence_90: Acidic leathers are particularly vulnerable to [[Red_rot|red rot]], which causes powdering of the surface and a change in consistency.
sentence_91: Damage from red rot is aggravated by high temperatures and relative humidities.
sentence_92: Although it is chemically irreversible, treatments can add handling strength and prevent disintegration of red rotted leather.
sentence_93: Exposure to long periods of low relative humidities (below 40%) can cause leather to become desiccated, irreversibly changing the fibrous structure of the leather.
sentence_94: Chemical damage can also occur from exposure to environmental factors, including ultraviolet light, ozone, acid from sulfurous and nitrous pollutants in the air, or through a chemical action following any treatment with tallow or oil compounds.
sentence_95: Both oxidation and chemical damage occur faster at higher temperatures.
sentence_96: Various treatments are available such as [[Conditioner_(chemistry)|conditioners]].
sentence_97: Saddle soap is used for cleaning, conditioning, and softening leather.
sentence_98: Leather shoes are widely conditioned with [[Shoe_polish|shoe polish]].
sentence_99: In countries with significant populations of individuals observing religions which place restrictions on material choices, leather vendors typically clarify the kinds of leather in their products.
sentence_100: For example, leather shoes bear a label that identifies the animal from which the leather came.
sentence_101: This labeling helps a [[Muslim|Muslim]] to not accidentally purchase pigskin or a [[Hindu|Hindu]] to avoid cattleskin; it facilitates religious observance and respect.
sentence_102: Many vegetarian Hindus do not use any kind of leather.
sentence_103: Such [[Taboo|taboos]] increase the demand for religiously neutral leathers such as [[Ostrich|ostrich]] and [[Deer|deer]].
sentence_104: Judaism forbids the comfort of wearing leather shoes on [[Yom_Kippur|Yom Kippur]], [[Tisha_B'Av|Tisha B'Av]], and during mourning.
sentence_105: Also, see [[Tefillin|Teffilin]] and [[Sefer_Torah|Torah Scroll]].
sentence_106: [[Jainism|Jainism]] prohibits the use of leather, since it is obtained by killing animals.
sentence_107: Many forms of [[Artificial_leather|artificial leather]] have been developed, usually involving polyurethane or vinyl coatings applied to a cloth backing.
sentence_108: Many names and brands for such artificial leathers exist, including "pleather", a portmanteau of "plastic leather", and the brand name [[Naugahyde|Naugahyde]].
sentence_109: Another alternative is cultured leather which is lab-grown using [[Cell_culture|cell culture]] methods, mushroom-based materials and gelatin-based textile made by upcycling meat industry waste.

title: Louis Pasteur
sentence_0: "Pasteur" redirects here.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Pasteur_(disambiguation)|Pasteur (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: Louis Pasteur [[Foreign_Member_of_the_Royal_Society|ForMemRS]] ([[English|/ˈluːi pæˈstɜːr/]], French: [[French|[lwi pastœʁ]]; December 27, 1822 – September 28, 1895) was a French [[Biologist|biologist]], [[Microbiologist|microbiologist]], and chemist renowned for his discoveries of the principles of [[Vaccination|vaccination]], [[Fermentation|microbial fermentation]], and [[Pasteurization|pasteurization]].
sentence_3: He is remembered for his remarkable breakthroughs in the causes and prevention of [[Diseases|diseases]], and his discoveries have saved many lives ever since.
sentence_4: He reduced mortality from [[Puerperal_fever|puerperal fever]] and created the first vaccines for [[Rabies|rabies]] and [[Anthrax|anthrax]].
sentence_5: His medical discoveries provided direct support for the [[Germ_theory_of_disease|germ theory of disease]] and its application in clinical medicine.
sentence_6: He is best known to the general public for his invention of the technique of treating [[Milk|milk]] and [[Wine|wine]] to stop bacterial contamination, a process now called [[Pasteurization|pasteurization]].
sentence_7: He is regarded as one of the three main founders of [[Bacteriology|bacteriology]], together with [[Ferdinand_Cohn|Ferdinand Cohn]] and [[Robert_Koch|Robert Koch]], and is popularly known as the "father of [[Microbiology|microbiology]]".
sentence_8: Pasteur was responsible for disproving the doctrine of [[Spontaneous_generation|spontaneous generation]].
sentence_9: He performed experiments that showed that, without contamination, microorganisms could not develop.
sentence_10: Under the auspices of the French Academy of Sciences, he demonstrated that in sterilized and sealed flasks, nothing ever developed; and, conversely, in sterilized but open flasks, microorganisms could grow.
sentence_11: Although Pasteur was not the first to propose the [[Germ_theory|germ theory]], his experiments indicated its correctness and convinced most of Europe that it was true.
sentence_12: Today, he is often regarded as one of the fathers of germ theory.
sentence_13: Pasteur made significant [[#Molecular_asymmetry|discoveries]] in chemistry, most notably on the molecular basis for the asymmetry of certain crystals and [[Racemization|racemization]].
sentence_14: Early in his career, his investigation of [[Tartaric_acid|tartaric acid]] resulted in the first resolution of what is now called [[Chirality_(chemistry)|optical isomers]].
sentence_15: His work led the way to the current understanding of a fundamental principle in the structure of organic compounds.
sentence_16: He was the director of the [[Pasteur_Institute|Pasteur Institute]], established in 1887, until his death, and his body was interred in a vault beneath the institute.
sentence_17: Although Pasteur made groundbreaking experiments, his reputation became associated with various controversies.
sentence_18: Historical reassessment of his notebook revealed that he practiced deception to overcome his rivals.
sentence_19: Louis Pasteur was born on December 27, 1822, in [[Dole,_Jura|Dole, Jura]], [[France|France]], to a [[Catholic|Catholic]] family of a poor [[Tanner_(occupation)|tanner]].
sentence_20: He was the third child of Jean-Joseph Pasteur and Jeanne-Etiennette Roqui.
sentence_21: The family moved to [[Marnoz|Marnoz]] in 1826 and then to [[Arbois|Arbois]] in 1827.
sentence_22: Pasteur entered primary school in 1831.
sentence_23: He was an average student in his early years, and not particularly academic, as his interests were [[Fishing|fishing]] and [[Sketch_(drawing)|sketching]].
sentence_24: He drew many pastels and portraits of his parents, friends and neighbors.
sentence_25: Pasteur attended secondary school at the Collège d'Arbois.
sentence_26: In October 1838, he left for Paris to join the Pension Barbet, but became homesick and returned in November.
sentence_27: In 1839, he entered the Collège Royal at [[Besançon|Besançon]] to study philosophy and earned his Bachelor of Letters degree in 1840.
sentence_28: He was appointed a tutor at the Besançon college while continuing a degree science course with special mathematics.
sentence_29: He failed his first examination in 1841.
sentence_30: He managed to pass the baccalauréat scientifique (general science) degree in 1842 from Dijon but with a mediocre grade in chemistry.
sentence_31: Later in 1842, Pasteur took the entrance test for the [[École_Normale_Supérieure|École Normale Supérieure]].
sentence_32: He passed the first set of tests, but because his ranking was low, Pasteur decided not to continue and try again next year.
sentence_33: He went back to the Pension Barbet to prepare for the test.
sentence_34: He also attended classes at the [[Lycée_Saint-Louis|Lycée Saint-Louis]] and lectures of [[Jean-Baptiste_Dumas|Jean-Baptiste Dumas]] at the Sorbonne.
sentence_35: In 1843, he passed the test with a high ranking and entered the École Normale Supérieure.
sentence_36: In 1845 he received the licencié ès sciences (Master of Science) degree.
sentence_37: In 1846, he was appointed professor of physics at the Collège de Tournon (now called Lycée Gabriel-Faure []) in [[Ardèche|Ardèche]], but the chemist Antoine Jérôme Balard wanted him back at the École Normale Supérieure as a graduate laboratory assistant (agrégé préparateur).
sentence_38: He joined Balard and simultaneously started his research in [[Crystallography|crystallography]] and in 1847, he submitted his two thesis, one in chemistry and the other in physics.
sentence_39: After serving briefly as professor of physics at the Dijon Lycée in 1848, he became professor of chemistry at the [[University_of_Strasbourg|University of Strasbourg]], where he met and courted [[Marie_Laurent|Marie Laurent]], daughter of the university's [[Rector_(academia)|rector]] in 1849.
sentence_40: They were married on May 29, 1849, and together had five children, only two of whom survived to adulthood; the other three died of [[Typhoid|typhoid]].
sentence_41: Pasteur was appointed professor of chemistry at the University of Strasbourg in 1848, and became the chair of chemistry in 1852.
sentence_42: In 1854, he was named dean of the new faculty of sciences at [[University_of_Lille|University of Lille]], where he began his studies on fermentation.
sentence_43: It was on this occasion that Pasteur uttered his oft-quoted remark: "dans les champs de l'observation, le hasard ne favorise que les esprits préparés" ("In the field of observation, chance favors only the prepared mind").
sentence_44: In 1857, he moved to Paris as the director of scientific studies at the [[École_Normale_Supérieure|École Normale Supérieure]] where he took control from 1858 to 1867 and introduced a series of reforms to improve the standard of scientific work.
sentence_45: The examinations became more rigid, which led to better results, greater competition, and increased prestige.
sentence_46: Many of his decrees, however, were rigid and authoritarian, leading to two serious student revolts.
sentence_47: During "the bean revolt" he decreed that a mutton stew, which students had refused to eat, would be served and eaten every Monday.
sentence_48: On another occasion he threatened to expel any student caught smoking, and 73 of the 80 students in the school resigned.
sentence_49: In 1863, he was appointed professor of geology, physics, and chemistry at the [[École_nationale_supérieure_des_Beaux-Arts|École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts]], a position he held until his resignation in 1867.
sentence_50: In 1867, he became the chair of organic chemistry at the Sorbonne, but he later gave up the position because of poor health.
sentence_51: In 1867, the École Normale's laboratory of physiological chemistry was created at Pasteur's request, and he was the laboratory's director from 1867 to 1888.
sentence_52: In Paris, he established the Pasteur Institute in 1887, in which he was its director for the rest of his life.
sentence_53: In Pasteur's early work as a chemist, beginning at the École Normale Supérieure, and continuing at Strasbourg and Lille, he examined the chemical, optical and crystallographic properties of a group of compounds known as [[Tartrates|tartrates]].
sentence_54: He resolved a problem concerning the nature of [[Tartaric_acid|tartaric acid]] in 1848.
sentence_55: A solution of this compound derived from living things [[Optical_rotation|rotated]] the [[Plane_of_polarization|plane of polarization]] of light passing through it.
sentence_56: The problem was that tartaric acid derived by chemical synthesis had no such effect, even though its chemical reactions were identical and its elemental composition was the same.
sentence_57: Pasteur noticed that crystals of tartrates had small faces.
sentence_58: Then he observed that, in [[Racemic_mixture|racemic mixtures]] of tartrates, half of the crystals were right-handed and half were left-handed.
sentence_59: In solution, the right-handed compound was [[Dextrorotatory|dextrorotatory]], and the left-handed one was levorotatory.
sentence_60: Pasteur determined that optical activity related to the shape of the crystals, and that an asymmetric internal arrangement of the molecules of the compound was responsible for twisting the light.
sentence_61: The (2R,3R)- and (2S,3S)- tartrates were isometric, non-superposable mirror images of each other.
sentence_62: This was the first time anyone had demonstrated [[Chirality_(chemistry)|molecular chirality]], and also the first explanation of [[Isomer|isomerism]].
sentence_63: Some historians consider Pasteur's work in this area to be his "most profound and most original contributions to science", and his "greatest scientific discovery."

section_4.value: Fermentation and germ theory of diseases

sentence_64: Pasteur was motivated to investigate fermentation while working at Lille.
sentence_65: In 1856 a local wine manufacturer, M. Bigot, whose son was one of Pasteur's students, sought for his advice on the problems of making beetroot alcohol and souring.
sentence_66: According to his son-in-law, René Vallery-Radot, in August 1857 Pasteur sent a paper about lactic acid fermentation to the Société des Sciences de Lille, but the paper was read three months later.
sentence_67: A memoire was subsequently published on November 30, 1857.
sentence_68: In the memoir, he developed his ideas stating that: "I intend to establish that, just as there is an alcoholic ferment, the yeast of beer, which is found everywhere that sugar is decomposed into alcohol and carbonic acid, so also there is a particular ferment, a lactic yeast, always present when [[Lactic_acid_fermentation|sugar becomes lactic acid]]."
sentence_69: Pasteur also wrote about alcoholic fermentation.
sentence_70: It was published in full form in 1858.
sentence_71: [[Jöns_Jacob_Berzelius|Jöns Jacob Berzelius]] and [[Justus_von_Liebig|Justus von Liebig]] had proposed the theory that fermentation was caused by decomposition.
sentence_72: Pasteur demonstrated that this theory was incorrect, and that yeast was responsible for fermentation to produce alcohol from sugar.
sentence_73: He also demonstrated that, when a different microorganism contaminated the wine, lactic acid was produced, making the wine sour.
sentence_74: In 1861, Pasteur observed that less sugar fermented per part of yeast when the yeast was exposed to air.
sentence_75: The lower rate of fermentation aerobically became known as the Pasteur effect.
sentence_76: Pasteur's research also showed that the growth of micro-organisms was responsible for spoiling beverages, such as beer, wine and milk.
sentence_77: With this established, he invented a process in which liquids such as milk were heated to a temperature between 60 and 100 °C.
sentence_78: This killed most bacteria and moulds already present within them.
sentence_79: Pasteur and [[Claude_Bernard|Claude Bernard]] completed tests on blood and urine on April 20, 1862.
sentence_80: Pasteur patented the process, to fight the "diseases" of wine, in 1865.
sentence_81: The method became known as [[Pasteurization|pasteurization]], and was soon applied to beer and milk.
sentence_82: Beverage contamination led Pasteur to the idea that micro-organisms infecting animals and humans cause disease.
sentence_83: He proposed preventing the entry of micro-organisms into the human body, leading [[Joseph_Lister,_1st_Baron_Lister|Joseph Lister]] to develop [[Antiseptic|antiseptic]] methods in surgery.
sentence_84: In 1866, Pasteur published Etudes sur le Vin, about the diseases of wine, and he published Etudes sur la Bière in 1876, concerning the diseases of beer.
sentence_85: In the early 19th century, [[Agostino_Bassi|Agostino Bassi]] had shown that [[Muscardine|muscardine]] was caused by a fungus that infected silkworms.
sentence_86: Since 1853, two diseases called [[Pébrine|pébrine]] and [[Flacherie|flacherie]] had been infecting great numbers of [[Silkworm|silkworms]] in southern France, and by 1865 they were causing huge losses to farmers.
sentence_87: In 1865, Pasteur went to [[Alès|Alès]] and worked for five years until 1870.
sentence_88: Silkworms with pébrine were covered in corpuscles.
sentence_89: In the first three years, Pasteur thought that the corpuscles were a symptom of the disease.
sentence_90: In 1870, he concluded that the corpuscles were the cause of pébrine (it is now known that the cause is a [[Microsporidian|microsporidian]]).
sentence_91: Pasteur also showed that the disease was hereditary.
sentence_92: Pasteur developed a system to prevent pébrine: after the female moths laid their eggs, the moths were turned into a pulp.
sentence_93: The pulp was examined with a microscope, and if corpuscles were observed, the eggs were destroyed.
sentence_94: Pasteur concluded that bacteria caused flacherie.
sentence_95: The primary cause is currently thought to be viruses.
sentence_96: The spread of flacherie could be accidental or hereditary.
sentence_97: Hygiene could be used to prevent accidental flacherie.
sentence_98: Moths whose digestive cavities did not contain the microorganisms causing flacherie were used to lay eggs, preventing hereditary flacherie.
sentence_99: Following his fermentation experiments, Pasteur demonstrated that the skin of grapes was the natural source of yeasts, and that sterilized grapes and grape juice never fermented.
sentence_100: He drew grape juice from under the skin with sterilized needles, and also covered grapes with sterilized cloth.
sentence_101: Both experiments could not produce wine in sterilized containers.
sentence_102: His findings and ideas were against the prevailing notion of [[Spontaneous_generation|spontaneous generation]].
sentence_103: He received a particularly stern criticism from [[Félix_Archimède_Pouchet|Félix Archimède Pouchet]], who was director of the [[Muséum_d'Histoire_Naturelle_de_Rouen|Rouen Museum of Natural History]].
sentence_104: To settle the debate between the eminent scientists, the French Academy of Sciences offered the Alhumbert Prize carrying 2,500 [[Francs|francs]] to whoever could experimentally demonstrate for or against the doctrine.
sentence_105: Pouchet stated that air everywhere could cause spontaneous generation of living organisms in liquids.
sentence_106: In the late 1850s, he performed experiments and claimed that they were evidence of spontaneous generation.
sentence_107: [[Francesco_Redi|Francesco Redi]] and [[Lazzaro_Spallanzani|Lazzaro Spallanzani]] had provided some evidence against spontaneous generation in the 17th and 18th centuries, respectively.
sentence_108: Spallanzani's experiments in 1765 suggested that air contaminated broths with bacteria.
sentence_109: In the 1860s, Pasteur repeated Spallanzani's experiments, but Pouchet reported a different result using a different broth.
sentence_110: Pasteur performed several experiments to disprove spontaneous generation.
sentence_111: He placed boiled liquid in a flask and let hot air enter the flask.
sentence_112: Then he closed the flask, and no organisms grew in it.
sentence_113: In another experiment, when he opened flasks containing boiled liquid, dust entered the flasks, causing organisms to grow in some of them.
sentence_114: The number of flasks in which organisms grew was lower at higher altitudes, showing that air at high altitudes contained less dust and fewer organisms.
sentence_115: Pasteur also used [[Swan_neck_flask|swan neck flasks]] containing a fermentable liquid.
sentence_116: Air was allowed to enter the flask via a long curving tube that made dust particles stick to it.
sentence_117: Nothing grew in the broths unless the flasks were tilted, making the liquid touch the contaminated walls of the neck.
sentence_118: This showed that the living organisms that grew in such broths came from outside, on dust, rather than spontaneously generating within the liquid or from the action of pure air.
sentence_119: These were some of the most important experiments disproving the theory of spontaneous generation, for which Pasteur won the Alhumbert Prize in 1862.

sentence_121: Pasteur's later work on diseases included work on [[Chicken_cholera|chicken cholera]].
sentence_122: He received cultures from [[Jean_Joseph_Henri_Toussaint|Jean Joseph Henri Toussaint]], and cultivated them in chicken broth.
sentence_123: During this work, a culture of the responsible [[Bacterium|bacteria]] had spoiled and failed to induce the disease in some [[Chicken|chickens]] he was infecting with the disease.
sentence_124: Upon reusing these healthy chickens, Pasteur discovered he could not infect them, even with fresh bacteria; the weakened bacteria had caused the chickens to become [[Immune|immune]] to the disease, though they had caused only mild symptoms.
sentence_125: In 1879, his assistant, [[Charles_Chamberland|Charles Chamberland]] (of French origin), had been instructed to inoculate the chickens after Pasteur went on holiday.

sentence_128: Chamberland assumed an error had been made, and wanted to discard the apparently faulty culture, but Pasteur stopped him.
sentence_129: He inoculated the chickens with virulent bacteria that killed other chickens, and they survived.
sentence_130: Pasteur concluded that the animals were now immune to the disease.
sentence_131: In December 1879, Pasteur used a weakened culture of the bacteria to inoculate chickens.
sentence_132: The chickens survived, and when he inoculated them with a virulent strain, they were immune to it.
sentence_133: In 1880, Pasteur presented his results to the French Academy of Sciences, saying that the bacteria were weakened by contact with oxygen.
sentence_134: In the 1870s, he applied this immunization method to [[Anthrax|anthrax]], which affected [[Cattle|cattle]], and aroused interest in combating other diseases.
sentence_135: Pasteur cultivated bacteria from the blood of animals infected with anthrax.
sentence_136: When he inoculated animals with the bacteria, anthrax occurred, proving that the bacteria was the cause of the disease.
sentence_137: Many cattle were dying of anthrax in "cursed fields".
sentence_138: Pasteur was told that sheep that died from anthrax were buried in the field.
sentence_139: Pasteur thought that earthworms might have brought the bacteria to the surface.
sentence_140: He found anthrax bacteria in earthworms' excrement, showing that he was correct.
sentence_141: He told the farmers not to bury dead animals in the fields.
sentence_142: In 1880, Pasteur's rival [[Jean_Joseph_Henri_Toussaint|Jean-Joseph-Henri Toussaint]], a [[Veterinary_surgeon|veterinary surgeon]], used [[Carbolic_acid|carbolic acid]] to kill anthrax bacilli and tested the vaccine on sheep.
sentence_143: Pasteur thought that this type of killed vaccine should not work because he believed that attenuated bacteria used up nutrients that the bacteria needed to grow.
sentence_144: He thought oxidizing bacteria made them less virulent.
sentence_145: In early 1881, Pasteur discovered that growing anthrax bacilli at about 42 °C made them unable to produce spores, and he described this method in a speech to the French Academy of Sciences on February 28.
sentence_146: Later in 1881, veterinarian Hippolyte Rossignol proposed that the Société d'agriculture de Melun organize an experiment to test Pasteur's vaccine.
sentence_147: Pasteur agreed, and the experiment, conducted at Pouilly-le-Fort on sheep, goats and cows, was successful.
sentence_148: Pasteur did not directly disclose how he prepared the vaccines used at Pouilly-le-Fort.
sentence_149: His laboratory notebooks, now in the [[Bibliothèque_Nationale|Bibliothèque Nationale]] in Paris, show that he actually used heat and [[Potassium_dichromate|potassium dichromate]], similar to Toussaint's method.
sentence_150: The notion of a weak form of a disease causing immunity to the virulent version was not new; this had been known for a long time for [[Smallpox|smallpox]].
sentence_151: Inoculation with smallpox ([[Variolation|variolation]]) was known to result in a much less severe disease, and greatly reduced mortality, in comparison with the naturally acquired disease.
sentence_152: [[Edward_Jenner|Edward Jenner]] had also studied [[Vaccination|vaccination]] using [[Cowpox|cowpox]] ([[Vaccinia|vaccinia]]) to give cross-immunity to smallpox in the late 1790s, and by the early 1800s vaccination had spread to most of Europe.
sentence_153: The difference between smallpox vaccination and [[Anthrax|anthrax]] or [[Chicken_cholera|chicken cholera]] vaccination was that the latter two disease organisms had been artificially weakened, so a naturally weak form of the disease organism did not need to be found.
sentence_154: This discovery revolutionized work in infectious diseases, and Pasteur gave these artificially weakened diseases the generic name of "[[Vaccine|vaccines]]", in honour of Jenner's discovery.
sentence_155: Main article: [[Koch–Pasteur_rivalry|Koch–Pasteur rivalry]]
sentence_156: In 1876, [[Robert_Koch|Robert Koch]] had shown that [[Bacillus_anthracis|Bacillus anthracis]] caused anthrax.
sentence_157: In his papers published between 1878 and 1880, Pasteur only mentioned Koch's work in a footnote.
sentence_158: Koch met Pasteur at the Seventh International Medical Congress in 1881.
sentence_159: A few months later, Koch wrote that Pasteur had used impure cultures and made errors.
sentence_160: In 1882, Pasteur replied to Koch in a speech, to which Koch responded aggressively.
sentence_161: Koch stated that Pasteur tested his vaccine on unsuitable animals and that Pasteur's research was not properly scientific.
sentence_162: In 1882, Koch wrote "On the Anthrax Inoculation", in which he refuted several of Pasteur's conclusions about anthrax and criticized Pasteur for keeping his methods secret, jumping to conclusions, and being imprecise.
sentence_163: In 1883, Pasteur wrote that he used cultures prepared in a similar way to his successful fermentation experiments and that Koch misinterpreted statistics and ignored Pasteur's work on silkworms.
sentence_164: In 1882, Pasteur sent his assistant [[Louis_Thuillier|Louis Thuillier]] to southern France because of an [[Epizootic|epizootic]] of [[Swine_erysipelas|swine erysipelas]].
sentence_165: Thuillier identified the bacillus that caused the disease in March 1883.
sentence_166: Pasteur and Thuillier increased the bacillus's virulence after passing it through pigeons.
sentence_167: Then they passed the bacillus through rabbits, weakening it and obtaining a vaccine.
sentence_168: Pasteur and Thuillier incorrectly described the bacterium as a figure-eight shape.
sentence_169: Roux described the bacterium as stick-shaped in 1884.
sentence_170: Pasteur produced the first vaccine for [[Rabies|rabies]] by growing the virus in rabbits, and then weakening it by drying the affected nerve tissue.
sentence_171: The rabies vaccine was initially created by [[Emile_Roux|Emile Roux]], a French doctor and a colleague of Pasteur, who had produced a killed vaccine using this method.
sentence_172: The vaccine had been tested in 50 dogs before its first human trial.
sentence_173: This vaccine was used on 9-year-old [[Joseph_Meister|Joseph Meister]], on July 6, 1885, after the boy was badly mauled by a rabid dog.
sentence_174: This was done at some personal risk for Pasteur, since he was not a licensed physician and could have faced prosecution for treating the boy.
sentence_175: After consulting with physicians, he decided to go ahead with the treatment.
sentence_176: Over 11 days, Meister received 13 inoculations, each inoculation using viruses that had been weakened for a shorter period of time.
sentence_177: Three months later he examined Meister and found that he was in good health.
sentence_178: Pasteur was hailed as a hero and the legal matter was not pursued.
sentence_179: Analysis of his laboratory notebooks shows that Pasteur had treated two people before his vaccination of Meister.
sentence_180: One survived but may not actually have had rabies, and the other died of rabies.
sentence_181: Pasteur began treatment of Jean-Baptiste Jupille on October 20, 1885, and the treatment was successful.
sentence_182: Later in 1885, people, including four children from the United States, went to Pasteur's laboratory to be inoculated.
sentence_183: In 1886, he treated 350 people, of which only one developed rabies.
sentence_184: The treatment's success laid the foundations for the manufacture of many other vaccines.
sentence_185: The first of the Pasteur Institutes was also built on the basis of this achievement.

sentence_188: Prior to this, few doctors or their assistants practiced these procedures.
sentence_189: A French national hero at age 55, in 1878 Pasteur discreetly told his family never to reveal his laboratory notebooks to anyone.
sentence_190: His family obeyed, and all his documents were held and inherited in secrecy.
sentence_191: Finally, in 1964 Pasteur's grandson and last surviving male descendant, Pasteur Vallery-Radot, donated the papers to the French national library ([[Bibliothèque_nationale_de_France|Bibliothèque nationale de France]]).
sentence_192: Yet the papers were restricted for historical studies until the death of Vallery-Radot in 1971.

Geison]] published an analysis of Pasteur's private notebooks in his The Private Science of Louis Pasteur, and declared that Pasteur had given several misleading accounts and played deceptions in his most important discoveries.
sentence_195: [[Max_Perutz|Max Perutz]] published a defense of Pasteur in [[The_New_York_Review_of_Books|The New York Review of Books]].
sentence_196: Based on further examinations of Pasteur's documents, French immunologist Patrice Debré concluded in his book Louis Pasteur (1998) that, in spite of his genius, Pasteur had some faults.
sentence_197: A book review states that Debré "sometimes finds him unfair, combative, arrogant, unattractive in attitude, inflexible and even dogmatic".
sentence_198: Scientists before Pasteur had studied fermentation.
sentence_199: In the 1830s, [[Charles_Cagniard-Latour|Charles Cagniard-Latour]], [[Friedrich_Traugott_Kützing|Friedrich Traugott Kützing]] and [[Theodor_Schwann|Theodor Schwann]] used microscopes to study yeasts and concluded that yeasts were living organisms.
sentence_200: In 1839, [[Justus_von_Liebig|Justus von Liebig]], [[Friedrich_Wöhler|Friedrich Wöhler]] and [[Jöns_Jacob_Berzelius|Jöns Jacob Berzelius]] stated that yeast was not an organism and was produced when air acted on plant juice.
sentence_201: In 1855, [[Antoine_Béchamp|Antoine Béchamp]], Professor of Chemistry at the University of Montpellier, conducted experiments with sucrose solutions and concluded that water was the factor for fermentation.
sentence_202: He changed his conclusion in 1858, stating that fermentation was directly related to the growth of moulds, which required air for growth.
sentence_203: He regarded himself as the first to show the role of microorganisms in fermentation.
sentence_204: Pasteur started his experiments in 1857 and published his findings in 1858 (April issue of Comptes Rendus Chimie, Béchamp's paper appeared in January issue).
sentence_205: Béchamp noted that Pasteur did not bring any novel idea or experiments.
sentence_206: On the other hand, Béchamp was probably aware of Pasteur's 1857 preliminary works.
sentence_207: With both scientists claiming priority on the discovery, a dispute, extending to several areas, lasted throughout their lives.
sentence_208: However, Béchamp was on the losing side, as the [[BMJ|BMJ]] obituary remarked: His name was "associated with bygone controversies as to priority which it would be unprofitable to recall".
sentence_209: Béchamp proposed the incorrect theory of [[Microzyme|microzymes]].
sentence_210: According to K. L. Manchester, [[Anti-vivisectionist|anti-vivisectionists]] and proponents of [[Alternative_medicine|alternative medicine]] promoted Béchamp and microzymes, unjustifiably claiming that Pasteur plagiarized Béchamp.
sentence_211: Pasteur thought that [[Succinic_acid|succinic acid]] inverted sucrose.
sentence_212: In 1860, [[Marcellin_Berthelot|Marcellin Berthelot]] isolated [[Invertase|invertase]] and showed that succinic acid did not invert sucrose.
sentence_213: Pasteur believed that fermentation was only due to living cells.
sentence_214: [[Hans_Ernst_August_Buchner|Hans Buchner]] discovered that [[Zymase|zymase]] catalyzed fermentation, showing that fermentation was catalyzed by enzymes within cells.
sentence_215: [[Eduard_Buchner|Eduard Buchner]] also discovered that fermentation could take place outside living cells.
sentence_216: Pasteur publicly claimed his success in developing the anthrax vaccine in 1881.
sentence_217: However, his admirer-turned-rival Toussaint was the one who developed the first vaccine.
sentence_218: Toussaint isolated the bacteria that caused chicken cholera (later named [[Pasteurella|Pasteurella]] in honour of Pasteur) in 1879 and gave samples to Pasteur who used them for his own works.
sentence_219: On July 12, 1880, Toussaint presented his successful result to the French Academy of Sciences, using an attenuated vaccine against anthrax in dogs and sheep.
sentence_220: Pasteur on grounds of jealousy contested the discovery by publicly displaying his vaccination method at Pouilly-le-Fort on May 5, 1881.
sentence_221: Pasteur gave a misleading account of the preparation of the anthrax vaccine used in the experiment at Pouilly-le-Fort.
sentence_222: He used potassium dichromate to prepare the vaccine.
sentence_223: The promotional experiment was a success and helped Pasteur sell his products, getting the benefits and glory.
sentence_224: Pasteur experiments are often cited as against medical ethics, especially on his vaccination of Meister.

sentence_227: His closest partner [[Émile_Roux|Émile Roux]], who had medical qualifications, refused to participate in the [[Clinical_trial|clinical trial]], likely because he considered it unjust.
sentence_228: However, Pasteur executed vaccination of the boy under the close watch of practising physicians [[Jacques-Joseph_Grancher|Jacques-Joseph Grancher]], head of the Paris Children's Hospital's paediatric clinic, and [[Alfred_Vulpian|Alfred Vulpian]], a member of the Commission on Rabies.
sentence_229: He was not allowed to hold the syringe, although the inoculations were entirely under his supervision.

sentence_238: Pasteur was awarded 1,500 [[Franc|francs]] in 1853 by the Pharmaceutical Society for the synthesis of [[Racemic_acid|racemic acid]].
sentence_239: In 1856 the [[Royal_Society|Royal Society]] of London presented him the [[Rumford_Medal|Rumford Medal]] for his discovery of the nature of racemic acid and its relations to polarized light, and the [[Copley_Medal|Copley Medal]] in 1874 for his work on fermentation.
sentence_240: He was elected a [[List_of_Fellows_of_the_Royal_Society_elected_in_1869|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS) in 1869]].
sentence_241: The French Academy of Sciences awarded Pasteur the 1859 [[Montyon_Prizes|Montyon Prize]] for experimental physiology in 1860, and the Jecker Prize in 1861 and the Alhumbert Prize in 1862 for his experimental refutation of spontaneous generation.
sentence_242: Though he lost elections in 1857 and 1861 for membership to the French Academy of Sciences, he won the 1862 election for membership to the mineralogy section.
sentence_243: He was elected to permanent secretary of the physical science section of the academy in 1887 and held the position until 1889.
sentence_244: In 1873 Pasteur was elected to the [[Académie_Nationale_de_Médecine|Académie Nationale de Médecine]] and was made the commander in the Brazilian [[Order_of_the_Rose|Order of the Rose]].
sentence_245: In 1881 he was elected to a seat at the [[Académie_française|Académie française]] left vacant by [[Émile_Littré|Émile Littré]].
sentence_246: Pasteur received the [[Albert_Medal_(Royal_Society_of_Arts)|Albert Medal]] from the [[Royal_Society_of_Arts|Royal Society of Arts]] in 1882.
sentence_247: In 1883 he became foreign member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.
sentence_248: On June 8, 1886, the Ottoman Sultan Abdul Hamid II awarded Pasteur with the [[Order_of_the_Medjidie|Order of the Medjidie]] (I Class) and 10000 Ottoman liras.
sentence_249: He was awarded the [[Cameron_Prize_for_Therapeutics_of_the_University_of_Edinburgh|Cameron Prize for Therapeutics of the University of Edinburgh]] in 1889.
sentence_250: Pasteur won the Leeuwenhoek Medal from the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences for his contributions to [[Microbiology|microbiology]] in 1895.
sentence_251: Pasteur was made a Chevalier of the [[Legion_of_Honour|Legion of Honour]] in 1853, promoted to Officer in 1863, to Commander in 1868, to Grand Officer in 1878 and made a Grand Cross of the Legion of Honor in 1881.

sentence_265: Main article: [[Pasteur_Institute|Pasteur Institute]]
