title: Smithfield, Utah
sentence_0: Smithfield is a city in [[Cache_County,_Utah|Cache County]], [[Utah|Utah]], United States.
sentence_1: The population was 9,495 at the [[2010_United_States_Census|2010 census]], with an estimated population of 12,025 in 2019.
sentence_2: It is included in the [[Logan,_Utah|Logan, Utah]]-[[Idaho|Idaho]] [[Logan_metropolitan_area|Metropolitan Statistical Area]], and is the second largest city in the area after [[Logan,_Utah|Logan]], the [[County_seat|county seat]].
sentence_3: Smithfield is home to [[Sky_View_High_School|Sky View High School]].
sentence_4: According to the [[United_States_Census_Bureau|United States Census Bureau]], the city has a total area of 5.0 square miles (12.9 km), all land.
sentence_5: At the [[2000_United_States_Census|2000 census]] there were 7,261 people in 2,066 households, including 1,782 families, in the city.
sentence_6: The population density was 1,686.6 people per square mile (650.5/km).
sentence_7: There were 2,159 housing units at an average density of 501.5 per square mile (193.4/km).
sentence_8: The [[Race_and_ethnicity_in_the_United_States_Census#2000_census|racial makeup]] of the city was 95.23% White, 0.12% African American, 0.23% Native American, 0.48% Asian, 0.04% Pacific Islander, 2.82% from other races, and 1.06% from two or more races.
sentence_9: Hispanic or Latino of any race were 5.04%.
sentence_10: Of the 2,066 households 53.2% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 78.5% were married couples living together, 6.1% had a female householder with no husband present, and 13.7% were non-families.
sentence_11: 12.2% of households were one person and 6.8% were one person aged 65 or older.
sentence_12: The average household size was 3.51 and the average family size was 3.85.
sentence_13: The age distribution was 37.8% under the age of 18, 12.1% from 18 to 24, 25.8% from 25 to 44, 16.2% from 45 to 64, and 8.0% 65 or older.
sentence_14: The median age was 25 years.
sentence_15: For every 100 females, there were 99.5 males.
sentence_16: For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 96.6 males.
sentence_17: The median household income was $47,745 and the median family income was $49,828.
sentence_18: Males had a median income of $35,708 versus $21,076 for females.
sentence_19: The per capita income for the city was $14,933.
sentence_20: About 4.5% of families and 6.2% of the population were below the [[Poverty_line|poverty line]], including 6.6% of those under age 18 and 8.0% of those age 65 or over.
sentence_21: Smithfield is home to Sunrise, Birch Creek, Summit Elementary, and Sky View, a county high school.

title: Amusement park
sentence_0: "Amusement Park" redirects here.
sentence_1: For other uses, see [[Amusement_Park_(disambiguation)|Amusement Park (disambiguation)]].
sentence_2: "Theme Park" redirects here.
sentence_3: For other uses, see [[Theme_Park_(disambiguation)|Theme Park (disambiguation)]].
sentence_4: An amusement park is a park that features various attractions, such as rides and games, as well as other events for entertainment purposes.
sentence_5: A theme park is a type of amusement park that bases its structures and attractions around a central theme, often featuring multiple areas with different themes.
sentence_6: Unlike temporary and mobile [[Travelling_funfair|funfairs]] and [[Traveling_carnival|carnivals]], amusement parks are stationary and built for long-lasting operation.
sentence_7: They are more elaborate than city parks and [[Playground|playgrounds]], usually providing attractions that cater to a variety of age groups.
sentence_8: While amusement parks often contain themed areas, theme parks place a heavier focus with more intricately-designed themes that revolve around a particular subject or group of subjects.
sentence_9: Amusement parks evolved from European fairs, [[Pleasure_garden|pleasure gardens]] and large [[Picnic|picnic areas]], which were created for people's [[Recreation|recreation]].
sentence_10: World's fairs and other types of international expositions also influenced the emergence of the amusement park industry.
sentence_11: [[Lake_Compounce|Lake Compounce]] opened in 1846 and is considered the oldest, continuously-operating amusement park in North America.
sentence_12: The first theme parks emerged in the mid-twentieth century with the opening of [[Holiday_World_&_Splashin'_Safari|Santa Claus Land]] in 1946, [[Santa's_Workshop_(New_York_amusement_park)|Santa's Workshop]] in 1949, and Disneyland in 1955.
sentence_13: The amusement park evolved from three earlier traditions: traveling or periodic fairs, pleasure gardens and exhibitions such as world fairs.
sentence_14: The oldest influence was the periodic fair of the [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]] - one of the earliest was the [[Bartholomew_Fair|Bartholomew Fair]] in England from 1133.
sentence_15: By the 18th and 19th centuries, they had evolved into places of entertainment for the masses, where the public could view freak shows, acrobatics, conjuring and [[Juggling|juggling]], take part in competitions and walk through [[Menagerie|menageries]].
sentence_16: A wave of innovation in the 1860s and 1870s created mechanical rides, such as the steam-powered [[Carousel|carousel]] (built by Thomas Bradshaw, at the Aylsham Fair), and its derivatives, notably from Frederick Savage of [[King's_Lynn|King's Lynn]], Norfolk whose fairground machinery was exported all over the world; his "galloping horses" innovation is seen in carousels today.
sentence_17: This inaugurated the era of the modern funfair ride, as the working classes were increasingly able to spend their surplus wages on entertainment.
sentence_18: The second influence was the [[Pleasure_garden|pleasure garden]].
sentence_19: An example of this is the world's oldest amusement park, [[Dyrehavsbakken|Bakken]] ("The Hill"), opened in mainland Europe in 1583.
sentence_20: It is located north of [[Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in Klampenborg, [[Denmark|Denmark]].
sentence_21: Another early garden was the [[Vauxhall_Gardens|Vauxhall Gardens]], founded in 1661 in London.
sentence_22: By the late 18th century, the site had an admission fee for its many attractions.
sentence_23: It regularly drew enormous crowds, with its paths often noted for romantic assignations; tightrope walkers, hot air balloon ascents, concerts and fireworks providing amusement.
sentence_24: Although the gardens were originally designed for the elites, they soon became places of great social diversity.
sentence_25: Public [[Firework|firework]] displays were put on at [[Marylebone_Gardens|Marylebone Gardens]], and Cremorne Gardens offered music, dancing and animal acrobatics displays.
sentence_26: [[Prater|Prater]] in [[Vienna|Vienna]], [[Austria|Austria]], began as a royal hunting ground which was opened in 1766 for public enjoyment.
sentence_27: There followed coffee-houses and cafés, which led to the beginnings of the [[Wurstelprater|Wurstelprater]] as an amusement park.
sentence_28: The concept of a fixed park for amusement was further developed with the beginning of the world's fairs.
sentence_29: [[The_Great_Exhibition|The first World fair]] began in 1851 with the construction of the landmark [[The_Crystal_Palace|Crystal Palace]] in London, England.
sentence_30: The purpose of the exposition was to celebrate the industrial achievement of the nations of the world and it was designed to educate and entertain the visitors.
sentence_31: American cities and business also saw the world's fair as a way of demonstrating economic and industrial success.
sentence_32: The [[World's_Columbian_Exposition|World's Columbian Exposition]] of 1893 in [[Chicago,_Illinois|Chicago, Illinois]] was an early precursor to the modern amusement park.
sentence_33: The fair was an enclosed site, that merged entertainment, engineering and education to entertain the masses.
sentence_34: It set out to bedazzle the visitors, and successfully did so with a blaze of lights from the "White City."
sentence_35: To make sure that the fair was a financial success, the planners included a dedicated amusement concessions area called the Midway Plaisance.
sentence_36: Rides from this fair captured the imagination of the visitors and of amusement parks around the world, such as the first steel [[Ferris_wheel|Ferris wheel]], which was found in many other amusement areas, such as the [[Prater|Prater]] by 1896.
sentence_37: Also, the experience of the enclosed ideal city with wonder, rides, culture and progress (electricity), was based on the creation of an illusory place.
sentence_38: The "[[Midway_(fair)|midway]]" introduced at the Columbian Exposition would become a standard part of most amusement parks, fairs, carnivals and circuses.
sentence_39: The midway contained not only the rides, but other concessions and entertainments such as [[Shooting_range#Shooting_gallery|shooting galleries]], [[Penny_arcade_(venue)|penny arcades]], [[Games_of_chance|games of chance]] and shows.
sentence_40: Main article: [[Trolley_park|Trolley park]]
sentence_41: Many modern amusement parks evolved from earlier pleasure resorts that had become popular with the public for day-trips or weekend holidays, for example, seaside areas such as Blackpool, [[United_Kingdom|United Kingdom]] and [[Coney_Island|Coney Island]], [[United_States|United States]].
sentence_42: In the United States, some amusement parks grew from picnic groves established along rivers and lakes that provided bathing and water sports, such as [[Lake_Compounce|Lake Compounce]] in [[Connecticut|Connecticut]], first established as a picturesque picnic park in 1846, and Riverside Park in [[Massachusetts|Massachusetts]], founded in the 1870s along the [[Connecticut_River|Connecticut River]].
sentence_43: The trick was getting the public to the seaside or resort location.
sentence_44: For [[Coney_Island|Coney Island]] in [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn]], New York, on the Atlantic Ocean, a horse-drawn streetcar line brought pleasure seekers to the beach beginning in 1829.
sentence_45: In 1875, a million passengers rode the Coney Island Railroad, and in 1876 two million visited Coney Island.
sentence_46: Hotels and amusements were built to accommodate both the upper classes and the working class at the beach.
sentence_47: The first [[Carousel|carousel]] was installed in the 1870s, the first [[Roller_coaster|roller coaster]], the "[[Switchback_Railway|Switchback Railway]]", in 1884.
sentence_48: In England, Blackpool was a popular beachside location beginning in the 1700s.
sentence_49: It rose to prominence as a seaside resort with the completion in 1846 of a branch line to Blackpool from Poulton on the main [[Preston_and_Wyre_Joint_Railway|Preston and Wyre Joint Railway]] line.
sentence_50: A sudden influx of visitors, arriving by rail, provided the motivation for entrepreneurs to build accommodation and create new attractions, leading to more visitors and a rapid cycle of growth throughout the 1850s and 1860s.
sentence_51: In 1879, large parts of the promenade at Blackpool were wired.
sentence_52: The lighting and its accompanying pageants reinforced Blackpool's status as the North of England's most prominent holiday resort, and its specifically working class character.
sentence_53: It was the forerunner of the present-day [[Blackpool_Illuminations|Blackpool Illuminations]].
sentence_54: By the 1890s, the town had a population of 35,000, and could accommodate 250,000 holidaymakers.
sentence_55: The number of annual visitors, many staying for a week, was estimated at three million.
sentence_56: In the final decade of the 19th century, electric [[Trolley_line|trolley lines]] were developed in many large American cities.
sentence_57: Companies that established the trolley lines also developed [[Trolley_park|trolley parks]] as destinations of these lines.
sentence_58: Trolley parks such as [[Atlanta|Atlanta]]'s , or [[Reading,_Pennsylvania|Reading's]] were initially popular natural leisure spots before local streetcar companies purchased the sites, expanding them from picnic groves to include regular entertainments, mechanical amusements, dance halls, sports fields, boat rides, restaurants and other resort facilities.
sentence_59: Some of these parks were developed in resort locations, such as bathing resorts at the seaside in [[New_Jersey|New Jersey]] and [[New_York_(state)|New York]].
sentence_60: A premiere example in New Jersey was [[Atlantic_City|Atlantic City]], a famous vacation resort.
sentence_61: Entrepreneurs erected amusement parks on piers that extended from the boardwalk out over the ocean.
sentence_62: The first of several was the Ocean Pier in 1891, followed later by the [[Steel_Pier|Steel Pier]] in 1898, both of which boasted rides and attractions typical of that time, such as Midway-style games and electric trolley rides.
sentence_63: The boardwalk also had the first Roundabout installed in 1892 by William Somers, a wooden predecessor to the [[Ferris_Wheel|Ferris Wheel]].
sentence_64: Somers installed two others in [[Asbury_Park|Asbury Park]], New Jersey and [[Coney_Island|Coney Island]], New York.
sentence_65: Another early park was the [[Eldorado_Amusement_Park|Eldorado Amusement Park]] that opened in 1891 on the banks of the [[Hudson_River|Hudson River]], overlooking [[New_York_City|New York City]].
sentence_66: It consisted of 25 acres.
sentence_67: The first permanent enclosed entertainment area, regulated by a single company, was founded in Coney Island in 1895: [[Sea_Lion_Park|Sea Lion Park]] at [[Coney_Island|Coney Island]] in Brooklyn.
sentence_68: This park was one of the first to charge admission to get into the park in addition to sell tickets for rides within the park.
sentence_69: In 1897, Sea Lion Park was joined by [[Steeplechase_Park|Steeplechase Park]], the first of three major amusement parks that would open in the Coney Island area.
sentence_70: George Tilyou designed the park to provide thrills and entertainment.
sentence_71: The combination of the nearby population center of [[New_York_City|New York City]] and the ease of access to the area made Coney Island the embodiment of the American amusement park.
sentence_72: Coney Island also featured [[Luna_Park_(Coney_Island,_1903)|Luna Park]] (1903) and [[Dreamland_(Coney_Island,_1904)|Dreamland]] (1904).
sentence_73: Coney Island was a huge success and by year 1910 attendance on days could reach a million people.
sentence_74: Fueled by the efforts of [[Frederick_Ingersoll|Frederick Ingersoll]] who borrowed the name, other "[[Luna_Park|Luna Parks]]" were quickly erected worldwide and opened to rave reviews.
sentence_75: The first amusement park in England was opened in 1896 - the [[Blackpool_Pleasure_Beach|Blackpool Pleasure Beach]] by W. G. Bean.
sentence_76: In 1904, Sir [[Hiram_Maxim|Hiram Maxim]]'s Captive Flying Machine was introduced; he had designed an early aircraft powered by steam engines that had been unsuccessful and instead opened up a pleasure ride of flying carriages that revolved around a central pylon.
sentence_77: Other rides included the 'Grotto' (a fantasy ride), 'River Caves' (a [[Roller_coaster#Scenic_railways|scenic railway]]), [[Water_chute|water chutes]] and a toboganning tower.
sentence_78: Fire was a constant threat in those days, as much of the construction within the amusement parks of the era was wooden.
sentence_79: In 1911, Dreamland was the first Coney Island amusement park to completely burn down; in 1944, Luna Park also burned to the ground.
sentence_80: Most of Ingersoll's Luna Parks were similarly destroyed, usually by [[Arson|arson]], before his death in 1927.
sentence_81: During the [[Gilded_Age|Gilded Age]], many Americans began working fewer hours and had more disposable income.
sentence_82: With new-found money and time to spend on leisure activities, Americans sought new venues for entertainment.
sentence_83: Amusement parks, set up outside major cities and in rural areas, emerged to meet this new economic opportunity.
sentence_84: These parks served as source of fantasy and escape from real life.
sentence_85: By the early 1900s, hundreds of amusement parks were operating in the United States and Canada.
sentence_86: Trolley parks stood outside many cities.
sentence_87: Parks like Atlanta's Ponce de Leon and Idora Park, near Youngstown, OH, took passengers to traditionally popular picnic grounds, which by the late 1890s also often included rides like the Giant Swing, [[Carousel|Carousel]], and Shoot-the-Chutes.
sentence_88: These amusement parks were often based on nationally known parks or [[List_of_world's_fairs|world's fairs]]: they had names like [[Coney_Island|Coney Island]], [[White_City_(Shrewsbury,_Massachusetts)|White City]], [[Luna_Park,_Coney_Island_(1903)|Luna Park]], or [[Dreamland_(Coney_Island,_1904)|Dreamland]].
sentence_89: The American Gilded Age was, in fact, amusement parks' Golden Age that reigned until the late 1920s.
sentence_90: The Golden Age of amusement parks also included the advent of the kiddie park.
sentence_91: Founded in 1925, the original Kiddie Park is located in San Antonio, Texas and is still in operation today.
sentence_92: The kiddie parks became popular all over America after World War II.
sentence_93: This era saw the development of the new innovations in [[Roller_coasters|roller coasters]] that included extreme drops and speeds to thrill the riders.
sentence_94: By the end of the First World War, people seemed to want an even more exciting entertainment, a need met by roller coasters.
sentence_95: Although the development of the automobile provided people with more options for satisfying their entertainment needs, the amusement parks after the war continued to be successful, while urban amusement parks saw declining attendance.
sentence_96: The 1920s is more properly known as the Golden Age of roller coasters, being the decade of frenetic building for these rides.
sentence_97: In England, [[Dreamland_Margate|Dreamland Margate]] opened in 1880 with Frederick Savage's [[Carousel|carousel]] the first amusement ride installed.
sentence_98: In 1920 the [[Scenic_Railway_(Dreamland)|Scenic Railway]] [[Rollercoaster|rollercoaster]] opened to the public with great success, carrying half a million passengers in its first year.
sentence_99: The park also installed other rides common to the time including a smaller roller coaster, the Joy Wheel, Miniature Railway, The Whip and the River Caves.
sentence_100: A ballroom was constructed on the site of the Skating Rink in 1920 and in 1923 a Variety Cinema was built on the site.
sentence_101: Between 1920 and 1935 over £500,000 was invested in the site, constantly adding new rides and facilities and culminating in the construction of the Dreamland Cinema complex in 1934 which stands to this day.
sentence_102: Meanwhile, the [[Blackpool_Pleasure_Beach|Blackpool Pleasure Beach]] was also being developed.
sentence_103: Frequent large-scale investments were responsible for the construction of many new rides, including the Virginia Reel, Whip, Noah's Ark, [[Big_Dipper_(Blackpool)|Big Dipper]] and Dodgems.
sentence_104: In the 1920s the "Casino Building" was built, which remains to this day.
sentence_105: In 1923, land was reclaimed from the sea front.
sentence_106: It was at this period that the park moved to its 44-acre (180,000 m2) current location above what became Watson Road, which was built under the Pleasure Beach in 1932.
sentence_107: During this time Joseph Emberton, an architect famous for his work in the amusement trade was brought in to redesign the architectural style of the Pleasure Beach rides, working on the "Grand National" roller coaster, "Noah's Ark" and the Casino building to name a few.

section_5.value: Depression and post-World War II decline

sentence_108: The [[Great_Depression|Great Depression]] of the 1930s and [[World_War_II|World War II]] during the 1940s saw the decline of the amusement park industry.
sentence_109: War caused the affluent urban population to move to the suburbs, television became a source of entertainment, and families went to amusement parks less often.
sentence_110: By the 1950s, factors such as [[Urban_decay|urban decay]], [[Crime|crime]], and even [[Desegregation|desegregation]] in the ghettos led to changing patterns in how people chose to spend their free time.
sentence_111: Many of the older, traditional amusement parks closed or burned to the ground.
sentence_112: Many would be taken out by the wrecking ball to make way for [[Suburban|suburban]] housing and [[Urban_development|development]].
sentence_113: In 1964, [[Steeplechase_Park|Steeplechase Park]], once the king of all amusement parks, closed down for good.
sentence_114: The traditional amusement parks which survived, for example, [[Kennywood|Kennywood]], in [[West_Mifflin,_Pennsylvania|West Mifflin, Pennsylvania]], and [[Cedar_Point|Cedar Point]], in [[Sandusky,_Ohio|Sandusky, Ohio]], did so in spite of the odds.
sentence_115: The amusement park industry's offerings range from immersive theme parks such as the [[Walt_Disney_World|Walt Disney World Resort]] and [[Universal_Orlando_Resort|Universal Orlando Resort]] to thrilling coaster parks such as the [[Six_Flags|Six Flags]] parks and [[Cedar_Fair|Cedar Fair]] parks.
sentence_116: Countless smaller ventures exist across the United States and around the world.
sentence_117: Simpler theme parks directly aimed at smaller children have also emerged, such as Legoland.
sentence_118: Examples of amusement parks in shopping malls exist in West Edmonton Mall, [[Pier_39|Pier 39]] and [[Mall_of_America|Mall of America]].
sentence_119: Family fun parks starting as miniature golf courses have begun to grow to include batting cages, go-karts, bumper cars, bumper boats and water slides.
sentence_120: Some of these parks have grown to include even roller coasters, and traditional amusement parks now also have these competition areas in addition to their thrill rides.
sentence_121: In 2015, theme parks in the United States had a revenue of US$8 billion and theme parks in [[China|China]] had a revenue of US$4.6 billion, with China expected to overtake the United States by 2020.
sentence_122: Some parks use rides and attractions for educational purposes.
sentence_123: Disney was the first to successfully open a large-scale theme park built around education.
sentence_124: Named [[Epcot|Epcot]], it opened in 1982 as the second park in the Walt Disney World Resort.
sentence_125: There are also [[Holy_Land_USA|Holy Land USA]] and the [[Holy_Land_Experience|Holy Land Experience]], which are theme parks built to inspire Christian piety.
sentence_126: [[Dinosaur_World_(theme_parks)|Dinosaur World]] entertains families with [[Dinosaur|dinosaurs]] in natural settings, while the [[SeaWorld|SeaWorld]] and Busch Gardens parks also offer educational experiences, with each of the parks housing several thousand animals, fish and other sea life in dozens of attractions and exhibits focusing on animal education.
sentence_127: Created in 1977, the [[Puy_du_Fou|Puy du Fou]] is a much celebrated theme park in [[Vendée|Vendée]], [[France|France]].
sentence_128: It is centered around European, French and local history.
sentence_129: It received several international prizes.
sentence_130: Some theme parks did evolve from more traditional amusement park enterprises, such as [[Knott's_Berry_Farm|Knott's Berry Farm]].
sentence_131: In the 1920s, [[Walter_Knott|Walter Knott]] and his family sold berries from a roadside stand, which grew to include a restaurant serving fried chicken dinners.
sentence_132: Within a few years, lines outside the restaurant were often several hours long.
sentence_133: To entertain the waiting crowds, Walter Knott built a Ghost Town in 1940, using buildings relocated from real old west towns such as the [[Calico,_San_Bernardino_County,_California|Calico, California]] ghost town and [[Prescott,_Arizona|Prescott, Arizona]].
sentence_134: In 1968, the Knott family fenced the farm, charged admission for the first time, and Knott's Berry Farm officially became a theme park.
sentence_135: Because of its long history, [[Knott's_Berry_Farm|Knott's Berry Farm]] currently claims to be "America's First Theme Park."
sentence_136: Knott's Berry Farm is now owned by Cedar Fair Entertainment Company.
sentence_137: [[Lake_Compounce|Lake Compounce]] in [[Bristol,_Connecticut|Bristol, Connecticut]] may be the true oldest continuously operating amusement park in the United States, open since 1846.
sentence_138: Santa Claus Town, which opened in [[Santa_Claus,_Indiana|Santa Claus, Indiana]] in 1935 and included [[Santa's_Candy_Castle|Santa's Candy Castle]] and other Santa Claus-themed attractions, is considered the first themed attraction in the United States: a precursor to the modern day theme park.
sentence_139: Santa Claus Land (renamed [[Holiday_World_&_Splashin'_Safari|Holiday World]] in 1984) opened in 1946 in [[Santa_Claus,_Indiana|Santa Claus, Indiana]] and many people will argue that it was the first true Theme Park despite Knott's history.
sentence_140: In the 1950s the Herschend family took over operation of the tourist attraction, Marvel Cave near [[Branson,_Missouri|Branson, Missouri]].
sentence_141: Over the next decade they modernized the cave, which led to large numbers of people waiting to take the tour.
sentence_142: The Herschend family opened a recreation of the old mining town that once existed atop Marvel Cave.
sentence_143: The small village eventually became the theme park, Silver Dollar City.
sentence_144: The park is still owned and operated by the Herschends and the family has several other parks including [[Dollywood|Dollywood]], [[Celebration_City|Celebration City]] and [[Wild_Adventures|Wild Adventures]].
sentence_145: The first regional amusement park, as well as the first [[Six_Flags|Six Flags]] park, [[Six_Flags_over_Texas|Six Flags over Texas]] was officially opened in 1961 in [[Arlington,_Texas|Arlington, Texas]].
sentence_146: The first Six Flags amusement park was the vision of Angus Wynne, Jr. and helped create the modern, competitive amusement park industry.
sentence_147: In the late 1950s, Wynne visited Disneyland and was inspired to create an affordable, closer, and larger amusement park that would be filled with fantasy.
sentence_148: He followed in the steps of Disney and had subdivisions within the park that reflected different lands.
sentence_149: The subdivisions included the Old South and other sections that referenced Wynne's background.
sentence_150: By 1968, the second [[Six_Flags|Six Flags]] park, [[Six_Flags_Over_Georgia|Six Flags Over Georgia]], opened, and in 1971, Six Flags Over Mid-America (now [[Six_Flags_St._Louis|Six Flags St. Louis]]) opened near [[St._Louis,_Missouri|St.
sentence_151: Louis, Missouri]].
sentence_152: Also in 1971 was the opening of the [[Walt_Disney_World|Walt Disney World]] resort complex in [[Florida|Florida]], with the [[Magic_Kingdom|Magic Kingdom]] (1971), [[Epcot|Epcot]] (1982), [[Disney's_Hollywood_Studios|Disney's Hollywood Studios]] (1989) and Disney's Animal Kingdom (1998).
sentence_153: Amusement parks collect much of their revenue from admission fees paid by guests attending the park.
sentence_154: Other revenue sources include parking fees, food and beverage sales and souvenirs.
sentence_155: Practically all amusement parks operate using one of two admission principles:
sentence_156: In amusement parks using the pay-as-you-go scheme, a guest enters the park at little or no charge.
sentence_157: The guest must then purchase rides individually, either at the attraction's entrance or by purchasing ride tickets (or a similar exchange method, like a token).
sentence_158: The cost of the attraction is often based on its complexity or popularity.
sentence_159: For example, a guest might pay one ticket to ride a [[Carousel|carousel]] but four tickets to ride a [[Roller_coaster|roller coaster]].
sentence_160: The park may allow guests to purchase a pass providing unlimited admissions to all attractions within the park for a specified duration of time.
sentence_161: A wristband or pass is then shown at the attraction entrance to gain admission.
sentence_162: [[Disneyland_Park_(Anaheim)|Disneyland]] opened in 1955 using the pay-as-you-go format.
sentence_163: Initially, guests paid the ride admission fees at the attractions.
sentence_164: Within a short time, the problems of handling such large amounts of coins led to the development of a ticket system that, while now out of use, is still part of the amusement-park lexicon.
sentence_165: In this new format, guests purchased ticket books that contained a number of tickets, labeled "A," "B" and "C." Rides and attractions using an "A-ticket" were generally simple, with "B-tickets" and "C-tickets" used for the larger, more popular rides.
sentence_166: Later, the "D-ticket" was added, then finally the "[[E_ticket|E-ticket]]", which was used on the biggest and most elaborate rides, like [[Space_Mountain_(Disneyland)|Space Mountain]].
sentence_167: Smaller tickets could be traded up for use on larger rides, so that for example two or three A-tickets would equal a single B-ticket.
sentence_168: Disneyland, as well as the [[Magic_Kingdom|Magic Kingdom]] at Walt Disney World, abandoned this practice in 1982.
sentence_169: An amusement park using the pay-one-price scheme will charge guests a single admission fee.
sentence_170: The guest is then entitled to use most of the attractions (usually including flagship roller coasters) in the park as often as they wish during their visit.
sentence_171: A daily admission pass (daypass) is the most basic fare on sale, also sold are season tickets which offer holders admission for the entire operating year (plus special privileges for the newest attractions), and [[Fast_Lane_(Cedar_Fair)|express passes]] which gives holders priority in bypassing lineup queues for popular attractions.
sentence_172: Pay-one-price format parks also have attractions that are not included in the admission charge; these are called "up-charge attractions" and can include [[Skycoaster|Skycoasters]] or [[Go-kart|go-kart tracks]], or games of skill where prizes are won.
sentence_173: When Angus Wynne, founder of [[Six_Flags_Over_Texas|Six Flags Over Texas]], first visited [[Disneyland_Park_(Anaheim)|Disneyland]] upon its opening in 1955, he noted that park's pay-as-you-go format as a reason to make his park pay-one-price.
sentence_174: He thought that a family would be more likely to visit his park if they knew, up front, how much it would cost to attend.
sentence_175: See [[List_of_amusement_rides|List of amusement rides]]
sentence_176: Mechanized thrill machines are a defining feature of amusement parks.
sentence_177: Early rides include the [[Carousel|carousel]], which originally developed from cavalry training methods first used in the [[Middle_Ages|Middle Ages]].
sentence_178: By the 19th century, carousels were common in parks around the world.
sentence_179: Another such ride which shaped the future of the amusement park was the [[Roller_coaster|roller coaster]].
sentence_180: The origins of roller coasters can be traced back to 17th-century Russia, where gravity-driven attractions, which at first only consisted of individual sleds or carts riding freely down chutes on top of specially constructed snow slopes with piles of sand at the bottom for braking, were used as winter leisure activities.
sentence_181: These crude and temporarily built curiosities, known as [[Russian_Mountains|Russian Mountains]], were the beginning of the search for even more thrilling amusement park rides.
sentence_182: The Columbian Exposition of 1893 was a particularly fertile testing ground for [[Amusement_ride|amusement rides]] and included some that the public had never seen before, such as the world's first Ferris wheel, one of the most recognized products of the fair.
sentence_183: In the present day, many rides of various types are set around a specific theme.
sentence_184: Parks contains a mixture of attractions which can be divided into several categories.
sentence_185: [[Flat_ride|Flat rides]] are usually considered to be those that move their passengers in a plane generally parallel to the ground.
sentence_186: There is a core set of [[Flat_ride|flat rides]] which most amusement parks have, including the [[Enterprise_(ride)|enterprise]], [[Tilt-a-whirl|tilt-a-whirl]], [[Gravitron|gravitron]], chairswing, swinging inverter ship, twister, and top spin.
sentence_187: However, there is constant innovation, with new variations on ways to spin and throw passengers around appearing in an effort to keep attracting customers.
sentence_188: Manufactures such as [[Huss_Rides|Huss]] and [[Zamperla|Zamperla]] specialise in creating flat rides among other amusement attractions.
sentence_189: Main article: [[Roller_coaster|Roller coaster]]
sentence_190: Amusement parks often feature multiple roller coasters of primarily timber or steel construction.
sentence_191: Fundamentally, a roller coaster ride is one in which a specialized railroad system with steep drops and sharp curves, passengers sit and are restrained in cars, usually with two or more cars joined to form a train.
sentence_192: Some roller coasters feature one or more inversions (such as [[Vertical_loop|vertical loops]]) which turn the riders upside down.
sentence_193: Over the years there have been many roller coaster manufacturers with a variety of types of roller coasters.
sentence_194: Manufacturers today include:
sentence_195: Amusement park railways have had a long and varied history in American amusement parks as well as overseas.
sentence_196: Some of the earliest park trains were not really trains; they were [[Tram|trolleys]], which brought park patrons to the parks on regular rail lines from the cities to the end of the rail lines where the parks were located.
sentence_197: As such, some older parks, such as [[Kennywood|Kennywood]] in [[Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]], were referred to as [[Trolley_park|trolley parks]].
sentence_198: The earliest park trains that only operated on lines within the park's boundaries, such as the one on the [[Ridable_miniature_railway|ridable miniature]] Zephyr Railroad in Dorney Park, were mostly custom-built.
sentence_199: A few parks trains (such as the [[Disneyland_Railroad|Disneyland Railroad]], [[Walt_Disney_World_Railroad|Walt Disney World Railroad]], and Dollywood Express) operate using locomotives that had working careers on common carrier railways.
sentence_200: Amusement park railways tend to be [[Narrow_gauge_railway|narrow gauge]], meaning the space between their rails is smaller than that of 4 ft 8 ⁄2 in (1,435 mm) [[Standard_gauge|standard gauge]] railroads.
sentence_201: Some specific narrow gauges that are common on amusement park railroads are [[3_ft_gauge_railways|3 ft]] (914 mm) gauge, [[2_ft_6_in_gauge_railways|2 ft 6 in]] (762 mm) gauge, [[2_ft_and_600_mm_gauge_railways|2 ft]] (610 mm) gauge, and [[Fifteen-inch_gauge_railway|15 in]] (381 mm) gauge.
sentence_202: Past and present manufacturers include:
sentence_203: Main article: [[Water_ride|Water ride]]
sentence_204: Amusement parks with water resources generally feature a few water rides, such as the [[Log_flume_(attraction)|log flume]], bumper boats, [[Rapids|rapids]] and rowing boats.
sentence_205: Such rides are usually gentler and shorter than roller coasters and many are suitable for all ages.
sentence_206: Water rides are especially popular on hot days.
sentence_207: Main article: Dark ride
sentence_208: Overlapping with both train rides and water rides, dark rides are enclosed attractions in which patrons travel in guided vehicles along a predetermined path, through an array of illuminated scenes which may include lighting effects, animation, music and recorded dialogue, and other special effects.
sentence_209: Main article: [[Ferris_wheel|Ferris wheel]]
sentence_210: Ferris wheels are the most common type of [[Amusement_ride|amusement ride]] at [[State_fair|state fairs]] and county fairs in the US.
sentence_211: Transport rides are used to take large numbers of guests from one area to another, as an alternative to walking, especially for parks that are large or separated into distant areas.
sentence_212: Transport rides include chairlifts, [[Monorail|monorails]], [[Aerial_tram|aerial trams]], and escalators.
sentence_213: [[Ocean_Park_Hong_Kong|Ocean Park Hong Kong]] is well known for its 1.5-kilometre (0.9 mi) cable car connecting the Lowland and Headland areas of the park, and for having the world's second longest outdoor escalator in the Headland.
sentence_214: Both transportation links provide scenic views of the park's hilly surroundings and, while originally intended for practicality rather than thrills or enjoyment, have become significant park attractions in their own right.

sentence_2: There are a total of 2,186 such divisions in Hebei, divided into 1 [[District_public_office|district public office]] ([[Nanshan_District,_Zhuolu_County|Nanshan District, Zhuolu County]]) 241 [[Subdistrict_(China)|subdistricts]], 939 [[Town_(China)|towns]], 954 [[Townships_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China|townships]], and 51 [[Ethnic_township|ethnic townships]], the last type mainly designated for the [[Hui_Chinese|Hui]], [[Manchu_people|Manchu]], and/or [[Mongols|Mongol]] [[Ethnic_groups_of_China|ethnic groups]].
sentence_3: This list is divided first into the prefecture-level cities then the county-level divisions.

sentence_0: Zhang Quanyi (Chinese: 張全義) (852 – April 29, 926), né Zhang Juyan (張居言) or Zhang Yan (張言), known as Zhang Zongshi (張宗奭) during [[Later_Liang_(Five_Dynasties)|Later Liang]], [[Courtesy_name|courtesy name]] Guowei (國維), formally Prince Zhongsu of Qi (齊忠肅王), was a late [[History_of_China|Chinese]] dynasty [[Tang_Dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] warlord who later was a senior official during the succeeding [[Later_Liang_(Five_Dynasties)|Later Liang]] and Later Tang.
sentence_1: He was credited for rebuilding the city of Luoyang from utter destruction from the warfares in the late Tang period into a prosperous city.

section_1.value: Background and service under Huang Chao

sentence_2: Zhang Quanyi was born in 852, during the reign of [[Emperor_Xuānzong_of_Tang|Emperor Xuānzong]].
sentence_3: His biography in the [[Old_History_of_the_Five_Dynasties|History of the Five Dynasties]] indicated that he was originally named Zhang Juyan, and his biography in the [[New_History_of_the_Five_Dynasties|New History of the Five Dynasties]] indicated that he was originally named Zhang Yan.
sentence_4: His family was from Linpu (臨濮, in modern [[Heze|Heze]], [[Shandong|Shandong]]), and both his grandfather Zhang Lian (張璉) and father Zhang Cheng (張誠) were farmers.
sentence_5: Zhang Quanyi himself served as a farm inspector for the Linpu County government, but in his service was often insulted by the county magistrate.
sentence_6: Therefore, when, late in the Qianfu era (874-879) of Emperor Xuānzong's grandson [[Emperor_Xizong_of_Tang|Emperor Xizong]], when the region was overrun by the major agrarian rebel [[Huang_Chao|Huang Chao]], Zhang joined Huang's army.
sentence_7: After Huang captured the Tang imperial capital [[Chang'an|Chang'an]] and forced Emperor Xizong to flee to Chengdu around the new year 881, Huang established a new state of Qi with himself as emperor.
sentence_8: Zhang served in Huang's government as the minister of civil service affairs (吏部尚書, Libu Shangshu) and the director of transportation.

section_2.value: Service under Zhuge Shuang and Zhuge Zhongfang

sentence_9: After Huang Chao was eventually defeated by Tang forces and chased out of Chang'an, Zhang Quanyi joined the army of the Tang general [[Zhuge_Shuang|Zhuge Shuang]] the military governor ([[Jiedushi|Jiedushi]]) of Heyang Circuit (河陽, headquartered in modern [[Jiaozuo|Jiaozuo]], Henan).
sentence_10: He distinguished himself serving under Zhuge, and Zhuge eventually made him the prefect of Ze Prefecture (澤州, in modern [[Jincheng|Jincheng]], Shanxi).
sentence_11: Zhuge died in 886.
sentence_12: Zhang and another officer of Zhuge's, Liu Jing (劉經), supported Zhuge's son Zhuge Zhongfang (諸葛仲方) as acting military governor.
sentence_13: Liu, however, controlled the governance of the circuit, drawing resentment from other officers.
sentence_14: Late in 886, Liu became suspicious of the officer [[Li_Hanzhi|Li Hanzhi]], and he decided to use Luoyang as a base to launch a surprise attack on Li's base at Minchi (æ¾ æ± , in modern Luoyang).
sentence_15: Li defeated him, however, forcing him to abandon Luoyang and flee north of the [[Yellow_River|Yellow River]] back to the circuit capital Heyang.
sentence_16: Li gave chase, and was about to chase the Yellow River, when Liu sent Zhang to try to stop Li.
sentence_17: However, as Zhang also resented Liu's hold on the circuit governance, he instead joined Li, and they jointly attacked Heyang but could not capture it.
sentence_18: They then withdrew to Huai Prefecture (懷州, in modern Luoyang).
sentence_19: As this Heyang Circuit internecine confrontation was going on, the former Tang general [[Qin_Zongquan|Qin Zongquan]], who had declared himself emperor at Fengguo Circuit (奉國, headquartered in modern [[Zhumadian|Zhumadian]], Henan), sent his general [[Sun_Ru|Sun Ru]] toward Heyang, and Sun soon captured the city.
sentence_20: Zhuge Zhongfang fled to Xuanwu Circuit (宣武, headquartered in modern [[Kaifeng|Kaifeng]], Henan).
sentence_21: Sun thereafter claimed the title of military governor of Heyang.
sentence_22: However, Zhang and Li occupied Huai and Ze Prefectures, respectively, and resisted Sun.
sentence_23: After Qin thereafter suffered a major defeat at the hands of Xuanwu's military governor [[Zhu_Wen|Zhu Quanzhong]], Sun withdrew from Heyang.
sentence_24: Zhang and Li rejoined forces, with Li taking over Heyang and Zhang taking over Luoyang; they then jointly sought aid from the major warlord [[Li_Keyong|Li Keyong]] the military governor of Hedong Circuit (河東, headquartered in modern [[Taiyuan|Taiyuan]], Shanxi).
sentence_25: Li Keyong sent his officer An Jinjun (安金俊) to take over Ze Prefecture as prefect and to aid Li Hanzhi and Zhang; he also commissioned Li Hanzhi as the military governor of Heyang and Zhang as the mayor of Henan Municipality (河南, i.e., Luoyang).

section_3.value: As vassal of Li Hanzhi/Li Keyong

sentence_26: At the time that Zhang Quanyi took over as the mayor of Henan, it was said by historical accounts that the city had been laid waste by the wars, with the remnants of the population gathered within three castles of the city, totaling less than 100 households.
sentence_27: Zhang set up his headquarters at one of those castles, Zhongzhou (中州), while selecting 18 capable officers and sending them out to the 18 counties of the municipality other than the two in the city center, to be in charge of rebuilding their counties and welcoming the refugee population back.
sentence_28: He simplified the laws, making murder the only capital offense, while the other offenses were punishable only by caning; he also exempted the people from taxes.
sentence_29: As a result, the refugee population returned in droves, and he trained them in the military arts so that they could defend themselves.
sentence_30: Within a few years, the city recovered to appearing to be like the old days before the wars, and the fields were no longer fallow, but filled with mulberries and hemp.
sentence_31: It was said that the larger counties were capable of producing 7,000 soldiers, and the smaller counties 2,000.
sentence_32: It was said that Zhang governed with intelligence and that his subordinates could not deceive him.
sentence_33: He rewarded the households that was particularly good at farming wheat or sericulture with clothes and tea.
sentence_34: Under his rule, Henan became a rich city again.
sentence_35: Meanwhile, Zhang initially had a cordial relationship with Li Hanzhi, whose Heyang Circuit his Henan Municipality belonged to, and they even cut their own arms to swear to be brothers.
sentence_36: However, Li Hanzhi viewed Zhang's promotion of farming lightly.
sentence_37: He also made a habit of making all kinds of material demands on Zhang, to the point that whenever he was not satisfied with what Zhang supplied his army, he would arrest Zhang's subordinates and cane them.
sentence_38: Initially, Zhang put on the appearance of fearing Li Hanzhi and doing everything to appease him.
sentence_39: In 888, when Li Hanzhi was on a campaign against the army of Huguo Circuit (護國, headquartered in modern Yuncheng, Shanxi), Huguo's military governor [[Wang_Chongying|Wang Chongying]] sent secret emissaries to persuade Zhang to turn against Li Hanzhi.
sentence_40: Zhang agreed, and he launched a surprise attack on Heyang at night, capturing it and taking Li Hanzhi's household captive.
sentence_41: He then claimed the title of military governor of Heyang for himself.
sentence_42: Li Hanzhi fled to Ze Prefecture and sought aid from Li Keyong.
sentence_43: Li Keyong sent his officer [[Kang_Junli|Kang Junli]], commanding five other officers ([[Li_Cunxiao|Li Cunxiao]], Xue Atan (薛阿檀), Shi Yan (史儼), An Jinjun, and An Xiuxiu (安休休) to aid Li Hanzhi in trying to recapture Heyang.
sentence_44: They put Heyang under siege, and the food supplies ran out.
sentence_45: Zhang Quanyi thus sent his wife and children to Zhu Quanzhong as hostages to seek aid from him.
sentence_46: Zhu sent his officers [[Ding_Hui_(general)|Ding Hui]], [[Ge_Congzhou|Ge Congzhou]], and Niu Cunjie (牛存節) to aid Zhang.
sentence_47: They defeated the Hedong forces, and then postured to cut off the Hedong forces' return path to Hedong through the Taihang Mountains.
sentence_48: In fear, Kang took his army and withdrew.
sentence_49: Zhu commissioned Ding the acting military governor of Heyang and recommissioned Zhang as the mayor of Henan.
sentence_50: It was said that because Zhang was appreciative of Zhu's saving his life, he never had any thoughts of turning against Zhu from this point on, and he plenteously supplied Zhu's army in Zhu's subsequent campaigns.
sentence_51: Soon thereafter, Henan was turned into its own circuit (Youguo (佑國)), and then-reigning [[Emperor_Zhaozong_of_Tang|Emperor Zhaozong]] (Emperor Xizong's brother and successor) commissioned Zhang its military governor.
sentence_52: In 890, when the imperial government, at the request of Zhu's and that of [[Li_Kuangwei|Li Kuangwei]] the military governor of Lulong Circuit (盧龍, headquartered in modern [[Beijing|Beijing]], declared a general campaign against Li Keyong, Zhang led an army to participate in Zhu's operation, along with Ge and Zhu's son Zhu Youyu (朱友裕), to wrest Zhaoyi Circuit (昭義, headquartered in modern Changzhi, Shanxi) from Li Keyong's control.
sentence_53: The campaign, however, eventually ended in failure when Li Keyong's main forces crushed the imperial forces commanded by the chancellor [[Zhang_Jun_(Tang_chancellor)|Zhang Jun]], and Li Keyong was able to retain Zhaoyi at that point.
sentence_54: Later in the year, Zhang received the honorary chancellor title of Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi (同中書門下平章事).
sentence_55: In 892, after Zhu, for reasons unclear to history, requested that then-military governor of Heyang, Zhao Keyu (趙克裕), be demoted, Zhang was made the military governor of Heyang, in addition to Youguo.
sentence_56: (However, at some point, Ding was made acting military governor of Heyang again, and in 899 was made full military governor.)
sentence_57: In 896, by which time Emperor Zhaozong had fled to Zhenguo Circuit (鎮國, headquartered in modern [[Weinan|Weinan]], Shaanxi), which was then governed by [[Han_Jian_(Zhenguo_warlord)|Han Jian]], due to attacks on Chang'an by [[Li_Maozhen|Li Maozhen]] the military governor of Fengxiang Circuit (鳳翔, headquartered in modern Baoji, Shaanxi), Zhu Quanzhong and Zhang were submitted repeated joint petitions for the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang.
sentence_58: In fear, Li Maozhen apologized to the emperor, repaired the palace and office buildings at Chang'an, and welcomed Emperor Zhaozong back to Chang'an.
sentence_59: In 898, Emperor Zhaozong bestowed the greater honorary chancellor title of Shizhong on Zhang.
sentence_60: In 900, when the [[Eunuch_(court_official)|eunuch]] [[Liu_Jishu|Liu Jishu]] briefly overthrew Emperor Zhaozong in a coup and replaced him with his son [[Li_Yu,_Prince_of_De|Li Yu, Prince of De]] the Crown Prince, Zhang Jun, who had by that point retired to Changshui (長水), one of the counties of Henan, went to meet with Zhang Quanyi to encourage him and the other military governors to start a campaign to restore Emperor Zhaozong.
sentence_61: There was no record of any actual action taken by Zhang Quanyi.
sentence_62: (However, in 901, Emperor Zhaozong was restored in a countercoup headed by the imperial guard officers Sun Dezhao (孫德昭), Dong Yanbi (董彥弼), and Zhou Chenghui (周承誨).
sentence_63: Shortly after, Zhang Quanyi was given the honorary chancellor title of Zhongshu Ling (中書令).
sentence_64: By 903, Zhu Quanzhong had taken Emperor Zhaozong under his control, and was planning on eventually usurping the Tang throne.
sentence_65: He feared that Zhang Jun would again encourage the military governors to attack him.
sentence_66: He thus ordered Zhang Quanyi to kill Zhang Jun.
sentence_67: Zhang Quanyi sent his officer Yang Lin (楊麟) to take a group of soldiers, disguised as bandits, to attack Zhang Jun's mansion and slaughter his household.
sentence_68: Only Zhang Jun's son [[Zhang_Ge|Zhang Ge]] escaped the slaughter.
sentence_69: Subsequently, Zhu Quanzhong destroyed Chang'an and moved Emperor Zhaozong to Luoyang.
sentence_70: He then moved Zhang Quanyi to be the military governor of Tianping Circuit (天平, headquartered in modern [[Tai'an|Tai'an]], [[Shandong|Shandong]].
sentence_71: He also had Zhang created the Prince of Dongping.
sentence_72: In 904, by which point Zhu had assassinated Emperor Zhaozong and replaced him with his son [[Emperor_Ai_of_Tang|Li Zuo]] the Prince of Hui (as Emperor Ai), Zhang Quanyi was again made the mayor of Henan; he was additionally also made the military governor of Zhongwu Circuit (å¿ æ­¦, headquartered in modern Weinan), apparently commanding it remotely, and the overall commander of the imperial guards.
sentence_73: In 907, Zhu Quanzhong had Emperor Ai yield the throne to him, ending Tang and starting a new [[Later_Liang_(Five_Dynasties)|Later Liang]] as its Emperor Taizu.
sentence_74: He made Zhang Quanyi the military governor of Heyang, in addition to being the mayor of Henan, again, and created him the Prince of Wei.
sentence_75: Soon thereafter, he changed Zhang Quanyi's name to Zhang Zongshi, apparently due to naming taboo as his own name included the character "Quan."
sentence_76: In 908, in addition to his other offices, Zhang was also made Taibao (太保) and the military governor of Zhenguo Circuit (鎮國, headquartered in modern [[Sanmenxia|Sanmenxia]], Henan).
sentence_77: In 910, he was additionally made the military governor of Xuanyi Circuit (宣義, headquartered in modern [[Anyang|Anyang]], Henan.
sentence_78: In 911, Emperor Taizu spent the summer at Zhang's summer mansion.
sentence_79: He used the opportunity to have sexual relations with virtually every woman in Zhang's household.
sentence_80: Zhang's son Zhang Jizuo (張繼祚), humiliated, wanted to assassinate the emperor.
sentence_81: Zhang Zongshi pointed out that it was because of Emperor Taizu's initially stopping Li Hanzhi's attack that the Zhang household was preserved, and he managed to persuade Zhang Jizuo not to carry out the assassination.
sentence_82: (According to Zhang's biography in the New History of the Five Dynasties, the women that Emperor Taizu had sexual relations with included even Zhang Zongshi's wife Lady Chu and his daughters.)

section_7.value: During Zhu Yougui's and Zhu Zhen's reigns

sentence_83: In 912, Emperor Taizu was assassinated by his son [[Zhu_Yougui|Zhu Yougui]] the Prince of Ying, who took the throne thereafter.
sentence_84: As part of the governmental reorganization that took place after Zhu Yougui took the throne, he disbanded the headquarters for financial matters at the eastern capital [[Kaifeng|Kaifeng]] (which previously had been the headquarters of Xuanwu Circuit while Zhu Quanzhong governed it), which Emperor Taizu had created and had named Jianchang Palace (建昌宮).
sentence_85: The responsibility of overseeing the financial matters was transferred to Zhang Zongshi.
sentence_86: Zhang was also made the military governor of Xuanwu Circuit (whose headquarters had been moved to modern [[Shangqiu|Shangqiu]], Henan by that point).
sentence_87: In 913, Zhu Yougui's younger brother [[Zhu_Zhen|Zhu Youzhen]] the Prince of Jun overthrew him and took the throne, and subsequently moved the capital from Luoyang to Kaifeng, but it appeared that Zhang remained in charge of the financial matters of the state.
sentence_88: In 917, Zhu Youzhen (who had changed his name to Zhu Zhen) further bestowed on Zhang the title of Deputy Generalissimo of All Circuits (天下兵馬副元帥).
sentence_89: (The Generalissimo title belonged to [[Qian_Liu|Qian Liu]] the Prince of Wuyue, whose state was a Later Liang vassal state.)
sentence_90: In 921, Zhu Zhen, suspicious of the intentions of the major general [[Liu_Xun_(Later_Liang)|Liu Xun]], who had sought retirement, approved Liu's retirement and had him reside at Luoyang.
sentence_91: He then ordered Zhang to poison Liu to death.
sentence_92: In 923, Zhu Zhen, with the territory of his Later Liang state north of the [[Yellow_River|Yellow River]] gradually taken piece by piece by his rival [[Emperor_Zhuangzong_of_Later_Tang|Li Cunxu]] the Prince of Jin (Li Keyong's son and successor), planned a major counterattack.
sentence_93: At the recommendation of his close associates [[Zhao_Yan_(Later_Liang)|Zhao Yan]] and Zhang Hanjie (張漢傑), he made the general [[Duan_Ning|Duan Ning]], whose military abilities was not respected by the army, the overall commander of the operations.
sentence_94: Zhang Zongshi, knowing that Duan was not the appropriate commander and that the army generals were more respectful of another general, [[Wang_Yanzhang|Wang Yanzhang]], submitted a petition stating:
sentence_95: Despite Zhang's petition (and similar remarks made by the chancellor [[Jing_Xiang|Jing Xiang]]), Zhu Zhen continued to leave Duan in command.
sentence_96: Subsequently, before Duan could start his operations, Li Cunxu made a surprise maneuver across the Yellow River around Duan's army, and directly attacked Kaifeng.
sentence_97: Zhu Zhen, unable to resist and unable to flee, committed suicide.
sentence_98: Li Cunxu, who had by that point declared himself the emperor of a new dynasty, Later Tang (as its Emperor Zhuangzong), and claimed to be the legitimate successor to Tang, entered Kaifeng and took over virtually all of the Later Liang territory.
sentence_99: The Later Liang military governors, including Zhang Zongshi, largely immediately submitted to the Later Tang emperor.
sentence_100: In winter 923, Zhang went to Kaifeng to pay homage to Emperor Zhuangzong, and he changed his name back to Quanyi.
sentence_101: He submitted a large amount of money and horses as tribute.
sentence_102: Emperor Zhuangzong had his son [[Li_Jiji|Li Jiji]] and brother Li Cunji (李存紀) honor Zhang as an older brother.
sentence_103: Subsequently, when Emperor Zhuangzong considered opening up the tomb of Emperor Taizu of Later Liang, Zhang, still grateful to Emperor Taizu for his survival, submitted a petition stating that while the two states were rivals, such an action at this point would be meaningless and would merely show Emperor Zhuangzong to be vengeful.
sentence_104: Emperor Zhuangzong agreed and did not do so, although he still destroyed the memorials built for Emperor Taizu on his tomb.
sentence_105: Soon thereafter, at Zhang's suggestion, Emperor Zhuangzong moved the capital to Luoyang.
sentence_106: He bestowed on Zhang the title of Shangshu Ling (尚書令).
sentence_107: He also changed Zhang's princely title to Prince of Qi.
sentence_108: In 924, Emperor Zhuangzong and his wife [[Empress_Liu_(Li_Cunxu's_wife)|Empress Liu]] visited Zhang's mansion for a feast.
sentence_109: At the feast, Empress Liu, claiming that she lost her parents in her youth and that she missed having parents, asked to treat Zhang as her father.
sentence_110: Zhang, in fear, initially declined, but eventually accepted.
sentence_111: Thereafter, Empress Liu and he often sent messengers back and forth, and he submitted much tribute to her.
sentence_112: In 926, Emperor Zhuangzong, who had alienated his soldiers due to his failure to properly reward them for their contributions during his campaigns, was facing a mutiny by the Weibo Circuit (魏博, headquartered in modern [[Handan|Handan]], Hebei) army.
sentence_113: He initially sent the general [[Yuan_Xingqin|Li Shaorong]] to try to suppress the rebellion, but Li Shaorong was unable to do so.
sentence_114: Zhang, instead, recommended the senior general, and Emperor Zhuangzong's adoptive brother, [[Li_Siyuan|Li Siyuan]].
sentence_115: Upon Li Siyuan's arrival at Weibo, however, his own soldiers mutinied and forced Li Siyuan to join the Weibo soldiers in the rebellion.
sentence_116: Li Siyuan subsequently led his army south, toward Kaifeng.
sentence_117: When Zhang heard this, he became fearful as he was the one who had recommended Li Siyuan, and he stopped eating.
sentence_118: He died soon thereafter.

sentence_0: Monreith House is a [[Listed_building|category A listed]] [[Georgian_architecture|Georgian]] mansion located 1.5 kilometres (0.93 mi) east of the village of [[Port_William,_Scotland|Port William]] in [[Mochrum|Mochrum]] parish in the historical county of Wigtownshire in [[Dumfries_and_Galloway|Dumfries and Galloway]], Scotland.
sentence_1: The classical-style house was designed by Alexander Stevens in 1791, for [[Maxwell_Baronets#Maxwell_of_Monreith_(1635)|Sir William Maxwell, 4th Baronet]].
sentence_2: The new house replaced the now-ruined Myrton Castle on the estate.
sentence_3: The grounds of the house are included in the [[Inventory_of_Gardens_and_Designed_Landscapes_in_Scotland|Inventory of Gardens and Designed Landscapes in Scotland]], the national listing of significant gardens, and are classed as "outstanding" in five out of six categories.
sentence_4: The Maxwell family first acquired Monreith in the 15th century, and built Myrton Castle on the estate.
sentence_5: William Maxwell of Monreith was created a baronet of Nova Scotia in 1681.
sentence_6: Magdalene Blair, wife of the third baronet, made tapestries of the gardens in the mid 17th century, which remain in the house.
sentence_7: Sir William Maxwell, 4th Baronet, inherited the estate in 1771 and commissioned the present Monreith House from Alexander Stevens (1739–1796) in 1791.
sentence_8: Sir William also laid out the grounds of the house as they largely remain today.
sentence_9: In 1821 the porch was added to designs by [[Robert_Smirke_(architect)|Sir Robert Smirke]].
sentence_10: [[Sir_Herbert_Maxwell,_7th_Baronet|Sir Herbert Maxwell]] (1845–1937) succeeded as 7th Baronet in 1877.
sentence_11: He sat as Member of Parliament for [[Wigtownshire_(UK_Parliament_constituency)|Wigtownshire]] from 1880 to 1906, and was admitted to the [[Privy_Council_of_the_United_Kingdom|Privy Council]] in 1897.
sentence_12: He also served as [[Lord_Lieutenant_of_Wigtown|Lord Lieutenant of Wigtown]] until 1935.
sentence_13: In 1911 he published a book on Scottish gardens, and developed a substantial plant collection at Monreith.
sentence_14: Following his death and the [[Second_World_War|Second World War]], the house was rented and the gardens declined.
sentence_15: His grandson was [[Gavin_Maxwell|Gavin Maxwell]] author of Ring of Bright Water who was born at The [[Elrig|House of Elrig]] on the estate.
sentence_16: The 9th baronet Sir Michael inherited the estate in the 1980s and carried out restoration work to the house, including the creation of holiday accommodation.
sentence_17: In March 2011, Monreith House was the subject of a [[Channel_4|Channel 4]] television documentary presented by hotelier [[Ruth_Watson|Ruth Watson]] as part of her [[Country_House_Rescue|Country House Rescue]] series.
sentence_18: The Monreith Cross is a 10th-century free-standing carved stone cross.
sentence_19: The cross stands 2.3 metres (7 ft 7 in) high, and the circular head is 0.45 metres (1 ft 6 in) across.
sentence_20: The cross originally stood on a hill known as the Mowr or Moure, but was moved several times.
sentence_21: In 1974 it was removed from the Monreith estate for conservation, and is now on display in the Whithorn Museum.

title: The Hunger Games (film)
sentence_0: The Hunger Games is a 2012 American [[Utopian_and_dystopian_fiction|dystopian]] [[Science_fiction_film|science fiction]] [[Action_film|action film]] directed by [[Gary_Ross|Gary Ross]] and based on [[Suzanne_Collins|Suzanne Collins]]'s [[The_Hunger_Games_(novel)|2008 novel of the same name]].
sentence_1: It is the first installment in [[The_Hunger_Games_(film_series)|The Hunger Games film series]] and was produced by [[Nina_Jacobson|Nina Jacobson]] and Jon Kilik, with a screenplay by Ross, Collins, and [[Billy_Ray_(screenwriter)|Billy Ray]].
sentence_2: The film stars [[Jennifer_Lawrence|Jennifer Lawrence]], [[Josh_Hutcherson|Josh Hutcherson]], [[Liam_Hemsworth|Liam Hemsworth]], [[Woody_Harrelson|Woody Harrelson]], [[Elizabeth_Banks|Elizabeth Banks]], [[Lenny_Kravitz|Lenny Kravitz]], [[Stanley_Tucci|Stanley Tucci]], and [[Donald_Sutherland|Donald Sutherland]].
sentence_3: Set in a dystopian post-apocalyptic future in the nation of [[Panem|Panem]], where a boy and a girl from each of the nation's 12 Districts are chosen annually as "tributes" and forced to compete in The Hunger Games, an elaborate televised fight to the death, [[Katniss_Everdeen|Katniss Everdeen]] ([[Jennifer_Lawrence|Jennifer Lawrence]]) volunteers to take her younger sister's place.
sentence_4: With her district's male tribute, [[Peeta_Mellark|Peeta Mellark]] ([[Josh_Hutcherson|Josh Hutcherson]]), Katniss travels to the Capitol to train and compete in the games.
sentence_5: Development of The Hunger Games began in March 2009 when [[Lions_Gate_Entertainment|Lions Gate Entertainment]] entered into a co-production agreement with Color Force, which had acquired the rights a few weeks earlier.
sentence_6: Collins collaborated with Ray and Ross to write the screenplay.
sentence_7: The screenplay expanded the character of Seneca Crane to allow several developments to be shown directly to the audience and Ross added several scenes between Crane and Coriolanus Snow.
sentence_8: The main characters were cast between March and May 2011.
sentence_9: Principal photography began in May 2011 and ended in September 2011, with filming taking place in [[North_Carolina|North Carolina]].
sentence_10: The film was released on March 21, 2012, in some European countries and in the US and UK on March 23, 2012, in both conventional theaters and digital IMAX theaters.
sentence_11: Japan received it last, on September 28.
sentence_12: When the film was released, it set records for opening day ($67.3 million) and opening weekend for a non-sequel.
sentence_13: At the time of its release, the film's opening weekend gross ($152.5 million) was the third-largest of any film in North America.
sentence_14: It is the first film since [[Avatar_(2009_film)|Avatar]] to remain in first place at the North American box office for four consecutive weekends.
sentence_15: The film was a massive box-office success by grossing over $694 million worldwide against its budget of $78 million, making it the third-highest-grossing film in the United States and [[2012_in_film#Highest-grossing_films|ninth-highest-grossing film of 2012]].
sentence_16: It was released on DVD and [[Blu-ray|Blu-ray]] on August 18, 2012.
sentence_17: With 7,434,058 units sold, the DVD was the best-selling DVD of 2012.
sentence_18: The second installment, The Hunger Games: Catching Fire, was released on November 22, 2013, in the United States.
sentence_19: The Hunger Games received positive reviews from critics, with praise for its themes and messages, as well as [[Jennifer_Lawrence|Jennifer Lawrence]]'s portrayal of Katniss; some criticism was levelled at the film's reliance on [[Shaky_camera|shaky cam]], especially in the action sequences, and its similarities to other works.
sentence_20: The film's soundtrack featured the song "[[Safe_&_Sound_(Taylor_Swift_song)|Safe & Sound]]", which was sung by American singer [[Taylor_Swift|Taylor Swift]] featuring [[The_Civil_Wars|The Civil Wars]]; it won a [[Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_Visual_Media|Grammy Award]] and was nominated for a [[Golden_Globe_Award|Golden Globe Award]] for [[Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song|Best Original Song]].
sentence_21: For her performance, Lawrence won the [[Saturn_Awards|Saturn Award]] for [[Saturn_Award_for_Best_Actress|Best Actress]], the [[Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association_Award|Broadcast Film Critics Association Award]] for Best Actress in an Action Movie, the [[Empire_Award|Empire Award]] for [[Empire_Award_for_Best_Actress|Best Actress]] and was also nominated for the [[New_York_Film_Critics_Circle_Award|New York Film Critics Circle Award]] for Best Actress.
sentence_22: The nation of Panem is divided into 12 districts, ruled from the Capitol.
sentence_23: As punishment for a failed revolt, each district is forced to select two tributes, one boy and one girl between the ages of 12 and 18, to fight to the death in the annual Hunger Games until there is only one survivor.
sentence_24: After her 12-year-old sister Primrose is chosen for the 74th Hunger Games, 16-year-old [[Katniss_Everdeen|Katniss Everdeen]] of District 12 volunteers to take her place.
sentence_25: She and fellow tribute [[Peeta_Mellark|Peeta Mellark]] are escorted to the Capitol by their chaperone Effie Trinket and mentor Haymitch Abernathy, the Games' only living winner from District 12.
sentence_26: Haymitch stresses the importance of gaining sponsors, as they can provide potentially life-saving gifts during the Games.
sentence_27: While training, Katniss observes the "Careers" (Marvel, Glimmer, Cato and Clove), volunteers from the wealthy Districts 1 and 2 who have trained for the Games from an early age.
sentence_28: During a televised interview with Caesar Flickerman, Peeta expresses his love for Katniss, which she initially sees as an attempt to attract sponsors; she later learns his admission is genuine.
sentence_29: At the start of the Games, Katniss ignores Haymitch's advice and grabs some of the supplies placed around the Cornucopia, a structure at the starting point, and narrowly escapes death.
sentence_30: Half of the 24 tributes die in the initial melee, and only eleven, including all four Careers, survive the first day.
sentence_31: Katniss tries to stay away from the others, but Seneca Crane, the Head Gamemaker, triggers a forest fire to drive her towards them.
sentence_32: She runs into the Careers, with whom Peeta has seemingly allied, and flees up a tree.
sentence_33: Peeta advises the Careers to wait her out.
sentence_34: The next morning, Katniss notices Rue, District 11's young female tribute, hiding in an adjacent tree.
sentence_35: Rue draws her attention to a nest of [[The_Hunger_Games_universe#Tracker_Jackers|tracker jackers]], genetically modified poisonous wasps.
sentence_36: Using a knife, Katniss saws off the branch holding the nest, causing it to fall on the Careers sleeping below; Glimmer dies, but the others escape.
sentence_37: Katniss becomes disoriented from being stung a few times.
sentence_38: Peeta returns and tells her to flee.
sentence_39: Rue helps Katniss recover, and they become friends and allies.
sentence_40: Katniss destroys the supplies the Careers stockpiled by detonating mines guarding them, while Rue provides a distraction.
sentence_41: Katniss later finds and frees Rue from a trap, but Marvel throws a spear at Katniss which impales Rue.
sentence_42: Katniss kills him with an arrow.
sentence_43: She comforts Rue and, after she dies, adorns her body with flowers.
sentence_44: This triggers a riot in District 11.
sentence_45: President Coriolanus Snow warns Crane about the unrest.
sentence_46: Haymitch persuades Crane to change the rules to allow two winners provided they are from the same district, suggesting that this will pacify the public.
sentence_47: After the announcement, Katniss finds a gravely wounded Peeta.
sentence_48: Another announcement promises that what each survivor needs the most will be provided at the Cornucopia the next morning.
sentence_49: Despite Peeta's vehement opposition, Katniss leaves to get medicine for him, but she is ambushed and overpowered by Clove, who gloats about Rue's death and prepares to kill her.
sentence_50: [[List_of_The_Hunger_Games_characters#Thresh|Thresh]], District 11's male tribute, overhears and kills Clove.
sentence_51: He spares Katniss once, for Rue's sake.
sentence_52: The medicine heals Peeta overnight.
sentence_53: While hunting for food, Katniss hears a cannon go off, signalling a death.
sentence_54: She races to Peeta, who has unwittingly collected deadly nightlock berries.
sentence_55: They discover "Foxface", District 5's female tribute, dead from eating what she assumed were edible berries from watching Peeta.
sentence_56: Crane then unleashes genetically modified beasts which kill Thresh and force Katniss, Peeta, and Cato - the last three survivors - onto the Cornucopia's roof.
sentence_57: Cato gets Peeta in a headlock and uses him as a human shield against Katniss's bow.
sentence_58: Peeta directs Katniss to shoot Cato's hand, enabling Peeta to throw him to the beasts below.
sentence_59: Katniss kills him with an arrow to end his suffering.
sentence_60: Crane then revokes the rule change allowing two victors to win.
sentence_61: Peeta urges Katniss to shoot him, but she convinces him to eat nightlock together.
sentence_62: Just before they do, Crane hastily declares them co-victors.
sentence_63: Afterward, Haymitch warns Katniss that she has made enemies through these acts of defiance.
sentence_64: Snow has Crane locked in a room with nightlock berries, after which the wily President considers his next move.
